Runtime SDK deep probe: Bun, Deno, Cloudflare

What the Sentry SDKs actually do on Bun, Deno and Cloudflare Workers, measured by running 74 reproductions on two SDK versions, and where the docs are silent or wrong about it.

SDK versionsdevelop = getsentry/sentry-javascript at 6f2da7483d (the v11 line, package version 10.67.0, built in ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs, installed from npm pack tarballs or worktree symlinks); 10.73.0 = the published release from npm
Runtimesbun 1.4.0 and 1.3.14 (CI pin), deno 2.9.0 and 2.8.3 (CI pin), wrangler 4.56 to 4.129 with local workerd, node v26.5.0 as the driver
Method74 probes, one agent each, both versions where the behavior exists on both. Every probe ran a real app against a local envelope sink (qs/sink.mjs via tunnel), drove it from a separate process, and waited for a sentinel event. Each broken or partial result was then handed to two independent agents told to make it work, one with the documented setup, one with a different reasonable configuration. Docs coverage was checked per probe in a separate pass.
Whereprobe apps and logs under scratchpad/deep/<ID>/, records in deep/probe-results.json, toolbox for re-running in deep/TOOLBOX.md, this report regenerated by deep/build-report.py
Daterounds one and two 2026-09-04, round three 2026-09-06 and 2026-09-07

Snapshot check on 2026-09-07

Both repositories moved after the snapshots. Docs: getsentry/sentry-docs master is at b568ebbd3 (2026-09-04); of the 70 commits since 046ce5942, none touches the Bun, Deno, Cloudflare, Hono or Elysia guides or their platform includes, and the only audited framework guide file that changed is guides/astro/profiling/index.mdx. Every docs citation in this report still holds. SDK: develop is at d6426ad581 (2026-09-07), 127 commits past 6f2da7483d. The ones that touch the audited packages: the Deno stream-cancellation fix c619da370 (changes F24), the new dataCollection.queues option in 21ee24506 (not probed), the postgres.js and SQL helper move into server-utils in 37fd6a5c8 and 5ab39b51b (no behavior change probed here), a Vercel AI token-usage fix, and a Next.js Turbopack warning change. Nothing landed for @sentry/bun, @sentry/elysia, @sentry/hono or the framework SDKs other than Nuxt and Next.js, so the framework matrix stands.

Nothing was committed. Four stray log files landed in the repo root during the runs (app1314.log, drive-.json, run-.log, sink1314.log); they are junk and can be deleted.

The follow-up round added ten more behaviors (F41 to F50), run and verified the same way.

A third round, finished 2026-09-07, ran the full cross product of 17 frameworks and 3 runtimes against develop only: 51 cells, 170 independent refutations, one docs verdict per cell. It replaces the earlier framework table; see Framework matrix on develop, verified.

Verdict legend per probe: works behaves as the docs or the reasonable expectation say; partial part of it does; broken does not; not-run could not be run here.

The short version

Bun. The Bun.serve path is solid on both versions: errors, route names from routes: {}, per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, enrichment, logs, metrics. On the published 10.73.0 everything that goes through Node APIs is not: outgoing fetch produces no span and no trace headers, and a node:http server (which is what Express, Koa, Hapi, Fastify and next start use) gets no transactions and no request isolation, so tags leak between concurrent requests. develop fixes both with fetchIntegration and bunHttpServerIntegration. Library spans need a Bun.build with the Sentry plugin on both versions; on 10.73.0 that covers database drivers and the OpenAI SDK, on develop also Express, Koa, Hapi and Fastify. Two things no page says: Bun.serve never captures request bodies, and a Bun.serve streaming response ends its span when the handler returns, not when the stream ends. The database span loss for lazily loaded drivers is a Bun bug in node:diagnostics_channel (channels are garbage collected when nothing holds them) that hits both Bun versions, with an SDK-side fix available.

Deno. The base SDK is good: errors, Deno.serve and node:http spans, isolation, incoming continuation, enrichment, logs, metrics, deno compile. Outgoing fetch is still not traced. The library hook (import "@sentry/deno/import") is where the trouble is: it needs a local node_modules, it needs --allow-env or it crashes, it cannot transform anything that loads statically before it registers (so the OpenAI SDK is never instrumented), it turns any .mjs it does transform into a crash, and it breaks every require() of a JSON file (Express, Hapi, Fastify, mysql2) through a Deno bug. What works with the hook today: mysql and pg style CommonJS drivers that load lazily. Fastify and mysql2 (3.20 and later) work without the hook on develop, because they publish their own channels (on 10.73.0 the mysql2 integration has to be passed in from @sentry/server-utils). Oak works when mounted on Deno.serve instead of app.listen(). denoCronIntegration crashes on Deno 2.9.0 unless Deno.cron is redefined as a writable property first.

Cloudflare. The broadest and best-covered runtime. Errors, isolation, continuation, env-based config, D1, R2, Queues, Durable Objects with storage and alarms, RPC, Workflows, scheduled handlers with cron monitors, Pages, logs, metrics, the Vite plugin, and every framework we tried on 10.73.0 (SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, React Router 7, TanStack Start, Next.js via OpenNext, Hono) work. What no page says: errors thrown inside ctx.waitUntil() are lost on both versions; KV produces no spans; queue and R2 spans exist; a Pages middleware also spans static assets; sessions only exist if you drive them with the @sentry/core session API. 10.73.0 has two defects fixed on develop: all scheduled and queue invocations of an isolate share one trace id, and dataCollection: { httpBodies: [] } is ignored. develop has two regressions of its own: the cached client makes Dedupe drop repeated errors across requests, and the @sentry/cloudflare/request entry runs without an async-context strategy, which under the new stream lifecycle turns some requests into legacy transaction envelopes and drops events.

Framework matrix on develop, verified

Develop only (v11 line at 6f2da7483d, packages 10.67.0 from npm pack). One Opus agent per framework and runtime cell, 51 cells, the full cross product of 17 frameworks and 3 runtimes, each probing eight capabilities against the same envelope sink. Every capability called broken or partial was handed to a second, independent Opus agent that rebuilt the app from scratch and tried to refute it: 170 refutations. The table shows the verified state. ✓ works with the documented wiring. ✓* works, but only with extra wiring that no page shows today (the cell record has the exact snippet). ◐ partial. ✗ confirmed broken. · not run (no browser surface in the probe app, or the capability was not exercised in that cell). A cell counts as ✓* only when the extra wiring uses shipped public exports; where the only working path was a hand-written integration built from core primitives, the cell stays ✗ and the cell record keeps the snippet.

What the refutations changed

The grid below holds 72 capabilities that work only with extra wiring, 17 that stay partial and 19 that stay broken, out of 351 that ran. Every one of those went through at least one independent refutation, several through two. That ratio is the finding: the framework SDKs run on Bun and Deno, but they are Node SDKs, and nothing in the docs tells a Bun or Deno user what to add. The root causes are few and repeat across cells.

Only one combination of the 51 does not run at all: Fastify on Workers. Everything else boots, including four Node HTTP frameworks on workerd behind the enable_nodejs_http_server_modules flag, Oak and Fresh outside Deno, and Elysia outside Bun. Those paths carry real Sentry data and no page documents them.

Nine root causes behind the whole grid

#Root causeCells it hitsVerified fixWhere it belongs
R1Framework SDKs on Bun get no request or fetch instrumentation. @sentry/nextjs, nuxt, sveltekit, astro, react-router, tanstackstart-react, solidstart and remix initialize the Node SDK. Bun never publishes http.server.request.start and Node's undici fetch channels never fire, so route names, isolation, incoming trace and outgoing fetch are all silently absent.Nuxt, React Router, TanStack, SolidStart, Remix, SvelteKit, Astro, Next.js on BunInstall @sentry/bun next to the framework SDK and add bunServerIntegration() or bunHttpServerIntegration() (whichever server the framework uses) plus fetchIntegration() to the server init, gated on typeof Bun !== "undefined". The repo's own e2e app nextjs-16-bun does exactly this.A "Running on Bun" section on every framework guide, or one guides/bun/frameworks.mdx that the framework guides link to.
R2Bun garbage-collects diagnostics channels. Bun's registry holds channels weakly; when only Sentry's subscriber references a channel, it is dropped before the driver first loads. Node keeps subscribed channels alive.db spans on Astro, Next.js, SvelteKit, TanStack, SolidStart, Nuxt on Bun (K11 from round one, now shown in six frameworks)Pin the channels after Sentry.init() (globalThis.__sentryPinnedChannels = names.map(n => dc.tracingChannel(n))) or import the driver at startup. The SDK could keep the references itself in @sentry/bun.SDK fix first; until then a Bun caveat on the database integration pages.
R3Drivers without native diagnostics channels need the Bun bundle. mysql2 ≥ 3.20 publishes its own channels and works under plain bun app.ts. mysql@2, Express, Koa, Fastify, Hapi and the AI SDKs need Bun.build with sentryBunPlugin().Elysia, Fastify, NestJS, Remix, Hono on BunDocument the split: which libraries need the plugin build and which do not. NestJS must also list its optional peers as external or the build fails.Bun guide, "Library instrumentation" section, plus a table of drivers.
R4@sentry/deno ships no fetch integration. getDefaultIntegrations() in packages/deno/src/sdk.ts has denoHttpIntegration only, which subscribes to node:http channels. A global fetch() gets no http.client span and no sentry-trace header, so every trace stops at the first downstream service.outgoing fetch on all 17 Deno cells with the documented wiring; 7 recover it with a shipped integration (winterCGFetchIntegration from @sentry/vercel-edge, fetchIntegration from @sentry/cloudflare or @sentry/elysia), Remix through its own installGlobals(), Nuxt only under the stream lifecycle, and 8 stay broken because only a hand-written integration was tried thereUserland integration from addFetchInstrumentationHandler + instrumentFetchRequest (about 20 lines, verified on both lifecycles), or fetchIntegration from @sentry/cloudflare, or winterCGFetchIntegration from @sentry/vercel-edge (Next.js already depends on it). The SDK fix is small: reuse the Bun fetch integration in the Deno defaults.SDK fix; Deno guide must state the limit and show the snippet until then.
R5Deno's import hook and its two bugs. Registering any Module.registerHooks load hook breaks CJS require("*.json") (denoland/deno#36240, fix in denoland/deno#36243), and the hook cannot transform modules that load statically before it registers.Hapi, Koa, NestJS, SvelteKit, Fresh, React Router, TanStack on DenoTwo shapes, both verified: (a) keep the hook, add a short JSON load hook before the framework import; (b) skip the hook and bundle with esbuild plus sentryOrchestrionPlugin() from @sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild, or use the framework's build-time Vite plugin (sentryReactRouter, TanStack noExternals). Koa needs the hook registered after Koa is imported.Deno guide, "Library instrumentation": the hook path and the bundle path side by side.
R6Deno leaks the AsyncLocalStorage store out of a handler that awaits a dynamic import(). Node does not. Scope data (tags, user, breadcrumbs) from one request shows up on the next.Fresh on Deno (confirmed), Nuxt on Deno with the deno_server preset (partial)App-level only: replace the isolation scope in a middleware before ctx.next(). Nuxt: build with the default node-server preset and run that output with deno run.Deno guide caveat; Fresh and Nuxt on Deno sections.
R7Node HTTP frameworks on Workers need build-time instrumentation, and a wrangler-bundled Worker gets none. Express, Koa, Hapi and NestJS boot on workerd behind enable_nodejs_http_server_modules with httpServerHandler from cloudflare:node. Route names, framework spans and database spans then depend on the channels being injected at build time; a plain wrangler dev or wrangler deploy emits none and logs no warning.Express, Koa, Hapi, NestJS, Fresh, Elysia on CloudflareBuild with Vite and sentryCloudflareVitePlugin(), or with sentryOrchestrionPlugin() from @sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild for non-Vite builds. Koa additionally requires the app, every use and listen to be constructed inside the fetch handler, because the instrumented use starts a span at worker startup and workerd rejects that.A "Node HTTP frameworks on Workers" page, plus a shared build-time-instrumentation page: sentryOrchestrionPlugin is exported from six entry points and documented nowhere.
R8Frameworks that catch their own errors report nothing. Fresh's default error handler, Hapi's transmit path on workerd, SolidStart's Nitro error path and NestJS's exception layer all swallow the throw before it reaches the runtime handler the SDK wraps.Fresh on all three runtimes, Hapi on Cloudflare, SolidStart on Bun and Cloudflare, NestJS everywherePer framework: a Fresh middleware or error route that calls captureException for Fresh (the console-capture integration for the error level also works), an onRequest extension for Hapi on workerd, an h3 middleware for SolidStart, and the documented SentryGlobalFilter for NestJS.Each framework page needs the hook named. The BunServer page's blanket "captures errors automatically" claim needs qualifying.
R9A framework with no Sentry integration is named by method or URL only. Oak, Fresh and SolidStart have no route instrumentation, so the server span carries the raw URL under the static lifecycle and the bare method under the default stream lifecycle.Oak and Fresh on all three runtimes, SolidStart on all three runtimesA middleware that renames the root span from the matched route and then sets sentry.segment.name.source to route. Renaming alone leaves the source as custom. On Bun, Oak can also get real names by passing a routes map to Bun.serve.The transaction-name page must document the source attribute, and each framework page needs the snippet.

Framework-specific notes that survived verification

  • Next.js. Bun: R1 and R2; a project directory named app above the app/ router breaks route names (rename the root). Deno: needs enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false or every request fails with SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'; fetch via winterCGFetchIntegration. Cloudflare (OpenNext): outgoing fetch needs @sentry/cloudflare installed explicitly and its fetchIntegration() in the server config; mysql2 needs disableEval: true.
  • Nuxt. Bun: R1 fixes four capabilities with two integrations; Nitro bundling mysql2 breaks every query (genFunc$1 is not a function) until nitro.externals lists it. Deno: do not use the deno_server preset; the default node-server output runs under Deno with route names and incoming trace intact, and isolation still partial. Cloudflare: route names need a second Nitro plugin that renames the root span from the matched route (verified with public @sentry/cloudflare exports).
  • SvelteKit. Bun: R1 (fetch) and R2 (db). Deno: db spans need createRequire(import.meta.url)("mysql2/package.json") before Sentry.init so the JSON is cached before the hook registers. Cloudflare: route names are confirmed broken, the Cloudflare segment span keeps the URL; a user-land handle between initCloudflareSentryHandle and sentryHandle renames it; on npm or Yarn installs add ssr.noExternal: [/^@sentry\//] or db spans are missing (pnpm needs nothing).
  • Astro. Bun: R1 (fetch) and R2 (db). Deno: fetch is R4. Cloudflare: everything works with the documented wiring.
  • React Router. Bun: the probe had dropped the documented export const instrumentations = [Sentry.createSentryServerInstrumentation()]; with it, plus R1, everything but db spans works, and db spans follow with bunHttpServerIntegration(). Bun's react-dom/server has no renderToPipeableStream, so the entry must use renderToReadableStream. Deno: use the sentryReactRouter Vite plugin with ssr.noExternal: true instead of the require hook. Cloudflare: works.
  • TanStack Start. Bun: R1, plus sentryTanstackStart() must be the first Vite plugin so Nitro does not bundle the SDK; db spans need the R2 pin. Deno: pass noExternals to the Nitro plugin and use Vite 8. Cloudflare: works.
  • Remix. Bun: bundle the server with Bun.build + sentryBunPlugin() (never bun server.mjs), drop "sideEffects": false from the app package.json or the db module is tree-shaken, and wrap the Express handler call yourself for isolation and incoming trace. Cloudflare: use withSentry as the Worker entry instead of wrapRequestHandler for isolation; import from @sentry/remix/cloudflare, never bare @sentry/remix.
  • SolidStart. Runs on all three runtimes. Route names are confirmed broken on every runtime: SolidStart mounts the whole app as one Nitro catch-all handler, so spans are named by URL (source: "url"). Errors thrown in file API routes or during page render are turned into a 500 by SolidStart and never reach Sentry without an h3 middleware (Bun) or a Nitro plugin forwarding the error hook (Cloudflare). Bun also needs R1 and R2.
  • NestJS. Bun: must be bundled; the docs-prescribed @sentry/nestjs init loses route names on Bun, initialize from @sentry/bun and add nestIntegration() from @sentry/nestjs. Deno: R5 (JSON hook) restores route names; fetch is R4.
  • Hono. Bun and Cloudflare: everything works. Do not pass external: ["@sentry/*"] to Bun.build with Hono, it splits the bundled Hono from the external @sentry/hono and the patches miss. Deno: R4 only.
  • Elysia. Works, two defects: sdk.name reports sentry.javascript.bun (SDK bug in @sentry/elysia, the options spread drops the metadata) and db spans follow R3.
  • Express, Fastify, Koa, Hapi on Bun. Everything works with the plugin build; Fastify and Koa also unbundled for mysql2. On Deno all four hit R4 (Fastify recovers with a shipped integration, the other three were only tried with a hand-written one), Hapi and Koa also R5; Koa additionally needs the hook registered after the Koa import for db spans.
  • Oak. Runs on all three runtimes. On Deno mount with Deno.serve(app.fetch), never app.listen(). On Bun and Workers it must be installed through the JSR npm bridge, because Oak's current line ships only to JSR and the npm package stops at 14.1.0. Route names are R9 everywhere; on Bun a routes map built from the router at startup fixes them.
  • Fresh. Runs on all three runtimes, and the built server is a plain fetch handler, so Workers and Bun need no adapter. Errors are R8, route names are R9. On Deno isolation is confirmed broken through the runtime's AsyncLocalStorage leak. On Workers the Sentry Vite plugin must not go in Fresh's config, because there is no Cloudflare worker environment for it to instrument and it breaks the driver; bundle the wrangler entry separately with the orchestrion esbuild plugin.
  • Elysia beyond Bun. Runs on Deno and on Workers. On Workers it needs new Elysia({ aot: false }), or workerd refuses to start the Worker, and then everything but database spans works with no extra wiring. On Deno the documented wiring is actively wrong: Sentry.init from @sentry/elysia delegates to the Bun SDK, which does not instrument Deno.serve, so every request in the process shares one trace, tags and request URLs bleed between requests, and no server span exists. Initialize from @sentry/deno and keep withElysia, at the cost of losing Elysia attribution in sdk.name.
  • Remix and SolidStart on Deno. Remix works fully once installGlobals() from @remix-run/node restores an instrumentable fetch and the server is bundled with the orchestrion esbuild plugin with enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false. SolidStart is the weakest cell in the matrix: errors, route names, isolation and outgoing fetch all fail, and the guide's own verification snippet produces no issue there.
  • Fastify on Workers. The only combination of the 51 that does not run. Constructing the app at module scope throws a disallowed-global-scope error, and lazy construction on first request then hits a second workerd restriction that blocks serving.

Docs gaps per runtime, one line per framework

It must say: (1) A static `import "@sentry/deno/import"` as the first import of the entry file does not work for Koa — Deno instantiates the whole module graph, including `koa`, before any module body executes, so the hook is registered too late; load it with the CLI flag instead (`deno run --import=./preload.ts main.ts`). (2) On Deno 2.9.0, registering any `Module.registerHooks` load hook breaks CJS `require('*.json')` (denoland/deno#36240), and Koa's `statuses` dependency does exactly that, so the app must also register a JSON-restoring load hook (`registerHooks({ load(url, ctx, next) { const r = next(url, ctx); return url.endsWith('.json') ? { ...r, format: 'json' } : r; } })` or the `readFileSync` equivalent); with the flag plus that hook, route names work. (3) An alternative that avoids the runtime hook entirely and was verified for both error capture and library spans: bundle the Koa app with esbuild and `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild` (`format: 'esm'`, `external: ['@sentry/deno', '@sentry/server-utils']`, plus a `createRequire` banner) and run the bundle with Deno — no import hook and no manual `app.on('error')` handler needed. (4) For database spans without bundling, keep `import "@sentry/deno/import"` out of the static import list and register it in the entry body after Koa is imported (`await import('@sentry/deno/import')`), then dynamically import the driver. Isolation, incoming trace continuation and logs need no caveat. Outgoing `fetch` is not instrumented — no `http.client` span, no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` — in both `static` and `stream` lifecycles; the page must ship the userland fetch integration built from `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` / `defineIntegration` / `getClient` / `instrumentFetchRequest`, and note `node:http`/`node:https` are traced normally.

  • Oak no guides/deno/frameworks/oak.mdx (new), with the `Deno.serve(app.fetch)` vs `app.listen()` warning as its first section
    An Oak page must exist and must lead with the mounting shape, because the two Oak mounting styles are not equivalent for Sentry: mount with `Deno.serve(app.fetch)` and never with `app.listen()` — under `app.listen()` handlers run outside the request's async context, so there is no active span and errors are never captured at all. With `Deno.serve(app.fetch)`, errors, isolation, incoming trace continuation, database spans and logs all work with no extra wiring. Two caveats must be documented. (1) Route names: Oak spans are named by HTTP method only until the app names them; register a `router.use()` middleware BEFORE any route on that router that reads `ctx.matched?.at(-1)?.path` and calls `Sentry.updateSpanName(Sentry.getActiveSpan(), \`${ctx.request.method} ${route}\`)`. (2) Outgoing requests: `@sentry/deno` does not instrument Deno's global `fetch` — no `http.client` span, no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` header, so the downstream service starts a new trace. Two fixes were verified in both trace lifecycles: use `node:http` for the outgoing call (zero code beyond the client swap — `http.get(url, ...)` produced `http.client GET <url>` plus both headers), or keep `fetch` and register a userland fetch integration built from `@sentry/core` primitives. The page must also show the `deno.json` shape the run needed: `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual", "imports": {"@oak/oak": "jsr:@oak/oak@^17", "@sentry/deno": "npm:@sentry/deno"}}` with the SDK present in a real `node_modules`.

    A Fresh 2 page must exist and state that Fresh on Deno is viable but that nothing framework-specific is instrumented automatically — a hand-written middleware is required. It must document, in this order: (1) Setup — scaffold with `deno run -A jsr:@fresh/init@^2`, set `"nodeModulesDir": "manual"` in `deno.json`, keep `import "@sentry/deno/import"` as the first line of `instrument.ts` and `instrument.ts` as the first import of `main.ts`. (2) Errors — Fresh catches route errors itself and returns its own 500 page, so unhandled errors never reach Sentry on their own; the verified fix is `integrations: [Sentry.captureConsoleIntegration({ levels: ['error'], handled: false })]` in `Sentry.init`, which reports them as real exceptions carrying the request's trace id, in both `deno task dev` and the `deno serve _fresh/server.js` build. (3) Route names — spans stay unparameterized unless the app renames them: register a middleware right after `staticFiles()` that reads `ctx.route` and calls `Sentry.updateSpanName` on the root span, which is the only way to get `sentry.segment.name.source: 'route'`. (4) Isolation — per-request isolation is not reliable on Deno: Deno leaks the AsyncLocalStorage store out of a handler that awaits a dynamic `import()` (Node does not), so `Sentry.setTag`/`setUser`/`setContext`/`addBreadcrumb` from one request can attach to every later request; the app-level mitigation is to replace the isolation scope in the middleware before `ctx.next()` (new `Sentry.Scope`, `setClient(Sentry.getClient())`, carry over the propagation context and SDK processing metadata). (5) Outgoing fetch — no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers for native `fetch`; ship the userland `fetchTracingIntegration` built from `addFetchInstrumentationHandler`, `defineIntegration` and `instrumentFetchRequest`. (6) Database spans — `@fresh/plugin-vite` sets `resolve.noExternal: true`, so every instrumented driver must be listed in BOTH `ssr: { external: [...] }` (for `deno task dev`) and `environments: { ssr: { build: { rollupOptions: { external: [...] } } } }` (for `deno task build`); `ssr.external` alone does not survive the build. Parameterized transaction names require build-time instrumentation, either the Cloudflare Vite plugin or the orchestrion plugin for esbuild, rollup or webpack, with a plain-wrangler fallback that renames the root span in an onPreResponse extension. Database spans need the same build-time instrumentation. Isolation, incoming trace, outgoing fetch and logs work unaided.

A parameterless server route such as `/api/health` is reported as bare `GET` under the default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'`, and as the full request URL under `traceLifecycle: 'static'` — in both cases with a URL-derived name rather than the Nitro route pattern. The page must state this limitation and show the ship-today fix that was verified to produce identical output to a patched SDK: a second Nitro server plugin registered next to the Sentry one that uses only public `@sentry/cloudflare` exports (`getActiveSpan`, `getRootSpan`, `spanToJSON`) to rename the root span to the matched Nitro route and set the segment-name source accordingly.

(1) Route names are confirmed broken on Workers: unlike the Node SvelteKit SDK, the transaction/segment span is named by the Cloudflare request handler and keeps the raw URL — `GET /users/42` with `transaction_info.source: url` under `traceLifecycle: 'static'`, and bare `GET` with source `url` under the default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` — never the SvelteKit route id. The page must state this and show the verified fix: a user-land `handle` inserted between `initCloudflareSentryHandle` and `sentryHandle` in the `sequence`, which renames the Cloudflare segment span using `getActiveSpan`/`getRootSpan` from `@sentry/sveltekit`; it works in both lifecycles. (2) Database spans come from the build-time transform that `sentrySvelteKit()` (:387) already installs, so no extra setup is needed and the connection may live at module scope or inside the handler — but only on pnpm's isolated `node_modules`. On a flat `node_modules` (npm or Yarn) the spans are missing until `ssr: { noExternal: [/^@sentry\//] }` is added to `vite.config.js`; that single regex is the minimal fix (naming only `@sentry/core` is not enough, and `@opentelemetry/api` need not be listed).

(1) Error capture: on Cloudflare Workers and Pages the `handleError` import must come from `@sentry/remix/cloudflare`, never bare `@sentry/remix` — the bare specifier silently captures nothing in a `webworker` SSR build. Both `export const handleError = sentryHandleError` and `wrapHandleErrorWithSentry` work from that subpath, on both trace lifecycles, for loaders, actions, resource routes and thrown 5xx Responses. (2) Request isolation: the worker entry must be wrapped with `withSentry` from `@sentry/cloudflare` around a handler built with `instrumentBuild` from `@sentry/remix/cloudflare`. `wrapRequestHandler` from `@sentry/cloudflare/request` exists only for runtimes that cannot enable `nodejs_compat` (Shopify Oxygen); on Workers it does not establish isolation unless `setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy` is called first. Without the plugin, queries run normally, no `db` span appears, and the SDK logs no warning. The `_experimental.useDiagnosticsChannelInjection: true` requirement stated on the Vite plugin page is no longer needed on the v11 line and must be corrected there too. It must then document the two capabilities that need extra work beyond that wrapper. (1) Server errors are not captured by the wrapper alone: add a Nitro server plugin that forwards Nitro's `error` hook to `Sentry.captureException` and register it with `server.plugins: ['./src/server-plugin.ts']` in `app.config.ts`. (2) Route names are wrong: add `src/middleware.ts` (registered via `middleware: './src/middleware.ts'` in `app.config.ts`) that builds a radix3 router from vinxi's route manifest and renames the Cloudflare root span per request using `getActiveSpan`/`getRootSpan`/`spanToJSON` and the segment-name-source attribute. With those in place isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing fetch, logs and client-side errors all work; database spans were not exercised.

Hono on Bun M-hono-bun

Hono 4.10.x (`hono@4`) with `@sentry/hono/bun` 10.67.0 (develop, v11 line) · Bun 1.4.0 (`bun`), both unbundled (`bun app.ts`) and as a `Bun.build` bundle with `sentryBunPlugin` · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Packages: `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-hono-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bun-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz hono@4 mysql2@3 mysql@2` (npm, not `bun add`; bun then reads the resulting node_modules fine).

Entry file (`app.ts`) — no separate instrument file, no `--preload`; the middleware does the init:

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono';
import * as Sentry from '@sentry/hono/bun';
import { sentry } from '@sentry/hono/bun';
import mysql from 'mysql2';

const conn = mysql.createConnection({ host: '127.0.0.1', port: 3307, user: 'root', database: 'app' }); // MODULE SCOPE

const app = new Hono();
app.use(sentry(app, { dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' }));

app.get('/users/:id', c => c.json({ id: c.req.param('id') }));
export default { port: 41800, fetch: app.fetch };   // Bun idiom, NOT `serve(app)`
```

Run unbundled: `bun app.ts`. Everything except legacy-`mysql` spans works this way.

Bundled (only needed for drivers that do not publish diagnostics_channel themselves, e.g. `mysql@2`) — `build.ts`:

```ts
import { sentryBunPlugin } from '@sentry/bun/plugin';
await Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./app.ts'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', sourcemap: 'external', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] });
```

`bun run build.ts && bun dist/app.js`. Note: do NOT pass `external: ['@sentry/*']` here — that splits `hono` (bundled) from `@sentry/hono` (external) and the Hono patches then apply to a different Hono copy. With no `external` at all the bundle works and every capability below still passes.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksAn error thrown in `app.get('/boom')` is captured with mechanism `auto.http.hono.context_error`, handled=false, transaction `GET /boom`, and stack frames with context lines; the transaction is marked `internal_error`. Hono's default onError still returns 500 to the client, so the error is not swallowed from Sentry's point of view - the middleware reads `context.error` in its response handler. Identical unbundled and bundled, in both `static` and `stream` lifecycle.
route names✓ works`GET /users/:id` with `source: "route"` and `http.route: /users/:id` on the server span, from the parameterized Hono route. In `traceLifecycle: 'static'` it is the transaction name; in `stream` the `http.server` span is named `GET /users/:id` and carries `http.route`. No method-only fallback, so the Hono middleware's route resolution overrides the bare Bun.serve naming.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent `GET /iso/:tag` requests (each `Sentry.setTag('req-tag', ...)`, then a 150-250ms await, then `captureException`) produced three events each carrying only its own tag and its own trace id, and three transactions with the matching tag and trace id. No cross-talk. Lifecycle: static.
incoming trace✓ worksA request with `sentry-trace: aaaa...-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` plus baggage yields a transaction with `trace_id: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` and `parent_span_id: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`. Same in stream lifecycle (trace `cccc...`, parent `dddddddddddddddd`). Lifecycle: static and stream.
outgoing fetch✓ works`fetch()` from inside a handler to a local recorder produced a child span `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41802/rec` under `GET /fetchout` (static) / low-cardinality `http.client GET 127.0.0.1` in stream, and the recorder saw `sentry-trace: <same trace id>-<span id>-1` plus a full baggage header including `sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Ffetchout`. Note this contrasts with Deno finding K2.
db spans✓ worksModule-scope `mysql2@3.24.3` connection queried inside a handler gives `db SELECT * FROM users` (static) / `db SELECT users` (stream) WITHOUT any bundle - mysql2 >=3.x publishes `mysql2:query` tracing channels itself and the SDK's DC subscriber picks them up under plain `bun app.ts`. Legacy `mysql@2` gives NO span unbundled and DOES get `db SELECT * FROM users` after a `Bun.build` with `sentryBunPlugin()`. So the Bun plugin build is needed only for drivers without native diagnostics_channel; for mysql2 it is optional.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info('hono-bun-log-line', { where: 'handler' })` inside a handler arrives as a `log` envelope item `info: hono-bun-log-line` about 5s later (timer flush). Works unbundled and bundled; no `enableLogs` option needed on develop.
client errors· not-runNo browser surface in this cell - Hono on Bun is a server-only app, so there is no client-side SDK to probe.

Headline: Hono on Bun is the strongest of the non-Node runtimes I saw here — every one of the seven capabilities passed, unbundled, with the single middleware line the docs already show. Nothing was broken or partial. Two findings worth acting on: 1. The "Bun needs a bundle for library spans" rule is now driver-dependent, not blanket. `mysql2@3.24.3` ships its own `node:diagnostics_channel` tracing channels (`node_modules/mysql2/lib/tracing.js:9-31`, channels `mysql2:query` / `mysql2:execute` / `mysql2:connect`), and the SDK's `@sentry/server-utils` mysql2 DC subscriber picks them up under plain `bun app.ts`. Legacy `mysql@2` has no such channels and stays silent until built with `sentryBunPlugin`. This softens the established Bun fact ("records NO library spans") — it is true for build-time-injected drivers, false for drivers with native DC. Any docs page should say which case a reader is in rather than "bundle or nothing". 2. Bundle boundary: `external: ['@sentry/*']` (the shape the toolbox lists for the generic Bun app) is actively wrong for Hono, because it leaves `hono` inside the bundle and `@sentry/hono` outside, so the prototype patches land on a different Hono instance. Bundling everything (`Bun.build` with no `external`) worked for all seven capabilities including the Hono route names. Worth stating explicitly in the docs if a bundle recipe is ever added. Other observations: - `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` (the develop default) already carries `http.route` and the `GET /users/:id` name on the `http.server` span, so route naming does not depend on choosing `static`. Stream also shows the new low-cardinality client names (`http.client GET 127.0.0.1`, `db SELECT users`) versus static's full descriptions. - The error mechanism is `auto.http.hono.context_error`, i.e. the middleware reads `c.error` after `await next()`. An error thrown by a middleware registered *before* `sentry(app, ...)` would not reach that check; I did not probe that ordering. - Cleanup: all five server processes killed (pids captured in `*.pid`), no listeners left on 41733/41799-41802, and `node_modules` (118M) removed. `dist/` and the source files remain.

Elysia on Bun M-elysia-bun

Elysia 1.4 (@sentry/elysia 10.67.0, develop / v11 line) · bun 1.4.0 · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Elysia runs on bun with no adapter. Wiring that a docs page would show:

1. `npm install elysia mysql2` then `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-elysia-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bun-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz` (npm, not `bun add`; bun then reads node_modules fine). In real life: `bun add @sentry/elysia`.

2. `instrument.ts`:
```ts
import * as Sentry from '@sentry/elysia';
Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0 /*, traceLifecycle: 'static' */ });
```

3. `app.ts` — `import './instrument';` as the FIRST line, then:
```ts
import * as Sentry from '@sentry/elysia';
import { Elysia } from 'elysia';
import mysql from 'mysql2/promise';
const pool = mysql.createPool({ host:'127.0.0.1', port:3307, user:'root', database:'app' }); // module scope
const app = Sentry.withElysia(new Elysia())
  .get('/users/:id', ({ params }) => ({ id: params.id }))
  .listen(41372);
```
`withElysia` must wrap the fresh `new Elysia()` before any route is chained.

4. Run: `bun app.ts`. No `--preload` needed, no `@elysiajs/opentelemetry`, no Bun build plugin for the base capabilities. (Init inline in the entry, as the docs page shows, works too; a separate instrument file is not required because `withElysia` does the patching, not a module-load hook.)

5. Only if you use a driver that does not publish node:diagnostics_channel itself (e.g. `mysql`@2): add a bundle step — `build.ts` with `Bun.build({ entrypoints:['./app.ts'], outdir:'./dist', target:'bun', sourcemap:'external', plugins:[sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin`, then `bun dist/app.js`. Do NOT mark `elysia`/`@sentry/elysia` external, no `external` at all works.

With DEBUG=1 the plain run logs `Sentry Logger [warn]: No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping.` and then `[instrumentation:mysql] Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly` / `Integration installed: Mysql` — the SDK does subscribe to `orchestrion:mysql:query`, nothing ever publishes it. packages/server-runtime-injection/src/register.ts:123 requires `module.registerHooks` for the runtime hook, and its `Module.register` fallback at line 127 is explicitly gated `&& !globalAny.Bun && !globalAny.Deno`. On bun 1.4.0 `require('node:module').registerHooks` is `undefined` (only `register` exists), so neither branch is reachable. packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/bundler/bun.ts states this outright: "This is BUILD-ONLY. Runtime instrumentation (`bun run`) is intentionally not offered: a module returned by a runtime `onLoad` plugin in Bun loses its CommonJS named exports" (pending oven-sh/bun#31770). So the split is by driver, not by framework: any library that publishes node:diagnostics_channel itself (mysql2) is instrumented under plain `bun app.ts`; any library the SDK must inject channels into (mysql@2, and by the same mechanism pg, redis, ioredis, mongodb, kafkajs, ...) needs `bun build` with sentryBunPlugin. Reference app agreement: the repo's own dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/bun-mysql runs `bun run dist/app.js` off a `build.ts` using `sentryBunPlugin()` and asserts exactly these mysql attributes, while dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/elysia-bun runs `bun src/app.ts` unbundled and has no db route at all. There is no e2e app combining Elysia and a database, so this combination is untested upstream. Elysia-specific note: nothing about Elysia is the limiter. `Sentry.withElysia(new Elysia())` survives the bundle unchanged (route names, middleware spans, `src=route` all identical bundled vs unbundled), and building with no `external` at all works.
Workaround: For drivers that do not publish node:diagnostics_channel themselves (mysql@2, pg, redis, ioredis, mongodb, ...), add a build step and run the bundle instead of the source. build.ts: `import { sentryBunPlugin } from '@sentry/bun/plugin'; await Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./app.ts'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', sourcemap: 'external', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })`, then `bun dist/app.js`. Do not pass `external` (and never `packages: 'external'` or `'*'`); the plugin strips instrumented packages back out of `external`, but a blanket strategy defeats it and only produces a console warning. Elysia and @sentry/elysia can be bundled with no special handling. The alternative workaround is to pick a driver that publishes its own channels: mysql2 needs no build step at all.

Root cause in packages/elysia/src/sdk.ts: `const options = { ...userOptions, ... }` copies the options BEFORE `applySdkMetadata(userOptions, 'elysia', ...)` runs, so the elysia `_metadata` is written onto `userOptions` and never reaches the `options` object handed to `@sentry/bun`'s `init`, which then stamps its own metadata. verified: confirmed-broken Reproduced exactly, and could not refute it with any wiring. @sentry/elysia 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on bun 1.4.0, elysia 1.4. Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-elysia-bun-sdkname/ (RERUN.sh has every command; node_modules removed after the run, RERUN.sh reinstalls it). Wirings tried, all with `Sentry.withElysia(new Elysia())` wrapping the fresh instance before routes, `bun app.ts`, no --preload, no bundler: A) separate instrument.ts imported as the first line of app.ts, traceLifecycle 'stream' (default) -> BROKEN B) init inline at the top of the entry file, traceLifecycle 'static' -> BROKEN The repo's own e2e app (~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/elysia-bun/src/app.ts) uses exactly shape B (inline init, traceLifecycle 'static'), so the reference app is affected too. `grep -rn "sentry.javascript.elysia"` over packages/ and dev-packages/ returns zero hits: nothing in the repo asserts the SDK name, which is why this ships unnoticed. A) sink, stream lifecycle, GET /users/42 + /boom + sentinel: CLIENT_SDK_METADATA={"sdk":{"name":"sentry.javascript.bun","packages":[{"name":"npm:@sentry/bun","version":"10.67.0"}],"version":"10.67.0"}} event | env=sentry.javascript.bun@10.67.0 | pkgs=npm:@sentry/bun | elysia-boom event | env=sentry.javascript.bun@10.67.0 | pkgs=npm:@sentry/bun | sentinel span | env=sentry.javascript.bun@10.67.0 | ... sentryOnRequest | Request | ... | GET /users/:id B) sink, static lifecycle, inline init: CLIENT_SDK_METADATA={"sdk":{"name":"sentry.javascript.bun","packages":[{"name":"npm:@sentry/bun","version":"10.67.0"}],"version":"10.67.0"}} transaction | env=sentry.javascript.bun@10.67.0 | pkgs=npm:@sentry/bun | GET /users/:id (http.server) event | env=sentry.javascript.bun@10.67.0 | pkgs=npm:@sentry/bun | elysia-boom The `CLIENT_SDK_METADATA` line is `Sentry.getClient().getOptions()._metadata` read in the app itself, so this is settled inside `init`, before any transport or event processor, and no init placement, entry shape, lifecycle, or bundler variant can move it. Root cause confirmed at source, exactly as reported. packages/elysia/src/sdk.ts: export function init(userOptions: ElysiaOptions = {}): NodeClient | undefined { const options = { ...userOptions, platform: 'javascript', runtime: getRuntime(), serverName: ... }; applySdkMetadata(userOptions, 'elysia', ['elysia', options.runtime.name]); ... return initNode(options); } `applySdkMetadata` (packages/core/src/utils/sdkMetadata.ts) does `(options._metadata = options._metadata || {}).sdk = ...`. When the caller passes no `_metadata`, the spread has already produced an `options` object with no `_metadata` key, so `applySdkMetadata` creates a brand-new object on `userOptions` that `options` never sees. `options` then reaches `@sentry/bun`'s `_init`, which does `applySdkMetadata(userOptions, 'bun')` correctly (packages/bun/src/sdk.ts:143 — before its own spread) and stamps `sentry.javascript.bun`. Sibling packages get the ordering right, which shows this is a plain slip and not a design choice: packages/hono/src/bun/sdk.ts:25, node/sdk.ts:20, deno/sdk.ts:25 all call `applySdkMetadata(options, 'hono', [...])` on the already-copied object. One-line SDK fix, proven: patch `applySdkMetadata(userOptions, "elysia"` -> `applySdkMetadata(options, "elysia"` in node_modules/@sentry/elysia/build/{esm,cjs}/sdk.js, rerun wiring A unchanged: CLIENT_SDK_METADATA={"sdk":{"name":"sentry.javascript.elysia","packages":[{"name":"npm:@sentry/elysia","version":"10.67.0"},{"name":"npm:@sentry/bun","version":"10.67.0"}],"version":"10.67.0"}} event | env=sentry.javascript.elysia@10.67.0 | pkgs=npm:@sentry/elysia,npm:@sentry/bun | elysia-boom span | env=sentry.javascript.elysia@10.67.0 | ... GET /users/:id Both the envelope header and the event payload then carry `sentry.javascript.elysia` with both packages listed, on stream and static lifecycle alike. Same `init` is used by the elysia-node entry, so @sentry/elysia on node is affected identically (not separately run here).
Workaround: User-land workaround, verified end to end: pass an empty `_metadata` object to `Sentry.init`, which makes the spread in `init` share the object reference so the elysia metadata written onto `userOptions` also lands on `options`. Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, _metadata: {}, } as any); Result (probe file app-metadata-fix.ts, static lifecycle): CLIENT_SDK_METADATA={"sdk":{"name":"sentry.javascript.elysia","packages":[{"name":"npm:@sentry/elysia","version":"10.67.0"},{"name":"npm:@sentry/bun","version":"10.67.0"}],"version":"10.67.0"}} transaction | env=sentry.javascript.elysia@10.67.0 | pkgs=npm:@sentry/elysia,npm:@sentry/bun | GET /users/:id (http.server) event | env=sentry.javascript.elysia@10.67.0 | pkgs=npm:@sentry/elysia,npm:@sentry/bun | sentinel `_metadata` is an internal option and needs a TypeScript cast, so this is a stopgap for someone blocked on SDK-name-based routing or quotas, not something to put in a guide. The real fix is the one-line reorder in packages/elysia/src/sdk.ts (move `applySdkMetadata` above the spread, as @sentry/bun and @sentry/hono already do, or call it on `options`).

Docs today

A dedicated Elysia guide exists and it is Bun-first, so the combination is documented — with three factual mismatches against develop. - ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/elysia/index.mdx:1-25 — title Elysia, `sdk: sentry.javascript.elysia`, `fallbackGuide: javascript.bun`, ALPHA alert, prerequisites "Elysia v1.4.0+, Bun or Node.js 18+ (with @elysiajs/node adapter)". - index.mdx:47-50 — "You do **not** need `@elysiajs/opentelemetry`. The `@sentry/elysia` SDK handles all instrumentation natively." Confirmed for the Bun tab. - index.mdx:56 `bun add @sentry/elysia`; index.mdx:78-104 the Bun `Sentry.init(...)` + `Sentry.withElysia(new Elysia()).get(...).listen(3000)` snippet. This exact shape works as written. - ~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:1 — the include opens with a stray browser paragraph ("The `BrowserTracing` integration creates a new transaction for each page load and navigation event...") on a server guide. - javascript.elysia.mdx:5 — claims "The Handle span uses `op: 'request_handler.elysia'`; all other lifecycle spans use `op: 'middleware.elysia'`". Observed ops are plain `handler` and `middleware`, with no `.elysia` suffix, in both lifecycles. - javascript.elysia.mdx:11 — "**Bun**: The SDK creates root server spans via Elysia's `.wrap()` API with `continueTrace` for trace propagation. No additional runtime instrumentation needed." Accurate, but it is the only place the runtime split is described, and nothing anywhere says that non-diagnostics-channel libraries (`mysql`@2, Express, etc.) still need a `@sentry/bun/plugin` build on Bun. - ~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/performance/enable-stream-mode/javascript.elysia.mdx:25 — "To revert to transaction mode, set `traceLifecycle` to `'static'` (the default) or remove the option entirely." On develop the default is `'stream'` (verified: `traceLifecycle default: "stream"`), so this sentence is inverted. - No docs page mentions the `sdk.name` reporting at all; nothing warns that events arrive tagged as the Bun SDK.

Documented: partial

The Bun-first wiring on this page is correct as published — errors, route names, isolation, incoming trace, outgoing fetch and logs all work following it. What is missing is the database/library limit observed on Bun: under a plain `bun app.ts` the SDK produces db spans only for drivers that publish `node:diagnostics_channel` events themselves (`mysql2` does, so it needs no build step); for `mysql`@2 and every other instrumented library (Express, Koa, Fastify, Hapi, AI SDKs) there are no spans at all unless the app is bundled with `Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./app.ts'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', sourcemap: 'external', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin` and run as `bun dist/app.js`. The alert at :47-50 ("handles all instrumentation natively") reads as an unconditional promise and must be qualified for Bun. Separately, the shipped SDK reports `sentry.javascript.bun` on every event, transaction and span, contradicting this page's own `sdk: sentry.javascript.elysia` frontmatter — the verified finding is that this is an SDK defect to fix in code, so no docs sentence should be written for it and the frontmatter should stay as-is.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/elysia/index.mdx — new "Database and library instrumentation on Bun" section after Configure, plus a qualifier on the alert at :47-50.

~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/elysia/index.mdx:4-5 (`sdk: sentry.javascript.elysia`, `fallbackGuide: javascript.bun`); elysia/index.mdx:23-25 (prerequisites: Elysia v1.4.0+, Bun or Node.js 18+); elysia/index.mdx:47-50 ("You do **not** need `@elysiajs/opentelemetry`. The `@sentry/elysia` SDK handles all instrumentation natively."); elysia/index.mdx:56-57 (`bun add @sentry/elysia`)

Elysia on bun is the smoothest of the non-Node runtime combinations probed: no adapter, no preload flag, no bundler, and every core capability except db-driver breadth works out of the box with the docs' own snippet. Two SDK bugs found by reading `packages/elysia/src/sdk.ts` and confirmed at runtime: 1. `sdk.name` is `sentry.javascript.bun`, never `sentry.javascript.elysia`. `const options = { ...userOptions, platform, runtime, serverName }` is built BEFORE `applySdkMetadata(userOptions, 'elysia', ['elysia', options.runtime.name])`, so the elysia metadata is written to `userOptions` and dropped; `initNode(options)` then stamps the Bun metadata. Fix is to call `applySdkMetadata(options, ...)`. This also means the docs' `sdk: sentry.javascript.elysia` front-matter never matches what Sentry receives. 2. `getDefaultIntegrations` in the same file filters `getBunDefaultIntegrations(options)` by `bunServerIntegration().name` (= `'BunServer'`) to drop "Bun's competing root span". The Bun default set on develop no longer contains `BunServer`; it contains `BunHttpServer` (`bunHttpServerIntegration`), so the filter removes nothing and `BunHttpServer` stays in the list (observed in the integration dump). Harmless in practice here because `bunHttpServerIntegration` patches `node:http.Server.prototype.emit`, not `Bun.serve`, and Elysia on Bun uses `Bun.serve` — no duplicate root span was ever observed. Still a dead filter whose stated purpose is unmet. Smaller observations: - Events captured inside a handler (`/iso/:tag`) have `transaction: null`; the isolation scope's transaction name is only set from `onAfterHandle`/`onError`, which run after the handler body. Errors thrown from the handler are fine because `onError` sets the name before capturing. - In static lifecycle the `AfterResponse` phase span never appears in `spans[]` (the root span has already ended); in stream lifecycle it does appear. Not wrong, just an asymmetry worth knowing when comparing lifecycles. - The SDK's own hooks show up as user-visible spans named `sentryOnRequest`, `sentryOnAfterHandle`, `sentryOnError`. The source calls this a deliberate tradeoff; it is noise in every single trace. - Span envelopes flush on a ~5s timer even in stream lifecycle, so span assertions need the same sentinel discipline as logs. - Contradiction with the established Bun fact "no library spans without a `@sentry/bun/plugin` bundle": `mysql2` does produce db spans under plain `bun app.ts`, because modern `mysql2` publishes `node:diagnostics_channel` events itself (`node_modules/mysql2/lib/tracing.js`) and the SDK subscribes to them. The rule still holds for drivers that need the injected channels — `mysql`@2 gave nothing until the plugin build. - Cleanup done: all bun/node processes killed, `node_modules` removed (122M). Ports used: 41371-41375 (apps), 41999 (sink).

Express on Bun M-express-bun

Express 4.22.1 · Bun 1.4.0 · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

1) Deps: express@4 (4.22.1 verified) + mysql@2, and the develop SDK. Symlink node_modules/@sentry/{bun,node,core,server-utils,server-runtime-injection} to the worktree packages, or `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{bun,node,core,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry}-10.67.0.tgz express mysql`.

2) instrument.ts (loaded first):
   import * as Sentry from "@sentry/bun";
   Sentry.init({ dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 });

3) app.ts: `import "./instrument";` as the very first line, then `import express from "express"`. Create the mysql connection at MODULE SCOPE. Plain `app.listen(port)`; no Bun.serve needed. `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` after the routes is required only for the un-bundled run (see below); it is harmless (no duplicate event) in the bundled one.

4) build.ts — THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING STEP for every framework/library span and for automatic error capture:
   import { sentryBunPlugin } from "@sentry/bun/plugin";
   await Bun.build({ entrypoints: ["./app.ts"], outdir: "./dist", target: "bun", external: ["@sentry/*"], sourcemap: "external", plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] });

5) Run: `bun build.ts && bun dist/app.js`. The app can log `globalThis.__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__.bundler`, which printed `["express","mysql"]` — that is the signal the channels were injected.

Do NOT run `bun app.ts` / `bun --preload ./instrument.ts app.ts` for an Express app: it boots and serves fine, but you get url-sourced transaction names, no middleware/handler/db spans, and NO error capture at all unless you also call setupExpressErrorHandler.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksBundled with sentryBunPlugin, an error thrown in `app.get('/boom', ...)` arrives as a single event with mechanism `auto.http.express`, handled:false, transaction `GET /boom`, and context lines; the transaction is still sent with status internal_error, so Express does not swallow it. Adding `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` does not duplicate the event. WITHOUT the bundle the error is not captured at all (only a url-named transaction arrives) unless setupExpressErrorHandler is called, which then yields mechanism `auto.middleware.express`. Confirmed in both stream and static lifecycles.
route names✓ worksBundled: static lifecycle gives transaction name `GET /users/:id` with source `route`, op `http.server`; stream lifecycle gives span `http.server GET /users/:id` with `http.route: /users/:id`, plus children `handler /users/:id`, `middleware expressInit`, `middleware query2`. Un-bundled the same route is named `GET /users/42` with source `url` and no children.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent GET /iso/{alpha,beta,gamma} handlers, each doing Sentry.setTag('who', ...), then a randomized 60-120ms await, then captureException: each event carried exactly its own tag and a distinct trace id, and each matching transaction carried only its own tag. No cross-talk in either lifecycle.
incoming trace✓ worksA request with `sentry-trace: aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899-1122334455667788-1` plus a sentry baggage header produced a server span/transaction with trace_id aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899 and parent_span_id 1122334455667788; the express child spans hang off the local server span. Bundled run, both lifecycles.
outgoing fetch✓ works`fetch()` from inside the handler to the local recorder produced an `http.client` span inside the /fetchout server span, and the recorder saw `sentry-trace: 2817899b...-b6dd3e4e19fed040-1` plus a baggage header containing sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Ffetchout. The span name differs by lifecycle: stream names it low-cardinality `GET 127.0.0.1`, static describes it `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:47231/__record`.
db spans✓ worksmysql@2 connection created at module scope, queried inside GET /db: static lifecycle gives child span `db SELECT id, name FROM users LIMIT 2` under the `GET /db` transaction; stream gives `db SELECT users`. Instrumentation path: the Bun.build + sentryBunPlugin bundle (orchestrion channel injection, bundler reported `["express","mysql"]`). It was needed — the un-bundled run produced no db span.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info('hello from express on bun', { route: '/log' })` inside the handler arrived as a log envelope `info: hello from express on bun` after the ~7s flush timer, in both the bundled and the un-bundled runs.

Docs today

No page anywhere in ~/dev/sentry-docs (rev 046ce5942, 2026-09-01) mentions Express and bun together: `grep -rni express docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/` and `grep -rni bun docs/platforms/javascript/guides/express/` are both empty, and the Express guide (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/express/index.mdx:4) declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` with `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, so it only ever shows `@sentry/node` on Node. `sentryBunPlugin` / `@sentry/bun/plugin` / `Bun.build` appear nowhere in docs/ or platform-includes/ at all. Worse, the one place the bun guide touches bundling actively contradicts what I measured: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx:98 warns "Sentry's auto-instrumentation does not work with bundled code, including Bun's single-file executables ... you'll need to manually instrument your code" — whereas on develop a `Bun.build` bundle with `sentryBunPlugin()` is the only way to get Express route names, middleware/handler spans, db spans and automatic Express error capture on bun. A reader following the bun guide's `--preload` path (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx:94) plus the Express guide's `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler` (platform-includes/getting-started-use/javascript.express.mdx:15 and :34) would get errors but url-named transactions and zero library spans, and a reader who took line 98 at face value would never try the bundle at all.

Documented: no

A page must say that Express 4 (4.22.1 verified) runs unchanged on Bun 1.4.0 and that the full feature set is available there. It must show the Bun-specific substitutions the Express guide cannot: install `@sentry/bun` rather than `@sentry/node`, put `Sentry.init` in an `instrument.ts` loaded before the app with Bun's `--preload` flag rather than `node --import`, and state that in that shape errors, route names, request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans and logs were all observed working with no `Bun.build` step; the `mysql` db span required the `Bun.build` bundle with `sentryBunPlugin()`, the unbundled run produced none.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/express.mdx (new)

~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/express/index.mdx:4-5 (`sdk: sentry.javascript.node`, `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`); express/index.mdx:12 (`<PlatformContent includePath="getting-started-node" />`, Node-only); ~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/getting-started-node/javascript.mdx:88,95 (`node --import ./instrument.mjs app.mjs` as the only run shape); ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx:106 (`bun --preload ./instrument.js app.js`, no framework named). No page mentions Express and Bun together in either direction.

Verdicts come from the bundled run; every capability reproduced in both `stream` and `static`, and I noted the two places the lifecycles disagree (http.client span naming, span-vs-transaction envelope shape). The headline finding for this cell is the bundle boundary, not any single capability. Express on bun has two distinct behaviours on the same SDK build: - `bun app.ts` / `bun --preload ./instrument.ts app.ts`: transaction source `url` (`GET /users/42`), no middleware/handler spans, no db span, and NO error event for a throwing route unless `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` is added (which then reports mechanism `auto.middleware.express`). Logs and the node:http server span still work. The SDK emits no warning about the missing instrumentation unless `debug: true`. - `bun dist/app.js` built with `Bun.build({ external: ["@sentry/*"], plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })`: bundler reports `["express","mysql"]`, source `route`, full middleware/handler/db span tree, and automatic error capture with mechanism `auto.http.express` — setupExpressErrorHandler becomes unnecessary and does not double-report. So the answer to the setup hint's question: setupExpressErrorHandler is REQUIRED only on the un-bundled path and OPTIONAL (safe, non-duplicating) on the bundled path. A docs page should still show it, because it is the only thing that makes the un-bundled quick start capture errors at all. Other details worth carrying forward: - `external: ["@sentry/*"]` matters: it is what lets the process-wide client from the un-bundled instrument.ts and the injected channels in the bundle agree on one client. - The mysql connection is at module scope, per known finding K11; I did not re-derive the in-request case. - Express itself needs no adaptation to run on bun: express@4.22.1 with plain `app.listen()` serves correctly with no Sentry present. - The middleware span named `middleware query2` (not `query`) shows up in every trace. That is express 4's own `query` middleware, and the trailing `2` looks like a name-collision suffix from the instrumentation — cosmetic, but odd enough to mention. - Environmental snag, not a finding: port 41338 was already held by another agent's server and bun reported `error: Failed to start server. Is port 41338 in use?`. I switched to ephemeral ports (`PORT=0`) for the app and 47231 for the sink. - Cleanup done: every started process killed by captured pid, `rm -rf node_modules` in the task dir; the dir is now 3.6M (mostly dist/app.js plus logs).

Setup the docs would have to show

Plain `bun run` is enough for everything except database spans. No Bun plugin build is needed for Fastify itself.

Packages (npm, not `bun add` — bun cannot resolve the tarballs' transitive @sentry/*@10.67.0):
  npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bun-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz \

instrument.mjs:
  import * as Sentry from "@sentry/bun";
  Sentry.init({ dsn: "...", tracesSampleRate: 1.0 });   // add traceLifecycle: "static" for transaction envelopes

app.mjs — `import "./instrument.mjs";` as the very first line, then `import Fastify from "fastify"`. `bun --preload ./instrument.mjs app.mjs` works equally.

Run: `bun app.mjs`.

Only for db spans, add the bundle step (build.mjs):
  import { sentryBunPlugin } from "@sentry/bun/plugin";
  await Bun.build({ entrypoints: ["./app.mjs"], outdir: "./dist", target: "bun", external: ["@sentry/*"], sourcemap: "external", plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] });
then `bun dist/app.js`. The mysql connection must be created at module scope (finding K11).
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksAn error thrown from an async route handler is captured with mechanism `auto.function.fastify`, handled:false, and is attached to the `GET /error` transaction (trace + parent_span_id set). Fastify still swallows it into its own 500 JSON response body, so the client sees `{"statusCode":500,...,"message":"fastify boom"}` while Sentry gets the unhandled event; the server transaction status is `internal_error`. Works identically on plain `bun run` and on the plugin build, both lifecycles.
route names✓ worksParameterized route `/users/:id` yields `GET /users/:id` with `source: route` on the static-lifecycle transaction, and `http.server GET /users/:id` on the stream-lifecycle span envelope. No plugin build needed; Fastify's own diagnostics channels drive this. Child spans in every request: `handler GET /users/:id` and `handler fastify - route-handler`.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent `/iso?n=1..3` requests, each with a staggered 50/100/150ms await between setTag and captureException, produced three events each carrying only its own `reqtag` and a distinct trace id (1dbd9698…, 9cb161c7…, 8cec8614…). In static lifecycle the tag also lands on the matching transaction only. No cross-request bleed.
incoming trace✓ worksA request with `sentry-trace: aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899-1122334455667788-1` plus a sentry baggage header continued the trace: transaction trace_id `aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899`, parent_span_id `1122334455667788`, name still `GET /users/:id` source route. Same in stream lifecycle (`[aabbccdd/p:11223344] http.server GET /users/:id`).
outgoing fetch✓ works`fetch()` from inside a handler to a local recorder produced `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41338/hit` as a child of the server transaction, and the recorder saw both `sentry-trace` (same trace id as the transaction, sampled=1) and a full `baggage` header including `sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fdownstream`. Note the stream-lifecycle span name is the low-cardinality `http.client GET 127.0.0.1`; the static-lifecycle description keeps the full URL.
db spans✓* works-waModule-scope `mysql@2` connection: NO db span on plain `bun run` (the `GET /db` transaction has only the two fastify handler spans) — the query runs fine, it is just uninstrumented and the SDK is silent about it. With the Bun plugin build (`sentryBunPlugin()` from `@sentry/bun/plugin`, `external: ["@sentry/*"]`) the same handler emits `db SELECT id, name FROM users`. So the plugin build IS needed, but only for the database, not for Fastify. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. The Bun plugin build is NOT required for db spans on Fastify + Bun. The reported "partial" is driver-specific, not a Bun/Fastify limitation: `mysql@2` needs the bundle, `mysql2 >= 3.20.0` does not. EXACT CHANGE: use `mysql2` (tested 3.24.3) instead of `mysql@2.18.1`. Nothing else changes — same `instrument.mjs`, same `import "./instrument.mjs"` first line, plain `bun app.mjs`, no `Bun.build`, no `sentryBunPlugin()`. Why: `mysql2 >= 3.20.0` publishes native `node:diagnostics_channel` channels (`mysql2:query`, `:execute`, `:connect`, `:pool:connect`). `mysql2Integration` in `@sentry/server-utils` subscribes to them EAGERLY in `setupOnce()` (packages/server-utils/src/integrations/mysql2/index.ts:149-166), so no require-hook and no build-time channel injection is involved. `mysql@2` has no native channels, so it only works through the orchestrion transform that `@sentry/bun/plugin` applies at bundle time — which is exactly what the repo's own e2e app does (dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/bun-mysql/{build.ts,src/app.ts}, `mysql: 2.18.1`, `bun run dist/app.js`). EVIDENCE — one Fastify process, both drivers at module scope, plain `bun appH.mjs`, traceLifecycle static (runH-drive.log): GET /db-mysql1 | ["handler GET /db-mysql1","handler fastify - route-handler"] <- mysql@2: NO db span GET /db-mysql2-query | ["handler GET /db-mysql2-query","handler fastify - route-handler","db SELECT id, name FROM users"] GET /db-mysql2-execute| ["handler GET /db-mysql2-execute","handler fastify - route-handler","db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = ?"] GET /db-mysql2-pool | ["handler GET /db-mysql2-pool","handler fastify - route-handler","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT name FROM users WHERE id = ?"] Same app, traceLifecycle stream (default), runJ-items.json — identical result, low-cardinality names: span | ["handler /db-mysql1","handler /db-mysql1","http.server GET /db-mysql1"] span | ["db SELECT users","handler /db-mysql2-query","handler /db-mysql2-query","http.server GET /db-mysql2-query"] span | ["db SELECT users","handler /db-mysql2-execute","handler /db-mysql2-execute","http.server GET /db-mysql2-execute"] span | ["db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users","handler /db-mysql2-pool","handler /db-mysql2-pool","http.server GET /db-mysql2-pool"] The span is full quality, not degraded (runL-items.json, raw attributes): {"name":"SELECT users","attributes":{"sentry.origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel","sentry.op":"db","db.system.name":"mysql","db.query.text":"SELECT id, name FROM users","db.query.summary":"SELECT users","db.operation.name":"SELECT","db.namespace":"app","server.address":"127.0.0.1","server.port":3307,"sentry.segment.name":"GET /db-mysql2-query","sentry.sdk.name":"sentry.javascript.bun"}} K11 does NOT apply to mysql2 on this path. A route that `await import("mysql2/promise")`s and creates the connection INSIDE the request still gets spans, because the channel subscription happens at `Sentry.init()` time, not at module-load time (runM-drive.log, plain `bun app2.mjs`): GET /db-lazy | ["handler GET /db-lazy","handler fastify - route-handler","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = ?"] WHAT DOES NOT RESCUE mysql@2: registering the plugin as a runtime Bun plugin instead of a build plugin. `bun --preload ./preload-plugin.mjs app3.mjs`, where preload-plugin.mjs is `Bun.plugin(sentryBunPlugin()); await import("./instrument.mjs")`, crashes at import (runK-app.log): SyntaxError: Missing 'default' export in module '.../node_modules/mysql/index.js' at <parse> (1:1) So for `mysql@2` the `Bun.build` + `sentryBunPlugin()` step from the toolbox/e2e recipe is genuinely the only route, and the bundle-vs-runtime distinction is real. COMMANDS (probe files in $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-fastify-bun-dbspans/): npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{bun,node,core,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry}-10.67.0.tgz fastify@5 mysql@2 mysql2@3 PORT=52117 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs & # or ./sinkraw.mjs for full span attributes SINK_PORT=52117 APP_PORT=52118 LIFECYCLE=static bun appH.mjs & # plain bun run, no build step SINK_PORT=52117 APP_PORT=52118 node driveH.mjs # separate plain-node driver, sentinel-gated Files: appH.mjs (fastify, mysql@2 AND mysql2 at module scope, four db routes + /sentinel), app2.mjs (mysql2 only, incl. /db-lazy), app3.mjs (mysql@2, no instrument import, for the --preload variant), instrument.mjs, driveH.mjs, drive2.mjs, sinkraw.mjs, preload-plugin.mjs; logs runH-*, runJ-*, runK-app.log, runL-items.json, runM-*. Ports note: my first attempt used sink port 47311 and another concurrently running agent's app was tunneling into it, polluting the items list (runI-drive.log shows foreign `GET /users/7` transactions). Reran on 52117/52121, which were clean. Bun 1.4.0, @sentry/bun 10.67.0, fastify 5.12.3, mysql 2.18.1, mysql2 3.24.3, MariaDB on 127.0.0.1:3307.
Workaround: Use `mysql2` (>= 3.20.0) rather than `mysql@2`. Create the connection or pool at module scope (or lazily — either works), keep `import "./instrument.mjs"` as the first line of the entry, and run `bun app.mjs` with no build step; db spans appear under the Fastify handler spans in both `stream` and `static` trace lifecycles. If you are stuck on `mysql@2`, the bundle really is required: `Bun.build({ entrypoints: ["./app.mjs"], outdir: "./dist", target: "bun", external: ["@sentry/bun", "mysql"], plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` then `bun dist/app.js` — the plugin strips instrumented packages back out of `external` so `mysql` gets bundled and transformed. Registering `sentryBunPlugin()` as a runtime `Bun.plugin` via `--preload` is not an alternative; it breaks `mysql`'s CJS default export.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info("hello from fastify on bun", { route: "/log" })` inside a handler arrived as a log envelope item `info: hello from fastify on bun`, carrying the trace id of the enclosing `GET /log` request (b9433ec3… matches that request's server span). Flushed on the timer; readable after ~7s. Works on both plain run and plugin build.

Headline: the setup hint is right — Fastify needs no Bun plugin build. Fastify publishes its own diagnostics channels, and the develop SDK subscribes to them directly, so plain `bun app.mjs` already gives route-named server transactions with source `route`, unhandled-error capture with `auto.function.fastify`, per-request isolation, trace continuation, http.client spans with propagation headers, and logs. This contradicts the toolbox's own Bun bullet ("It records NO library spans (databases, AI, Express, Koa, Hapi, Fastify)"): for Fastify on Bun 1.4.0 that is no longer true, and it is the single most docs-relevant finding here. Express on Bun presumably still needs the bundle; Fastify does not. The bundle is needed for exactly one of the seven capabilities: db spans. mysql@2 at module scope is invisible on plain `bun run` and produces `db SELECT id, name FROM users` under `sentryBunPlugin()`. The SDK emits no warning about the missing instrumentation without `debug: true`, so a user gets a Fastify app that looks fully instrumented and silently has no database visibility — the most likely real-world trap for this combination. Span shape: every request carries two child spans, `handler GET /<route>` and `handler fastify - route-handler`. Not a duplicate; they are the request-handler and route-handler hook spans. Both have op `handler` and neither carries a `sentry.source` attribute in the stream envelope, so in stream lifecycle only the parent `http.server` span is route-named. Stream vs static: identical verdicts for all seven capabilities. Errors, isolation, incoming trace, outgoing fetch and logs were all confirmed under stream (run A) and re-confirmed under static (runs B and C); route-name `source: route` is only directly assertable under static (`transaction_info.source`), which is why the route-names verdict is quoted from runs B/C. db spans confirmed under static in run C, absence confirmed under both A and B. One naming difference worth flagging to whoever writes the guide: the outgoing client span is `http.client GET 127.0.0.1` in stream lifecycle (the new low-cardinality naming) but `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41338/hit` in static. Same span, different name depending on lifecycle. Cleanup: sink (pid 58989) and recorder (pid 58990) killed, all app processes killed, ports 41337-41341 verified free via lsof, `node_modules` removed (4.8M left, mostly `dist/`). MariaDB container untouched.
