Koa on Bun M-koa-bun

Koa 2.16.4 + @koa/router 12.0.2 · bun 1.4.0 (macOS arm64) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Koa runs on bun unchanged. Full Sentry wiring, which is what a docs page would have to show:

1. Install: `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bun-10.67.0.tgz ... koa @koa/router mysql` (here: node_modules/@sentry/{bun,core,node,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry} symlinked to $W/packages/*, koa/@koa/router/mysql symlinked from the worktree).

2. `instrument.ts`:
```ts
import * as Sentry from '@sentry/bun';
Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tunnel: 'http://127.0.0.1:52734/', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' /* or default 'stream' */ });
```

3. `app.ts` starts with `import './instrument';` as the very first line, then Koa + @koa/router, and a MODULE-SCOPE `mysql.createConnection({host:'127.0.0.1',port:3307,user:'root',database:'app'})`.

4. A Bun plugin build is mandatory (this is the whole story for Koa on Bun), `build.ts`:
```ts
import { sentryBunPlugin } from '@sentry/bun/plugin';
await Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./app.ts'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', external: ['@sentry/*'], sourcemap: 'external', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] });
```

5. Run: `bun run build.ts && bun dist/app.js`.

`Sentry.setupKoaErrorHandler(app)` (which the Koa/Node guide tells you to call) is NOT needed here, the bundled koaIntegration captures handler errors on its own with mechanism `auto.middleware.koa`.

Without the plugin build (`bun --preload ./instrument.ts app.ts` or `bun app.ts`), Koa is completely uninstrumented: no router span, no db span, url-sourced transaction names, and handler errors are never captured at all.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksWith the plugin build, `throw new Error('koa boom')` inside a router handler arrives as an event with mechanism `auto.middleware.koa`, handled:false, contextlines present, and the enclosing transaction gets status `internal_error`. Koa does not swallow it from Sentry's view, it also prints its own stderr trace and returns HTTP 500. No `Sentry.setupKoaErrorHandler(app)` call was made. Without the plugin build the same request produces only a transaction with status internal_error and NO event: the error is lost.
route names✓ worksWith the plugin build the segment is `GET /users/:id` with source `route` (static: `transaction_info.source=route`; stream: `sentry.segment.name.source=route`, `http.route=/users/:id`), plus a child `router /users/:id` span (op `router`, origin `auto.http.koa`). Without the plugin build it degrades to `GET /users/42` with source `url` and no child span.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent `/iso?tag=alpha|bravo|charlie` requests (each with a randomized 50-150ms await between setTag and captureException) produced three events carrying exactly their own tag and their own trace id, matching their own transaction's trace id. No cross-talk. Ran under traceLifecycle 'static'.
incoming trace✓ worksA request to /users/99 with `sentry-trace: aaaa...-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` and a matching baggage header continued the trace: transaction trace_id `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`, parent_span_id `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`. traceLifecycle 'static'.
outgoing fetch✓ works`fetch('http://127.0.0.1:52740/downstream')` from inside a Koa handler produced an `http.client` span in the same trace (static: `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:52740/downstream`; stream: `http.client | GET 127.0.0.1`, the new low-cardinality name) and the recorder saw both `sentry-trace` and a full `baggage` header with `sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Ffetch` and `sentry-sampled=true`.
db spans✓ worksA module-scope `mysql` (mysql@2 driver) connection queried inside the handler produced `db SELECT id, name FROM users` (static) / `db | SELECT users` (stream, low-cardinality name) as a child of the Koa router span. Instrumentation path: the Bun plugin build (`sentryBunPlugin()` in `Bun.build`), and it was required: the identical unbundled run produced zero db spans.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info('hello from koa on bun', { route: '/log' })` inside a handler arrived as a `log` envelope carrying the request's trace id, in both lifecycles and in both the bundled and unbundled runs (logs do not need the plugin build).

~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/koa/index.mdx:4-5 (`sdk: sentry.javascript.node`, `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`); koa/index.mdx:12 (`<PlatformContent includePath="getting-started-node" />`); ~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/getting-started-node/javascript.mdx:95 (`node --import ./instrument.mjs app.mjs`); ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx:106. `grep -rin bun` over guides/koa/ and `grep -rin koa` over guides/bun/ both return nothing.

Two findings worth carrying forward. 1. The unbundled Koa-on-Bun failure is worse than the established "no library spans" note (toolbox: Bun records NO library spans for Express/Koa/Hapi/Fastify). Route names silently degrade to url source AND the thrown handler error never reaches Sentry at all. Koa's default `ctx.onerror` writes to stderr and answers 500, and with no koaIntegration patch in place there is nothing between Koa and the http server subscription that turns the 500 into an event. The practical consequence: a user following the Bun guide verbatim gets transactions and logs and believes the setup works, while every route error is dropped. The SDK emits no warning unless `debug: true`. 2. Contradiction with the docs Alert at bun/index.mdx:96-100. The claim that auto-instrumentation does not work with bundled code is exactly inverted for the Bun plugin path: `sentryBunPlugin()` inside `Bun.build` is what makes auto-instrumentation work. The Alert is presumably about generic bundlers, but as written it steers Bun users away from the only working setup. Other observations: - `mechanism: auto.middleware.koa`, `sentry.origin: auto.http.koa`, span op `router` with `koa.name` / `koa.type` / `http.route` attributes. - Module-scope mysql connection was used, per K11. Not re-derived: I did not test a request-scope connection. - Low-cardinality naming from the recent commits is visible in stream mode: `http.client | GET 127.0.0.1` and `db | SELECT users`, while static mode still shows the descriptive `GET http://127.0.0.1:52740/downstream` / `SELECT id, name FROM users`. - Ports used: 52732 (bare check), 52734 (sink), 52740 (recorder), 52742/52744 (app). All processes killed and all five ports verified free before returning. node_modules under the probe dir are symlinks only (dir total 2.3M, mostly dist/app.js + sourcemap), so nothing was deleted.

Hapi on Bun M-hapi-bun

@hapi/hapi 21.3.10 · Bun 1.4.0 (@sentry/bun 10.67.0, develop @ 6f2da7483d) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Hapi runs on Bun unchanged, and the full Sentry feature set requires the Bun plugin build, not `bun --preload`.

Packages: `@sentry/bun` (+ its `@sentry/{core,node,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry}` deps), `@hapi/hapi`, `mysql`.

instrument.ts:
```ts
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/bun";
Sentry.init({ dsn: "...", tracesSampleRate: 1.0 /*, traceLifecycle: "static" */ });
```

app.ts, first line `import "./instrument";`, then `import Hapi from "@hapi/hapi"`. Create the mysql connection at module scope (K11). Do NOT call `setupHapiErrorHandler` — on develop the error handler is auto-registered from the orchestrion `@hapi/hapi` `start`/`initialize` channels (`packages/node/src/integrations/tracing/hapi.ts:5` marks the export `@deprecated`). Just `await server.start()`.

build.ts:
```ts
import { sentryBunPlugin } from "@sentry/bun/plugin";
await Bun.build({ entrypoints: ["./app.ts"], outdir: "./dist", target: "bun",
  external: ["@sentry/*"], sourcemap: "external", plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] });
```

Run: `bun run build.ts && bun dist/app.js`. All seven capabilities pass from this shape.

Counterfactual (matters for the docs): plain `bun app.ts` / `bun --preload ./instrument.ts app.ts` gives NO hapi instrumentation at all — transactions are `GET /users/42` with `source: "url"`, no `router` span, no `db` span, and the handler error is **not captured at all** (silently swallowed by hapi's 500). In that unbundled mode `await Sentry.setupHapiErrorHandler(server)` before `server.start()` does restore error capture (mechanism `auto.function.hapi`) but still yields no route names and no spans. Calling it in the bundled app is harmless: exactly one event, confirming the JSDoc idempotency claim.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksAn error thrown in a Hapi route handler is captured automatically in the plugin build with mechanism `auto.function.hapi`, handled:false, transaction `GET /error`, request url and a context line; hapi still answers 500 to the client. No `setupHapiErrorHandler` call is needed. Stream and static lifecycle both. Without the plugin build the error is swallowed entirely (no event) unless `setupHapiErrorHandler` is called explicitly.
route names✓ worksParameterized route `/users/{id}` yields server span/transaction `GET /users/{id}` with `source: "route"` (static lifecycle) plus a nested `router /users/{id}` child; stream lifecycle emits the same pair as `http.server GET /users/{id}` + `router /users/{id}`. Unbundled it degrades to `GET /users/42` with `source: "url"` and no router span.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent requests to `/iso/{tag}` each setting a distinct tag and capturing an error produced three events with exactly one tag each (`who: alpha|bravo|charlie`), three distinct trace ids, and each event's trace id matches its own transaction's trace id. No tag bleed. Verified in both lifecycles.
incoming trace✓ worksA request with `sentry-trace: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` and a sentry baggage header produced a server transaction on trace `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` with `parent_span_id: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`. Works bundled and unbundled.
outgoing fetch✓ works`fetch` from inside a handler produced `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41400/rec/from-hapi` (static) / low-cardinality `http.client GET 127.0.0.1` (stream) as a child of the `router /downstream` span, and the recorder saw `sentry-trace` on the request's own trace with the client span id as parent, plus a full baggage header including `sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fdownstream`.
db spans✓ worksA module-scope `mysql` connection queried inside the handler produced `db SELECT id, name FROM users` (static) / `db SELECT users` (stream) nested under `router /db`. Instrumentation path: the Bun plugin build (`sentryBunPlugin()` in `Bun.build`) — it was required; the unbundled run produced no db span at all.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info("hapi-log-line", { route: "/log" })` inside a handler arrived as a `log` envelope item `info: hapi-log-line` after the timer flush. Works bundled and unbundled (logs do not depend on the plugin).

Docs today

No page mentions Hapi on Bun. The two guides are disjoint and each is wrong for this combination. - ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hapi/index.mdx:3-11 sets `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` / `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, so the Hapi guide only ever shows `@sentry/node`; grepping the whole guide directory for "bun" returns nothing. - ~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/getting-started-use/javascript.hapi.mdx:17 and :42 both still instruct `await Sentry.setupHapiErrorHandler(server);` before `server.start()`. On develop that export is `@deprecated` (packages/node/src/integrations/tracing/hapi.ts:5-12) because the handler auto-registers from the orchestrion `@hapi/hapi` start/initialize channels; my bundled run confirms it is unnecessary and idempotent. - ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx:96-98 carries an Alert titled "Bundled Code Limitation" claiming "Sentry's auto-instrumentation does not work with bundled code" and telling users to manually instrument instead. For Hapi (and mysql) on Bun this is backwards: `bun --preload ./instrument.js app.js` (the command the guide shows at :106) produces url-sourced transaction names, no router or db spans, and silently loses handler errors; only the `sentryBunPlugin()` `Bun.build` bundle gives route names, db spans and automatic error capture. The Bun guide never mentions `@sentry/bun/plugin` or `Bun.build` at all, and its guide directory never mentions hapi.

Documented: no

A page must say `@hapi/hapi` 21.3.10 runs unchanged on Bun 1.4.0 with `@sentry/bun`, and must state the run shape the observation actually required: build the app with `Bun.build({ target: 'bun', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin` and run the bundle — `bun --preload ./instrument.ts` alone was not sufficient for the full feature set. In the bundled shape errors, route names, request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans, `mysql` db spans and logs all work. This is a second cell contradicting the Bun guide's alert at bun/index.mdx:96-98, and neither `sentryBunPlugin` nor `Bun.build` is named anywhere in the docs.

Ports used: sink/recorder 41400, app 41401, bare-hapi viability check 41338. All processes killed; `lsof` on both ports returns nothing. node_modules here is only symlinks into the worktree, so it costs no disk and was left in place for rerunability; total dir size 6.3M (mostly dist bundles). Notable observations beyond the seven capabilities: 1. `setupHapiErrorHandler` on develop: deprecated and genuinely unnecessary in the supported (plugin-build) setup, but it is the *only* thing that makes handler errors reach Sentry when a user follows the current Bun guide (`--preload`, no bundle). That is a real trap: a Bun+Hapi user following the Bun guide loses every route-handler error with no warning at all (the SDK only warns with `debug: true`). Worth either keeping the docs mention with a "unbundled only" caveat or fixing the Bun guide to recommend the plugin build. 2. The `router` child span carries the raw route path in stream lifecycle (`router /users/{id}`) and the method-prefixed form in static (`router GET /users/{id}`). Not a defect, just an inconsistency between lifecycles. 3. `http.client` span naming differs by lifecycle in this build: stream emits the new low-cardinality `http.client GET 127.0.0.1`, static emits `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41400/rec/from-hapi`. Consistent with the two recent low-cardinality span-name commits on develop. 4. K11 was respected up front (module-scope mysql connection), so this run does not re-derive it. I did not test a per-request mysql require on Hapi. 5. Sampling gotcha avoided: the driver is a plain `node` process (`drive.mjs`), not a Sentry-initialized one. 6. Hapi's own 500 body is unchanged by the SDK in every variant (`{"statusCode":500,"error":"Internal Server Error","message":"An internal server error occurred"}`), i.e. Sentry observes the error without altering the response.

Oak 17.2.0 (jsr:@oak/oak, installed on Bun via the JSR npm registry as @jsr/oak__oak) · Bun 1.4.0 (darwin-aarch64), @sentry/bun develop (10.67.0, tarballs from worktree audit-runtime-docs) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Oak runs on Bun. As on Deno, the mount shape decides whether the SDK works at all: `Bun.serve({ fetch: req => app.fetch(req) })` works end to end; `app.listen()` is effectively unsupported.

Install (Oak is JSR-only, so a docs page must show the JSR npm registry step — `bun add @oak/oak` alone fails):
  .npmrc:
    @jsr:registry=https://npm.jsr.io
  npm install "@oak/oak@npm:@jsr/oak__oak@17.2.0"
  npm install @sentry/bun mysql2
(In this probe the SDK came from the develop tarballs: `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{bun,node,core,opentelemetry,server-utils,server-runtime-injection}-10.67.0.tgz mysql2`. `bun add` cannot resolve the tarballs' transitive @sentry/*@10.67.0 deps; npm install + `bun app.ts` is fine.)

instrument.ts:
  import * as Sentry from "@sentry/bun";
  Sentry.init({ dsn: "___PUBLIC_DSN___", tracesSampleRate: 1.0 });

app.ts:
  import "./instrument";                 // must be the first line (or `bun --preload ./instrument.ts app.ts`)
  import * as Sentry from "@sentry/bun";
  import { Application, Router } from "@oak/oak";
  import mysql from "mysql2";

  const db = mysql.createConnection({ host: "127.0.0.1", port: 3307, user: "root", database: "app" }); // MODULE SCOPE

  const router = new Router();

  // route naming: register this as ROUTER middleware, not application middleware.
  // ctx.matched is already populated here and it runs BEFORE the handler, so it also
  // names the span on the error path.
  router.use((ctx, next) => {
    const span = Sentry.getActiveSpan();
    const route = ctx.matched?.at(-1)?.path;
    if (span && route) {
      Sentry.updateSpanName(span, `${ctx.request.method} ${route}`);
      span.setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, "route");
    }
    return next();
  });

  router.get("/users/:id", ctx => { ctx.response.body = { id: ctx.params.id }; });

  const app = new Application();
  app.use(router.routes());
  app.use(router.allowedMethods());

  // Correct mount. app.listen() must NOT be used.
  Bun.serve({ port: 3000, hostname: "127.0.0.1", fetch: (req: Request) => app.fetch(req) });

Run: `bun app.ts` (no bundle, no Bun plugin needed for any capability probed here, including the mysql2 db span).

No error middleware is needed on this path: Oak's `fetch` logs "[uncaught application error]" and then re-throws, so the error escapes into the Bun.serve wrapper and the SDK captures it automatically.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksBun.serve(app.fetch), no middleware: the handler throw is captured automatically with mechanism `auto.http.bun.serve`, handled:false, hasContextLine true, sdk sentry.javascript.bun, and the request span goes status=error; Oak does not swallow it (it logs "[uncaught application error]" and re-throws out of app.fetch). With an optional try/catch middleware the event instead carries mechanism `oak` handled:false and dedupeIntegration keeps only one. Stream and static lifecycle both. Under app.listen() the error NEVER reaches Sentry unless a manual middleware captures it, and the manual capture then lands on a stale process-level trace id.
route names◐ partialOut of the box the span is `http.server GET` with sentry.segment.name.source = url (stream) / transaction `GET` (static): Bun.serve names the span before Oak has matched anything, and Oak's fetch mount gives Bun.serve no `routes:{}` map. A 6-line ROUTER-level middleware reading ctx.matched.at(-1).path plus updateSpanName + SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE='route' produces `http.server GET /users/:id` src=route (stream) and `GET /users/:id` source=route (static). Because it is router middleware and runs before the handler, it also names the error path: static gave `GET /error` source=route status=internal_error, unlike the Deno cell where the after-next() middleware missed it. Under app.listen() the middleware is a silent no-op (getActiveSpan() is undefined for all 9 requests). verified: partial Could NOT refute the "partial" report. Out of the box, with `Bun.serve({ fetch: req => app.fetch(req) })`, the server span carries no route. Reproduced in both lifecycles and in a bundle; the only thing that changes it is user code at the mount, not SDK config. Root cause read from the SDK source, not guessed: `~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/packages/bun/src/integrations/bunserver.ts:194-224` — `wrapRequestHandler(..., route?)` sets `SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE='route'` + `url.template` only when a `route` string is passed, and the only caller that passes one is `instrumentBunServeRoutes` iterating `serveOptions.routes` (line 127-176). No `routes` map means `routeName = parsedUrl.pathname` and source `url`. Nothing in the SDK reads an Oak/Koa-style router. Variants I ran (all against my own sink on 127.0.0.1:53197, app ports 54101-54119): 1) Baseline, `fetch: req => app.fetch(req)`, stream: SPAN name=GET op=http.server status=ok src=url tmpl=- SPAN name=GET op=http.server status=error src=url tmpl=- SPAN name=SELECT users op=db status=ok src=- tmpl=- 2) Baseline, static: TX name=GET /users/7 source=url status=ok tmpl=- TX name=GET /error source=url status=internal_error tmpl=- (Note a correction to the original report: static does NOT give a bare `GET`; it gives the raw pathname with source=url, i.e. a high-cardinality name.) 3) Bundled with `@sentry/bun/plugin` (`Bun.build({ target:'bun', external:['@sentry/*'], plugins:[sentryBunPlugin()] })`, then `bun dist/app.js`) — identical to baseline: === BUNDLED MODE=fetch SPAN name=GET op=http.server src=url (x5; db span present, so the plugin did work, it just does not know Oak) 4) Init placement (import "./instrument" first line vs `--preload`) and `traceLifecycle` make no difference to the source attribute. 5) `app.listen({ port })` mount: server spans DO arrive (contradicting "effectively unsupported"), but method-only and with no request context: {"type":"span","items":["http.server GET"],"raw":[{"name":"GET","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.bun.serve"}]} (x5, /error one has status error) The naming middleware logs `[naming] /users/7 span=false route=/users/:id` for every request — `getActiveSpan()` is undefined inside Oak middleware under listen — and the thrown error produced no event and `/db` produced no db span. So under listen the spans exist but are unnameable and context-free. BETTER WORKAROUND THAN THE ONE REPORTED (this is the one thing I would change in the finding). Instead of a per-request Sentry middleware, derive Bun's `routes` map from the Oak router at mount time. It contains zero Sentry API, runs once, and makes the SDK's own route naming fire: const handler = (req: Request) => app.fetch(req); const routes: Record<string, typeof handler> = {}; for (const r of router) routes[r.path] = handler; Bun.serve({ port, hostname: "127.0.0.1", routes, fetch: handler }); === MODE=derived LIFECYCLE=stream SPAN name=GET /users/:id op=http.server status=ok src=route tmpl=/users/:id SPAN name=GET /db op=http.server status=ok src=route tmpl=/db SPAN name=GET /error op=http.server status=error src=route tmpl=/error === MODE=derived LIFECYCLE=static TX name=GET /users/:id source=route status=ok tmpl=/users/:id TX name=GET /error source=route status=internal_error tmpl=/error {"exception":"Error: oak bun boom","mechanism":"auto.http.bun.serve","handled":false} Same result bundled. It also sets `url.template`, which the reported middleware does not. Limits of that workaround, measured with Oak's exotic path shapes (tricky.ts): `Bun.serve` accepts them without throwing, and anything it does not match falls through to the `fetch` handler, so behavior is never changed, only the name. `/api/opt` (matching `/api/opt/:a?`) and `/api/star/a/b` (matching `/api/star/(.*)`) fell through and got `SPAN name=GET ... src=url`. And Bun ignores an inline regex constraint, so `/api/num/abc` — which Oak 404s — was still labeled `SPAN name=GET /api/num/:id(\d+) status=error src=route`. Plain and `:param` routes are exact. Repo reference: the only Bun e2e app, `~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/bun-mysql/src/app.ts`, mounts a bare `fetch(req)` with manual `url.pathname` branching, so the repo itself has no example of route-named Bun spans and no Oak app at all. Files (rerunnable): $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-oak-bun-routenames/ — app.ts (MODE=fetch|routes|derived|wildcard|listen, NAMING=on for the middleware variant), instrument.ts, tricky.ts, build.ts, sink.mjs, drive.sh, run2.sh/run3.sh, logs r2-*.log, r3-*.log. Commands: `PORT=53197 node sink.mjs &` then `./run3.sh derived stream 54105`. Sink and all app processes were killed.
Workaround: Give Bun.serve a `routes` map derived from the Oak router at startup, and keep `fetch` as the fallback: `const handler = (req: Request) => app.fetch(req); const routes: Record<string, typeof handler> = {}; for (const r of router) routes[r.path] = handler; Bun.serve({ port, routes, fetch: handler });`. This yields `GET /users/:id` with `sentry.segment.name.source=route` and `url.template` in both stream and static lifecycles, on the error path too, bundled or not, with no Sentry-specific code. Routes using regex constraints, optional params or `(.*)` are named imprecisely or fall back to the method-only name; list those explicitly in the map if their names matter. The alternative is the reported router-level middleware (`Sentry.updateSpanName` + `SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE`), which also works but runs per request and does not set `url.template`. Neither works under `app.listen()`.
isolation✓ worksBun.serve(app.fetch), stream lifecycle: three concurrent GET /iso/:tag requests (each setTag('who', tag), 60-120ms await, setTag('who2', tag), captureException) produced three events with exactly their own tags {who: X, who2: X} and three distinct trace ids, each equal to its own http.server span trace id. Under app.listen() this is broken exactly as on Deno: all three events carried who=charlie and one shared stale trace id a2cdf2f5080346759b636800a82cb887.
incoming trace✓ worksA request carrying sentry-trace + baggage continues the trace before Oak is involved (the Bun.serve wrapper runs continueTrace). Stream: `http.server GET /users/:id` with trace_id aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa and parent_span_id 1111111111111111. Static: transaction `GET /ok` trace cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc parent 3333333333333333. This is the one capability that also works under app.listen() (trace bbbb... parent 2222222222222222), because it is read in the Bun.serve callback, not in the handler.
outgoing fetch✓ worksfetch() from inside an Oak handler to a local recorder produced `http.client GET 127.0.0.1` (origin auto.http.fetch) as a child of the request segment on the same trace id, and the recorder saw both headers: sentry-trace 0b22b3d098774f229c80398d8f002378-899c8c8d7d6377f8-1 and a full baggage with sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fdownstream. Static lifecycle nests it as `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41402/rec/from-oak` inside the `GET /downstream` transaction. No Deno-style K2 gap on Bun. Under app.listen() the client span still fires and still carries headers, but as its own root segment on the process-level trace, disconnected from the request.
db spans✓ worksModule-scope mysql2 connection queried in the handler: stream gives `db SELECT users` with parent_span_id = the request segment and the same trace id, origin auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel, db.query.text 'SELECT id, name FROM users', db.system mysql; static nests `db SELECT id, name FROM users` inside the `GET /db` transaction. Instrumentation path: NONE was needed - plain `bun app.ts`, no Bun.build/sentryBunPlugin bundle, because mysql2 publishes its own diagnostics_channel events that the SDK subscribes to. (A driver without native diagnostics_channel support would still need the sentryBunPlugin bundle per the Bun baseline.) Under app.listen() the db span disappears entirely - it is not emitted at all, not even as a detached root.
logs✓ worksSentry.logger.info('hello from oak', { route: '/log' }) inside a handler arrived as a log envelope correlated to the request: `info: hello from oak :: trace=865f3beb418f416dacf9e2abd9300128`, the same trace id as the `http.server GET /log` span. Stream lifecycle, Bun.serve mount. Under app.listen() the log arrives but is stamped with the stale process trace (a2cdf2f5...) instead of the request's.
client errors· not-runOak is a server-only framework with no browser surface; this probe ran server-side on Bun only.

Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions Oak on any runtime: `grep -rin '\boak\b' docs/platforms/javascript platform-includes` and `grep -rn '@oak/oak|jsr:@oak|oakserver' docs platform-includes` both return nothing. The Bun guide is a single 214-line page, ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx, plus configuration/integrations/contextlines.mdx. It names no framework at all and never mentions Bun.serve (`grep -n 'Bun.serve|routes:'` on that file is empty), so nothing tells a user that the mount shape decides whether the SDK works, or that server spans are method-only until they name them. Install step is `bun add @sentry/bun` (index.mdx:38) and init is `instrument.js` (index.mdx:54-59), with `bun --preload ./instrument.js app.js` at index.mdx:94-106. index.mdx:98 carries an Alert stating "Sentry's auto-instrumentation does not work with bundled code, including Bun's single-file executables" - which is the opposite of the sentryBunPlugin bundle path that the Bun baseline needs for library spans; `grep -rn 'sentryBunPlugin|bun/plugin' docs platform-includes` returns nothing, so that plugin is undocumented. Nothing in the docs mentions mysql2 or database spans on Bun either.

Documented: no

A page must say: Oak 17 runs on Bun, but only mounted as Bun.serve({ fetch: req => app.fetch(req) }); app.listen() is effectively unsupported with @sentry/bun. Install needs the JSR npm registry because Oak is JSR-only: an .npmrc with @jsr:registry=https://npm.jsr.io plus npm install "@oak/oak@npm:@jsr/oak__oak@17.2.0". On Bun the server span name comes from the routes map passed to Bun.serve, so a fetch-only mount produces spans named GET with source url, in both lifecycles, bundled or not. Document the verified workaround: build a routes map from the Oak router at startup and keep fetch as the fallback. Errors, per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing fetch spans, mysql2 database spans and logs all work. Client-side errors were not exercised and must not be claimed.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/oak.mdx (or guides/oak/index.mdx with fallbackGuide: javascript.bun, the Elysia pattern). Also: common/configuration/integrations/bunserver.mdx must gain a section stating that server span names come from the Bun.serve routes map.

guides/bun/index.mdx:1-214 (the whole Bun guide; names no framework, never mentions Bun.serve or a routes map); common/configuration/integrations/bunserver.mdx:18 (only description of Bun.serve instrumentation, says nothing about span naming); guides/bun/ has no framework subtree; grep for oak and for the JSR npm registry over docs and platform-includes returns zero hits.

Headline: Oak on Bun is the best Oak result so far, and the whole story fits on one docs page, but only if the page says three things. 1. Mount shape. `Bun.serve({ fetch: req => app.fetch(req) })` gives everything: auto error capture, per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, nested db and http.client spans, correlated logs. `app.listen()` silently loses errors (zero events without a manual capture), loses the db span entirely, detaches the fetch client span onto a process-level root trace, stamps logs with that stale trace, and leaks isolation scopes across concurrent requests (all three concurrent events carried who=charlie and one shared trace id). Root cause is the same as the Deno cell: Oak's own server drains requests through an async queue, so the handler body escapes the AsyncLocalStorage context the Bun.serve wrapper opened. Note the span origin under app.listen() is still `auto.http.bun.serve`, i.e. Oak's listen() path does use Bun.serve internally on Bun - the SDK sees the request, it is only the handler body that escapes the context. This is one SDK issue shared across Deno and Bun and probably every framework with its own accept loop. 2. Route names are not automatic, and the middleware placement matters more than on Deno. Registering the naming middleware on the ROUTER (`router.use`) rather than the application makes it run before the handler with ctx.matched already populated, so it also names the error path - `GET /error` came back source=route status=internal_error, which the Deno cell's after-next() variant could not do. `updateSpanName` alone stamps source `custom`; the explicit `SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE='route'` attribute is what produces src=route. 3. Install. Oak ships on JSR only. `bun add @oak/oak` fails; the working line is an `.npmrc` with `@jsr:registry=https://npm.jsr.io` plus `npm install "@oak/oak@npm:@jsr/oak__oak@17.2.0"`. Any Oak-on-Bun page has to lead with that. Two findings that generalize past Oak: - The Bun baseline "no library spans without a bundle" is not universal. mysql2 produced a correctly parented `db SELECT users` span under plain `bun app.ts` with no Bun.build and no sentryBunPlugin, because mysql2 publishes its own diagnostics_channel events. The bundle is needed for drivers/frameworks the SDK has to patch, not for ones that self-publish. The docs alert at bun/index.mdx:98 telling users bundling breaks auto-instrumentation is also stale relative to sentryBunPlugin. - Outgoing fetch works fully on Bun (span + sentry-trace + baggage), so the Deno K2 gap is Deno-only; an Oak page for Bun needs no workaround section there. Error middleware is optional on the Bun.serve path and should be presented that way: without it the error still arrives as `auto.http.bun.serve` handled:false because Oak re-throws after logging "[uncaught application error]". A user who registers an Oak `error` event listener would stop that re-throw and then does need the manual capture. Cleanup: all five bun processes plus my sink and recorder were killed (`kill $pid`); the remaining sink.mjs/recorder.mjs processes on the box belong to other agents. `rm -rf node_modules` ran, freeing 125M; rerunning needs the two npm install lines above.

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:41401/__items ; curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:41401/__items?raw=1'

Fresh on Bun M-fresh-bun

Fresh 2 (@fresh/core 2.3.3, Vite-based, scaffolded with jsr:@fresh/init@2) · bun 1.4.0 (build step run with deno 2.9.0) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Fresh 2 builds with Deno/Vite but the built server runs on bun unchanged. Exact wiring:

1. Scaffold + build with deno (deno is only a build-time tool here):
   `deno run -A -r jsr:@fresh/init@2 ./app --force --tailwind`
   `cd app && deno task build`  ->  `_fresh/server.js` which is literally
   `import server from "./server/server-entry.mjs"; export default { fetch: server.fetch };`
   The SSR bundle has zero bare imports by default, so bun needs nothing from Deno at runtime.
   Only `Deno.serve` (used by `app.listen()`, not by the default export), `Deno.stat`/`Deno.open`
   (static-file serving) and `Deno.readTextFileSync` (error code frames, inside try/catch) survive
   in the bundle, so the `fetch` path is Deno-free.

2. Keep the SDK and the db driver out of the SSR bundle so bun resolves them at runtime.
   app/vite.config.ts:
     export default defineConfig({
       plugins: [fresh(), tailwindcss()],
       ssr: { external: ["@sentry/bun", "mysql2", "mysql2/promise"] },
       build: { rollupOptions: { external: [/^@sentry\//, /^mysql2/] } },
     });

3. Install the SDK in the PARENT directory of the Fresh app (not in app/, whose node_modules is
   Deno-managed and gets pruned by npm). Bun resolves bare imports by walking up from the bundled
   file at app/_fresh/server/assets/*.js, so a node_modules one level above app/ is found:
     npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bun-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz \
       $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz \
       $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz mysql2

4. instrument.ts (parent dir):
     import * as Sentry from "@sentry/bun";
     Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel: "http://127.0.0.1:<sink>/", tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: "stream"|"static" });

5. entry.ts (parent dir) - init first, then the Fresh bundle, then Bun.serve:
     import "./instrument.ts";
     import server from "./app/_fresh/server.js";
     Bun.serve({ port, fetch: (req: Request) => server.fetch(req) });

6. Run: `bun entry.ts`. No `Bun.build` / `sentryBunPlugin` step was needed (see db spans).

Baseline check without Sentry: `PORT=41340 bun app/_fresh/server.js` boots ("Started development
server: http://localhost:41340"), SSRs `/` and serves fs routes and `app.get()` routes identically
to `deno serve -A _fresh/server.js`. Static assets under /assets are the one thing that would need
Deno.stat/Deno.open; the HTML references them but I did not exercise them.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✗ brokenOut of the box a throw in a Fresh route handler does NOT reach Sentry: Fresh catches it, logs it to stderr and renders its own 500 page. The Bun.serve span still ends with status internal_error, but no event envelope is produced. Adding a Fresh middleware that wraps ctx.next() in try/catch and calls Sentry.captureException fixes it, giving mechanism 'fresh.middleware', handled:false, with request data and context lines attached. Both results from traceLifecycle 'static'. verified: confirmed-broken Could not refute. Reproduced the reported behaviour exactly and found the structural cause, plus three working wirings (one more than reported) and one init-only fallback that is too fragile to recommend. Root cause (not a Bun SDK bug, a Fresh design fact): the SSR bundle's `App.handler()` ends with a catch-all that never rethrows: app/_fresh/server/server-entry.js:6394 } catch (err) { ctx.error = err; return await DEFAULT_ERROR_HANDLER(ctx); } app/_fresh/server/server-entry.js:6104 DEFAULT_ERROR_HANDLER = async (ctx) => { ... console.error(error); return new Response("Internal server error", { status: 500 }); } `@sentry/bun`'s Bun.serve instrumentation only captures what escapes the fetch handler (packages/bun/src/integrations/bunserver.ts:274-282 `catch (e) { captureException(e, { mechanism: { type: 'auto.http.bun.serve', handled: false } }) }`), so nothing is captured; the span still gets `internal_error` from the 500 status. Fresh also has an internal `#onError` listener slot (compileMiddlewares(..., onError), server-entry.js:5441) but `App` hard-codes it to NOOP and never exposes a setter, so there is no SDK-side hook to attach to. Fresh is fully bundled into `_fresh/server/server-entry.js`, so no import hook (`@sentry/server-runtime-injection`, which has no Fresh support anyway) can ever see it; bundling with `Bun.build` + `sentryBunPlugin` cannot change this. Runs (sink 51873, app 51874, one bun process per run, sentinel-gated): R1 baseline, traceLifecycle static -> /boom and /boomasync return 500, no event envelope: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /boom","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"internal_error","trace_id":"6d79854c03884617956129af36dd7c81","sdk":"sentry.javascript.bun","spans":[]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /boomasync","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"internal_error","trace_id":"c4f93db8c4894e7eabfd273536ee04de","sdk":"sentry.javascript.bun","spans":[]} next envelope is the sentinel: {"type":"event","message":"sentinel",...,"trace_id":"ed4fc95ec8694e2d9ff1a766defd38a0"} R2 baseline, traceLifecycle stream -> identical, still no event (only the sentinel arrives). The lifecycle is irrelevant to this. R4 `app.onError("*", ctx => Sentry.captureException(ctx.error, ...))` (NEW, not in the report) -> works, and unlike the middleware it needs no try/catch/rethrow: {"type":"event","exception":"Error: fresh-bun-route-boom","mechanism":"fresh.onError","handled":false,"sdk":"sentry.javascript.bun","runtime":"bun","hasContextLine":true,"trace_id":"73e498fee222408e94f17ef32aee4a1f","request":{"url":"http://127.0.0.1:51874/boom","method":"GET",...}} R6 `routes/_error.tsx` handler calling `Sentry.captureException(ctx.error)` (NEW; the file-system form, matches what the Fresh/CF and Fresh/Deno probes used) -> works: {"type":"event","exception":"Error: fresh-bun-route-boom","mechanism":"fresh._error","handled":false,"sdk":"sentry.javascript.bun","runtime":"bun","hasContextLine":true,"trace_id":"d5c401a999a443fdaa7b25da8f22e9b0","request":{...}} R5 the reported middleware -> reproduced verbatim: mechanism "fresh.middleware", handled false, request data, context lines, same trace_id as the transaction. R3 init-only variant, `integrations: [Sentry.captureConsoleIntegration({ levels: ["error"] })]` and NO app code at all -> the error IS captured, correctly linked to the transaction trace, but as handled:true with a console mechanism: {"type":"event","exception":"Error: fresh-bun-route-boom","mechanism":"auto.core.capture_console","handled":true,...,"trace_id":"5b6945bf31124192a2872d7e2afc46bd"} R8 the same init-only variant AFTER adding a `routes/_error.tsx` -> nothing is captured at all (transactions only, then the sentinel), because a custom error route replaces `DEFAULT_ERROR_HANDLER` and its `console.error`. So the console trick silently stops working the moment the app gets an error page; do not document it as the fix. All four route-error events carry request URL/method/headers and context lines, and share the trace_id of their `http.server` transaction, so once captured the data is complete. Fresh's own OpenTelemetry spans ("middlewares", route spans, plus its `span.updateName(\`${method} ${pattern}\`)` at server-entry.js:6371) never reach Sentry either: every transaction came back with `spans:[]`. Files: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-fresh-bun-errors/{instrument.ts,entry.ts,run.sh,app/main.ts,app/routes/boom.tsx,app/routes/boomasync.tsx,app/routes/_error.tsx,items-r*.json,app-r*.log}. `app/main.ts` compiles all wirings in and selects with `globalThis.__WIRING`, set from the `WIRING` env var in `entry.ts`. Rerun: `PORT=51873 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs &` then `bash run.sh <baseline|middleware|onerror|errorroute> <static|stream> <0|1 captureConsole> <tag>`. Rebuild after touching app/: `cd app && deno task build` (works offline, ~2s).
Workaround: Capture from a Fresh error hook; all three work identically on bun, pick one. Cleanest is the file-system error route, `app/routes/_error.tsx`: import * as Sentry from "@sentry/bun"; import { define } from "../utils.ts"; export const handler = define.handlers({ GET(ctx) { Sentry.captureException(ctx.error, { mechanism: { type: "fresh._error", handled: false } }); return new Response("Internal server error", { status: 500 }); }, }); Programmatic equivalent in `main.ts`: `app.onError("*", ctx => { Sentry.captureException(ctx.error, { mechanism: { type: "fresh.onError", handled: false } }); return new Response("Internal server error", { status: 500 }); })`. The middleware form from the report (`try { return await ctx.next() } catch (err) { Sentry.captureException(err, ...); throw err }`) also works but must be registered before every other `app.use`, or errors thrown by earlier middleware escape it. Do NOT rely on `captureConsoleIntegration`: it happens to catch these errors only while Fresh's built-in error page is in use, and stops capturing entirely as soon as the app defines `_error.tsx` or `onError`.
route names✓* works-waOut of the box the server span is named from the URL: name 'GET /users/42', source 'url' (origin auto.http.bun.serve) - the Bun.serve integration has no idea Fresh matched /users/:id. Fresh exposes the matched pattern as ctx.route, so a middleware calling Sentry.updateSpanName(getRootSpan(span), `${ctx.req.method} ${ctx.route}`) yields 'GET /users/:id'; in traceLifecycle 'stream' the span then reports source 'route', in 'static' the transaction reports source 'custom' (updateSpanName forces custom and a later setAttribute('sentry.source','route') does not win). verified: works-after-all REFUTED. The "source is stuck on 'custom' in traceLifecycle 'static'" half of the partial verdict is an artifact of the original probe using the v10 attribute key. On develop (v11) the transaction source is read from `sentry.segment.name.source` (exported as `Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE` from `@sentry/bun`), not from `sentry.source`. `packages/core/src/tracing/sentrySpan.ts:451` does `const source = this._attributes[SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE]` and `packages/core/src/utils/spanUtils.ts:492-498` shows `updateSpanName()` deliberately stamps that attribute with 'custom'. Setting the correct key AFTER (or instead of) `updateSpanName` wins in both lifecycles. The prior probe's middleware (variant A) set `rootSpan.setAttribute("sentry.source", "route")`, which on v11 is an unread attribute, so 'custom' stayed. I re-ran the prior agent's own Fresh-on-bun app with four middleware variants x both lifecycles, plus a Bun.serve `routes` variant, against a local sink. --- baseline, middleware present but no naming (VARIANT=NONE) --- static: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/42","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","trace_attrs":{"source_attr":"url"}} stream: {"type":"span","raw":[{"name":"GET","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.bun.serve","source":"url"}]} (confirms the out-of-the-box half of the claim; in stream the name is the bare method, not the URL) --- A: Sentry.updateSpanName(root, name) + setAttribute("sentry.source","route") [the prior probe] --- static: {"name":"GET /users/:id","source":"custom","trace_attrs":{"source_attr":"custom","legacy_source_attr":"route"}} stream: {"name":"GET /users/:id","is_segment":true,"source":"custom","custom_span_name":"GET /users/:id"} Note: the prior report said stream reports source 'route' for this variant. It does not, it reports 'custom' there too. So variant A is worse than reported, and the working fix is the same in both lifecycles. --- B: root.updateName(name) + setAttribute("http.route", route) + setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, "route") [the fix, mirrors the SDK's own express patch-layer.ts:344-346] --- static: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_attrs":{"source_attr":"route","http_route":"/users/:id"}} stream: {"type":"span","raw":[{"name":"GET /users/:id","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.bun.serve","source":"route","http_route":"/users/:id"}]} error route, static: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /boom","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"internal_error","trace_attrs":{"source_attr":"route","http_route":"/boom"}} followed by {"type":"event","exception":"Error: fresh-bun-route-boom","mechanism":"fresh.middleware","handled":false,"trace_id":"50561738703e4162a8f20be818c05e26"} on the same trace. --- C: same as B plus "url.template" --- identical to B (source 'route'). --- D: Sentry.updateSpanName(root, name) THEN setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, "route") --- static: {"name":"GET /users/:id","source":"route","trace_attrs":{"source_attr":"route"}} stream: {"name":"GET /users/:id","is_segment":true,"source":"route","custom_span_name":"GET /users/:id"} So the order does not matter, only the key does. D additionally keeps `sentry.custom_span_name` so nothing downstream can rename it; B is the closer match to what the SDK's own framework integrations write. --- E: no Sentry code in the app at all, Fresh route patterns registered on Bun.serve instead --- Bun.serve({ port, routes: { "/users/:id": (req) => server.fetch(req) }, fetch: (req) => server.fetch(req) }) static: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","trace_attrs":{"source_attr":"route"}} This is fully automatic (bunserver.ts:206-218 parameterizes only when `request.params` is non-empty), but you must hand-enumerate every parameterized Fresh route, and a param-less route registered there still reports 'url'. Variant B is the practical answer. Repro (probe dir $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-fresh-bun-routenames/): files: app/main.ts (middleware, VARIANT env switch A/B/C/D), entry.ts, entry-routes.ts (variant E), instrument.ts, sink.mjs (extended to surface sentry.segment.name.source / sentry.source / http.route / sentry.custom_span_name), run.sh, run2.sh PORT=41871 node sink.mjs & zsh run.sh static B v2-static-B # then read items-v2-static-B.json zsh run.sh stream B v2-stream-B zsh run2.sh static NONE v2-static-bunroutes entry-routes.ts npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{bun,node,core,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry}-10.67.0.tgz mysql2 (node_modules was already present; app/_fresh is the prebuilt SSR bundle, rebuild with `cd app && deno task build`) Wiring is otherwise exactly the prior probe's: SDK external to the Fresh SSR bundle, node_modules one level above app/, `bun entry.ts`. Not tested: whether the same middleware works under `deno serve` (out of scope, this is the bun probe). No Fresh e2e app exists in dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications and there is no Fresh guide under ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/, so there is no documented Fresh wiring to compare against.
Workaround: Fresh 2 on bun, middleware in app/main.ts (registered before app.fsRoutes()): import * as Sentry from "@sentry/bun"; const sentryMiddleware = define.middleware(async (ctx) => { const span = Sentry.getActiveSpan(); const rootSpan = span && Sentry.getRootSpan(span); if (rootSpan && ctx.route) { rootSpan.updateName(`${ctx.req.method} ${ctx.route}`); rootSpan.setAttribute("http.route", ctx.route); rootSpan.setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, "route"); // "sentry.segment.name.source" } try { return await ctx.next(); } catch (err) { Sentry.captureException(err, { mechanism: { type: "fresh.middleware", handled: false } }); throw err; } }); app.use(sentryMiddleware); Yields name 'GET /users/:id' with source 'route' in both traceLifecycle 'stream' and 'static'. Do NOT use `setAttribute('sentry.source', 'route')`, that key is v10 and is ignored on v11.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent GETs to /iso/alpha|beta|gamma, each doing Sentry.setTag before and after a randomised 50-150ms await, then captureException. Each event carried exactly its own tags ({probe_tag, probe_tag_after} both equal to its own name) and its own trace id, matching the trace id the handler read back from the active span. traceLifecycle 'static'.
incoming trace✓ workscurl with sentry-trace: aaaa...aaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1 and a matching baggage header produced a transaction with trace_id aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa and parent_span_id bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb; the captureMessage inside the handler landed on the same trace id, and Sentry.getActiveSpan() was set inside the route handler. traceLifecycle 'static'.
outgoing fetch✓ worksA plain global fetch() from inside a Fresh route handler to a local recorder produced an http.client span (origin auto.http.fetch; 'http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41413/rec' in static, 'http.client GET 127.0.0.1' in stream) as a child of the http.server segment, and the recorder saw sentry-trace with the same trace id plus a full baggage header including sentry-sampled=true.
db spans✓ worksmysql2 spans appeared with NO Bun plugin build: plain `bun entry.ts`, instrumentation path is the runtime diagnostics-channel injection (origin auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel). The requirement is only that mysql2 stays external to the Vite SSR bundle and that the pool is created at module scope - I put createPool in app/dbpool.ts and imported it from main.ts so it evaluates at server startup, avoiding K11. Spans: 'db mysql2.pool.connect', 'db mysql2.connect', 'db SELECT id, name FROM users' (static) / 'db SELECT users' (stream), all children of the http.server segment. This refines the toolbox note that Bun library spans need a Bun.build + sentryBunPlugin bundle; here they did not.
logs✓ worksSentry.logger.info('fresh-bun-log-probe', { where: 'route-handler' }) inside a route handler arrived as a log envelope after ~7s: {"type":"log","items":["info: fresh-bun-log-probe"]}. No enableLogs option needed on develop.
client errors· not-runOnly the server side was probed. Fresh's client entry is a Vite-built preact island bundle, so @sentry/browser would have to be added to app/client.ts; not attempted inside the time box.

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions Fresh at all, on bun or on Deno. `ls ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/` has no `fresh` entry (angular, astro, aws-lambda, azure-functions, bun, capacitor, cloudflare, connect, cordova, deno, effect, electron, elysia, ember, express, fastify, firebase, gatsby, gcp-functions, hapi, hono, koa, nestjs, nextjs, nitro, node, nuxt, react, react-router, remix, solid, solidstart, svelte, sveltekit, tanstackstart-react, vue, wasm). The bun guide is a single page, ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx, plus a `configuration/` dir, and it names no framework. A case-insensitive grep for "fresh" across docs/platforms/javascript/ and platform-includes/ only hits the English word, e.g. docs/platforms/javascript/common/session-replay/configuration.mdx and platform-includes/metrics/usage/javascript.mdx.

Documented: no

A page must say: Fresh 2 is built with Deno and Vite but the built server runs unchanged on Bun (deno task build emits _fresh/server.js exporting { fetch }). Errors are NOT captured automatically, which contradicts the blanket claim on the BunServer page: Fresh's App.handler() catches every route and middleware error and renders its own 500, so nothing reaches Bun.serve; show capturing from app/routes/_error.tsx with captureException and an explicit mechanism. Route names need a middleware registered in app/main.ts before app.fsRoutes() that renames the root span from ctx.route and then sets the attribute sentry.segment.name.source to route; updateSpanName alone leaves the source as custom. Isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing fetch spans, db spans and logs work. Client errors were not exercised.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/fresh/index.mdx (fallbackGuide: javascript.bun, plus a Deno-runtime note). Also change common/configuration/integrations/bunserver.mdx:18 to qualify automatic error capture, and common/enriching-events/transaction-name/index.mdx:90-103 to document setting sentry.segment.name.source to route.

No guides/fresh entry among the 37 guides and no Fresh framework hits in docs or platform-includes; guides/bun/index.mdx:1-214 documents only the --preload flow; guides/bun/index.mdx:96-100 (Bundled Code Limitation alert) gives no guidance for a Vite-built SSR bundle on Bun; common/configuration/integrations/bunserver.mdx:18 claims errors are captured automatically; common/enriching-events/transaction-name/index.mdx:90-103 documents updateSpanName but never the name source; grep for sentry.segment.name.source returns nothing.

Key findings a docs page would have to carry: 1. Fresh 2 on bun is real and needs no shim. The Vite SSR build emits `_fresh/server.js` as `export default { fetch }` with zero bare imports, which is exactly Bun.serve's entry shape. Deno is only a build-time dependency. `Deno.serve` in the bundle sits inside `app.listen()`, which the default export never calls. The Deno-only bits that DO remain on a hot path are `Deno.stat`/`Deno.open` in Fresh's static-file serving, so `/assets/*` under bun is the one thing I would expect to break; I did not exercise it (the HTML references the asset, I only asserted on the SSR HTML and the route handlers). 2. Installing the SDK is the non-obvious step. The Fresh app dir's node_modules is Deno-managed (`nodeModulesDir: "manual"`, no package.json), and `npm install` there prunes the Vite/preact tree the build needs. Putting node_modules one directory ABOVE the app works because bun resolves bare specifiers by walking up from app/_fresh/server/assets/*.js. A docs page should either say that, or tell users to add a real package.json to the Fresh app. 3. @sentry/bun and the db driver must be `ssr.external` in vite.config.ts. If they are bundled into server-entry.js, Sentry.init in the bundle would run a second copy of the SDK and the diagnostics-channel injection has nothing to hook. 4. Both defects here are "framework has no Sentry integration" defects, and both have the same one-middleware fix, which is what a Fresh guide would need to ship: - Fresh swallows route-handler throws entirely (500 page, span status internal_error, no event). - The Bun.serve span is named from the raw URL (`GET /users/42`, source url), never from the matched pattern. Fresh does expose `ctx.route` (= "/users/:id"), so the data is available. Note the source inconsistency after `updateSpanName`: stream lifecycle reports source "route", static lifecycle reports "custom", and setting `sentry.source` back to "route" after updateSpanName does not stick in static. 5. Contradicts the standing Bun note that library spans need a `Bun.build` + `sentryBunPlugin` bundle: mysql2 spans came through on plain `bun entry.ts` with origin auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel. What mattered was module-scope pool creation reached from the server entry (app/dbpool.ts imported by main.ts), not a build-time plugin. Worth re-checking on the plain Bun/express template, since it changes the recommended setup. 6. One transient during the very first bun run: `/api/:name` 404'd on the first request after boot while `/` succeeded, and the request never reached the logger middleware. It did not reproduce on any later run (same bundle, same command). Likely a race between Bun's server accepting connections and Fresh's lazy fs-route module import; I did not chase it further and would not report it as a finding without a repro. Cleanup: sink (86385), recorder (86434) and all three app processes (87155, 94101, 95878) were killed; node_modules removed from both app/ and the probe dir (the probe dir is now 688K). No 10.73.0 was installed; everything ran against the $REPRO/_toolbox/pack 10.67.0 develop tarballs.

NestJS on Bun M-nestjs-bun

NestJS 11 (@nestjs/core + @nestjs/platform-express) with @sentry/nestjs + @sentry/bun · bun 1.4.0 (macOS arm64), SDK develop 6f2da7483d / 10.67.0 tarballs · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

NestJS boots on Bun unchanged (no Sentry needed to get there): `bun src/main.ts` printed the usual `[RouterExplorer] Mapped {/users/:id, GET} route` lines and served requests. Decorators need a tsconfig.json with `"experimentalDecorators": true, "emitDecoratorMetadata": true`; Bun honours it both at runtime and in Bun.build.

Packages (one npm install; bun add cannot resolve the tarballs' transitive @sentry/*@10.67.0):
  npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-nestjs-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bun-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz \
    $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz \
    $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz @nestjs/core@11 @nestjs/common@11 @nestjs/platform-express@11 reflect-metadata rxjs mysql

src/instrument.ts (init from @sentry/bun, not @sentry/node):
  import * as Sentry from '@sentry/bun';
  Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 });

src/main.ts, first line before anything Nest:
  import './instrument';
  import 'reflect-metadata';
  import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core'; ...

src/app.module.ts (both pieces required; the filter is not optional, see errors):
  import { SentryModule, SentryGlobalFilter } from '@sentry/nestjs/setup';
  @Module({ imports: [SentryModule.forRoot()], controllers: [AppController],
            providers: [{ provide: APP_FILTER, useClass: SentryGlobalFilter }] })

build.ts (required for express/middleware/db spans and for route names; @sentry/* must NOT be external, and Nest's lazily required optional peers MUST be):
  import { sentryBunPlugin } from '@sentry/bun/plugin';
  await Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./src/main.ts'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', sourcemap: 'external',
    external: ['@nestjs/microservices', '@nestjs/microservices/microservices-module', '@nestjs/websockets',
               '@nestjs/websockets/socket-module', '@nestjs/platform-express/multer', 'class-validator',
               'class-transformer', 'cache-manager'],
    plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] });

Run: `bun run build.ts && bun dist/main.js`. Without the `external` list the build fails outright with `error: Could not resolve: "@nestjs/microservices/microservices-module"` (plus class-validator/class-transformer) because Nest's `loadPackage()` requires are statically visible to Bun's bundler. This is the one Nest-specific step a docs page would have to spell out.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksA throw in a controller reaches Sentry with mechanism `auto.http.nestjs.global_filter`, handled false, and a context line, in both the unbundled and bundled runs; the response is a normal Nest 500. Nest DOES swallow it without the filter: with the APP_FILTER provider removed (NO_FILTER=1) the same request produced only `transaction GET /error internal_error` and no event at all, so SentryGlobalFilter is mandatory, not a nicety.
route names◐ partialBundled with sentryBunPlugin the server span/transaction is `GET /users/:id` with source `route` (static lifecycle) and `http.server GET /users/:id` (stream lifecycle), including express `middleware`/`handler /users/:id` children. Plain `bun src/main.ts` (no bundle) gives `GET /users/42` with source `url` and zero child spans, because only the base node:http server instrumentation is active and Nest's express router is never patched. verified: partial Could not refute; the reported split reproduces exactly, and the unbundled case is in fact slightly worse than reported. Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-nestjs-bun-routenames (node_modules removed after the run; reinstall with the npm install line from the report, then `bun run build.ts`). Sink on 38911, app ports 38912-38922, all processes killed. Variants tried (all with `import './instrument'` first line, SentryModule.forRoot() + APP_FILTER SentryGlobalFilter, tsconfig with experimentalDecorators/emitDecoratorMetadata): V1 `bun src/main.ts`, LIFECYCLE=static (baseline, src/main.ts + src/instrument.ts, log v1-unbundled-static.log): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/42","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.bun","spans":[]} V2 `bun run build.ts && bun dist/main.js`, static (build.ts with sentryBunPlugin + the @nestjs/microservices/websockets/multer/class-validator/class-transformer/cache-manager externals): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["middleware <anonymous>","middleware jsonParser","middleware urlencodedParser","handler /users/:id"]} V9 same bundle, LIFECYCLE=stream: {"type":"span","items":["middleware urlencodedParser","middleware jsonParser","middleware <anonymous>","handler /users/:id","http.server GET /users/:id"],"raw":[...{"name":"GET /users/:id","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.server"}]} V10 unbundled + stream (the DEFAULT lifecycle) — worse than the original report, which only measured static. The segment span carries no path at all, so every route collapses into one name: {"type":"span","items":["http.server GET"]} V3 init from `@sentry/nestjs` instead of `@sentry/bun`, unbundled (src/instrument-nest.ts + src/main-nest.ts): NO server span of any kind, and events lose their transaction name: {"type":"event","message":"sentinel","sdk":"sentry.javascript.nestjs","runtime":"node","trace_id":"42a7973198d5472f82838f826da7be5e"} <- no "transaction" field, no transaction/span envelope at all app log (debug:true): `Sentry Logger [warn]: No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping.` V4 `@sentry/bun` + explicit `nestIntegration()` unbundled: unchanged, `GET /users/42` source `url`. V5 `bun --preload ./src/instrument.ts src/main-noinit.ts` (different init placement): unchanged, `GET /users/42` source `url`. V6 runtime plugin registration in a preload (`plugin(sentryBunPlugin())` from `bun`, preload-runtime-plugin.ts): app does not boot — [probe] runtime plugin registered SyntaxError: Export named 'Injectable' not found in module '.../node_modules/@nestjs/common/index.js' This is the exact limitation the SDK documents in packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/bundler/bun.ts ("BUILD-ONLY ... a module returned by a runtime onLoad plugin in Bun loses its CommonJS named exports", oven-sh/bun#31770). Bun 1.4.0 also has `node:module.registerHooks === undefined`, and packages/server-runtime-injection/src/register.ts explicitly excludes Bun from the `Module.register` fallback, so there is no runtime injection path on Bun by construction. Root cause of the partial: on Bun the route name comes only from the express instrumentation's `http.route`, which is injected at bundle time by sentryBunPlugin; without a bundle nothing patches Nest's express router, and the SDK prints no warning at all unless `debug: true` (v1-unbundled-static.log contains zero Sentry output).
Workaround: Unbundled Bun can be given real route names from user code with a global Nest interceptor (src/route-name2.interceptor.ts + src/main-rename2.ts): read `req.route.path`, then on the root span call `updateName(`${req.method} ${route}`)`, `setAttribute('http.route', route)` and — this is the load-bearing part on develop — `setAttribute('sentry.segment.name.source', 'route')`. Static: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route"}; stream: {"type":"span","items":["http.server GET /users/:id"]}. Setting the old `sentry.source` attribute instead does NOT work: `updateName()` calls INTERNAL_setSegmentNameSourceIfSegment(span,'custom') (packages/core/src/tracing/sentrySpan.ts:232) and the earlier interceptor variant that set `sentry.source` produced {"name":"GET /users/:id","source":"custom"}. The interceptor only fixes the name/source; the express `middleware`/`handler` child spans stay absent. The supported fix remains bundling with sentryBunPlugin.

Runtime instrumentation (`bun run`) is currently not supported." and packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/bundler/bun.ts:22-26 gives the exact reason my attempt A hit: "a module returned by a runtime `onLoad` plugin in Bun loses its CommonJS named exports. When https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/31770 lands, we can revisit." The same file also notes "Bun has no runtime fallback here, so bundling is the only injection path." Reference app: the repo has no NestJS-on-Bun e2e app. The Bun+db reference is dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/bun-mysql, whose build.ts uses the identical `Bun.build` + `sentryBunPlugin()` pattern and whose start script is `bun run dist/app.js` — i.e. the bundler is the documented, only path, and this is not NestJS-specific (it applies to express/koa/fastify/AI spans on Bun equally). One improvement over the reported wiring: `@sentry/bun` and `mysql` may stay in `external` (the plugin strips instrumented packages back out of `external`), so only the app and the instrumented libraries pass through the bundler and the SDK/OTel stack is not bundled. Verified in build-b.ts / dist-b — db spans still recorded (evidence 5 above). The NestJS-specific `external` entries (@nestjs/microservices[/microservices-module], @nestjs/websockets[/socket-module], @nestjs/platform-express/multer, class-validator, class-transformer, cache-manager) remain mandatory; without them the build fails with `error: Could not resolve: "@nestjs/microservices/microservices-module"`. Note: a concurrent agent's Nuxt app (verify4-M-nuxt-bun-isolation, pid 67335) was also tunnelling into port 47311, so two stray items from ports 47312/47313 appear in my first sink dump; they are not mine and I left that process alone.
Workaround: There is no unbundled workaround; the bundle is the only path. Minimal working recipe (verified, build-b.ts): import { sentryBunPlugin } from '@sentry/bun/plugin'; await Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./src/main.ts'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', sourcemap: 'external', external: ['@sentry/bun', 'mysql', '@nestjs/microservices', '@nestjs/microservices/microservices-module', '@nestjs/websockets', '@nestjs/websockets/socket-module', '@nestjs/platform-express/multer', 'class-validator', 'class-transformer', 'cache-manager'], plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()], }); then `bun run build.ts && bun dist/main.js`. `@sentry/bun` and the instrumented drivers may be listed in `external` (the plugin un-externalizes instrumented packages itself); the six @nestjs optional-peer entries plus class-validator/class-transformer/cache-manager must be listed or the build fails to resolve them. src/main.ts must start with `import './instrument';` then `import 'reflect-metadata';`, instrument.ts must init `@sentry/bun`, app.module.ts needs `SentryModule.forRoot()` plus `{ provide: APP_FILTER, useClass: SentryGlobalFilter }`, and tsconfig.json needs experimentalDecorators + emitDecoratorMetadata. Do NOT try `Bun.plugin(sentryBunPlugin())` at runtime: it breaks @nestjs/common's CommonJS named exports and the app will not boot.

client errors· not-runNo browser surface. This is a headless NestJS HTTP API on Bun, so @sentry/browser client-side error capture does not apply.

Docs today

No page anywhere in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions NestJS on Bun. `grep -rci bun docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nestjs/index.mdx` returns 0 and `grep -rni nest docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/` returns nothing. The Nest.js guide is Node-only by construction: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nestjs/index.mdx:5 sets `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, its prerequisites include (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nestjs/index.mdx:14 -> platform-includes/getting-started-prerequisites/javascript.node.mdx:7) demand "Node version `18.0.0` or above", and the install tabs (platform-includes/getting-started-install/javascript.nestjs.mdx:3-15) offer npm/yarn/pnpm only, no bun tab. The Bun guide (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx, 214 lines) names no framework at all. Nothing documents the two steps that actually decide the outcome here: initialising with @sentry/bun instead of @sentry/node, and the Bun.build + sentryBunPlugin step with Nest's optional peers marked external.

Documented: no

A page must say NestJS 11 (`@nestjs/core` + `@nestjs/platform-express`) boots on Bun 1.4.0 unchanged, given a `tsconfig.json` with `experimentalDecorators` and `emitDecoratorMetadata` — Bun honours it both at runtime and inside `Bun.build`. It must then state the central Bun rule this cell demonstrates: the SDK instruments libraries (mysql/mysql2, Express, the Nest middleware and handler spans, AI SDKs) only in code that passes through `Bun.build` with `sentryBunPlugin()` from `@sentry/bun/plugin`; running `bun src/main.ts` directly produces server transactions with no child spans and no route names, and there is no runtime hook that recovers them. It must give the build recipe including the workaround the build itself forces: Nest's lazily required optional peers must be listed in `external` (`@nestjs/microservices`, `@nestjs/microservices/microservices-module`, and the rest) or the build fails outright with `error: Could not resolve: "@nestjs/microservices/microservices-module"`. Route names remained only partial even in the bundled shape, which the page must not overpromise.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/nestjs.mdx (new)

~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nestjs/index.mdx:4-5 (`sdk: sentry.javascript.nestjs`, `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`); nestjs/index.mdx:14 (prerequisites include, resolving to the Node prerequisites); nestjs/index.mdx:75 (`{filename: main.ts}` init snippet, Node-only); ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx:96-98. `grep -ci bun` over guides/nestjs/index.mdx returns 0; `grep -rni nest` over guides/bun/ returns nothing.

NestJS runs on Bun cleanly, and the Sentry story splits sharply on whether you bundle. - Unbundled (`bun src/main.ts`, the shape a user copies from the Nest docs) you get errors with the right nestjs mechanism, isolation, trace continuation, outgoing fetch spans with headers, and logs, but URL-named transactions (`GET /users/42`, source `url`) and no middleware, handler or db spans. Nothing warns about this unless `debug: true` is set. This matches the known Bun finding that library spans need the plugin build. - Bundled with `sentryBunPlugin()` everything lands: `GET /users/:id` source `route`, express middleware/handler children, and the mysql span. The one Nest-specific gotcha is that Bun's bundler statically resolves Nest's `loadPackage()` requires, so `@nestjs/microservices`, `@nestjs/websockets`, `class-validator`, `class-transformer`, `cache-manager` must be listed in `external` or the build fails; keeping `@sentry/*` bundled (as the task hint says) worked and is required for the plugin's injected channels to line up. - The route name comes from the express layer, not from Nest: there are no Nest-specific spans (no `Controller.method` / nestjs interceptor spans) in either lifecycle. `SentryModule.forRoot()` was imported as the docs prescribe but contributed no visible spans on Bun; the only thing that demonstrably mattered from @sentry/nestjs was SentryGlobalFilter. - SentryGlobalFilter is load-bearing: remove the APP_FILTER provider and Nest's built-in exception layer swallows the throw completely (transaction with internal_error, zero events). A docs page for this combination must not present it as optional. - Static vs stream: route naming, db and http.client spans, isolation and trace continuation were verified in BOTH lifecycles and agreed. Static was used for the tag/trace-id assertions because tags and nested spans[] are easier to read there; stream additionally showed the low-cardinality names (`db SELECT users`, `http.client GET 127.0.0.1`). - All five processes were killed and node_modules (131M) removed. Ports used: 53101 (sink) and 53102-53105 (apps); 47311/47312 were already taken by other agents.

Next.js on Bun M-nextjs-bun

Next.js 15.5.4 (app router) with @sentry/nextjs 10.67.0 (develop, v11 line) · bun 1.4.0, run as `bun --bun next build` / `bun --bun next start` · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Next.js 15.5.4 builds and serves on bun with `bun --bun`, and @sentry/nextjs initializes there. Exact wiring a docs page would have to show:

1. Packages: `npm install next@15.5.4 react react-dom` plus `npm install <pack>/sentry-{nextjs,node,core,opentelemetry,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,react,browser,browser-utils,bundler-plugins,vercel-edge}-10.67.0.tgz`. Use npm, not `bun add`. Pin `typescript@5.x`: TypeScript 6 has no `./lib/typescript.js` in its exports map, so Next's verifyTypeScriptSetup dies with `The "id" argument must be of type string. Received undefined` (a Next/TS6 problem, not a bun one, node fails identically).

2. `next.config.mjs`:
```js
import { withSentryConfig } from '@sentry/nextjs/config';
export default withSentryConfig({}, { silent: true, sourcemaps: { disable: true }, telemetry: false, disableLogger: true });
```
NOTE for docs: on develop, `withSentryConfig` is NO LONGER exported from `@sentry/nextjs`; it lives on the `@sentry/nextjs/config` subpath. Importing it from the main entry fails on bun AND on node with `SyntaxError: Export named 'withSentryConfig' not found in module .../build/cjs/index.server.js`. Every published Next.js docs snippet uses the old import.

3. `instrumentation.ts` (unchanged from the node recipe):
```ts
export async function register() {
  if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'nodejs') await import('./sentry.server.config');
}
export { captureRequestError as onRequestError } from '@sentry/nextjs';
```

4. `sentry.server.config.ts`: `Sentry.init({ dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' })`. `sendDefaultPii` no longer exists on develop and is a TS build error.

5. Run: `bun --bun ./node_modules/.bin/next build` then `bun --bun ./node_modules/.bin/next start -p <port>`. `--bun` is required, without it bun shells out to node.

No Sentry-specific bun step exists and none is possible: Next.js is built by webpack/turbopack, so the `sentryBunPlugin()` `Bun.build` path documented for plain Bun apps is unreachable, and `@sentry/nextjs/build/import-hook.mjs` no-ops under bun.

Reported `contexts.runtime` on every event and transaction is `{"name":"node","version":"v26.3.0"}`, which is bun's node-compat `process.version`. Nothing in the payload says bun, even though `process.versions.bun === '1.4.0'` is available.

Under `bun --bun next start -p 52910`: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /app/api/users/[id]","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /app/api/users/[id]/route","start response"]} {"type":"event","exception":"Error: verify4 route handler boom","mechanism":"auto.function.nextjs.route_handler","transaction":"GET /api/error","trace_id":"382cc20271df406fb2ee7edcb79de3c3"} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /app/api/error","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"internal_error","trace_id":"382cc20271df406fb2ee7edcb79de3c3"} The same casedir build served with plain `node ./node_modules/.bin/next start -p 38477` is byte-for-byte the same failure: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /app/api/users/[id]","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_id":"597708a593df4aa395ee7e75e0115c7d"} {"type":"event","exception":"Error: verify4 route handler boom","transaction":"GET /api/error","trace_id":"7455549702bd410a8dac164f5e5a72ad"} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /app/api/error","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"internal_error","trace_id":"7455549702bd410a8dac164f5e5a72ad"} ROOT CAUSE (Next.js, not Sentry, not bun). node_modules/next/dist/server/route-modules/app-route/helpers/get-pathname-from-absolute-path.js: function getPathnameFromAbsolutePath(absolutePath) { let appDir = '/app/'; if (!absolutePath.includes(appDir)) { appDir = '\\app\\'; } const [, ...parts] = absolutePath.split(appDir); const relativePath = appDir[0] + parts.join(appDir); ... } It strips everything up to and including the FIRST `/app/` in the resolved page path. When the project root (or any ancestor directory) is named `app`, that first `/app/` is the ancestor, so the real app-router segment survives: `/…/casedir/app/app/api/error/route.ts` -> `/app/api/error/route`. module.js:574-582 then does `tracer.setRootSpanAttribute('next.route', route)`. @sentry/nextjs hoists that attribute onto the root span and the isolation scope in packages/nextjs/src/server/handleOnSpanStart.ts:57-86, so the transaction becomes `GET /app/api/error`. `captureRequestError` instead uses Next's `errorContext.routePath` (packages/nextjs/src/common/captureRequestError.ts:41), which is correct, which is exactly why the two names disagree. Both build manifests (`.next/app-path-routes-manifest.json`) are identical in control and variant (`{"/api/error/route": "/api/error", ...}`), confirming the divergence is purely this runtime helper. Cross-check against the repo's own reference app, dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/nextjs-16-bun (read-only): it uses the same `withSentryConfig` from `@sentry/nextjs/config`, `traceLifecycle: 'static'`, and tests/route-handler.test.ts asserts `transactionEvent?.transaction === 'GET /route-handler/[xoxo]/node'` with no `/app` prefix — matching my control. That app additionally installs `@sentry/bun` and adds `bunHttpServerIntegration({ spans: false })` + `fetchIntegration()`, but those are for request isolation, not route names; my control produced correct names without them. Not re-tested here: the isolation finding (the missing third concurrent event) from the same probe — that is a different capability and the reference app's `bunHttpServerIntegration({ spans: false })` is the documented answer to it.
