Workaround: Do not name the Next.js project root directory (or any ancestor directory of it) `app`. Rename it to anything else (`web`, `my-app`, the project name) and rebuild — route names come out as `GET /api/users/[id]` with `transaction_info.source: "route"`, and events and transactions carry the same name. There is no SDK-side or bun-side setting that helps; `traceLifecycle: 'static'` and `'stream'` behave the same, and plain node fails identically, so this is a Next.js path-resolution bug (`getPathnameFromAbsolutePath` splits on the first `/app/`), not an SDK or runtime issue.

Adding `fetchIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun` to `Sentry.init` in `sentry.server.config.ts` restores both the `http.client` span and the propagation headers, under BOTH trace lifecycles. BASELINE (no fetchIntegration, traceLifecycle 'static') - reproduces the report: recorder /__hits: {"url":"/hit","sentry-trace":null,"baggage":null,"traceparent":null} sink: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /app/api/fetchout","op":"http.server","spans":["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /app/api/fetchout/route","start response"]} -> no http.client span, no headers. `Integration installed: NodeFetch` is present in server-baseline.log but never fires: bun's native fetch emits no undici diagnostics channels. FIX (app/sentry.server.config.ts): import { fetchIntegration } from '@sentry/bun'; import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nextjs'; Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static', integrations: [fetchIntegration()] }); plus `@sentry/bun` in the app's dependencies. server-fix.log shows `Integration installed: Fetch` alongside `Integration installed: NodeFetch`. AFTER, traceLifecycle 'static' (server-fix.log): recorder /__hits: "sentry-trace": "7d2699e81a7a482e988f1af7b36ce9e8-9987b591f02565e2-1" "baggage": "sentry-environment=production,sentry-public_key=public,sentry-trace_id=7d2699e81a7a482e988f1af7b36ce9e8,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fapi%2Ffetchout,sentry-sampled=true,sentry-sample_rand=0.367495436561904,sentry-sample_rate=1" sink transaction "GET /app/api/fetchout", trace_id 7d2699e81a7a482e988f1af7b36ce9e8: spans: ["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /app/api/fetchout/route","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41822/hit","start response"] the http.client span is {"op":"http.client","description":"GET http://127.0.0.1:41822/hit","span_id":"9987b591f02565e2","origin":"auto.http.fetch"} The header's span id (9987b591f02565e2) and trace id match the emitted http.client span exactly, so the downstream service continues the same trace. AFTER, default 'stream' lifecycle, and with NO explicit tracePropagationTargets (server-stream.log): recorder: "sentry-trace": "aa02efe64b2e4b9bb7a5c77e35a85235-95cf1f8492e6e32d-1", baggage present sink span envelope, env trace aa02efe64b2e4b9bb7a5c77e35a85235: http.client | GET 127.0.0.1 | span_id 95cf1f8492e6e32d | origin auto.http.fetch http.server | GET /app/api/fetchout | span_id 8431cd66b22af755 | origin auto Same trace, header span id equals the http.client span id. (Note the low-cardinality stream span name `GET 127.0.0.1` vs the static-lifecycle description `GET http://127.0.0.1:41822/hit`; that is the expected develop naming, not a defect.) Reference used: the repo's own e2e app ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/nextjs-16-bun/ already does exactly this. Its sentry.server.config.ts imports `bunHttpServerIntegration` and `fetchIntegration` from `@sentry/bun` next to `Sentry.init` from `@sentry/nextjs`, its package.json lists `@sentry/bun` as a dependency, and tests/propagation.test.ts asserts the http.client span id equals the downstream `sentry-trace` span id. So the SDK ships and tests this combination; only the docs are silent. Everything else the report says about the wiring held: `withSentryConfig` is only on `@sentry/nextjs/config` on develop, `bun --bun` is required, `contexts.runtime` is still {"name":"node","version":"v26.3.0"}-style (my sink showed runtime "node"). Those are separate findings; this capability is not broken. Commands: (in app/) `PROBE_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:41821/ PROBE_RECORDER=http://127.0.0.1:41822/hit bun --bun ./node_modules/.bin/next build` then `... next start -p 41823`; drive with `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:41823/api/fetchout` followed by `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:41823/api/sentinel` (sentinel captures a message and flushes). All started processes were killed.
Workaround: Add `@sentry/bun` to the Next.js app's dependencies and register its `fetchIntegration()` in the server init: // sentry.server.config.ts import { fetchIntegration } from '@sentry/bun'; import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nextjs'; Sentry.init({ dsn: process.env.SENTRY_DSN, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, integrations: [fetchIntegration()], }); No build, bundler or hook change is needed; `bun --bun next build` / `bun --bun next start` are unchanged. `@sentry/node`'s NodeFetch integration stays installed and simply never fires, so there is no double instrumentation. The same file should normally also add `bunHttpServerIntegration({ spans: false })` for per-request isolation (see the repo's nextjs-16-bun e2e app), which is a separate capability from this one.
db spans✓* works-waA module-scope `mysql2/promise` pool queried from a route handler produced no `db` span; the transaction contained only Next's own three spans. Both instrumentation paths fail. (a) Runtime hook: `[Sentry] Runtime hook not registered` - `@sentry/nextjs/build/import-hook.mjs` no-ops on bun, and stays unregistered whether launched plainly, with `NODE_OPTIONS="--import ..."` (bun ignores it), or with `bun --bun --preload ./node_modules/@sentry/nextjs/build/import-hook.mjs`. (b) Build-time injection: `[Sentry] Bundler plugin ran, injected libraries=[]`, because Next's server build leaves `mysql2` as a bare `require("mysql2/promise")` external; tested with and without `serverExternalPackages: ['mysql2']`, identical. The Bun.build + `sentryBunPlugin()` path that rescues plain Bun apps does not exist for Next.js, so no path works. The SDK does detect bun and subscribes eagerly (`[instrumentation:mysql2] Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly`), so it silently believes it is instrumented. traceLifecycle 'static'. verified: works-after-all REFUTED, and the reported diagnosis is wrong. db spans DO arrive on Next.js + bun with the stock documented wiring (`withSentryConfig` from `@sentry/nextjs/config`, `instrumentation.ts` register(), `sentry.server.config.ts`) once four lines in `instrumentation.ts` keep the SDK's diagnostics channels reachable. No import hook, no bundler injection, no `serverExternalPackages` change and no `bun --preload` are involved. ROOT CAUSE. mysql2 resolves to 3.24.3, and from 3.20.0 mysql2 publishes to `node:diagnostics_channel` itself (`node_modules/mysql2/lib/tracing.js`), gated on `shouldTrace(channel) = channel.hasSubscribers ?? channel.start?.hasSubscribers ?? false`. The SDK matches that: `packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/config/mysql2.ts:26` makes mysql2 >= 3.20.0 `registrationOnly` (so orchestrion injection deliberately does NOT apply to this version), and `packages/server-utils/src/integrations/mysql2/index.ts:150-161` subscribes eagerly in `setupOnce` via `subscribeMysql2DiagnosticChannels`. On bun 1.4.0 a subscriber does not keep its channel alive: the subscription is dropped at the first GC, so mysql2's gate is closed and it never publishes. Verbatim from $V/gctest.mjs under bun (node prints `true/true/true`): right after true after gc false after tick false kept after tick true true KEPT start The "Bundler plugin ran, injected libraries=[]" and "Runtime hook not registered" lines the report chased are red herrings for mysql2 >= 3.20 — neither path is supposed to instrument it. EVIDENCE, Next.js 15.5.4 + bun 1.4.0, same build, only the keep-alive toggled (sink 127.0.0.1:41337, traceLifecycle static): keep-alive ON : {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/db","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /api/db/route","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT id, name FROM users","start response"]} keep-alive OFF : GET /api/db ["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /api/db/route","start response"] stream lifecycle, keep-alive ON: {"type":"span","items":["resolve page components","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users"],"raw":[... {"name":"SELECT users","origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel"}]} A debug route reading the channel state confirms the mechanism: without the keep-alive `{"mysql2:query":{"start":false,...}}`, with it `{"mysql2:query":{"start":true,"end":true,"asyncStart":true}, ...}`. Not Next-specific: plain `bun sdkdc.mjs` with `@sentry/node` + a module-scope mysql2 pool gives `"spans":[]`, and `bun sdkdc-keep.mjs` (identical but retaining the channels) gives `"spans":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT id,name FROM users"]`. Same code on node needs no keep-alive. Things tried that are NOT the fix: un-externalizing mysql2 so webpack bundles it (`config.serverExternalPackages = config.serverExternalPackages.filter(p => p !== 'mysql2')`) builds fine and does bundle mysql2, but injects nothing — the orchestrion config skips mysql2 >= 3.20.0 on purpose (`grep -c "orchestrion:mysql2" .next/server/app/api/db/route.js` → 0). Making `dc.tracingChannel` return a per-name singleton also does not help; bun already caches the underlying named channels, it just does not keep them alive. REAL SDK FIX: `subscribeMysql2DiagnosticChannels` (and the other eager `waitForTracingChannelBinding` subscribers: redis, knex, dataloader, mongoose) must hold a module-level reference to every channel they subscribe to. That single change would make this capability work on bun with zero user code. Workaround: In `instrumentation.ts`, keep the SDK's diagnostics channels reachable after init (bun only; harmless on node): import diagnosticsChannel from 'node:diagnostics_channel'; export async function register() { if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'nodejs') { await import('./sentry.server.config'); globalThis.__sentryKeptChannels = ['mysql2:query', 'mysql2:execute', 'mysql2:connect', 'mysql2:pool:connect'] .map(name => diagnosticsChannel.tracingChannel(name)); } } export { captureRequestError as onRequestError } from '@sentry/nextjs'; Everything else stays stock: `withSentryConfig({}, {...})` from `@sentry/nextjs/config`, a module-scope `mysql2/promise` pool, `bun --bun ./node_modules/.bin/next build` then `bun --bun ./node_modules/.bin/next start -p <port>`. No `serverExternalPackages` change, no `NODE_OPTIONS`, no `--preload`. Add the driver's own channel names to the list for other databases (mysql2 3.20+ publishes `mysql2:query`, `mysql2:execute`, `mysql2:connect`, `mysql2:pool:connect`).

The Next.js guide (~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/index.mdx) names only Node.js/Edge/browser runtimes (index.mdx:53 lists sentry.edge.config.ts "Runs in edge runtimes"; index.mdx:144-147 branch on NEXT_RUNTIME === "nodejs" | "edge" only) and never mentions bun. The Bun guide is two entries (~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx plus configuration/) and never mentions Next.js. The only place the two meet is ~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/logs/usage/javascript.nextjs.mdx:7, an incidental line: "Using `printf` log syntax only works server-side in the Node.js and Bun runtimes." That implies bun is a supported Next.js server runtime without any page saying how to set it up or what breaks on it. Separately, every Next.js docs snippet still imports withSentryConfig from "@sentry/nextjs", which throws on develop; it now lives on "@sentry/nextjs/config".

Documented: no

A page must say Next.js 15.5.4 (app router) builds and serves under `bun --bun next build` / `bun --bun next start` and that `@sentry/nextjs` initializes there, then name the three things the Node path does not need. (1) Install `@sentry/bun` alongside `@sentry/nextjs` and add `fetchIntegration()` and `bunHttpServerIntegration({ spans: false })` from it to `integrations` in `sentry.server.config.ts`; without them outgoing `fetch` produces no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers, because the Node SDK's HTTP instrumentation relies on undici diagnostics channels Bun never publishes. (2) After `Sentry.init()`, keep a strong reference to the tracing channels (`mysql2:query`, `mysql2:execute`, `mysql2:connect`, `mysql2:pool:connect`, `ioredis:command`, `ioredis:connect`) on `globalThis` — Bun collects channels that only Sentry's subscriber references, so the subscriptions made at init are gone a tick later and no db span is recorded. (3) State which `instrumentation.ts` branch runs under `bun --bun`, since the documented `register()` at :144-147 covers only `nodejs` and `edge`. A separate troubleshooting note applies to Node and Bun equally: do not name the project root, or any ancestor of your `app/` directory, `app` — Next.js derives the route on its OpenTelemetry spans by splitting the route file's absolute path on the first `/app/` segment, so an extra `app` segment degrades transaction names, span segment names and `event.transaction` to `transaction_info.source: "url"`; with the root renamed (e.g. `nextapp`) they read `GET /api/users/[id]` with `source: "route"`.

Time-boxed to ~25 min for the scaffold; both scaffold blockers were resolved so no not-run was needed. Two scaffold failures that looked like bun bugs but are not: - `The "id" argument must be of type string. Received undefined` from `next build` is Next 15.5.4's verifyTypeScriptSetup resolving `typescript/lib/typescript.js` against a TypeScript 6 install whose exports map has no such subpath. Node 26 reproduces it identically (ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED). Fix is `typescript@5.x`, and Next auto-installs the bad version when tsconfig.json is present. - `Export named 'withSentryConfig' not found` is a develop API move, not bun. Node fails the same way. Bun-specific behaviour actually observed: - The SDK detects bun and takes its `Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly` branch for every diagnostics-channel instrumentation, then still reports `contexts.runtime.name: "node"` on the wire. `process.versions.bun` is available (1.4.0) and unread. - `[Sentry] Runtime hook not registered` is the single line that explains the db-span gap, and it is only visible with `debug: true`. A user on bun gets a silently half-instrumented SDK: no db/library spans, no outgoing http.client spans, no outgoing trace headers, and no warning. - Bun ignores `NODE_OPTIONS=--import`; `bun --bun --preload` loads the file but the hook still declines to register. Overall shape: everything that rides on Next.js's own OpenTelemetry emission plus the Sentry scope machinery works (errors, route names, isolation, incoming trace, logs). Everything that needs module patching, whether at runtime or at build time, does not. All processes killed (sink 69262, recorder 69264, next 82995). app/node_modules (440MB) and app/.next removed. Sources kept.

Setup the docs would have to show

Nuxt on bun works, and Sentry works on it, but ONLY if `sentry.server.config.ts` initializes `@sentry/bun` instead of `@sentry/nuxt`. Both variants below build and boot; the capability verdicts differ sharply.

(`cd $W/packages/bundler-plugins && npm pack --pack-destination $REPRO/_toolbox/pack`). Without it npm pulls the
registry 10.67.0, and `nuxt build` dies before doing anything:
  ERROR An error occurred while importing the module @sentry/nuxt/module: TypeError: (0 , _core.nodeStackLineParser) is not a function
(develop moved `nodeStackLineParser` to the `@sentry/core/server` export; the registry build still imports it from `@sentry/core`).

nuxt.config.ts:
  export default defineNuxtConfig({
    compatibilityDate: '2025-07-15',
    modules: ['@sentry/nuxt/module'],
    sentry: { autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import', debug: true },
    sourcemap: { server: false, client: false },
  })
`top-level-import` is the only viable init placement on bun: bun ignores NODE_OPTIONS and has no
`--import` flag, so the documented `node --import ./.output/server/sentry.server.config.mjs` path
does not exist here. The module injects `import './sentry.server.config.mjs';` as line 1 of
`.output/server/index.mjs` and prints "[Sentry] Successfully added the Sentry import to the server entry file".

  import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nuxt'

CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksAn error thrown from `server/api/error.ts` reaches Sentry on both variants with mechanism `auto.function.nuxt.nitro`, handled=false, via the Nitro `error` hook (`sentryCaptureErrorHook`). The framework does not swallow it; the route still returns 500 and the error is also printed by Nitro. The sink's `values[0]` shows `chained/handled=true` only because LinkedErrors adds the h3-wrapped cause; the outer value carries the real mechanism. Stream lifecycle.
route names✓* works-waWith `@sentry/nuxt` (@sentry/node) on bun there is no server span at all, so there is no name to report — the nitro `bun` preset serves through `Bun.serve`, which @sentry/node does not instrument. With `@sentry/bun` in sentry.server.config.ts the segment is `GET /users/:id` with `http.route=/users/:id`, `sentry.segment.name.source=route`, plus `url.path.parameter.id=55` and `params.id=55` from the Nuxt `updateRouteBeforeResponse` hook. Unparameterized routes stay method-only (`GET`, source=url), which matches the documented stream-lifecycle default. Stream lifecycle. verified: works-after-all Refuted the "you must swap @sentry/nuxt for @sentry/bun" half of the report. Route names work with the Nuxt SDK still in charge, on both nitro presets and both trace lifecycles, once the Bun server integrations are added to the existing `@sentry/nuxt` init. The SDK name stays `sentry.javascript.nuxt` and the Nuxt `updateRouteBeforeResponse` hook parameterizes the segment exactly as it does on node. Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-nuxt-bun-routenames/ (app/, variants/, RESULTS.txt, build-*.log, run-*.log, sink.mjs). Same app as the original probe: Nuxt 4.5.2, @sentry/nuxt 10.67.0 from $REPRO/_toolbox/pack tarballs (incl. sentry-bundler-plugins-10.67.0.tgz, which is now present in $REPRO/_toolbox/pack), `autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import'`, bun 1.4.0. Commands (sink on 52411, app on 52413): cd app && npm install --no-audit --no-fund PORT=52411 node sink.mjs & cd app && NITRO_PRESET=bun npx nuxt build && PORT=52413 bun run .output/server/index.mjs & curl 127.0.0.1:52413/users/55 ; curl 127.0.0.1:52413/api/ping ; curl 127.0.0.1:52413/api/sentinel A. Baseline reproduced (documented wiring, `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nuxt'` only, NITRO_PRESET=bun). Sink after 2x /api/ping, /users/55, sentinel — one event, ZERO spans: [ { "type": "event", "message": "sentinel", "sdk": "sentry.javascript.nuxt", "trace_id": "ace725ca354540439915c4ea19403d9d" } ] B. New negative data point: the same plain `@sentry/nuxt` init with NITRO_PRESET=node-server, still run under `bun run .output/server/index.mjs`, is also ZERO spans. So it is not the `bun` preset that breaks it — @sentry/node's OTel `httpIntegration` does not patch `node:http` under bun either. Switching preset is not a workaround. D. THE FIX, bun preset. sentry.server.config.ts: import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nuxt' import { bunServerIntegration } from '@sentry/bun' Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, integrations: [bunServerIntegration()] }) Sink (stream lifecycle, verbatim, trimmed): { "type": "span", "trace_id": "acc9bd4a165947ffb6df7639dd4e8886", "items": [ { "name": "GET /users/:id", "op": "http.server", "is_segment": true, "origin": "auto.http.bun.serve", "seg_name": "GET /users/:id", "seg_source": "route", "http_route": "/users/:id", "params": { "url.path": "/users/55", "http.route": "/users/:id", "url.path.parameter.id": "55", "params.id": "55" } } ] } { "type": "span", "trace_id": "81e52356...", "items": [ { "name": "GET", "op": "http.server", "seg_source": "url", "params": { "url.path": "/api/ping" } } ] } Sentinel event and its span share trace_id, so isolation is intact in this variant too. C. Same fix covers the node-server preset under bun, via the second integration: integrations: [bunServerIntegration(), bunHttpServerIntegration()] // NITRO_PRESET=node-server { "type": "span", "trace_id": "e45376ecd53448bdb3bcbebf9c053985", "items": [ { "name": "GET /users/:id", "op": "http.server", "is_segment": true, "origin": "auto.http.server", "seg_name": "GET /users/:id", "seg_source": "route", "http_route": "/users/:id", "params": { "url.path": "/users/55", "http.route": "/users/:id", "url.path.parameter.id": "55", "params.id": "55" } } ] } F. Both integrations on the bun preset: no duplicate spans (only `auto.http.bun.serve` fires; `node:http` is not on the path), and the error route keeps a route-scoped event: { "type": "event", "exception": "Error: nuxt-bun-route-error", "sdk": "sentry.javascript.nuxt", "transaction": "GET /api/error", "trace_id": "1000382ec15e4d42bede7d03decfbcb5" } G. Other trace lifecycle (`traceLifecycle: 'static'`, bun preset, both integrations) — transaction envelopes, names correct: { "type": "transaction", "name": "GET /users/:id", "op": "http.server", "source": "route", "status": "ok", "sdk": "sentry.javascript.nuxt", "data": { "sentry.origin": "auto.http.bun.serve", "http.route": "/users/:id", "url.path.parameter.id": "55", "params.id": "55" }, "spans": [] } { "type": "transaction", "name": "GET /api/ping", "op": "http.server", "source": "url", "spans": [] } Static lifecycle also gives unparameterized routes a full-path name (`GET /api/ping`); stream lifecycle leaves them method-only, which is the documented stream default, not a Nuxt/bun defect. Mechanism: `@sentry/nuxt`'s `updateRouteBeforeResponse` hook calls `setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute` (packages/server-utils/src/utils/setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute.ts), which no-ops unless the root span already carries `sentry.op === 'http.server'`. Nothing in the @sentry/node path creates that span under bun, so the hook silently does nothing; either bun integration supplies the span and the hook then names it. `@sentry/bun`'s own `getDefaultIntegrationsWithoutPerformance()` (packages/bun/src/sdk.ts:71-72) already ships both, which is why the @sentry/bun variant worked. Remaining gaps (not the capability under test): `spans: []` in static lifecycle — no nitro/h3 child spans on bun; and `@sentry/nuxt` does not detect bun and add these integrations itself, so with the documented snippet the failure is silent (no warning even with `debug: true`). Cleanup: app and sink processes killed, ports 52411/52413 free, app/node_modules removed.
Workaround: In `sentry.server.config.ts`, keep the `@sentry/nuxt` init and add the Bun server integrations (also `npm install @sentry/bun`): import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nuxt' import { bunServerIntegration, bunHttpServerIntegration } from '@sentry/bun' Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, integrations: [bunServerIntegration(), bunHttpServerIntegration()], }) `bunServerIntegration()` covers `NITRO_PRESET=bun` (Bun.serve), `bunHttpServerIntegration()` covers `NITRO_PRESET=node-server` run under bun; listing both is safe on either preset and produces no duplicate spans. Keep `autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import'` in `nuxt.config.ts` — bun ignores NODE_OPTIONS and has no `--import`, so the documented `node --import ./.output/server/sentry.server.config.mjs` launch does not exist on bun. Packages must be installed with `npm install` (bun cannot resolve the transitive `@sentry/*` pins). Real fix in the SDK: `@sentry/nuxt`'s server SDK should detect the bun runtime and add these two integrations by default, the way `@sentry/bun` does, instead of installing an OTel `httpIntegration` that silently never patches.
isolation✓* works-waThree concurrent /api/iso requests: with `@sentry/nuxt` the tags isolate correctly (probe_tag alpha/beta/gamma each on its own event) but every event in the process carries ONE trace id (6d1c0582624d4ee98971eadb94b1bf24 for the whole process lifetime) and a stale `transaction` leaked from an unrelated earlier request. Root cause: `patchEventHandler` clones the isolation scope but never resets its propagation context, and `sentryCaptureErrorHook` calls `getCurrentScope().setTransactionName()` — on node the OTel http server span supplies both per request, on Bun.serve nothing does. With `@sentry/bun` all three requests get distinct trace ids and their own tag, and each event's trace id matches its own http.server span. Stream lifecycle. verified: works-after-all Reproduced the reported breakage exactly, then refuted it with a one-line, user-land change that keeps `@sentry/nuxt` as the SDK. Setup (all files under $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-nuxt-bun-isolation/): Nuxt 4.5.2, nitropack 2.13.4, h3 1.15.11, bun 1.4.0, @sentry/nuxt 10.67.0 from develop (tarballs), `sentry: { autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import', debug: true }`. cd app && NITRO_PRESET=bun npx nuxt build PORT=52882 node ../sink5.mjs & # sink records trace_id, tags, transaction cd app && PORT=52881 bun run .output/server/index.mjs & APP_PORT=52881 SINK=http://127.0.0.1:52882 node ../drive.mjs drive.mjs does one GET /api/error (to plant a transaction name), then three concurrent GET /api/iso?tag=alpha|beta|gamma (each `Sentry.setTag('probe_tag', tag)`, jittered delay, `captureException`), then GET /api/sentinel (`captureMessage('sentinel')` + `flush`) as the sentinel. A. Documented wiring, `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nuxt'` only (runA3.log / resultA3.json) — BROKEN, matches the report: {"type":"event","exception":"nuxt-bun-route-error","transaction":"GET /api/error","trace_id":"76bca958a82c46aab4f5405c9198799f"} {"type":"event","exception":"iso-alpha","transaction":"GET /api/error","trace_id":"76bca958a82c46aab4f5405c9198799f","tags":{"probe_tag":"alpha"}} {"type":"event","exception":"iso-beta","transaction":"GET /api/error","trace_id":"76bca958a82c46aab4f5405c9198799f","tags":{"probe_tag":"beta"}} {"type":"event","exception":"iso-gamma","transaction":"GET /api/error","trace_id":"76bca958a82c46aab4f5405c9198799f","tags":{"probe_tag":"gamma"}} {"type":"event","message":"sentinel","transaction":"GET /api/error","trace_id":"76bca958a82c46aab4f5405c9198799f"} Tags isolate; one trace id for the whole process; `GET /api/error` leaks onto every later event; zero spans. Server log: `Patched h3 event handler. Created new isolation scope.` x6, `Using existing` x0. C. Same wiring plus `traceLifecycle: 'static'` (runC.log / resultC.json) — BROKEN identically. All five events carry trace_id f94fd5bbf8b2479aae04cfcf2ec1fd5c and `"transaction":"GET /api/error"`. The other trace lifecycle does not rescue it. B. THE FIX — add `bunServerIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun` to the same `@sentry/nuxt` init (runB.log / resultB.json) — WORKS: {"type":"event","exception":"iso-alpha","trace_id":"7ab860dec0e64078a9a4dcda65a6b3ee","tags":{"probe_tag":"alpha"}} {"type":"event","exception":"iso-gamma","trace_id":"338781f4e60c404c929c9f31b5e6868c","tags":{"probe_tag":"gamma"}} {"type":"event","exception":"iso-beta","trace_id":"697555049144412d9c9eac533bdccc80","tags":{"probe_tag":"beta"}} {"type":"span","name":"GET /api/iso","op":"http.server","trace_id":"7ab860dec0e64078a9a4dcda65a6b3ee"} {"type":"span","name":"GET /api/iso","op":"http.server","trace_id":"338781f4e60c404c929c9f31b5e6868c"} {"type":"span","name":"GET /api/iso","op":"http.server","trace_id":"697555049144412d9c9eac533bdccc80"} {"type":"event","message":"sentinel","trace_id":"b11aa6ac64934e9696d32a2095aa4eba"} Three distinct trace ids, each event's trace id equal to its own http.server span's, no stale transaction on any event, spans present and route-named. `sdk` stays `sentry.javascript.nuxt`. Server log flips to `Integration installed: BunServer` and `Patched h3 event handler. Using existing isolation scope.` x5, `Created new` x0 — the Bun.serve wrapper's `withIsolationScope` + `continueTrace` now runs first, so `patchEventHandler` correctly reuses the request-scoped isolation scope instead of cloning the default one. Mechanism confirmed: packages/nuxt/src/runtime/utils/patchEventHandler.ts clones `getDefaultIsolationScope()` and never touches the propagation context, so every clone inherits the same process-lifetime trace id. On node the OTel http server span supplies a fresh propagation context and transaction name per request; under the nitro `bun` preset the server is `Bun.serve` and nothing in `@sentry/node`'s default integrations touches it. `bunServerIntegration` (packages/bun/src/integrations/bunserver.ts) proxies `Bun.serve` and does exactly the missing work. Residual gap (not the capability under test): in variant B the manually captured `iso-*` events carry no `transaction` field at all. Only errors that flow through nitro's `error` hook get one, via `sentryCaptureErrorHook`'s `getCurrentScope().setTransactionName()`. `bunServerIntegration` sets the span name but not the scope's transaction name, so `Sentry.captureException` called directly inside a handler produces an event with no transaction. That is strictly better than the wrong, stale name in variant A. Caveat: `bunServerIntegration()` is an undocumented cross-package import for Nuxt users and requires adding `@sentry/bun` as an explicit dependency. The proper fix is for `@sentry/nuxt`'s server SDK (or `patchEventHandler`) to detect `process.versions.bun` and either install this integration or, at minimum, call `newIsolationScope.setPropagationContext({ traceId: generateTraceId() })` when it creates the clone.
Workaround: In `sentry.server.config.ts`, install `@sentry/bun` alongside `@sentry/nuxt` and pass its Bun.serve integration: import { bunServerIntegration } from '@sentry/bun' import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nuxt' Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, integrations: [bunServerIntegration()], }) Build with `NITRO_PRESET=bun npx nuxt build` and `sentry: { autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import' }` (bun ignores NODE_OPTIONS and has no `--import`, so the documented `node --import ./.output/server/sentry.server.config.mjs` path is unavailable). Run with `bun run .output/server/index.mjs`. This restores per-request trace ids, stops the stale transaction name leaking across requests, and additionally turns on route-named `http.server` spans, while keeping the `sentry.javascript.nuxt` SDK and all Nuxt-specific instrumentation. Replacing the init with `@sentry/bun` entirely also works but gives up the Nuxt SDK identity.
incoming trace✓* works-waA request carrying `sentry-trace: 12345678901234567890123456789012-1234567890123456-1` plus baggage is ignored under `@sentry/nuxt` — the event still carries the process-constant trace id, no parent. Under `@sentry/bun` the same request produces `GET /users/:id trace=12345678901234567890123456789012 parent=1234567890123456`, i.e. the trace is continued. Stream lifecycle. verified: works-after-all The original report is correct about the documented wiring, and I found the exact one-line change that makes the capability work while keeping `@sentry/nuxt`. Stack: Nuxt 4.5.2 / Nitro 2.13.4, `NITRO_PRESET=bun`, run as `PORT=41417 bun run .output/server/index.mjs` (bun 1.4.0), `@sentry/nuxt` 10.67.0 from develop, `autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import'`, stream lifecycle. Probe request always: curl -H 'sentry-trace: 12345678901234567890123456789012-1234567890123456-1' -H 'baggage: sentry-trace_id=...,sentry-sampled=true' http://127.0.0.1:41417/users/42 (and /api/error) VARIANT A - documented wiring, `Sentry.init` from `@sentry/nuxt` (confirms the report): event trace=04550485aa0a4475854eeb4f49385996 parent=None name=GET /api/error msg=nuxt-bun-route-error event trace=04550485aa0a4475854eeb4f49385996 parent=None name=GET /api/error msg=sentinel No `span` envelope at all; incoming trace id ignored; the later sentinel (a different request) reuses the same trace id and even the same `transaction` name, i.e. isolation is gone too. VARIANT D - same `@sentry/nuxt` init plus `integrations: [bunServerIntegration()]` from `@sentry/bun` (THE FIX): event trace=12345678901234567890123456789012 parent=1234567890123456 name=GET /api/error msg=nuxt-bun-route-error span trace=12345678901234567890123456789012 parent=1234567890123456 seg=True name=GET /users/:id op=http.server span trace=12345678901234567890123456789012 parent=1234567890123456 seg=True name=GET op=http.server event trace=77e88d5450834c69bae4818d7d3c9b1a parent=None name=None msg=sentinel Incoming trace continued (trace id AND parent span id), an `http.server` segment span is emitted, the parameterized route name `GET /users/:id` survives (the Nuxt route detector sets source=route, so streaming keeps the route in the name), isolation is restored (sentinel gets its own trace), and the SDK identity stays `sentry.javascript.nuxt` - unlike the previously reported workaround of initializing `@sentry/bun`, which reports `sentry.javascript.bun` and drops the Nuxt event processors. Boot log shows `Integration installed: BunServer` next to the normal Node integrations; no conflict with the (inert) `Http` integration. VARIANT E - control, `Sentry.init` from `@sentry/bun`: byte-identical trace behavior to D. ROOT CAUSE (verified, not theory): on develop `@sentry/node`'s request isolation, trace continuation and server span all hang off one diagnostics channel - `packages/core/src/integrations/http/constants.ts:3` `HTTP_ON_SERVER_REQUEST = 'http.server.request.start'`, subscribed in `packages/node/src/integrations/http/httpServerIntegration.ts:146`. Bun 1.4.0 never publishes that channel. Direct probe (`dc-probe.mjs`, subscribe + `node:http` server + one fetch): bun -> channel fired: 0 node -> channel fired: 1 So this is preset-independent: the `bun` preset serves via `Bun.serve` (no `node:http` at all), and even the `node-server` preset run under bun gets no event, which is why the boot log also prints `No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping`. `@sentry/bun` continues the trace because `bunServerIntegration` patches `Bun.serve` and calls `continueTrace` itself (`packages/bun/src/integrations/bunserver.ts:243`). `bunServerIntegration` only depends on `@sentry/core` APIs, which is why dropping it into a Nuxt/Node client works. Stream lifecycle. verified: works-after-all Reproduced the failure, then made it work without leaving `@sentry/nuxt`. Setup identical to the original probe (Nuxt 4.5.2, `NITRO_PRESET=bun npx nuxt build`, `PORT=41117 bun run .output/server/index.mjs`, bun 1.4.0, develop tarballs incl. worktree-packed `@sentry/bundler-plugins`). A. DOCUMENTED WIRING — `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nuxt'`, stream lifecycle, no extra integrations. Confirms the original report: rec: REC {"url":"/rec","sentry-trace":null,"baggage":null,"traceparent":null} sink __items after GET /api/fetchout + sentinel: ONLY the sentinel event, zero span/transaction items. B. `@sentry/nuxt` + `integrations: [fetchIntegration()]` from `@sentry/bun`, stream lifecycle — fetch capability restored: sink: {"type":"span","trace_id":"b7ff4bc4b37d4feb86ac284928c14f4b","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1"],"raw":[{"name":"GET 127.0.0.1","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.fetch"}]} rec: REC {"url":"/rec","sentry-trace":"b7ff4bc4b37d4feb86ac284928c14f4b-b5557932d8628c33-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,sentry-public_key=abc123,sentry-trace_id=b7ff4bc4b37d4feb86ac284928c14f4b,...,sentry-sampled=true,sentry-sample_rate=1"} Span + both headers are there, but it is a root span (`is_segment:true`) because nothing produces a request span. Same two integrations, DEFAULT stream lifecycle (the lifecycle the finding was filed under) — parity there too: sink: {"type":"span","trace_id":"c71f61af9f02425192d71c960ec1ec03","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","http.server GET"],"raw":[{"name":"GET 127.0.0.1","status":"ok","parent_span_id":"bb7cd5edfe766473","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.http.fetch"},{"name":"GET","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.bun.serve"}]} rec: REC {"url":"/rec","sentry-trace":"c71f61af9f02425192d71c960ec1ec03-888de8a191bd6862-1","baggage":"...sentry-trace_id=c71f61af9f02425192d71c960ec1ec03..."} The `http.client` span is a child of the `http.server` segment span, exactly as under `@sentry/bun`. As a bonus, `bunServerIntegration()` also restores per-request trace isolation: in D the fetchout trace (c71f...) and the sentinel trace (1aac...) are distinct, whereas in A they shared one trace id. Root cause (source, not inference): `@sentry/nuxt` server = `@sentry/node`, whose outgoing-HTTP instrumentation is the OTel http/undici one; bun's global `fetch` is neither `node:http` nor undici, so nothing patches it. `@sentry/bun` adds two things `@sentry/node` does not (packages/bun/src/sdk.ts `getDefaultIntegrationsWithoutPerformance()`): `fetchIntegration()` (packages/bun/src/integrations/fetch.ts — `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest`, i.e. it patches `globalThis.fetch`) and `bunServerIntegration()` (patches `Bun.serve`, which is what the nitro `bun` preset entry calls). Both are public exports of `@sentry/bun` (packages/bun/src/index.ts:207-209) and both are additive, so passing them in `integrations` keeps every `@sentry/nuxt` default. Not tested / out of scope: the `node-server` preset under node (unaffected, undici path works there), and whether the server span gets a route name (it stays `GET` in stream lifecycle — that is the separate routenames finding).
Workaround: Keep `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nuxt'` and add the two bun-specific integrations by hand. `sentry.server.config.ts`: import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nuxt' import { fetchIntegration, bunServerIntegration } from '@sentry/bun' Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, integrations: [fetchIntegration(), bunServerIntegration()], }) Requires `@sentry/bun` as a dependency alongside `@sentry/nuxt`. `fetchIntegration()` alone is enough to get the `http.client` span and the `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers; `bunServerIntegration()` additionally gives the parent `http.server` span and per-request trace isolation. Build/run unchanged: `NITRO_PRESET=bun npx nuxt build` with `sentry: { autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import' }`, then `bun run .output/server/index.mjs`. Real fix for the SDK: `@sentry/nuxt`'s server init should detect bun (`typeof Bun !== 'undefined'`) and pull in `fetchIntegration()` + `bunServerIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun` itself, the way `@sentry/bun`'s own `getDefaultIntegrations` does.
db spans✓* works-waInstrumentation path: none of the special ones. mysql2 v3 publishes its own `diagnostics_channel` tracingChannels (`mysql2:query`, `mysql2:connect`, `mysql2:pool:connect`) and @sentry/bun subscribes eagerly ('[instrumentation:mysql2] Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly'), so NO Bun plugin build was needed. The Nuxt module's build-time orchestrion pass injected nothing into the nitro bundle at all ('[Sentry] Bundler plugin ran, injected libraries=[]'; zero `orchestrion:` channel names in .output/server/index.mjs) on either preset. Under `@sentry/bun` a module-scope pool query yields `db SELECT users` with db.query.text/db.query.summary/db.namespace and origin `auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel`; under `@sentry/nuxt` no db span appears. Separately, the query itself always fails inside the nitro bundle with `genFunc$1 is not a function` (a rollup commonjs interop break on mysql2's generate-function) — this reproduces identically on the node-server preset under plain node, so it is a Nitro/mysql2 bundling bug, not a bun or Sentry one. Stream lifecycle. verified: works-after-all Refuted on both halves of the report. Under the DOCUMENTED wiring (`import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nuxt'`, sdk stays `sentry.javascript.nuxt`), Nuxt 4.5.2 on bun 1.4.0 with `NITRO_PRESET=bun` produces fully attributed db spans nested under the request span, and the mysql2 query does NOT have to fail. Two independent, separately provable causes were behind the "partial": CAUSE 1 - the missing parent span, not missing instrumentation. `@sentry/server-utils` mysql2 subscriber binds its channels with `{ requiresParentSpan: true }` (worktree packages/server-utils/src/integrations/mysql2/mysql2-dc-subscriber.ts:125 and :144). On bun, `@sentry/nuxt` alone creates no `http.server` span (the h3 patch logs only "Patched h3 event handler. Created new isolation scope."), so every mysql2 span is suppressed. Adding `integrations: [bunServerIntegration()]` (imported from `@sentry/bun`, init still from `@sentry/nuxt`) restores the parent and the db spans appear. Proof that instrumentation was never absent: the `mysql` v2 driver (which the repo's own e2e app nuxt-4/server/api/db-mysql.ts uses) has NO `requiresParentSpan`, and under plain `@sentry/nuxt` on bun it already emitted a complete span - as its own root transaction: {"name":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 0","info":{"source":"custom"},"trace":{"op":"db","origin":"auto.db.mysql","data":{"db.system.name":"mysql","db.namespace":"app","db.query.text":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 0","db.query.summary":"SELECT users","server.address":"127.0.0.1","server.port":3307}}} That also refutes "the build-time orchestrion pass injected nothing": with a driver that needs injection present, `grep -o "orchestrion:[a-z0-9:._-]*" .output/server/index.mjs` -> `orchestrion:mysql:query`, and the boot log shows `[instrumentation:mysql] Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly`. The earlier "injected libraries=[]" was an artifact of the app only using mysql2, which publishes its own channels and needs no injection. CAUSE 2 - `genFunc$1 is not a function` is a Nitro bundling bug with a one-line fix, not an unfixable blocker. `nitro: { externals: { external: ['mysql2', 'mysql2/promise'] } }` keeps mysql2 out of the rollup bundle; the query then returns rows on the first try (`[warmdb] mysql2 ok`, `{"rows":[{"id":1,"name":"ada"},{"id":2,"name":"linus"}]}`). Confirmed the bug is Nitro's, not bun's or Sentry's: the same unexternalized build on `node-server` under plain node fails the same way, and there it also breaks the `mysql` v2 driver (`TypeError: SqlString.format is not a function`) which bun happens to tolerate. FINAL WORKING RUN, documented wiring, static lifecycle (variant F, $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-nuxt-bun-dbspans/run-b/app-F.log): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/db","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.nuxt","spans":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > ?"],"spanDetail":[{"op":"db","desc":"mysql2.pool.connect","origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel","db_ns":"app"},{"op":"db","desc":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > ?","origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel","db_text":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > ?","db_summary":"SELECT users","db_ns":"app"}]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/dbmysql","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.nuxt","spans":["db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 0"],"spanDetail":[{"op":"db","desc":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 0","origin":"auto.db.mysql","db_text":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 0","db_summary":"SELECT users","db_ns":"app"}]} OTHER TRACE LIFECYCLE - stream (the develop default, variant G, run-b/app-G.log): same result, db spans parented to the Bun.serve segment, low-cardinality names: {"type":"span","trace_id":"378df42b...","items":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db SELECT users","http.server GET"],"raw":[{"name":"SELECT users","parent_span_id":"afcc488535e06f05","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel","op":"db","db_text":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > ?","db_summary":"SELECT users","db_ns":"app"},{"name":"GET","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.bun.serve","op":"http.server"}]} {"type":"span","trace_id":"f43c68b5...","items":["db SELECT users","http.server GET"],"raw":[{"name":"SELECT users","parent_span_id":"b1313fbd37da1d4c","origin":"auto.db.mysql","op":"db","db_text":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 0","db_summary":"SELECT users","db_ns":"app"}]} NEW GOTCHA FOUND (bundler variant E, run-b/app-E.log): on bun, externalizing is driver-dependent. With `external: ['mysql','mysql2','mysql2/promise']`, mysql2 still gets spans (it publishes its own channels and the SDK subscribes eagerly) but `mysql` v2 gets NONE - `{"name":"GET /api/dbmysql","op":"http.server","spans":[]}` - because bun has no require hook ("No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping") and an external module cannot receive the build-time orchestrion injection. So on bun: drivers that publish their own channels (mysql2) must be external; drivers that need Sentry's injection (mysql v2) must stay bundled. VARIANTS RUN (all `NITRO_PRESET=bun npx nuxt build` + `PORT=51842 bun run .output/server/index.mjs`, sink `PORT=51841 node sink.mjs`, MariaDB 127.0.0.1:3307): A @sentry/nuxt, no externals: mysql2 crashes genFunc$1, no mysql2 span; mysql v2 works, orphan root db span. B @sentry/nuxt + externals[mysql2]: both queries succeed; mysql2 spans only under a manual `Sentry.startSpan` parent; mysql v2 orphan root span. C @sentry/bun + externals[mysql2]: full nesting (the previously reported working variant). D @sentry/nuxt, no externals, node-server preset under node: both drivers break in the bundle (genFunc$1 / SqlString.format), spans still recorded - proves the bundling bug is Nitro's. E @sentry/bun + externals[mysql,mysql2]: mysql v2 loses its span (see gotcha). F @sentry/nuxt + bunServerIntegration() + externals[mysql2], static: works. G same as F, stream lifecycle: works. Probe files (rerun after `npm install` per the package.json in app/, node_modules removed to save disk): $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-nuxt-bun-dbspans/app/{nuxt.config.ts,sentry.server.config.ts,server/utils/dbpool.ts,server/utils/dbconn.ts,server/api/{db,dbmysql,dbspan,dbmysqlspan,sentinel}.ts,server/plugins/warmdb.ts}; logs in $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-nuxt-bun-dbspans/run-b/; sink at $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-nuxt-bun-dbspans/sink.mjs. app/ is left in the variant-F/G state. All processes killed.
Workaround: Keep the documented `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nuxt'` init and add two things. In sentry.server.config.ts: `import { bunServerIntegration } from '@sentry/bun'` and pass `integrations: [bunServerIntegration()]` to `Sentry.init` - the nitro `bun` preset serves through `Bun.serve`, which the Node-based Nuxt SDK does not instrument, and mysql2 spans are bound with `requiresParentSpan: true` so they are dropped without a request span. In nuxt.config.ts: `nitro: { externals: { external: ['mysql2', 'mysql2/promise'] } }` - bundling mysql2 through Nitro's rollup breaks the driver itself (`genFunc$1 is not a function`, and on node `SqlString.format is not a function` for mysql v2). Do not externalize drivers that rely on Sentry's build-time channel injection (`mysql` v2, and anything else without its own diagnostics channels): on bun there is no runtime require hook, so an external module of that kind is never instrumented.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info('nuxt-bun-log-line', { where: 'handler' })` inside a handler arrives as a log envelope on both variants (waited past the 5s flush timer, then sent a sentinel). Stream lifecycle.

Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/ mentions bun at all — `grep -rni "bun" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/` returns 0 hits, and `grep -rni "nuxt" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/` returns 0 hits. The combination is undocumented in both directions. Every documented server-init path for Nuxt is node-only and cannot be followed on bun: - docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/index.mdx:68 — `node --import ./.output/server/sentry.server.config.mjs .output/server/index.mjs` - docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/index.mdx:90 — `NODE_OPTIONS='--import ./.nuxt/dev/sentry.server.config.mjs' nuxt dev` - docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/install/cli-import.mdx:37,49,62,67 — the same flag, plus the NODE_OPTIONS form bun has neither `--import` nor NODE_OPTIONS support, so the only reachable install method is docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/install/limited-server-tracing.mdx:32 (`autoInjectServerSentry: "top-level-import"`), which is what I used. Two things that page gets wrong for this runtime: - Its warning block (limited-server-tracing.mdx:19) claims top-level-import can only instrument native Node APIs and "will not capture data from database calls, queues, ORMs, third-party libraries". My node control run with exactly that setting produced `db SELECT users`, `db mysql2.pool.connect` and `http.client` spans, so on develop the restriction is weaker than documented. - Nothing warns that on a non-node runtime the same setting silently degrades to errors+logs only, with a single process-wide trace id. There is no page telling a bun user to import `@sentry/bun` in `sentry.server.config.ts` instead, which is the only wiring that actually works here.

Documented: wrong

The presets page's "work out of the box" claim, with only Cloudflare excepted, is contradicted by the `bun` Nitro preset run under `bun .output/server/index.mjs`: `@sentry/nuxt` uses the Node HTTP instrumentation, which never sees `Bun.serve`, so with the documented setup alone there is no request span — every event shares one trace and one scope across concurrent requests, transactions are not route-named, incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` is not continued, and outgoing `fetch()` from server routes gets no `http.client` span and sends no trace headers. The page must add a Bun section stating that you install `@sentry/bun` alongside `@sentry/nuxt` and add `bunServerIntegration()` and `fetchIntegration()` from it to `integrations` in `sentry.server.config.ts`, which restores `http.server` segment spans named `GET /users/:id` with `sentry.segment.name.source=route`, per-request trace ids and per-request isolation, and outgoing-fetch spans and headers. For database spans it must additionally say to stop Nitro from bundling `mysql2` in `nuxt.config.ts` — otherwise every query 500s with `genFunc$1 is not a function`, with or without Sentry. Finally, the start command at nuxt/index.mdx:68 cannot be followed on Bun and needs a documented Bun equivalent.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/features/nitro-deployment-presets.mdx — new "Bun" section alongside the Cloudflare Pages one (and a Bun start command next to docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/index.mdx:68)

~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/features/nitro-deployment-presets.mdx:7 ("provides support for different Nitro deployment presets, most of which **work out of the box**"); nitro-deployment-presets.mdx:9-11 (Cloudflare Pages is the only preset carved out); ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/index.mdx:68 (`node --import ./.output/server/sentry.server.config.mjs .output/server/index.mjs` as the documented start command). `grep -rni bun` over guides/nuxt/ and `grep -rni nuxt` over guides/bun/ both return 0.

Headline: Nuxt itself runs fine on bun via `NITRO_PRESET=bun`, and @sentry/nuxt installs and boots, but the SDK a docs page would tell you to init (`@sentry/nuxt`, i.e. @sentry/node under the hood) is effectively tracing-blind on bun. Swapping one import in `sentry.server.config.ts` to `@sentry/bun` recovers server spans, route names, trace continuation, request isolation, outgoing-fetch propagation and db spans. That one-line difference is the whole finding. Why the documented path degrades: the nitro `bun` preset serves through `Bun.serve`, not `node:http`. @sentry/node's HTTP server instrumentation never fires, so (a) no `http.server` span exists, (b) `setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute` is a documented no-op without an active span so route names go nowhere, and (c) nothing resets the propagation context per request. `@sentry/nuxt`'s `patchEventHandler` (packages/nuxt/src/runtime/utils/patchEventHandler.ts) clones the isolation scope but never calls `setPropagationContext`, so on bun every event in the process lifetime shares the trace id minted at scope creation. Separately, `sentryCaptureErrorHook` (packages/nuxt/src/runtime/hooks/captureErrorHook.ts:48) writes the transaction name with `getCurrentScope().setTransactionName(...)`; with no per-request current-scope fork on bun that lands on the global scope and leaks the last-seen route onto unrelated events. Both are cheap to fix in the Nuxt runtime and would help every non-node nitro preset, not just bun. Also logged on the bun run: `[Sentry] Runtime hook not registered` (node prints "registered"), which is the visible symptom of the module-hook layer being unavailable. Orchestrion: the Nuxt module wires `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` into the nitro rollup config and force-inlines every instrumented package, yet the built `.output/server/index.mjs` contains no injected channels on EITHER preset (`[Sentry] Bundler plugin ran, injected libraries=[]`, zero `orchestrion:` strings). Build-time instrumentation appears to be a no-op in the Nitro rollup pipeline. It happens not to matter for mysql2, because mysql2 v3 ships its own `diagnostics_channel` tracingChannels that @sentry/bun subscribes to eagerly, but any library that relies on orchestrion injection would get nothing here. Worth a separate look — one suspicious detail is that `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` spreads `codeTransformerRollup(...)` and then overrides its `options`/`buildStart` hooks. Unrelated blocker worth recording for whoever reruns this: `@sentry/bundler-plugins` is not in $REPRO/_toolbox/pack and the registry's 10.67.0 is incompatible with develop's core — `nuxt build` fails at module import with `nodeStackLineParser is not a function` until you pack it from the worktree. I added it to $REPRO/_toolbox/pack. Third-party bug, not ours: a `mysql2` query inside a nitro bundle always throws `genFunc$1 is not a function` (rollup commonjs interop on mysql2's `generate-function` dependency). Reproduced identically on the node-server preset under plain node, so it is not bun-specific and not Sentry-caused. Sentry still emits the db span, with the failure recorded as `error.type: TypeError` on it. I could not observe a *successful* db query in a Nuxt build because of this; the span shape is confirmed, the success path is not. Cleanup: all four processes (app, sink, recorder, node control) were killed and ports 34117-34119 are free; app/node_modules (278 MB) was removed.

Setup the docs would have to show

Viable without Sentry: `npx sv create --template minimal --types ts app`, swap `adapter-auto` for `@sveltejs/adapter-node` in `vite.config.ts` (SvelteKit 2.70 has no `svelte.config.js` any more, kit config lives inside the `sveltekit()` Vite plugin), `npx vite build`, then `PORT=<port> bun build/index.js` -> "Listening on http://0.0.0.0:<port>" and routes answer. Sentry wiring that a docs page would have to show:

1. Packages. `npm install @sentry/sveltekit` (tarball install here needed the whole develop set on one command line, because npm cannot resolve the pinned 10.67.0 transitives from the registry): `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-sveltekit-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-browser-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-svelte-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-cloudflare-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bundler-plugins-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-browser-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-replay-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-replay-canvas-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-feedback-10.67.0.tgz`. `@sentry/bundler-plugins`, `@sentry/browser-utils`, `@sentry/replay`, `@sentry/replay-canvas` and `@sentry/feedback` were NOT in `$REPRO/_toolbox/pack` and had to be packed from the worktree; without the packed `@sentry/browser-utils` the client build dies with `"getComponentName" is not exported by @sentry/browser-utils` (registry 10.67.0 browser-utils lacks it).

2. `vite.config.ts` — `sentrySvelteKit()` first in `plugins`, then `sveltekit()`:
```ts
import adapter from '@sveltejs/adapter-node';
import { sveltekit } from '@sveltejs/kit/vite';
import { sentrySvelteKit } from '@sentry/sveltekit/vite';   // NOT '@sentry/sveltekit' on develop
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    sentrySvelteKit({ autoUploadSourceMaps: false, adapter: 'node' }),
    sveltekit({
      adapter: adapter(),
      experimental: { instrumentation: { server: true }, tracing: { server: true } },
    }),
  ],
});
```

3. `src/instrumentation.server.ts` (needs `experimental.instrumentation.server: true` above):
```ts
import * as Sentry from '@sentry/sveltekit';
Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, tunnel: process.env.SENTRY_TUNNEL });
```

4. `src/hooks.server.ts`:
```ts
import * as Sentry from '@sentry/sveltekit';
export const handleError = Sentry.handleErrorWithSentry();
export const handle = Sentry.sentryHandle();
```

5. Run: `npx vite build && PORT=<port> bun build/index.js`.

Two setup facts a docs page must state and does not:
- On develop the Vite plugin lives at `@sentry/sveltekit/vite`. The docs' `import { sentrySvelteKit } from "@sentry/sveltekit"` fails hard: `SyntaxError: The requested module '.../@sentry/sveltekit/build/esm/index.server.js' does not provide an export named 'sentrySvelteKit'`.
- Without `experimental.instrumentation.server: true` + `src/instrumentation.server.ts` (i.e. calling `Sentry.init()` from `hooks.server.ts` the old way) while `experimental.tracing.server: true` is set, NO transaction/span envelopes are emitted at all — errors still arrive. This reproduces identically on node, so it is a general SDK/kit-tracing ordering issue, not a bun issue.

Works: {"type":"span","trace_id":"9c3744ed5cfb41dbbe64f805d7c168ae","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","function sveltekit.resolve","http.server GET /api/out"],"raw":[{"name":"GET 127.0.0.1","status":"ok","parent_span_id":"86a5c25f5a0f846b","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.http.fetch"}, ...]} rec: [{"url":"/__rec/from-sveltekit","sentry-trace":"9c3744ed5cfb41dbbe64f805d7c168ae-9f2e7863e9616724-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,sentry-public_key=public,sentry-trace_id=9c3744ed5cfb41dbbe64f805d7c168ae,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fapi%2Fout,sentry-sampled=true,sentry-sample_rand=0.58...,sentry-sample_rate=1","traceparent":null}] Same trace id as the server span, both headers present. 3) bunfetch-static — the other trace lifecycle also works, and here the client span is visibly nested: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/out","op":"http.server","source":"route","trace_id":"07d9c3ce3fcc4a87aa05485c2cc650f5","spans":["function sveltekit.resolve","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:47627/__rec/from-sveltekit"]} This is the difference from Remix on bun (verify4-M-remix-bun-outgoingfetch), where 'static' dropped the parentless client span: `sentryHandle()` keeps an active server span in scope, so the fetch span has a parent and survives `onlyIfParent`. 4) guarded-stream — the form a docs page should show, `integrations: typeof globalThis.Bun !== 'undefined' ? [fetchIntegration()] : []` — identical result to (2). 5) node-bunfetch-stream — node v26.5.0 control on the SAME build shows why the guard is required: the bun fetch integration and @sentry/node's undici instrumentation both fire, producing a DUPLICATE span: {"type":"span","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","http.client GET 127.0.0.1","function sveltekit.resolve","http.server GET /api/out"]} Root cause the reporter identified is correct and unchanged: @sentry/node's NodeFetch instrumentation is undici-diagnostics-channel based and bun publishes no `undici:request:*` channels. `@sentry/bun`'s `fetchIntegration` (packages/bun/src/integrations/fetch.ts) instead uses core's `addFetchInstrumentationHandler`/`instrumentFetchRequest`, which patch `globalThis.fetch` directly and therefore work on bun. It is in the Bun SDK's default integration list, but a SvelteKit app initializes through `@sentry/sveltekit` -> `@sentry/node`, so it is never added. Not run: bun CI pin 1.3.14 — $SCRATCH/bun1314 is no longer on disk (`env: .../bun1314/bun-darwin-aarch64/bun: No such file or directory`), recorded as bunfetch-static-b1314 with empty items/rec. Also unchanged from the original report (not part of this capability, but confirmed while rebuilding): the Vite plugin is at `@sentry/sveltekit/vite` on develop, and `experimental.instrumentation.server: true` + `src/instrumentation.server.ts` is required for any span envelope at all.
Workaround: Add `@sentry/bun` as a dependency and register its `fetchIntegration()` in `src/instrumentation.server.ts`, guarded so it only applies on bun: ```ts import { fetchIntegration } from '@sentry/bun'; import * as Sentry from '@sentry/sveltekit'; const isBun = typeof globalThis.Bun !== 'undefined'; Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, integrations: isBun ? [fetchIntegration()] : [], }); ``` Then `npx vite build && PORT=<port> bun build/index.js`. Works with both `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` (default) and `'static'`. Without the `isBun` guard, a node run of the same build emits two `http.client` spans per request.
db spans✓* works-waA module-scope `mysql2/promise` pool queried from `/api/db` produced no db span on bun. mysql2 3.24.3 publishes its own `mysql2:query`/`execute`/`connect` tracing channels and Sentry's `Mysql2` integration subscribes to them, but on bun `tracingChannel('mysql2:query').start.hasSubscribers` is `false` (node: `true`), so nothing is ever recorded. Instrumentation path: no Bun plugin build was used or needed — SvelteKit's own Vite/rolldown build is the bundle, and the Sentry Vite plugin did inject into it (`globalThis.__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION_INJECT__ = orchestrionModuleInjected("mysql2", mysql2Integration)` sits in the emitted route chunk). The failure is on the subscriber side at startup: `Sentry.init` logs `No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping.` on bun, yet the acs binding the subscriber waits for IS present later (`acs.getTracingChannelBinding()` returns truthy at request time on both runtimes), so `waitForTracingChannelBinding`'s single 1 ms retry window is simply missed on bun. verified: works-after-all Reproduced the reported failure, then made db spans appear on bun with a one-line app change. The reported diagnosis (missed `waitForTracingChannelBinding` retry window) is WRONG: the SDK does subscribe, and then bun garbage-collects the subscription. Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-sveltekit-bun-dbspans (app/ = SvelteKit app, micro/ = no-framework isolators, RERUN.md = exact commands). Sink: `PORT=41777 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs`. Build/run: `cd app && npx vite build && PORT=<port> SENTRY_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:41777/ bun build/index.js`, drive with `curl /api/db`. A/B on ONE build config (default traceLifecycle 'stream'), only `app/src/instrumentation.server.ts` differs. A. Documented wiring (Sentry.init only) — BROKEN, matches the report: curl /api/db -> {"rows":[{"id":1,"name":"ada"},{"id":2,"name":"linus"}],"subs":false} {"type":"span","items":["function sveltekit.resolve","http.server GET /api/db"]} B. Same file with `import 'mysql2/promise';` added (position in the file is irrelevant — the import evaluates before the `Sentry.init()` call either way) — WORKS: curl /api/db -> {...,"subs":true} {"type":"span","items":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users","function sveltekit.resolve","http.server GET /api/db"]} With traceLifecycle:'static' the same change gives: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/db","op":"http.server","source":"route","spans":["function sveltekit.resolve","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT * FROM users"]} Root cause (isolated without SvelteKit, Vite or any bundler, in micro/ with plain `@sentry/node` + mysql2 3.24.3 under `bun app.mjs`): bun: "after init, mysql2:query hasSubscribers = true" then "at query time, mysql2:query hasSubscribers = false" -> only ["test probe-root"] in the sink. node (same file): true / true -> ["db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users","test probe-root"]. The SDK debug log on bun shows the subscription DID happen: "Sentry Logger [log]: [instrumentation:mysql2] Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly" / "[instrumentation:mysql2] subscribing to channels". So the async-context binding was present at init; nothing was missed. micro/dc-gc.mjs (pure runtime test, no Sentry): subscribe to `dc.tracingChannel('probe:chan')` without retaining the object -> bun "immediately: true", "after gc: false"; node "after gc: true". Retaining the channel object keeps the subscribers alive on bun (dc-gc2.mjs). i.e. bun holds diagnostics_channel channels weakly and drops their subscribers once the channel object is unreachable; Node keeps a subscribed channel alive. Sequence in the failing case: Sentry subscribes to `mysql2:query`/`:execute`/`:connect`/`:pool:connect` at `Sentry.init()`, before mysql2 is loaded, and keeps no reference to those channels (`subscribeMysql2DiagnosticChannels` in packages/server-utils/src/integrations/mysql2/mysql2-dc-subscriber.ts subscribes and drops the wrapper). bun collects them; mysql2 then loads and creates fresh, subscriber-less channels of the same names. Loading mysql2 first (or pinning the channels) keeps the object alive so Sentry's subscription survives — that is exactly why the workaround works, and why plain bundled Bun apps where the driver is already in the graph do get db spans. This is not mysql2-specific: every diagnostics-channel integration that subscribes at `init()` before its module loads is exposed on bun. Three fixes verified on bun (micro/app-b.mjs, app-c.mjs, app-d.mjs — all produce ["db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users", ...]): - `import 'mysql2/promise'` in the same file as `Sentry.init()` (before or after the Sentry import), - creating the pool in that file, - user-side pinning: `globalThis.__keep = ['mysql2:query','mysql2:execute','mysql2:connect','mysql2:pool:connect'].map(n => require('node:diagnostics_channel').tracingChannel(n))`. SDK-side fix (not applied, repo untouched): retain a module-level strong reference to every channel the SDK subscribes to. Two setup facts from the original report reproduce and still hold: the Vite plugin is `@sentry/sveltekit/vite` on develop, and `experimental.instrumentation.server: true` + `src/instrumentation.server.ts` is required or no span/transaction envelopes are emitted at all. Processes started (sink 41777, bun servers on 43117/52341/52987/53829) were all killed; micro/node_modules removed.
Workaround: In `src/instrumentation.server.ts`, import the database driver in the same file as `Sentry.init()` — `import 'mysql2/promise';` next to `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/sveltekit';` (order within the file does not matter). That keeps the `mysql2:*` diagnostics channels reachable so bun cannot garbage-collect Sentry's subscription before mysql2 loads. Creating the pool in that file works equally well. Generic form for any channel-based integration on bun: hold a strong reference to the channels, e.g. `globalThis.__sentryKeepChannels = ['mysql2:query','mysql2:execute','mysql2:connect','mysql2:pool:connect'].map(n => tracingChannel(n))` from `node:diagnostics_channel`.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info('sveltekit-bun-log-line', { where: 'route-handler' })` inside `/api/log` arrived as a `log` envelope after the ~7 s flush timer, in both lifecycles.
client errors· not-runNot probed: this cell is a server-runtime probe driven by curl with no browser. The client bundle did build once `@sentry/browser-utils` was packed from the worktree, and the SSR HTML carries the sentry-trace/baggage meta tags the client SDK would continue from.

Docs today

No Sentry docs page mentions SvelteKit on bun. `grep -rin bun` across `~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/sveltekit/` and `~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.sveltekit.mdx` returns nothing. What the docs do say, by implication: `~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/sveltekit/index.mdx:9` categorises the guide as `server-node`, and the adapter-compatibility box at `~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.sveltekit.mdx:35-49` lists only Node.js runtimes as fully supported (`adapter-node` at :42), adapter-cloudflare as the one supported non-Node runtime (:44), and says at :45-46 "Currently not supported — Non-Node.js server runtimes, such as Vercel's edge runtime, are not yet supported". So bun is neither claimed nor excluded by name; a reader would land in the "other adapters/runtimes might work, not officially supported" bucket at :47-48. Two concrete docs defects surfaced by this probe, both runtime-independent: the Vite plugin import at :383, :421 and :476 (`import { sentrySvelteKit } from "@sentry/sveltekit"`) does not exist on develop and must be `@sentry/sveltekit/vite`; and the "SvelteKit 3" tab at :244-248 writes `sveltekit({ tracing: { server: true } })` while kit 2.70.3 requires `sveltekit({ experimental: { tracing: { server: true }, instrumentation: { server: true } } })`.

Documented: no

A page must say the `@sveltejs/adapter-node` build output runs on Bun 1.4.0 as `bun build/index.js`, that errors, route names, request isolation, incoming trace continuation and logs work there unchanged, and name the two capabilities that do not. Outgoing `fetch()` from server routes gets no `http.client` span and carries no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers, because `@sentry/sveltekit`'s server side is `@sentry/node` and its fetch instrumentation relies on Node's undici diagnostics channel, which Bun does not emit; install `@sentry/bun` alongside `@sentry/sveltekit` and pass its `fetchIntegration()` into `Sentry.init` in `src/instrumentation.server.ts`, gated on the runtime so Node builds do not get a duplicate span. Database spans are absent because on Bun `node:diagnostics_channel` drops a channel's subscribers as soon as the channel object is garbage collected, so a driver first imported inside a lazily loaded route chunk is never instrumented; until this is fixed in the SDK, pin the mysql2 tracing channels in `src/instrumentation.server.ts` immediately after `Sentry.init()`. The page should also note that SvelteKit 2.70 has no `svelte.config.js` — kit config lives inside the `sveltekit()` Vite plugin — since the adapter swap is part of the setup.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/sveltekit.mdx (new); and add Bun to the adapter/runtime compatibility box at platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.sveltekit.mdx:36-48

~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/sveltekit/index.mdx:5-9 (`categories: [javascript, browser, server, server-node]`); ~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.sveltekit.mdx:36 ("designed to work out of the box with several SvelteKit adapters and their underlying server runtimes"); javascript.sveltekit.mdx:42 (Adapter-node listed as supported, runtime unqualified). `grep -rin bun` across guides/sveltekit/ and that include returns nothing.

Scope: probed the develop SDK only (worktree 6f2da7483d, version 10.67.0). 10.73.0 was never installed. What bun costs you, precisely: everything that rides on SvelteKit's own request path works (errors, route names, isolation, incoming trace, SSR trace meta tags, logs, static and stream lifecycles both). Everything that rides on Node diagnostics-channel instrumentation is silently dead (outgoing fetch spans + propagation headers, mysql2 db spans, and by extension every other library integration in @sentry/node). The failure is silent unless `debug: true` is on, where it shows as one line: "No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping." I verified the same `build/` directory run under node emits the missing spans, so the SvelteKit build and the Vite-plugin injection are not the problem — the runtime is. Refinement on the root cause, since it is not the obvious one: the injected orchestrion marker IS present in the emitted route chunk, bun DOES implement `diagnostics_channel.tracingChannel` correctly (verified standalone in `dctest.mjs`: `start.hasSubscribers` flips to `true` on subscribe, `traceCallback`/`tracePromise` are functions), and the async-context binding the subscriber waits for IS available on bun at request time (`/api/acs` returns `binding: true` on both runtimes). What never happens on bun is the subscribe itself. `waitForTracingChannelBinding` (packages/core/src/asyncContext/tracing-channel-binding.ts:9) checks the binding once, then retries exactly once after `setTimeout(..., 1)` and gives up. On bun the acs is evidently installed later than that window. A larger/looping retry, or re-checking on the first client request, would likely light up the whole library-instrumentation surface on bun for every @sentry/node-based framework SDK, not just SvelteKit. Worth a targeted experiment before anyone writes a "SvelteKit on bun" docs page. Two findings that are NOT bun-specific but showed up here and reproduce on node with the identical build: - With `experimental.tracing.server: true` but `Sentry.init()` still called from `hooks.server.ts` (the pre-instrumentation.server wiring), the SDK emits zero transaction/span envelopes. Errors still flow. Silent, and an easy trap for anyone following an older guide. - With kit tracing on, a route that 500s yields `status: "ok"` on the `http.server` span. `instrumentHandle` only calls `setHttpStatus` on the span it created itself; when `event.tracing.enabled` it reuses kit's root span and passes no span, so the status is never set (packages/sveltekit/src/server-common/handle.ts, `resolveWithSentry`). Also of note: `request.url` on captured events reads `https://127.0.0.1:41338/...` for a plain-HTTP adapter-node server on both runtimes. Packaging gap for other agents: `$REPRO/_toolbox/pack` was missing `@sentry/bundler-plugins`, `@sentry/browser-utils`, `@sentry/replay-internal`, `@sentry/replay-canvas` and `@sentry/feedback`, all of which `@sentry/sveltekit` needs. I packed them from the worktree; they are in `$REPRO/_toolbox/pack` now. Without the packed `browser-utils` the client build fails with a "Missing export getComponentName" from `@sentry/browser-utils` — registry 10.67.0 and develop 10.67.0 are not the same code. adapter-bun was not tried: adapter-node worked on bun on the first attempt, so a second adapter would only have added disk. `mysql` (v2) was not tried separately; mysql2 3.24.3 was enough to establish the channel-subscription failure, and the same subscriber path serves both. Cleanup: all servers and the sink killed, ports 41337-41346 free, `app/node_modules` removed (probe dir now 7.1 MB).

Astro on Bun M-astro-bun

Astro 7.3.1 with @astrojs/node 10.x standalone adapter, @sentry/astro 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) · bun 1.4.0 (darwin arm64), running the Node-adapter build output `dist/server/entry.mjs` · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Astro's Node standalone build runs on bun unchanged. Working wiring:

1. Packages (npm install, not `bun add` — bun cannot resolve the tarballs' transitive `@sentry/*@10.67.0`):
   npm install astro @astrojs/node mysql2
   npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-astro-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz \
               $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-browser-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz \
               $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz
   plus `$REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bundler-plugins-10.67.0.tgz` packed from the worktree — see notes, the npm-published 10.67.0 does not work with develop's core.

2. astro.config.mjs:
   import node from '@astrojs/node';
   import sentry from '@sentry/astro';
   export default defineConfig({
     output: 'server',
     adapter: node({ mode: 'standalone' }),
     integrations: [sentry({ sourcemaps: { disable: true }, enabled: { client: false, server: true } })],
     vite: { ssr: { noExternal: ['mysql2'] } },   // required for build-time db instrumentation
   });

3. sentry.server.config.mjs at the project root (the integration finds it by name and injects it):
   import * as Sentry from '@sentry/astro';
   if (!Sentry.isInitialized()) {
     Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static', sendDefaultPii: true });
   }

4. Build and run — the `--preload` is NOT optional (see notes: the integration only injects init into `.astro` page chunks, so an app whose first request hits an API route runs uninstrumented):
   npx astro build
   PORT=<port> HOST=127.0.0.1 bun --preload ./sentry.server.config.mjs dist/server/entry.mjs

The `isInitialized()` guard exists because the config is then evaluated twice (once preloaded, once inlined in the index page chunk).

Astro does not swallow it: it re-throws, returns HTTP 500 and its own [ERROR] logger prints it; the transaction is finished with status `internal_error`. traceLifecycle static; identical under stream.
route names✓ works`GET /users/42` produces `transaction: "GET /users/[id]"`, `source: "route"`, `http.route: "/users/[id]"` (Astro's own bracket param syntax, not `:id`). The span is created by the Astro middleware's `instrumentRequestStartHttpServerSpan`, not by @sentry/node's httpIntegration, so it is unaffected by bun's lack of OTel http instrumentation. Same result in both lifecycles; under stream the span envelope carries `sentry.segment.name.source: route`.

The middleware's `withIsolationScope` works on bun.

The exact same build run under `node --import ./sentry.server.config.mjs dist/server/entry.mjs` does produce `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41502/rec` and sends both headers, so this is a bun failure, not an Astro one: @sentry/node's NodeFetch integration relies on undici's `undici:request:*` diagnostics channels, which bun's native fetch does not publish. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. The diagnosis was right (bun's native fetch never publishes undici's `undici:request:*` channels, so @sentry/node's NodeFetch instrumentation is dead on bun), but the conclusion "no outgoing-fetch instrumentation on Astro+bun" is wrong: @sentry/bun ships a channel-free fetch integration (`fetchIntegration`, built on `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest`, i.e. a global `fetch` monkey-patch) that is exported from the package's main entry and can be added to an @sentry/astro server init. Adding it makes both the `http.client` span and the propagation headers appear.
