runtime (verified from the same build: bun -> 1 span, node -> 1 span, both with correct headers). SDK-side observation (not a blocker for users, worth a backlog item): @sentry/astro's server init always uses @sentry/node's default integration set, which contains only the undici-channel-based fetch instrumentation. Nothing in the SDK detects that it is running on bun and swaps in the bun-safe `fetchIntegration` the way `@sentry/bun`'s own `init()` does. Every framework SDK whose server half is @sentry/node (astro, nuxt, sveltekit, solidstart, react-router, remix, ...) will lose outgoing-fetch spans and trace propagation the moment its Node build is run on bun. A runtime check in the shared server default-integration list (`getDefaultIntegrations` / `@sentry/server-utils`) would fix all of them at once. It is node-only; no bun variant exists in the e2e matrix for any Node-adapter framework app. All started processes (sink 77188, recorder 77189, app 85307) were killed; ports 47311-47313 are free.
Workaround: In `sentry.server.config.mjs`, add @sentry/bun's `fetchIntegration` behind a bun check (install `@sentry/bun` alongside `@sentry/astro`; the guard is required, without it node builds emit two `http.client` spans per request): import * as Sentry from '@sentry/astro'; import { fetchIntegration as bunFetchIntegration } from '@sentry/bun'; const isBun = typeof globalThis.Bun !== 'undefined'; if (!Sentry.isInitialized()) { Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, integrations: isBun ? [bunFetchIntegration()] : [], }); } Then build and run as before: `npx astro build && bun --preload ./sentry.server.config.mjs dist/server/entry.mjs`. No change to astro.config.mjs, the adapter, the entry shape, or the trace lifecycle is needed, and the fix holds for both `traceLifecycle: 'static'` and the default `'stream'`.
db spans✓* works-waNo db span on bun in either mysql2 path. Instrumentation path used: the Astro integration's own `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` (Vite build-time channel injection) plus `vite.ssr.noExternal: ['mysql2']` — no Bun build plugin was needed or used, and the injection demonstrably worked (the built chunk contains `tr_ch_apm_tracingChannel("orchestrion:mysql2:query")` wrapping `BaseConnection.query`). With mysql2 3.19.1 (orchestrion range) Sentry subscribes to `orchestrion:mysql2:query` on bun (verified: `start.hasSubscribers = true`) yet the injected wrapper reads `hasSubscribers = false` from its own channel handle and never publishes; the identical dist run on node emits `db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 0` as a child span. With mysql2 3.24.3 (native `mysql2:*` channel range) Sentry never subscribes at all on bun (`mysql2:query -> false`) while node gives `true`, because `waitForTracingChannelBinding`'s single 1ms retry loses the race against init on bun. Module-scope `createConnection`; traceLifecycle static. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. db spans do work on bun 1.4.0 with Astro 7.3.1 + @astrojs/node standalone + @sentry/astro 10.67.0 (develop), on both trace lifecycles and on both mysql2 code paths, after adding four lines to `sentry.server.config.mjs`. The other agent's two diagnoses (an "injected wrapper reads its own hasSubscribers=false" mystery and a "waitForTracingChannelBinding 1ms race") are both symptoms of one Bun runtime bug that I isolated to a 12-line script. ROOT CAUSE (Bun, not the SDK, not Astro): Bun's `node:diagnostics_channel` registry does not keep a channel alive once it has subscribers. Node's registry does (its WeakReference map is incRef'd when a channel becomes active). On Bun, as soon as the *creator* of the handle drops it, the channel is collected and every subscriber is silently dropped; the next `tracingChannel(name)` call, from mysql2's `lib/tracing.js` or from the orchestrion-injected wrapper, gets a brand-new object with no subscribers. That is exactly why Sentry reads `hasSubscribers = true` and the wrapper reads `false`: two different channel objects for the same name. Minimal repro, $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-astro-bun-dbspans/weak1.mjs (A drops the handle, B keeps it on globalThis): == bun 1.4.0 == == node v26.5.0 == sync A: true B: true sync A: true B: true afterGC A: false B: true afterGC A: true B: true +200ms A: false B: true +200ms A: true B: true B fired A fired / B fired This also explains toolbox finding K11 ("a driver whose instrumented module first loads inside a request gets no spans on Bun") — under Astro the db page chunk loads on the first request, long after `Sentry.init()` in the preload, so a GC has always run in between. The 1ms `waitForTracingChannelBinding` retry is a red herring: my run showed `mysql2:query start.hasSubscribers` = true synchronously after init on bun and false at +0ms, i.e. Sentry does subscribe, then loses it. BASELINE (reproduces the report), `bun --preload ./sentry.server.config.mjs dist/server/entry.mjs`, traceLifecycle static, sink 53117 — 4 db routes, all empty: transaction | GET /db2 | [] transaction | GET /pool2 | [] transaction | GET /db1 | [] transaction | GET /pool1 | [] event | sentinel FIXED, same build, same bun, only the pin added (traceLifecycle static): transaction | GET /db2 | ['db mysql2.connect', 'db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > ?'] transaction | GET /pool2 | ['db mysql2.pool.connect', 'db mysql2.connect', 'db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > ?'] transaction | GET /db1 | ['db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 1'] transaction | GET /pool1 | ['db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 1'] FIXED with traceLifecycle 'stream' (the develop default), same pin: span | ['db mysql2.connect', 'db SELECT users', 'http.server GET /db2'] span | ['db mysql2.pool.connect', 'db mysql2.connect', 'db SELECT users', 'http.server GET /pool2'] span | ['db SELECT users', 'http.server GET /db1'] span | ['db SELECT users', 'http.server GET /pool1'] Both mysql2 ranges are covered by the one fix: /db2 and /pool2 use mysql2 3.24.3's native `mysql2:query|execute|connect|pool:connect` channels; /db1 and /pool1 use mysql@2.18.1 through the Astro integration's build-time `orchestrion:mysql:query` injection. So the orchestrion path the report tested with mysql2 3.19.1 is not separately broken — the same pin revives it. Variants tried: - Pin as a separate preload before init (`pinboot.mjs`) — works. - Pin inside `sentry.server.config.mjs` after `Sentry.init()` (`sentry.server.config.pin3.mjs`) — works, and this is the form I recommend (same file the Astro integration already injects, no extra preload entry needed beyond the `--preload` the app needs anyway). - Generic form, patching `tracingChannel`/`channel` on the CJS module object via `createRequire` to retain every channel ever created (`pinall2.mjs`) — works and needs no channel-name list; this is the shape an SDK-side fix would take. Patching the ESM namespace object instead throws `TypeError: Attempted to assign to readonly property` on bun, so `createRequire` is required for the generic form. - Importing the drivers before init (`dbboot.mjs`: `import 'mysql2'; import 'mysql'`) — PARTIAL: fixes mysql2 (its own module-scope consts then own the channels) but not mysql@2, whose channels exist only in the Astro-bundled, orchestrion-transformed copy. So "load your driver early" is not a sufficient instruction. - Node control with the same pin — unchanged, all db spans present. The pin is harmless on Node, so it can be applied unconditionally. - No `--preload` at all is still required to be avoided (the integration only inlines init into `.astro` page chunks); that is the other agent's separate finding and I did not re-derive it. - bun 1.3.14 (CI pin): not-run, `$SCRATCH/bun1314` no longer exists on this machine. SDK-side fix location: `packages/server-utils/src/tracing-channel.ts` `bindTracingChannelToSpan()` receives the `TracingChannel` object and subscribes to it but keeps no reference; pushing the channel into a module-level array there (or in `packages/core/src/asyncContext/tracing-channel-binding.ts`'s callers) would make every channel-based integration — mysql2, mysql, redis, knex, graphql, mongoose, vercel-ai, postgres, the AI providers — survive GC on Bun. The repo's own reference app `dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/astro-7` runs `node ./dist/server/entry.mjs` and never exercises bun, which is why this is uncovered. Files (rerunnable): $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-astro-bun-dbspans/ — `weak1.mjs` (runtime bug in isolation), `astro.config.mjs`, `sentry.server.config.mjs` (baseline), `sentry.server.config.pin3.mjs` (fix), `pinboot.mjs`, `pinall2.mjs`, `dbboot.mjs`, `src/pages/{db1.astro,db2.astro,pool1.ts,pool2.ts,sentinel.ts}`, `src/db-lib.ts`, logs `runA.log` (baseline) through `runG.log` (node control), `dist/` kept. `node_modules` removed; reinstall with `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{astro,browser,browser-utils,bundler-plugins,core,feedback,node,opentelemetry,replay,replay-canvas,server-runtime-injection,server-utils}-10.67.0.tgz astro@^7.3.1 @astrojs/node@^11.1.5 mysql2 mysql`, then `npx astro build`. Run: `PORT=<p> HOST=127.0.0.1 SENTRY_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:<sink>/ bun --preload ./sentry.server.config.pin3.mjs dist/server/entry.mjs`.
Workaround: Add a channel pin to `sentry.server.config.mjs` (works before or after `Sentry.init()`, harmless on Node), then run with `bun --preload ./sentry.server.config.mjs dist/server/entry.mjs`: import * as Sentry from '@sentry/astro'; import * as dc from 'node:diagnostics_channel'; if (!Sentry.isInitialized()) { Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }); } // Bun drops diagnostics_channel subscriptions at the next GC; holding the // channel objects keeps Sentry's subscriptions alive. globalThis.__sentryPinnedChannels ??= [ 'mysql2:query', 'mysql2:execute', 'mysql2:connect', 'mysql2:pool:connect', 'orchestrion:mysql:query', 'orchestrion:mysql2:query', 'orchestrion:mysql2:execute', ].map(name => dc.tracingChannel(name)); For a driver-agnostic version, retain every channel instead of listing names (must go in a file preloaded before `Sentry.init()`, and must patch the CJS module object — the ESM namespace is read-only on bun): import { createRequire } from 'node:module'; const dc = createRequire(import.meta.url)('node:diagnostics_channel'); const kept = (globalThis.__keptChannels = []); const [oc, ot] = [dc.channel, dc.tracingChannel]; dc.channel = n => { const c = oc(n); kept.push(c); return c; }; dc.tracingChannel = n => { const t = ot(n); kept.push(t); return t; }; await import('./sentry.server.config.mjs');

Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions Astro on bun. `grep -rni bun docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/` returns nothing (the guide is only index.mdx plus profiling/), and `grep -rni astro docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/` returns nothing. The closest statement is the runtime alert at docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/index.mdx:21-28: "This SDK currently only works on Node runtimes, such as Node adapter or Vercel with Lambda functions. If you use Cloudflare Workers or Cloudflare Pages, refer to our Astro on Cloudflare guide. Other non-Node runtimes, like Vercel's Edge runtime, are currently not supported." The page's `categories` front matter (index.mdx:5-9) is `javascript, browser, server, server-node`. Bun is not named as either supported or unsupported, so a reader gets no answer either way.

Documented: wrong

The runtime alert tells a reader that a non-Node runtime is unsupported, but Astro 7.3.1's `@astrojs/node` standalone build (`dist/server/entry.mjs`) runs on Bun 1.4.0 with `@sentry/astro` and delivers working errors, route names, request isolation, incoming trace continuation and logs. The alert must be amended to name Bun explicitly as working on the Node adapter output, and the page must state the two caveats observed. Outgoing `fetch` is not instrumented under Bun, because `@sentry/node`'s HTTP integration listens on undici's `undici:request:*` diagnostics channels and Bun's native fetch does not publish them — install `@sentry/bun` and add its `fetchIntegration()` to `sentry.server.config.mjs`, guarded on `typeof globalThis.Bun !== 'undefined'` so Node deployments of the same build do not double-span. Database spans are dropped because Bun holds diagnostics channels weakly and a channel with subscribers is not kept alive, so every subscription made at `Sentry.init()` is lost on the next tick — until this is fixed in the SDK, keep the channels reachable by storing them on `globalThis` after `Sentry.init()` (`orchestrion:mysql2:query`, `orchestrion:mysql2:execute`, `orchestrion:mysql:query`, `mysql2:query`, `mysql2:execute`, ...).

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/index.mdx:21-28 — amend the runtime alert to name Bun, and add a "Running on Bun" section covering the fetch integration and the diagnostics-channel pinning

~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/index.mdx:21-28 ("This SDK currently only works on Node runtimes, such as Node adapter or Vercel with Lambda functions... Other non-Node runtimes, like Vercel's Edge runtime, are currently **not supported**."); astro/index.mdx:4 (`sdk: sentry.javascript.astro`). `grep -rni bun` over guides/astro/ and `grep -rni astro` over guides/bun/ both return nothing.

Five things a docs page would have to say, none of which any page says today. 1. `@sentry/bundler-plugins` must come from the same build as the rest. Installing the develop tarballs alongside the npm-published `@sentry/bundler-plugins@10.67.0` makes `npx astro build` die before it does anything: "The requested module '@sentry/core' does not provide an export named 'ServerRuntimeClient'". The published build imports `ServerRuntimeClient` from `@sentry/core`; develop moved it to `@sentry/core/server` (worktree packages/bundler-plugins/build/esm/core/sentry/telemetry.js:2 already uses the new path). Packing it from the worktree fixes it. This is a develop-vs-npm skew, not a bun issue, but it blocks any Astro probe. 2. `bun --preload ./sentry.server.config.mjs` is mandatory, and that is a real gap rather than a bun quirk. The integration injects the server init with `injectScript('page-ssr', ...)`, which lands only in `.astro` page modules — after `astro build`, `grep -rln "Sentry.init" dist/server/chunks/*.mjs` matches exactly one file, the `index.astro` chunk. Astro loads page chunks lazily, so a deployment whose traffic starts on an API route (`src/pages/*.ts`) runs completely uninstrumented until someone renders an `.astro` page: my first run sent zero envelopes for `/boom`, `/users/42` and `/sentinel`, then started working the moment I requested `/`. `--preload` (or `node --import`) closes it, at the cost of the config being evaluated twice, hence the `isInitialized()` guard. 3. Astro's own middleware is what makes this runtime usable at all. Errors, route-parametrised transaction names, isolation and incoming-trace continuation all come from `@sentry/astro/middleware`, which builds the `http.server` span itself when it does not find one. None of them go through @sentry/node's OTel http instrumentation, which is why they survive on bun while everything that *does* depend on runtime hooks (fetch, db) dies. 4. Two independent bun defects sink db spans, and they are worth filing separately. - mysql2 >= 3.20.0 (native `mysql2:*` channels): Sentry never subscribes on bun. `Mysql2Integration.setupOnce` calls `waitForTracingChannelBinding`, whose only retry is a single `setTimeout(..., 1)`. On bun that timer fires before the async-context strategy is registered and the code gives up (`fired count: 0`); on node the same timer lands after init (`fired at 188 ms`) and it works. Unref'd timers do fire on bun, so this is an ordering race, not a timer bug — raising the retry count or retrying until the client is ready would fix it. - mysql2 < 3.20.0 (orchestrion build-time injection): the Vite plugin injects correctly and Sentry subscribes (`start.hasSubscribers = true` read from a preloaded module in the running app), yet the injected wrapper inside the bundled chunk reads `false` from its own `tracingChannel` handle and skips the publish. I could not reduce this: a minimal `createRequire('diagnostics_channel').tracingChannel(...)` in a dynamically imported chunk (mini/main.mjs) works fine on bun, and identity checks inside the real chunk gave contradictory answers between two patched copies of the same file. The observable fact is solid, though: the identical `dist/` emits `db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 0` under node and nothing under bun. 5. Two smaller things. `vite.ssr.noExternal: ['mysql2']` is required — the Node adapter externalises node_modules by default, and the orchestrion plugin can only transform what Vite bundles; no Bun build plugin was involved. And a connection pool is not enough: mysql2's `lib/base/pool.js:183` calls `conn.query(cmdQuery)` with no trailing callback, and orchestrion's `Callback` wrapper passes such calls through untraced, so the probe uses a module-scope `createConnection` (I did not separately confirm the pool gap on node). Cosmetic noise seen on bun that is probably worth a look: `Sentry Logger [error]: Failed to read file: native` / `Could not find line 2 in file native`, from ContextLines trying to open bun's synthetic `native:7:39` stack frame, once per captured event. Astro 7 builds through rolldown-vite; the orchestrion Vite plugin handled it without complaint. Runtime context reported as `"runtime":"node"` — bun is not distinguished, which will make these events hard to find in an issue stream. Environment notes: npm blocked the `esbuild`, `fsevents` and `@sentry/cli` postinstall scripts; esbuild's native binary was present anyway and sourcemap upload was disabled, so neither mattered. Port 41337 was taken by another agent mid-run, hence the switch to 52341. All processes were killed and node_modules removed (242M).

Setup the docs would have to show

Viable, but NOT with the stock template — one file has to be rewritten for Bun.

1. Scaffold: `npx create-react-router@latest ./app --template remix-run/react-router-templates/node-custom-server --no-git-init --no-install --yes` (React Router 8, Express 5, `server.js`).
2. `npm install` (base deps), then install the develop SDK from tarballs — all @sentry/* on one command line so npm resolves the 10.67.0 transitive pins:
   `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-react-router-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-browser-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-react-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bundler-plugins-10.67.0.tgz mysql2`
   NOTE: `@sentry/bundler-plugins@10.67.0` is a dependency of `@sentry/react-router` and was NOT in $REPRO/_toolbox/pack; I packed it from the worktree (`cd $W/packages/bundler-plugins && npm pack --pack-destination $REPRO/_toolbox/pack`). Without it npm cannot install @sentry/react-router at all.
3. REQUIRED Bun workaround: `npx react-router reveal`, then rewrite `app/entry.server.tsx` to use `renderToReadableStream` instead of `renderToPipeableStream`. Bun resolves `react-dom/server` to `server.bun.js`, which exports only ["default","renderToReadableStream","renderToStaticMarkup","renderToString","resume","version"]. This also means `Sentry.createSentryHandleRequest({ renderToPipeableStream, createReadableStreamFromReadable, ... })` — the wiring the React Router docs and the react-router-8-framework e2e app show — CANNOT be used on Bun. The only usable server entry API is `Sentry.wrapSentryHandleRequest(myHandler)` plus `export const handleError = Sentry.createSentryHandleError({ logErrors: true })`.
4. `instrument.server.mjs`: `Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' })` from `@sentry/react-router`.
5. `server.js`: `import "./instrument.server.mjs";` as the very first line (Bun has no `--import` ESM loader), then the stock Express server, then `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler(app)`.
6. `vite.config.ts`: add `sentryReactRouter({ sourcemaps: { disable: true } }, config)` after `reactRouter()`.
7. Build with node (`npx react-router build`), run with `PORT=<port> bun server.js`.

That setup boots and serves 200s. It records errors and logs. It records NO spans of any kind and has NO request isolation — see capabilities.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksAn error thrown in a `/users/:id` loader reaches Sentry as an unhandled event with `mechanism.type: "react-router"`, `handled: false`, stack frames with context lines, sdk `sentry.javascript.react-router`. React Router does not swallow it: it also lands in the app log and the request returns 500. The mechanism comes from `Sentry.createSentryHandleError` exported as `handleError` from entry.server; `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler` never sees it because React Router turns loader throws into a 500 response. The event carries NO `transaction`, no request context and no per-request trace id.
route names✓* works-waNo server transaction or span envelope is produced at all on Bun, in either lifecycle, so there is no name to inspect. The error event for `GET /users/1?mode=error` also has `transaction: undefined` — `wrapSentryHandleRequest`/`updateRootSpanWithRoute` both bail out because `getActiveSpan()` returns undefined. In the loader `Sentry.getActiveSpan()` is null on every request. Root cause: @sentry/node on develop logs `No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping.` then `No diagnostics-channel injection detected. Channel-based integrations will not record spans.`; node:http is a builtin so neither the Vite/orchestrion plugin nor sentryBunPlugin can inject into it. Identical with traceLifecycle 'static' and 'stream'. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. React Router 8 framework mode on Bun 1.4.0 with @sentry/react-router 10.67.0 (develop) does produce server transactions/spans with parameterized route names, in BOTH lifecycles. The prior probe's app was missing one line of the documented wiring. THE ONE CHANGE (in `app/entry.server.tsx`): `export const instrumentations = [Sentry.createSentryServerInstrumentation()];` That is React Router 8's own `instrumentations` export. The SDK's `createSentryServerInstrumentation()` (packages/react-router/src/server/createServerInstrumentation.ts:55) is called directly by React Router, so it needs no diagnostics-channel injection and no node:http patching. Its `request` hook explicitly handles the "no existing root span" case (`if (existingRootSpan) { updateSpanName(...) } else { await startSpan({ name: unparameterizedName, ... }) }`), i.e. it starts the HTTP server span itself when @sentry/node has not created one. That is exactly the Bun situation. The `No diagnostics-channel injection detected` warning is real and unchanged, and is irrelevant to this capability. EVIDENCE, bun 1.4.0, traceLifecycle 'static' ($REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-reactrouter-bun-routenames/v2-items-bun-static.json, verbatim, trimmed): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.react-router","spans":["function /users/:id"]} {"type":"event","exception":"Error: loader boom on bun","mechanism":"react_router.loader","handled":false,"transaction":"GET /users/:id"} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["function /"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /flush","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["function /flush"]} EVIDENCE, bun 1.4.0, traceLifecycle 'stream' (v2-items-bun-stream.json, span envelope raw entries): {"name":"GET /users/:id","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.react_router.instrumentation_api"} {"name":"/users/:id","status":"ok","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.function.react_router.instrumentation_api"} {"name":"GET /","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.react_router.instrumentation_api"} {"name":"GET /flush","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.react_router.instrumentation_api"} Each specific sub-claim of the report is refuted: - "No server transaction or span envelope is produced at all on Bun, in either lifecycle" — false, see both blocks above. - "The error event for GET /users/1?mode=error has transaction: undefined" — false, it is `"transaction":"GET /users/:id"`, and the mechanism sharpens from `react-router` to `react_router.loader`. - "In the loader Sentry.getActiveSpan() is null on every request" — false. The loader probe (`app/app/routes/users.tsx` renders `Sentry.getActiveSpan()`) prints `SPAN[desc=none op=none root=none]` instead of `NO-ACTIVE-SPAN`; the span exists, its name is simply not assigned until React Router matches the route. - "Identical with traceLifecycle 'static' and 'stream'" — true only in the sense that both now work. MINIMALITY: `wrapSentryHandleRequest` is NOT needed for route names. With `export default handleRequest;` (unwrapped) and only the `instrumentations` export, names are still `GET /users/:id` / source `route` (v2-items-bun-static-nowrap.json). The Sentry Vite plugin is not needed either — this app's vite.config.ts has only `tailwindcss()` and `reactRouter()`. NO NODE REGRESSION: same build under `node` gives one transaction per request, `GET /users/:id`, source `route`, plus the Express middleware spans (v2-items-node-static.json). Adding the export does not double-instrument. The report's Bun-specific setup facts hold and are NOT refuted: the stock template's `renderToPipeableStream` entry cannot run on Bun (`react-dom/server` resolves to `server.bun.js`), so the entry must be rewritten to `renderToReadableStream`, and `Sentry.createSentryHandleRequest({ renderToPipeableStream, createReadableStreamFromReadable })` — the wiring the docs and the repo e2e app `react-router-8-framework` show — is unusable on Bun. The refutation is that this does not cost you route names, because the `instrumentations` export is an independent, runtime-agnostic path. REMAINING (separate capabilities, not route names): on Bun every request in a run shares one trace_id (`88278811acb34c09a0409425f8dd2d43` for all 7 items) while node gives 5 distinct ones — request isolation is still broken; the error request's transaction is `status:"ok"` on Bun vs `internal_error` on node; and `request`/`user.ip_address` are absent from Bun events. Workaround: Add `export const instrumentations = [Sentry.createSentryServerInstrumentation()];` to `app/entry.server.tsx`. This is the whole fix; it is documented (sentry-docs manual-setup.mdx:286) but was omitted in the probe app. On Bun it is not optional the way it is on Node: it is the only source of server spans, because @sentry/node cannot inject into node:http there. The entry still has to use `renderToReadableStream` on Bun, and `Sentry.createSentryHandleRequest({ renderToPipeableStream, createReadableStreamFromReadable })` still cannot be used — neither of which matters for route names once the `instrumentations` export is present. `Sentry.wrapSentryHandleRequest` is optional for this capability.
isolation✓* works-waBadly broken, and the most serious finding. Three concurrent `/users/:id?mode=isolation&tag=...` requests (delays 300/150/50 ms) each called `Sentry.setTag` then `captureException`. All three events, plus a sentinel captured afterwards, carry `probe_tag: "charlie"` (last writer wins) and all four share one trace id `75b8f65c357d4cafa81856d25173c558`, the process-lifetime propagation context that stayed identical across every request in the run. There is no per-request isolation scope because there is no http server instrumentation to fork one, so tags from one user's request leak into every other user's events. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. The leak is real with the reported wiring, but it is a one-line fix, and the SDK already ships the integration that fixes it. ROOT CAUSE (proved directly, not theorised): the Node SDK's per-request isolation scope is forked by the subscriber to the Node **core** diagnostics channel `http.server.request.start` (packages/core/src/integrations/http/server-subscription.ts:132-175 `getIsolationScope().clone()` … `withIsolationScope(...)`, subscribed in packages/node/src/integrations/http/httpServerIntegration.ts:146). This channel is published by Node itself, not by the orchestrion/`--import` injection, so the "no diagnostics-channel injection" warning is a red herring here. Bun simply never publishes it. Direct probe ($REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-reactrouter-bun-isolation/run2/dc.mjs, subscribe + one request to a `node:http` server): bun 1.4.0 -> {"runtime":"bun","seen":[]} node v26.5.0 -> {"runtime":"node","seen":["http.server.request.start","http.server.response.finish"]} `@sentry/react-router` never forks an isolation scope itself (wrapSentryHandleRequest and createSentryServerInstrumentation only rename the root span), so with no channel there is no request boundary at all. BASELINE (reproduced, bun 1.4.0, traceLifecycle 'static', three concurrent /users/:id?mode=isolation with delays 300/150/50 plus a sentinel) — run2/drive-A.out + sink: {"tag":"alpha", "loader":{"tag":"alpha","isolationTagAfterWait":"bravo","traceId":"047d9e55bdbc455f9dbc2f1a4e596f44"}} {"tag":"bravo", "loader":{"tag":"bravo","isolationTagAfterWait":"bravo","traceId":"047d9e55bdbc455f9dbc2f1a4e596f44"}} {"tag":"charlie","loader":{"tag":"charlie","isolationTagAfterWait":"bravo","traceId":"047d9e55bdbc455f9dbc2f1a4e596f44"}} {"type":"event","exception":"isolation probe charlie","tags":{"probe_tag":"bravo"},"user":{"id":"user-bravo"},"trace_id":"047d9e55bdbc455f9dbc2f1a4e596f44"} {"type":"event","exception":"isolation probe alpha","tags":{"probe_tag":"bravo"},"user":{"id":"user-bravo"},"trace_id":"047d9e55bdbc455f9dbc2f1a4e596f44"} {"type":"event","message":"sentinel","tags":{"probe_tag":"bravo"},"user":{"id":"user-bravo"},"trace_id":"047d9e55bdbc455f9dbc2f1a4e596f44"} (last writer wins, one process-lifetime trace — matches the report; the winning tag is just race-dependent.) FIX (run2/drive-B.out, traceLifecycle 'static'): each request gets its own isolation scope, its own tag/user, its own trace id, AND a route-named `http.server` transaction: {"type":"event","exception":"isolation probe charlie","tags":{"probe_tag":"charlie"},"user":{"id":"user-charlie","ip_address":"::ffff:127.0.0.1"},"transaction":"GET /users/3","trace_id":"6eb5d85d678c4ee9a325e6f165090b89"} {"type":"event","exception":"isolation probe bravo","tags":{"probe_tag":"bravo"},"user":{"id":"user-bravo",...},"transaction":"GET /users/2","trace_id":"f2adafbe160d488c93e8519d756825f2"} {"type":"event","exception":"isolation probe alpha","tags":{"probe_tag":"alpha"},"user":{"id":"user-alpha",...},"transaction":"GET /users/1","trace_id":"8391582d09234f919951cf44c74d4200"} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","route":"/users/:id","tags":{"probe_tag":"alpha"},"trace_id":"8391582d09234f919951cf44c74d4200","spans":["middleware <anonymous>"]} {"type":"event","message":"sentinel","tags":{"runtime":"node"},"transaction":"GET /flush","trace_id":"3d48ec63ebd64a07ac6c391b87f21eb9"} <- no leaked probe_tag Four distinct trace ids, no cross-request tag/user bleed. Same result on the default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` (run2/drive-C.out): three distinct trace ids, per-request tags, and `span` envelopes "http.server GET /users/:id trace=<per-request id>". So this also refutes the "records NO spans of any kind" line in the setup summary: the missing http server instrumentation was the cause of both. SECOND, DEPENDENCY-FREE WORKAROUND (run2/drive-D.out): an Express middleware `app.use((req,res,next) => Sentry.withIsolationScope(() => { Sentry.getCurrentScope().setPropagationContext({ traceId: crypto.randomUUID().replace(/-/g,''), sampleRand: Math.random() }); next(); }))` also isolates correctly (per-request tags, distinct trace ids), proving AsyncLocalStorage itself is healthy on Bun. But it yields no transactions, no route names and no request data, so it is strictly worse than the integration. Prior art in this repo: dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/nextjs-16-bun/sentry.server.config.ts:1,16 already does exactly this (`bunHttpServerIntegration({ spans: false })`) for the same reason. There is no react-router-on-Bun e2e app, so nothing carried the pattern over. The integration's own JSDoc (packages/bun/src/integrations/bunHttpServer.ts:86-101) describes this precise failure mode. Workaround: Install `@sentry/bun` alongside `@sentry/react-router` and add its `bunHttpServerIntegration()` to the server-side `Sentry.init`, in `instrument.server.mjs`: import * as Sentry from '@sentry/react-router'; import { bunHttpServerIntegration } from '@sentry/bun'; Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, integrations: [bunHttpServerIntegration()], }); Nothing else changes: same `server.js`, same `wrapSentryHandleRequest` entry, works with both `traceLifecycle: 'static'` and the default `'stream'`. It patches `http.Server.prototype.emit` and hands each server to the same core instrumentation the Node SDK gets from the `http.server.request.start` channel, so it restores per-request isolation scopes, per-request trace ids, request data on events, and route-named `http.server` transactions in one step. Pass `{ spans: false }` only when another layer already emits incoming-request spans (as nextjs-16-bun does); for a custom Express/React Router server leave spans on. If adding a second SDK package is unacceptable, an Express middleware wrapping `next()` in `Sentry.withIsolationScope` plus a fresh `setPropagationContext` isolates tags and traces too, but produces no transactions, route names or request data.

EXACT CHANGE (instrument.server.mjs), plus `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bun-10.67.0.tgz` (same version as the rest): import * as Sentry from '@sentry/react-router'; import { bunHttpServerIntegration } from '@sentry/bun'; Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static', integrations: [bunHttpServerIntegration()], }); ROOT CAUSE (proved directly, verify4-.../dc-probe.mjs — same script under both runtimes): --- node: CHANNELS_SEEN=["server.request.start","server.response.finish"] --- bun 1.4.0: CHANNELS_SEEN=[] Bun's `node:http` never publishes the built-in `http.server.request.start` diagnostics channel that `@sentry/node`'s `httpServerIntegration` subscribes to (packages/node/src/integrations/http/httpServerIntegration.ts:1 `subscribe` from node:diagnostics_channel; the listener that does `continueTrace` + `withIsolationScope` lives in packages/core/src/integrations/http/server-subscription.ts). Nothing else in the React Router server path continues the trace: `wrapSentryHandleRequest` only renames the root span, and `createSentryServerInstrumentation` (the RR8 instrumentation API) calls `startSpan` on the *process-wide* propagation context when no root span exists. `@sentry/bun` already ships the missing piece — `bunHttpServerIntegration()` (packages/bun/src/integrations/bunHttpServer.ts) patches `http.Server.prototype.emit` and hands the server to core's `instrumentServer`, exactly the path the node SDK gets from the channel. It is in @sentry/bun's default integrations but NOT in the react-router/node ones, and it works fine on a NodeClient. CAVEAT: @sentry/bun must resolve to the same @sentry/core instance/version as @sentry/react-router (10.67.0 here); a duplicated core would break the patch silently.
Workaround: Install `@sentry/bun` at the same version and add `bunHttpServerIntegration()` from it to the `@sentry/react-router` `Sentry.init()` in the server instrument file. This restores incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation, per-request isolation scopes, request data and request sessions on Bun. If pulling in @sentry/bun is undesirable, the same effect can be had in userland by patching `http.Server.prototype.emit` and calling the `http.server.request.start` listener returned by `getHttpServerSubscriptions()` from `@sentry/core/server` (that is literally what bunHttpServerIntegration does).
outgoing fetch✓* works-waA `fetch()` from inside the loader to a local recorder produced no `http.client` span and no propagation headers. The recorder echoed exactly `{"connection":"keep-alive","user-agent":"Bun/1.4.0","accept":"*/*","host":"127.0.0.1:52817","accept-encoding":"gzip, deflate, br, zstd"}` — no sentry-trace, no baggage. The NodeFetch integration installs but does nothing on Bun. This differs from @sentry/bun, which does instrument fetch; @sentry/react-router pulls in @sentry/node instead. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. The default `@sentry/react-router` init on Bun really does nothing for outgoing fetch (the report is right about the default), but one added integration fixes it completely, no bundler and no code change in the loader. EXACT CHANGE, in `instrument.server.mjs`: import * as Sentry from "@sentry/react-router"; import { fetchIntegration, bunHttpServerIntegration } from "@sentry/bun"; Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, integrations: process.versions.bun ? [fetchIntegration(), bunHttpServerIntegration()] : [], }); plus `@sentry/bun@10.67.0` in the install line (`$REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bun-10.67.0.tgz`). `fetchIntegration()` alone is enough for the capability under test; `bunHttpServerIntegration()` additionally supplies the incoming-request span and per-request isolation that the report also found missing. Why the default fails: `nativeNodeFetchIntegration` (packages/node/src/integrations/node-fetch/index.ts) calls `instrumentUndici()`, which is undici-diagnostics-channel based; Bun implements no such channel, hence the `No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks` warning. `@sentry/bun`'s `fetchIntegration` (packages/bun/src/integrations/fetch.ts) instead wraps global `fetch` via core's `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest`, which works on Bun. It is a plain `defineIntegration` over `@sentry/core` primitives, so it composes with a `@sentry/react-router` client with no dual-core problem (npm dedupes both to one `@sentry/core` 10.67.0). Workaround: Install `@sentry/bun` alongside `@sentry/react-router` and add its integrations in `instrument.server.mjs`, gated on Bun: `integrations: process.versions.bun ? [fetchIntegration(), bunHttpServerIntegration()] : []` (both imported from `@sentry/bun`). `fetchIntegration()` restores `http.client` spans and `sentry-trace`/`baggage` on outgoing `fetch`; `bunHttpServerIntegration()` adds the `http.server GET /route` parent span and per-request isolation. React Router 8 (framework mode, Express custom server) on bun 1.4.0 with @sentry/react-router 10.67.0 (develop) DOES emit `db` spans, nested under a route-named `http.server` root span. The reported failure has two independent causes, neither of which is a missing instrumentation path. Cause 1 (the db spans): mysql2 >= 3.20.0 (I installed 3.24.3) publishes its OWN `node:diagnostics_channel` tracing channels (`mysql2:query`, `mysql2:execute`, `mysql2:connect`, `mysql2:pool:connect`) — see packages/server-utils/src/integrations/mysql2/mysql2-dc-subscriber.ts:20-23 and index.ts:68-71 ("mysql2 >= 3.20.0 ... which the transform intentionally leaves alone"). So NO orchestrion injection, NO `ssr.noExternal: ["mysql2"]`, NO `Bun.build` + `sentryBunPlugin` is needed at all — the whole `orchestrion:mysql2:*` chase in the original probe was the wrong path for this mysql2 version. What actually breaks it is that Bun's `node:diagnostics_channel` keeps channel objects WEAKLY: the SDK subscribes at `Sentry.init()` time and then drops its reference, the channel object is collected, and when mysql2 later loads it creates a fresh channel with no subscribers. Holding any reference to those channels past init fixes it. (Same root cause the nextjs/sveltekit bun probes found — $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-nextjs-bun-dbspans/REPRO.md, $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-sveltekit-bun-dbspans/RERUN.md.) Cause 2 (the missing root span): the probe's `app/entry.server.tsx` never exported `instrumentations`. Adding `export const instrumentations = [Sentry.createSentryServerInstrumentation()]` produces the `GET /users/:id` root span on Bun with no other change (`bunHttpServerIntegration()` also produces one, but is not required — run F below had it disabled). A/B on one build, one binary (bun 1.4.0), one sink: CONTROL (no keepalive, 4 requests over 12 s) — runH-control-soak.log: 0 db spans: ["function /users/:id"] 0 db spans: ["function /users/:id"] 0 db spans: ["function /users/:id"] 0 db spans: ["function /users/:id"] FIX A — `await import("mysql2/promise")` in instrument.server.mjs (runC): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.react-router","spans":["function /users/:id","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?","db mysql2.pool.connect","db SELECT name FROM users"]} FIX B — explicit channel pin `globalThis.__sentryKeptChannels = ["mysql2:query","mysql2:execute","mysql2:connect","mysql2:pool:connect"].map(n => dc.tracingChannel(n))` (runB): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["function /users/:id","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?","db mysql2.pool.connect","db SELECT name FROM users"]} Import order is irrelevant — `import "mysql2/promise"` BEFORE `Sentry.init()` works identically (runJ, same span list). traceLifecycle `stream` (the develop default) works too, with low-cardinality names (runD): {"type":"span","items":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users","db mysql2.pool.connect","db SELECT users","function /users/:id","http.server GET /users/:id"]} Without `bunHttpServerIntegration()` (runF, `instrumentations` export only) — root span still present, db spans still present: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","spans":["function /users/:id","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?","db mysql2.pool.connect","db SELECT name FROM users"]} Stability: 6 requests over 24 s all carried 4-5 db spans (runG-soak) — not a warm-up artifact. Node control on the exact same build, no keepalive, no pin (runI): db spans present, so this is Bun-specific, not a React Router or SDK wiring defect. Not covered: bun 1.3.14. `$SCRATCH/bun1314/` no longer exists on this machine (`no such file or directory`), so the CI-pin cross-check could not be rerun; the sibling nextjs/sveltekit probes report the same GC behavior on 1.3.14. Rerun (all absolute paths under S=$SCRATCH): V=$REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-reactrouter-bun-dbspans-v2 # my dir; app copied from $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-reactrouter-bun-incomingtrace/app, then `npm install mysql2` PORT=51733 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs > $V/sink.log 2>&1 & cd $V/app && npx react-router build PORT=51742 SENTRY_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:51733/ bun server.js # control: 0 db spans PORT=51737 SENTRY_KEEPALIVE=driver SENTRY_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:51733/ bun server.js # fix A: db spans PORT=51736 SENTRY_PIN=1 SENTRY_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:51733/ bun server.js # fix B: db spans curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/users/1?mode=db"; curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/flush"; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:51733/__items Files: $V/app/instrument.server.mjs (init + both toggles, SENTRY_PIN / SENTRY_KEEPALIVE), $V/app/instrument.pre.mjs + $V/app/server.pre.js (import-before-init variant), $V/app/app/db.server.ts (module-scope mysql2 pool, 127.0.0.1:3307), $V/app/app/routes/users.tsx (`?mode=db`), $V/app/app/entry.server.tsx (Bun-compatible renderToReadableStream + wrapSentryHandleRequest + createSentryHandleError + `export const instrumentations`), logs runA..runJ in $V/. Reference e2e app ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/react-router-8-framework uses `Sentry.createSentryHandleRequest({ renderToPipeableStream, createReadableStreamFromReadable, ServerRouter })` and does NOT export `instrumentations`; that wiring is unusable on Bun (react-dom/server.bun.js has no renderToPipeableStream), so the repo has no Bun-shaped reference for this framework.
Workaround: Keep a reference to the diagnostics channels alive past `Sentry.init()`. Easiest: add `import "mysql2/promise";` (or whatever DB driver the app uses) to the file that calls `Sentry.init()` — either order relative to `init()` works. Equivalent explicit form: `import * as dc from "node:diagnostics_channel"; globalThis.__sentryKeptChannels = ["mysql2:query","mysql2:execute","mysql2:connect","mysql2:pool:connect"].map(n => dc.tracingChannel(n));` after `Sentry.init()`. Separately, for a route-named `http.server` root span on Bun, export `const instrumentations = [Sentry.createSentryServerInstrumentation()]` from `app/entry.server.tsx` (or add `bunHttpServerIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun` to `integrations`). Neither `ssr.noExternal` nor `Bun.build` + `sentryBunPlugin` is needed for mysql2 >= 3.20.0.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info('probe log from loader', { id })` inside the loader arrives as a `log` envelope after the ~7s flush timer: `info: probe log from loader`. Its trace_id is the process-wide propagation-context id (`77a8afb086af461b90fa06d4ab8b864f`), not a per-request one, so logs from concurrent requests are not separable by trace.

Docs today

No page mentions the combination. `~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/` contains only `index.mdx`, `manual-setup.mdx` and `profiling/`; `grep -rin "bun" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/` returns nothing, and `grep -rin "react.router" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/` returns nothing. The React Router guide declares `categories: [javascript, browser, server, server-node]` (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/index.mdx:5-9) and says at docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/index.mdx:156 "The wizard also creates a server configuration file for Node.js runtime." The Bun guide (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx) names no frameworks at all. So the docs neither claim nor deny Bun support for React Router; a reader following either guide lands in the broken state described above.

Documented: no

A page must say React Router 8 framework mode with a custom Express/Node server runs on Bun 1.4.0 but that the stock `node-custom-server` template's `server.js` has to be rewritten for Bun, and must state plainly that `@sentry/react-router` is inert on Bun on its own: only errors and logs arrive; there are no route names, no per-request isolation, no incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation, no outgoing `fetch` spans, and no database spans (child spans are additionally suppressed by `requiresParentSpan` once no request span exists). The cause and fix must both be documented: Bun's `node:http` does not emit the `http.server.request.start` diagnostics channel the Node SDK opens the request span from, so install `@sentry/bun` at the same version (deduped to one `@sentry/core`) and pass `integrations: [fetchIntegration(), bunHttpServerIntegration()]` from it to the `Sentry.init` in the instrumentation file imported as the very first line of `server.js`, and import your database driver at startup. The Node-only start commands at manual-setup.mdx:413-414 need a documented Bun equivalent.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/react-router.mdx (new)

~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/index.mdx:5-9 (`categories: [javascript, browser, server, server-node]`); ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/manual-setup.mdx:413-414 (`NODE_OPTIONS='--import ./instrument.server.mjs' react-router dev` / `... react-router-serve ./build/server/index.js`); manual-setup.mdx:449 ("automatic instrumentation will be incomplete" warning for the direct-import fallback). `grep -rin bun` over guides/react-router/ and `grep -rin react.router` over guides/bun/ both return nothing.

What a docs page would have to say, if one existed: 1. The stock React Router node template does not run on Bun at all, Sentry aside. `react-dom/server` resolves to `server.bun.js`, which has no `renderToPipeableStream`. The user must rewrite `app/entry.server.tsx` around `renderToReadableStream`. That is a React Router/Bun issue, not a Sentry one, but it has a Sentry consequence: `Sentry.createSentryHandleRequest` takes `renderToPipeableStream` as a required option, so the canonical Sentry wiring (docs and the react-router-8-framework e2e app) is unusable on Bun. Only `Sentry.wrapSentryHandleRequest` works. 2. `@sentry/bundler-plugins@10.67.0` is a runtime dependency of `@sentry/react-router` and is not in $REPRO/_toolbox/pack, so it must be packed from the worktree before anything installs. Worth flagging for whoever maintains the pack directory. 3. The substantive finding: on the develop (v11) line `@sentry/node` has dropped the OTel SDK and takes all of its instrumentation from diagnostics channels registered by `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` (its only remaining OTel dep is `@opentelemetry/api`). The registration API (module.registerHooks / the `--import` loader) does not exist on Bun, so the SDK logs `No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping.` and node:http is never patched. With no `http.server` root span there is no request-scoped isolation scope, and that cascades into every other capability: no transactions, no route names, no trace continuation, no fetch propagation, no db spans, cross-request tag leakage, and one process-lifetime trace id shared by every event and log. 4. Build-time injection does not rescue it. I confirmed the Vite/orchestrion plugin really does inject `orchestrion:mysql2:query` into the bundled driver, and that `Bun.build` + `sentryBunPlugin()` really does inject `orchestrion:router:handle` into the bundled Express and silences the `No diagnostics-channel injection detected` warning — and still no span is emitted, on bun 1.4.0 and on the CI pin 1.3.14. This is consistent with and extends the established K11 finding: on Bun the injected channels do not fire even for a module-scope driver loaded at startup. And because the missing root span comes from node:http, a builtin nothing can rewrite, no amount of bundling can fix the server side. 5. Practical consequence: React Router on Bun with @sentry/react-router today is an error-and-log-only SDK with a correctness hazard (tag and trace leakage across concurrent requests). Supporting the combination needs either a Bun-native http server instrumentation in @sentry/node (or a Bun.serve adapter like @sentry/bun's), or an explicit docs statement that the React Router server SDK requires Node. 6. `traceLifecycle` made no difference: I ran both 'static' and 'stream' and got zero span/transaction envelopes either way, so every result above is lifecycle-independent. Bun reports `process.version` as v26.3.0 (1.4.0) / v24.3.0 (1.3.14), and the SDK's `runtime` context plus its own `runtime: node` tag both say node, so events sent from Bun are indistinguishable from Node events in Sentry. Cleanup: both processes killed (ports 52817/52818 confirmed free), app/node_modules removed; the probe directory is now 9.1 MB.

TanStack Start on Bun M-tanstack-bun

TanStack Start (React) 1.168.35 + @tanstack/react-router 1.170.18, nitro 3 beta node-server preset, @sentry/tanstackstart-react 10.67.0 (develop / v11 line) · bun 1.4.0 · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

TanStack Start itself runs on bun without Sentry: `vite build` (nitro node-server preset) then `PORT=<p> bun .output/server/index.mjs` serves SSR pages and `server.handlers` API routes correctly.

Wiring Sentry the way the docs page describes DOES NOT BUILD with npm-installed develop packages, so a docs page for this combination cannot be written as-is today. What the docs currently prescribe (manual-setup/index.mdx): install @sentry/tanstackstart-react; `instrument.server.mjs` with Sentry.init at the root; `src/server.ts` wrapping the server entry with `wrapFetchWithSentry`; `src/start.ts` adding `sentryGlobalRequestMiddleware` / `sentryGlobalFunctionMiddleware`; `sentryTanstackStart()` in vite.config.ts; run with `node --import ./.output/server/instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`. On bun the run command becomes `bun --preload ./instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`, and that part works (Sentry.init runs, `getClient()` is truthy).

Three build blockers hit before anything ran:
1. Any `import ... from '@sentry/tanstackstart-react'` inside the server module graph (src/server.ts, src/start.ts, src/router.tsx, or any route file) makes `vite build` fail in the nitro environment with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getVariableForExportName')`. Patching rollup to log showed the null re-export target is `__exports` imported by `@sentry/server-runtime-injection/build/esm/vendored/source-map/lib/base64.js` (that package's ESM build re-exports through `_virtual/*.js` namespace shims that rollup cannot resolve once the package is partially externalized by nitro's dep tracing).
2. Adding `sentryTanstackStart()` to vite.config.ts together with a `mysql` import fails the SSR build earlier: `"default" is not exported by "node_modules/@sentry/conventions/dist/attributes.mjs"` — the build-time diagnostics-channel injection emits a CJS `require('@sentry/conventions/attributes')` that rollup resolves to the .mjs.
3. Tarball packaging friction (not an SDK bug for real users): the registry `@sentry/bundler-plugins@10.67.0` imports `ServerRuntimeClient` from `@sentry/core`, which develop removed, and `@sentry/browser` 10.67.0 (develop) pulls registry `@sentry/feedback` / `@sentry/replay` / `@sentry/replay-canvas` / `@sentry/browser-utils` which break the client build. Fixed by packing feedback/replay-internal/replay-canvas/browser-utils from the worktree and nesting the registry @sentry/core under @sentry/bundler-plugins.

Working setup actually probed (docs would have to describe this, or the build bugs must be fixed):
- `npm install @tanstack/react-start@1.168.35 @tanstack/react-router@1.170.18 react react-dom nitro@3.0.260610-beta mysql vite@7.3.2 @vitejs/plugin-react-swc vite-tsconfig-paths` plus the Sentry tarballs.
- `vite.config.ts`: `tsConfigPaths(), tanstackStart(), nitro(), viteReact()` — WITHOUT `sentryTanstackStart()`.
- `instrument.server.mjs` at the app root: `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/tanstackstart-react'; Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1, traceLifecycle }); globalThis.__PROBE_SENTRY__ = Sentry;`
- `src/probe/sentry.ts` shim re-exporting `wrapFetchWithSentry`, `sentryGlobalRequestMiddleware`, `sentryGlobalFunctionMiddleware`, `setTag`, `captureException`, `captureMessage`, `logger` off `globalThis.__PROBE_SENTRY__`, so no `@sentry/*` specifier ever enters the rollup graph. `src/server.ts` and `src/start.ts` import from that shim instead of the package.
- Build: `npx vite build`. Run: `PORT=41500 bun --preload ./instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksAn error thrown from a route's `server.handlers.GET` reaches Sentry with mechanism `auto.middleware.tanstackstart.request`, handled:false, and a context line; the route still returns 500. This requires `wrapFetchWithSentry` on the server entry — with the plain (unwrapped) entry the same request produced no event at all, only the later sentinel. traceLifecycle: 'static'.
route names✓* works-waNo `transaction` and no `span` envelope arrives for any request on bun — not for the parameterized `/api/user/$id`, not for the SSR `/` page — under either traceLifecycle 'static' or 'stream'. The SDK logs `Integration installed: Http` but bun has no way to patch node:http, so no server root span exists and nothing to name. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. Parameterized route names DO work for TanStack Start on bun 1.4.0 with @sentry/tanstackstart-react 10.67.0 (develop). Two changes were needed, both one-liners. ROOT CAUSE of the reported breakage (read from source, then confirmed): `wrapFetchWithSentry` never creates a root span for a page or API request. Looking at ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/packages/tanstackstart-react/src/server/wrapFetchWithSentry.ts, it only calls `updateSpanWithRouteParametrization(...)`, which does `getActiveSpan()` / `getRootSpan()` and returns early when there is none. (It does start its own span, but only for `_serverFn` / `createServerFn` URLs.) The incoming-request span is supposed to come from `httpIntegration`'s node:http diagnostics channel, which bun does not emit. So the missing span, not the naming, is what is broken on bun. FIX 1 (makes the span exist) — add `bunHttpServerIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun` to `Sentry.init` in instrument.server.mjs. This is legitimate on this stack: nitro 3's node-server preset bundles srvx's NODE adapter (`.output/server/_libs/srvx.mjs` line 901: `server = nodeHTTP.createServer(this.serveOptions, handler)`), so the server really is a `node:http` server, and `bunHttpServerIntegration` patches `http.Server.prototype.emit` and hands the server to the same core instrumentation the Node SDK uses. Unlike the Next.js-on-bun case, TanStack Start emits no server spans of its own, so keep the default `spans: true` (do NOT pass `spans: false`, which the nextjs-16-bun e2e app uses). Precedent for mixing the packages already exists at dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/nextjs-16-bun/sentry.server.config.ts. FIX 2 (makes it build) — `build.rollupOptions.external: [/^@sentry\//, /^@opentelemetry\//]` in vite.config.ts. This clears build blocker 1 exactly: `npx vite build` then succeeds with plain `import { wrapFetchWithSentry } from '@sentry/tanstackstart-react'` in src/server.ts and `sentryGlobalRequestMiddleware`/`sentryGlobalFunctionMiddleware` in src/start.ts, so the globalThis shim the earlier probe needed is unnecessary. Verified in the built output: `.output/server/_ssr/index.mjs:1: import { wrapFetchWithSentry } from "@sentry/tanstackstart-react";`. FIX 2 side effect — externalizing @sentry means the SDK module is never transformed by vite, so `makeRoutePatternPlugin` (packages/tanstackstart-react/src/vite/routePatterns.ts) cannot substitute `__SENTRY_ROUTE_PATTERNS__` inside wrapFetchWithSentry.js. The identifier stays free and resolves off globalThis at runtime, so the app supplies it in instrument.server.mjs: globalThis.__SENTRY_ROUTE_PATTERNS__ = ['/api/user/$id', '/api/ping', '/api/sentinel', '/param/$id', '/']; (sorted the way the plugin sorts: more segments first, static before dynamic). Isolation scope and propagation context are effectively process-global on bun. verified: works-after-all Reproduced the report exactly, then refuted it with a one-line init change. Also refuted their build blocker #1 with a vite `ssr.external` entry, so the DOCUMENTED wiring (real `import { wrapFetchWithSentry } from '@sentry/tanstackstart-react'` in `src/server.ts`, real `sentryGlobalRequestMiddleware`/`sentryGlobalFunctionMiddleware` in `src/start.ts`) builds and runs on bun — no globalThis shim needed. ROOT CAUSE (source, not guesswork). Request isolation in the v11 line is done entirely by core's `instrumentServer` (packages/core/src/integrations/http/server-subscription.ts:175 `withIsolationScope(...)` + `continueTrace(...)`), reached from `packages/node/src/integrations/http/httpServerIntegration.ts:146` via `subscribe('http.server.request.start', ...)`. Bun's `node:http` never publishes that diagnostics channel, so on bun the node-based `@sentry/tanstackstart-react` server SDK never forks an isolation scope. Neither `wrapFetchWithSentry` nor `sentryGlobalRequestMiddleware` calls `withIsolationScope` themselves (packages/tanstackstart-react/src/server/wrapFetchWithSentry.ts, .../server/globalMiddleware.ts), so nothing else covers the gap. `@sentry/bun` already ships the fix as a default integration: `packages/bun/src/integrations/bunHttpServer.ts` patches `http.Server.prototype.emit` and hands the server to the same core `instrumentServer` — its own doc comment names this exact bug ("servers built on node:http ... do not get a fresh isolation scope and trace per request, so unrelated requests can end up sharing one trace"). It is exported (`packages/bun/src/index.ts:208`) but is NOT in the node/framework-SDK default set, which is why the framework SDK misses it on bun. THE CHANGE (`instrument.server.mjs`, everything else as documented): import * as Sentry from '@sentry/tanstackstart-react'; import { bunHttpServerIntegration } from '@sentry/bun'; Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1, integrations: [bunHttpServerIntegration()] }); BEFORE — documented wiring, `bun --preload ./instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`, three concurrent `GET /api/tag?tag=alpha|beta|gamma` then a sentinel (app/run-doc-nofix.log, sink verbatim, trimmed): {"type":"event","exception":"Error: boom-alpha","sdk":"sentry.javascript.tanstackstart-react","trace_id":"b5b719c000e440bdba4c59baa1b87175","tags":{"probe_tag":"gam... {"type":"event","exception":"Error: boom-beta","sdk":"sentry.javascript.tanstackstart-react","trace_id":"b5b719c000e440bdba4c59baa1b87175","tags":{"probe_tag":"gamm... {"type":"event","exception":"Error: boom-gamma","sdk":"sentry.javascript.tanstackstart-react","trace_id":"b5b719c000e440bdba4c59baa1b87175","tags":{"probe_tag":"gam... {"type":"event","message":"sentinel","sdk":"sentry.javascript.tanstackstart-react","trace_id":"b5b719c000e440bdba4c59baa1b87175",... Run unchanged: `bun --preload ./instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`. If another layer already emits incoming-request spans, pass `bunHttpServerIntegration({ spans: false })` to keep only the isolation and trace reset. To make the documented wiring build at all under nitro 3 beta, also add to `vite.config.ts`: ssr: { external: ['@sentry/tanstackstart-react', '@sentry/node', '@sentry/core', '@sentry/server-utils', '@sentry/server-runtime-injection', '@sentry/opentelemetry', '@sentry/conventions'] }, environments: { ssr: { build: { rollupOptions: { external: [/^@sentry\//, '@opentelemetry/api'] } } }, nitro: { build: { rollupOptions: { external: [/^@sentry\//, '@opentelemetry/api'] } } }, }, The real SDK fix is for `@sentry/node`'s (and therefore every framework server SDK's) default integrations to include `bunHttpServerIntegration()` when `process.versions.bun` is set — the integration and its guard (`if (!process.versions.bun || hasPatched) return;`) already exist in `packages/bun/src/integrations/bunHttpServer.ts`.
incoming trace✓* works-waA request with `sentry-trace: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` and a matching baggage header produced an error event with trace_id `cb920373c9c8468ea6e937e1bb372c04` (the process-global one) and no parent_span_id. The incoming headers were ignored. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. Adding `bunHttpServerIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun` to the TanStack Start `Sentry.init` in `instrument.server.mjs` makes incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation work completely on Bun. No other change is needed: same build, same `bun --preload` run command, same app code. Root cause of the original observation (measured, not theorised): Bun's `node:http` does not publish the `http.server.request.start` diagnostics channel that `@sentry/node`'s `httpServerIntegration` subscribes to (`packages/core/src/integrations/http/constants.ts:3`, `packages/node/src/integrations/http/httpServerIntegration.ts:1`). That subscription is the only place the Node SDK calls `continueTrace()` on the incoming headers (`packages/core/src/integrations/http/server-subscription.ts:176-196`) and the only place it opens a per-request isolation scope. `@sentry/tanstackstart-react` itself never reads the request headers: `wrapFetchWithSentry` only starts a span for `_serverFn` paths and injects meta tags, and `sentryGlobalRequestMiddleware` only calls `captureException` — neither continues a trace. Direct proof the channel is missing on Bun (probe file `.../verify4-M-tanstack-bun-incomingtrace/dcheck.mjs`): --- node RUNTIME node fired= ["http.server.request.start","http.server.response.finish"] --- bun RUNTIME bun fired= [] The nitro node-server preset serves through `node:http`, so on Bun nothing ever fired and the SDK fell back to the process-global propagation context. BASELINE (reproduces the report), `PORT=43118 bun --preload ./instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`, request carries `sentry-trace: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` + matching baggage: {"type":"event","exception":"Error: TanStack Bun API Route Error","mechanism":"auto.middleware.tanstackstart.request","trace_id":"9517450acf214446aa37d22c949d09e0","span_id":"b6790f9399d73991","dsc":{"environment":"production","public_key":"public","trace_id":"9517450acf214446aa37d22c949d09e0"}} {"type":"event","message":"sentinel","trace_id":"9517450acf214446aa37d22c949d09e0"} No `parent_span_id`, no request data, no transaction, and the unrelated sentinel shares the same trace: the process-global one. FIXED, only `integrations: [bunHttpServerIntegration()]` added, `traceLifecycle: 'static'`: {"type":"event","exception":"Error: TanStack Bun API Route Error","mechanism":"auto.middleware.tanstackstart.request","transaction":"GET /api/error","trace_id":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","parent_span_id":"bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb","span_id":"bd35a30444f3f166","dsc":{"trace_id":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","public_key":"public","sample_rate":"1","sampled":"true","environment":"upstream","transaction":"upstream-tx"}} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/error","op":"http.server","status":"internal_error","trace_id":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","parent_span_id":"bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb"} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/user/123","op":"http.server","status":"ok","trace_id":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","parent_span_id":"bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb"} {"type":"event","message":"sentinel","transaction":"GET /api/sentinel","trace_id":"10661f321cc14feba550bbece416aef7"} Trace id, parent span id and the full incoming DSC (`environment: upstream`, `transaction: upstream-tx`) are all adopted, the sentinel gets its own fresh trace (per-request isolation is restored too), and request headers/`user.ip_address` are attached. Same result with the shipped default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'`: {"type":"span","trace_id":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","items":["http.server GET"],"raw":[{"name":"GET","status":"error","parent_span_id":"bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.server"}]} and for an SSR pageload (`GET /`) as well as API routes. Control: the same build under `node --import ./instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`, WITHOUT the extra integration, already continues the trace (`trace_id: aaaa…`, `parent_span_id: bbbb…`), so the gap is Bun-specific, not a TanStack Start SDK gap. Notes / caveats: - `@sentry/bun` must be installed alongside `@sentry/tanstackstart-react`; both resolve to one hoisted `@sentry/core@10.67.0`, and mixing the Node-based `Sentry.init` with the Bun integration works. - Leave `spans` at its default `true`. TanStack Start does not emit its own incoming-request span, so the integration supplies the missing `http.server` segment (name is method-only, `GET`, since nitro's node-server has no route info at that layer). - A static `import { bunHttpServerIntegration } from '@sentry/bun'` in `instrument.server.mjs` works; no dynamic import needed. - The three build blockers the earlier probe reported are unchanged and were not retested; they are irrelevant to this fix because `instrument.server.mjs` sits outside the rollup module graph, so the one-line change applies identically to the documented wiring once those build bugs are fixed. No duplicate span: `NodeFetch` still installs on bun but is inert, so `Fetch` + `NodeFetch` together emit exactly one http.client span. ROOT CAUSE of the original report: `nodeFetchIntegration` hooks undici's diagnostics channels, which bun does not emit (the run prints "No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping."). `@sentry/bun`'s `fetchIntegration` instead patches global `fetch` via `addFetchInstrumentationHandler`, which works on bun. The framework SDK's `getDefaultIntegrations` has no bun branch, so nothing supplies it automatically. The build-time channel injection is in the output: `grep -c orchestrion:mysql:query app/.output/server/chunks/build/router-CkZFiwOD.mjs` -> 2. What made it work is the dependency set, not the framework: install the whole develop tarball set as overrides (@sentry/{tanstackstart-react,react,browser,node,core,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry,bundler-plugins,browser-utils,feedback,replay,replay-canvas}) — see app/package.json `pnpm.overrides`. A prior npm attempt in this dir also built once nitro resolved (build-npm2.log, same "✓ built"); its earlier failure (build-npm.log) was `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find module 'nitro/vite'`, i.e. a missing dep, not a rollup/export bug. So `@sentry/tanstackstart-react` never has to be hidden behind a globalThis shim. 2) ROOT CAUSE OF THE MISSING DB SPANS IS BUN GC, NOT INJECTION. Bun 1.4.0 drops diagnostics_channel subscribers as soon as the channel object is collected; the SDK subscribes as `diagnosticsChannel.tracingChannel(NAME).subscribe(...)` and keeps no reference (packages/server-utils/src/integrations/mysql.ts and every other channel integration; the Bun/Deno eager branch is packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/instrumentation.ts:100). Minimal proof, v2-gc.mjs: bun 1.4.0: immediately after subscribe: true / after Bun.gc(true): false / kept-reference channel after Bun.gc(true): true node 26.5: immediately after subscribe: true / after Bun.gc(true): true Same signal in-app (prior run-bun-obs.log): "[obs] after init: [ true, true, true, true, true ]" then "[obs] t+6s: [ false, false, false, false, false ]". 3) BEFORE/AFTER ON THE SAME FRESH BUILD (traceLifecycle stream, default; sink on 41733, app on 41732, driven by curl). Control, exactly the documented file, `bun --preload ./.output/server/instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs` (v2-final-control.log, 0 `op: db` lines): [{"type":"span","trace_id":"0dc439df66c44631a20b0e3413ae2d49","items":["middleware globalRequestMiddleware"]}, {... same ...}] Fixed, same file plus three retained channels (v2-final-fixed.log, 4 `op: db` lines): [{"type":"span","trace_id":"c0b4010f5e1f481db289e5588c24bb7e","items":["middleware globalRequestMiddleware","db SELECT","db SELECT users"],"raw":[{"name":"globalRequestMiddleware","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.middleware.tanstackstart"},{"name":"SELECT","parent_span_id":"a3415e4d3b0f19ce","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.db.mysql"},{"name":"SELECT users","parent_span_id":"a3415e4d3b0f19ce","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.db.mysql"}]}, {... second request identical ...}] `traceLifecycle: 'static'` also records them (v2-run-bun-fixed-static.log) but each db span arrives as its OWN transaction envelope ({"type":"transaction","name":"SELECT 1 + 1 AS solution","op":"db","parent_span_id":...}) because the `middleware globalRequestMiddleware` root finishes before the queries do — stream is the better shape here. Unrelated to db spans, bun still has no `http.server` root span for the nitro node-server (node run of the same build has one: run-node-stream.log "root description: GET /api/db-mysql"); on bun the segment is the request middleware span. Caveats: only bun 1.4.0 was available ($SCRATCH/bun1314 no longer exists), so I could not check whether older bun keeps subscribers. The effect is not TanStack-specific — it is every channel-based integration on bun (mysql, mysql2, other db and AI integrations), and it explains why bun db-span probes pass in small/short-lived apps and fail in a heavy vite/nitro bundle where GC actually runs.
Workaround: Add to instrument.server.mjs, after Sentry.init (full file at .../verify4-M-tanstack-bun-dbspans/instrument.server.bun-fix.mjs): import diagnosticsChannel from 'node:diagnostics_channel'; globalThis.__sentryKeepChannelsAlive = [ 'orchestrion:mysql:query', 'orchestrion:mysql2:query', 'orchestrion:mysql2:execute', ].map(name => diagnosticsChannel.tracingChannel(name)); then run the documented command with bun: `bun --preload ./.output/server/instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`. Any strong reference works; keeping it on globalThis is what survives. Patching `dc.tracingChannel` from the preload does NOT work (v2-run-bun-keepall.log: "[v2] channels retained after init = 0") because the SDK's `import * as diagnosticsChannel` namespace does not see the patched property, so the channel names have to be listed. Real fix belongs in the SDK: retain the channel objects at the subscribe sites in packages/server-utils/src/integrations/* (or centrally for the Bun/Deno eager branch in packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/instrumentation.ts), which would make this work with no user-side code.

No page mentions the combination. `~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/tanstackstart-react/` contains 11 files and none of them contains the string "bun" (or "deno"); the only runtime named besides Node is Cloudflare, once, as an exclusion: `manual-setup/index.mdx:391` "This setup doesn't work for Cloudflare deployments." The single documented run command is `manual-setup/index.mdx:372` `"start": "node --import ./.output/server/instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs"`, and `manual-setup/index.mdx:383` frames the alternative as "when you can't configure Node.js CLI flags". Conversely `~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/` never mentions TanStack. `manual-setup/index.mdx:17` does flag the whole SDK as beta ("compatible with TanStack Start 1.0 RC and is currently in beta").

Documented: no

A page must say TanStack Start (React) 1.168.35 on the nitro 3 node-server preset runs on Bun 1.4.0 as `bun .output/server/index.mjs`, and give the Bun equivalent of the sole documented start command: `bun --preload ./instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`. It must state that with the documented wiring alone the SDK instruments nothing on Bun — no transaction or span at all, so route names such as `GET /api/user/$id` never appear, there is no request isolation, no incoming trace continuation and no outgoing `fetch` span — because Bun does not emit the `http.server.request.start` diagnostics channel the Node SDK relies on. The four fixes must be documented: install `@sentry/bun` at the same version and pass `integrations: [fetchIntegration(), bunHttpServerIntegration()]` to `Sentry.init` in `instrument.server.mjs`, guarded on `typeof globalThis.Bun !== 'undefined'`; wrap the handler call in the server entry with `Sentry.withIsolationScope(() => handler.fetch(request))` on Bun only (on Node the extra fork hides request tags); add a first `vite.config.ts` plugin keeping `@sentry/*` external in the nitro server build, without which `vite build` dies with "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getVariableForExportName')"; and pin each driver's orchestrion tracing channel in a preload module, since Bun's GC drops the SDK's diagnostics-channel subscriptions and db, cache and AI spans stop being recorded shortly after startup.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/tanstackstart-react.mdx (new)

~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/tanstackstart-react/index.mdx:5-9 (`categories: [javascript, server, server-node, browser]`); ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/tanstackstart-react/manual-setup/index.mdx:372 (the single documented start command, `node --import ./.output/server/instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`); manual-setup/index.mdx:391 ("This setup doesn't work for Cloudflare deployments." — the only non-Node runtime named anywhere in the guide). None of the 11 files in that guide contains the string "bun".

Bottom line: TanStack Start runs on bun, and @sentry/tanstackstart-react initializes on bun, but only errors and logs work. Everything that depends on per-request async context or on module patching — server transactions/route names, isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing fetch headers and spans, db spans — is broken, and the failures are all one root cause: on bun there is no way to install the diagnostics-channel injection hooks or patch node:http, so @sentry/node's server span never exists and the isolation scope is never forked. The SDK says both out loud with debug:true ("No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping." and "No diagnostics-channel injection detected."), which is honest but it does not warn that request isolation is gone; silently sharing one process-global isolation scope and one process-global trace id across concurrent requests is the most dangerous finding here, because it leaks tags (and would leak user data) between users' requests without any error. Separately, the docs wiring does not even build with develop packages installed via npm. A single `import { wrapFetchWithSentry } from '@sentry/tanstackstart-react'` in the server module graph kills `vite build`'s nitro pass with a rollup null-module crash traced to `@sentry/server-runtime-injection`'s vendored source-map ESM (`_virtual/*.js` `__exports` re-export shims). That is runtime-independent — it would hit a Node user on npm just the same — so it deserves checking against the repo's pnpm-based e2e app, which builds the identical wiring fine; the difference is almost certainly npm hoisting versus pnpm symlinks changing what nitro's dep tracing externalizes. Adding `sentryTanstackStart()` on top, with a `mysql` import present, fails earlier and differently: the build-time channel injection emits `require('@sentry/conventions/attributes')` inside a CJS module and rollup resolves that specifier to `attributes.mjs`, which has no default export. I worked around both by keeping every `@sentry/*` specifier out of the bundle: `instrument.server.mjs` is `--preload`ed by bun and stashes the namespace on `globalThis`, and `src/probe/sentry.ts` re-exports from there. That is not a shape any docs page should recommend, but it let the seven capabilities be measured rather than reported as not-run. One more thing worth chasing outside this cell: the same build, on Node v26.5.0, is fine with `node .output/server/index.mjs` and completely broken with `node --import ./instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs` — every API route answers 200 with a two-byte `{}` body and nothing reaches the sink. That looks like @sentry/node's http instrumentation colliding with nitro/srvx on Node 26, and it means the documented TanStack Start start command may be broken on current Node independently of bun. Constraints on the numbers: single machine, one bun version (1.4.0), one nitro beta (I also tried 3.0.260903-beta with the same rollup crash), one TanStack Start version. The db-span verdict is "no span observed" rather than "instrumentation proven impossible" — the injection path could not be tested at all because the build that would produce it fails.
