Remix on Bun M-remix-bun

Remix v2 (@remix-run/dev 2.17.x vite plugin + @remix-run/express adapter), @sentry/remix 10.67.0 (develop, v11 line) · Bun 1.4.0 (`bun x remix vite:build`, then `bun server.mjs` / `bun dist/server.js`) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Remix v2 runs on Bun without changes, and @sentry/remix initializes on Bun (`Sentry.isInitialized() === true`). But there are TWO different run shapes on Bun and NEITHER gives a correct SDK; a docs page would have to pick one and disclose what it loses.

Packages (npm install, not `bun add`, so the tarballs' transitive @sentry/*@10.67.0 resolve):
  npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-remix-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz \
    $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-react-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-browser-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz \
    $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz \
    $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bun-10.67.0.tgz
  plus @remix-run/{dev,express,node,react,server-runtime}, express, react, react-dom, vite, mysql2.

instrument.mjs (module scope):
  import * as Sentry from '@sentry/remix';
  Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' });

server.mjs: `import './instrument.mjs';` as the FIRST line, then the standard express adapter
(`createRequestHandler({ build: await import('./build/server/index.js') })`). mysql2 pool created at
module scope in server.mjs.

app/entry.server.tsx: `export const handleError = Sentry.sentryHandleError;`
vite.config.ts: `plugins: [remix(), sentryRemixVitePlugin()]`.

Build: `bun x remix vite:build` — works unmodified on Bun (vite 5 + esbuild darwin-arm64 binary).

Mode A (plain, what a Node docs page tells you to do):
  NODE_ENV=production bun server.mjs
  -> errors, isolation, incoming-trace continuation, trace headers on outgoing fetch, logs.
  -> ZERO transaction/span envelopes. No route names, no db spans, no http.client spans.

Mode B (Bun's documented instrumentation path — bundle with the orchestrion plugin):
  build-server.ts:
    import { sentryBunPlugin } from '@sentry/bun/plugin';
    await Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./server.mjs'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun',
      external: ['@sentry/remix','@sentry/node','@sentry/core','@sentry/bun','@sentry/server-utils',
                 '@sentry/opentelemetry','@sentry/server-runtime-injection'],
      plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] });
  then `bun build-server.ts && NODE_ENV=production bun dist/server.js`
  -> full span tree (route names, LOADER spans, mysql2 spans, http.client spans), errors, logs.
  -> request ISOLATION IS GONE: one trace id for the whole process, tags leak across requests,
     incoming sentry-trace ignored.

Root cause of the Mode B defect: @sentry/remix's per-request `withIsolationScope` + `continueTrace` live
in `instrumentServer()`, which monkeypatches `createRequestHandler` via a CJS
`loadModule('@remix-run/server-runtime', module)` (packages/remix/src/server/instrumentServer.ts:538).
`sentryBunPlugin` force-un-externalizes every instrumented package (`withoutInstrumentedExternals` in
packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/bundler/bun.ts) so `@remix-run/server-runtime` is inlined into the
bundle, and the monkeypatch lands on the unused node_modules copy. The plugin does not let you keep that
package external, so on Bun you can have spans or isolation, not both.

Mechanism is the Remix `handleError` hook wired as `export const handleError = Sentry.sentryHandleError`. WHY IT WORKS. bunHttpServerIntegration patches http.Server.prototype.emit and hands each server to core's getHttpServerSubscriptions, which is what does withIsolationScope + continueTrace per request (packages/bun/src/integrations/bunHttpServer.ts:118-155). `spans: false` keeps that isolation but suppresses its own url-named http.server span, so the remix tracing-channel span (packages/remix/src/server/integrations/tracing-channel.ts, renamed to the matched route by enrichActiveSpanWithRoute) stays the segment. This is the piece @sentry/remix never gets on Bun on its own, because its init() goes through @sentry/node's defaults, not @sentry/bun's. OTHER VARIANTS I TRIED, all worse (kept in the dir): - Mode A2, plain bun + `Sentry.instrumentBuild(build, { instrumentTracing: true })` (the Cloudflare/Hydrogen wiring, server-a.mjs with INSTRUMENT_BUILD=1): spans appear but there is no request root, so each loader becomes its own transaction: {"type":"transaction","name":"routes/users.$id","op":"function","source":"custom"}. No route name. - Mode C, plain bun + `bunHttpServerIntegration()` with spans left on: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/42","op":"http.server","source":"url"} — url, not route, and it is a *different* trace from the loader work, because @sentry/remix's own createRequestHandler monkeypatch calls continueTrace with empty headers, and core's continueTrace ends with `withActiveSpan(null, callback)` (packages/core/src/tracing/trace.ts:216), detaching the parent. Adding instrumentBuild on top does not help: the http.server span is in trace 32cc9e26… while routes/users.$id is in 889940e5…. - Mode D (server-d.mjs) proves the async context itself is fine on Bun: `[mw sync] true GET /probe`, `[mw async] true GET /probe`, `[before remix] true GET /probe`, then hasActiveSpan:false inside the loader. - `bun --preload ./node_modules/@sentry/remix/build/import-hook.mjs server-a.mjs` with SENTRY_DEBUG=1 changes nothing and prints the reason: "Sentry Logger [warn]: [Sentry] No diagnostics-channel injection detected. Channel-based integrations will not record spans." @sentry/server-runtime-injection's register.js takes the Module.register() branch only when `!globalThis.Bun`, and Bun has no Module.registerHooks (bun -e: node ver 26.3.0, registerHooks undefined, register function). So bundling is not optional on Bun, and no init placement or trace lifecycle substitutes for it. - traceLifecycle 'stream' vs 'static' makes no difference to any of the above. SEPARATE TRAP worth a line in docs, hit in this probe: with `"sideEffects": false` in package.json (which the Remix templates ship), Bun.build tree-shakes `import './instrument.mjs'` out of the bundle entirely. The server starts, prints nothing, and emits zero envelopes — indistinguishable from Mode A. dist-a/ is that bundle, kept as evidence (grep -c isInitialized dist-a/server-a.js -> 0).
Workaround: On Bun, build the Remix express server with Bun.build + sentryBunPlugin() (required — Bun has no runtime channel injection), and add `bunHttpServerIntegration({ spans: false })` from @sentry/bun to the Sentry.init() in instrument.mjs. Also drop `"sideEffects": false` from package.json, or Bun.build tree-shakes the `import './instrument.mjs'` line out of the bundle and the SDK never initializes.

Route-named transactions and LOADER spans are unchanged. 3) Incoming trace continuation also comes back (drive-trace2.mjs sends sentry-trace with trace ids 000..1/2/3): {"t":"event","ex":"Error: iso-error-a","tags":{"probe_tag":"tag-a"},"tid":"00000000000000000000000000000001"} {"t":"event","ex":"Error: iso-error-b","tags":{"probe_tag":"tag-b"},"tid":"00000000000000000000000000000002"} {"t":"event","ex":"Error: iso-error-c","tags":{"probe_tag":"tag-c"},"tid":"00000000000000000000000000000003"} {"t":"transaction","tid":"00000000000000000000000000000001","name":"GET iso/:id"} (and 2, 3) Reproduced twice (fresh process, and after a prior batch). 4) `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` behaves the same: {"t":"span","tid":"0edcea279d10401ab7443acfdbcfcac0","items":["function LOADER routes/iso.$id","http.server GET iso/:id"]} — one distinct trace id per request, matching each event's trace id. 5) `bunHttpServerIntegration()` with the default `spans: true` also isolates correctly and adds express middleware spans, but the transaction is then named after the express route: {"t":"transaction","name":"GET *","src":"route","spans":["middleware query2","middleware expressInit","handler *","http.server GET iso/:id","function LOADER routes/iso.$id"]}. Use `spans: false` to keep `GET iso/:id` as the transaction name. Why it works: the isolation the reporter saw missing normally comes from `@sentry/node`'s http-server subscription on `http.server.request.start`, which Bun's node:http never publishes; the Remix CJS monkeypatch (instrumentServer.ts:538 -> wrapRequestHandler, instrumentServer.ts:349/393 withIsolationScope + continueTrace) is the only fallback and is defeated when `sentryBunPlugin` inlines `@remix-run/server-runtime`. `packages/bun/src/integrations/bunHttpServer.ts` exists exactly for this: it patches `http.Server.prototype.emit` and hands the server to the same core instrumentation (`getHttpServerSubscriptions`). It is a default integration of `@sentry/bun` only, so a framework SDK (`@sentry/remix` -> `@sentry/node`) running on Bun does not get it unless you add it by hand. So the defect is real for the documented wiring, but it is a one-line init fix, not an architectural "spans or isolation, pick one". Caveat, unbundled mode: plain `bun server.mjs` with the integration added also starts emitting url-named `http.server` transactions, but the error events then land on a different trace id than the transaction ({"t":"transaction","name":"GET /iso/c","tid":"18b05349c9cb4f2d86d64c38a3b14b2c"} vs {"t":"event","ex":"Error: iso-error-c","tid":"539497cc9be44fb5b9a3ef6084578f28"}), because the still-live CJS monkeypatch opens a second isolation scope and a second trace inside the first. Isolation itself is correct there (tags do not leak). So the integration should be recommended for the bundled run shape, which is the one that has spans anyway. Rerun: see README-rerun-verify.txt in the probe dir. All processes started were killed.
Workaround: In the Remix server init file, add `@sentry/bun`'s Bun http-server integration to the Node/Remix init: import { bunHttpServerIntegration } from '@sentry/bun'; import * as Sentry from '@sentry/remix'; Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, integrations: [bunHttpServerIntegration({ spans: false })], }); (`@sentry/bun` must be installed; keep it in the `external` list of the `Bun.build` config next to the other `@sentry/*` packages. `spans: false` avoids the express-level `GET *` transaction name replacing the Remix route name; `spans: true` is fine if you want express middleware spans and can live with `GET *`.)

Two alternatives I tried and rejected: - Mode D, `external: ['@remix-run/express']` so the adapter resolves the node_modules copy and the `instrumentServer()` monkeypatch lands: incoming trace is continued (recorder shows aaaa…-a104c5acc07daf3a-1 with sentry-environment=upstream), but every transaction disappears again — identical to Mode A. Not a fix. - `@remix-run/server-runtime` in `external` is impossible: `withoutInstrumentedExternals` strips it, and `instrumentedModuleNames()` also injects '@remix-run/node' precisely so server-runtime is force-bundled (packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/config/index.ts:93-99). Mechanism, corrected from the earlier report: on Node, per-request isolation and `continueTrace` do NOT come from `instrumentServer()` at all — they come from `httpServerIntegration`, which `httpIntegration()` always sets up (packages/node/src/integrations/http/index.ts:88-105) and which subscribes to Node's `http.server.request.start` diagnostics channel (packages/node/src/integrations/http/httpServerIntegration.ts:1-7, packages/core/src/integrations/http/constants.ts:3). Bun does not emit that channel, so on Bun that layer is inert in every mode. In Mode A the `instrumentServer()` monkeypatch (packages/remix/src/server/instrumentServer.ts:349,393) is the only thing left doing `withIsolationScope`/`continueTrace`; in the bundle it is dead, and the channel-based `remixIntegration` that replaces it only opens spans — packages/remix/src/server/integrations/tracing-channel.ts contains no isolation or trace-continuation code. The middleware puts that missing layer back in user land. Control: `WRAP=1 node server.mjs` on Node produces exactly the same output as plain Node (transaction on aaaa…/bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb, fresh ids elsewhere), so the snippet is a no-op on Node and safe to ship in a shared server.mjs. Residual gap under the fix (not the capability under test, but a docs page should say it): events emitted from the Bun bundle carry no `request` data and no `event.transaction` — `{"type":"event","message":"sentinel",...,"trace_id":"c914f3f231554870a1c38a11618b0ac7","parent_span_id":"a2599ab7e4fac917"}` with no `request` key, where Node's control run has `"transaction":"GET /sentinel"` and a full `request` object. That metadata is set by `isolationScope.setTransactionName` / `setSDKProcessingMetadata` inside the dead monkeypatch.
Workaround: Build the server with `Bun.build` + `sentryBunPlugin()` as Bun's docs prescribe, and add one express middleware ahead of the Remix handler in server.mjs: const remixHandler = createRequestHandler({ build: await import('./build/server/index.js') }); app.all('*', (req, res, next) => { Sentry.withIsolationScope(() => Sentry.continueTrace( { sentryTrace: req.headers['sentry-trace'] || '', baggage: req.headers['baggage'] || '' }, () => remixHandler(req, res, next), ), ); }); It restores per-request isolation and incoming-trace continuation without costing any span, and it is a no-op on Node, so the same server.mjs works on both runtimes.

Plain `bun server.mjs` must be documented as giving errors and logs only — no transactions and no spans at all, not even a request span, and no outgoing-`fetch` span or trace headers. The working shape is to bundle the server entry with `Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./server.mjs'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin`, keeping `@sentry/*` external, and run `bun dist/server.js`; that yields route-named `http.server` transactions (`GET users/:id`, source `route`), `LOADER routes/users.$id` children, database spans and the outgoing `http.client` span with `sentry-trace`/`baggage`. The page must also state the two app-side requirements the bundle imposes: remove `"sideEffects": false` from the app's `package.json` or `Bun.build` tree-shakes the side-effect-only db import out and mysql2 is never transformed, and put `express` back on `external` after `sentryBunPlugin()` has run. Finally, because the bundle inlines `@remix-run/server-runtime`, Sentry's `createRequestHandler` patch never runs, so the app must hold the adapter handler in a variable and wrap it itself in `Sentry.withIsolationScope(...)` (not as a `next()`-style middleware) to get per-request isolation and incoming trace continuation.

Headline: Remix v2 itself is fully viable on Bun 1.4.0 — `bun x remix vite:build` and `bun server.mjs` both work unmodified, and @sentry/remix initializes. But there is no Bun run shape that gives a correct SDK, and the two shapes fail in opposite directions: - Plain `bun server.mjs`: correct isolation, correct incoming-trace continuation, errors, logs, trace headers on outgoing fetch — and ZERO span/transaction envelopes. Consistent with the established Bun finding that `bun run` gets no orchestrion transform; here it also costs the `http.server` transaction entirely, because @sentry/remix disables @sentry/node's incoming request spans (`disableIncomingRequestSpans: true`, packages/remix/src/server/integrations/http.ts) and relies on the injected `@remix-run/server-runtime` channels for the request span. - `Bun.build` + `sentryBunPlugin()`: complete span tree (route names with `source: route`, LOADER spans, mysql2 spans, http.client spans) — and request isolation is gone. Every request in the process shares one trace id, and tags set in one request are attached to every later event including unrelated ones. This is a data-correctness bug, not just a missing feature: it cross-contaminates events between concurrent users. The isolation defect is structural, not a Bun runtime quirk. @sentry/remix's only per-request `withIsolationScope`/`continueTrace` lives in `instrumentServer()` (packages/remix/src/server/instrumentServer.ts:349, :538), which reaches Remix by a CJS `loadModule('@remix-run/server-runtime', module)` monkeypatch. `sentryBunPlugin` calls `withoutInstrumentedExternals` (packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/bundler/bun.ts) to force-bundle every instrumented package, so `@remix-run/server-runtime` is inlined and the monkeypatch patches a dead node_modules copy. The plugin deliberately offers no escape hatch for this (its comment says a blanket external strategy is warned about, not supported), so the two mechanisms are mutually exclusive by construction. The same hazard would hit any bundled Remix server, Bun or not — Bun is just the runtime where bundling is mandatory. Suggested fix direction for the SDK: move the isolation-scope fork and `continueTrace` off the CJS monkeypatch and onto the already-injected `orchestrion:@remix-run/server-runtime:requestHandler` tracing channel (packages/remix/src/server/integrations/tracing-channel.ts currently starts spans there but never touches the isolation scope), so bundled builds get isolation for free. Node control, run from the identical source tree with `node --import ./node_modules/@sentry/remix/build/import-hook.mjs server.mjs`, is fully correct on every capability — so nothing here is a Remix-SDK-wide regression. Two smaller observations: the Bun bundle drops `hasContextLine` (no sourcemaps configured in build-server.ts; adding `sourcemap: 'external'` would likely restore it, untested), and the Bun bundle is `target: 'bun'` so it cannot be run under node as a same-artifact control (`TypeError: __require is not a function`). Environment: all processes started (sink 27419, recorder 41519, app 33851, node control 33853) were killed; app-a/node_modules removed. Ports 41317 and 52731 were occupied by other agents mid-run, hence the odd port numbers. `@sentry/remix` was installed from the pre-built $REPRO/_toolbox/pack tarball, so nothing needed packing from the worktree.

SolidStart on Bun M-solidstart-bun

SolidStart 2 (@solidjs/start 2.0.2 + nitro 3.0.260610-beta + vite 8) · bun 1.4.0 (running the nitro node output `.output/server/index.mjs`) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

SolidStart 2 builds a plain nitro node output and `bun .output/server/index.mjs` serves it fine (Bun ran page routes, file API routes and parameterized routes with no patching). Wiring the develop SDK the way a docs page would:

packages (npm, not `bun add` — the tarballs' transitive @sentry deps need npm; `--legacy-peer-deps` is required because @sentry/nitro@10.67.0 pins `nitro@">=3.0.0-0 <4.0.0 || 3.0.260311-beta || 3.0.260415-beta"` which semver-prerelease rules do not let `nitro@3.0.260610-beta` satisfy):
  npm install --legacy-peer-deps $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{solidstart,nitro,node,core,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry,solid,browser,browser-utils,replay,replay-canvas,feedback,bundler-plugins}-10.67.0.tgz
  (`sentry-nitro-10.67.0.tgz` is not in $REPRO/_toolbox/pack by default; I packed it with `(cd $W/packages/nitro && npm pack --pack-destination $REPRO/_toolbox/pack)`.)

vite.config.ts:
  import { sentrySolidStart } from '@sentry/solidstart/vite';
  import { solidStart } from '@solidjs/start/config';
  import { nitro } from 'nitro/vite';
  export default defineConfig({ plugins: [ solidStart({ appRoot: './src', middleware: './src/middleware.ts' }), sentrySolidStart({ sourcemaps: { disable: true } }), nitro({ serverDir: './server' }) ] });

server/plugins/sentry.ts (nitro plugin, build-time instrumentation, no `--import` preload):
  import * as Sentry from '@sentry/solidstart';
  import { definePlugin } from 'nitro';
  export default definePlugin(() => { Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' }); });

src/middleware.ts: `createMiddleware({ onBeforeResponse: [sentryBeforeResponseMiddleware()] })`.

run: `npx vite build` (build under node), then `PORT=<port> bun .output/server/index.mjs`.

Sentry.init() succeeds under bun (`Sentry.isInitialized() === true`), transactions/spans/logs are delivered, so this setup is publishable — but half the capabilities below are dead on bun and a docs page would have to say so.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors◐ partialA server function wrapped in `withServerActionInstrumentation` reports: exception "probe-server-action-error", mechanism `auto.function.solidstart`, handled=false, with context lines, attached to the `GET /server-error` transaction. A plain `throw` inside a file API route (`src/routes/api/boom.ts`, `export function GET(){ throw ... }`) is swallowed: the response is 500 and the transaction is recorded with status `internal_error`, but no event is ever sent. That swallowing is identical on node with the same build, so it is SolidStart/nitro behavior, not a bun regression. verified: partial Reproduced the report exactly, found the root cause in the build output, and made the broken half work with a 6-line user-side middleware. The other half (SSR page render errors) stays swallowed even then. Setup (same as the report): @solidjs/start 2.0.2 + nitro 3.0.260610-beta + vite 8, develop SDK tarballs, `sentrySolidStart()` in vite.config.ts, `Sentry.init` in `server/plugins/sentry.ts`, `sentryBeforeResponseMiddleware()` in `src/middleware.ts`, `npx vite build` then `bun .output/server/index.mjs`. Sink on 41777, app on 41778, sentinel = `GET /api/sentinel` (captureMessage + flush) after every probe request, so absence is deterministic. RUN A - baseline, docs wiring, bun, traceLifecycle 'static' ($REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-solidstart-bun-errors/run-a-baseline.log). `src/routes/api/boom.ts` = `export function GET(){ throw new Error('probe-api-route-error') }`. Confirmed swallowed: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/boom","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"internal_error","spans":["middleware GET /api/boom","http.server GET /api/boom"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/boom-async","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"internal_error",...} {"type":"event","exception":"Error: Error thrown from Solid Start E2E test app server route","mechanism":"auto.function.solidstart","handled":false,...} {"type":"event","message":"sentinel","mechanism":"generic","handled":true,...} No `event` for either boom route, before the sentinel. Async throws behave identically to sync ones. ROOT CAUSE (read from `.output/server/`, not guessed). SolidStart 2 builds its SSR renderer as its own Nitro service with its own h3 app: `_ssr/ssr.mjs` ends with `const app = new H3(); app.use(handler); return app;` - constructed with NO config, so `config.onError` is undefined. h3's `prepareResponse` then does `if (error.unhandled && !config.silent) console.error(error)` and, with no `onError`, returns `errorResponse(...)` directly. The 500 Response is handed back to the outer Nitro app as a normal response, so the main app's `onError` in `.output/server/index.mjs` line 350 (`createH3App({ onError(error, event){ captureError(error,{event}); ... } })`) - the thing that calls `hooks.callHook("error", ...)`, i.e. what `@sentry/nitro`'s server plugin hooks - never runs. A previous run of this same probe registered an extra `nitroApp.hooks.hook('error', ...)` by hand and its `[probe] nitro error hook fired` line never printed (`run-hook.log`), which matches. PROOF the Nitro side is fine and only the SolidStart service swallows - RUN C ($V/run-c-nitroroute.log): added `server/routes/nitro-boom.ts` = `defineHandler(() => { throw new Error('probe-nitro-route-error') })`, no user error handling at all: {"type":"event","exception":"Error: probe-nitro-route-error","mechanism":"auto.http.nitro.onTraceError","handled":false,"hasContextLine":true} {"type":"event","exception":"Error: probe-nitro-route-error","mechanism":"chained","handled":true,...} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /nitro-boom","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"internal_error",...} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/boom","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"internal_error",...} <- still no event (Side observation, not this capability: the Nitro route error is reported twice, once as `auto.http.nitro.onTraceError` handled=false and once as `chained` handled=true.) RUN B - the fix, bun, 'static' ($V/run-b-mw.log). `src/middleware.ts` wraps `next()` (see workaround). Both the sync and the async API-route throw now arrive: {"type":"event","exception":"Error: probe-api-route-error","mechanism":"solidstart.middleware","handled":false,"sdk":"sentry.javascript.solidstart","runtime":"node","hasContextLine":true} {"type":"event","exception":"Error: probe-api-route-error-async","mechanism":"solidstart.middleware","handled":false,...,"hasContextLine":true} {"type":"event","exception":"Error: Error thrown from Solid Start E2E test app server route","mechanism":"auto.function.solidstart","handled":false,...} plus the three `internal_error` transactions and the sentinel. RUN D - same fix, bun, traceLifecycle 'stream' ($V/run-d-mw-stream.log): works, error event plus `{"type":"span",...,"raw":[{"name":"GET /api/boom","origin":"auto.http.nitro.h3"},{"name":"GET","status":"error","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.nitro.srvx"}]}`. RUN E - same fix, node instead of bun ($V/run-e-mw-node.log): works and is actually richer, the event carries request data and the transaction name, which it does not on bun: {"type":"event","exception":"Error: probe-api-route-error","mechanism":"solidstart.middleware","handled":false,"transaction":"GET /api/boom","request":{"url":"http://127.0.0.1:41778/api/boom","method":"GET",...}} So the swallow is a SolidStart 2 / nitro issue, not a bun regression, and the fix is runtime-independent - matching the original report's node cross-check. RUN F - alternative fix, `entry-server.tsx` keeps the handler and sets `handler.config.onError` ($V/run-f-onerror.log). `createHandler()` returns the h3 app instance (`StartHandler extends H3`), so this reaches the SSR service directly. It fires (`[probe] h3 onError fired probe-api-route-error`) and delivers an event, but by then h3 has already wrapped the throw in an `HTTPError`, so the reported exception chain is `HTTPError` with the real error as a `chained` cause (`{"type":"event","exception":"Error: probe-api-route-error","mechanism":"chained","handled":true,...}` - values[0] is the cause). Grouping would key on `HTTPError`. The middleware is the better shape. RUN G - remaining gap ($V/run-g-mw-page.log). A component that throws during SSR (`src/routes/page-error.tsx`, `export default function PageError(){ throw new Error('probe-page-render-error') }`) is NOT rescued by the middleware: Solid's renderer catches it inside the render, so `next()` resolves and the middleware sees no throw. Only the transaction arrives: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /page-error","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"internal_error","spans":["middleware GET /page-error","http.server GET /page-error"]} {"type":"event","exception":"Error: probe-api-route-error","mechanism":"solidstart.middleware","handled":false,...} <- the API route in the same run No event for the page render error, before the sentinel. That surface stays dark with every variant I tried. REFERENCE APP: `~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/solidstart-2/` has no `src/routes/api/**` route and no server-render-throw route at all - its only server error test is the `withServerActionInstrumentation` page. So the SDK's own e2e suite does not cover the case that is broken. Files (all rerunnable, `node_modules` removed after the run): - app: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-solidstart-bun-errors/app (src/middleware.ts, src/entry-server.tsx, src/routes/api/{boom,boom-async,ok,sentinel}.ts, src/routes/page-error.tsx, src/routes/server-error.tsx, server/plugins/sentry.ts, server/routes/nitro-boom.ts, vite.config.ts) Both fixes are gated by env vars so one build covers every variant: `PROBE_MW=1` (middleware) and `PROBE_ONERROR=1` (h3 config.onError). - Rerun: `cd app && npm install --legacy-peer-deps && npx vite build`; `PORT=41777 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs &`; `SENTRY_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:41777/ SENTRY_LIFECYCLE=static PORT=41778 [PROBE_MW=1] bun .output/server/index.mjs`; then `curl 127.0.0.1:41778/api/boom`, `curl 127.0.0.1:41778/api/sentinel`, `curl 127.0.0.1:41777/__items`. - A stray `app/app/` directory is a copy I made by mistake at the start; nothing reads it (no `rm` allowed).
Workaround: Add an h3 middleware that wraps `next()` in `src/middleware.ts`. `createMiddleware` accepts a raw h3 `Middleware[]` in SolidStart 2, so this is a supported shape and composes with the Sentry meta-tag middleware: ```ts // src/middleware.ts import * as Sentry from '@sentry/solidstart'; import { createMiddleware } from '@solidjs/start/middleware'; export default createMiddleware([ async (event, next) => { try { return await next(); } catch (error) { Sentry.captureException(error, { mechanism: { handled: false, type: 'solidstart.middleware' } }); throw error; } }, ...createMiddleware({ onBeforeResponse: [Sentry.sentryBeforeResponseMiddleware()] }), ]); ``` This catches sync and async throws from `src/routes/**/*.ts` file API routes on both bun and node, in both `traceLifecycle` modes, with context lines and `handled: false`, and it keeps the original error as the top-level exception. It does not catch errors thrown while a page component renders on the server. Alternative that reaches the same h3 app but reports worse: in `entry-server.tsx`, keep the value from `createHandler(...)` and set `handler.config.onError = error => Sentry.captureException(error, { mechanism: { handled: false, type: '...' } })`. h3 has already wrapped the throw in an `HTTPError` at that point, so the issue groups as `HTTPError` with the real error attached as a chained cause.
route names✗ brokenBoth a parameterized page route and a parameterized API route produce a transaction, but never a parameterized name: `/users/456` -> `GET /users/456` and `/api/users/789` -> `GET /api/users/789`, both with `source: "url"`. Identical on node (the repo's own solidstart-2 e2e test asserts `transaction === 'GET /users/6'`, i.e. it enshrines url source). Under the default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` this degrades further: since the source is not `route`, the http.server span name collapses to the method, `http.server GET`, with `src: "url"`. verified: confirmed-broken Confirmed, and root-caused: the SDK never parameterizes SolidStart 2 file routes, on bun 1.4.0 and on node 26 alike. This is not a bun defect and not an SDK defect in the nitro instrumentation itself. Setup (all in $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-solidstart-bun-routenames/app): the repo's own `dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/solidstart-2` app, docs-shaped wiring (`solidStart()` + `sentrySolidStart()` + `nitro({ serverDir: './server' })`, `Sentry.init` in `server/plugins/sentry.ts`, `sentryBeforeResponseMiddleware()` in `src/middleware.ts`), develop tarballs from $REPRO/_toolbox/pack via `npm install --legacy-peer-deps`, `npx vite build`, then `PORT=47033 SENTRY_TUNNEL=... bun .output/server/index.mjs`. One build serves every run; behavior is switched by env (`SENTRY_LIFECYCLE`, `PROBE_ROUTEFIX`, `PROBE_DIAG`). ROOT CAUSE. `packages/nitro/src/runtime/hooks/captureTracingEvents.ts:getParameterizedRoute()` reads `event.context.matchedRoute.route` and explicitly returns undefined for the catch-all `'/**'`. SolidStart 2 mounts its whole router as one nitro catch-all, so every page route and every `src/routes/api/**` route arrives with `matchedRoute.route === '/**'`. My diagnostic subscription on `tracing:h3.request:start` (bun, r1-bun-static-baseline.log): [PROBE h3.request:start] {"type":"route","url":"/users/456","matchedRoute":{"route":"/**"},"params":{"_":"users/456"},...} [PROBE h3.request:start] {"type":"route","url":"/api/users/789","matchedRoute":{"route":"/**"},"params":{"_":"api/users/789"},...} [PROBE h3.request:start] {"type":"route","url":"/nitro/users/7","matchedRoute":{"route":"/nitro/users/:id"},"params":{"id":"7"},...} PROOF THE MECHANISM WORKS ON BUN. I added a nitro-native route `server/routes/nitro/users/[id].ts`. Same bun process, same run: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/456","op":"http.server","source":"url",...} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/users/789","op":"http.server","source":"url",...} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /nitro/users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route",...} Under `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` (r3) the same split shows in the segment span: {"name":"GET","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.nitro.srvx","source":"url"} <- /users/456 {"name":"GET","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.nitro.srvx","source":"url"} <- /api/users/789 {"name":"GET /nitro/users/:id","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.nitro.srvx","source":"route","http_route":"/nitro/users/:id"} So `setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute`, the h3 channel and the srvx segment rename all work correctly under bun. Only SolidStart's own routes are invisible to them. NODE PARITY (r5, same build, `node .output/server/index.mjs`): `{"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/456","source":"url"}` and `{"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/users/789","source":"url"}` — byte-identical naming to bun, which matches the repo's own e2e assertion `transactionEvent?.transaction === 'GET /users/6'` (dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/solidstart-2/tests/performance.server.test.ts:6). WHAT DID NOT REFUTE IT: the other trace lifecycle (stream is strictly worse — the segment collapses to `GET`, `source: "url"`), a different init placement (the nitro plugin is the only shape SolidStart 2 supports; there is no `--import` preload in this build), and the bundler wiring (`sentrySolidStart()` has no route-naming knob; `@sentry/solidstart` does not re-export `setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute`, only `getActiveSpan`/`getRootSpan`/`updateSpanName`). WHAT DOES REFUTE IT, in app code only (see workaround): renaming the root span from inside the SolidStart request gives correct parameterized names on bun, in both lifecycles, and identically on node. bun/static (r2): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route",...} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route",...} bun/stream (r4): {"name":"GET /users/:id","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.nitro.srvx","source":"route","http_route":"/users/:id"} {"name":"GET /api/users/:id","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.nitro.srvx","source":"route","http_route":"/api/users/:id"} node/static (r6): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","source":"route"} / {"name":"GET /api/users/:id","source":"route"} Residual after the workaround: the child h3/middleware spans keep the raw URL (`middleware GET /users/456`, `http.server GET /users/456`) in both lifecycles; only the segment/transaction name is fixed. Workaround: Rename the root span from inside the SolidStart request. Works on bun and node, in both trace lifecycles, no SDK change. src/setServerRouteName.ts: import * as Sentry from '@sentry/solidstart'; export function setServerRouteName(method: string, route: string): void { const activeSpan = Sentry.getActiveSpan(); const rootSpan = activeSpan && Sentry.getRootSpan(activeSpan); if (!rootSpan) return; rootSpan.setAttribute('http.route', route); rootSpan.updateName(`${method} ${route}`); rootSpan.setAttribute('sentry.segment.name.source', 'route'); } Page routes, once in src/app.tsx inside the Router root (runs during SSR, inside the request's async context): function ServerRouteName() { if (isServer) { const pattern = useCurrentMatches().at(-1)?.route.pattern; // '/users/:id' const method = getRequestEvent()?.request.method ?? 'GET'; if (pattern) setServerRouteName(method, pattern); } return null; } // <SentryRouter root={props => (<MetaProvider><ServerRouteName />...)}> (`useCurrentMatches` from '@solidjs/router', `getRequestEvent`/`isServer` from 'solid-js/web'.) API routes (`src/routes/api/**`) are not rendered by the router, so each handler calls it itself: export function GET(event) { setServerRouteName('GET', '/api/users/:id'); ... } Alternative with no app code: move the endpoint to a nitro-native route under `server/routes/` (with `nitro({ serverDir: './server' })`); those get `GET /nitro/users/:id`, `source: "route"` automatically on bun. Not an option for SolidStart pages.
isolation✓* works-waThree concurrent `/api/iso?tag=alpha|beta|gamma` requests all produced events tagged `probe_tag: gamma` and all shared one trace id `b50f8a470d9a4d4888e6b2f9d62fedb6` — which was the same trace id every request in that whole process used, before and after, and the stale gamma tag leaked into later unrelated requests. The identical build on node gives three distinct trace ids and the correct tag per event. Root cause: on bun the node:http server instrumentation never fires (node emits three http.server spans per request, bun only two — the `Http` integration's outer span is missing), so nothing forks the isolation scope or starts a per-request trace, and everything falls back to the process-global propagation context. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. The reported breakage reproduces exactly with the docs-shaped wiring, and it is fixed by one line in the nitro plugin: adding `bunHttpServerIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun` to the `Sentry.init()` options. `@sentry/bun` on develop ships this integration precisely for this gap and its own `init()` enables it by default; `@sentry/solidstart` (which calls `@sentry/node`'s `init`) does not. Root cause confirmed at the source: server-side request isolation lives only in `httpServerIntegration`, which does `subscribe(HTTP_ON_SERVER_REQUEST, ...)` on the `http.server.request.start` node:http diagnostics channel (`packages/node/src/integrations/http/httpServerIntegration.ts:151`, channel name at `packages/core/src/integrations/http/constants.ts:3`). Bun does not publish that channel, so `instrumentServer()` (`packages/core/src/integrations/http/server-subscription.ts:96`) — the code that clones the isolation scope and calls `continueTrace` — never runs. `@sentry/nitro`'s h3/srvx `dc.tracingChannel` subscribers do fire on bun, which is why spans exist, but they only call `startInactiveSpan` and never fork isolation. `packages/bun/src/integrations/bunHttpServer.ts:88-95` documents the same diagnosis and closes it by patching `http.Server.prototype.emit` and handing the server to the same core instrumentation. EXACT CHANGE (server/plugins/sentry.ts): import { bunHttpServerIntegration } from '@sentry/bun'; import * as Sentry from '@sentry/solidstart'; import { definePlugin } from 'nitro'; export default definePlugin(() => { Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static', integrations: [bunHttpServerIntegration()] }); }); plus `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bun-10.67.0.tgz` alongside the other tarballs. Workaround: Add `@sentry/bun` as a dependency and pass `bunHttpServerIntegration()` in the `integrations` array of the `Sentry.init()` call in `server/plugins/sentry.ts`. It patches `http.Server.prototype.emit` to hand each nitro node:http server to the same core request instrumentation the Node SDK gets from the `http.server.request.start` diagnostics channel that bun does not publish, which restores the per-request isolation scope and per-request trace. Use `bunHttpServerIntegration({ spans: false })` if you want to keep only nitro's own h3/srvx spans instead of also getting the core `http.server` span (node emits that span too, so the default is the parity choice). The integration no-ops on node (`process.versions.bun` guard), so a single build runs on both runtimes.
incoming trace✓* works-waA request carrying `sentry-trace: 12345678901234567890123456789012-1234567890abcdef-1` plus a matching baggage header produced `GET /api/hello` on the process-global trace id, with no `parent_span_id`. Same cause as isolation: the srvx/h3 tracing channels only start spans, nothing calls continueTrace, and the node:http layer that would has no effect under bun. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. The reported diagnosis is right about the mechanism but wrong that nothing can fix it: the SDK already ships the fix, `bunHttpServerIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun`, and adding it to the existing `Sentry.init()` restores incoming-trace continuation (and per-request isolation) to full node parity, with no change to the build, the preset, or the entry shape. ROOT CAUSE, isolated (probe $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-solidstart-bun-incomingtrace/dc-probe.mjs): node dc-probe.mjs -> {"runtime":"node","hits":["start:/probe","finish"],"hasTracingChannel":true} bun dc-probe.mjs -> {"runtime":"bun","hits":[],"hasTracingChannel":true} Bun 1.4.0's `node:http` never publishes the `http.server.request.start` diagnostics channel that `@sentry/node`'s `httpServerIntegration` subscribes to (packages/core/src/integrations/http/constants.ts:3, packages/node/src/integrations/http/httpServerIntegration.ts `wrapServerEmitRequest`, which is where `propagation.extract` + the isolation scope happen). It is the node:http path that matters here, not Bun.serve: the nitro `node-server` preset resolves `srvx` through the `node` export condition at build time, so `.output/server/_libs/srvx.mjs` starts with `import "node:http"` and contains zero `Bun.serve` references even when run under bun. The nitro srvx/h3 tracing channels (packages/nitro/src/runtime/hooks/captureTracingEvents.ts) really do only `startInactiveSpan`, so with no continuation upstream every request lands on the process-global propagation context. The exact change (app-side, no SDK patch) === In app/server/plugins/sentry.ts, right after Sentry.init(): import dc from 'node:diagnostics_channel'; (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>).__sentryPinnedChannels = [ 'mysql2:query', 'mysql2:execute', 'mysql2:connect', 'mysql2:pool:connect', 'orchestrion:mysql:query', 'orchestrion:mysql2:query', 'orchestrion:mysql2:execute', ].map(name => dc.tracingChannel(name)); A/B on the IDENTICAL build (`npx vite build`, then `PORT=<p> SENTRY_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:45123/ SENTRY_LIFECYCLE=static [PIN_CHANNELS=1] bun .output/server/index.mjs`), sink lines verbatim: --- NO PIN (vrun-h-final-nopin.log): {"n":"GET /api/db","spans":["middleware GET /api/db","http.server GET /api/db"]} --- PIN (vrun-i-final-pin.log): {"n":"GET /api/db","spans":["middleware GET /api/db","http.server GET /api/db","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]} Same for the `mysql` (v2.x) driver, which needs orchestrion build-time injection rather than mysql2's own channels (vrun-e-bun-pin-static-both.log): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/db-mysql1","spans":["middleware GET /api/db-mysql1","http.server GET /api/db-mysql1","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]} Works on both lifecycles. traceLifecycle 'stream' with the pin (vrun-f-bun-pin-stream.log): {"t":"span","items":["middleware GET /api/db","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users","http.server GET","http.server GET","middleware GET /api/sentinel"]} === 2. Root cause: bun drops diagnostics_channel subscriptions on GC === Not an injection problem. deep/verify4-M-solidstart-bun-dbspans/dctest3.mjs subscribes three ways without keeping a reference to the channel object, forces GC, then publishes: $ bun dctest3.mjs -> {"runtime":"bun","plainSubscribe":0,"channelSubscribe":0,"tracing":0} $ node --expose-gc dctest3.mjs -> {"runtime":"node","plainSubscribe":1,"channelSubscribe":1,"tracing":1} bun 1.4.0 collects a channel that still has subscribers when nothing else holds it; node keeps subscribed channels alive. The SDK subscribes eagerly on Bun (packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/instrumentation.ts: "Bun and Deno have no such channel limit ... there we just subscribe immediately") and then discards the channel: subscribeMysql2DiagnosticChannels -> bindTracingChannelToSpan(tracingChannel(name), ...) throws away the returned handle (packages/server-utils/src/integrations/mysql2/mysql2-dc-subscriber.ts:93-126, packages/server-utils/src/tracing-channel.ts:120,200). Between the nitro plugin's Sentry.init() and the first request bun GCs, so the subscription is gone before mysql2 publishes. This is generic: every channel-based integration on bun is exposed, not just db. === 3. The SDK-side one-liner also fixes it, with zero app changes === Patched node_modules/@sentry/server-utils/build/esm/tracing-channel.js to retain what it subscribes to (`const __SENTRY_RETAINED_CHANNELS__ = []` + `__SENTRY_RETAINED_CHANNELS__.push(handle.channel, channel)` after `handle.channel.subscribe(subscribers)`), rebuilt, ran WITHOUT the app pin (vrun-g-bun-sdkretain-nopin.log): {"t":"transaction","n":"GET /api/db","spans":["middleware GET /api/db","http.server GET /api/db","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]} {"t":"transaction","n":"GET /api/db-mysql1","spans":["middleware GET /api/db-mysql1","http.server GET /api/db-mysql1","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]} The patch was reverted afterwards (original kept at tracing-channel.orig.js) and the final .output is the unpatched baseline, so a re-run reproduces the broken/fixed A/B above. === 4. What the original report got wrong === - "mysql2 is externalized by nitro, so build-time injection never sees it" — false. The stock build bundles and transforms it: .output/server/_ssr/promise-4o3jIiz1.mjs contains `dc.tracingChannel("mysql2:query")` (x5 channels) and `globalThis.__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION_INJECT__ = orchestrionModuleInjected("mysql2", mysql2Integration)`. The `mysql` v2 driver chunk .output/server/_ssr/db-mysql1-*.mjs contains `orchestrion:mysql:query`. No `ssr.noExternal` needed. - "[Sentry] Bundler plugin ran, injected libraries=[]" is a red herring: mysql2 >= 3.20 is a `registrationOnly` orchestrion entry (packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/config/mysql2.ts) and publishes its own channels, so an empty list says nothing about whether db spans can work. - "No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks" is irrelevant here — the runtime hook is only a second path to injection, and the bundler already did the job. === 5. Not tested === bun 1.3.14 (the CI pin at $SCRATCH/bun1314 no longer exists on disk), so I cannot say whether this is a bun 1.4.0 regression. Commands to rerun: `PORT=45123 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs &`; `cd app && npx vite build`; `PORT=45131 SENTRY_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:45123/ SENTRY_LIFECYCLE=static bun .output/server/index.mjs` (no db spans) vs the same with `PIN_CHANNELS=1` (db spans); `curl http://127.0.0.1:45123/__items`.
Workaround: Hold a strong reference to the diagnostics channels after Sentry.init() in server/plugins/sentry.ts, so bun's GC cannot unsubscribe the SDK: `import dc from 'node:diagnostics_channel'; globalThis.__sentryPinnedChannels = ['mysql2:query','mysql2:execute','mysql2:connect','mysql2:pool:connect'].map(n => dc.tracingChannel(n));` (add 'orchestrion:mysql:query' for the `mysql` v2 driver, and the matching 'orchestrion:<lib>:<event>' names for other instrumented libraries). Works identically as a `bun --preload pin.mjs .output/server/index.mjs` file if you cannot touch the nitro plugin. The proper fix belongs in the SDK: `bindTracingChannelToSpan` must retain the channel it subscribes to (verified to work).

Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions SolidStart on Bun. `grep -rin "bun" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/` returns zero hits across index.mdx, install/, features/ and profiling/; `grep -rin "solid" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/` also returns zero hits. The SolidStart guide's only front-matter runtime signal is `categories: [browser, server]` plus a beta warning (~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/index.mdx:5-14), and the Bun guide is scoped to `sdk: sentry.javascript.bun` (~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx:3). The solidstart-guide hits for "bun" that a broad grep turns up are all unrelated platform-includes (feature flags, sourcemaps). So the docs neither promise nor warn about this combination.

Documented: no

A page must say the SolidStart 2 nitro node output runs on Bun 1.4.0 as `bun .output/server/index.mjs` and give the Bun equivalent of the `node --import ./.output/server/instrument.server.mjs` start command documented at index.mdx:309-310. It must state that on Bun, with the documented setup alone, requests are not isolated (every request shares one trace and one scope, so tags and user leak between concurrent requests), incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` is not continued, and outgoing `fetch()` produces no `http.client` span and sends no trace headers — because Bun does not emit the `http.server.request.start` diagnostics channel and its native fetch does not publish undici's channels. The fix: install `@sentry/bun` alongside `@sentry/solidstart` and add `bunHttpServerIntegration()` and `fetchIntegration()` to the `Sentry.init()` in `server/plugins/sentry.ts` (guard the fetch one on the runtime so a Node deployment of the same build does not get two spans). For database spans it must say only drivers publishing their own `node:diagnostics_channel` events (mysql2 3.20.0+) are recorded on Bun, and only if the driver is loaded at startup — add `import 'mysql2/promise';` as the first import of `server/plugins/sentry.ts` — because Bun's GC otherwise collects the SDK's subscriptions; drivers Sentry instruments by build-time code injection are not recorded at all. Two further observed facts hold on Node as well and belong on the SolidStart guide itself: server transactions are named from the raw request URL (`GET /users/456`, `source: "url"`) rather than the route pattern, because SolidStart mounts its whole app as a single Nitro catch-all so the SDK's Nitro route parameterization never fires; and errors thrown in a file API route (`src/routes/api/*.ts`) or during page render are turned into a 500 by SolidStart's internal h3 app before nitro's error hook, so no event is sent — only `withServerActionInstrumentation`, or a user-supplied h3 middleware via `createMiddleware`, captures them.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/solidstart.mdx (new); plus route-naming and unreported-server-error notes on docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/index.mdx

~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/index.mdx:5-8 (`categories: [browser, server]`, no runtime named); solidstart/index.mdx:289 ("add an `--import` flag to the `NODE_OPTIONS` environment variable"); solidstart/index.mdx:309-310 (`start:node`: `node --import ./.output/server/instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`); ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/install/cli-import.mdx:33,45. `grep -rin bun` over guides/solidstart/ and `grep -rin solid` over guides/bun/ both return 0.

Root cause for the four broken capabilities is one thing: SolidStart 2's nitro output bundles srvx's **node** adapter (`.output/server/_libs/srvx.mjs` contains `node_modules/srvx/dist/adapters/node.mjs`), so the server is node:http-shaped, but @sentry/node's node:http server instrumentation has no effect under bun. Node emits three http.server spans per request (node:http outer + srvx + h3); bun emits only two (srvx + h3). The node:http layer is what forks the isolation scope and calls continueTrace, so on bun there is no per-request isolation, no per-request trace, and no trace continuation. @sentry/nitro's own srvx/h3 tracing channels do fire on bun (spans, parenting and nesting are all correct within a request) but they only start spans, they never fork isolation or continue a trace. Second, independent bun gap: `module.registerHooks` is unavailable, so `No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping` — the runtime path that instruments externalized deps like mysql2 is gone. The build-time replacement (`sentryOrchestrionPlugin` inside `sentrySolidStart()`) reported `injected libraries=[]` in every build I made, including one where I forced `ssr: { noExternal: ['mysql2'] }` and verified mysql2 really was inlined into `.output/server/_ssr/ssr.mjs`. So on this stack there is currently no working path to db spans on bun; a `@sentry/bun` plugin build is not applicable because the server is built by vite/nitro, not `Bun.build`. Not bun-specific, and worth flagging separately for the SolidStart guide regardless of runtime: (a) a plain `throw` in a file API route is never reported — only server functions wrapped in `withServerActionInstrumentation` are; (b) transaction/span source is always `url`, never `route`, even for `/users/[id]`, which under the develop default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` collapses the http.server span name to the bare method. Also observed: `contexts.runtime.name` is reported as `node` when running under bun (bun sets process.versions.node), so bun-run events are indistinguishable from node-run events in Sentry. Port hazard worth passing on: my first attempt used 41501/41502, both already held by another agent's node processes. Bun's srvx binds `[::]` while node binds `127.0.0.1`, so both listeners coexisted and every `curl 127.0.0.1` silently hit the *other* agent's server, producing plausible-looking wrong responses. Verify with `lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN` before trusting any result. @sentry/nitro's peer range (`>=3.0.0-0 <4.0.0 || 3.0.260311-beta || 3.0.260415-beta`) does not accept `nitro@3.0.260610-beta`, which is what the repo's own solidstart-2 e2e app pins; npm refuses without `--legacy-peer-deps`. That is a real install-time papercut for anyone following a docs page with npm.

Setup the docs would have to show

Packages (npm install into the task dir, then run with Deno; `deno.json` has `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}` so the SDK's Deno import hook can see a real local `node_modules`):

  npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-deno-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-hono-10.67.0.tgz \
              $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz \
              $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz hono@4 mysql@2

Entry file (`main.ts`), init happens inside the middleware, no separate instrument file:

  import "@sentry/deno/import";              // FIRST line, required only for db/library spans
  import { Hono } from "hono";
  import { sentry } from "@sentry/hono/deno";
  import * as Sentry from "@sentry/hono/deno";   // re-exports all of @sentry/deno
  import mysql from "mysql";

  const conn = mysql.createConnection({ host: "127.0.0.1", port: 3307, user: "root", database: "app" }); // MODULE scope

  const app = new Hono();
  app.use("*", sentry(app, { dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: "static" }));
  app.get("/users/:id", c => c.json({ id: c.req.param("id") }));
  Deno.serve({ port: 52818, hostname: "127.0.0.1" }, app.fetch);

Run command:

  deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main.ts

Notes on the wiring a docs page would have to add beyond today's page: (a) `@sentry/hono` must be installed into a local `node_modules` (`deno add npm:@sentry/hono` / `npm install @sentry/hono`), (b) `deno.json` needs `nodeModulesDir` set (`"manual"` with a prepared `node_modules`, or `"auto"`), (c) `import "@sentry/deno/import";` as the first line if you want database/library spans, (d) the `--allow-*` set above (`--allow-sys` and `--allow-read` are needed by the SDK).
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksAn error thrown in `app.get("/error")` reaches Sentry as an unhandled event with mechanism `auto.http.hono.context_error`, `handled:false`, stack frames with context lines, `sdk: sentry.javascript.hono`, and `transaction: "GET /error"`. Hono itself swallows it into a 500 response (curl saw 500, no crash), but the middleware's `responseHandler` reads `context.error` so nothing is lost; the server span is marked `internal_error`. Same in both lifecycles.
route names✓ works`/users/:id` produced `GET /users/:id` with `transaction_info.source: "route"` and `http.route: "/users/:id"` in static lifecycle, and in the default stream lifecycle the `http.server` span carried name `GET /users/:id`, `sentry.segment.name.source: route` and `http.route: /users/:id`. This is the Hono middleware overriding the method-only name that `@sentry/deno`'s `Deno.serve` instrumentation would otherwise give.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent requests to `/tag/alpha|beta|gamma`, each doing `Sentry.setTag` then a 60ms await then `captureException`, produced three events with exactly one tag each (`reqtag: alpha|beta|gamma`) and three distinct trace ids; each event's trace id matches its own transaction's trace id. No cross-talk. Static lifecycle.
incoming trace✓ worksA request with `sentry-trace: aaaa…aaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` plus a matching baggage header produced a transaction with `trace_id: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` and `parent_span_id: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`, so the trace is continued. Static lifecycle.
outgoing fetch✓* works-waA global `fetch()` from inside a handler to a local recorder produced NO `http.client` span (the `/downstream` transaction has `spans: []`) and the recorder saw NO `sentry-trace` and NO `baggage` header. This is Deno-level finding K2, unchanged by Hono, and it holds in both lifecycles and with or without the import hook. Contrast probe in the same app: `node:http` `http.get` from the same handler DID produce `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:52817/rec/downstream-http` and did send both headers, so only the WinterCG `fetch` path is uninstrumented. verified: works-after-all Reproduced exactly, and found the root cause in the source plus a working userland fix. PORT=41873 node recorder.mjs & APP_PORT=41881 REC_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:41873 TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:41872/ LIFECYCLE=static VARIANT=baseline \ deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main.ts BASELINE (documented wiring, `sentry(app, {...})` middleware, static lifecycle, hook ON) — claim reproduced: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /downstream","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.hono","spans":[]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /downstream-req","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.hono","spans":[]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /downstream-span","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.hono","spans":["function manual wrapper"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /downstream-http","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.hono","spans":["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41873/rec/downstream-http"]} Recorder (baseline): {"url":"/rec/downstream-fetch","sentryTrace":null,"baggage":null,"traceparent":null} {"url":"/rec/downstream-fetch-req","sentryTrace":null,"baggage":null,"traceparent":null} {"url":"/rec/downstream-fetch-inspan","sentryTrace":null,"baggage":null,"traceparent":null} {"url":"/rec/downstream-http","sentryTrace":"ea70df9c9f4e4ff29577fc577cdb407d-89e7ac74aea66012-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,...,sentry-sampled=true"} Variants tried that do NOT fix it: `traceLifecycle: 'static'` and `'stream'`; hook ON and hook OFF; `fetch(url)` and `fetch(new Request(url))`; the fetch wrapped in an explicit `Sentry.startSpan` (the manual span is recorded, the fetch inside it still produces no child span and no headers); `tracePropagationTargets: [/.*/]` explicitly set. Hono is irrelevant: the same `Deno.serve` handler shows the identical split between `fetch` (nothing) and `node:http` (span + headers). ROOT CAUSE (source, not inference): `@sentry/deno` ships no fetch integration at all. packages/deno/src/sdk.ts `getDefaultIntegrations()` lists denoServeIntegration + denoHttpIntegration (node:http diagnostics channels) and no fetch one, and packages/deno/src/index.ts exports none. `@sentry/bun` (packages/bun/src/integrations/fetch.ts) and `@sentry/cloudflare` (packages/cloudflare/src/integrations/fetch.ts) each ship a byte-for-byte equivalent `fetchIntegration` built only from `@sentry/core` exports (`addFetchInstrumentationHandler`, `instrumentFetchRequest`, `shouldPropagateTraceForUrl`, `isSentryRequestUrl`, `LRUMap`); Deno simply has no counterpart. So this is an SDK gap, not a Deno-runtime limitation. PROOF IT IS A GAP, NOT A RUNTIME LIMIT — two fixes, both verified working on Deno 2.9.0: (a) userland integration (fetch-integration.ts) using the same @sentry/core primitives, passed as `integrations: [denoFetchIntegration()]` to `sentry(app, {...})` (the Hono middleware merges user integrations with the defaults via buildFilteredIntegrations): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /downstream","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41873/rec/downstream-fetch"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /downstream-req","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41873/rec/downstream-fetch-req"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /downstream-span","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["function manual wrapper","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41873/rec/downstream-fetch-inspan"]} {"url":"/rec/downstream-fetch","sentryTrace":"bdf0ce2895fd4d70ab0f1a4af9ba5f26-89769c77dac4af77-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,sentry-public_key=public,sentry-trace_id=bdf0ce2895fd4d70ab0f1a4af9ba5f26,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fdownstream,sentry-sampled=true,sentry-sample_rate=1"} Also works in stream lifecycle and with the import hook removed (main-nohook.ts, LIFECYCLE=stream): {"type":"span","trace_id":"9f8ec3a4e99146fca9eba5c7eb84f25c","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","http.server GET /downstream"],"raw":[{"name":"GET 127.0.0.1","status":"ok","parent_span_id":"8de739a4baaa4459","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.http.fetch"},{"name":"GET /downstream","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.deno"}]} (b) shipped-package variant: `import { winterCGFetchIntegration } from "@sentry/vercel-edge"` and pass `integrations: [winterCGFetchIntegration()]`. Imports cleanly under Deno and works identically: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /downstream","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41873/rec/downstream-fetch"]} {"url":"/rec/downstream-fetch","sentryTrace":"23b38766306b4aa7820ff6af9f2f198f-982fd6c7f9eedf14-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,...,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fdownstream,sentry-sampled=true"} Verdict stays confirmed-broken: nothing in the documented wiring, no init placement, neither lifecycle and neither hook state produces the span or the headers. It only works once you add a fetch integration the SDK does not ship for Deno. Test coverage note: the repo's own Deno e2e app has a fetch test that does not cover this. dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/deno/tests/fetch.test.ts asserts only that the *manual* wrapper span exists (`description: 'test-outgoing-fetch', origin: 'manual'`) around the `fetch` in src/app.ts:135 — it never asserts an `http.client` child span or propagated headers, which is why the gap passes CI. There is no `hono` + Deno e2e app (only `hono-4` on Node and `deno`/`deno-streamed`). Docs today say nothing about it: `grep -i fetch` under ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/ hits only breadcrumbs.mdx:23 (`### fetch` breadcrumb section); the Deno guide has no integrations page listing a fetch integration, and the Hono guide's Deno tab (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hono/index.mdx:320-347) shows the plain `sentry(app, {...})` snippet with no mention of outgoing requests. Cleanup: all processes killed, node_modules removed.
Workaround: Add a fetch integration yourself, since `@sentry/deno` ships none. Either (a) install `@sentry/vercel-edge` and pass its shipped integration: import { winterCGFetchIntegration } from "@sentry/vercel-edge"; app.use("*", sentry(app, { dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, integrations: [winterCGFetchIntegration()] })); or (b) write a ~20-line integration from `@sentry/core` primitives (verified file: fetch-integration.ts in the probe dir): import { addFetchInstrumentationHandler, defineIntegration, getClient, instrumentFetchRequest, isSentryRequestUrl, LRUMap, shouldPropagateTraceForUrl } from "@sentry/core"; const urlMap = new LRUMap(100); const spans = {}; export const denoFetchIntegration = defineIntegration(() => ({ name: "DenoFetch", setupOnce() { addFetchInstrumentationHandler(d => { const client = getClient(); if (!client || isSentryRequestUrl(d.fetchData.url, client)) return; instrumentFetchRequest(d, () => true, url => shouldPropagateTraceForUrl(url, client.getOptions().tracePropagationTargets, urlMap), spans, { spanOrigin: "auto.http.fetch" }); }); }, })); Both give `http.client` spans and send `sentry-trace` + `baggage`, in both trace lifecycles and with or without the `@sentry/deno/import` hook. If you cannot add an integration, switch the outgoing call to `node:http` / `node:https`, which `denoHttpIntegration` already instruments. Real fix for the SDK: port packages/bun/src/integrations/fetch.ts (or packages/cloudflare/src/integrations/fetch.ts, they are identical and use only `@sentry/core`) to `packages/deno/src/integrations/fetch.ts` and add it to `getDefaultIntegrations()` in packages/deno/src/sdk.ts, plus an e2e assertion on an `http.client` span with propagated headers (today dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/deno/tests/fetch.test.ts only checks the manual wrapper span).
db spans✓ worksA module-scope `mysql` (mysql@2) connection queried inside `/db` produced `db SELECT id, name FROM users` as a child span in static lifecycle and `db SELECT users` in stream lifecycle (low-cardinality name, parent = the http.server span). Instrumentation path: the Deno import hook, `import "@sentry/deno/import";` as the first line of the entry. It WAS needed: with that single line removed and everything else identical, `/db` returns rows but the transaction has `spans: []`, and the SDK prints no warning.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info("hello from hono deno", { route: "/log" })` inside a handler arrived as a `log` envelope item `info: hello from hono deno` about 8s after the request (timer flush). Static lifecycle; logs are on by default, no `enableLogs` option needed.

Docs today

~/dev/sentry-docs does document Hono on Deno, but the snippet is incomplete for anything beyond the basics. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hono/index.mdx:12` claims support for "Cloudflare Workers, Node.js, Bun, and Deno"; `:89` gives the runtime peer dep as `deno add npm:@sentry/deno`; `:320-348` is the Deno tab: `import { sentry } from "@sentry/hono/deno"` + `app.use(sentry(app, {...}))` + `Deno.serve(app.fetch)`. That snippet is correct and works as written for errors, route names, isolation, trace continuation and logs. What it never mentions: (a) `import "@sentry/deno/import";` as the first line — the string `deno/import` appears nowhere in `docs/` or `platform-includes/` (0 hits), yet without it there are no database spans and no warning; (b) `deno.json` `nodeModulesDir`, which the import hook needs to transform npm packages; (c) the `--allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys` permission set; (d) the install block at `:44-58` only offers npm/yarn/pnpm tabs for `@sentry/hono` itself, with no `deno add npm:@sentry/hono` tab even though the runtime tab at `:89` has one. There is no Hono mention anywhere under `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/`.

Documented: partial

This is the only Deno cell with a real page, and the snippet at :320-348 is correct as far as it goes: errors, route names, isolation, incoming trace continuation, db spans and logs all worked exactly as written. Two things must be added. (1) Install: `deno add npm:@sentry/deno` at :89 is not sufficient for the observed working setup, which needed the packages installed with `npm install` into the project so a real on-disk `node_modules` exists, plus `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}` in `deno.json`, because the Deno SDK's import hook resolves through a local `node_modules`. The Deno tab must show the `deno.json` and the npm-based install, not just `deno add`. (2) Outgoing HTTP: a Deno tab caveat under tracing must state that `@sentry/hono/deno` does not instrument the global `fetch()` — an outgoing `fetch()` produces no `http.client` span and receives no `sentry-trace` or `baggage` header, so the downstream service starts a new trace; only `node:http`/`node:https` clients are traced automatically. This was re-verified as confirmed-broken in both `static` and `stream` trace lifecycles and with the Deno import hook both on and off. The page must ship the working restoration: add `@sentry/core` as a direct dependency, define a `denoFetchIntegration()` from its public primitives (`addFetchInstrumentationHandler`, `defineIntegration`, `getClient`, `instrumentFetchRequest`, `isSentryRequestUrl`), and register it as `sentry(app, { integrations: [denoFetchIntegration()] })` — that restores both the span and the propagation headers.

Ports: sink/recorder 52817, app 52818 (41337/47311 and 41338/47312 were already held by other agents' node and workerd processes; check with lsof before picking). All processes killed and `node_modules` removed before returning. Lifecycle attribution: errors, isolation, incoming trace, logs, outgoing fetch and the hook on/off db comparison came from `traceLifecycle: 'static'`; route names and db spans were additionally confirmed under the default `'stream'` lifecycle, where the `http.server` span already carries the parameterized name, `sentry.segment.name.source: route` and `http.route`, so the Hono middleware's naming does not depend on the lifecycle. Two things worth flagging beyond the capability list: 1. The `fetch` gap (K2) is the only real hole and it is invisible: a Hono handler calling `fetch` to another service produces no client span and, more importantly, propagates no `sentry-trace`/`baggage`, so distributed traces silently break at the first hop. `node:http` from the same handler works fully, which makes the gap look like a Deno-runtime `fetch` patching miss rather than a Hono issue. 2. The db-span dependency on `@sentry/deno/import` is a documentation gap, not a bug: it works, it is just undiscoverable, and the failure mode is silent (rows returned, no span, no debug warning even though the middleware ran). Deno's known K3 bug (`require('*.json')` failing under the hook, which breaks Express/Hapi/Fastify/Koa) did not bite here: Hono is pure ESM and `mysql@2` imports fine with the hook active. `@sentry/hono/deno` re-exports all of `@sentry/deno`, so `Sentry.setTag`, `Sentry.captureException`, `Sentry.logger` and `Sentry.getActiveSpan` are all available from the one specifier; no separate `@sentry/deno` import is needed in app code.

Elysia on Deno M-elysia-deno

Elysia 1.4.30 · Deno 2.9.0 (nodeModulesDir: "manual", Deno.serve + app.fetch) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Elysia runs on Deno unchanged: `new Elysia().get(...)` mounted with `Deno.serve({port}, app.fetch)`, deno.json `{"nodeModulesDir":"manual"}`, deps installed with npm. Two Sentry wirings exist and they behave very differently.

(A) The wiring a docs page would show today (@sentry/elysia, the documented package):
  npm install elysia@1 mysql@2 $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{elysia,bun,node,core,deno,opentelemetry,server-utils,server-runtime-injection}-10.67.0.tgz
  instrument.ts: `import "@sentry/deno/import";` then `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/elysia"; Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static'|'stream' })`
  app.ts: `import "./instrument.ts";` as the first line, `Sentry.withElysia(new Elysia()).get(...)`, `Deno.serve({port,hostname}, app.fetch)`
  run: `deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --allow-ffi app.ts`
  This loads and inits fine but is BROKEN for tracing/isolation: withElysia's `isBun()` guard is false on Deno, so it takes the Node branch that assumes an HTTP-instrumentation root span, and @sentry/bun does not instrument Deno.serve. Result: no root span, no isolation scope, no continueTrace.

(B) The wiring that actually works, but is not reachable through any public export:
  `import "@sentry/deno/import"; import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno"; Sentry.init({...})` plus
  `import { withElysia } from "./node_modules/@sentry/elysia/build/esm/withElysia.js";`
  @sentry/deno instruments Deno.serve and supplies the root span + isolation scope, and withElysia's Node branch then works exactly as intended. A docs page cannot show this today because @sentry/elysia's package entry re-exports all of @sentry/bun, and @sentry/deno exports no withElysia. Shipping it would need a `@sentry/elysia/deno` subpath or a withElysia re-export from @sentry/deno.

R2 (v4r2.ts, @sentry/deno init + `@elysiajs/node` adapter + app.listen, needs --unstable-net for Deno.listen reusePort): also correct — {"name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","sdk":"sentry.javascript.deno"}. R4 (v4r4.ts, the documented Node.js wiring on Deno: @sentry/elysia init + @elysiajs/node adapter): BROKEN the same way as A — Request/Parse/.../AfterResponse each their own `source":"custom"` transaction, sdk sentry.javascript.bun. So the deciding factor is which init runs, not the adapter or the lifecycle: `@sentry/elysia`'s init is `@sentry/bun`'s (packages/elysia/src/sdk.ts), which instruments neither `Deno.serve` nor Deno's `node:http`, and it additionally filters out `bunServerIntegration`, so nothing creates a root span. `withElysia`'s `isBun()` guard (`typeof Bun !== 'undefined'`, packages/elysia/src/withElysia.ts) is false on Deno, so it takes the "HTTP instrumentation already made a root span" branch. With `@sentry/deno` init that assumption holds and the whole path works unchanged. Minor, not runtime-specific: a `captureException` called inside the handler has no `transaction` field, because `updateRouteTransactionName` sets the isolation-scope name in onAfterHandle/onError, i.e. after the handler ran. Errors thrown out of the handler (onError path) do carry `"transaction":"GET /boom"`. Reference read-only: ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/elysia-{bun,node}/src/app.ts — both use `Sentry.init` from `@sentry/elysia`; there is no Deno e2e app for Elysia.
Workaround: On Deno, do not call `@sentry/elysia`'s `init()`. Init with `@sentry/deno` and take only `withElysia` from `@sentry/elysia` — both are public exports, no deep import into build/esm needed: import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno"; Sentry.init({ dsn: "...", tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }); import { withElysia } from "@sentry/elysia"; import { Elysia } from "elysia"; const app = withElysia(new Elysia()).get("/users/:id", ({ params }) => ({ id: params.id })); Deno.serve({ port: 3000 }, app.fetch); Works with `Deno.serve` + `app.fetch` and with the `@elysiajs/node` adapter + `app.listen()`, and in both `traceLifecycle: 'static'` and `'stream'`. Prepend `import "@sentry/deno/import";` as the first line only if you also want library (database, AI) spans. Cost of this wiring: events are tagged `sdk: sentry.javascript.deno` rather than an elysia SDK identifier, and Elysia-specific default-integration tuning in `@sentry/elysia`'s `init` is not applied (on Deno that tuning is a no-op anyway — it only removes `bunServerIntegration`).
isolation✓* works-waWiring (A): three concurrent /tag/:t requests plus a later sentinel all carried the same process-wide trace id (f694377a31684aa6a2a074082b4262e8, unchanged across every request for the process lifetime); the sentinel event inherited `reqtag: bbb` from another request and the `tagged-aaa` event carried transaction `GET /sentinel`. Cause: withElysia only calls withIsolationScope/continueTrace inside its isBun() branch. Wiring (B): correct, three distinct trace ids, each event carrying only its own tag. Static lifecycle. verified: works-after-all Could not refute, and the reporter understated it. Cause confirmed in the develop source: withElysia's app.wrap splits on isBun(); only the Bun branch calls withIsolationScope, continueTrace and startSpanManual, and the other branch assumes an ambient HTTP instrumentation already made a root span. On Deno getActiveSpan() is undefined, so every lifecycle phase span is created with no parent and becomes its own segment. Wiring A, static lifecycle, three concurrent tagged requests plus a sentinel: every transaction and event carries trace 997332243bf041728ef90a079c4ae195 and tags {"reqtag":"ccc"}, and request.url on every event, including the sentinel that was GET /sentinel, is http://127.0.0.1:36681/tag/ccc, the last request to run the Elysia onRequest hook. So url and transaction name bleed too, not only tags and trace id. Stream lifecycle: one trace id for all four requests, every phase span is_segment true, no root span. Wiring C (init from @sentry/deno, withElysia from the public @sentry/elysia entry) is correct in both lifecycles: four distinct trace ids, each event carrying only its own tag and its own url, transactions named GET /tag/:t with source route, and the Elysia lifecycle spans nested under the Deno root span. The reporter's deep import is unnecessary and its bare-specifier form does not resolve at all: @sentry/elysia's exports map has only the root and package.json, so importing the build subpath throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. Only a relative filesystem path works, which is a hack; importing the public entry is enough because @sentry/elysia loads fine under Deno as long as its init is never called. Under wiring C sdk.name is sentry.javascript.deno on both events and spans, so Elysia framework attribution is lost, because applySdkMetadata for elysia lives only in the init you are no longer calling.
Workaround: Initialise with @sentry/deno and keep withElysia from the public @sentry/elysia entry: Sentry.init from @sentry/deno, then withElysia(new Elysia()).get(...) served with Deno.serve({port}, app.fetch). denoServeIntegration is already a default integration in @sentry/deno and is publicly exported, so no extra integrations entry is needed; it wraps Deno.serve and does the isolation scope and trace continuation that withElysia's non-Bun branch assumes someone else did. Costs: sdk.name becomes sentry.javascript.deno and framework metadata is dropped, and Sentry helpers must come from @sentry/deno. Both namespaces resolve the single hoisted @sentry/core. The SDK fix is to widen the isBun gate to 'no ambient HTTP instrumentation', or to give @sentry/elysia's init a Deno path.

Sentry.init from @sentry/elysia is the Bun init with bunServerIntegration filtered out, and Deno.serve is not node:http, so nothing continues the trace. Wiring A, static lifecycle, request carrying sentry-trace 12345678901234567890123456789012-1234567890123456-1: {"type":"transaction","name":"Handle","op":"handler","source":"custom","trace_id":"e8c1d6eeb7a34df68651fdd2784c8889","sdk":"sentry.javascript.bun"} and the sentinel event on the same id. Downstream is wrong rather than absent: the outgoing fetch is instrumented and does send sentry-trace and baggage, but with the process-wide trace id, and the same wrong id is echoed back in the response headers.
