Workaround: Two verified. (1) Keep @sentry/elysia and mount the app yourself: Deno.serve({port}, request => Sentry.withIsolationScope(() => Sentry.continueTrace({ sentryTrace: request.headers.get('sentry-trace') || '', baggage: request.headers.get('baggage') }, () => Sentry.startSpan({ name: request.method, attributes: { 'sentry.op': 'http.server', 'sentry.source': 'url' } }, () => app.fetch(request))))). This keeps the Bun SDK's fetch instrumentation, so downstream propagation also works. (2) Init with @sentry/deno and deep-import withElysia from ./node_modules/@sentry/elysia/build/esm/withElysia.js (the package exports map has no subpath): incoming continuation works, outgoing fetch still carries no headers.

Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions Elysia on Deno. The Elysia guide at docs/platforms/javascript/guides/elysia/index.mdx:25 lists prerequisites as "Bun or Node.js 18+ (with @elysiajs/node adapter)" and its install/init snippets have only Bun and Node.js tabs (index.mdx:55, :59, :82, :111). The runtime section in platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:11-12 documents exactly two runtimes: "**Bun**: The SDK creates root server spans via Elysia's `.wrap()` API with `continueTrace` for trace propagation" and "**Node.js**: The SDK uses Node's HTTP instrumentation for root spans". Deno is the unlisted third case, and it is the one where neither mechanism fires. grep for "elysia" under docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/ returns nothing, and grep for "deno" under docs/platforms/javascript/guides/elysia/ returns nothing.

Documented: wrong

A page must state that Elysia 1.4 runs unchanged on Deno 2.9, mounted with Deno.serve and app.fetch, with nodeModulesDir manual and deps installed with npm, and that the wiring the guide shows today is wrong for this runtime. With Sentry.init from @sentry/elysia, route names, isolation and incoming trace continuation are all broken on Deno, because that init delegates to @sentry/bun, which does not instrument Deno.serve; every Elysia lifecycle phase becomes its own root transaction. The correct wiring is the Deno import hook, Sentry.init from @sentry/deno before Deno.serve, and only withElysia imported from @sentry/elysia. Separately, the Deno SDK does not instrument global fetch; add a fetch integration for http.client spans and trace headers. With that wiring, errors, database spans and logs work. The parameterized-route-names claim and the two-runtime list must both be corrected.

Page to write: Change platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:9-12 (add a Deno bullet) and :6 (qualify the route-name claim); change guides/elysia/index.mdx:25 and add Deno tabs to the install and configure snippets at :52-70 and :78-120; change common/configuration/integrations/fetchIntegration.mdx:1-12, whose Cloudflare-only scope the Deno run contradicts.

guides/elysia/index.mdx:25 (lists only Bun and Node 18+ with the node adapter); :52-70 install snippet has only Bun and Node tabs; :78-120 configure snippet shows Sentry.init from @sentry/elysia, which delegates to @sentry/bun and does not instrument Deno.serve; platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:9-12 enumerates exactly two runtimes and :6 claims parameterized route names; grep for deno over guides/elysia returns zero; common/configuration/integrations/fetchIntegration.mdx:1-12 is scoped to Cloudflare and claims it only works in Workers.

Root cause of the (A) failures is one line in packages/elysia/src/withElysia.ts: `function isBun() { return typeof Bun !== 'undefined'; }` gates the whole root-span / withIsolationScope / continueTrace block. On Deno that is false, so withElysia falls through to the Node branch `const activeSpan = getActiveSpan(); if (activeSpan) rootSpanForRequest.set(...)`, which silently does nothing because @sentry/bun does not instrument Deno.serve. Nothing warns; the app looks instrumented (spans do arrive) but every lifecycle span is its own root segment and the whole process shares one trace and one isolation scope for its entire lifetime. The condition should be "no HTTP-server instrumentation created a root span" rather than "is Bun". @sentry/deno already provides that root span and isolation scope, which is what makes (B) work end to end. Second bug seen in (A): events are tagged `sdk: sentry.javascript.bun` and `contexts.runtime.name: bun` while running on Deno. In packages/elysia/src/sdk.ts the object `options` is spread from `userOptions` BEFORE `applySdkMetadata(userOptions, 'elysia', ...)` runs, so the elysia metadata never reaches the client and the bun SDK identity survives; `getRuntime()` correctly returns a non-bun runtime but the runtime context is overwritten downstream by @sentry/bun. Third: withElysia is reachable only through @sentry/elysia's package entry, which re-exports the entirety of @sentry/bun. So the working Deno configuration cannot be written by a user following any public API; it needs a deep import into build/esm/withElysia.js. A `@sentry/elysia/deno` subpath (or re-exporting withElysia from @sentry/deno) would make (B) documentable. Environment notes: mysql2 is unusable on Deno whenever the @sentry/deno import hook is loaded (K3 confirmed, mysql2/lib/connection_config.js:13 requires a JSON file); mysql@2 works. Ports 43711 (sink), 43712 (app A), 43713 (recorder), 43714 (app B), 41338 (bare) were used; 41337 was already held by another agent. All four processes were killed and node_modules (123M) removed.

Express on Deno M-express-deno

Express 5.2.1 (router 2.x) · Deno 2.9.0 · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Express 5 runs on Deno unmodified. Full Sentry instrumentation (route names, handler spans, express error capture, db spans) requires the `@sentry/deno/import` hook, and that hook currently needs a one-line user-land workaround for denoland/deno#36240 or Express cannot even be imported.

Packages (npm install into the task dir, then symlink the develop SDK):
  npm install express@5 mysql@2
  ln -s $W/packages/{core,deno,server-runtime-injection,server-utils} node_modules/@sentry/

deno.json:
  { "nodeModulesDir": "manual" }

instrument-jsonfix.ts (loaded first, before any app import):
  import "@sentry/deno/import";
  import "./jsonfix.ts";              // <-- required, see below
  import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno";
  Sentry.init({ dsn: "...", tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: "static" });

jsonfix.ts (the "second load hook"; without it the app never boots):
  import * as Module from "node:module";
  Module.registerHooks({
    load(url, context, nextLoad) {
      const result = nextLoad(url, context);
      if (url.endsWith(".json") && result.format !== "json") result.format = "json";
      return result;
    },
  });

app.ts:
  import "./instrument-jsonfix.ts";
  import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno";
  import express from "express";
  import mysql from "mysql";
  const conn = mysql.createConnection({ host: "127.0.0.1", port: 3307, user: "root", database: "app" }); // module scope
  const app = express();
  app.get("/users/:id", ...); app.listen(41733, "127.0.0.1", ...);

Run:
  deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys app.ts

No `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` call is needed (and none is exported from `@sentry/deno`); the channel-based `expressIntegration()` in the default set captures route errors on its own once the hook is active.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksWith the import hook + jsonfix, a throw in `app.get('/error')` reaches Sentry as an unhandled event with mechanism `auto.http.express` (handled:false), correct `transaction: "GET /error"`, request url and context lines; Express still returns 500 to the client. Without the import hook the error is NOT captured at all — Express's default error handler swallows it and only Deno's stderr shows the stack. Importing `setupExpressErrorHandler` from `@sentry/server-utils` restores capture without the hook (mechanism `auto.middleware.express`), but `@sentry/deno` does not re-export it, so there is no supported no-hook path. Both lifecycles.
route names✓ workstraceLifecycle 'static': transaction `GET /users/:id`, op `http.server`, source `route`, plus a child `handler /users/:id`. traceLifecycle 'stream': span `http.server GET /users/:id` with `http.route: /users/:id`. Requires the hook: without it every transaction is `GET /users/42` with source `url` and zero child spans.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent GET /iso/{alpha,beta,gamma} (each setTag('who', tag), random 60-120ms await, then captureException) produced three events, each carrying only its own tag and its own distinct trace_id, matching its own request url. Stream lifecycle.
incoming trace✓ worksGET /users/9 with `sentry-trace: aaaa…aaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` and a matching baggage header produced an `http.server GET /users/:id` span with trace_id `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` and parent_span_id `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`. Stream lifecycle.
outgoing fetch✗ brokenA `fetch()` from inside the /downstream handler to a local recorder produced NO `http.client` span (stream lifecycle: only handler + http.server; static lifecycle: transaction `GET /downstream` with spans `["handler /downstream"]`) and the recorder saw `sentry-trace: null, baggage: null`. This is the known Deno K2 gap and it is not fixed by the Express instrumentation; distributed tracing out of an Express-on-Deno handler is dead unless the user switches to node:http. verified: confirmed-broken Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-express-deno-outgoingfetch/ (express@5.2.1, symlinked develop SDK, deno.json `{"nodeModulesDir":"manual"}`, `@sentry/deno/import` + the deno#36240 jsonfix load hook). REPRODUCED (default integrations, stream lifecycle) — `bash run-b.sh baseline stream 52121`: {"type":"span","items":["handler /downstream","http.server GET /downstream"],"raw":[{"name":"/downstream","origin":"auto.http.express"},{"name":"GET /downstream","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.server"}]} recorder: {"url":"/hit-fetch","sentry-trace":null,"baggage":null,"traceparent":null} Same request via node:http in the same app does get a span and headers: {"type":"span","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","handler /downstream-http","http.server GET /downstream-http"] ... origin "auto.http.client"} recorder: {"url":"/hit-nodehttp","sentry-trace":"befad6f8...-983bab417e96d0e1-1","baggage":"...sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fdownstream-http,sentry-sampled=true..."} REFUTED, the "dead unless you switch to node:http" part. Root cause is not Express and not Deno: `packages/deno/src/sdk.ts` `getDefaultIntegrations()` simply ships no fetch integration. `packages/bun/src/integrations/fetch.ts` and `packages/cloudflare/src/integrations/fetch.ts` are byte-for-byte equivalent, runtime-agnostic, and built only from `@sentry/core` exports (`addFetchInstrumentationHandler`, `instrumentFetchRequest`, `isSentryRequestUrl`) that patch `globalThis.fetch`. Deno has `globalThis.fetch`, so that code works there unchanged. WORKS with a ~25-line user-land integration (userland-fetch-integration.ts) passed as `integrations: [denoFetchIntegration()]`. stream (`bash run-b.sh fetchint stream 52122`): {"type":"span","trace_id":"60217e698f7c4acb9cde5aeafa13dd4b","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","handler /downstream","http.server GET /downstream"],"raw":[{"name":"GET 127.0.0.1","status":"ok","parent_span_id":"9d8fab8b0d462c15","origin":"auto.http.fetch"},...]} recorder: {"url":"/hit-fetch","sentry-trace":"60217e698f7c4acb9cde5aeafa13dd4b-8e20fe10c8dc2b31-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,sentry-public_key=public,sentry-trace_id=60217e698f7c4acb9cde5aeafa13dd4b,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fdownstream,sentry-sampled=true,sentry-sample_rate=1"} static (`bash run-b.sh fetchint static 52123`): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /downstream","op":"http.server","source":"route","spans":["handler /downstream","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:52118/hit-fetch"]} Trace ids match the server span, the client span is a child of the express handler span, and both lifecycles behave. ALSO WORKS with zero custom code by importing the shipped Cloudflare one on Deno (`instrument-cf.ts`, `bash run-c.sh app-cf.ts stream 58221 58222 58223 cf-stream`): `import { fetchIntegration } from "@sentry/cloudflare"` → {"type":"span","trace_id":"89938fe80bac42db8a0094aa5d43476a","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","handler /downstream","http.server GET /downstream"] ... origin "auto.http.fetch"} recorder: {"url":"/hit-fetch-cf","sentry-trace":"89938fe80bac42db8a0094aa5d43476a-bc38198b4153b049-1","baggage":"...sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fdownstream..."} It proves the mechanism but is not a wiring anyone should ship (pulls the Cloudflare SDK into a Deno app). So: the reported observation is correct for the default integration set, and the "known Deno K2 gap" is real, but it is a one-file omission in `@sentry/deno`, not a runtime limitation, and it is fully fixable today without touching the app's transport. Partial because nothing in the shipped `@sentry/deno` surface or in the docs offers this — no `fetchIntegration` is exported from `@sentry/deno`, and `denoHttpIntegration` is node:http-only (it subscribes to `node:diagnostics_channel`, so it can never see `fetch`). SDK fix, one PR: copy `packages/bun/src/integrations/fetch.ts` to `packages/deno/src/integrations/fetch.ts`, export `fetchIntegration` from `packages/deno/src/index.ts`, and add `fetchIntegration()` to `getDefaultIntegrations()` in `packages/deno/src/sdk.ts` next to `denoHttpIntegration()`. Ports 52117/52118 collided with another agent mid-run (run-c-*.log without a tag suffix); that run was discarded and rerun on 58221-58223, which is the evidence quoted above. All processes I started were killed. `node_modules` (express + 4 SDK symlinks) left in place so the probe reruns as-is.
Workaround: Add a fetch integration in user land. Create `userland-fetch-integration.ts`: import { addFetchInstrumentationHandler, defineIntegration, getClient, instrumentFetchRequest, isSentryRequestUrl } from "@sentry/core"; const spans: Record<string, any> = {}; export const denoFetchIntegration = defineIntegration(() => ({ name: "DenoUserlandFetch", setupOnce() { addFetchInstrumentationHandler((handlerData: any) => { const client = getClient(); if (!client || isSentryRequestUrl(handlerData.fetchData.url, client)) return; instrumentFetchRequest(handlerData, () => true, () => true, spans, { spanOrigin: "auto.http.fetch" }); }); }, })); then `Sentry.init({ ..., integrations: [denoFetchIntegration()] })`. Works on both trace lifecycles, produces `http.client` spans with origin `auto.http.fetch` parented under the Express handler span, and sends `sentry-trace` + `baggage` downstream. Switching the call site to `node:http` also works (that path is instrumented by `denoHttpIntegration`), but it is no longer necessary.
db spans✓ worksA module-scope `mysql@2` connection queried inside the handler produced `db SELECT id, name FROM users` as a child of `handler /db` under the request trace (static), and `db SELECT users` with the request trace_id (stream). Instrumentation path: the Deno import hook (`import "@sentry/deno/import"`), which was required — it is the same hook that needs the jsonfix workaround, so on Express there is no way to get db spans without also applying the workaround.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info('hello from express on deno', { route: '/log' })` inside the handler arrived as a log envelope (`info: hello from express on deno`) after the ~7s flush timer. Works with and without the import hook.

Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions Express on Deno, and no page anywhere mentions the Deno import hook. `grep -rni express docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/` returns nothing and `grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/express/` returns nothing. `grep -rn "@sentry/deno/import\|registerHooks" docs/ platform-includes/` returns nothing at all — the hook that every Express capability on Deno depends on is undocumented. The Deno guide (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:44 and :63) shows only `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno"; Sentry.init({...})`, i.e. exactly the no-hook configuration that in my run produced url-source transactions, no handler spans, no db spans and no error capture for Express routes. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/express/index.mdx:3-5 pins the Express guide to `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` with `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, so it only ever describes the Node SDK. The Deno guide has no framework section at all (no Express, Oak, Hono or Fresh). platform-includes/configuration/integrations/javascript.deno.mdx does not list `expressIntegration`, even though it is in `@sentry/deno`'s default integration set.

Documented: no

An Express-on-Deno page must exist, and before it can describe any capability it must document the `@sentry/deno/import` hook, which is currently undocumented repo-wide even though every Express capability on Deno depends on it. It must say: Express 5 runs on Deno unmodified; route names, handler spans, Express error capture and database spans all require `import "@sentry/deno/import"`; and that hook currently needs a one-line user-land workaround for denoland/deno#36240 (registering any module load hook makes `require('*.json')` compile as JavaScript) or Express cannot even be imported. It must show the workaround (a `Module.registerHooks` load hook that returns JSON sources as JSON, either the `readFileSync` form or the delegating `nextLoad` form) and the `deno.json` with `"nodeModulesDir": "manual"` plus an on-disk `node_modules`. With that in place errors, route names, isolation, incoming trace continuation, database spans and logs all work. The one remaining gap is outgoing HTTP: `@sentry/deno` instruments only `node:http`/`node:https`, so a native `fetch()` gets no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers. The page must ship the copy-paste integration rather than telling readers to switch clients — the verified guidance is explicitly not to swap to `node:http`, but to define an integration from public `@sentry/core` exports (`addFetchInstrumentationHandler`, `defineIntegration`, `getClient`, `instrumentFetchRequest`, `isSentryRequestUrl`) after `import "@sentry/deno/import"` and pass it to `Sentry.init`, which restores both the span and the headers.

Page to write: guides/deno/frameworks/express.mdx (new), plus a new "The Deno import hook" section in guides/deno/index.mdx (currently absent from :1-232) that the framework pages link to

`grep -rni express docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/` returns nothing and `grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/express/` returns 0 hits; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/express/index.mdx:4-5 declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` / `fallbackGuide: javascript.node` and :12 is a bare `<PlatformContent includePath="getting-started-node" />`, i.e. the whole guide is @sentry/node on Node; `grep -rn "@sentry/deno/import\|registerHooks" docs/ platform-includes/` returns nothing anywhere in the repo

Headline finding: Express on Deno is fully instrumentable on develop, but only via a workaround that no user could guess. 1. denoland/deno#36240 (K3) is confirmed and is fatal on Express: `import "@sentry/deno/import"` makes `require('./codes.json')` in `statuses` throw `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'`, so Express never imports. Express 5 crashes in `statuses`; the failure is not Express-specific but hits it first. 2. The "second load hook" fix works completely. A 6-line user-land `Module.registerHooks({ load })` that forces `format: "json"` for `.json` URLs (registered AFTER `@sentry/deno/import`) makes the entire path work: Express boots, and errors, route names, handler spans, isolation, incoming trace continuation, db spans and logs all behave. This is a small enough patch that the SDK could plausibly ship it inside `registerDiagnosticsChannelInjection()` for Deno (packages/server-runtime-injection/src/register.ts:123, the `mod.registerHooks({ resolve, load })` branch) rather than leaving it to users. That is the single highest-value fix for this cell. 3. The no-hook path is silently degraded, not just less detailed. Without the hook the SDK captures NOTHING for a thrown route error — Express's default handler swallows it and no warning is printed. Combined with the fact that the docs' Deno snippet is exactly the no-hook snippet, a user following the docs today gets an Express app whose 500s are invisible in Sentry. 4. `setupExpressErrorHandler` is exported from `@sentry/server-utils` (packages/server-utils/src/index.ts:56) but is not re-exported from `@sentry/deno` (packages/deno/src/index.ts has no such export). It works when imported from `@sentry/server-utils` directly (mechanism `auto.middleware.express`), so re-exporting it would give Deno users a supported no-hook fallback. 5. Outgoing `fetch` (K2) is the one hard gap: no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` on the wire, so an Express handler on Deno cannot continue a trace downstream. `@sentry/deno` ships `denoHttpIntegration`, so `node:http` clients are the only propagating option today. 6. `expressIntegration()` is already in the Deno default integration set (packages/deno/src/sdk.ts:48 via `getTracingIntegrations()`); it needed no explicit `integrations: []` entry. 7. Not re-derived (established in TOOLBOX): Deno fetch span/header gap (K2), Deno json-require crash (K3). Everything else above was observed in this run on Deno 2.9.0 / Express 5.2.1 / router 2.x / develop @ 10.67.0 via worktree symlinks. Cleanup: all five app processes, the sink and the recorder were killed (`kill $pid; wait $pid`); ports 41733/41734/41735 verified free. The 5.2 MB node_modules was kept so the probe is rerunnable.

Evidence and commands
### 1. Express 5 on Deno 2.9.0 WITHOUT Sentry — boots and serves
$ deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys bare.ts
PORT=51437
$ curl http://127.0.0.1:51437/users/42
{"id":"42"}

Fastify on Deno M-fastify-deno

Fastify 5.12.3 · Deno 2.9.0 (`deno` on PATH), @sentry/deno 10.67.0 from develop (6f2da7483d) tarballs · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Fastify 5 runs on Deno unchanged, and the develop @sentry/deno SDK instruments it with NO import hook and NO bundler step. The `@sentry/deno/import` hook must NOT be used: it breaks Fastify at import (K3).

1. `package.json` (`{"type":"module"}`) + `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-deno-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz fastify@5 mysql2@3`

2. `deno.json`:
```json
{
  "nodeModulesDir": "manual",
  "imports": { "@sentry/deno": "npm:@sentry/deno", "fastify": "npm:fastify", "mysql2": "npm:mysql2" }
}
```

3. `instrument.ts` (no `import "@sentry/deno/import"` line):
```ts
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno";
Sentry.init({ dsn: "...", tracesSampleRate: 1.0 /*, traceLifecycle: "static" */ });
```

4. `main.ts` — `import "./instrument.ts";` as the very first line, then `import Fastify from "fastify"`. Create DB pools at module scope. No `setupFastifyErrorHandler(app)` call is needed; `fastifyIntegration()` is already in `getErrorIntegrations()` and is on by default in the Deno SDK, and it hooks the `fastify.initialization` diagnostics channel that Fastify publishes itself.

5. Run: `deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main.ts`
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksA throw in `app.get('/error')` reaches Sentry as an unhandled event with mechanism `auto.function.fastify`, `handled: false`, correct `transaction: "GET /error"` and a `parent_span_id` linking it to the request span; source context lines are attached. Fastify still swallows the error at the wire level (client gets HTTP 500) but the SDK captures it via the integration's `onError` hook, and the http.server span gets `status: internal_error`. Same in both lifecycles.
route names✓ worksParameterized route `/users/:id` yields `GET /users/:id` with `source: "route"` and `http.route: /users/:id` under `traceLifecycle: 'static'`, and the identical `http.server | GET /users/:id` name plus `http.route=/users/:id` on the span envelope under the default `'stream'` lifecycle. No method-only fallback.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent GETs to `/iso/:tag` (alpha/bravo/charlie, each with a randomized 40-100ms await between `Sentry.setTag` and `captureException`) produced three events each carrying exactly one `probe_tag` and three distinct trace ids, with the matching transaction carrying the same single tag. No cross-request bleed. Lifecycle: static.
incoming trace✓ worksA request with `sentry-trace: aaaa...aaaa-1234567890abcdef-1` plus a `baggage` header produced a transaction with `trace_id: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` and `parent_span_id: 1234567890abcdef`. Lifecycle: static.
outgoing fetch✓* works-waA global `fetch()` from inside a Fastify handler produces NO `http.client` span and sends NO `sentry-trace`/`baggage` (recorder saw both headers null) — Deno K2 reproduced, and Fastify does not change it. A `node:http` request from the same handler DOES get `http.client | GET 127.0.0.1` and both headers, so `node:http`/`undici` is the working escape hatch. Confirmed in both lifecycles. verified: works-after-all The default is broken exactly as reported, but the capability is NOT unreachable: one line in `Sentry.init({ integrations: [...] })` gives a full `http.client` span plus `sentry-trace`/`baggage` on a global `fetch()` from a Fastify handler, in both lifecycles. Fastify is irrelevant to the whole thing; this is a plain `@sentry/deno` gap. ROOT CAUSE (read from the develop source, not guessed): `@sentry/deno` ships NO fetch tracing integration. `packages/deno/src/sdk.ts:29-49` `getDefaultIntegrations()` lists `breadcrumbsIntegration()`, `denoServeIntegration()`, `denoHttpIntegration()`, ... and nothing that creates client spans for global `fetch`. `packages/deno/src/index.ts` exports no `fetchIntegration`/`winterCGFetchIntegration`. The fetch wrapper itself IS installed on Deno (`packages/deno/src/integrations/breadcrumbs.ts:48` calls `addFetchInstrumentationHandler`), it is only ever used for breadcrumbs. `@sentry/cloudflare` (`src/integrations/fetch.ts`, in its defaults at `src/baseSdk.ts:60`) and `@sentry/vercel-edge` (`src/integrations/wintercg-fetch.ts`) both have the missing piece; `@sentry/deno` never got it. The repo's own reference app agrees this is a known gap: `dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/deno/tests/fetch.test.ts` is named "Outbound fetch inside Sentry span creates transaction" and asserts only the hand-written `Sentry.startSpan({name:'test-outgoing-fetch'})` wrapper with `origin: 'manual'`. No test anywhere asserts an `http.client` span or a propagated header for a Deno `fetch`. A) BASELINE, REPRODUCED (Fastify 5.6.1 on Deno 2.9.0, @sentry/deno 10.67.0, `traceLifecycle:'static'`, no integrations) — recorder saw: {"url": "/downstream-fetch", "via": "global-fetch", "sentry-trace": null, "baggage": null, "traceparent": null} {"url": "/downstream-nodehttp", "via": "node-http", "sentry-trace": "408b4a4cc94d47a297eb379980467692-ba9ab9760e683345-1", "baggage": "sentry-environment=production,...,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fnodehttp,sentry-sampled=true,..."} sink: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /fetch","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["handler GET /fetch","handler fastify - route-handler"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /nodehttp","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["handler GET /nodehttp","handler fastify - route-handler","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41872/downstream-nodehttp"]} Same in `traceLifecycle:'stream'`: {"type":"span","items":["handler /fetch","handler /fetch","http.server GET /fetch"]} <- no http.client B) FIX 1, a SHIPPED Sentry integration, zero user code (`VARIANT=wintercg`, `traceLifecycle:'static'`): `import { winterCGFetchIntegration } from "@sentry/vercel-edge"` and pass `integrations: [winterCGFetchIntegration()]` to the Deno `Sentry.init`. It runs unmodified under Deno: {"url": "/downstream-fetch", "via": "global-fetch", "sentry-trace": "0b00717195da444987c0a8990af8e976-b2e77c2afd71b122-1", "baggage": "sentry-environment=production,sentry-public_key=public,sentry-trace_id=0b00717195da444987c0a8990af8e976,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Ffetch,sentry-sampled=true,sentry-sample_rand=0.3710628730989548,sentry-sample_rate=1"} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /fetch","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["handler GET /fetch","handler fastify - route-handler","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41872/downstream-fetch"]} This is the decisive result: the SDK code that fixes this already exists and needs only to be exported from, and defaulted in, `@sentry/deno`. It is not a Deno platform limitation. C) FIX 2, a ~25-line user-land integration built only from public `@sentry/core` exports (`addFetchInstrumentationHandler`, `instrumentFetchRequest`, `isSentryRequestUrl`, `shouldPropagateTraceForUrl`, `LRUMap`, `defineIntegration`) — avoids depending on `@sentry/vercel-edge`. `traceLifecycle:'static'`: {"url": "/downstream-fetch", "via": "global-fetch", "sentry-trace": "fd5dea1d9bb241ff972a772023fc5295-af78cd2e36dee448-1", "baggage": "...sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Ffetch,sentry-sampled=true..."} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /fetch","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["handler GET /fetch","handler fastify - route-handler","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41872/downstream-fetch"]} `traceLifecycle:'stream'` (default), same integration: {"type":"span","trace_id":"bde4f44873d24499a5728b68be6c2330","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","handler /fetch","handler /fetch","http.server GET /fetch"],"raw":[{"name":"GET 127.0.0.1","status":"ok","parent_span_id":"a1d0d5977655a2d4","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.http.fetch"}, ...]} The client span is correctly parented under the Fastify server segment and carries `origin: "auto.http.fetch"`; the stream-lifecycle name is the low-cardinality `GET 127.0.0.1`, as expected. Notes / things I did NOT do: I did not use `@sentry/deno/import` (K3 still applies, it breaks Fastify at import), no bundler, no build step. `tracePropagationTargets: [/.*/]` was set only because the downstream host is an IP literal; it is not part of the fix. Both fixes were confirmed against the same running Fastify app, so the "Fastify does not change it" half of the original report stands. Files (all re-runnable): $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-fastify-deno-outgoingfetch/run-b/ — `main.ts` (Fastify, /fetch /nodehttp /sentinel), `instrument.ts` (VARIANT=baseline|fetchint|wintercg), `fetch-integration.ts` (Fix 2), `recorder.mjs` (downstream header recorder, /__headers), `sink.mjs`, `deno.json`, `package.json`, logs `app-baseline-static.log`, `app-baseline-stream.log`, `app-fetchint-static.log`, `app-fetchint-stream2.log`, `app-wintercg-static.log`. Rerun: `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-deno-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-vercel-edge-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz fastify@5`, then `PORT=41871 node sink.mjs &`, `PORT=41872 node recorder.mjs &`, then `VARIANT=fetchint TRACE_LIFECYCLE=static SINK_PORT=41871 REC_PORT=41872 APP_PORT=41874 deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main.ts`. node_modules removed after the run.
Workaround: Add a fetch tracing integration to `Sentry.init` in the Deno app; nothing else changes. Cheapest form, using an already-shipped Sentry integration: ```ts import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno"; import { winterCGFetchIntegration } from "@sentry/vercel-edge"; Sentry.init({ dsn: "...", tracesSampleRate: 1.0, integrations: [winterCGFetchIntegration()] }); ``` If pulling in `@sentry/vercel-edge` is unacceptable, the same result comes from ~25 lines over public `@sentry/core` exports (verified, `fetch-integration.ts` in the probe dir): ```ts import { addFetchInstrumentationHandler, defineIntegration, getClient, instrumentFetchRequest, isSentryRequestUrl, LRUMap, shouldPropagateTraceForUrl } from "@sentry/core"; const spans = {}; const headersUrlMap = new LRUMap(100); export const denoFetchIntegration = defineIntegration(() => ({ name: "DenoUserlandFetch", setupOnce() { addFetchInstrumentationHandler(handlerData => { const client = getClient(); if (!client || isSentryRequestUrl(handlerData.fetchData.url, client)) return; instrumentFetchRequest(handlerData, () => true, url => shouldPropagateTraceForUrl(url, client.getOptions().tracePropagationTargets, headersUrlMap), spans, { spanOrigin: "auto.http.fetch" }); }); }, })); ``` Both work with and without Fastify and in both trace lifecycles. The previously reported `node:http`/`undici` escape hatch is still valid but is no longer necessary: callers can keep using global `fetch`. SDK fix this points at: export `fetchIntegration` from `@sentry/deno` and add it to `getDefaultIntegrations()` in `packages/deno/src/sdk.ts`, reusing `packages/cloudflare/src/integrations/fetch.ts` / `packages/vercel-edge/src/integrations/wintercg-fetch.ts` (they are already byte-for-byte siblings). Then extend `dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/deno/tests/fetch.test.ts`, which today only asserts a `origin: 'manual'` span, to assert an `http.client` span and a propagated `sentry-trace` header.
db spans✓ worksA module-scope `mysql2.createPool` queried inside the handler produced `db mysql2.pool.connect`, `db mysql2.connect` and `db SELECT id, name FROM users` (stream lifecycle names it `db | SELECT users`) nested under the fastify request span. Instrumentation path: NONE needed — no Deno import hook, no bundler plugin. mysql2 >= 3.20.0 publishes its own `mysql2:query`/`mysql2:connect`/`mysql2:pool:connect` diagnostics channels and `mysql2-dc-subscriber.ts` subscribes to them directly. This matters because the Deno import hook (which the toolbox says is required for mysql spans) cannot be used with Fastify at all.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info('hello from fastify on deno', { route: '/log' })` arrived as a `log` envelope after ~7s, correlated to the request trace id. Lifecycle: static.

Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions Fastify on Deno. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/fastify/index.mdx:4` declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` and `:5` `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, so the whole Fastify guide is @sentry/node only; grepping the guide for "deno" returns nothing. Conversely `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx` (232 lines) never says "fastify", never mentions any framework, and never mentions the `@sentry/deno/import` hook or `nodeModulesDir` — it only shows `import * as Sentry from "npm:@sentry/deno"` + `Sentry.init`. The only place the two strings co-occur anywhere in the repo is generic `PlatformSection supported=[...]` lists such as `docs/platforms/javascript/common/tracing/index.mdx:58`, which list `javascript.fastify` and `javascript.deno` as separate platforms, not as a combination. So the docs today say nothing about this combination, and in particular give no warning that the Deno import hook (the mechanism other guides would reach for to get library spans) makes Fastify fail to boot.

Documented: no

A Fastify-on-Deno page must exist and must state the opposite of what the other Deno framework pages need: Fastify 5 runs on Deno unchanged and `@sentry/deno` instruments it with NO import hook and NO bundler step, and `@sentry/deno/import` must NOT be used because it breaks Fastify at import. Setup is a `package.json` with `{"type":"module"}`, an npm install of `@sentry/deno` into a real `node_modules`, and `deno.json` with `"nodeModulesDir": "manual"`. With that, errors, route names, isolation, incoming trace continuation, database spans and logs all work. The single documented limitation must be outgoing HTTP: on Deno the SDK does not instrument the global `fetch()` — outgoing `fetch()` calls produce no `http.client` span and carry no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers, so traces do not continue into the downstream service. The page must say this is a Deno-runtime property, not a Fastify one, that it applies to every framework on Deno, and that it is not changed by the `traceLifecycle` setting. It must give the user-land fix that works on the shipped build today: register a fetch integration built from `@sentry/core` primitives (the `@sentry/bun` fetch integration body works verbatim, since it depends on nothing Bun-specific).

Page to write: guides/deno/frameworks/fastify.mdx (new), explicitly warning against `import "@sentry/deno/import"`; the shared fetch caveat belongs in guides/deno/index.mdx

docs/platforms/javascript/guides/fastify/index.mdx:4 `sdk: sentry.javascript.node`, :5 `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, :12-14 only `<PlatformContent includePath="getting-started-primer" />` + `getting-started-node`; `grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/fastify/` returns 0 hits; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-232 never mentions Fastify, any framework, the `@sentry/deno/import` hook, or `nodeModulesDir`

Headline: Fastify on Deno is the best-behaved framework/runtime pair I would expect from this matrix — six of seven capabilities work with zero build step and zero extra configuration, and the one failure (outgoing `fetch`) is a pre-existing Deno-wide gap (K2), not a Fastify problem. Two findings worth a docs page: 1. The instrumentation mechanism is diagnostics channels that Fastify and mysql2 publish themselves, so the Deno import hook is not just unnecessary, it is harmful. `fastifyIntegration()` subscribes to `fastify.initialization` (packages/server-utils/src/integrations/fastify/instrumentation.ts, comment at the `instrumentFastifyInstance` JSDoc), and it is already in `getErrorIntegrations()` (packages/server-utils/src/integrations/index.ts:60), which the Deno SDK includes by default (packages/deno/src/sdk.ts). Likewise `mysql2-dc-subscriber.ts` subscribes to `mysql2:query`/`mysql2:execute`/`mysql2:connect`/`mysql2:pool:connect`, published by mysql2 >= 3.20.0. That is why db spans appeared with no hook and no bundler — which is important, because K3 makes the hook unusable here. 2. K3 is reproduced exactly and is fatal, not degraded: adding `import "@sentry/deno/import";` makes the process die at import with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` from `ajv/dist/core.js:21` doing `require("./refs/data.json")`. Any docs page that tells Deno users to add the import hook for library instrumentation would break every Fastify app. Deno bug denoland/deno#36240. Other observations: - `setupFastifyErrorHandler(app)` is a documented step in the Fastify/Node guide but is a no-op on develop (packages/server-utils/src/integrations/fastify/index.ts, `@deprecated Remove this call`). Errors were captured without it. - Both fastify spans per request are `handler` op: one `<pluginName> - route-handler` wrapper and one route-URL-named span. Under stream lifecycle the sink shows them both as `handler | /users/:id`; under static as `handler GET /users/:id` + `handler fastify - route-handler`. - The `http.client` span from `node:http` is named `GET 127.0.0.1` (low-cardinality naming from the recent `feat: Emit low-cardinality http.client span names for node:http and undici` commit), not the full URL. - Ports 41337 (my first sink pick) was already taken by another agent; I moved to 47021/47022/47025 and 41339. - Everything ran on `deno` 2.9.0; I did not additionally exercise the CI pin at `$SCRATCH/deno283/deno`. - Processes killed and `node_modules` removed before returning.

Evidence and commands
Viability, bare Fastify with no Sentry (bare.log):
  READY http://127.0.0.1:53370

Koa on Deno M-koa-deno

Koa 3.2.1 + @koa/router 15.7.0 · Deno 2.9.0 (aarch64-apple-darwin), @sentry/deno 10.67.0 from develop (worktree tarball) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Koa runs on Deno, and the base Deno SDK works with it, but ONLY with the Deno import hook OFF. Wiring a docs page would have to show:

1) package.json + `npm install koa @koa/router mysql $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{deno,core,server-utils,server-runtime-injection}-10.67.0.tgz`
2) deno.json:
   { "nodeModulesDir": "manual",
     "imports": { "@sentry/deno": "npm:@sentry/deno", "koa": "npm:koa", "@koa/router": "npm:@koa/router", "mysql": "npm:mysql" } }
3) instrument.ts (must be evaluated before the Koa app module):
   import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno";
   Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: "static" });
4) main.ts: `import "./instrument.ts"; import "./app.ts";`  -- NO `import "@sentry/deno/import";`
5) Because the Koa integration cannot attach its own error handler, the app must register one by hand:
   app.on("error", err => Sentry.captureException(err, { mechanism: { type: "manual.koa.onerror", handled: false } }));
   (@sentry/deno does not export `setupKoaErrorHandler`; @sentry/node and @sentry/bun do. `attachKoaErrorHandler` is exported from @sentry/server-utils but is not a documented user API.)
6) Run: `deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main.ts`

Adding `import "@sentry/deno/import";` (the documented way to get library instrumentation on Deno) makes the process die at import time before the server ever listens. There is therefore no configuration in which Koa spans, Koa's auto error handler, or db spans are available on Deno.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓* works-waKoa swallows the route error into its own `app.onerror` default logger; with the SDK wired the standard way (no hook) NO event reaches Sentry for GET /boom, only a transaction with status internal_error. The Koa integration's auto error handler (attachKoaErrorHandler, driven by the `orchestrion:koa:callback` channel) never fires because the channel is only injected by the import hook, which crashes Koa. A hand-written `app.on('error', e => Sentry.captureException(e, {mechanism:{type:'manual.koa.onerror',handled:false}}))` does work and produces a correctly scoped event (right trace_id, transaction 'GET /boom'). @sentry/deno exports no `setupKoaErrorHandler`, unlike @sentry/node and @sentry/bun. traceLifecycle static and stream both. verified: works-after-all REFUTED — see above.
Workaround: Do not use `import "@sentry/deno/import"` with Koa on Deno (it crashes in `statuses` on `require('./codes.json')`). Instead inject the channels at build time: `npm i -D esbuild`, then bundle the entry with `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild` (`platform:'node'`, `format:'esm'`, `bundle:true`, `external:['@sentry/deno','@sentry/server-utils']`, and a `createRequire` banner), and run the emitted bundle with `deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys dist/main.js`. Koa's auto error handler, middleware/router spans and route-named transactions all work; no `app.on('error')` and no `setupKoaErrorHandler` needed.
route names✓* works-waNo route name at all. Under traceLifecycle 'static' the server transaction is named from the raw URL: name 'GET /users/42', source 'url'. Under the default 'stream' lifecycle the server span is just 'GET' with no `http.route` and no `sentry.source` attribute. The parameterized name '/users/:id' never appears because the Koa router instrumentation (which is what sets http.route via setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute) requires the import hook. Spans come from denoHttpIntegration (node:http), not from Koa. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. Parameterized route names DO appear for Koa on Deno 2.9.0 with @sentry/deno 10.67.0 (develop), under BOTH trace lifecycles, provided (a) the import hook is loaded via `deno run --import=<preload>` rather than as the entry's first `import`, and (b) that preload first registers a `node:module` load hook that serves `.json` with `format: "json"` (works around denoland/deno#36240, the crash the original probe hit). Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-koa-deno-routenames/ (koa 3.2.1, @koa/router 15.7.0, deno 2.9.0, tarball SDK 10.67.0, deno.json nodeModulesDir "manual"). Files: json-fix.ts (the shim), preload.ts (`import "./json-fix.ts"; import "@sentry/deno/import";`), instrument.ts (Sentry.init with tunnel + LIFECYCLE env), app.ts (routes /users/:id, /boom, /sentinel; app.on('error') only when ERR_HANDLER=1), main-nohook.ts (`import "./instrument.ts"; import "./app.ts";`), main-dyn.ts (json-fix + hook + `await import()`), b-sink.mjs (raw envelope sink), logs b-*.log / b-*.ndjson. --- 1. stream lifecycle, dynamic-import entry (main-dyn.ts), sink b-dyn.ndjson --- TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:47313/ LIFECYCLE=stream APP_PORT=47314 ERR_HANDLER=1 deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main-dyn.ts ORCH= {"runtime":["koa"]} SPAN name="/users/:id" op=router seg=false http.route="/users/:id" segname="GET /users/:id" origin=auto.http.koa SPAN name="GET /users/:id" op=http.server seg=true http.route="/users/:id" source=route segname="GET /users/:id" origin=auto.http.server SPAN name="GET /boom" op=http.server seg=true http.route="/boom" source=route SPAN name="GET /sentinel" op=http.server seg=true http.route="/sentinel" source=route --- 2. static lifecycle, `--import=./preload.ts` (main-nohook.ts unchanged), sink b-preload.ndjson --- TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:47315/ LIFECYCLE=static APP_PORT=47316 deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --import=./preload.ts main-nohook.ts TRANSACTION name="GET /users/:id" source=route op=http.server http.route="/users/:id" span op=router desc="/users/:id" route="/users/:id" origin=auto.http.koa TRANSACTION name="GET /boom" source=route op=http.server http.route="/boom" TRANSACTION name="GET /sentinel" source=route op=http.server http.route="/sentinel" --- 3. bonus, same run shape WITHOUT the manual app.on('error') (b-noerrh.ndjson): the Koa integration's own error handler fires, so point (5) of the reported wiring is unnecessary too --- TRANSACTION name="GET /boom" source=route route="/boom" spans=router /boom EVENT "koa boom" transaction="GET /boom" mech=auto.middleware.koa handled=false --- What the original probe hit, reproduced and explained --- (a) `--import=./b-preload-nofix.ts` (hook only, no JSON shim) still dies before listen: error: Uncaught (in promise) SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':' var codes = require('./codes.json') at Object.<anonymous> (.../node_modules/statuses/index.js:15:13) (b) The documented shape `import "@sentry/deno/import"` as the entry's first line does NOT instrument Koa even once the JSON shim is added: it boots, but Koa is never transformed. Both orders were tried (main-hook-jsonfix-before.ts and main-hook-jsonfix-after.ts), both print `ORCH= {"runtime":[]}`, and the stream run then yields exactly the reported symptom: SPAN name="GET" op=http.server seg=true http.route=undefined source=url segname="GET" Deno source-loads the whole static ESM graph (including the npm CJS facades) before the entry's first statement runs, so the injection hook registers too late; only `--import` / `await import()` defers Koa past hook registration. Deno 2.8.3 (CI pin) was not tested: $SCRATCH/deno283/deno does not exist on this machine.
Workaround: Two changes to the reported wiring, both in user land, no SDK change: 1. preload.ts import "./json-fix.ts"; import "@sentry/deno/import"; json-fix.ts (works around denoland/deno#36240: with any `node:module` hook registered, Deno compiles CJS `require('*.json')` as JS): import { registerHooks } from "node:module"; import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"; import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url"; registerHooks({ load(url, context, nextLoad) { if (url.endsWith(".json")) { return { format: "json", source: readFileSync(fileURLToPath(url), "utf8"), shortCircuit: true }; } return nextLoad(url, context); }, }); 2. Load it with the flag, not as an entry import: deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --import=./preload.ts main.ts where main.ts is just `import "./instrument.ts"; import "./app.ts";` (Equivalent alternative: keep the imports in main.ts but make the app load dynamic, `import "./json-fix.ts"; import "@sentry/deno/import"; await import("./instrument.ts"); await import("./app.ts");`) With this, `http.route` and the `GET /users/:id` name with source `route` appear in both `stream` and `static` lifecycles, Koa `router` spans appear, and the Koa auto error handler works, so the manual `app.on("error", ...)` from the reported wiring can be dropped.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent GET /iso/{alpha,beta,gamma} each set Sentry.setTag('req_tag', ...) and captured an exception. Each event carried exactly its own tag and its own trace_id, and each matching transaction carried the same tag and trace_id. No cross-talk. traceLifecycle static.
incoming trace✓ worksGET /users/99 with `sentry-trace: aaaa...aaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` and a sentry- baggage produced a transaction with trace_id 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa' and parent_span_id 'bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb'. Continuation is handled by denoHttpIntegration, so it is independent of Koa. traceLifecycle static.
outgoing fetch✗ broken`fetch()` from inside a Koa handler to the local recorder produced no http.client span (transaction 'GET /downstream' has spans: []) and the recorder saw sentry-trace: null, baggage: null. This is Deno finding K2 and it also holds inside Koa. A `node:http` client request from the same handler DOES work: span 'http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:38219/api/node-http' nested in the request transaction, and the recorder saw both sentry-trace and baggage. traceLifecycle static. verified: confirmed-broken Reproduced the reported behavior exactly, and then made it work with a user-land integration, so the finding is real but its "no configuration exists" framing is too strong. Root cause (source, not Koa): `@sentry/deno` ships NO fetch tracing integration. `packages/deno/src/sdk.ts` default integrations are eventFilters, requestData, functionToString, linkedErrors, dedupe, breadcrumbs, denoContext, denoServe, denoHttp, contextLines, normalizePaths, globalHandlers + server-utils error/tracing integrations. The only `fetch` code in `packages/deno/src` outside the transport is `integrations/breadcrumbs.ts` (breadcrumbs only). The built entry exports no fetch integration at all (grep of `build/esm/index.d.ts` for `*Integration` returns denoHttp/denoServe/denoKoa/... and nothing fetch-related). `denoHttpIntegration` subscribes only to `http.client.request.created` / `http.server.request.start` on `node:diagnostics_channel`, which Deno's native `fetch` never emits. Node's equivalent (`packages/node/src/integrations/node-fetch/`) is undici-based and does not apply to Deno. The repo's own e2e app confirms this is the intended state: `dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/deno/tests/fetch.test.ts` asserts only a span the app itself created with `Sentry.startSpan({name:'test-outgoing-fetch'})` and `origin: 'manual'` -- there is no assertion of an `http.client` span from fetch. Koa is irrelevant to the failure. BASELINE (main-nohook.ts, traceLifecycle static, koa 3.2.1 + @koa/router 15.7.0, deno 2.9.0, @sentry/deno 10.67.0 from $REPRO/_toolbox/pack): {"type": "transaction", "name": "GET /downstream", "op": "http.server", "source": "url", "status": "ok", "trace_id": "9fdb81124a494836b44b610897f3402f", "sdk": "sentry.javascript.deno", "spans": [], "hasRequestData": false} {"type": "transaction", "name": "GET /downstream-http", "op": "http.server", "source": "url", "status": "ok", "trace_id": "7bbab1d627cd4e5a96b36ced2030dc8e", "sdk": "sentry.javascript.deno", "spans": ["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:47312/api/node-http"], "hasRequestData": false} recorder /__seen: {"url": "/api/fetch", "sentry-trace": null, "baggage": null, "traceparent": null} {"url": "/api/node-http", "sentry-trace": "7bbab1d627cd4e5a96b36ced2030dc8e-9c7626c1c137801b-1", "baggage": "sentry-environment=production,...,sentry-sampled=true,sentry-sample_rate=1"} BASELINE, traceLifecycle stream (same gap, so the lifecycle is not the variable): {"type": "span", "trace_id": "bb6dd9be4c93446f9bb189a2d5df7810", "items": ["http.server GET"], "raw": [{"name": "GET", "status": "ok", "is_segment": true, "origin": "auto.http.server"}]} <- /downstream, fetch span missing {"type": "span", "trace_id": "63be2ba831a14f5faf95a52c60a975e9", "items": ["http.client GET 127.0.0.1", "http.server GET"], "raw": [{"name": "GET 127.0.0.1", "status": "ok", "parent_span_id": "b2f6e4dbb7a7101e", "is_segment": false, "origin": "auto.http.client"}, ...]} <- /downstream-http works IMPORT HOOK: reconfirmed dead on arrival with a fresh install. `deno run ... main-hook.ts` (line 1 `import "@sentry/deno/import";`) -> `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` at `node_modules/statuses/index.js:15` (`var codes = require('./codes.json')`), i.e. Deno K3 (denoland/deno#36240). Koa cannot be reached with the hook on, so the hook is not a route to fetch spans either. WORKS WITH A USER-LAND INTEGRATION (this is the refutation): a ~20-line integration built from public `@sentry/core` exports (`addFetchInstrumentationHandler`, `instrumentFetchRequest`, `isSentryRequestUrl`) registered via `Sentry.init({ integrations: [manualFetchIntegration()] })` produces a correctly parented client span AND propagates headers, on both lifecycles, with the hook OFF (so Koa still boots). static: {"type": "transaction", "name": "GET /downstream", "op": "http.server", "source": "url", "status": "ok", "trace_id": "d765a5ef83114bf9b7b1869b70b077c2", "sdk": "sentry.javascript.deno", "spans": ["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:47312/api/fetch"], "hasRequestData": false} recorder: {"url": "/api/fetch", "sentry-trace": "d765a5ef83114bf9b7b1869b70b077c2-aef48b44f861ccfc-1", "baggage": "sentry-environment=production,sentry-public_key=public,sentry-trace_id=d765a5ef83114bf9b7b1869b70b077c2,sentry-sampled=true,sentry-sample_rand=0.19519996821777663,sentry-sample_rate=1"} stream: {"type": "span", "trace_id": "eb2f8aa6a1564b3aaa17e0c4ce7b1448", "items": ["http.client GET 127.0.0.1", "http.server GET"], "raw": [{"name": "GET 127.0.0.1", "status": "ok", "parent_span_id": "bb63bc61ff041db5", "is_segment": false, "origin": "auto.http.fetch"}, {"name": "GET", "status": "ok", "is_segment": true, "origin": "auto.http.server"}]} So: broken out of the box on every supported configuration (both lifecycles, hook on or off, Koa or not), but the runtime is capable and the fix is ~20 lines of app code. Fixing it properly is an SDK change: add a fetch integration to `packages/deno/src/integrations/` modelled on `packages/cloudflare/src/integrations/fetch.ts` and put it in `getDefaultIntegrations`; `packages/deno/src/integrations/breadcrumbs.ts` already patches global fetch for breadcrumbs, so the instrumentation hook is present and only the span/header half is missing. Probe files (rerunnable; node_modules removed after the run, reinstall with the npm line below): $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-koa-deno-outgoingfetch/ app.ts, deno.json, package.json, recorder.mjs instrument.ts (baseline), main-nohook.ts, main-hook.ts fetch-integration.ts + instrument-fetchfix.ts + main-fetchfix.ts (the working variant) run-b-base2.log, run-b-stream2.log, run-b-fix.log, run-b-fixstream2.log, run-b-hook.log Commands: npm install --no-audit --no-fund koa@3.2.1 @koa/router@15.7.0 $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-deno-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz PORT=39418 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs & PORT=47312 node recorder.mjs & TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:39418/ RECORDER=http://127.0.0.1:47312 PORT=51907 LIFECYCLE=static deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main-nohook.ts (swap main-nohook.ts for main-fetchfix.ts / main-hook.ts; drive with curl /downstream, /downstream-http, /sentinel; read curl http://127.0.0.1:39418/__items and http://127.0.0.1:47312/__seen) Caveat on ports: another agent's Next.js app was tunneling into ports 47311/47312 during part of the run, so some sink reads contain `sentry.javascript.nextjs` items; the deno items quoted above are the ones from this probe (all my final reads used a private sink on 39418). Docs pages checked: ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/ contains only index.mdx plus configuration/integrations/{breadcrumbs,contextlines}.mdx. The single fetch mention is breadcrumbs.mdx:23-27 ("Log HTTP requests done with the Fetch API"), which is accurate. There is no Koa page and no outgoing-request/distributed-tracing page for Deno, so nothing in the docs currently overclaims -- but nothing warns either.
Workaround: Register a fetch integration by hand in the app; `@sentry/deno` has none. In instrument.ts, before `Sentry.init`: // fetch-integration.ts import { addFetchInstrumentationHandler, defineIntegration, getClient, instrumentFetchRequest, isSentryRequestUrl } from "@sentry/core"; const spans: Record<string, any> = {}; export const manualFetchIntegration = defineIntegration(() => ({ name: "ManualFetch", setupOnce() { addFetchInstrumentationHandler(handlerData => { const client = getClient(); if (!client || isSentryRequestUrl(handlerData.fetchData.url, client)) return; instrumentFetchRequest(handlerData, () => true, () => true, spans, { spanOrigin: "auto.http.fetch" }); }); }, })); then `Sentry.init({ ..., integrations: [manualFetchIntegration()] })`. `@sentry/core` must be an explicit dependency and mapped in deno.json's import map. This gives a correctly parented `http.client` span (origin `auto.http.fetch`) plus `sentry-trace`/`baggage` on the outgoing request, on both `traceLifecycle: 'static'` and `'stream'`, and it works with the Deno import hook OFF, which is the only mode in which Koa boots at all. Two lower-effort fallbacks if you do not want a custom integration: wrap the call in `Sentry.startSpan(...)` (gives a `manual`-origin span, still no headers), or attach headers yourself from `Sentry.getTraceData()`. Both are strictly worse. For anything that runs over `node:http`/`node:https` instead of `fetch`, no workaround is needed: `denoHttpIntegration` already produces the span and the headers.
db spans✓* works-waModule-scope mysql@2 pool queried inside the handler: no db span at all without the import hook (transaction 'GET /db' has spans: []). The instrumentation path that would give db spans on Deno is the import hook (`import "@sentry/deno/import"`), and that path cannot be used with Koa (see evidence). Proved the hook itself is fine in this same directory with a Koa-free node:http entry: it emits a db span, but as its own ROOT transaction ('SELECT name FROM users LIMIT 1', op db, source custom) with a DIFFERENT trace_id from the enclosing 'GET /db' request, so even there it is not parented to the request. No Bun plugin / Vite plugin path applies on Deno. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. Koa 3.2.1 + @koa/router 15.7.0 on Deno 2.9.0 with @sentry/deno 10.67.0 (develop tarballs) DOES produce a mysql db span that is a proper child of the Koa request transaction. Two changes to the original probe's wiring are needed, and the second one is the reason the original probe saw no usable span even in its Koa-free control. CHANGE 1 - register the import hook AFTER Koa's module graph is loaded, not as the first import. The hook is a Deno module-load hook: it only transforms modules loaded after it is registered. Koa's `statuses` package does `require('./codes.json')`, which the hook cannot handle (Deno bug denoland/deno#36240), so `import "@sentry/deno/import"` as line 1 kills the process. But if Koa is imported statically first and the hook is then registered with a top-level `await import("@sentry/deno/import")`, Koa is already in the module cache and never re-transformed, while `mysql` - dynamically imported after the hook - IS transformed and instrumented. CHANGE 2 - use `mysql.createConnection`, not `mysql.createPool`. With `createPool` the db span is emitted but as its own ROOT transaction in a DIFFERENT trace from the request. This is what the original probe hit in its node:http control, and it is NOT a Koa or node:http problem: with the exact same entry, same hook ordering and same Koa app, swapping `createPool` for `createConnection` moves the span onto the request transaction. Every pooled query in the process also shared one single trace_id, i.e. the pool's queries run in the async context captured when the pool was built, not the request's. The repo's own e2e app (~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/deno-mysql/src/app.ts) uses `createConnection` for exactly this reason (its comments call out the AsyncLocalStorage restore in `denoMysqlIntegration`). Context propagation inside the Koa handler itself is fine either way: a `/manual` route reported `{"hadActiveSpan":true}` and its manual span nested correctly (`"spans":["manual manual-child"]`), so the detachment is specific to the pooled driver path. === SINK LINES === A) Baseline, no hook (main-a-nohook.ts, static) - reproduces the original claim: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","trace_id":"419a69126b2546daa96eb1d9121ee2dd","sdk":"sentry.javascript.deno","spans":[]} B) Documented ordering, hook first (main-b-hook.ts) - still crashes, confirmed on this run: error: Uncaught (in promise) SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':' var codes = require('./codes.json') at Object.<anonymous> (.../verify4-M-koa-deno-dbspans/node_modules/statuses/index.js:15:13) C) Late hook + createPool (main-c-koafirst.ts, static) - db span exists but detached, and both requests' db spans share one trace_id: {"type":"transaction","name":"SELECT name FROM users LIMIT 1","op":"db","source":"custom","status":"ok","trace_id":"b8c50373ca7d4348a101bdbc9f18996f","spans":[]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","trace_id":"b0bb774d3cd84660bb397977764e5d88","spans":[]} {"type":"transaction","name":"SELECT name FROM users LIMIT 1","op":"db","source":"custom","status":"ok","trace_id":"b8c50373ca7d4348a101bdbc9f18996f","spans":[]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /manual","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","trace_id":"361ab9f7ca4e45919d9214b921abbc8b","spans":["manual manual-child"]} D) Late hook + createConnection (main-d-koafirst-conn.ts, static) - Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions Koa on Deno, in either direction. - ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/koa/index.mdx:4 declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` and :5 `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`; its whole body is `<PlatformContent includePath="getting-started-node" />` (line 12). `grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/koa/` returns nothing. - ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx never mentions Koa or any framework; `grep -rni "express|koa|fastify|hono|framework"` over that file returns nothing. The guide is still flagged beta (index.mdx:12-16) and its only configuration/integrations pages are breadcrumbs.mdx and contextlines.mdx. - The Deno import hook is undocumented everywhere: `grep -rn "deno/import|import-hook|@sentry/deno/import" docs/ platform-includes/` returns zero hits across the whole docs repo. So the one switch that decides whether Koa boots at all on Deno is not described on any page.

Documented: no

A Koa-on-Deno page must exist and must document instrumentation timing, which is where every Koa capability succeeded or failed. It must say: (1) A static `import "@sentry/deno/import"` as the first import of the entry file does not work for Koa — Deno instantiates the whole module graph, including `koa`, before any module body executes, so the hook is registered too late; load it with the CLI flag instead (`deno run --import=./preload.ts main.ts`). (2) On Deno 2.9.0, registering any `Module.registerHooks` load hook breaks CJS `require('*.json')` (denoland/deno#36240), and Koa's `statuses` dependency does exactly that, so the app must also register a JSON-restoring load hook (`registerHooks({ load(url, ctx, next) { const r = next(url, ctx); return url.endsWith('.json') ? { ...r, format: 'json' } : r; } })` or the `readFileSync` equivalent); with the flag plus that hook, route names work. (3) An alternative that avoids the runtime hook entirely and was verified for both error capture and library spans: bundle the Koa app with esbuild and `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild` (`format: 'esm'`, `external: ['@sentry/deno', '@sentry/server-utils']`, plus a `createRequire` banner) and run the bundle with Deno — no import hook and no manual `app.on('error')` handler needed. (4) For database spans without bundling, keep `import "@sentry/deno/import"` out of the static import list and register it in the entry body after Koa is imported (`await import('@sentry/deno/import')`), then dynamically import the driver. Isolation, incoming trace continuation and logs need no caveat. Outgoing `fetch` is not instrumented — no `http.client` span, no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` — in both `static` and `stream` lifecycles; the page must ship the userland fetch integration built from `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` / `defineIntegration` / `getClient` / `instrumentFetchRequest`, and note `node:http`/`node:https` are traced normally.

Page to write: guides/deno/frameworks/koa.mdx (new), with an "Instrumentation timing on Deno" section covering `--import` vs static import and the JSON load-hook workaround

docs/platforms/javascript/guides/koa/index.mdx:4 `sdk: sentry.javascript.node`, :5 `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, :12 body is only `<PlatformContent includePath="getting-started-node" />`; `grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/koa/` returns nothing; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-232 never mentions Koa or any framework, and no page in the repo mentions `@sentry/deno/import` or `Module.registerHooks`

Headline: Koa itself runs fine on Deno, and the base @sentry/deno SDK gives useful telemetry alongside it, but the Deno import hook and Koa are mutually exclusive. `import "@sentry/deno/import";` kills the process at import time on `statuses/index.js` -> `require('./codes.json')` (denoland/deno#36240, the same root cause as the known `generator-function/require.mjs` failure, but a different file on koa@3.2.1 — koa@3 dropped generator-function, so the first `require('*.json')` in its graph is `statuses`). I also confirmed this is NOT scoped to a local node_modules: with `nodeModulesDir: "none"` the same crash happens inside Deno's global npm cache copy of statuses. Consequences that a docs page would have to state plainly: 1. Zero Koa spans on Deno. No middleware span, no router span, no `http.route`, no `sentry.source: route`. Server spans come from denoHttpIntegration only and are named from the raw URL (static) or just `GET` (stream). 2. Zero automatic error capture on Deno. Koa swallows handler errors into `app.on('error')`; the SDK's auto-attach runs off the `orchestrion:koa:callback` channel, which the hook injects, so it never fires. Users must register `app.on('error', ...)` themselves. @sentry/deno does not re-export `setupKoaErrorHandler` (deprecated but present on @sentry/node, @sentry/bun, astro, aws-serverless, elysia, gcp-serverless, remix, solidstart, sveltekit). The internal helper is reachable as `import { attachKoaErrorHandler } from '@sentry/server-utils'` but that is not a user-facing API. 3. `debug: true` is actively misleading here: it prints "[instrumentation:koa] subscribing to channels" and "Integration installed: Koa" with no hook loaded and nothing instrumented. Same for Mysql/Mysql2. A user reading the debug log would conclude Koa is instrumented. 4. Deno fetch (K2) reproduces inside Koa: no span, no propagation headers. `node:http` client calls from the same handler do get an http.client span with sentry-trace and baggage, so that is the only working outgoing-propagation path. 5. Side observation from the hook sanity check (main-hook-nokoa.ts, no Koa involved): the mysql span from a module-scope pool arrives as its OWN root transaction with a different trace_id than the enclosing http.server transaction, i.e. db spans on Deno are not parented to the request even when the hook works. Worth a separate cell. Time spent was inside the box; the only thing I did not attempt was patching Deno or shimming `require('*.json')`, which is out of scope for a docs recommendation. Processes: all killed (deno app, sink 38217, recorder 38219, plus an orphaned recorder I had started on 41400, pid 91059, killed by explicit pid). `node_modules` removed.

  import "./init.ts";             // Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle })
  import "./app-body.ts";         // Hapi.server(...), routes, module-scope mysql connection

json-fix.mjs (the JSON load-hook fix) is mandatory for Hapi on Deno. Without it the app never boots: @hapi/validate/lib/common.js does require('../package.json') and, with any Module.registerHooks load hook registered, Deno compiles that JSON through the CJS compiler. It is 12 lines:
  import * as Module from 'node:module';
  import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
  import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
  Module.registerHooks({ load(url, context, nextLoad) {
    if (url.endsWith('.json')) return { format: 'json', source: readFileSync(fileURLToPath(url), 'utf8'), shortCircuit: true };
    return nextLoad(url, context);
  } });
It must be imported AFTER @sentry/deno/import so it sits first in the hook chain and JSON never reaches Deno's default loader.

No Sentry.setupHapiErrorHandler(server) call: @sentry/deno on develop does not export it, and hapiIntegration is already in getDefaultIntegrations via getErrorIntegrations()/getTracingIntegrations() from @sentry/server-utils.

Run: deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main.ts

"json-fix.mjs must be imported AFTER @sentry/deno/import" is false. main-fixfirst.ts imports json-fix.mjs FIRST, then the hook, then init, then the app (v4-fixfirst-static) and produces byte-identical telemetry: `"name":"GET /users/{id}","source":"route","spans":["router GET /users/{id}"]`. Order of the two hook registrations does not matter. 2. Route names do NOT actually require the hook or the JSON workaround. With plain documented wiring (init + app, no `@sentry/deno/import`, no json-fix) plus a 6-line hapi `ext`, names are fully parameterized in both lifecycles — v4-manual2-nohook-static: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/{id}","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":[]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":[]} v4-manual2-nohook-stream: {"type":"span","items":["http.server GET /users/{id}"],"raw":[{"name":"GET /users/{id}","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.server"}]} What you lose without the hook is only the `router` child span, the mysql `db` span and the `auto.function.hapi` unhandled-error capture — not the route name. Gotcha found while building that: `Sentry.getRootSpan(span).updateName(...)` forces the segment name source to `custom` (core spanUtils.js:254-265, INTERNAL_setSegmentNameSourceIfSegment). Setting the plain string `'sentry.source'` afterwards does nothing (v4-manual-nohook-static gave `"name":"GET /users/{id}","source":"custom"`); you must set the exported `Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE` key (`sentry.segment.name.source`) to `'route'` after updateName. Why CI never sees this: the repo's own Deno hapi test, ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/deno-integration-tests/suites/orchestrion-hapi/test.ts, never imports @hapi/hapi — it hand-publishes `orchestrion:@hapi/hapi:route` on the diagnostics channel against a fake route object, so the real import path under Deno's load hook is untested. The root defect is Deno's (denoland/deno#36240): with any Module.registerHooks load hook registered, `nextLoad` returns `format: undefined` for a .json URL and Deno then compiles it as CJS; the SDK's loadSync passes such results straight through untouched (hook.js:113-128). Not run: Deno 2.8.3 (the $SCRATCH/deno283 pin has been cleaned off disk) and nodeModulesDir "auto" (the JSON defect is in Deno's load-hook chain, independent of resolution mode).
Workaround: Two, and they are independent. (A) For route names only, no hook and no JSON fix needed — keep the documented wiring (`import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno"; Sentry.init(...)`) and add to the hapi server: `server.ext('onPreHandler', (request, h) => { const a = Sentry.getActiveSpan(); if (a) { const root = Sentry.getRootSpan(a); root.updateName(`${request.method.toUpperCase()} ${request.route.path}`); root.setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, 'route'); root.setAttribute('http.route', request.route.path); } return h.continue; });` — the SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE line must come after updateName, which otherwise leaves source `custom`. Gives `GET /users/{id}` source `route` in static and `http.server GET /users/{id}` in stream. (B) For full hapi instrumentation (router span, db spans, unhandled route errors) you still need `import "@sentry/deno/import"` plus a JSON load hook in the same entry: `import * as Module from 'node:module'; import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'; import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'; Module.registerHooks({ load(url, ctx, next) { return url.endsWith('.json') ? { format: 'json', source: readFileSync(fileURLToPath(url), 'utf8'), shortCircuit: true } : next(url, ctx); } });` — it can be imported before or after `@sentry/deno/import`, order does not matter, but it must come before the app.

Every route span and the node:http client span are otherwise correct, so this is a single missing integration, not broken tracing. Workaround: A 25-line userland integration restores both the span and the headers, in both lifecycles, with and without the import hook. ./fetch-integration.ts: import { addFetchInstrumentationHandler, defineIntegration, getClient, instrumentFetchRequest, isSentryRequestUrl, LRUMap, shouldPropagateTraceForUrl } from '@sentry/core'; const headersUrlMap = new LRUMap<string, boolean>(100); const spanMap: Record<string, any> = {}; export const denoFetchIntegration = defineIntegration(() => ({ name: 'DenoUserlandFetch', setupOnce() { addFetchInstrumentationHandler(handlerData => { const client = getClient(); if (!client) return; if (isSentryRequestUrl(handlerData.fetchData.url, client)) return; instrumentFetchRequest(handlerData, () => true, url => shouldPropagateTraceForUrl(url, client.getOptions().tracePropagationTargets, headersUrlMap), spanMap, { spanOrigin: 'auto.http.fetch' }); }); }, })); then Sentry.init({ ..., integrations: [denoFetchIntegration()] }). B - fetchfix, static: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /downstream","source":"route","spans":["router GET /downstream","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41972/api/downstream"]} and recorder {"url":"/api/downstream","sentryTrace":"c38ced0aae64439480dd3f79e4b69bf4-833ca5279dc94ae1-1","baggage":"...sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fdownstream,sentry-sampled=true..."} C - fetchfix, stream: {"type":"span","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","router /downstream","http.server GET /downstream"],"raw":[{"name":"GET 127.0.0.1","origin":"auto.http.fetch",...}]} plus the headers. D - fetchfix without the import hook (main-nohook.ts): the http.client span and headers still appear; only the Hapi router span and route-based transaction name are lost (source drops to "url"). No SDK source change is needed, and the same shim is runtime-generic: it only uses exports already public from @sentry/core.
