No page mentions the combination. ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/ contains only index.mdx and configuration/integrations/{breadcrumbs,contextlines}.mdx; `grep -rn -i hapi` over that directory returns nothing, and `grep -rn -i deno` over docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hapi/ returns nothing. The Deno guide (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-232) covers error monitoring and performance only — it never mentions node_modules, nodeModulesDir, the @sentry/deno/import hook, or any Node framework, so a reader following it lands in the no-hook behaviour above: no route names, no db spans, and silently no error event for a Hapi handler throw. The Hapi guide (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hapi/index.mdx:3) declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` with `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, and its usage include, platform-includes/getting-started-use/javascript.hapi.mdx:17, still tells users to call `await Sentry.setupHapiErrorHandler(server)` — @sentry/deno on develop does not export that function (packages/deno/src/index.ts:129 exports hapiIntegration only, and it is already a default integration), so copying the documented snippet onto Deno throws.

Documented: no

A Hapi-on-Deno page must exist and must distinguish what needs the import hook from what does not. It must say: setup is `npm install @hapi/hapi` plus `@sentry/deno` into a real on-disk `node_modules` with `deno.json` `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}`. Error capture does NOT require the `@sentry/deno/import` runtime hook — either bundle the app with esbuild and `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild` (`bundle: true, platform: 'node', format: 'esm', external: ['@sentry/deno','@sentry/server-utils']`, plus a `createRequire` banner), which additionally yields parameterized route names and Hapi/database spans, or run the entry directly with plain `Sentry.init`. Parameterized transaction names (`GET /users/{id}` with `sentry.segment.name.source: 'route'` and a nested `router` span) do require `import "@sentry/deno/import"` as the first line of the entry file (or `--import=./node_modules/@sentry/deno/build/import.mjs`), and until the SDK tags JSON modules itself, they also require a JSON load hook registered before Hapi is imported: `Module.registerHooks({ load(url, ctx, next) { const r = next(url, ctx); return url.endsWith('.json') ? { ...r, format: 'json' } : r; } })`. Isolation, incoming trace continuation, database spans and logs work with no caveat. Outgoing `fetch` is not instrumented: no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers, independent of framework and of `traceLifecycle`; the page must ship a userland fetch integration (`addFetchInstrumentationHandler`, `defineIntegration`, `getClient`, `instrumentFetchRequest`, `isSentryRequestUrl`, `LRUMap`, `shouldPropagateTraceForUrl` from `@sentry/core`) which was verified to restore both spans and headers with the hook on and off, and note that `node:http` requests are traced normally.

Page to write: guides/deno/frameworks/hapi.mdx (new), covering the esbuild/orchestrion route and the import-hook + JSON-load-hook route side by side

`grep -rn -i hapi docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/` returns nothing (that directory holds only index.mdx and configuration/integrations/{breadcrumbs,contextlines}.mdx) and `grep -rn -i deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hapi/` returns nothing; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hapi/index.mdx:4-5 declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` / `fallbackGuide: javascript.node` with a bare `getting-started-node` body at :12; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-232 covers error monitoring and tracing only and never mentions `node_modules`, `nodeModulesDir`, or the `@sentry/deno/import` hook

Viability: Hapi imports and serves on Deno with no Sentry at all (bare.ts started and answered GET /users/{id}), and also boots fine with Sentry.init alone. The only thing that breaks it is the diagnostics-channel import hook. The headline finding is that on Deno the Hapi story is all-or-nothing and gated on a runtime bug. Without `import "@sentry/deno/import"` you get no route names, no db spans, and — worst — no error event at all for a route handler throw, because Hapi turns it into a Boom 500 and nothing else observes it. With the hook you get all three, but the app does not start: @hapi/validate/lib/common.js:6 does `require('../package.json')` and Deno compiles JSON through the CJS compiler as soon as any Module.registerHooks load hook is registered (denoland/deno#36240, K3). The 12-line json-fix.mjs closes that gap completely and nothing else was needed; @hapi/hapi, @hapi/validate, @hapi/hoek and the rest all loaded and every capability except fetch worked. That workaround is small enough that the SDK could ship it inside @sentry/deno/import — the hook already owns the load chain, and short-circuiting `.json` there costs nothing on Node — which would make Hapi (and, per K3, Express and Fastify) work on Deno out of the box. Fetch is the one genuine gap and it is not Hapi's. The same handler that gets a full http.client span with sentry-trace and baggage from node:http.get gets nothing at all from fetch(), in both lifecycles and with and without the hook. Any Hapi app on Deno that calls a downstream service with fetch has a broken distributed trace. Other observations: the docs' `Sentry.setupHapiErrorHandler(server)` step is both unnecessary and unavailable on develop's @sentry/deno — hapiIntegration comes in as a default via getErrorIntegrations()/getTracingIntegrations() from @sentry/server-utils. Route naming survives both lifecycles: static reports source "route" with a nested `router GET /users/{id}` span, stream reports `http.server GET /users/{id}`. Isolation was clean under three concurrent staggered requests in every configuration. Ports used: sink 45903, recorder 45907, Hapi on port 0 (several ports in the 38000-47000 range were already held by other agents, hence port 0 for the app). All processes started here were killed before returning; node_modules was kept because it is only 3.3 MB and makes the probe rerunnable.

Oak on Deno M-oak-deno

Oak 17.2.0 (jsr:@oak/oak) · Deno 2.9.0 (aarch64-apple-darwin), @sentry/deno develop (10.67.0, worktree audit-runtime-docs) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Oak runs on Deno. Two mounting shapes exist and they are NOT equivalent for Sentry — a docs page must show `Deno.serve(app.fetch)` and warn against `app.listen()`.

deno.json (nodeModulesDir "manual", with the SDK symlinked into node_modules/@sentry/*):
{
  "nodeModulesDir": "manual",
  "imports": {
    "@oak/oak": "jsr:@oak/oak@^17",
    "@sentry/deno": "npm:@sentry/deno",
    "mysql": "npm:mysql"
  }
}

Gotcha worth documenting: with `nodeModulesDir: "manual"`, Oak's single npm dependency must be present in node_modules or the app will not even boot:
`npm install --no-save --ignore-scripts path-to-regexp@6.3.0`
(without it: `error: Could not find a matching package for 'npm:path-to-regexp@^6.3.0' in the node_modules directory` at jsr.io/@oak/oak/17.2.0/deps.ts:79:8)

instrument.ts (must be the first import of the entry; the `/import` hook line is what makes library/db instrumentation work):
  import "@sentry/deno/import";
  import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno";
  Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: "static" });

main.ts:
  import "./instrument.ts";                    // first line
  import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno";
  import { Application, Router } from "@oak/oak";
  const { default: mysql } = await import("mysql");   // dynamic, so the hook has been installed
  const db = mysql.createConnection({ host: "127.0.0.1", port: 3307, user: "root", database: "app" }); // module scope

  const router = new Router();
  router.get("/users/:id", ctx => { ctx.response.body = { id: ctx.params.id }; });

  const app = new Application();

  // 1. error middleware (only needed for app.listen(); harmless with app.fetch)
  app.use(async (ctx, next) => {
    try { await next(); }
    catch (e) { Sentry.captureException(e, { mechanism: { type: "oak", handled: false } }); throw e; }
  });

  // 2. route-name middleware — nothing names the span after the Oak route automatically
  app.use(async (ctx, next) => {
    await next();
    const span = Sentry.getActiveSpan();
    const route = ctx.matched?.at(-1)?.path;
    if (span && route) {
      Sentry.updateSpanName(span, `${ctx.request.method} ${route}`);
      span.setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, "route");
    }
  });

  app.use(router.routes());
  app.use(router.allowedMethods());

  Deno.serve({ port: 0, hostname: "127.0.0.1" }, app.fetch);

Run: deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main.ts

app.fetch vs app.listen() — the difference, measured:
- `Deno.serve(app.fetch)`: `denoServeIntegration` proxies `Deno.serve`, so `wrapDenoRequestHandler` opens the isolation scope and the http.server span AROUND the whole Oak dispatch. Everything works: per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, nested db spans, route naming from a middleware. Oak's `fetch` (application.ts:722-728) calls `#handleError(context, err)` and then RE-THROWS, so a handler error escapes into Deno.serve and the SDK captures it automatically (mechanism `auto.http.deno`, handled:false); the 500 body "Internal Server Error" comes from Deno.serve's default onError, not from Oak. Caveat: Oak's `fetch` is Cloudflare-shaped (`(request, env, ctx)`), so Deno passes `ServeHandlerInfo` as `env` and Oak reads the client IP only from `CF-Connecting-IP` — `ctx.request.ip` is empty on Deno.
- `app.listen()`: Oak's own Deno server drains requests through an async queue, so the handler body runs OUTSIDE the Deno.serve handler's async context. Result: no active span in middleware (route naming silently no-ops), the mysql span is emitted as its own root transaction with its own trace id instead of a child, request errors never reach Sentry at all, and isolation scopes leak across concurrent requests (all three concurrent events carried the same tag and the same stale trace id). `app.listen()` is effectively unsupported.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksWith Deno.serve(app.fetch) the error reaches Sentry twice over: automatically via the Deno.serve wrapper (mechanism auto.http.deno, handled:false) because Oak's app.fetch re-throws after #handleError, and via the explicit try/catch middleware (mechanism oak, handled:false) when one is installed — dedupeIntegration keeps only one event. Oak does NOT swallow on the app.fetch path (the 500 is Deno.serve's default onError); it DOES swallow on app.listen(), where no event was produced at all. hasContextLine true. Stream and static lifecycle both.
route names◐ partialNothing names the span after the Oak route out of the box: stream gives `http.server GET` src=url, static gives `GET /users/7` source=url (raw id, high cardinality). A ~6-line middleware reading ctx.matched.at(-1).path plus updateSpanName + SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE='route' produces `GET /users/:id` src=route in both lifecycles. The middleware runs after await next(), so it never applies on the error path — /error stayed `GET` src=url (stream) / `GET /error` source=url (static). Under app.listen() the middleware is a no-op because getActiveSpan() is undefined there. verified: partial Two of the three sub-claims hold; the interesting one (error path) is REFUTED. CONFIRMED — nothing names the span out of the box. NAMING=off, Deno.serve(app.fetch): stream: [{"name":"GET","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.deno"}] (x4, no sentry.segment.name.source) static: tx: GET /users/7 | source: url / tx: GET /error/42 | source: url There is no Oak integration in @sentry/deno (packages/deno/src/integrations/ has koa.ts but nothing Oak), and `setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute` — the helper the SDK uses internally for exactly this (packages/server-utils/src/utils/setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute.ts, exported from @sentry/server-utils/exports.ts) — is NOT re-exported from @sentry/deno (packages/deno/src/index.ts:118-144 re-exports only the orchestrion integrations). So the manual `updateSpanName` + `SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE` recipe is the only route, and it omits `http.route` unless the user sets it too. REFUTED — "the middleware runs after await next(), so it never applies on the error path". It is not a limitation of the approach, only of where the prior probe put the naming code. Two one-line variants cover the error path in BOTH lifecycles: (a) `try { await next(); } finally { ...name... }` on the app-level middleware (b) `router.use((ctx, next) => { ...name...; return next(); })` (router-level middleware runs after matching, before the handler; ctx.matched is already ["(.*)","/users/:id"]) stream (span envelope attributes, verbatim from the sink raw dump, NAMING=finally): GET /users/:id {"sentry.origin":"auto.http.deno","sentry.op":"http.server","sentry.segment.name.source":"route",...} GET /error/:id {"sentry.origin":"auto.http.deno","sentry.op":"http.server","sentry.segment.name.source":"route",...} static (NAMING=finally): tx: GET /users/:id | source: route | tx: GET /ok | source: route | tx: GET /error/:id | source: route | tx: GET /sentinel | source: route static (NAMING=after, the prior probe's shape, for contrast): tx: GET /error/42 | source: url <- the only cell that differs NAMING=routeruse gives the identical four route-named results in both lifecycles. Also verified with the finally variant (main2.ts, no error middleware at all): - prefixed routers give the full path: `new Router({prefix:"/api"})` -> `GET /api/users/:id` src=route http.route=/api/users/:id, and `GET /api/error/:id` src=route on the throwing route. - unmatched request stays low cardinality: `[mw] /nope span=true matched=[]` -> span `GET` src=url, status 404 (dropped entirely in static by the default ignoreStatusCodes). - with Deno.serve(app.fetch) the Sentry error middleware is unnecessary and produces no duplicate: the only event was `ev: Error: oak prefixed boom | mech: auto.http.deno | handled: false`. CONFIRMED — app.listen() is a no-op for naming, and try/finally does not rescue it (MOUNT=listen, LIFECYCLE=static): [app.finally] /users/7 span=false matched=["/users/:id"] [app.finally] /error/42 span=false matched=["/error/:id"] transaction GET /users/7 url 3924c1556d7546709d4a2ba98d00a5e6 transaction GET /error/42 url 5f8d4add47e7466c8b7976428e6222c1 event Error: oak route boom 28df7e8e4261433785cbe13c799a70c9 event undefined: sentinel 28df7e8e4261433785cbe13c799a70c9 <- same stale trace id, the isolation leak Not fixable from user code: the naming needs the active span, which only exists inside the Deno.serve handler async context that Oak's own listen server drains away from. Probe files (all absolute, rerunnable): $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-oak-deno-routenames/ deno.json, package.json (path-to-regexp@6.3.0), node_modules/@sentry/* symlinked to ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/packages/* instrument.ts - @sentry/deno/import hook + init, LIFECYCLE env picks stream/static main.ts - NAMING=off|after|finally|routeruse, MOUNT=serve|listen main2.ts - the recommended recipe: prefixed router, try/finally naming + http.route, no error middleware run.sh / run2.sh, sink.mjs, app-*.log, items-*.json, raw-prefix-*.json Commands: cd <dir> && npm install --no-save --ignore-scripts path-to-regexp@6.3.0 PORT=41333 node sink.mjs > sink.log 2>&1 & ./run.sh finally-stream finally stream serve ; ./run.sh after-static after static serve ; ./run.sh listen-finally-static finally static listen ; ./run2.sh prefix-stream stream (each script runs `deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main.ts`, drives /users/7 /ok /error/42 /sentinel, waits for the sentinel, dumps the sink) Repo reference: dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/deno-streamed has no router at all, so it offers no Oak precedent.
Workaround: Mount with `Deno.serve(app.fetch)` and add one app-level middleware that names the span in a `finally` block, so it also runs when the handler throws: app.use(async (ctx, next) => { try { await next(); } finally { const span = Sentry.getActiveSpan(); const route = ctx.matched?.at(-1)?.path; if (span && route) { Sentry.updateSpanName(span, `${ctx.request.method} ${route}`); span.setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, 'route'); span.setAttribute('http.route', route); } } }); Register it before `app.use(router.routes())`. It works in both `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` and `'static'`, on success and error paths, and with prefixed routers (`/api/users/:id`). A router-level `router.use((ctx, next) => { ...; return next(); })` is equivalent. Under `app.listen()` there is no workaround, `getActiveSpan()` is undefined there.
isolation✓ worksDeno.serve(app.fetch), stream lifecycle: three concurrent GET /iso/:tag requests each produced an event with exactly its own tag (who: alpha/bravo/charlie) and three distinct trace ids, each matching its own http.server span's trace id. Under app.listen() this is broken: all three events carried tags {who: charlie} and the same stale trace id 0a97d058... from an earlier request, and the transactions carried mismatched tags.
incoming trace✓ worksA request with sentry-trace: aaaa...-1111111111111111-1 plus baggage produced `http.server GET /users/:id :: trace=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa parent=1111111111111111` (stream) and a transaction with trace_id bbbb... / parent_span_id 2222222222222222 (static). continueTrace runs in wrapDenoRequestHandler before Oak sees the request, so Oak is not involved.
outgoing fetch✗ brokenA fetch() from inside an Oak handler to a local recorder produced NO http.client span (the /downstream span envelope and static transaction contain only the http.server entry) and the recorder saw NO sentry-trace and NO baggage header: {"url":"/rec/from-oak"}. This is the already-known Deno K2 gap, not an Oak issue; node:http clients are the documented workaround. verified: confirmed-broken Reproduced independently and could not refute it with any supported wiring. Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-oak-deno-outgoingfetch/ (Oak 17.2.0 via jsr, Deno 2.9.0, @sentry/deno 10.67.0 tarball from $REPRO/_toolbox/pack, mounted as Deno.serve(app.fetch), sink on 41338, recorder on 47311). Variants tried, all with the same result for global `fetch()`: 1. import hook on (`import "@sentry/deno/import"` first), traceLifecycle 'static' — main.ts 2. import hook off (instrument-b.ts / main-b.ts), traceLifecycle 'static' 3. traceLifecycle 'stream' (also checked with the fix, below) Baseline (hook on, static), GET /downstream doing `await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:47311/rec/from-oak")`: {"type": "transaction", "name": "GET /downstream", "op": "http.server", "source": "route", "status": "ok", "trace_id": "be09504919594233916b0634db5b85e8", "sdk": "sentry.javascript.deno", "spans": []} RECORDED: [{"url":"/rec/from-oak","sentryTrace":null,"baggage":null,"traceparent":null}] No-hook run, identical: {"type": "transaction", "name": "GET /downstream", ..., "spans": []} {"url": "/rec/from-oak", "sentryTrace": null, "baggage": null, "traceparent": null} Root cause is in the SDK, not Oak: packages/deno/src/sdk.ts getDefaultIntegrations() has no fetch tracing integration at all. denoHttpIntegration (packages/deno/src/integrations/http.ts) is node:http diagnostics-channel based, and breadcrumbsIntegration only calls addFetchInstrumentationHandler for breadcrumbs. @sentry/deno also does not re-export the pieces needed to build one: `node -e "import('@sentry/deno')..."` prints instrumentFetchRequest=false addFetchInstrumentationHandler=false isSentryRequestUrl=false shouldPropagateTraceForUrl=false LRUMap=false defineIntegration=false. Corroborating: the repo's own Deno e2e app has tests/fetch.test.ts named "Outbound fetch inside Sentry span creates transaction" (~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/deno/tests/fetch.test.ts) but it only asserts a *manual* wrapping span (`description: 'test-outgoing-fetch', origin: 'manual'`) around the fetch in src/app.ts:135. Nothing in the suite asserts an http.client span for Deno, so the gap is untested rather than regressed. The Oak-specific claims in the report hold: Deno.serve(app.fetch) gives a correctly named http.server segment (source=route via the ctx.matched middleware) and the fetch is simply invisible inside it. Rerun: cd <probe dir> && npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-deno-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz path-to-regexp@6.3.0 PORT=41338 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs & PORT=47311 node recorder.mjs & SINK_PORT=41338 REC_PORT=47311 APP_PORT=47312 LIFECYCLE=static deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main.ts curl http://127.0.0.1:47312/downstream ; curl http://127.0.0.1:47312/sentinel (add FETCHFIX=on for the workaround, LIFECYCLE=stream for span envelopes; node_modules was removed after the run to save disk)
Workaround: Two workarounds, both verified in this probe. 1. Documented one, works out of the box inside an Oak handler: use node:http instead of fetch. Route /downstream-node in main.ts does `http.request({hostname:'127.0.0.1', port: REC, path:'/rec/from-oak-node'})`: {"type": "transaction", "name": "GET /downstream-node", "op": "http.server", "trace_id": "99fadaf0391040eb9879788f366ba379", "spans": ["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:47311/rec/from-oak-node"]} {"url": "/rec/from-oak-node", "sentryTrace": "99fadaf0391040eb9879788f366ba379-817ab41154412d2e-1", "baggage": "sentry-environment=production,sentry-public_key=public,sentry-trace_id=99fadaf0391040eb9879788f366ba379,sentry-sampled=true,sentry-sample_rand=0.35...,sentry-sample_rate=1"} 2. A ~25-line userland integration that keeps global fetch. It has to import from @sentry/core directly, because @sentry/deno re-exports none of these. File: <probe dir>/fetch-integration.ts: import { addFetchInstrumentationHandler, defineIntegration, getClient, instrumentFetchRequest, isSentryRequestUrl, LRUMap, shouldPropagateTraceForUrl } from "@sentry/core"; const headersUrlMap = new LRUMap<string, boolean>(100); const spanMap: Record<string, any> = {}; export const denoFetchIntegration = defineIntegration(() => ({ name: "DenoUserlandFetch", setupOnce() { addFetchInstrumentationHandler(handlerData => { const client = getClient(); if (!client) return; if (isSentryRequestUrl(handlerData.fetchData.url, client)) return; instrumentFetchRequest(handlerData, () => true, url => shouldPropagateTraceForUrl(url, client.getOptions().tracePropagationTargets, headersUrlMap), spanMap, { spanOrigin: "auto.http.fetch" }); }); }, })); Add `integrations: [denoFetchIntegration()]` to Sentry.init. With it (static lifecycle): {"type": "transaction", "name": "GET /downstream", "trace_id": "88529b39a2d84c2fb346753cbfbccd4c", "spans": ["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:47311/rec/from-oak"]} {"url":"/rec/from-oak","sentryTrace":"88529b39a2d84c2fb346753cbfbccd4c-b043d5e1ec6397d2-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,...,sentry-trace_id=88529b39a2d84c2fb346753cbfbccd4c,sentry-sampled=true,..."} And with traceLifecycle 'stream': {"type":"span","trace_id":"672151c7cba245f0b4680aa09b41bdb6","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","http.server GET /downstream"],"raw":[{"name":"GET 127.0.0.1","status":"ok","parent_span_id":"afb4176f3d9a0ec3","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.http.fetch"},{"name":"GET /downstream","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.deno"}]} The child span, the parent link and the propagated headers are all correct, so the missing piece is only that @sentry/deno ships no such default integration (and does not export the building blocks). Note the streamed span name is `GET 127.0.0.1` (host only), unlike the static description which carries the full URL.
db spans✓ worksModule-scope mysql@2 connection queried inside the handler: static lifecycle gives the db span nested under the request transaction (`db SELECT id, name FROM users` with db.query.text and db.system mysql), stream gives `db SELECT users` with parent=acaa9154f7296eee sharing the request's trace id. Instrumentation path: the Deno import hook (`import "@sentry/deno/import"` as the first line, driver pulled in with `await import("mysql")` after init). The hook is required — no Bun-style bundle or Vite plugin is involved on Deno. Under app.listen() the same query produced a detached root transaction named `SELECT id, name FROM users` (op db, source custom) on its own trace id.
logs✓ worksSentry.logger.info("hello from oak", { route: "/log" }) inside the handler arrived as a log envelope, correlated to the request trace: `info: hello from oak :: trace=96ff9d665adc4729880bc3fa893f4c63`, the same trace id as the `http.server GET /log` span. Stream lifecycle.
client errors· not-runNo browser/client surface — Oak is a server-only framework and this probe ran server-side on Deno only.

Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions Oak on any runtime. `grep -rin '\boak\b' ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs ~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes` returns nothing, and `grep -rl '@oak/oak|jsr:@oak'` returns nothing. The Deno guide is a single 232-line page, ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx, plus configuration/integrations/{breadcrumbs,contextlines}.mdx; it names no framework at all — not Oak, not Fresh, not Hono, and it does not even mention Deno.serve. It also never mentions the import hook: index.mdx:41-44 shows only `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno";` as the first import, with no `import "@sentry/deno/import";` line anywhere in the repo (`grep -rn 'sentry/deno/import' ~/dev/sentry-docs` is empty), and nothing about `nodeModulesDir`. A user following the page as written today would get errors, method-named spans and logs, but no db spans, because the hook line is missing.

Documented: no

An Oak page must exist and must lead with the mounting shape, because the two Oak mounting styles are not equivalent for Sentry: mount with `Deno.serve(app.fetch)` and never with `app.listen()` — under `app.listen()` handlers run outside the request's async context, so there is no active span and errors are never captured at all. With `Deno.serve(app.fetch)`, errors, isolation, incoming trace continuation, database spans and logs all work with no extra wiring. Two caveats must be documented. (1) Route names: Oak spans are named by HTTP method only until the app names them; register a `router.use()` middleware BEFORE any route on that router that reads `ctx.matched?.at(-1)?.path` and calls `Sentry.updateSpanName(Sentry.getActiveSpan(), \`${ctx.request.method} ${route}\`)`. (2) Outgoing requests: `@sentry/deno` does not instrument Deno's global `fetch` — no `http.client` span, no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` header, so the downstream service starts a new trace. Two fixes were verified in both trace lifecycles: use `node:http` for the outgoing call (zero code beyond the client swap — `http.get(url, ...)` produced `http.client GET <url>` plus both headers), or keep `fetch` and register a userland fetch integration built from `@sentry/core` primitives. The page must also show the `deno.json` shape the run needed: `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual", "imports": {"@oak/oak": "jsr:@oak/oak@^17", "@sentry/deno": "npm:@sentry/deno"}}` with the SDK present in a real `node_modules`.

Page to write: guides/deno/frameworks/oak.mdx (new), with the `Deno.serve(app.fetch)` vs `app.listen()` warning as its first section

`grep -rin '\boak\b' docs/ platform-includes/` and `grep -rl '@oak/oak\|jsr:@oak' docs/` return nothing; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-232 names no framework and never mentions `Deno.serve` (only bare `deno run` at :106 and :125); guides/deno/ contains only index.mdx and configuration/integrations/{breadcrumbs,contextlines}.mdx

Headline: Oak is fine on Deno, but the mount shape decides whether the SDK works at all. `Deno.serve(app.fetch)` is the only shape worth documenting; `app.listen()` silently loses errors, route names and span parenting, and actively leaks isolation scopes between concurrent requests (a correctness bug a user would experience as wrong tags/users on events). Root cause: Oak's `listen()` server drains requests through its own async queue, so the handler body escapes the AsyncLocalStorage context that `wrapDenoRequestHandler` opened inside the Deno.serve callback. `Deno.serve(app.fetch)` keeps the handler inside that context. This is worth an SDK issue independent of docs — Oak's listen path is the same shape other Deno frameworks with their own accept loops will have. Second gap: route names are not automatic. `denoServeIntegration` names the span before Oak has matched anything, so every request is `GET` (stream) or the raw URL (static). The 6-line `ctx.matched.at(-1).path` middleware in the setup field fixes it and is what a docs page must ship. Two caveats to document with it: it runs after `await next()`, so it never fires on the error path (the `/error` span keeps `src=url`), and it needs `SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE = 'route'` explicitly because `updateSpanName` alone stamps source `custom`. Third: Oak's `app.fetch` is typed as a Cloudflare fetch handler `(request, env, ctx)`. On Deno the second argument is `ServeHandlerInfo`, and Oak resolves the client IP only from the `CF-Connecting-IP` header, so `ctx.request.ip` is empty. Harmless for Sentry (the SDK reads the address from `info.remoteAddr` itself), but it will confuse anyone comparing `ctx.request.ip` with the `client.address` on the span. Fourth: with `nodeModulesDir: "manual"` Oak does not boot until `path-to-regexp@^6.3.0` is present in node_modules — a hard blocker that any docs page pairing Oak with the symlinked/manual SDK setup has to call out. Also note `npm install` in that directory deletes sibling symlinks, so the `@sentry/*` links must be re-created after it. Errors reaching Sentry twice (auto `auto.http.deno` from the Deno.serve wrapper plus a manual `oak` capture from the middleware) is currently masked by `dedupeIntegration`. Only one event arrived in every run. Docs should therefore present the error middleware as optional on the `app.fetch` path and required only if the user registers an Oak `error` listener (which would stop the re-throw). Outgoing fetch is the known Deno K2 gap and reproduced unchanged here (no span, no headers); nothing Oak-specific. Client errors are not applicable — Oak is server-only. Cleanup: all four deno processes and the sink were killed (`kill $pid; wait $pid`). node_modules left in place at 128K (one npm package plus symlinks) so the probe reruns without a reinstall; say the word and it can go.

Fresh on Deno M-fresh-deno

Fresh 2 (@fresh/core 2.3.3, @fresh/plugin-vite 1.1.2, scaffolded with jsr:@fresh/init@2.3.3) · deno 2.9.0, @sentry/deno 10.67.0 from develop (6f2da7483d), tarballs in $REPRO/_toolbox/pack · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Fresh 2 runs on Deno unchanged, and the Sentry Deno SDK can be wired into it, but nothing about the framework is instrumented automatically: a hand-written middleware is required for both errors and route names.

1) Scaffold: `deno run -A jsr:@fresh/init@^2 ./app` (vite mode, the default). `deno.json` gets `"nodeModulesDir": "manual"` and the init populates `node_modules` with a Deno-style `.deno` layout.

2) Install the SDK into that same `node_modules` (the Deno import hook only transforms packages under a local `node_modules`, so the packages must be real directories there). `npm install` cannot be run in the app dir without pruning Deno's tree, so install into a side dir and copy in:
   `mkdir sdkdeps && cd sdkdeps && npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-deno-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz mysql@2`
   then `cp -R sdkdeps/node_modules/{@sentry,mysql,sqlstring,bignumber.js,readable-stream,...} app/node_modules/`.

3) `deno.json` imports: add `"@sentry/deno": "npm:@sentry/deno@10.67.0"`, `"@sentry/deno/import": "npm:/@sentry/deno@10.67.0/import"`, `"mysql": "npm:mysql@^2"`.

4) `app/instrument.ts`:
```ts
import "@sentry/deno/import";
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno";
Sentry.init({ dsn: "___DSN___", tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: "static" });
```

5) `app/main.ts` — `import "./instrument.ts";` as the FIRST line, before `import { App } from "fresh"`, then register a Sentry middleware immediately after `staticFiles()`:
```ts
app.use(async (ctx) => {
  const span = Sentry.getActiveSpan();
  if (span && ctx.route) {
    const root = Sentry.getRootSpan(span);
    Sentry.updateSpanName(root, `${ctx.req.method} ${ctx.route}`);
    root.setAttribute("http.route", ctx.route);
    root.setAttribute("sentry.segment.name.source", "route");
  }
  try { return await ctx.next(); }
  catch (e) { Sentry.captureException(e, { mechanism: { type: "fresh.middleware", handled: false } }); throw e; }
});
```
`ctx.route` is the matched Fresh route pattern (`/api/users/:id`); rethrowing keeps Fresh's own 500 page.

6) Run commands: dev `deno task dev --port <p>`; prod `deno task build && deno serve -A --port <p> _fresh/server.js`. No `--import` flag is needed in either shape: in dev the hook is loaded by `instrument.ts` inside the Vite SSR graph, and in the build everything (SDK included) is bundled into `_fresh/server/server-entry.mjs`.

Both shapes produce `http.server` spans: dev because the Vite dev server runs on `node:http` (`denoHttpIntegration`), the build because `deno serve` calls the JS `Deno.serve` after the entry module has run, so `denoServeIntegration`'s proxy is already installed.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors◐ partialFresh swallows every route error: App.handler() catches it and returns the 500 from DEFAULT_ERROR_HANDLER, so it never escapes to Deno.serve/node:http and Sentry's own handlers never see it. With no middleware, GET /api/boom produced only a 500 transaction and no event at all. The only mechanism that works is a user middleware that wraps `await ctx.next()` in try/catch, calls Sentry.captureException and rethrows; with it the event arrives in both vite dev and the `deno serve _fresh/server.js` build (mechanism is whatever you pass, here `fresh.middleware`, handled false), carries a context line, and shares the request's trace id. verified: partial Setup reused (and extended) the earlier probe app at $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-fresh-deno-errors/app (Fresh 2.3.3 + @fresh/plugin-vite 1.1.2, deno 2.9.0, @sentry/deno 10.67.0 from develop in app/node_modules, traceLifecycle static, tunnel to my sink on 52117). Probe files: app/instrument.ts, app/main.ts, app/early.ts, app/routes/_error.tsx, app/routes/api/boom2.ts, app/routes/throwpage.tsx; driver run-b/drive.sh; logs run-b/*.log. Commands: `SENTRY_MODE=<mode> SINK_PORT=52117 deno task dev --port 52118` and `deno task build && SENTRY_MODE=<mode> SINK_PORT=52117 deno serve -A --port 52119 _fresh/server.js`, then `run-b/drive.sh <appport> 52117 <label>` (hits /api/boom = programmatic app.get route, /api/boom2 = fs route handler, /throwpage = page render throw, then a captureMessage sentinel). CONFIRMED, no automatic capture. Baseline (no wiring), dev and prod, all three throw shapes: /api/boom -> 500 ; /api/boom2 -> 500 ; /throwpage -> 500 tx | GET /api/boom | src= url | status= internal_error | trace= 809d5817 tx | GET /api/boom2 | src= url | status= internal_error | trace= 96164bfa tx | GET /throwpage | src= url | status= internal_error | trace= 5bf72d3f event | sentinel | mech= generic handled= True This is structural: jsr @fresh/core 2.3.3 src/app.ts App.handler() ends in `catch (err) { ctx.error = err; return await DEFAULT_ERROR_HANDLER(ctx); }`, so nothing escapes to Deno.serve/node:http. (Note the transaction status IS internal_error, so 500s are at least visible as failed transactions.) REFUTED: the middleware is NOT the only mechanism. Four wirings all deliver the exception with the request's trace id, request data, and (in the built app) context lines, in BOTH `vite dev` and `deno serve _fresh/server.js`: 1) captureConsoleIntegration - init only, zero framework code, zero middleware. `integrations: [Sentry.captureConsoleIntegration({ levels: ['error'], handled: false })]`. It works because DEFAULT_ERROR_HANDLER does `console.error(error)` and core's console handler does `args.find(arg => arg instanceof Error)` -> captureException with the real stack. PROD: event | Error: fresh-deno-boom | mech= auto.core.capture_console handled= False | ctxline= True | trace= 91440922 event | Error: fresh-fsroute-boom | mech= auto.core.capture_console handled= False | ctxline= True | trace= f6f27fbc event | Error: fresh-render-boom | mech= auto.core.capture_console handled= False | ctxline= True | trace= 11c92867 DEV: same three, each on its transaction's trace (mech= auto.core.capture_console, tx= GET /api/boom etc.). 2) setErrorInterceptor from `jsr:@fresh/core@^2.3.3/internal` (public JSR export, `setErrorInterceptor(app, err => Sentry.captureException(err, ...))`, no ctx.next wrapping). Works in dev too even though @fresh/plugin-vite calls it per request - the compiled chain closes over the interceptor set at handler() time. PROD: event | Error: fresh-deno-boom | mech= fresh.errorInterceptor handled= False | ctxline= True | trace= 8800dad3 (+ the other two) 3) The reported try/catch middleware - reconfirmed, and it also covers fs routes and page renders, not just app.get routes (mech= fresh.middleware, all three, dev and prod). 4) routes/_error.tsx capturing `props.error` - works, but only for fs routes: /api/boom2 and /throwpage produced `mech= fresh._error`, /api/boom (registered via app.get, outside the fsRoutes segment) produced nothing. NEW LIMITATION the report missed: any programmatic Fresh error handler silently kills mechanisms 1-3, including the reported middleware. With `app.onError("*", () => new Response("custom error page", { status: 500 }))` registered, prod runs produced ZERO events in every wiring: PROD captureConsole + error page -> only tx rows + sentinel, no event (console.error is never reached) PROD setErrorInterceptor + error page -> only tx rows + sentinel, no event PROD middleware + error page -> only tx rows + sentinel, no event (the error never reaches the outer catch) Capturing inside the error handler itself is then the only option and does work: `app.onError("*", ctx => { Sentry.captureException(ctx.error, ...); return ... })` gave mech= fresh.onError for all three shapes in dev and prod. A file-based routes/_error.tsx behaves differently from app.onError: it renders the custom page AND the error still reaches an outer middleware, so combining the two double-captures (one of the two events is then dropped by the default dedupe integration - which one wins is not predictable). ROOT CAUSE of "nothing about the framework is instrumented" (bonus, bears on the routenames/spans cells): Fresh 2 ships its own OTel instrumentation - src/otel.ts does `trace.getTracer("fresh", VERSION)` at module scope, compileMiddlewares wraps every chain in `tracer.startActiveSpan("middlewares", ...)`, `recordSpanError` calls `span.recordException(err)`, and App.handler does `span.updateName(`${method} ${pattern}`)` + `span.setAttribute("http.route", pattern)` on the active OTel span. @sentry/deno DOES register a global OTel provider (build/esm/opentelemetry/tracer.js: `setupOpenTelemetryTracer(){ trace.disable(); trace.setGlobalTracerProvider(new SentryDenoTraceProvider()); }`) and there is exactly ONE @opentelemetry/api copy (1.9.1) in the built bundle - yet no Fresh span ever arrives (`tx | GET /api/users/42 | spans= []`). My /api/otel probe pins the reason: a tracer obtained AFTER init works, one obtained BEFORE init is dead forever, because `trace.disable()` replaces the ProxyTracerProvider singleton and orphans every ProxyTracer handed out earlier: {"tracer":"SentryDenoTracer","earlyTracer":"ProxyTracer","earlySpan":"NonRecordingSpan","span":"SentrySpan","globalVersion":"1.9.1"} (`span` = probe span started at request time -> real SentrySpan and it does show up: `tx | GET /api/otel | spans= ['probe-span']`; `earlySpan` = tracer captured in early.ts imported one line before instrument.ts -> NonRecordingSpan.) Fresh's module-level tracer is exactly this case, so all of Fresh's native spans and its http.route naming are silently discarded. Fixing Sentry.init to not orphan pre-existing tracers (or to set the delegate on the existing proxy provider) would light up Fresh middleware/render spans and route names for free. I could not find a user-side ordering fix: preloading with `deno serve -A --import=./instrument.ts _fresh/server.js` still left the pre-init tracer a NonRecordingSpan. Not applicable/not tried: no Fresh e2e app exists in the repo (dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications has deno, deno-mysql, deno-pg, deno-redis, deno-streamed only, all raw Deno.serve), and ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/ has no Fresh page at all. All processes I started were killed; ports 52117-52119 are free.
Workaround: Two-part wiring, both verified in `vite dev` and in the `deno serve _fresh/server.js` build. (a) If the app has no custom error handler, the cheapest capture is init-only, no framework code: `Sentry.init({ ..., integrations: [Sentry.captureConsoleIntegration({ levels: ['error'], handled: false })] })` in instrument.ts, imported as the first line of main.ts - Fresh's DEFAULT_ERROR_HANDLER console.errors every swallowed route, fs-route and render error and the integration turns it into a real exception event on the request's trace. (b) The moment the app registers an error handler (`app.onError("*", ...)`), that integration - and a try/catch middleware, and setErrorInterceptor - all go silent, so capture inside the handler instead: `app.onError("*", (ctx) => { Sentry.captureException(ctx.error, { mechanism: { type: 'fresh.onError', handled: false } }); return new Response("Internal server error", { status: 500 }); })`. A file-based routes/_error.tsx capturing props.error works too but covers only fs routes, not routes registered with app.get/post/etc. `setErrorInterceptor(app, err => Sentry.captureException(err, ...))` from `jsr:@fresh/core@^2.3.3/internal` is the least intrusive alternative to the try/catch middleware when there is no error handler.
route names✗ brokenNothing names the route automatically. Baseline stream lifecycle: `http.server | GET | src=url`; baseline static: `GET /api/users/42` with source=url — the raw path, high cardinality. Fresh does call `trace.getActiveSpan()` and `span.updateName(`${method} ${pattern}`)` + `http.route` in app.ts:444-447, but @opentelemetry/api resolves to the NoopTracer/ROOT context there, so it is a no-op. Setting the name from `ctx.route` in the middleware gives `GET /api/users/:id`, src=route, route=/api/users/:id in both lifecycles. verified: confirmed-broken Refutation attempt failed: no configuration of @sentry/deno 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) names a Fresh 2 route by itself. Both server shapes and both lifecycles still emit the raw URL, and app code is required in every case. I did find the exact root cause and a workaround that is smaller and better than the reported Fresh middleware. Root cause (sharper than the original report). @sentry/deno DOES ship an OTel bridge: `init()` calls `setupOpenTelemetryTracer()` unless `enableOpenTelemetrySetup: false` (app/node_modules/@sentry/deno/build/esm/sdk.js:48-50 -> build/esm/opentelemetry/tracer.js). It calls `trace.disable()` and `trace.setGlobalTracerProvider(new SentryDenoTraceProvider())`, so `trace.getTracer(...).startSpan()/startActiveSpan()` DO produce real Sentry spans - I see Fresh's own `via-tracer`/`handler` spans arriving. What it does not install is an OTel ContextManager, so `context.active()` is still the NoopContextManager and `trace.getActiveSpan()` returns undefined. Fresh 2's router (jsr @fresh/core 2.3.3 src/app.ts:444-448: `const span = trace.getActiveSpan(); if (span && pattern) { span.updateName(`${method} ${pattern}`); span.setAttribute("http.route", pattern); }`) therefore no-ops. The SDK's own JSDoc for `enableOpenTelemetrySetup` admits the gap: "This does not handle custom context handling, it will always work off the current scope." The prior report's "@opentelemetry/api resolves to the NoopTracer" is half right: the tracer is Sentry's, the CONTEXT is noop. Baseline (unchanged, my run) - vite dev, static: transaction | GET /api/users/42 | op=http.server | src=url | route=None | segsrc=url spans= [] transaction | GET /api/boom | op=http.server | src=url | route=None | segsrc=url spans= [] Baseline - `deno serve _fresh/server.js` build, static: identical (`GET /api/users/42 | src=url | route=None`). Working workaround, no Fresh middleware at all - register an OTel ContextManager in instrument.ts that resolves the SPAN key to the active Sentry root span (mode `ctxmgr-route`, app/instrument.ts). Fresh's built-in call then does all the naming: vite dev, static: transaction | GET /api/users/:id | op=http.server | src=route | route=/api/users/:id | segsrc=route vite dev, stream: span | http.server | GET /api/users/:id | src=route | route=/api/users/:id | seg=True deno serve build, stream: span | http.server | GET /api/users/:id | src=route | route=/api/users/:id | seg=True deno serve build, static: transaction | GET /api/users/:id | op=http.server | src=custom | route=/api/users/:id (mode `ctxmgr`, the plain variant) The plain bridge (return the Sentry root span object as-is, mode `ctxmgr`) already gives `GET /api/users/:id` + `http.route` but leaves `src=custom`, because core's `updateName` marks the source custom. Wrapping the span so that `setAttribute("http.route", ...)` also sets `sentry.segment.name.source: "route"` upgrades it to `src=route`. Child spans (`custom work`, `via-tracer`) still nest correctly under the segment with the bridge installed. Also re-checked and ruled out: `Deno.telemetry.contextManager` as the global context manager (mode `denootel`) - Deno's context never holds a Sentry span because the SDK called `trace.disable()`, so getActiveSpan stays undefined; there is no Fresh guide in ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/ (only `deno/index.mdx` + `deno/configuration`), and no Fresh e2e app in dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications (only deno, deno-mysql, deno-pg, deno-redis, deno-streamed), so there is no documented wiring to fall back on. Files (all under $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-fresh-deno-routenames/): app/instrument.ts (modes baseline | ctxmgr | ctxmgr-active | ctxmgr-route | denootel | middleware), app/main.ts, app/routes/api/{boom,child,sentinel}.ts, app/routes/api/users/[id].ts, sink2.mjs, report.py, run2.sh, runprod2.sh, drive2.sh, and the captured results out-base-static.txt, out-ctx-static.txt, out-ctx-stream.txt, out-ctxroute-static.txt, out-ctxroute-stream.txt, out-prod-base-static.txt, out-prod-ctx-static.txt, out-prod-ctxroute-stream.txt. Rerun: `PORT=51477 node sink2.mjs &` then `./run2.sh <mode> <static|stream> <label>` (vite dev, port 51478) or `cd app && deno task build` + `./runprod2.sh <mode> <lifecycle> <label>` (deno serve, port 51479); each writes out-<label>.txt.
Workaround: In instrument.ts, after Sentry.init, install an OTel ContextManager that maps the OTel active-span key to the active Sentry root span - then Fresh 2 names its own routes, in dev and in the build, in both lifecycles, with no Fresh middleware: const SPAN_KEY = Symbol.for("OpenTelemetry Context Key SPAN"); function bridgeSpan() { const active = Sentry.getActiveSpan(); if (!active) return undefined; const root = Sentry.getRootSpan(active); return { updateName(n) { Sentry.updateSpanName(root, n); return this; }, setAttribute(k, v) { root.setAttribute(k, v); if (k === "http.route") root.setAttribute("sentry.segment.name.source", "route"); return this; }, setAttributes(a) { for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(a)) this.setAttribute(k, v); return this; }, spanContext: () => root.spanContext(), isRecording: () => true, setStatus() { return this; }, recordException(e) { Sentry.captureException(e); return this; }, addEvent() { return this; }, end() {}, }; } class Ctx { constructor(m = new Map()) { this.m = m; } getValue(k) { return k === SPAN_KEY ? bridgeSpan() : this.m.get(k); } setValue(k, v) { const m = new Map(this.m); m.set(k, v); return new Ctx(m); } deleteValue(k) { const m = new Map(this.m); m.delete(k); return new Ctx(m); } } context.setGlobalContextManager({ active: () => new Ctx(), with: (_c, fn, self, ...a) => fn.call(self, ...a), bind: (_c, t) => t, enable() { return this; }, disable() { return this; }, }); (`context` from "@opentelemetry/api", which must be in deno.json imports.) Errors still need the try/catch middleware from the earlier report - this bridge only fixes naming. The alternative, if you already have a Fresh middleware, is the reported `Sentry.updateSpanName(root, `${ctx.req.method} ${ctx.route}`)` + `http.route` + `sentry.segment.name.source` middleware; it produces the same names.
isolation✗ brokenvite dev (node:http path): correct — three concurrent /api/iso?t=a|b|c requests each produced an event and a transaction with only its own tag and its own trace id, and later requests carried tags=None. The `deno serve _fresh/server.js` build leaks: after the same three concurrent requests, every subsequent transaction and event carried tags={'probe': 'a'}, and a purely sequential repeat (iso?t=solo, then /api/msg, then /api/sentinel) showed probe=solo on all three. So per-request state survives the request in the production shape. verified: confirmed-broken CONFIRMED, and broader than reported. The leak is not a Fresh problem, not a `deno serve` problem, and not a Sentry scope-management bug. It is a Deno `AsyncLocalStorage` defect: awaiting a dynamic `import()` inside `als.run()` restores the *inner* store into the enclosing (root) async context, permanently. Deno 2.9.0 only (2.8.3 is not on this machine, `$SCRATCH/deno283` does not exist). 1) Pure-Deno repro, zero Sentry, both server shapes (mini/pure-matrix.ts, `MODE=denoserve|nodehttp PORT=<p> deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys pure-matrix.ts`): Deno.serve: {"id":"r3","path":"/dyn","storeAtEntry":null,"storeInside":"r3"} {"id":"r4","path":"/plain","storeAtEntry":"r3","storeInside":"r4"} {"id":"r5","path":"/dyn-cached","storeAtEntry":"r3","storeInside":"r5"} {"id":"r6","path":"/plain","storeAtEntry":"r5","storeInside":"r6"} node:http: {"id":"r2","path":"/dyn","storeAtEntry":null,"storeInside":"r2"} {"id":"r3","path":"/plain","storeAtEntry":"r2","storeInside":"r3"} Node v26.5.0, same code (/tmp/nodehttp-check.mjs): storeAtEntry is null on every request. So node:http under Deno leaks too, i.e. the "vite dev is correct" half of the original report is luck, not correctness. 2) Which awaits leak (mini/leak-matrix.ts on Deno.serve, one request per op): {"op":"timer","storeAtRootAfter":null} {"op":"readfile","storeAtRootAfter":null} {"op":"wasm","storeAtRootAfter":null} {"op":"crypto","storeAtRootAfter":null} {"op":"dynimport_data","storeAtEntry":"dynimport_data#6"} <- next request inherits {"op":"dynimport_file","storeAtEntry":"dynimport_data#7"} <- cached module leaks too {"op":"timer","storeAtEntry":"dynimport_file#8"} <- and it sticks Only `await import()` leaks; the leak lands in the root context after the handler returns, so the *next* request enters already poisoned. 3) Why Fresh prod hits it: `vite build` splits every route into its own chunk and `_fresh/server/server-entry.mjs:6685` loads them lazily — `{ id: "/api/iso", mod: () => import("./assets/_fresh-route___api_iso-R3fdqHTX.mjs"), ... }`. The first request to each route therefore performs a dynamic import inside `wrapDenoRequestHandler`'s `withIsolationScope`, and leaks that request's isolation scope. Baseline `deno serve -A --port 41524 _fresh/server.js`, sequential: tx | GET /api/user | tags= undefined | user= undefined tx | GET /api/msg | ... event | probe-msg | user= "alice" | ctx= {"who":"alice"} <- leaked from /api/user tx | GET /api/iso | tags= {"probe":"first"} event | probe-msg | tags= {"probe":"first"} | user= "alice" | ctx= {"who":"alice"} tx | GET /api/msg | tags= {"probe":"first"} tx | GET /api/iso | tags= {"probe":"second"} <- 2nd hit, chunk cached, no import, does NOT re-leak event | probe-msg | tags= {"probe":"first"} ... <- still the first leak event | sentinel-7 | tags= {"probe":"first"} | user= "alice" | ctx= {"who":"alice"} Note the shape: only the request that performs the import leaks, which is why a warm sequential run over already-loaded routes can look clean. My first cold run (3 concurrent `/api/iso?t=a|b|c` as the first requests) did *not* leak; the sequential first-hit-per-route run always does. 4) Not framework-specific. Bare `Deno.serve` + `@sentry/deno`, no Fresh, no middleware (mini/server5.ts MODE=A, `deno serve -A -c deno2.json --port 41531 server5.ts`): tx | GET /dyn | tags= {"probe":"LEAK"} tx | GET /msg | tags= {"probe":"LEAK"} event | probe-msg | tags= {"probe":"LEAK"} tx | GET /msg | tags= {"probe":"LEAK"} event | probe-msg | tags= {"probe":"LEAK"} event | sentinel | tags= {"probe":"LEAK"} Any Deno app whose handler awaits a dynamic import (lazy route loading, lazy driver loading, code splitting) is affected. 5) Vite dev leaks identically once app code does the import (`deno task dev --port 41540`, /api/dyn awaits `import("data:text/javascript,...")`): tx | GET /api/dyn | tags= {"probe":"DEVLEAK"} tx | GET /api/msg | tags= {"probe":"DEVLEAK"} event | probe-msg | tags= {"probe":"DEVLEAK"} event | sentinel-9 | tags= {"probe":"DEVLEAK"} Dev's `/api/user` first hit did not leak, because Vite's SSR module runner resolves route modules without a native `import()`. Mechanism on the SDK side (packages/deno/src/wrap-deno-request-handler.ts:42 and packages/server-utils/src/async-context.ts): `withIsolationScope(cb)` clones the *ambient* current and isolation scopes. When the ambient store is the leaked one, the fork inherits its tags/user/contexts/breadcrumbs. The SDK code is correct for a correct ALS; it has no defence against a runtime that hands it a poisoned ambient store. Two candidate SDK-side fixes measured (mini/server5.ts, denoServeIntegration disabled so the boundary is mine): MODE=C (`withIsolationScope(cb)`, today's behaviour) reproduces the leak; MODE=B (`withIsolationScope(getDefaultIsolationScope().clone(), cb)`) clears it — `event | probe-msg | tags= undefined` for every request after the leaking one. MODE=B alone is not sufficient as a shipped fix: `withSetIsolationScope` does not mint a new trace id, so all requests shared one trace and later root spans were swallowed as children. A real fix needs to reset both scopes to the defaults at the request boundary, i.e. a "fresh context" primitive rather than a fork. I could not patch `app/node_modules/@sentry/deno/build/esm/wrap-deno-request-handler.js` to verify the fix inside the real Fresh build: the auto-mode classifier denied the in-place edit of a package-manager file. The MODE=B/C comparison is the substitute. Repo coverage: `dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/deno/tests/scope.test.ts` only asserts that `Sentry.withScope` tags do not leak *within* one request. No Deno test drives two requests and asserts the second one is clean, so nothing in CI would catch this. Rerun: `PORT=41520 node sink2.mjs &`; `(cd app && deno task build)`; `(cd app && SINK_PORT=41520 LIFECYCLE=static FRESH_ISO=0 deno serve -A --port 41524 _fresh/server.js &)`; `node driveU.mjs 41524 41520 "/api/user?u=alice" "/api/msg" "/api/iso?t=first" "/api/msg" "/api/sentinel?n=7"`.
Workaround: Two, both user-land, both verified. Best (fixes events AND transactions, keeps the SDK's request metadata): a first middleware that scrubs the isolation scope it inherited. In app/main.ts, run this before `ctx.next()` (FRESH_ISO=2 in my probe, `deno serve -A --port 41541 _fresh/server.js`): const iso = Sentry.getIsolationScope(); const d = iso.getScopeData(); for (const k of Object.keys(d.tags ?? {})) iso.setTag(k, undefined); for (const k of Object.keys(d.contexts ?? {})) iso.setContext(k, null); for (const k of Object.keys(d.extra ?? {})) iso.setExtra(k, undefined); iso.setUser(null); iso.clearBreadcrumbs(); iso.clearAttachments(); Result on the same sequence that leaked above: tx | GET /api/iso | tags= {"probe":"first"} event | probe-msg | tags= {} | user= undefined | ctx= undefined tx | GET /api/msg | tags= {} tx | GET /api/dyn | tags= {"probe":"DYN"} event | probe-msg | tags= {} | user= undefined tx | GET /api/iso | tags= {"probe":"second"} event | sentinel-10 | tags= {} | user= undefined | ctx= undefined Do NOT use the obvious `Sentry.withIsolationScope(new Sentry.Scope(), ...)` middleware (FRESH_ISO=1). It cleans events but silently misattributes transactions, because `Sentry.setTag` then writes to the user's scope while the transaction is still built from the SDK's leaked one: tx | GET /api/iso | tags= undefined <- probe=first lost tx | GET /api/msg | tags= {"probe":"first"} <- and applied to the next request instead Second, partial: keep Fresh in dev, or preload every route module at boot so no `import()` ever runs inside a request. That only shrinks the blast radius to one poisoned request per route; any other in-request dynamic import re-opens it.

This is the known Deno gap K2, not something Fresh causes. verified: confirmed-broken Reproduced exactly, and it is a @sentry/deno gap (K2), not a Fresh gap. Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-fresh-deno-outgoingfetch (Fresh 2.3.3 + @fresh/plugin-vite 1.1.2, deno 2.9.0, SDK from $REPRO/_toolbox/pack tarballs copied into app/node_modules). Two routes call out to a node:http recorder in the same request: /api/out uses global `fetch()`, /api/outnode uses `node:http.request()`. Driver: /run-b/drive.sh (sink 58101, recorder 58103, app 58105). A) vite dev, traceLifecycle static, stock SDK (no extra integration): transaction | GET /api/out | op=http.server | src=route | spans=[] transaction | GET /api/outnode | op=http.server | src=route | spans=["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:58103/__rec"] REC: [{"url":"/__rec?via=fetch","sentry-trace":null,"baggage":null,"traceparent":null}, {"url":"/__rec?via=nodehttp","sentry-trace":"99f997b2...-a15eefd75fd6ddc5-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,...,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fapi%2Foutnode,sentry-sampled=true,..."}] D) production build (`deno task build` then `deno serve -A --port 58105 _fresh/server.js`), static, stock SDK, same result: transaction | GET /api/out | op=http.server | src=route | spans=[] transaction | GET /api/outnode | op=http.server | src=route | spans=["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:58103/__rec"] REC: [{"url":"/__rec?via=fetch","sentry-trace":null,"baggage":null,...}, {"url":"/__rec?via=nodehttp","sentry-trace":"b6219c48...-a725b91224d50651-1",...}] So the only thing that fails is the global `fetch()`; `node:http` clients in the very same handler get an http.client span and both headers. Neither init placement, entry shape, nor lifecycle changes this: I tested vite dev and the bundled `_fresh/server.js`, and traceLifecycle static and stream. No variant of the framework wiring can fix it, because nothing in the request path is involved. Root cause, verified in the source rather than guessed: `@sentry/deno` has no fetch tracing integration at all. Its default integration list (packages/deno/src/sdk.ts getDefaultIntegrations) contains denoServeIntegration + denoHttpIntegration, and denoHttpIntegration (packages/deno/src/integrations/http.ts) subscribes only to the `node:http` diagnostics channels (getHttpClientSubscriptions / HTTP_ON_CLIENT_REQUEST), which Deno's native `fetch` never goes through. Nothing named `fetchIntegration` is exported from packages/deno/src/index.ts. Notably the monkey-patch itself works fine on Deno: the default `breadcrumbsIntegration` (packages/deno/src/integrations/breadcrumbs.ts:47) already calls `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` for fetch breadcrumbs. What is missing is a handler that calls `instrumentFetchRequest`, i.e. exactly the file `@sentry/cloudflare` already ships at packages/cloudflare/src/integrations/fetch.ts. I proved that by porting it into user land and re-running the same probe (app/fetch-tracing.ts, enabled by SENTRY_FETCH_TRACING=1): B2) vite dev, static, with the integration: transaction | GET /api/out | op=http.server | src=route | spans=["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:58103/__rec"] REC: [{"url":"/__rec?via=fetch","sentry-trace":"c63d512111a8494fb8d0d3bf177b62d0-a23f474f5c9a1061-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,sentry-public_key=public,sentry-trace_id=c63d512111a8494fb8d0d3bf177b62d0,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fapi%2Fout,sentry-sampled=true,sentry-sample_rate=1",...}] C) vite dev, traceLifecycle stream, with the integration: span | ["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","http.server GET /api/out"] E) production build (`deno serve _fresh/server.js`), static, with the integration: transaction | GET /api/out | op=http.server | src=route | spans=["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:58103/__rec"] REC: [{"url":"/__rec?via=fetch","sentry-trace":"da5b6e985cf2498bb56030cb5e62c25d-9e6ddd7760f6588e-1","baggage":"...sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fapi%2Fout,sentry-sampled=true,..."}] Because a ~20-line user-land integration using only publicly exported `@sentry/core` APIs restores the span, the correct parent/child nesting and both headers in every shape, the gap is purely a missing default integration in `@sentry/deno`, not a Deno platform limitation. I did not exercise Deno's native `--unstable-otel` fetch instrumentation: it exports through Deno's own OTLP pipeline and shares no trace context with the Sentry SDK, so it cannot produce a child of the Sentry server span. Repro: `cd app && SENTRY_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:58101/ REC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:58103 SENTRY_LIFECYCLE=static SENTRY_FETCH_TRACING=0|1 deno task dev --port 58105`, then `curl /api/out /api/outnode /api/sentinel`. Logs in run-b/*.server.log; all servers I started are killed.
Workaround: Register a user-land fetch tracing integration; it is a straight port of packages/cloudflare/src/integrations/fetch.ts and needs `"@sentry/core": "npm:@sentry/core@10.67.0"` in the deno.json import map. app/fetch-tracing.ts: import type { Span } from "@sentry/core"; import { addFetchInstrumentationHandler, defineIntegration, getClient, instrumentFetchRequest, isSentryRequestUrl } from "@sentry/core"; const spans: Record<string, Span> = {}; export const fetchTracingIntegration = defineIntegration(() => ({ name: "FetchTracing", setup() { addFetchInstrumentationHandler(handlerData => { const client = getClient(); if (!client || isSentryRequestUrl(handlerData.fetchData.url, client)) return; instrumentFetchRequest(handlerData, () => true, () => true, spans, { spanOrigin: "auto.http.deno.fetch" }); }); }, })); then `Sentry.init({ ..., integrations: [fetchTracingIntegration()] })` in instrument.ts. The `isSentryRequestUrl` guard is required, otherwise the SDK's own envelope requests get spans. Verified in vite dev and in the `deno serve _fresh/server.js` build, under both traceLifecycle static and stream. Alternative with no SDK-internal APIs: call the service with `node:http`/`node:https` instead of `fetch`, which denoHttpIntegration already instruments end to end (span + sentry-trace + baggage), as run A shows.
db spans✓* works-waInstrumentation path: the Deno import hook (`import "@sentry/deno/import"`), plus `ssr.external: ["mysql"]` in vite.config so the dev SSR graph loads the driver through Deno's loader; both were needed. In vite dev a module-scope `mysql@2` connection then yields `db | SELECT users` (stream) / `db SELECT * FROM users` nested in the http.server transaction (static). Two caveats: the very first query after `connection.connect()` came out as its own root transaction in a separate trace, only later queries nest; and `mysql2` cannot be used at all — externalized it hits the known Deno hook bug K3 (`Unexpected token ':'`), bundled it hits vite CJS interop (`__vite_ssr_import_0__.default.createConnection is not a function`). In the production build there is no db span at all and the route 500s: @fresh/plugin-vite sets `resolve.noExternal: true` (src/mod.ts:125) so the driver is bundled into `_fresh/server/assets/_fresh-route___api_db-*.mjs`, a user `resolve.external`/`ssr.external` does not override it, and the bundled driver dies at runtime with `Cannot find module './lib/_stream_readable.js'`. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. `mysql@2` db spans work on Fresh 2 / Deno 2.9.0 with @sentry/deno 10.67.0 (develop) in BOTH `vite dev` AND the production `deno task build` + `deno serve` shape, in both trace lifecycles. The report's "production build has no db span and the route 500s" is a vite-config problem, not an SDK or Fresh limitation. THE EXACT CHANGE (vite.config.ts). The report used only `ssr: { external: ["mysql"] }`, which vite's build ignores because @fresh/plugin-vite sets `resolve.noExternal: true`. Adding a rollup external for the ssr *environment* does override it: ```ts export default defineConfig({ plugins: [fresh(), tailwindcss()], ssr: { external: ["mysql"] }, // needed for vite dev environments: { // needed for the build ssr: { build: { rollupOptions: { external: ["mysql"] } } }, }, }); ``` I isolated both knobs: - `ssr.external` only -> build bundles the driver: `_fresh-route___api_db-aH-ILX-r.mjs 518.83 kB` plus rollup warnings `"default" is not exported by "node_modules/mysql/lib/protocol/Auth.js"` (this is the shape that 500s at runtime). ($D/buildB2.log) - `environments.ssr.build.rollupOptions.external` only -> build externalizes: `_fresh-route___api_db-CSs3YcfK.mjs 0.85 kB`, and the chunk's first line is literally `import mysql from "mysql";`. ($D/buildB3.log) - `environments...` only, no `ssr.external` -> vite DEV breaks: `ReferenceError: exports is not defined` on /api/db. So both lines are load-bearing, one per shape. PRODUCTION EVIDENCE (`deno task build && LIFECYCLE=static deno serve -A --port 38419 _fresh/server.js`, sink on 38417): ``` {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/db","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_id":"e823d5e594324d61ad35a0be9365c323","sdk":"sentry.javascript.deno","spans":["db SELECT * FROM users"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/db","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_id":"45e510e093b14d92a5b8cd568b2f4f2b","sdk":"sentry.javascript.deno","spans":["db SELECT * FROM users"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/sentinel","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_id":"82f4be9bc5244c9cbee055a1c731073c","spans":[]} ``` Note both requests carry the db span, including the first one — the report's "first query becomes its own root transaction" caveat does NOT occur in the built server, because the route chunk (and with it the module-scope `createConnection`/`connect`) is lazily imported inside the first request. PRODUCTION, stream lifecycle (`LIFECYCLE=stream`), correctly parented: ``` {"type":"span","trace_id":"8b08040879554589bb4d4f7dac42ee27","items":["db SELECT users","http.server GET /api/db"],"raw":[{"name":"SELECT users","status":"ok","parent_span_id":"91b9f3b0097e3dc7","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.db.mysql"},{"name":"GET /api/db","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.deno"}]} ``` VITE DEV EVIDENCE (`LIFECYCLE=static deno task dev --port 38418`), warm server: ``` transaction | GET /api/db | op=http.server | spans=["db SELECT * FROM users"] transaction | GET /api/db | op=http.server | spans=["db SELECT * FROM users"] transaction | GET /api/sentinel | op=http.server | spans=[] ``` The report's orphan-first-query caveat reproduces only when /api/db is the very first request the freshly started dev server ever handles: `transaction | SELECT * FROM users | op=db | source=custom | spans=[]` in its own trace, and that request's http.server transaction is missing entirely. Sending any other request first (I used /api/name-warm) makes every /api/db request nest correctly. It is a vite-dev first-request warmup artifact, not a db-instrumentation defect, and it does not exist in the build. WHAT STILL DOES NOT WORK: `mysql2`. With the rollup external it is now correctly externalized (0.84 kB chunk), and it then hits Deno hook bug K3 in production exactly as reported — `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` at `mysql2/lib/connection_config.js:13` (`require` of a .json file under `Module.registerHooks`), route 500s, error captured by the middleware. That is denoland/deno#36240 and hits every Deno framework, so it is not a Fresh gap. `mysql@2` is the driver to use on Deno. No SDK change, no init/entry change and no lifecycle change was needed: `instrument.ts` (`import "@sentry/deno/import"` first, then `Sentry.init`) imported as the first line of `main.ts` is exactly the wiring the repo's own reference app uses (~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/deno-mysql/src/app.ts:5, with the same `nodeModulesDir: "manual"`). Workaround: Add a rollup external for the ssr environment on top of `ssr.external`, because @fresh/plugin-vite sets `resolve.noExternal: true` (src/mod.ts:125) and a plain `ssr.external` / `resolve.external` does not override it at build time: ```ts // vite.config.ts export default defineConfig({ plugins: [fresh(), tailwindcss()], ssr: { external: ["mysql"] }, environments: { ssr: { build: { rollupOptions: { external: ["mysql"] } } }, }, }); ``` `ssr.external` covers `vite dev`, the `environments.ssr.build.rollupOptions.external` entry covers `vite build`. With both, `mysql@2` stays a real `import mysql from "mysql"` in the emitted route chunk, Deno resolves it through the import map to `node_modules`, and the `@sentry/deno/import` hook instruments it in the built server exactly as in dev. Use `mysql@2`, not `mysql2` (the latter hits Deno's `require`-a-.json hook bug). If the dev server's very first request is a db route, the query surfaces as its own root transaction; hit any other route once after startup.

The Deno guide is a single 232-line page, docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx, plus two integration pages (breadcrumbs, contextlines); it shows only `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno"` + `Sentry.init` "before importing any other modules" (index.mdx:44, :64) and says nothing about any framework, about `Deno.serve` vs `deno serve`, about route naming, or about a middleware. `grep -rniI "@sentry/deno/import\|nodeModulesDir" docs/ platform-includes/` returns nothing at all, so the import hook that this probe needed for db spans is undocumented everywhere.

Documented: no

A Fresh 2 page must exist and state that Fresh on Deno is viable but that nothing framework-specific is instrumented automatically — a hand-written middleware is required. It must document, in this order: (1) Setup — scaffold with `deno run -A jsr:@fresh/init@^2`, set `"nodeModulesDir": "manual"` in `deno.json`, keep `import "@sentry/deno/import"` as the first line of `instrument.ts` and `instrument.ts` as the first import of `main.ts`. (2) Errors — Fresh catches route errors itself and returns its own 500 page, so unhandled errors never reach Sentry on their own; the verified fix is `integrations: [Sentry.captureConsoleIntegration({ levels: ['error'], handled: false })]` in `Sentry.init`, which reports them as real exceptions carrying the request's trace id, in both `deno task dev` and the `deno serve _fresh/server.js` build. (3) Route names — spans stay unparameterized unless the app renames them: register a middleware right after `staticFiles()` that reads `ctx.route` and calls `Sentry.updateSpanName` on the root span, which is the only way to get `sentry.segment.name.source: 'route'`. The page must also explain why Fresh's own route enrichment has no effect: the Deno SDK registers an OpenTelemetry TracerProvider but no ContextManager, so `trace.getActiveSpan()` from `@opentelemetry/api` returns `undefined` and the `http.route` Fresh sets there is dropped. (4) Isolation — per-request isolation is not reliable on Deno: Deno leaks the AsyncLocalStorage store out of a handler that awaits a dynamic `import()` (Node does not), so `Sentry.setTag`/`setUser`/`setContext`/`addBreadcrumb` from one request can attach to every later request; the app-level mitigation is to replace the isolation scope in the middleware before `ctx.next()` (new `Sentry.Scope`, `setClient(Sentry.getClient())`, carry over the propagation context and SDK processing metadata). (5) Outgoing fetch — no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers for native `fetch`; ship the userland `fetchTracingIntegration` built from `addFetchInstrumentationHandler`, `defineIntegration` and `instrumentFetchRequest`. (6) Database spans — `@fresh/plugin-vite` sets `resolve.noExternal: true`, so every instrumented driver must be listed in BOTH `ssr: { external: [...] }` (for `deno task dev`) and `environments: { ssr: { build: { rollupOptions: { external: [...] } } } }` (for `deno task build`); `ssr.external` alone does not survive the build. Incoming trace continuation and logs need no caveat.

Page to write: guides/deno/frameworks/fresh.mdx (new, following the guides/cloudflare/frameworks/*.mdx pattern), plus a new guides/deno/frameworks/index.mdx listing the supported Deno frameworks

No page mentions Fresh: `grep -rniE "\bfresh\b" docs/platforms/javascript/` returns only docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/agents-sdk.mdx:39 ("a fresh conversation ID"), and there is no docs/platforms/javascript/guides/fresh/ directory; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-232 is the entire Deno guide (plus configuration/integrations/{breadcrumbs,contextlines}.mdx) and names no framework — its only wiring is `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno"` + `Sentry.init` at :43-88, `--allow-net` at :106 and `--allow-read` at :125

Fresh 2 runs on Deno without Sentry in all three shapes tested (vite dev, `deno task build`, `deno serve -A _fresh/server.js`), so viability was never in doubt; the interesting result is how much hand-wiring the SDK needs. What a Fresh docs page would have to say that no existing page says: - Fresh catches all route errors in App.handler() (src/app.ts:491-494) and in its `_error` command chain, so error capture is impossible without a user middleware that rethrows. There is no `app.onError(handler)` hook that gives Sentry the error; `App.onError(path, routeOrMiddleware)` is a route-shaped 500 page, and the internal `setErrorInterceptor` is not exported from `fresh`'s mod.ts. - Fresh already writes the route name onto the active OTEL span (src/app.ts:444-447) and opens `middlewares` / `render` / route spans through `tracer.startActiveSpan` (src/middlewares/mod.ts:143, src/render.ts:31, src/context.ts:344). None of it reaches Sentry. @sentry/deno does register a global OTEL TracerProvider (sdk.ts:115 -> opentelemetry/tracer.ts), but `trace.getActiveSpan()` needs a ContextManager, which Sentry does not install, and in dev the app resolves a second copy of @opentelemetry/api (Deno's `.deno` layout vs the one under node_modules), so the calls land on NoopTracer. Making Sentry a real OTEL context/tracer host on Deno would give Fresh route names and framework spans for free. - `@sentry/deno` does not export `wrapDenoRequestHandler`, so there is no supported way to instrument a `deno serve` default export by hand. It happened to work here only because `deno serve` calls the JS `Deno.serve` after the entry module ran, so the `denoServeIntegration` proxy was already in place. Two defects worth filing: 1. Isolation-scope/current-scope leak in the `deno serve` production shape: a `Sentry.setTag` in one request shows up on every later request's events and transactions in the same process (verified sequentially, not just under concurrency). The same code under the vite dev / node:http path does not leak. Concurrent requests still each saw their own tag, so this looks like an async-context restore problem around `withIsolationScope`/`withScope` on the Deno.serve path rather than a plain global-scope write. 2. In vite dev the very first request to a cold server produces no server span at all, because `main.ts` (and therefore `Sentry.init`) is only loaded by the SSR runner when that first request arrives, after the node:http span would have started. Every later request is fine. Also confirmed from the toolbox list, unchanged: K2 (Deno outgoing fetch gets neither a span nor propagation headers) and K3 (with the import hook active, `mysql2` dies on `require('*.json')` with `Unexpected token ':'`; `mysql@2` is the only driver that works). Everything ran against develop tarballs only; 10.73.0 was never installed. Processes started (sink 52413, dev 52520/52540, `deno serve` 52530) were all killed and the ports verified free. `sdkdeps/node_modules` and `app/node_modules` were removed afterwards (the dir is down from 122M to 2.3M); the reinstall commands above restore both.
