NestJS on Deno M-nestjs-deno

NestJS 10 (@nestjs/core + @nestjs/platform-express) with @sentry/nestjs 10.67.0 (develop / v11 line) · Deno 2.9.0 (aarch64-apple-darwin), npm compat, nodeModulesDir "manual" · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

NestJS itself boots on Deno unchanged. Sentry needs one undocumented workaround.

1. `npm install @nestjs/core@10 @nestjs/common@10 @nestjs/platform-express@10 reflect-metadata rxjs mysql2` plus the develop tarballs on ONE command line:
   `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-nestjs-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz`
   (@sentry/deno is NOT used and NOT needed; @sentry/nestjs -> @sentry/node runs on Deno as-is.)

2. `deno.json`:
   { "nodeModulesDir": "manual",
     "compilerOptions": { "experimentalDecorators": true, "emitDecoratorMetadata": true },
     "imports": { "@nestjs/core": "npm:@nestjs/core@10", "@nestjs/common": "npm:@nestjs/common@10", "@nestjs/platform-express": "npm:@nestjs/platform-express@10", "@sentry/nestjs": "npm:@sentry/nestjs@10.67.0", "@sentry/nestjs/setup": "npm:@sentry/nestjs@10.67.0/setup", "mysql2/promise": "npm:mysql2/promise", "reflect-metadata": "npm:reflect-metadata", "rxjs": "npm:rxjs" } }

3. `instrument.ts` — the workaround line is mandatory, without it the app cannot boot:
   (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>).__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__ = { runtimeUnavailable: true };
   import * as Sentry from "@sentry/nestjs";
   Sentry.init({ dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: "static" });
   The assignment must be evaluated before Sentry.init() (ESM hoisting is fine: the hook registration happens inside init(), not at module evaluation).

4. `main.ts`: `import "./instrument.ts";` as the first line, then `import "reflect-metadata";`, then Nest. Register BOTH pieces from @sentry/nestjs/setup:
   @Module({ imports: [SentryModule.forRoot()], controllers: [...], providers: [{ provide: APP_FILTER, useClass: SentryGlobalFilter }] })
   SentryModule.forRoot() alone registers only APP_INTERCEPTOR; without the explicit APP_FILTER every route-handler error is swallowed and no event is sent.

5. Run: `deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main.ts`

Why the workaround: Sentry.init() -> registerDiagnosticsChannelInjection() calls `Module.registerHooks({resolve,load})` because hasStableSyncModuleHooks() returns `true` unconditionally when globalThis.Deno is set (node_modules/@sentry/server-runtime-injection/build/esm/register.js:10-15 and :55-57). In Deno 2.9.0 ANY Module.registerHooks() call breaks `require('*.json')`. I isolated it with a no-op hook and no Sentry at all (probe try-hooks-noop.mts vs try-hooks-none.mts), so it is a Deno bug (same family as K3 / denoland/deno#36240), but the develop SDK walks straight into it on Deno.

errors✓ worksWith SentryGlobalFilter registered as APP_FILTER, a throw in a @Get handler arrives as an event with mechanism "auto.http.nestjs.global_filter", handled:false, sdk sentry.javascript.nestjs, transaction "GET /error", same traceId as the request transaction, and context_line frames present. Nest does swallow it if you only do SentryModule.forRoot(): my first run had the interceptor but no APP_FILTER and the sink got the internal_error transaction with no event at all. Both lifecycles.
route names✓* works-waA request to /users/42 produces transaction name "GET /users/42" with source "url" (static lifecycle) and span name "GET" with no source attribute (stream lifecycle). The parameterized route /users/:id never appears and source is never "route", because the express/nest route-name instrumentation is channel-based and the diagnostics-channel injection has to be switched off for the app to boot on Deno at all. There is no configuration that gives route names here. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. Parameterized route names DO work for NestJS 10 + @nestjs/platform-express with @sentry/nestjs 10.67.0 (develop) on Deno 2.9.0 — in BOTH lifecycles — as long as the diagnostics-channel injection stays ON. The original probe turned it off (`__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__ = { runtimeUnavailable: true }`) to get the app to boot; that is what removed route names, not an SDK limitation. Keeping injection on and neutralizing the Deno `require('*.json')` bug with a ~12-line `Module.registerHooks` shim in the instrument file gives the full express + nest span tree and `source: "route"`. EXACT CHANGE (only the instrument file changes; deno.json, main.ts, app module stay exactly as the original probe had them, and the `__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__` line is REMOVED): ```ts // instrument2.ts — this block must run before any framework import import * as Module from "node:module"; import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"; import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url"; Module.registerHooks({ load(url, context, nextLoad) { if (url.endsWith(".json")) { const src = readFileSync(fileURLToPath(url), "utf8"); return { format: "commonjs", source: `module.exports = ${src}`, shortCircuit: true }; } return nextLoad(url, context); }, }); import * as Sentry from "@sentry/nestjs"; Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: "static" }); ``` EVIDENCE (my sink, verbatim, trimmed). R1 baseline, the probe's own config (NO_INJECT=1, static) — reproduces the claim: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/42","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.nestjs","spans":[]} R2 with the JSON shim, injection ON, static: Sentry Logger [log]: Registered diagnostics-channel injection via Module.registerHooks() APP_LISTENING 41503 {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.nestjs","spans":["middleware query","middleware expressInit","middleware jsonParser","middleware urlencodedParser","handler /users/:id","function AppController.getUser","handler getUser"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"Create Nest App","op":"function","source":"custom",...} R3/R4 same shim, traceLifecycle "stream" (segment span attributes dumped by an extended sink): {"name":"GET /users/:id","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.http_server","source":"route","http_route":"/users/:id"} items: ["middleware urlencodedParser","middleware jsonParser","middleware expressInit","middleware query","handler Request handler","function AppController.getUser","handler /users/:id","http.server GET /users/:id"] R6 control, no workaround at all (default develop SDK on Deno 2.9.0) — app cannot boot, so the premise of the original report is correct: [Nest] ERROR [PackageLoader] No driver (HTTP) has been selected ... ensure to install the "@nestjs/platform-express" package R7 ordering control: the shim registered AFTER Sentry.init() works identically ("GET /users/:id", source "route"), so it only has to run before the framework imports, not before init(). Root cause, isolated without Sentry (try-hooks-noop.mjs vs try-hooks-jsonfix.mjs, run with plain deno): noop {resolve,load} passthrough hook -> STATUSES_FAIL Unexpected token ':' same + the .json branch -> STATUSES_OK function Not Found So Deno 2.9.0 compiles `require('*.json')` as JavaScript as soon as ANY `Module.registerHooks` load hook exists (denoland/deno#36240 family). The SDK's own sync hook is a pure passthrough for non-instrumented URLs (node_modules/@sentry/server-runtime-injection/build/esm/vendored/@apm-js-collab/tracing-hooks/hook.js:113 `loadSync`), so the SDK could carry this two-line `.json` branch itself and the workaround would disappear: on Deno, return `{format:'commonjs', source:'module.exports = '+text}` for `.json` URLs instead of the untouched `nextLoad` result. Where the route name comes from: packages/server-utils/src/integrations/express/instrumentation.ts:276 -> setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute(), which sets http.route, updateName(`${method} ${route}`) and sentry.segment.name.source='route'. It is reachable only through channel injection into `express`, which is why disabling injection loses the capability. The nestjs channel subscriber (packages/nestjs/src/integrations/orchestrion-subscriber.ts) only puts http.route on its own request-context span; it never renames the server span. Workaround: Do NOT set `__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__ = { runtimeUnavailable: true }` on Deno. Instead, at the top of the instrument file (before importing @nestjs/*), register a JSON load hook that hands `.json` files back as CommonJS: import * as Module from "node:module"; import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"; import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url"; Module.registerHooks({ load(url, context, nextLoad) { if (url.endsWith(".json")) { const src = readFileSync(fileURLToPath(url), "utf8"); return { format: "commonjs", source: `module.exports = ${src}`, shortCircuit: true }; } return nextLoad(url, context); }, }); then `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/nestjs"` and `Sentry.init(...)` as documented. The shim may sit before or after init(); it only has to run before the first framework import. With it, @nestjs/platform-express boots, injection stays on, and transactions/segment spans are named `GET /users/:id` with source `route` in both `traceLifecycle: "static"` and `"stream"`. The proper fix belongs in the SDK: `loadSync` in the vendored tracing-hooks should apply the same `.json` branch when `globalThis.Deno` is set.

No tag or trace bleed in either lifecycle.

Wiring matches the repo reference app exactly (~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/nestjs-basic/src/{instrument.ts,main.ts,app.module.ts}): instrument first import, SentryModule.forRoot() plus APP_FILTER SentryGlobalFilter. Sink = $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs on 41338, header recorder = recorder.mjs on 41339. 1) Baseline, traceLifecycle "static" (run-b-app-baseline-static.log): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /downstream","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.nestjs","spans":[]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /nodehttp","op":"http.server",...,"spans":["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41339/recorded-nodehttp"]} recorder: {"url":"/recorded-fetch","sentryTrace":null,"baggage":null,"traceparent":null} recorder: {"url":"/recorded-nodehttp","sentryTrace":"2749d481...-a9078a40d87f5795-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,..."} 2) Baseline, traceLifecycle "stream" (run-b-app-baseline-stream.log) — same gap, so the lifecycle is not the variable: {"type":"span","trace_id":"bcf456da...","items":["http.server GET"]} <- the fetch route {"type":"span","trace_id":"d0ae1ce5...","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","http.server GET"]} <- the node:http route 3) Explicitly adding the shipped integration, `nativeNodeFetchIntegration({ spans: true })` (run-b-app-nativefetch-static.log), changes nothing: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /downstream",...,"spans":[]} recorder: {"url":"/recorded-fetch","sentryTrace":null,"baggage":null,"traceparent":null} Root cause is structural, not wiring. packages/node/src/integrations/node-fetch/undici-instrumentation.ts instruments outgoing fetch purely by subscribing to the `undici:request:*` diagnostics channels; Deno's global fetch is its own Rust implementation and publishes nothing on those channels. Confirmation from the same app: the route that imports the npm `undici` package and calls its fetch DOES get a span and headers on Deno — {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /undicifetch",...,"spans":["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41339/recorded-undici"]} recorder: {"url":"/recorded-undici","sentryTrace":"082bb758...-aa0d7adaadbe3c62-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,..."} So the channel subscription itself works on Deno; only Deno's native fetch never reaches it. This is @sentry/node-level, not NestJS-level, and @sentry/deno has no fetch tracing either (packages/deno/src/integrations/ has only a breadcrumbs fetch handler, no instrumentFetchRequest), so switching SDKs does not help. Workaround: Three, all verified in this probe, none of them shipped behavior: 1) Best fix — a ~25-line userland integration built only from public @sentry/core exports, added to `integrations` in Sentry.init(). This is fetch-integration.ts in the probe dir: addFetchInstrumentationHandler(handlerData => { const client = getClient(); if (!client || isSentryRequestUrl(handlerData.fetchData.url, client)) return; instrumentFetchRequest(handlerData, () => true, url => shouldPropagateTraceForUrl(url, client.getOptions().tracePropagationTargets, headersUrlMap), spans, { spanOrigin: 'auto.http.fetch' }); }) Result with MODE=userland, static (run-b-app-userland-static.log): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /downstream",...,"spans":["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41339/recorded-fetch"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /downstream-request",...,"spans":["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41339/recorded-fetch-request"]} recorder: {"url":"/recorded-fetch","sentryTrace":"cfad0e3d...-9d8125a0dfe2c30f-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,..."} And with stream lifecycle (run-b-app-userland-stream.log): {"type":"span","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","http.server GET"],"raw":[{"name":"GET 127.0.0.1","origin":"auto.http.fetch",...}]} It handles both `fetch(url)` and `fetch(new Request(url))`, needs no Deno flags, and works under both trace lifecycles. 2) `import { request } from 'node:http'` instead of fetch — works untouched (span + sentry-trace + baggage), but changes call sites. 3) `globalThis.fetch = (await import('undici')).fetch` right after Sentry.init() — produces the span and headers for `fetch(url)` (run-b-app-undiciglobal-static.log), but breaks `fetch(new Request(url))` because Deno's global Request is not undici's: "TypeError: Failed to parse URL from [object Request] at new Request (node_modules/undici/lib/web/fetch/request.js:143:15)". Do not recommend it. The __SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__ = { runtimeUnavailable: true } line the original report describes is still mandatory just to boot the app; it is unrelated to the fetch gap (the gap is identical with and without diagnostics-channel injection).
db spans✓ worksA module-scope mysql2 pool queried inside GET /db produced db spans with NO instrumentation path needed: no Deno import hook, no bundler plugin, and in fact with the diagnostics-channel injection explicitly disabled. mysql2 3.24.3 ships its own node:diagnostics_channel publisher (node_modules/mysql2/lib/tracing.js) and @sentry/node's channel-subscribing mysql2 integration picks it up (debug log: "[instrumentation:mysql2] Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly"). Static lifecycle gives db mysql2.pool.connect / db mysql2.connect / db SELECT id, name FROM users; stream gives the low-cardinality db SELECT users. Caveat: with injection ENABLED mysql2 cannot even be imported (same JSON-require crash).

Flushed on the timer, visible after ~7s.
client errors· not-runNestJS on Deno is a server-only target in this cell; there is no browser bundle or client entry to instrument, so the browser-side capability does not apply.

Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions the combination. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nestjs/index.mdx:1-9` declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.nestjs`, `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, category `server-node`, and a grep for "deno" across `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nestjs/` returns nothing. From the other side, `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-40` is a manual-setup beta page for @sentry/deno that names no framework at all (grep for "framework|Express|Oak|Hono|Fresh" in it returns nothing), and a grep for "nest" across `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/` returns nothing. `platform-includes/getting-started-prerequisites/javascript.deno.mdx:7` only states "Deno version >= `2.0.0`". So the docs neither claim nor deny that NestJS runs on Deno, and nothing anywhere documents that @sentry/node's Module.registerHooks() registration breaks JSON requires on Deno or how to opt out of it.

Documented: no

A NestJS-on-Deno page must exist. It must say NestJS 10 (`@nestjs/core` + `@nestjs/platform-express`) boots on Deno unchanged and that `@sentry/nestjs` works there, with these specifics: install the Sentry packages in a single `npm install` command into a real `node_modules` and set `deno.json` `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}`; error capture, per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, database spans and logs all work. Two limitations must be stated plainly because neither has a workaround the reader can guess. (1) Route names are broken: transaction names are not parameterized on Deno, so `GET /users/123` is not collapsed to the route pattern — the page must say so rather than implying the Node behavior carries over. (2) Outgoing requests made with Deno's built-in global `fetch` are not traced by `@sentry/node` or any framework SDK built on it, including `@sentry/nestjs`: no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers, because that instrumentation listens on undici's diagnostics channels and Deno's native fetch publishes none of them. The page must ship the fix that was verified to cover both `fetch(url)` and `fetch(new Request(url))` on both trace lifecycles — a small integration built from public `@sentry/core` exports (`defineIntegration` + a headers/URL map + `instrumentFetchRequest`) passed to `Sentry.init` — and note `node:http` as the zero-integration alternative.

Page to write: guides/deno/frameworks/nestjs.mdx (new), with an explicit "Known limitations on Deno" section listing unparameterized route names and uninstrumented global fetch

docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nestjs/index.mdx:1-9 declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.nestjs`, `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, category `server-node`; `grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nestjs/` returns 0 hits; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-232 is a beta-flagged manual-setup page for `@sentry/deno` (beta Alert at :12-16) that names no framework at all

Headline: NestJS runs fine on Deno, and @sentry/nestjs (i.e. @sentry/node) initializes fine on Deno — but the develop SDK's default runtime injection makes the combination unbootable, and the fix is a one-line global that no docs page mentions and that is not a supported public option. 1. Root cause, worth a real fix. `hasStableSyncModuleHooks()` in `packages/server-runtime-injection/src/register.ts` (built copy: node_modules/@sentry/server-runtime-injection/build/esm/register.js:10-15) returns `true` for Deno unconditionally, so init() always calls `Module.registerHooks({resolve, load})`. Deno 2.9.0 then compiles every `require('*.json')` as JavaScript and throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'`. I proved this is Deno's bug with a no-op hook and zero Sentry code, but the SDK is the thing that triggers it, and the blast radius is large: express, statuses, fastify, mysql2, i.e. every Nest HTTP adapter. Two candidate fixes: gate the Deno branch behind a version check the way the Node branch is gated, or expose a documented opt-out (today the only lever is the undocumented `globalThis.__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__ = { runtimeUnavailable: true }` sentinel). 2. Second papercut. `SentryModule.forRoot()` registers only `APP_INTERCEPTOR` (setup.js:128,139); there is no `APP_FILTER`. My first run had forRoot() and nothing else and every route-handler throw was silently swallowed: 500 to the client, internal_error transaction, zero events. Adding `{ provide: APP_FILTER, useClass: SentryGlobalFilter }` fixed it immediately. Any Deno page would have to spell that out. 3. Pleasant surprise worth writing down: db spans need no instrumentation path at all on this stack. mysql2 3.24.3 publishes its own node:diagnostics_channel events (lib/tracing.js) and @sentry/node subscribes eagerly on Bun/Deno, so the query spans arrive with the injection hook explicitly disabled. Drivers without native channels would still be dark here, and there is no working escape hatch for them on Deno since the injection hook cannot be enabled. 4. `[Sentry] @sentry/server-runtime-injection was bundled into your application, so mysql2 ... load uninstrumented` fires on Deno in the default (injection-on) run even though nothing is bundled. Misleading message on this runtime. 5. Deprecation noise: Deno 2.9 prints `Warning experimentalDecorators compiler option is deprecated and may be removed at any time` on every run. NestJS 10 still needs it, so a docs page cannot avoid the warning. 6. traceLifecycle made no difference to any verdict. Static was easier to read (nested spans[] on the transaction); stream confirmed the same trace ids, parents, tags and db spans, with server spans named "GET" and the db span low-cardinality "SELECT users". 7. Not probed, out of scope for this cell: @sentry/deno was installed but never used — the Node SDK is what @sentry/nestjs pulls, and mixing in @sentry/deno would give a second client. Profiling, cron/@SentryCron, and GraphQL/microservice transports were not exercised. Cleanup done: app, sink and recorder processes killed (ports 52817/52818/52819 free), node_modules (150M) removed. Probe sources and logs kept.

cd $D && npm install --no-audit --no-fund $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-nestjs-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-deno-10.67.0.tgz

# sink + header recorder (pick fresh ports if 52817/52818/52819 are taken)
PORT=52817 node $D/sink.mjs > $D/sink3.log 2>&1 &      # extended sink: keeps tags, trace ids, parent span ids
node $D/recorder.mjs > $D/recorder.log 2>&1 &          # records sentry-trace / baggage on 52818

# 1. does bare NestJS boot on Deno without Sentry?  (yes)
cd $D && deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --allow-run --allow-ffi $D/app.ts

# 2. does @sentry/nestjs even init on Deno?  (yes)
cd $D && deno run --no-prompt -A $D/try-nestjs-sdk.ts

# 3. the blocker, and that it is Deno's not Sentry's
cd $D && deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys $D/try-express.ts               # injection ON  -> fails
cd $D && NO_INJECT=1 deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys $D/try-express.ts   # injection OFF -> ok
cd $D && deno run --no-prompt -A $D/try-hooks-noop.mts    # no-op Module.registerHooks, no Sentry -> STATUSES_FAIL
cd $D && deno run --no-prompt -A $D/try-hooks-none.mts    # no hooks                              -> STATUSES_OK
cd $D && deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys $D/try-fastify.ts               # fastify adapter also fails

# 4. the app + all probes
cd $D && NO_INJECT=1 LIFECYCLE=static APP_PORT=52819 deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys $D/main.ts &
cd $D && node $D/drive.mjs          # routes, error, downstream, db, log, incoming trace, 3x concurrent isolation, sentinel, then dumps recorder + sink
cd $D && NO_INJECT=1 LIFECYCLE=stream APP_PORT=52819 deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys $D/main.ts &
cd $D && node $D/drive.mjs

Next.js on Deno M-nextjs-deno

Next.js 15.5.4 (App Router, route handlers) · Deno 2.9.0 (aarch64-apple-darwin), `deno run -A node_modules/next/dist/bin/next build|start` · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Next.js 15 builds and serves on Deno 2.9 with no Sentry at all: `npm install next@15.5.4 react react-dom`, `deno.json` with `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}`, then `deno run -A node_modules/next/dist/bin/next build` and `... next start -p <port>`. Both worked first try.

Sentry wiring that actually works (three deviations from what a docs page would show today):

1. `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{nextjs,node,core,opentelemetry,react,browser,browser-utils,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,vercel-edge,bundler-plugins,replay,replay-canvas,feedback}-10.67.0.tgz` (npm resolves the transitive `@sentry/*@10.67.0` pins only if every tarball is on one command line).

2. `next.config.mjs` — `withSentryConfig` is NOT on the `@sentry/nextjs` main entry on develop, it is at `@sentry/nextjs/config`, and that subpath is CJS-only (`"./config": { "default": "./build/cjs/config/index.js" }`). Deno's CJS named-export detection does not see it, so the ESM named import fails. Must use default interop:
```js
import sentryConfigModule from '@sentry/nextjs/config';
const { withSentryConfig } = sentryConfigModule;
export default withSentryConfig({}, { silent: true, sourcemaps: { disable: true }, telemetry: false });
```
A CJS `next.config.js` with `require(...)` is not an option: Deno loads the root config as ESM and throws `ReferenceError: require is not defined`.

3. `instrumentation.js` at project root, standard shape (`register()` importing `./sentry.server.config.js` when `process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'nodejs'`, plus `onRequestError = Sentry.captureRequestError`).

4. **`sentry.server.config.js` MUST pass `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false`.** Without it every single request 500s (see evidence). This is the whole story of this cell:
```js
import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nextjs';
Sentry.init({
  dsn: '...', tunnel: 'http://127.0.0.1:41208/',
  tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static',
  enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false, // required on Deno
});
```
`Sentry.init()` in `@sentry/node` calls `registerDiagnosticsChannelInjection()` unconditionally (packages/node/src/sdk/index.ts:170), which on Deno takes the `Module.registerHooks({resolve, load})` branch (packages/server-runtime-injection/src/register.ts:123, guarded by `hasStableSyncModuleHooks(isDeno) === true`). With those hooks installed, Deno's `require()` of a `.json` file goes through `compileFunction` and throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` (denoland/deno#36240, the same K3 bug the `@sentry/deno` import hook hits). Next.js `require()`s its build manifests as JSON on every request, so every route handler dies before it runs. `buildTimeInstrumentation: false` in `withSentryConfig` does NOT help — the crash comes from `init()`, not from the injected bundle banner.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ works`throw new Error('boom-route-handler')` in an App-Router route handler reaches Sentry as an unhandled event with mechanism `auto.function.nextjs.route_handler`, `handled: false`, sdk `sentry.javascript.nextjs`, correctly linked to the `GET /api/error` transaction (same trace_id, parent_span_id set). The framework does not swallow it; the transaction is marked `internal_error`. Two caveats: `hasContextLine` is false (no source context on the frames), and `contexts.runtime` reports `{name: "node", version: "v26.3.0"}` — the Node SDK's Context integration reads `process.versions.node`, so a Deno-hosted Next.js app is indistinguishable from Node in Sentry. traceLifecycle: 'static'.

isolation✓ worksThree concurrent `GET /api/iso?tag={alpha,bravo,charlie}` (each `Sentry.setTag` then a randomized 150-350ms await then `captureException`) produced three events and three transactions, each carrying only its own `probe_tag` and its own trace id, with the event's trace id matching its own transaction's. No cross-talk. traceLifecycle: 'static'.
incoming trace✓ works`curl -H 'sentry-trace: aaaa…aaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1' -H 'baggage: sentry-trace_id=aaaa…,sentry-environment=probe,…'` produced a transaction with `trace_id: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` and `parent_span_id: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`. Continuation happens in the `node:http` server instrumentation, which works on Deno. traceLifecycle: 'static'.
outgoing fetch✓* works-waA `fetch()` from inside a route handler to a local recorder produced NO `http.client` span (the `GET /api/fetch` transaction contains only the three Next.js spans) and the recorder saw `sentry-trace: null, baggage: null`. Identical under traceLifecycle 'static' and 'stream'. This is the known Deno K2 gap (Deno's global `fetch` is not `node:http`-backed and the SDK's NodeFetch/undici instrumentation never sees it), and it is not fixed by Next.js' own fetch patching. Distributed tracing out of a Next.js-on-Deno server is therefore dead. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. The gap is real with the default integration set, but it is closed by one SDK-provided integration that already ships inside `@sentry/nextjs`'s own dependency tree: `winterCGFetchIntegration()` from `@sentry/vercel-edge`. It patches `globalThis.fetch` through `@sentry/core`'s `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest`, so it does not care that Deno's `fetch` is not `node:http`/undici-backed. It produces a correctly parented `http.client` span AND `sentry-trace` + `baggage` on the wire, under both trace lifecycles. Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-nextjs-deno-outgoingfetch (node_modules removed after the run; `npm install` restores it from package.json, which pins the $REPRO/_toolbox/pack 10.67.0 tarballs). Next.js 15.5.4, deno 2.9.0, `deno run -A node_modules/next/dist/bin/next build|start`, sink on 47311, recorder on 53471. Scenario runner: `./run.sh <tag> <FETCH_INT> <lifecycle> <port>` (Deno) and `./run-node.sh ...` (Node control). A ~25-line integration built only from `@sentry/core` public exports (`addFetchInstrumentationHandler`, `instrumentFetchRequest`, `shouldPropagateTraceForUrl`, `isSentryRequestUrl`, `LRUMap`, `defineIntegration`) — sentry-fetch-integration.js in the probe dir — gives the identical result (`./run.sh core core static 47321`): "spans":["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /api/fetch/route","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:53471/rec","start response"], trace_id e75ebde025c94c14a3b38782eb93e0cd, and rec-core.json "sentry-trace":"e75ebde025c94c14a3b38782eb93e0cd-81199147a6dea550-1". 5) IMPORTANT CAVEAT — the integration must be gated on Deno. The very same config run on Node (`./run-node.sh nodewcg wcg static 47322`) double-instruments, because `nativeNodeFetchIntegration`/undici is also live there: sink-nodewcg.json: "spans":["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /api/fetch/route","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:53471/rec","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:53471/rec","start response"] Gating on `typeof globalThis.Deno !== 'undefined'` (rebuilt into .next-v4auto) yields exactly one `http.client` span on BOTH runtimes: sink-auto-deno.json: "spans":[..., "http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:53471/rec","start response"] (trace_id 48ff81ae321741e4a414cc1c2a603d57) sink-auto-node.json: "spans":[..., "http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:53471/rec","start response"] (trace_id 3f764716e83349d395d7cd712e17e09c) Two secondary facts worth recording: - `winterCGFetchIntegration` is NOT re-exported from `@sentry/nextjs`. `node -e "require('@sentry/nextjs').winterCGFetchIntegration"` -> `undefined`. It must be imported from `@sentry/vercel-edge`, which is a direct dependency of `@sentry/nextjs` (checked node_modules/@sentry/nextjs/package.json), so npm/yarn hoisting resolves it without adding a dependency; pnpm's strict node_modules would need an explicit `@sentry/vercel-edge` entry. - Everything else the original report established still holds: `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false` is still mandatory, `withSentryConfig` still needs the default-interop import from `@sentry/nextjs/config`, and the baseline (no integration) still shows the exact failure that was reported. This verdict changes only the "distributed tracing is dead" conclusion.
Workaround: In `sentry.server.config.js`, add the WinterCG fetch integration, gated so it only loads on Deno (on Node it would duplicate every `http.client` span with undici's): ```js import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nextjs'; import { winterCGFetchIntegration } from '@sentry/vercel-edge'; const isDeno = typeof globalThis.Deno !== 'undefined'; Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false, // also required on Deno integrations: isDeno ? [winterCGFetchIntegration()] : [], }); ``` `@sentry/vercel-edge` is already a dependency of `@sentry/nextjs`, so nothing new needs installing under npm/yarn; add it explicitly to package.json under pnpm. If you would rather not import from the edge package, the same result comes from a small integration over `@sentry/core`'s `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest` (see sentry-fetch-integration.js in the probe dir) — both were verified to emit one `http.client` span with `sentry-trace`/`baggage` on Deno.
db spans✓* works-wa`mysql2` (module-scope `createPool`) DOES produce `db mysql2.pool.connect`, `db mysql2.connect`, `db SELECT id, name FROM users` — but only because mysql2 v3.24 ships its own native `diagnostics_channel` tracing channels (node_modules/mysql2/lib/tracing.js:19-31), which the Sentry channel integrations subscribe to eagerly on Bun/Deno. `mysql@2` (module-scope `createConnection`), which has no native channels and depends on injection, produced NO span at all in the same build. So: no instrumentation path is available. The runtime path (`Module.registerHooks`) is exactly what has to be disabled to make the app boot; there is no Deno import hook for the Node SDK (`@sentry/deno/import` is a different SDK); and `withSentryConfig`'s `buildTimeInstrumentation` (default true) only injects `require("@sentry/nextjs/orchestrion-runtime/register")` into the server chunks — it does not transform externalized `node_modules` deps, and that register call is itself the crashing one. Debug output confirms: `[Sentry] No diagnostics-channel injection detected. Channel-based integrations will not record spans.` traceLifecycle: 'static' and 'stream' both. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. `mysql@2` (module-scope `createConnection`, no native tracing channels, left external/unbundled) DOES produce a db span on Next.js 15.5.4 + Deno 2.9.0 with the develop SDK, with Sentry's runtime diagnostics-channel injection ENABLED. The claim's premise ("the runtime path is exactly what has to be disabled to make the app boot; there is no instrumentation path") is wrong on two counts. 1) The Deno `Module.registerHooks` JSON crash is avoidable, and not by Sentry's doing. Minimal repro, no Sentry, no Next (`$REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-nextjs-deno-dbspans/minhook2/main.cjs`, `MODE=<mode> deno run -A main.cjs`): passthrough -> json FAILED: SyntaxError Unexpected token ':' resolve-only -> json ok: {"a":1} load-only -> json FAILED: SyntaxError Unexpected token ':' json-format -> json ok: {"a":1} (load hook only sets result.format = 'json' for *.json) json-short -> json ok: {"a":1} json-wrap -> json ok: {"a":1} So it is the `load` hook alone that triggers it: Deno hands `.json` back through the hook chain with a format it then compiles as JavaScript. Re-tagging the result as `format: 'json'` fixes it. `chain3.cjs` shows the fix survives chaining: a json-tagging hook registered BEFORE Sentry's hooks (so it sits innermost) still wins, because Deno runs the last-registered hook first. Note the tag must be unconditional; when hooks are chained `result.format` arrives as `undefined`, so a `format === 'commonjs'` guard silently does nothing (`chain.cjs` -> still FAILS). 2) With that 8-line hook in `register()` of `instrumentation.js`, before `import('./sentry.server.config.js')`, and `enableRuntimeChannelInjection` left at its default (true), the app boots, every route returns 200, and injected drivers are instrumented. Sink (`traceLifecycle: 'static'`, run F, `rb-server-F-jsonhook.log`): TX GET /api/dbredis | ["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /api/dbredis/route","db.query set probe:key [1 other arguments]","db.query get probe:key","start response"] TX GET /api/dbmysql2 | ["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /api/dbmysql2/route","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT id, name FROM users","start response"] TX GET /api/dbmysql | ["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /api/dbmysql/route","db SELECT id, name FROM users","start response"] server log: Sentry Logger [log]: Registered diagnostics-channel injection via Module.registerHooks() [Tracing] Starting sampled span / op: db / name: SELECT id, name FROM users / root description: GET /api/dbmysql Sentry Logger [log]: [Tracing] Finishing "db" span "SELECT id, name FROM users" with ID a6397c626ac78ea1 `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` works too (run G, port 41348): span ["resolve page components","db SELECT users"] span ["executing api route (app) /api/dbmysql/route","start response","http.server GET /api/dbmysql"] Control (run C, injection on, no hook) reproduces the reported failure exactly: `/api/dbmysql -> Internal Server Error`, log line 128 ` ⨯ SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'`. 3) Second, independent refutation of "no instrumentation path is available": even with `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false`, BUILD-TIME instrumentation already works on Deno. `ioredis` (the one entry in `BUNDLE_SAFE_INSTRUMENTED_PACKAGES`, so `withSentryConfig` un-externalizes it and the orchestrion webpack loader transforms it) yields real spans with the runtime hook off (run A): TX GET /api/dbredis | [...,"db.query set probe:key [1 other arguments]","db.query get probe:key",...] So the docs' "channel-based integrations will not record spans" conclusion is too strong: what is missing on Deno is only the *runtime* path, and only for the packages Sentry keeps external. 4) Things that do NOT work, for completeness. Force-bundling `mysql` (wrapping Next's webpack `externals` functions to let the loader transform it, `BUNDLE_MYSQL=1`, `.next-bundlemysql`) does produce `Finishing "db" span "SELECT id, name FROM users"` but corrupts the driver — `Error: Received packet in the wrong sequence.` / `Cannot enqueue l after fatal error.` — and it does so on plain `node next start` too (`server-node-bundlemysql.log`), so that is a bundling defect, not a Deno one, and matches the comment on `BUNDLE_SAFE_INSTRUMENTED_PACKAGES`. Also, with the hook on, `mysql2` still logs `[instrumentation] failed to inject diagnostics-channel into mysql2: [TypeError: transform is not a function]` (the vendored transformer is stripped for that module because `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` ends up bundled into the Next server chunk); mysql2 is unaffected only because it ships native channels. `mysql@2` transformed fine, so the runtime path is genuinely functional, not accidentally so. SDK fix this points at: `packages/server-runtime-injection/src/register.ts` should wrap the vendored `loadSync` (`build/cjs/vendored/@apm-js-collab/tracing-hooks/hook.js`, which returns the untransformed result verbatim) and set `format: 'json'` for `.json` URLs when running on Deno. That one line would make the documented Next.js wiring work on Deno unmodified, with no `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false` and no user shim. Files: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-nextjs-deno-dbspans/{instrumentation.js,next.config.mjs,sentry.server.config.js,lib.js,app/api/*,minhook2/*,rb-server-*.log,RERUN2.txt}. Commands in RERUN2.txt. Ports 41341-41348. All processes killed, redis container stopped, node_modules removed.
Workaround: In `instrumentation.js`, register a JSON-tagging load hook before importing the Sentry server config, and leave `enableRuntimeChannelInjection` at its default: export async function register() { if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'nodejs') { process.getBuiltinModule('node:module').registerHooks({ load(url, context, nextLoad) { const result = nextLoad(url, context); if (url.endsWith('.json') && result) result.format = 'json'; return result; }, }); await import('./sentry.server.config.js'); } } Notes: the tag must be unconditional (when hooks are chained Deno reports `format: undefined`, so a `=== 'commonjs'` guard is a no-op); use `process.getBuiltinModule('node:module')`, since patching or reading `node:module` through the ESM namespace inside a webpack-bundled `instrumentation.js` does not reach the object `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` calls; and register it before `Sentry.init()` runs so it sits innermost in Deno's hook chain. Everything else stays as in the reported wiring (`@sentry/nextjs/config` default-interop import in `next.config.mjs`, `deno.json` with `nodeModulesDir: "manual"`).

client errors· not-runOnly the server runtime was probed. The browser bundle is produced by Next.js/webpack and served to a normal browser, so it is unaffected by the Deno host; nothing Deno-specific to test, and no browser driver was wired up in this cell.

Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions this combination. `grep -rniE "deno" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/` returns 0 hits across all 8 subtrees (index.mdx, manual-setup.mdx, configuration/, tracing/, logs/, profiling/, capturing-errors/, best-practices/). The reverse grep, `grep -rniE "next\.?js" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/`, also returns 0 hits — the Deno guide (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:12, still flagged "This SDK is currently in **beta**") only covers `@sentry/deno` with `Deno.serve`, never a Node-SDK-based framework hosted on Deno. `enableRuntimeChannelInjection` — the one option that makes this cell work — appears nowhere in the docs repo either. Separately, the docs still teach the pre-develop import path for the Next.js config wrapper: platform-includes/sourcemaps/overview/javascript.nextjs.mdx:44 shows `import { withSentryConfig } from "@sentry/nextjs";`, which is `undefined` on develop on Node as well as Deno (it lives at `@sentry/nextjs/config`; the repo's own e2e apps already use `require('@sentry/nextjs/config')`, e.g. dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/nextjs-15/next.config.js:1).

Documented: no

A Next.js-on-Deno page must exist. It must state that Next.js 15 App Router builds and serves on Deno 2.9 with `deno run -A node_modules/next/dist/bin/next build` and `... next start`, with `deno.json` `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}`, and then give the two deviations from the standard Next.js wiring, both of which are currently undocumented. (1) `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false` must be set in `Sentry.init()` in `sentry.server.config.js` or every request 500s with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` — Deno cannot run the diagnostics-channel module hook because `require()` of a `.json` file throws (denoland/deno#36240). The page must document this option, which does not appear anywhere in the docs today. With it set, database and library spans are recorded for drivers that carry their own `diagnostics_channel` support (mysql2 >= 3.11, ioredis >= 5.11, and ioredis < 5.11 via its bundled channel), while drivers that rely on the runtime module hook get no spans — the page must name that boundary rather than promising blanket db instrumentation. (2) Outgoing global `fetch()` produces no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers, because the Node SDK's HTTP client instrumentation only sees `node:http`/undici; the verified fix needs no extra install — add `integrations: [winterCGFetchIntegration()]` from `@sentry/vercel-edge` (already a dependency of `@sentry/nextjs`) to `Sentry.init()` in `sentry.server.config.js`, which restores both the span and the propagation headers. Errors, route names, isolation, incoming trace continuation and logs all work with no further caveat.

Page to write: guides/deno/frameworks/nextjs.mdx (new); additionally document `enableRuntimeChannelInjection` in docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/options.mdx (near the `traceLifecycle` SdkOption at :729) since it exists nowhere in the docs

`grep -rniE "deno" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/` returns 0 hits across all subtrees (index.mdx, manual-setup.mdx, configuration/, tracing/, logs/, profiling/, capturing-errors/, best-practices/), and the reverse `grep -rniE "next\.?js" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/` also returns 0; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/index.mdx:4-9 declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.nextjs` with category `server-node`; `grep -rn "enableRuntimeChannelInjection" docs/` returns nothing repo-wide, so the option every Next.js-on-Deno app needs is undocumented

Headline: Next.js on Deno is viable and the Sentry SDK is fully functional there, but the SDK as shipped bricks the app. A user following the Next.js docs verbatim on Deno gets a 100%-500 server with no indication that Sentry is the cause — the only clue is `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':' at Object.compileFunction (ext:core/01_core.js)`, which names neither Sentry nor JSON. The fix is one undocumented option, `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false`. Two candidate SDK changes: (a) skip the `Module.registerHooks` branch on Deno, or feature-test it by attempting a JSON require before committing to it, since the resulting instrumentation is nearly worthless on Deno anyway; (b) at minimum, document the option in the Deno and Next.js guides. `hasStableSyncModuleHooks()` (packages/server-runtime-injection/src/register.ts:20-23) currently returns `true` for Deno unconditionally with the comment "The minimum supported Deno (2.8.3) always has stable sync module hooks" — the hooks are stable, but registering them is destructive on Deno. Second finding, independent of Deno: `[instrumentation] failed to inject diagnostics-channel into mysql2: [TypeError: transform is not a function]` plus the always-on `@sentry/server-runtime-injection was bundled into your application` warning fire in a stock Next.js build. Next.js/webpack inlines `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` into `.next/server/`, tree-shaking the vendored meriyah transformer. This is the failure the warning was written for, and it happens on the default Next.js path — worth checking on plain Node too, it is probably not Deno-specific. Third: `contexts.runtime` says `{name: "node", version: "v26.3.0"}` for a Deno-hosted app, because the Node SDK's Context integration reads `process.versions.node`. There is no way to tell from a Sentry event that the app ran on Deno. If Deno hosting is to be supported at all, this needs a `globalThis.Deno` check. Fourth: `hasContextLine: false` on every exception event — the ContextLines integration reads no source lines under Deno + Next.js dist output. Environment gotcha that cost me two probe rounds and is worth passing to other agents: ports 41213 and 47311 were already held by other agents' `sink.mjs` instances, which answer `{}` to every request. That looks exactly like a broken Next.js build (all routes returning `{}`, no Sentry envelopes) rather than a port collision. Always `lsof -nP -iTCP:$P -sTCP:LISTEN` before binding. Cleanup: all six background processes killed (`server-opt`, `sink2`, `recorder`, and earlier servers); `node_modules` removed (418M reclaimed). `.next/` (173M) is left in place because the toolbox permits `rm` only on `node_modules`.

Nuxt on Deno M-nuxt-deno

Nuxt 4.5.2 (nitro 2.13.4 / h3 1.15.11) with @sentry/nuxt 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) · deno 2.9.0, nitro preset `deno_server`, output run with `deno run ... .output/server/index.mjs` · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Preset that worked: `deno_server` (set in nuxt.config.ts as `nitro: { preset: 'deno_server' }`; NITRO_PRESET env also works). `deno_deploy` was not needed.

Packages (npm, not bun/deno add):
  npm install nuxt@^4 vue mysql2
  npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{nuxt,node,core,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry,browser,vue,browser-utils,bundler-plugins,replay,replay-canvas,feedback}-10.67.0.tgz

nuxt.config.ts:
  export default defineNuxtConfig({
    compatibilityDate: '2025-01-01',
    modules: ['@sentry/nuxt/module'],
    sentry: { autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import', sourceMapsUploadOptions: { enabled: false } },
    nitro: { preset: 'deno_server' },
  });

sentry.server.config.ts at project root:
  import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nuxt';
  Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tunnel: 'http://127.0.0.1:30411/', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static', debug: true });

Build: `npx nuxt build` (do NOT pass --buildDir: it silently relocates the output to <buildDir>/.output and switches the preview command back to node, which also disables the Sentry server-config emission).

REQUIRED MANUAL STEP (SDK bug, see notes): after the build, prepend `import './sentry.server.config.mjs';` to `.output/server/index.mjs` yourself. With the deno_server preset the module writes that import into a bogus file literally named `.output/server/deno.json start` instead of the entry.

Run: cd .output && PORT=30415 deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env --allow-sys --allow-ffi --unstable-byonm ./server/index.mjs

The `--import ./.output/server/sentry.server.config.mjs` flow the Nuxt docs recommend has no Deno equivalent (`deno run` has no `--import`), so `autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import'` is the only viable install method here, and it carries the documented "only native Node APIs are instrumented" restriction.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksAn error thrown in a nitro route handler is captured and is not swallowed: `/api/error` returns HTTP 500 and an `event` envelope arrives with exception `nuxt-deno-boom`, mechanism `chained`, sdk `sentry.javascript.nuxt`, and a source context line. Mechanism is the Nuxt module's h3 layer (nitro `error` hook / captureErrorHook plus the `patchEventHandler` proxy on `nitroApp.h3App.handler`), not the Node http instrumentation. Lifecycle: static (same under stream). Side note: `contexts.runtime` is reported as `{name: node, version: v26.3.0}` (Deno's node-compat version), so events are indistinguishable from real Node.
route names✓* works-waNo `transaction` and no `span` envelope is ever emitted for an incoming request, at either lifecycle. `getActiveSpan()` inside a handler is undefined (`/api/trace` returns `{"name":null}`), because nitro's deno_server preset serves through `Deno.serve` and the Node SDK only instruments `node:http`. The only route information that survives is the scope transaction name on the error event, and it is the raw URL: an error in `/api/users/[id].get.ts` produces `"transaction":"GET /api/users/boom"`, never `/api/users/:id`. `@sentry/nuxt`'s `updateRouteBeforeResponse` hook bails out at `getActiveSpan()`, so the parameterized name and the `url.path.parameter.*` attributes are never applied. Source cannot be reported since there is no transaction envelope. verified: works-after-all The failure is caused by one line in the previous probe's `nuxt.config.ts` (`nitro: { preset: 'deno_server' }`), not by Deno. Drop that line and the *default* `node-server` Nitro output, run under `deno run`, produces full server transactions with parameterized route names, at parity with the same output run under Node. WORKS (deno 2.9.0, nuxt 4.5.2 / nitro 2.13.4, @sentry/nuxt 10.67.0 develop, `autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import'`): nuxt.config.ts -> `nitro: { preset: 'node-server' }` (i.e. just omit the preset), `npx nuxt build`, `cd .output/server && PORT=34415 deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env --allow-sys --allow-ffi --unstable-byonm ./index.mjs` The module also prepends `import './sentry.server.config.mjs';` to `.output/server/index.mjs` correctly here, so no manual patching is needed. Sink, `traceLifecycle: 'static'` (verbatim, trimmed): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","trace_id":"35e5078...","sdk":"sentry.javascript.nuxt","spans":[]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/trace","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok"} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/sentinel","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok"} `curl /api/trace` -> {"name":null,"op":null,"hasActive":true} # getActiveSpan() IS defined inside the handler Sink, default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` (same build, `SENTRY_LIFECYCLE=stream`): {"type":"span","trace_id":"f8e0455d...","items":["http.server GET /api/users/:id"],"raw":[{"name":"GET /api/users/:id","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.http_server"}]} Control, identical `.output` run under `node ./index.mjs` (port 34418): transaction 'GET /api/users/:id' source route, 'GET /api/trace' url, 'GET /api/users/boom' url -> byte-for-byte the same shape as Deno. Deno adds no gap. BROKEN CONTRAST, reproduced: rebuilt the same app with `NITRO_PRESET=deno_server` into `.output-deno2`. `curl /api/trace` -> {"name":null,"op":null,"hasActive":false}; zero `transaction` and zero `span` envelopes for 4 requests; only `event` items, both carrying `"transaction":"GET /api/users/boom"`. So the previous probe's observation is right for that preset (Nitro serves through `Deno.serve`, which @sentry/node does not instrument), but it is a preset choice, not a Deno limitation. Two real defects seen along the way, both narrower than the reported one: 1. `addSentryTopImport` writes the import into a file literally named `.output-deno2/server/deno.json start` (46 bytes: the import line plus the string "undefined"). Cause is `getFilenameFromNodeStartCommand` parsing Nitro's deno preset preview command `deno task --config .output-deno2/deno.json start` (packages/nuxt/src/vite/addServerConfig.ts:92-104); it takes the token after `--config` and the trailing `start` word. Only affects the `deno_server`/`deno_deploy` presets. 2. Route-name enrichment does not run on error responses, on Deno AND on Node alike: `/api/users/boom` yields `"name":"GET /api/users/boom","source":"url"`. Nitro v2 goes through `update-route-name-legacy.server.ts` (`beforeResponse` hook), which is not invoked for a thrown handler. Not runtime-specific, so it belongs to a separate finding.
Workaround: Do not set `nitro: { preset: 'deno_server' }`. Build the default `node-server` output (`npx nuxt build`) and run it with Deno: `cd .output/server && deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env --allow-sys --allow-ffi --unstable-byonm ./index.mjs`. Nitro's node-server entry uses `node:http`, which Deno's Node compat layer serves and which @sentry/node instruments, so `http.server` spans, `getActiveSpan()` inside handlers, and the `updateRouteBeforeResponse` hook (parameterized `GET /api/users/:id`, `source: "route"`, `url.path.parameter.*`) all work. Both `traceLifecycle: 'static'` and the default `'stream'` produce the parameterized name. If the `deno_server` preset is required for other reasons, there is no workaround for route names, and the sentry import must additionally be prepended to `.output/server/index.mjs` by hand.
isolation◐ partialThree concurrent `/api/tag?tag=alpha|beta|gamma` requests each set a distinct tag and captured a distinct error. All three events carried `"tags":{"probe_tag":"gamma"}` and all three carried the same trace id `8991806e4d9246c2bde0ae1409ebc746`, which was also the trace id of unrelated requests minutes earlier and of the later sentinel. Root cause is visible in the debug log: `patchEventHandler` only clones when the current isolation scope is the default one, so request 1 logs `Created new isolation scope` and every later request logs `Using existing isolation scope` and shares it. A leaked `transaction` field confirms it (a sentinel captured after an unrelated request carried `"transaction":"GET /api/error"`). Lifecycle: static. verified: partial Reproduced the report exactly, then found that the Nitro preset (not the SDK's `patchEventHandler` condition) is the deciding factor. Probe: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-nuxt-deno-isolation/ (RERUN.sh, app/, out-deno-server/, app-*.log, build-*.log). Same stack as reported: nuxt 4.5.2, nitropack 2.13.4, h3 1.15.11, @sentry/nuxt 10.67.0 from $REPRO/_toolbox/pack, deno 2.9.0, `autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import'`, `traceLifecycle: 'static'`, tunnel to a local sink on 41377. A) `nitro: { preset: 'deno_server' }` — CONFIRMED BROKEN, identical to the report. Build writes the entry import into the bogus file `.output/server/deno.json start`, so I prepended `import './sentry.server.config.mjs';` by hand; `cd .output && PORT=41380 deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env --allow-sys --allow-ffi --unstable-byonm ./server/index.patched.mjs`. Three concurrent `/api/tag?tag=alpha|beta|gamma` plus a later `/api/sentinel`: {"type":"event","exc":"Error: boom-alpha","tags":{"probe_tag":"gamma"},"user":{"id":"user-gamma"},"trace":"8d949dca0f264adf8738a350bcca5974"} {"type":"event","exc":"Error: boom-gamma","tags":{"probe_tag":"gamma"},"user":{"id":"user-gamma"},"trace":"8d949dca0f264adf8738a350bcca5974"} {"type":"event","exc":"Error: boom-beta","tags":{"probe_tag":"gamma"},"user":{"id":"user-gamma"},"trace":"8d949dca0f264adf8738a350bcca5974"} {"type":"event","msg":"sentinel","tags":{"probe_tag":"gamma"},"user":{"id":"user-gamma"},"trace":"8d949dca0f264adf8738a350bcca5974"} The handler responses show the same: `{"tag":"alpha","isolationTag":"gamma"}{"tag":"gamma","isolationTag":"gamma"}{"tag":"beta","isolationTag":"gamma"}`. Debug log: 1x "Patched h3 event handler. Created new isolation scope." then 4x "Using existing isolation scope." `getActiveSpan()` is undefined and no transaction/span envelope is ever sent, i.e. Deno.serve is not instrumented at all, so `patchEventHandler` is the only isolation mechanism and it refuses to fork a non-default scope. B) Same app, `NITRO_PRESET=node_server`, still run by `deno run ... ./server/index.mjs` — isolation between concurrent requests WORKS. The entry also gets `import './sentry.server.config.mjs';` injected automatically (no manual patch), `/api/trace` reports `{"hasActiveSpan":true}` with a `GET /api/trace` `http.server` span, and route-named transactions arrive: {"exc":"Error: boom-beta","tags":{"probe_tag":"beta"},"user":"user-beta","trace":"3cbcb1398eb64e7e8afd72451deb420e"} {"exc":"Error: boom-gamma","tags":{"probe_tag":"gamma"},"user":"user-gamma","trace":"c5b4c3d89e594b6d91986c4c6a8fe5da"} {"exc":"Error: boom-alpha","tags":{"probe_tag":"alpha"},"user":"user-alpha","trace":"55c8490f486742dc97402b9755b5543e"} Distinct tags, users and trace ids per concurrent request — the reported failure is gone. A residual leak remains, though: from a clean process, sentinel A is clean, one `/api/tag?tag=solo` runs, and every later request then inherits solo's scope data: A {"exc":"undefined: sentinel","msg":"sentinel","trace":"fd4872ac526c4491bbf76022f5e36815"} <- clean B {"exc":"Error: boom-solo","tags":{"probe_tag":"solo"},"user":"user-solo",...} C {"exc":"undefined: sentinel","msg":"sentinel","tags":{"probe_tag":"solo"},"user":"user-solo",...} E {"exc":"undefined: sentinel","msg":"sentinel","tags":{"probe_tag":"solo"},"user":"user-solo",...} <- still solo after the alpha/beta/gamma batch curl /api/trace -> {"hasActiveSpan":true,"isolationTags":{"probe_tag":"solo"}} So the first request's isolation scope becomes the process-wide baseline that every later fork clones; concurrent requests are isolated from each other but not from that baseline. C) Control: the identical `node_server` build run by `node ./server/index.mjs` is completely clean — three distinct tags/traces and sentinels with no tags at all ({"exc":"undefined: sentinel","msg":"sentinel","trace":"9feac759..."}). So the residual leak in (B) is Deno-specific, not a Nuxt-on-Node bug. Root cause notes: plain `AsyncLocalStorage` on deno 2.9.0 does not leak (probe alstest2/als2.mjs: `outerAtEntry` is null for every request, concurrent and sequential, under both `Deno.serve` and `node:http`), so the leak is in how the ambient OTel context/scope is established per request, not in Deno's ALS. `patchEventHandler`'s `isolationScope === getDefaultIsolationScope() ? clone() : reuse` is what turns that into total sharing on the deno_server preset, because nothing else ever forks there. Two incidental blockers found while setting this up: (1) installing `$REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-nitro-10.67.0.tgz` alongside `@sentry/nuxt` pulls `nitro@3.0.0` into node_modules, and `getNitroMajorVersion()` (packages/nuxt/src/vite/utils.ts:12, resolves the `nitro` package, not the nitro the app actually builds with) then takes the Nitro-v3 path on a nitropack-2.13.4 app: the build warns `"nitro/storage" ... could not be resolved` and the server dies at boot with `[ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED] Package subpath './storage' is not defined by "exports" in .../nitro/package.json`; `npm uninstall @sentry/nitro` fixes it. (2) `Scope.clear()` no longer exists on develop, so an app-level "clear the isolation scope in a first middleware" workaround for (B) fails with `TypeError: getIsolationScope$1(...).clear is not a function` and HTTP 500 on every route.
Workaround: Build with the `node_server` Nitro preset instead of `deno_server` and run that output under Deno: `nitro: { preset: 'node_server' }` in nuxt.config.ts (or `NITRO_PRESET=node_server npx nuxt build`), then `cd .output && PORT=<port> deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env --allow-sys --allow-ffi --unstable-byonm ./server/index.mjs`. That restores per-request isolation for concurrent requests, plus route-named `http.server` spans and transactions, and it also fixes the entry-injection bug (the Sentry import lands in index.mjs, no manual prepend, no bogus `deno.json start` file). It does not fix the residual leak: every request still inherits the tags/user set by the first request the process served, and there is no app-level fix for that on 10.67.0 because `Scope.clear()` was removed.

Headers work, spans only partly: the `http.client` child of an explicit `Sentry.startSpan` is emitted ({"type":"transaction","name":"manual-root-fetch",...,"spans":["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:28842/rec-inspan"]}), but the three parentless ones are dropped: `Sentry Logger [log]: Sending outcomes: [ { reason: "no_parent_span", category: "span", quantity: 3 } ]`. This is `packages/core/src/fetch.ts:104-117` - `shouldEmitSpan = hasParent || hasSpanStreamingEnabled(client)`. Nuxt-on-Deno has no server span at all (the separate route-names finding), so under `static` there is nothing to parent a top-level fetch to. Under the develop default `stream` this does not matter. Root cause: nothing in the Node-side default integration set instruments a non-undici global `fetch`. `nativeNodeFetchIntegration` (`packages/node/src/integrations/node-fetch/index.ts`) only subscribes to undici diagnostics channels, which Deno's Rust-native `fetch` never emits, and `@sentry/deno`'s own default set (`packages/deno/src/sdk.ts:29-47`: denoServe, denoHttp, breadcrumbs, ...) has no global-fetch integration either. The `@sentry/core` fetch primitives that the browser, Cloudflare and vercel-edge SDKs use work perfectly on Deno - they are simply never wired up on the server side. So this is a missing integration, not a runtime limitation, and finding K2 is fixable in the SDK. Cross-check under node was not possible: the `deno_server` output emits `npm:` specifiers and `node .output/server/index.mjs` dies with `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME ... Received protocol 'npm:'`. Workaround: Add a global-fetch integration to `sentry.server.config.ts`. Either `integrations: [winterCGFetchIntegration()]` imported from `@sentry/vercel-edge` (extra dependency, span origin `auto.http.wintercg_fetch`), or, with no new dependency, a small integration on top of `@sentry/core`: import { addFetchInstrumentationHandler, defineIntegration, getClient, instrumentFetchRequest, isSentryRequestUrl, LRUMap, shouldPropagateTraceForUrl } from '@sentry/core'; export const globalFetchIntegration = defineIntegration(() => { const spans: Record<string, any> = {}; const headersUrlMap = new LRUMap<string, boolean>(100); return { name: 'GlobalFetch', setupOnce() { addFetchInstrumentationHandler(handlerData => { const client = getClient(); if (!client || isSentryRequestUrl(handlerData.fetchData.url, client)) return; instrumentFetchRequest(handlerData, () => true, url => shouldPropagateTraceForUrl(url, client.getOptions().tracePropagationTargets, headersUrlMap), spans, { spanOrigin: 'auto.http.fetch' }); }); } }; }); Then `Sentry.init({ ..., integrations: [globalFetchIntegration()] })`. Keep the develop default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'`; with `traceLifecycle: 'static'` the headers still get attached but a fetch that is not inside an explicit `Sentry.startSpan` is dropped with `no_parent_span`, because Nuxt-on-Deno produces no server span to parent it to. This covers nitro's `$fetch`/ofetch too, since ofetch calls global `fetch`.
db spans✓* works-waNo instrumentation path exists for this combination: there is no Bun plugin, no Deno import hook (the app is a rolled-up nitro bundle, not a node_modules import graph), and no Cloudflare Vite plugin. The SDK's own build-time injection ran and injected nothing: `[Sentry] Bundler plugin ran, injected libraries=[]` and `[Sentry] Runtime hook registered, injected libraries=[]`. Separately, a module-scope `mysql2/promise` pool cannot even execute in the deno_server output: `/api/db` returns 500 with `genFunc$1 is not a function` (the `generate-function` dependency broken by nitro's rollup bundling for the deno preset). That second failure is a Nuxt/Deno packaging bug, not a Sentry one, but it means no db span is reachable either way. Lifecycle: static. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. Both halves of the claim are wrong. (1) "No instrumentation path exists / injected nothing." The @sentry/nuxt build-time bundler plugin DOES instrument mysql2 inside the nitro rollup bundle, even for `deno_server`. Proof from the built output (no runtime hook involved, mysql2 is fully bundled): $ grep -oE "tracingChannel\('[^']+'\)" .output/server/chunks/_/db.mjs | sort -u tracingChannel('mysql2:connect') tracingChannel('mysql2:execute') tracingChannel('mysql2:pool:connect') tracingChannel('mysql2:query') The runtime debug lines `[Sentry] Bundler plugin ran, injected libraries=[]` and `[Sentry] Runtime hook registered, injected libraries=[]` are MISLEADING: the bundler list is populated at build time in a different process and is always empty at runtime. The prior agent read those lines as the verdict; the bundle contradicts them. The app log also shows the channel integrations do subscribe on Deno: `[instrumentation:mysql2] Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly`. (2) "genFunc$1 is not a function / no db span reachable." Fixed by one nitro option, already present in the app under test: nitro: { preset: 'deno_server', externals: { inline: ['generate-function', 'named-placeholders'] } } With that, /api/db returns 200 with real rows from MariaDB. Sink evidence, deno_server preset, traceLifecycle 'static' (port 41352): {"type":"transaction","name":"manual-parent","op":"manual","source":"custom","status":"ok", "sdk":"sentry.javascript.nuxt","spans":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]} Same app, default lifecycle (stream, traceLifecycle line removed), port 41353: {"type":"span","trace_id":"025c66c6...","items":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db SELECT users","manual manual-parent"], "raw":[{"name":"SELECT users","status":"ok","parent_span_id":"b50b3bcbcacf1bb1","is_segment":false, "origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel"}, ...]} Low-cardinality name and correct origin, so the spans are genuine auto-instrumentation, not something the probe faked. The one real limit on `deno_server`: the db subscriber is registered with `requiresParentSpan: true` (packages/server-utils/src/integrations/mysql2/mysql2-dc-subscriber.ts:125 and :146), and the `deno_server` output serves via `Deno.serve`, not `node:http`, so no `http.server` span exists to be that parent. A bare `/api/db` therefore returns 200 with zero span envelopes; only a handler wrapped in `Sentry.startSpan` gets db spans. Confirmed in the app log: for `/api/db` there is only `Patched h3 event handler. Using existing isolation scope.` and no `[Tracing] Starting sampled span`. That limit disappears entirely with the `node-server` preset still run by `deno run` (port 41354, no code change, no manual span): {"type":"span","trace_id":"5b3bf407...","items":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users","http.server GET"], "raw":[{"name":"GET","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.http_server"}, {"name":"SELECT users","parent_span_id":"83a35a41fb874e0f","origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel"}, ...]} Each request also got its own trace id (5b3bf407 / bd510b7f / 7df3fe7d), and events carried request data and user IP, so this preset also fixes the reported "no server span at all" and shared-trace-id problems. It additionally fixes the reported SDK bug: with `node-server` the module correctly prepends `import './sentry.server.config.mjs';` to `.output/server/index.mjs`; only with `deno_server` does it write that line into a file literally named `.output/server/deno.json start`. Not reproduced/side note: `mysql` (v2, the callback driver) gets no channel injection in this bundle and its handler 500s with `TypeError: SqlString.format is not a function` — a separate nitro-bundling defect, out of scope here. Workaround: Two things, both one line. 1. Make mysql2 runnable in the nitro bundle (fixes `genFunc$1 is not a function`), in nuxt.config.ts: nitro: { externals: { inline: ['generate-function', 'named-placeholders'] } } 2. Prefer `nitro: { preset: 'node-server' }` (or `NITRO_PRESET=node-server`) and run the output with `deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env --allow-sys --allow-ffi --unstable-byonm --unstable-detect-cjs ./server/index.mjs`. Deno is still the runtime, but nitro serves over `node:http`, so you get `http.server` root spans, per-request traces, request data — and therefore db spans on ordinary route handlers with no code change. The SDK also injects `import './sentry.server.config.mjs';` into `.output/server/index.mjs` correctly with this preset. If you must keep `preset: 'deno_server'`: db spans still work, but only inside an explicit `Sentry.startSpan(...)` in the handler, because `Deno.serve` produces no request span to parent them. You must also create the entry wrapper yourself, since the module writes the config import into a file named `.output/server/deno.json start`: printf "import './sentry.server.config.mjs';\nimport './index.mjs';\n" > .output/server/boot.mjs cd .output && deno run ... ./server/boot.mjs

Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions Nuxt on Deno. `grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/` returns nothing, and `grep -rni "nuxt|nitro" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/` returns nothing; the Deno guide (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx, 232 lines) covers only plain `Deno.serve`/`Deno.cron`. The two Nuxt install pages that a user would land on both assume a Node process and both mislead here: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/install/cli-import.mdx:33 prescribes `node --import ./.output/server/sentry.server.config.mjs .output/server/index.mjs` (there is no `--import` on `deno run`), and cli-import.mdx:42 only says "Make sure to update the paths accordingly, especially when using a different Nitro preset". docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/install/limited-server-tracing.mdx:38 claims the SDK "will then automatically import this file at the top of the Nitro server entry file in the build output" - with the deno_server preset it does not (see notes). limited-server-tracing.mdx:18 does warn that only native Node APIs are instrumented under this method, which is consistent with what I measured, but it does not warn that request isolation and trace continuation are lost on a runtime whose server is not `node:http`.

Documented: wrong

The presets page must stop implying that every non-Cloudflare preset works out of the box and must add a Deno section saying the opposite for `deno_server`: with `nitro: { preset: 'deno_server' }` there is no request instrumentation — route names are not parameterized, every request shares one isolation scope and one trace id (so tags, users and breadcrumbs leak between requests), and incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers are not continued. The verified guidance is: do not set a Nitro preset on Deno. Keep the default `node-server` preset (`npx nuxt build`) and run the produced Node output under Deno with `cd .output/server && PORT=<port> deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env --allow-sys --allow-ffi --unstable-byonm ./index.mjs`, with `sentry: { autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import' }`; that restores route names, incoming trace continuation, per-request isolation and route-level errors with request data. The page must also cover the two remaining Deno gaps: (a) outgoing requests made with `fetch` or nitro's `$fetch` get no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers because Deno's fetch is not backed by `node:http`/undici — add `winterCGFetchIntegration()` from `@sentry/vercel-edge` in `sentry.server.config.ts` (and `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` in the verified configuration); (b) if `deno_server` is used anyway, database drivers must stay bundled — the verified config is `nitro: { preset: 'deno_server', externals: { inline: ['generate-function', 'named-placeholders'], external: ['mysql'] } }`, because externalizing a driver routes it through Deno's module hook where `require()` of a JSON file fails. Errors and logs work in all cases.

Page to write: guides/nuxt/features/nitro-deployment-presets.mdx — add a "Deno" section next to the existing "Cloudflare Pages" section at :9 and qualify the "work out of the box" claim at :7; cross-link a new guides/deno/frameworks/nuxt.mdx with the full start command and integration snippet

docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/features/nitro-deployment-presets.mdx:7 claims "The Sentry Nuxt SDK provides support for different Nitro deployment presets, most of which **work out of the box**" and the 11-line file then documents only Cloudflare Pages (:9-11) — the run contradicts this for the `deno_server` preset, which produced no request instrumentation at all; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/install/cli-import.mdx:33 prescribes `node --import ./.output/server/sentry.server.config.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`, a Node-only start command; `grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/` returns 0 hits and `grep -rniE "nuxt|nitro" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/` returns 0 hits

Bottom line: Nuxt 4 builds and runs fine on Deno with the `deno_server` preset, and @sentry/nuxt gives you errors and logs there, but everything that depends on a server span (route names, isolation, incoming trace, outgoing propagation, db spans) is dead, and the wiring the docs describe does not work unmodified. SDK bugs found (both in @sentry/nuxt 10.67.0 on develop): 1. `autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import'` writes to the wrong file with any non-node preset. `addSentryTopImport` (node_modules/@sentry/nuxt/build/module/module.mjs:170-176) derives the entry filename from `nitro.options.commands.preview` via `getFilenameFromNodeStartCommand` = `/[^/\\]+\.[^/\\]+$/` (module.mjs:52-56). For deno_server the preview command is `deno task --config .output/deno.json start`, so the regex yields the literal string `deno.json start`. The module then creates `.output/server/deno.json start` containing `import './sentry.server.config.mjs';\nundefined` (readFile of a nonexistent path -> `data` is undefined, and the error is never surfaced because the callback ignores `err`). The real entry `.output/server/index.mjs` is left untouched, so Sentry never initializes and the failure is completely silent even with `debug: true` (the success log fires regardless). Same trap applies to any preset whose preview command is not `node <file>.mjs`. Worth fixing twice over: (a) resolve the entry from `nitro.options.rollupConfig.output.entryFileNames` first rather than from the preview command string, and (b) check `err` in the readFile callback. 2. Request isolation collapses on any runtime without node:http server instrumentation. `patchEventHandler` (runtime/utils/patchEventHandler.js) clones the isolation scope only when `getIsolationScope() === getDefaultIsolationScope()`. On Node the http instrumentation has already forked per request so reusing it is right; on Deno nothing forks, request 1 installs a clone and every later request sees that clone as "existing" and reuses it forever. Tags, transaction names and the propagation context (hence the trace id) are then process-global. A `Deno.serve`-shaped runtime needs the h3 patch to fork unconditionally and to `continueTrace` from the incoming headers. Other observations: - `contexts.runtime` reports `{name: "node", version: "v26.3.0"}` on Deno 2.9.0, so events give no hint the app is on Deno. - Manual `Sentry.startSpan` works and produces a proper `transaction` envelope with nested `spans[]`, so the transport and tracing core are fine; only the automatic server span is missing. - `traceLifecycle: 'static'` was used for every result above. Under the default `'stream'` the picture is the same (no span envelopes for requests). - Nuxt/nitro bug unrelated to Sentry: a module-scope `mysql2/promise` pool throws `genFunc$1 is not a function` at query time in the deno_server bundle (the `generate-function` dependency is inlined by rollup and breaks). mysql2 is therefore unusable on this preset regardless of instrumentation. - Nuxt/tooling gotcha that cost time: `npx nuxt build --buildDir X` moves the output to `X/.output`, flips the preview command back to `node`, and drops the api route chunks; always build with the default buildDir when testing this combination. - Ports 41338/41339 were occupied by another agent's sink partway through, which silently swallowed one round of envelopes; all reported results were re-collected on 30411/30412/30413-30415. - All processes started were killed; `node_modules` was removed (275 MB freed). Rerun with RERUN.sh.
