SvelteKit on Deno M-sveltekit-deno

SvelteKit 2 (@sveltejs/kit 2.x, adapter-node 5.x, svelte 5, vite 6) + @sentry/sveltekit 10.67.0 (develop) · Deno 2.9.0 (aarch64-apple-darwin), running the adapter-node production build · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

SvelteKit runs on Deno via adapter-node with no changes: `vite build` under node, then `HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=<p> deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --allow-ffi build/index.js`. Verified with a bare app (no Sentry) first: `/ping` -> "pong", `/users/42` -> "user 42".

Sentry wiring that a docs page would have to show:

1) Install (develop tarballs; a released npm tree would just be `npm i @sentry/sveltekit`):
   npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-sveltekit-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-svelte-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-browser-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-browser-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-replay-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-replay-canvas-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-feedback-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bundler-plugins-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-cloudflare-10.67.0.tgz mysql2

2) vite.config.js — note the import path changed on develop:
   import { sveltekit } from '@sveltejs/kit/vite';
   import { sentrySvelteKit } from '@sentry/sveltekit/vite';   // NOT '@sentry/sveltekit' (v10 docs show the root entry)
   export default {
     plugins: [sentrySvelteKit({ autoUploadSourceMaps: false }), sveltekit()],
     ssr: { external: ['mysql2', '@sentry/sveltekit', '@sentry/node', '@sentry/core'] },
     build: { rollupOptions: { external: [/^mysql2/, /^@sentry\//] } },
   };
   The externals matter: without them Vite inlines mysql2 into the SSR chunk (it then fails on `lru.min` default export) and inlines the SDK, and the SDK prints
   "`@sentry/server-runtime-injection` was bundled into your application, so mysql2 ... load uninstrumented".

3) src/hooks.server.js — init at module top, then the two SvelteKit hooks:
   import * as Sentry from '@sentry/sveltekit';
   Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel: 'http://127.0.0.1:52431/', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'stream' | 'static' });
   export const handle = Sentry.sentryHandle();
   export const handleError = Sentry.handleErrorWithSentry();
   No `--import` / preload flag is needed on Deno: `Sentry.init` inside hooks.server.js is early enough, and the SDK logs "SDK initialized from ESM" plus "Registered diagnostics-channel injection via Module.registerHooks()".

4) Run: `HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=<p> deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --allow-ffi build/index.js`
   (`--allow-ffi` only for mysql2; drop it otherwise. No `deno.json` needed, no `@sentry/deno` involved: the server side is the full @sentry/node SDK and it boots cleanly on Deno, installing every integration including OpenTelemetry.)
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksA throw inside a +server.js GET handler reaches Sentry as an unhandled event with mechanism `auto.function.sveltekit.handle_error` (handled:false), sdk `sentry.javascript.sveltekit`, transaction `GET /boom`, stack frames with context lines, and the same trace_id as the request transaction. SvelteKit does not swallow it: the route returns 500 and `handleErrorWithSentry()` reports it. Observed in both stream and static lifecycle.
route names✓ worksParameterized route /users/42 is named `GET /users/[id]`, SvelteKit's own route id, not the raw URL. In static lifecycle the transaction carries `"source":"route"`. In stream lifecycle the span is `http.server GET /users/[id]` but the span item exposes no `sentry.source` attribute, so source could only be read from the static-lifecycle transaction.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent GET /iso?t=aaa|bbb|ccc, each doing Sentry.setTag then a 120ms await then captureException: each event carries exactly its own tag ({"iso_tag":"aaa"} etc.), no cross-talk, and three distinct trace ids. AsyncLocalStorage-based isolation works under Deno's node:async_hooks. Stream lifecycle.
incoming trace✓ worksA request with `sentry-trace: aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff00001111-1234567890abcdef-1` plus baggage continues the trace: the server span and the captured event both carry trace_id aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff00001111 and parent_span_id 1234567890abcdef, and Sentry.getActiveSpan() inside the handler reports the same. Stream lifecycle.
outgoing fetch✓* works-waA global `fetch()` from inside a handler to the local recorder produces NO http.client span (static-lifecycle transaction `GET /fetchout` has `"spans":[]`) and the recorder sees `sentryTrace: null, baggage: null`. Deno emits no undici diagnostics-channel events, so @sentry/node's NodeFetch integration never fires. Contrast probe: the same call made with `node:http` DOES work, giving `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:52432/rec-http` and both headers on the wire. Same class as the known Deno finding K2, now reproduced through @sentry/node rather than @sentry/deno. verified: works-after-all Reproduced exactly, then found a one-line fix that fully repairs it — so the finding stands for the documented wiring, and the gap is a missing integration, not a runtime limitation. Setup: SvelteKit 2.60 + adapter-node 5 + svelte 5 + vite 6, @sentry/sveltekit 10.67.0 (develop tarballs), `vite build` under node 26.5.0, run under deno 2.9.0 (aarch64-apple-darwin). hooks.server.js does `Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle })` at module top plus `sentryHandle()` / `handleErrorWithSentry()`. Sink on 51101, recorder on 51102. Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-sveltekit-deno-outgoingfetch/ (node_modules removed at the end; `npm install --no-audit --no-fund` recreates it, then `npx vite build`). A) BASELINE, documented wiring, traceLifecycle 'static' (run-b-app-baseline.log). Global `fetch()` -> no span; SvelteKit's own `event.fetch` -> no span either; `node:http` -> span, as reported: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /fetchout","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":[],"hasRequestData":false} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /eventfetch","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":[],"hasRequestData":false} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /httpout","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:51102/rec-http"],"hasRequestData":false} recorder: {"path":"/rec-fetch","sentryTrace":null,"baggage":null,"traceparent":null} {"path":"/rec-eventfetch","sentryTrace":null,"baggage":null,"traceparent":null} {"path":"/rec-http","sentryTrace":"69e303992a5c4eb4aa2e24cea0a62a16-9b363fae35f1e55e-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,...,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fhttpout,...","traceparent":null} Command: `HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=51110 SINK_PORT=51101 REC_PORT=51102 LIFECYCLE=static deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys build/index.js` Root cause confirmed in source, not guessed: @sentry/node's fetch instrumentation is purely a `diagnostics_channel` subscriber on `undici:request:create` / `undici:client:sendHeaders` / `undici:request:headers` / `undici:request:trailers` / `undici:request:error` (~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/packages/node/src/integrations/node-fetch/undici-instrumentation.ts:107-113). Deno's `fetch` is native Rust, not undici, so nothing ever publishes on those channels. Grepping `addFetchInstrumentationHandler|instrumentFetchRequest` across packages/node/src and packages/sveltekit/src returns nothing: neither package patches `globalThis.fetch`, so no option or init placement can fix this. `traceLifecycle`, init placement, and hook shape are all irrelevant to it. Variants tried and their outcome: traceLifecycle 'static' and 'stream' — no difference to the baseline break; SvelteKit's `event.fetch` instead of global `fetch` — same break (new data point the original probe did not have; it is worse than reported, since the framework's own fetch is affected too); init placement is fixed by SvelteKit (hooks.server.js top level) and already works, the SDK logs "SDK initialized from ESM"; the repo's own reference app dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/sveltekit-2-svelte-5/src/hooks.server.ts uses exactly the wiring tested (init + sentryHandle + handleErrorWithSentry, no fetch integration), confirming there is nothing extra a user is supposed to add. Deno 2.8.3 (CI pin) not tested: $SCRATCH/deno283 no longer exists on this machine. Verdict is confirmed-broken rather than works-after-all because no documented wiring, option, init placement, lifecycle or bundler variant fixes it — the only fixes are adding an integration that no SvelteKit/Node/Deno docs page mentions, one of which lives in the wrong package (@sentry/cloudflare) and one of which the user has to write.
Workaround: Either (a) one line, using shipped SDK code: `import { fetchIntegration } from '@sentry/cloudflare';` and `Sentry.init({ ..., integrations: [fetchIntegration()] })` in hooks.server.js — verified to produce the `http.client` span and both `sentry-trace` and `baggage` headers under both trace lifecycles, including for SvelteKit's `event.fetch`; or (b) copy the WinterCG fetch patcher into the app as a userland integration from `@sentry/core` primitives (`addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest` + `isSentryRequestUrl` + `shouldPropagateTraceForUrl`), see src/userland-fetch-integration.js in the probe dir. Both are ~equally effective; (a) drags @sentry/cloudflare into a Deno server dependency tree, (b) keeps the dependency list clean. The pre-existing escape hatch of switching the call to `node:http` also works but changes application code. The real fix belongs in the SDK: `@sentry/node` (or `@sentry/deno`) should ship a global-fetch integration and enable it when the undici diagnostics channels are absent, which is exactly the Deno case.
db spans✓* works-waNo db span, and worse: with Sentry loaded, importing mysql2 at all crashes the route. `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` registers `Module.registerHooks()`, its transform throws (`failed to inject diagnostics-channel into mysql2: TypeError: transform is not a function`), and then mysql2's `require('../package.json')` at connection_config.js:13 fails with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` — the hooked loader compiles JSON as JS. GET /db returns 500 and Sentry reports that SyntaxError as the app's error. The identical mysql2 module-scope connection and SELECT succeed under Deno with Sentry absent, so this is caused by the SDK. Instrumentation path used: none extra — the SDK's own Module.registerHooks runtime injection, which is what breaks; no Deno import hook (`@sentry/deno/import`) was involved. Same failure class as known Deno finding K3, reached through the Node SDK's injection path. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. SvelteKit 2 + adapter-node on Deno 2.9.0 with @sentry/sveltekit 10.67.0 (develop) does emit `db` spans, in both trace lifecycles. The report's two claims come apart: the mysql2 500 is real, but it is a Deno bug (denoland/deno#36240), not the absence of db instrumentation, and it does not affect the `mysql` driver at all. Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-sveltekit-deno-dbspans/ app/ SvelteKit 2.70 + adapter-node 5.5 + svelte 5 + vite 6, wiring identical to the report (sentrySvelteKit from '@sentry/sveltekit/vite', mysql/mysql2 + @sentry/* external, Sentry.init at the top of src/hooks.server.js, sentryHandle + handleErrorWithSentry) app/src/lib/db.js module-scope `mysql2/promise` connection -> route /db app/src/routes/db2/+server.js `mysql` v2 connection inside the handler -> route /db2 app/prewarm-json.mjs the one-line workaround, used via `deno run --preload` jsontest/t.mjs minimal repro: registerHooks pass-through + require('*.json') runD.log (no workaround, stream), runE.log (workaround, stream), runF.log (workaround, static), runG.log (--preload workaround, stream), runA.log/runB.log (earlier runs, same conclusions) 1) The `mysql` driver needs NO change whatsoever. Unmodified reported setup, `LIFECYCLE=stream`, sink on 41777: ping -> pong [200] db -> {"message":"Internal Error"} [500] db2 -> {"driver":"mysql","rows":2} [200] sink: span ['http.server GET /ping'] span ['db SELECT users', 'http.server GET /db2'] span ['http.server GET /sentinel'] raw: {"name": "SELECT users", "status": "ok", "parent_span_id": "...", "origin": "auto.db.mysql"} So "no db span" is wrong even in the exact configuration the report ran. 2) mysql2 works too once Deno's JSON bug is sidestepped. Warm mysql2's package.json into the CJS require cache before Sentry registers its hooks. Two equivalent forms, both verified: a) run flag only, no app code change (runG): HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=41784 deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --allow-ffi \ --preload ./prewarm-json.mjs build/index.js where prewarm-json.mjs is: import { createRequire } from 'node:module'; createRequire(import.meta.url)('mysql2/package.json'); b) the same two lines at the very top of src/hooks.server.js, above the `Sentry.init` import. Result (stream, runG): db -> {"driver":"mysql2","rows":2} [200] span ['db SELECT users', 'http.server GET /db'] span ['db SELECT users', 'http.server GET /db2'] raw origin for /db: "auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel" <- the SDK's channel injection really did instrument mysql2 on Deno Result (static, runF): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["db SELECT id, name FROM users"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db2",...,"spans":["db SELECT id, name FROM users"]} 3) The crash is Deno's, not the SDK's. jsontest/t.mjs registers a pass-through `Module.registerHooks({resolve,load})` with no Sentry anywhere: -- deno 2.9.0 no hook: json ok: {"a":1} -- deno 2.9.0 with pass-through hook: json FAIL: SyntaxError Unexpected token ':' -- node 26 with hook: json ok: {"a":1} Any library that `require()`s a .json at runtime breaks under Deno the moment anything registers sync module hooks. mysql2 does that at connection_config.js:13; `mysql` v2 does not, which is the whole difference between /db and /db2. Two secondary observations that stand independent of the verdict: - `[instrumentation] failed to inject diagnostics-channel into mysql2: TypeError: transform is not a function` is printed on every run, together with the always-on "`@sentry/server-runtime-injection` was bundled into your application" warning, yet the package is NOT bundled (the stack points at app/node_modules/@sentry/server-runtime-injection/build/esm/vendored/...) and mysql2 IS instrumented (origin auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel). One mysql2 file fails to transform under Deno while the ones that matter succeed, so the always-on warning is a false alarm here and sends users down the wrong path. - `[Sentry] Runtime hook registered, injected libraries=[]` is logged before any library loads, so it never reflects reality.
Workaround: Prime mysql2's package.json in the CJS require cache before Sentry's module hooks are installed. Either add a preload file and start the server with it (no app change): // prewarm-json.mjs import { createRequire } from 'node:module'; createRequire(import.meta.url)('mysql2/package.json'); HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=<p> deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --allow-ffi --preload ./prewarm-json.mjs build/index.js or put the same two lines at the very top of src/hooks.server.js, above the `@sentry/sveltekit` import and `Sentry.init`. The `mysql` (v2) driver needs no workaround at all. Both give a `db` span parented under the SvelteKit `http.server` span, in `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` and `'static'`.

Docs today

No docs page mentions SvelteKit on Deno. The Deno guide is a single page with no framework sub-pages (~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx, plus a configuration/ dir); it never says "sveltekit". The SvelteKit guide never says "deno". The only adapter/runtime statement lives in ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/sveltekit/manual-setup__v10.7.0.mdx:21-35, an Expandable titled "Notes on SvelteKit adapter compatibility": "Fully supported Node.js runtimes" lists adapter-auto/adapter-vercel/adapter-node (:26-28), "Supported non-Node.js runtimes" lists only adapter-cloudflare (:30), "Currently not supported: Non-Node.js server runtimes, such as Vercel's edge runtime" (:31-32), and "Other adapters ... might work, but they're not currently officially supported" (:33-34). Deno is not named on either side of that split, so a user cannot tell from the docs whether adapter-node output run under Deno counts as the supported adapter-node case or as an unsupported non-Node runtime. The current (unversioned) manual-setup.mdx is a 9-line stub with no adapter section at all.

Documented: wrong

The adapter-compatibility note must be corrected to say that SvelteKit runs on Deno through adapter-node with no source changes: build with `vite build` under Node, then start the adapter output with `HOST=… PORT=… deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --allow-ffi build/index.js`. Errors, route names, per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation and logs all work unchanged. Two Deno-specific caveats must be added. (1) Outgoing HTTP: `@sentry/node`'s fetch instrumentation is inert on Deno because it listens on undici `diagnostics_channel` events and Deno's global `fetch` is native, so neither a global `fetch()` nor SvelteKit's `event.fetch` produces an `http.client` span or carries `sentry-trace`/`baggage`. The verified fix is to register `fetchIntegration` from `@sentry/cloudflare` (already installed as a dependency of `@sentry/sveltekit`, so no new install) in `src/hooks.server.js`, gated to Deno so Node builds are not double-instrumented. (2) Database spans: they work on Deno with adapter-node and no flags for drivers that do not read their own `package.json` at import time (`mysql` needs nothing). Deno has an open bug (denoland/deno#36240) where registering any module hook makes `require('*.json')` compile as JavaScript, which breaks drivers like `mysql2`; the verified workaround is to force the driver's `package.json` into the CJS cache before `Sentry.init` runs, i.e. `createRequire(import.meta.url)('mysql2/package.json')` at the top of `src/hooks.server.js` followed by a dynamic `await import('@sentry/sveltekit')`.

Page to write: guides/sveltekit/manual-setup__v10.7.0.mdx:21-35 — correct the "Currently not supported" bullet and add Deno/adapter-node; restore an adapter-and-runtime compatibility section in guides/sveltekit/manual-setup.mdx (which currently has none), and add guides/deno/frameworks/sveltekit.mdx with the run command, the `fetchIntegration` snippet and the mysql2 `createRequire` workaround

The current docs/platforms/javascript/guides/sveltekit/manual-setup.mdx has no such expandable at all (its body is only `sentry-init/manual-setup-callout` + `getting-started-complete`, :1-9), so the v11 line now makes no runtime statement whatsoever; `grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/sveltekit/` returns 0 hits

Headline: SvelteKit + @sentry/sveltekit runs on Deno better than expected. The server side is the full @sentry/node SDK with OpenTelemetry, and it boots and works under Deno with no import hook, no --import flag, and no @sentry/deno involvement — Sentry.init in hooks.server.js is sufficient. Errors, route names with source "route", isolation across concurrent requests, incoming trace continuation and logs all work. Two things are broken and one docs bug. 1) Broken, and this is the serious one: with the SDK loaded, importing mysql2 crashes the app on Deno. `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` registers `Module.registerHooks()`; its code transformer throws on mysql2 ("TypeError: transform is not a function"), and after that mysql2's `require('../package.json')` fails with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` because the hooked CJS loader compiles JSON as JavaScript. The same connection and query succeed on Deno 2.9.0 when Sentry is absent. So this is not just "no db spans", the SDK takes a working route down. It is the same failure class as the known Deno finding K3 (denoland/deno#36240, JSON require under a module hook), but reached through the Node SDK's Module.registerHooks path rather than `@sentry/deno/import`, which means it also hits any Node-SDK-on-Deno deployment, not just apps that opted into the Deno hook. Any CJS dependency that does `require('*.json')` is affected. 2) Broken: global fetch gets no http.client span and no sentry-trace/baggage headers. Deno emits no undici diagnostics-channel events. The node:http contrast probe in the same handler works fully (span plus both headers), which pins the cause to the fetch instrumentation channel rather than to tracing or propagation. Consequence for a SvelteKit user: SvelteKit's idiomatic `event.fetch` / `fetch` calls in load functions and endpoints produce no distributed trace on Deno. 3) Develop API change vs docs: `sentrySvelteKit` is only exported from `@sentry/sveltekit/vite` on develop. Importing it from `@sentry/sveltekit` (what the v10 docs show) fails the Vite config load with "does not provide an export named 'sentrySvelteKit'". Whatever docs page covers SvelteKit needs updating for v11. Local packaging artifacts, not user-facing bugs: (a) npm resolved @sentry/bundler-plugins and @sentry/cloudflare from the registry at the released 10.67.0, which then failed against develop's @sentry/core with "does not provide an export named 'ServerRuntimeClient'"; passing those two develop tarballs on the install line fixed it. (b) Vite inlines mysql2 and the SDK into the SSR bundle unless you set ssr.external / rollupOptions.external, which the SDK itself warns about at runtime. Noise worth a docs or SDK note: on Deno the ContextLines integration spams "Failed to read file: ext:deno_node/async_hooks.ts ... ENOENT" and "Could not find line N in file ext:core/01_core.js" for every event, because Deno's internal frames use ext: URLs. Events still carry context lines for user frames (hasContextLine true). Ports used and released: sink 52431, recorder 52432, app 52433. All processes killed; node_modules (138M) removed. One mid-run gotcha for other agents: another agent's Deno server held 127.0.0.1:41337 while mine bound 0.0.0.0:41337, so curl silently hit theirs (an Astro 404 page). Bind HOST=127.0.0.1 explicitly.

CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksAn `Error` thrown from `GET` in `src/pages/boom.ts` reaches Sentry through the auto-added `@sentry/astro/middleware`; the event carries `mechanism: "auto.middleware.astro"`, `handled: false`, a `transaction` of `GET /boom`, the request URL, and source context lines. Astro does not swallow it: the route still returns 500 and Astro also logs the error itself, and in static lifecycle the transaction is `status: "internal_error"` on the same trace id. (Seen in both stream and static lifecycle.)
route names✓ works`/users/42` produces `GET /users/[id]` with `source: "route"` (static lifecycle transaction envelope) and the same low-cardinality name `http.server GET /users/[id]` in the stream-lifecycle span envelope. Astro's own route pattern is used, not the URL.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent `GET /iso?tag=alpha|beta|gamma` requests, each doing `Sentry.setTag` then a 150 ms await then `captureException`, produced three events with exactly their own tag (`{"probe_tag":"alpha"}` etc.) and three distinct trace ids. No cross-talk. (stream lifecycle)
incoming trace✓ worksA request to `/users/99` with `sentry-trace: aaaa…-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` and a `baggage` header continued the trace: the server transaction has `trace_id: "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"` and `parent_span_id: "bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb"`. (confirmed in both lifecycles)
outgoing fetch✓* works-waA global `fetch()` from inside a route handler to the local recorder produced NO `http.client` span (the `GET /outfetch` transaction has `spans: []`) and the recorder saw NO `sentry-trace` and NO `baggage` header. This is the known Deno gap (K2) and it is unchanged by Astro. `node:http` is instrumented fine on the same runtime and is a working workaround: `GET /outhttp` produced `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:44551/rec` and the recorder received both headers. verified: works-after-all Confirmed broken as reported, and I found the root cause plus a fully working user-side fix (see workaround), so nothing in the documented Astro/Deno wiring refutes it. Probe: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-astro-deno-outgoingfetch/ (Astro 7.3.1 output:'server' + @deno/astro-adapter 0.6.0 + @sentry/astro 10.67.0 develop, deno 2.9.0, built dist/server/entry.mjs). Full recipe in RERUN.md; logs app-v2-base.log / app-v2-cf.log / app-v2-custom-stream.log. Commands: npm install --no-audit --no-fund PORT=53821 node sink.mjs & PORT=53822 node rec.mjs & SINK_PORT=53821 REC_PORT=53822 LIFECYCLE=static [FETCH_FIX=cloudflare|custom] \ deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --allow-run dist/server/entry.mjs curl :53823/ ; curl :53823/outfetch ; curl :53823/outhttp ; curl :53823/sentinel curl :53821/__items ; curl :53822/__hits 1) BASELINE, stock wiring, traceLifecycle 'static' (broken, matches the report verbatim): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /outfetch","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_id":"672c185045bb409393cc084fc369f106","sdk":"sentry.javascript.astro","spans":[]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /outhttp","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_id":"e6005df74f8642a2a2aaa5c4b2fa4830","sdk":"sentry.javascript.astro","spans":["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:53822/rec"]} recorder hits: {"url":"/rec?via=fetch","sentryTrace":null,"baggage":null} {"url":"/rec?via=http","sentryTrace":"e6005df74f8642a2a2aaa5c4b2fa4830-92b4788a85970d32-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,...,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fouthttp,sentry-sampled=true,..."} 2) Things that do NOT change it: the other trace lifecycle (stream produces the same fetch-less span envelope), the documented Astro integration wiring, sourcemaps on/off, the src/middleware.ts init placement, node:http on the same process (always works). No bundler or Deno flag variant matters because the failure is below the SDK. 3) ROOT CAUSE (dc-probe.mjs, run under deno 2.9.0): after global fetch, channels fired: [] after node:http get, channels fired: ["http.client.request.created","http.client.request.start","http.client.response.finish"] Deno's global fetch publishes no node:diagnostics_channel events at all (neither "undici:request:*" nor "http.client.*"). @sentry/node's only outgoing-fetch path is the vendored undici diagnostics_channel instrumentation (packages/node/src/integrations/node-fetch/undici-instrumentation.ts, shipped as nativeNodeFetchIntegration), so it can never observe Deno's fetch. Export check on the installed builds: @sentry/node and @sentry/astro expose only `nativeNodeFetchIntegration`; a globalThis.fetch-patching `fetchIntegration` exists only in @sentry/bun (packages/bun/src/integrations/fetch.ts) and @sentry/cloudflare (packages/cloudflare/src/integrations/fetch.ts), plus `winterCGFetchIntegration` in @sentry/vercel-edge. @sentry/deno ships none. That asymmetry, not Astro, is the gap. 4) The repo's own e2e app agrees: ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/deno/tests/fetch.test.ts asserts only the hand-written `Sentry.startSpan({name:'test-outgoing-fetch'})` wrapper (`origin: 'manual'`) and never an `http.client` span, so the Deno suite does not cover automatic fetch instrumentation. astro-7 (the Astro reference app) runs on @astrojs/node, not Deno, so it never exercises this. 5) With a fetch integration added, the capability works completely (both lifecycles), which proves the runtime can support it and the only missing piece is SDK-shipped code: FETCH_FIX=cloudflare, static: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /outfetch","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_id":"87e311391b7b4e73bcd852eaeb4155d6","spans":["http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:53822/rec"]} {"url":"/rec?via=fetch","sentryTrace":"87e311391b7b4e73bcd852eaeb4155d6-9948eb2f76ac150b-1","baggage":"...sentry-trace_id=87e311391b7b4e73bcd852eaeb4155d6,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Foutfetch,sentry-sampled=true,sentry-sample_rate=1"} FETCH_FIX=custom, stream: {"type":"span","trace_id":"a26095c579e649eeb43ecb3e73d1507e","items":["http.client GET 127.0.0.1","http.server GET /outfetch"],"raw":[{"name":"GET 127.0.0.1","status":"ok","parent_span_id":"a5a58ddf030a4cf2","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.http.fetch"},{"name":"GET /outfetch","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.astro"}]} {"url":"/rec?via=fetch","sentryTrace":"a26095c579e649eeb43ecb3e73d1507e-b98ee9403a04bf8b-1","baggage":"...sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Foutfetch,sentry-sampled=true,..."} Side note reconfirmed: without src/middleware.ts importing sentry.server.config.js first, Sentry.init never runs for requests that only hit .ts/.js endpoint routes; the .astro page injection path is what warms it otherwise.
Workaround: Two, both verified end to end (span with correct parent + `sentry-trace` and `baggage` on the wire), on both traceLifecycle 'static' and 'stream'. A) Write a ~20-line integration from public @sentry/core exports (preferred; no cross-runtime package). File fetch-integration.js next to sentry.server.config.js: import { addFetchInstrumentationHandler, defineIntegration, getClient, instrumentFetchRequest, isSentryRequestUrl, LRUMap, shouldPropagateTraceForUrl } from '@sentry/core'; export const denoFetchIntegration = defineIntegration(() => { const headersUrlMap = new LRUMap(100); const spans = {}; return { name: 'DenoFetch', setupOnce() { addFetchInstrumentationHandler(handlerData => { const client = getClient(); if (!client || isSentryRequestUrl(handlerData.fetchData.url, client)) return; instrumentFetchRequest(handlerData, () => true, url => shouldPropagateTraceForUrl(url, client.getOptions().tracePropagationTargets, headersUrlMap), spans, { spanOrigin: 'auto.http.fetch' }); }); }}; }); then in sentry.server.config.js: `integrations: [denoFetchIntegration()]`. All seven core exports are present in the shipped @sentry/core 10.67.0 build. Produces `http.client` with origin `auto.http.fetch`. B) One-liner, if pulling an extra package is acceptable: `import { fetchIntegration } from '@sentry/cloudflare';` and `integrations: [fetchIntegration()]`. It is pure globalThis.fetch patching with no Workers-only APIs, so it loads and runs fine under Deno inside the Astro server bundle. Same span and headers, plus fetch breadcrumbs. C) If you only need the trace to continue and not the span: use `node:http`/`node:https` for the outgoing call (fully instrumented on Deno, verified in every run), or wrap the fetch in `Sentry.startSpan(...)` and attach headers from `Sentry.getTraceData()` yourself, which is what the repo's own deno e2e test does. Real fix belongs in the SDK: port the `fetchIntegration` that @sentry/bun and @sentry/cloudflare already have into @sentry/deno, and/or have @sentry/node fall back to globalThis.fetch patching when the undici diagnostics channels never fire.
db spans✓ worksA module-scope `mysql2.createPool` queried inside `GET /db` produced `db mysql2.pool.connect`, `db mysql2.connect` and `db SELECT id, name FROM users` (`db.query.text` set) as children of the server span. Instrumentation path: the `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` Vite plugin that `@sentry/astro` adds by itself during `astro build` — mysql2 is bundled into the SSR chunk and the built chunk contains 188 `orchestrion:*` channel markers. No Deno import hook and no manual Vite wiring were needed. Deno 2.9 additionally supports `Module.registerHooks()`, which the SDK registers at init, so the runtime path is available too.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info('astro-deno-log-line', { where: 'route' })` inside `GET /log` arrived as a log envelope (`{"type":"log","items":["info: astro-deno-log-line"]}`) after the ~5 s flush timer, in both lifecycles.

Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions Astro on Deno. The Astro guide actively says the opposite of what I measured: ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/index.mdx:23-27 carries an Alert titled "What runtime do you use?" reading "This SDK currently only works on Node runtimes, such as Node adapter or Vercel with Lambda functions. If you use Cloudflare Workers or Cloudflare Pages, refer to our Astro on Cloudflare guide. Other non-Node runtimes, like Vercel's Edge runtime, are currently not supported." `grep -rni deno` over docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/ returns nothing, and `grep -rni astro` over docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/ returns nothing (that guide is only index.mdx + configuration/, with no framework pages at all). So Deno is neither listed as supported nor listed as unsupported; a reader lands on "only Node runtimes" and concludes it will not work, which is wrong for @deno/astro-adapter on Deno 2.9.

Documented: wrong

The runtime Alert must be corrected: Deno is a supported runtime for `@sentry/astro`, not one of the excluded "other non-Node runtimes". A page must state that Astro SSR (`output: 'server'`) with `@deno/astro-adapter` runs under Deno by building normally and running the built `dist/server/entry.mjs` with Deno, that the Sentry packages must be installed with `npm install` into a real `node_modules` (not `deno add`), and that errors, route names, per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, database spans and logs all work with the standard `sentry.server.config.js` wiring. The one limitation to document is outgoing HTTP: requests made with the global `fetch()` are not instrumented on Deno — no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers — because Deno's native fetch emits none of the `undici:*` `diagnostics_channel` events the Node SDK subscribes to, so the downstream service starts a new trace. Two verified fixes must be shown: add `fetchIntegration` from `@sentry/cloudflare` (one extra install, one line in `sentry.server.config.js`; it uses only `@sentry/core` primitives and is runtime-agnostic), or use `node:http`/`node:https` for the calls that must be traced.

Page to write: guides/astro/index.mdx:22-31 — amend the "What runtime do you use?" Alert to name Deno as supported and link out; add guides/deno/frameworks/astro.mdx with the `@deno/astro-adapter` setup and the `fetchIntegration` snippet

docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/index.mdx:22-31 — Alert titled "What runtime do you use?": "This SDK currently only works on Node runtimes, such as Node adapter or Vercel with Lambda functions. If you use Cloudflare Workers or Cloudflare Pages, refer to our Astro on Cloudflare guide. Other non-Node runtimes, like Vercel's Edge runtime, are currently **not supported**." The run contradicts this: Astro 7.3.1 SSR with `@deno/astro-adapter` 0.6.0 and `@sentry/astro` on Deno 2.9.0 produced working errors, route names, isolation, incoming trace continuation, db spans and logs. `grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/` returns 0 hits, and guides/deno/ (index.mdx:1-232 plus two integration pages) never mentions Astro

1. Astro runs on Deno without Sentry (checked first, as asked): `@deno/astro-adapter@0.6.0` + astro 7.3.1 built and served `{"id":"42"}` from `/users/42` on Deno 2.9.0. The only build noise is three benign rolldown warnings from the adapter itself, e.g. "[IMPORT_IS_UNDEFINED] Import `start` will always be undefined because there is no matching export in '\0virtual:@deno/astro-adapter:config'" at node_modules/@deno/astro-adapter/src/server.ts:87 — the adapter still honours `deno({ port, hostname })`. 2. BIGGEST GAP, and it is Astro-side, not Deno-side: `@sentry/astro` injects the server init with `injectScript('page-ssr', ...)`, and Astro only applies `page-ssr` to `.astro` page components, not to `.ts`/`.js` endpoint routes. In a first run with no `src/middleware.ts` I hit `/boom` cold: the process printed zero "Sentry Logger" lines, the sink stayed empty, and only after I hit the one `.astro` page did init run. Verified in the build output: dist/server/chunks/index_CDQcGmve.mjs (from index.astro) contains `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/astro"` + the init, while dist/server/chunks/boom_DBViSP1b.mjs (from boom.ts) contains no Sentry import. An API-only Astro app on any adapter therefore silently reports nothing until an `.astro` page is rendered. My workaround — a project `src/middleware.ts` whose first statement imports `sentry.server.config.js` — makes init deterministic, because Astro loads the whole middleware sequence module graph before running any handler; the Sentry middleware is registered `order: 'pre'` and still wraps everything. A docs page for Astro-on-Deno would have to show this, since Deno has no equivalent of the Node `--import @sentry/astro/import` preload (`@sentry/astro/import` is just `import '@sentry/server-runtime-injection/import-hook'`, a Node loader hook). 3. `@sentry/node` under Deno's node compat is in far better shape than the docs imply. It installs every integration, logs "Registered diagnostics-channel injection via Module.registerHooks()" (Deno 2.9 has that API), and takes the "Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly" path for every library instrumentation. The Deno import hook from `@sentry/deno` is not involved anywhere. 4. db spans did NOT need any extra wiring. `@sentry/astro` adds `sentryOrchestrionPlugin({ buildTimeInstrumentation })` to the Vite config for every non-Cloudflare adapter, Astro's SSR build bundles mysql2 into the page chunk, and the emitted chunk carries the orchestrion channel publishes (188 `orchestrion:*` / `tracingChannel` hits in dist/server/chunks/db_*.mjs). So the answer to "which instrumentation path" is: the Vite build-time orchestrion plugin, applied automatically; no Bun plugin, no Deno import hook, no Cloudflare Vite plugin. 5. Deno K2 reproduces unchanged under Astro: global `fetch` gets neither an `http.client` span nor propagation headers. `node:http` gets both. That is the one capability that is broken here, and it is a runtime gap, not an Astro gap. 6. Cosmetic but user-visible: ContextLines repeatedly errors on Deno-internal stack frames — "Failed to read file: ext:core/01_core.js. Error: Error: ENOENT ..." and "Could not find line 475 in file ext:core/01_core.js" — printed for every captured error when `debug: true`. Events still carry correct context lines for app frames (`hasContextLine: true`). 7. I set `enabled: { client: false }` to keep the probe server-only; the client SDK path was not exercised, so "client errors" is not reported. 8. Housekeeping: both processes (deno app on 41337, sink on 44551) were killed; `node_modules` (242 MB) removed, leaving 1.7 MB of source, dist and logs. Nothing outside $REPRO/cells/M-astro-deno was touched. Only develop tarballs (10.67.0) were installed; 10.73.0 was never fetched.

React Router on Deno M-reactrouter-deno

React Router v7.18.3 (framework mode, SSR) · deno 2.9.0 · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

React Router framework mode runs on Deno, but NOT with the entry.server.tsx the docs show. Required wiring:

1. Packages (npm install, then run with deno):
   npm install react-router@^7 @react-router/dev@^7 @react-router/node@^7 react@^19 react-dom@^19 vite@^6 isbot@^5 mysql@^2
   npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-react-router-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-browser-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-react-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-browser-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-replay-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-replay-canvas-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-feedback-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bundler-plugins-10.67.0.tgz

2. deno.json: { "nodeModulesDir": "manual" }

3. app/entry.server.tsx MUST use the web-stream renderer, not the node one. Deno resolves `react-dom/server` through react-dom's `deno` export condition, which points at the browser build and has no `renderToPipeableStream`. Use `renderToReadableStream` from `react-dom/server` and return `new Response(body, ...)`. Then wrap it:
     export default wrapSentryHandleRequest(handleRequest);
     export const handleError = createSentryHandleError({ logErrors: true });
   both from `@sentry/react-router`.

4. instrument.server.mjs (plain @sentry/react-router init; the `node` export condition resolves under Deno and every Node integration installs):
     import * as Sentry from '@sentry/react-router';
     Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel: 'http://127.0.0.1:<sink>/', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' });

5. Server entry: a hand-written node:http adapter whose FIRST line is `import './instrument.server.mjs';`, then `createRequestHandler(build, 'production')` from `react-router` over `http.createServer`. The node:http server is what produces the http.server span and the isolation scope; a bare `Deno.serve` handler gets neither. `react-router-serve` and `NODE_OPTIONS='--import ./instrument.server.mjs'` (the two things the docs prescribe) are both unusable: Deno ignores NODE_OPTIONS, and react-router-serve goes through the renderToPipeableStream path Deno cannot load.

6. Build and run:
     npx react-router build
     PORT=<port> deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys server.mjs

7. Do not use mysql2 (see the db-spans finding). `mysql@2` works.

Docs: ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/ has no Deno mention at all, and .../guides/deno/index.mdx has no fetch caveat.
Workaround: Add a fetch integration by hand in instrument.server.mjs; nothing else is needed and both trace lifecycles work. Cheapest version, ~30 lines with no extra dependency (deno-fetch-integration.mjs in the probe dir): import { addFetchInstrumentationHandler, defineIntegration, getClient, instrumentFetchRequest, isSentryRequestUrl, LRUMap, shouldPropagateTraceForUrl } from '@sentry/core'; export const denoFetchIntegration = defineIntegration(() => { const headersUrlMap = new LRUMap(100); const spans = {}; return { name: 'DenoFetch', setupOnce() { addFetchInstrumentationHandler(handlerData => { const client = getClient(); if (!client) return; if (isSentryRequestUrl(handlerData.fetchData.url, client)) return; instrumentFetchRequest(handlerData, () => true, url => shouldPropagateTraceForUrl(url, client.getOptions().tracePropagationTargets, headersUrlMap), spans, { spanOrigin: 'auto.http.fetch' }); }); } }; }); then `Sentry.init({ ..., integrations: [denoFetchIntegration()] })`. Equivalent alternatives: `integrations: [fetchIntegration()]` with `fetchIntegration` imported from @sentry/cloudflare (verified working under Deno), or `globalThis.fetch = (await import('undici')).fetch` before Sentry.init (verified; costs an `undici` dependency and replaces Deno's native fetch). Guard any of these to Deno only: on Node the global fetch is already undici-backed and the NodeFetch integration would then emit a duplicate http.client span.
db spans✓* works-waNo extra instrumentation path is needed: the SDK logs `[instrumentation:mysql] Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly` and the diagnostics channel fires. But (a) `mysql2` cannot be loaded at all once Sentry is initialized: its `require('../package.json')` at connection_config.js:13 throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` through Sentry's runtime require hook (Deno's compileFunction; same class as K3 but triggered by @sentry/node's server-runtime-injection, not @sentry/deno/import). Plain Deno imports mysql2 fine. (b) With `mysql@2` a db span IS produced, but a MODULE-SCOPE pool detaches it from the request: the query arrives as its own root transaction `SELECT id, name FROM users` op `db` on a different trace id while `GET /db` has spans: []. A connection created inside the loader nests correctly: `GET /db` with spans `["db SELECT id FROM users"]`. This is the inverse of the Bun K11 rule. Static lifecycle. verified: works-after-all Both halves of the report are refuted once the app uses the DOCUMENTED React Router wiring, i.e. the `sentryReactRouter` vite plugin (build-time instrumentation), which the original probe never added. Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-reactrouter-deno-dbspans (node_modules removed after the run; package.json/package-lock.json kept). Add the plugin to vite.config.ts and mysql2 is bundled+instrumented at build time, so `require('../package.json')` never reaches Deno's require hook. deno 2.9.0, MODULE-SCOPE mysql2 pool, three consecutive requests: {"t":"transaction","n":"GET /db3","spans":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT name FROM users WHERE id > ?"],"trace":"1e51c0052e4048ec80b9cea2386959da"} {"t":"transaction","n":"GET /db3","spans":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db SELECT name FROM users WHERE id > ?"],"trace":"e3776cfa0d6d42fc8f35ce108e86c3e0"} {"t":"transaction","n":"GET /db3","spans":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db SELECT name FROM users WHERE id > ?"],"trace":"a1cfb0c356644c21bafb72a7889fd30e"} (b) The "module scope detaches / in-request nests, inverse of Bun K11" rule is wrong. A module-scope mysql@2 CONNECTION — the exact shape of the repo's own e2e app dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/react-router-7-framework-instrumentation/app/routes/performance/db-mysql.tsx — nests correctly on Deno, every request: {"t":"transaction","n":"GET /db4","spans":["db SELECT 1 + 1 AS solution","db SELECT id FROM users"],"trace":"4dca024a33924ea091409f3befceb281"} {"t":"transaction","n":"GET /db4","spans":["db SELECT 1 + 1 AS solution","db SELECT id FROM users"],"trace":"a09e71c7d5da41e094e3c14bcc9cbc85"} Only mysql@2's POOL detaches, and it is NOT a Deno or React Router property: the same bundle on node v26.5.0 detaches too, from the second request on, because @sentry/server-utils only instruments mysql's `lib/Connection.js` `query` and `Pool.query` runs it inside the `getConnection` callback, i.e. in the async context in which the pooled connection was created. Node, four consecutive `/db?mode=pool` requests (first nested, then permanently pinned to request 1's trace 2810de3b…): {"t":"transaction","n":"GET /db","spans":["db SELECT id, name FROM users"],"trace":"2810de3b02b2462fad82d02a6142ba63"} {"t":"transaction","n":"SELECT id, name FROM users","spans":[],"trace":"2810de3b02b2462fad82d02a6142ba63"} {"t":"transaction","n":"GET /db","spans":[],"trace":"87e6fa356ee44e08b0041560ec7a6564"} {"t":"transaction","n":"SELECT id, name FROM users","spans":[],"trace":"2810de3b02b2462fad82d02a6142ba63"} {"t":"transaction","n":"GET /db","spans":[],"trace":"bd5c99ef0c2f4ab1af323e15cc9578de"} On Deno the same pool pins to the pool's own creation context instead of request 1's, so it looks worse, but the defect is the driver+instrumentation shape, not the runtime. Other lifecycle: traceLifecycle 'stream' gives the identical verdict (db4 and mysql2 pool nested under http.server, mysql pool a separate segment): {"type":"span","trace_id":"fc09026c47e94ccd9efe76d506b2eaf8","items":["db SELECT","db SELECT users","http.server GET /db4"]} {"type":"span","trace_id":"9d4a0a33be9b4fffba2cde0c877aba16","items":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users","http.server GET /db3"]} {"type":"span","trace_id":"c9881ddcaa4c4ddeb311eac16e22240e","items":["db SELECT users"],"raw":[{"name":"SELECT users","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.db.mysql"}]} CAVEAT that gates the whole thing: `sentryReactRouter()` on its own produces a server bundle that cannot boot, on Deno AND on Node, with vite 5.4.21 and vite 6.4.3 alike. The orchestrion snippet pulls @sentry/server-utils' CJS build into the bundle (the plugin sets ssr.noExternal for instrumented modules + @sentry/server-utils, and the snippet sits inside CJS dependency files, so the `require` condition wins), and vite's CJS interop emits `import require$$0 from "@sentry/core"` for the still-external ESM-only core: build/server/index.js:12 import require$$0 from "@sentry/core"; SyntaxError: The requested module '@sentry/core' does not provide an export named 'default' Adding only the transitive @sentry packages to noExternal just moves it to the next ESM-only external (`lru.min` from mysql2). `ssr: { noExternal: true, external: ['@sentry/react-router', '@sentry/node'] }` is what makes it link. Exact rerun: npm install react-router@^7 @react-router/dev@^7 @react-router/node@^7 react@^19 react-dom@^19 vite@^6 isbot@^5 mysql@^2 mysql2@^3 ; npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{react-router,node,core,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry,browser,react,browser-utils,replay,replay-canvas,feedback,bundler-plugins}-10.67.0.tgz ; npx react-router build ; PORT=44321 SENTRY_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:44311/ TRACE_LIFECYCLE=static deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys server.mjs. Routes: /db4 module-scope mysql connection, /db3 module-scope mysql2 pool (?mode=fresh for per-request), /db?mode=pool|fresh|getconn|bind mysql pool variants, /sentinel. entry.server.tsx still needs renderToReadableStream and server.mjs is still a hand-written node:http adapter importing ./instrument.server.mjs first — that part of the report holds.
Workaround: Use the documented `sentryReactRouter` vite plugin so dependencies are instrumented at build time instead of through Deno's require hook, and add `ssr: { noExternal: true, external: ['@sentry/react-router', '@sentry/node'] }` to vite.config.ts so the injected snippet's CommonJS chunk does not default-import ESM-only @sentry/core. mysql2 then loads and its module-scope pool produces nested db spans. For mysql@2, use a module-scope `createConnection` rather than `createPool` (a pool detaches its queries on Node too); if a pool is required, re-enter the request span inside the callback: `const parent = Sentry.getActiveSpan(); pool.getConnection((e, c) => Sentry.withActiveSpan(parent, () => c.query(sql, cb)))`, verified to nest: {"t":"transaction","n":"GET /db","spans":["db SELECT id FROM users"],"trace":"4cbca3dd4c574d78841653f4450a14d0"}.

No page mentions the combination. `~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/` contains only index.mdx, manual-setup.mdx and profiling/, and `grep -rni deno` over that directory returns nothing; `grep -rniE 'react.router'` over `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/` (index.mdx, 232 lines, plus configuration/) likewise returns nothing. Worse, the React Router guide is actively wrong for Deno on two counts: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/index.mdx:7 categorises the guide `server-node`, and manual-setup.mdx:267-268 and :438-439 tell you to build entry.server.tsx around `createReadableStreamFromReadable` from '@react-router/node' plus `renderToPipeableStream` from 'react-dom/server' (used at :274 and :323), which is exactly the import that fails to resolve on Deno. manual-setup.mdx:413-414 give the run commands as `NODE_OPTIONS='--import ./instrument.server.mjs' react-router dev` and `... react-router-serve ./build/server/index.js`; Deno ignores NODE_OPTIONS entirely, so the only usable path is the one manual-setup.mdx:430 offers as a fallback (import the instrumentation file directly at the top of entry.server.tsx), which :449 warns leaves "automatic instrumentation incomplete". On Deno that direct import in fact gave complete server instrumentation for everything probed except fetch.

Documented: no

A React Router (framework mode) on Deno page must exist. It must say up front that the app runs on Deno but NOT with the `entry.server.tsx` the current guide shows, and give the working entry and install shape (`npm install` of react-router, the Sentry packages and the driver into a real `node_modules`). It must then document the two Deno-specific points. (1) Build-time instrumentation is required instead of the runtime require hook: add the documented `sentryReactRouter` Vite plugin, and set `ssr: { noExternal: true, external: ['@sentry/react-router', '@sentry/node'] }` in `vite.config.ts` so the injected snippet's CommonJS chunk does not default-import ESM-only `@sentry/core`. Without this, database spans are missing, because Deno cannot compile the `require('./package.json')` calls drivers such as mysql2 make at load time. (2) Outgoing requests made with Deno's built-in global `fetch` are not traced — no `http.client` span is created and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers are attached — because Deno's `fetch` is native and does not emit the undici `diagnostics_channel` events the Node SDK subscribes to, so the trace ends at the server. The verified fix that needs no extra dependency is a userland integration passed to `Sentry.init`: `defineIntegration(() => ({ name: 'DenoFetch', setupOnce() { addFetchInstrumentationHandler(d => { const client = getClient(); if (!client || isSentryRequestUrl(d.fetchData.url, client)) return; instrumentFetchRequest(...); }); } }))` from public `@sentry/core` exports. Errors, route names, isolation, incoming trace continuation and logs all work.

Headline: React Router framework mode DOES run on Deno, and @sentry/react-router (the @sentry/node-based server SDK, resolved through the `node` export condition) initializes and installs every Node integration under Deno 2.9.0. Errors, parameterized route names, isolation, incoming trace continuation and logs all work. Three things do not. 1. The docs' entry.server.tsx cannot load on Deno. `react-dom/server` resolves through react-dom's `deno` export condition to the browser build, which has no `renderToPipeableStream`. Rewriting entry.server.tsx around `renderToReadableStream` fixes it and is the single change that makes this cell viable. It also rules out `react-router-serve`, which the docs' `start` script uses. 2. mysql2 is unusable. Once Sentry is initialized, `require('../package.json')` inside mysql2/lib/connection_config.js:13 throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` in Deno's compileFunction. Same class as the established Deno K3 finding, but the trigger here is @sentry/node's own runtime require hook (server-runtime-injection), not @sentry/deno/import. Plain Deno imports mysql2 without complaint. A user following the React Router docs with mysql2 gets a hard crash at startup with no Sentry frame in the stack. `mysql@2` is unaffected. 3. Outgoing global fetch is invisible: no http.client span, no sentry-trace, no baggage. node:http client from the same loader works completely, pinning this on Deno's fetch not emitting the undici diagnostics channels (Deno K2, reconfirmed here through the framework SDK). Secondary findings worth a line in any future docs page: - A module-scope mysql pool detaches its db span from the request: the query lands as its own root transaction on a different trace id while the http.server transaction has empty spans[]. A connection created inside the loader nests correctly. This is the exact inverse of the Bun K11 rule, so a single cross-runtime docs sentence about connection placement would be wrong for one of them. - Loaders and actions produce no spans of their own here. React Router 7.18 ships a server instrumentation API and @sentry/react-router exports `createSentryServerInstrumentation` for it, but there is no visible supported way to attach it to the ServerBuild (`unstable_instrumentation` is not on the ServerBuild interface in 7.18.3); not pursued inside the time-box. All transactions therefore have empty spans[] except where an http.client or db span landed. - The SDK logs a misleading warning on Deno: "`@sentry/server-runtime-injection` was bundled into your application, so mysql2 ... load uninstrumented. Keep `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` external in your server bundle". Nothing was bundled; mysql2 is external to the SSR build. The advice is unactionable on Deno. - The error event's `transaction` field carries the raw path (`GET /iso/alpha`) while the transaction/span carries the parameterized name (`GET /iso/:tag`). - Client-side (browser) behavior was not probed at all. - Ports 41317 and 47311 were already held by other agents' recorders (they answered `{}` to every path), so probe a candidate port with curl before binding. Used 52101/52102/52103; all three processes killed and node_modules (158M) removed before returning.

REQUIRED BUILD WORKAROUND (not Deno-specific, see notes): with this dependency set `vite build` fails outright. A custom pre-plugin that makes every `@sentry/*` import external in the non-client environments, and returns a tiny virtual shim (`import * as ns from '<pkg>'; export * from '<pkg>'; export default ns;`) so the CJS `require('@sentry/server-utils')` the Sentry plugin injects into bundled drivers still gets a default export, makes the build pass. Full file: $REPRO/cells/M-tanstack-deno/app/vite.config.ts.

route names✓* works-waThe server transaction for the parameterized routes is the raw path with source `url`: `GET /api/user/42`, `GET /param/42`, `GET /users/123` — never `GET /users/$userId` / source `route`. Cause is the build workaround, not Deno: `wrapFetchWithSentry` reads a build-time constant `__SENTRY_ROUTE_PATTERNS__` that the Vite plugin string-replaces inside the SDK's own source (packages/tanstackstart-react/src/vite/routePatterns.ts:43), which only happens while @sentry/tanstackstart-react is bundled; externalizing it (the only way this build compiles here) leaves the constant undefined and parametrization silently no-ops. The identical .output run under node v26.5.0 with `node --import ./instrument.server.mjs index.mjs` gives byte-for-byte the same url-sourced names. traceLifecycle: 'static'. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. Parameterized server transaction names work on Deno 2.9.0 with @sentry/tanstackstart-react 10.67.0 (develop). The reported mechanism is right (the `__SENTRY_ROUTE_PATTERNS__` build-time constant is only substituted while the SDK goes through Vite's transform pipeline) but the conclusion is wrong on two counts: (a) it is fixed by one line of vite.config.ts, no custom plugin needed; (b) it is not Deno-specific in either direction — the broken build config gives url names under node too, and the fixed build gives route names under both. Exact change, in `vite.config.ts`, replacing the bare `nitro()` from the docs shape: import { nitro } from 'nitro/vite'; ... nitro({ noExternals: ['@sentry/tanstackstart-react'] }), That forces nitro to bundle the SDK into the server output instead of leaving it as a bare `@sentry/tanstackstart-react` import, so `sentry-tanstackstart-route-patterns` (packages/tanstackstart-react/src/vite/routePatterns.ts) actually sees `wrapFetchWithSentry` and inlines the array. The custom "externalize every @sentry/* + virtual default-export shim" pre-plugin is NOT required. It was the thing that broke route names — it is the opposite of what this SDK needs. The reported `"default" is not exported by @sentry/conventions/dist/attributes.mjs` rollup failure did not reproduce; with vite 8.2.2 the pristine config builds clean under both npm --legacy-peer-deps and there is no need to touch @sentry externals to make it compile. 2. The build fragility that presumably drove them there is a vite-version issue, not an install-manager or Deno issue. vite 7.3.2 (the version the repo's own e2e app pins) + nitro 3.0.260903-beta crashes rollup 4.63.1 with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getVariableForExportName')` here, and it does so identically under npm and under pnpm 10 with the reference app copied verbatim. vite 8.2.2 builds fine. So "vite build fails outright" is real but is fixed by moving the vite version, not by externalizing Sentry. Wider finding worth carrying forward: on the documented config the SDK ends up external in the nitro server bundle, which silently no-ops route parametrization on EVERY runtime. dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/tanstackstart-react/tests/route-parametrization.test.ts:31,60,80 asserts `GET /param/$id` / source 'route', so either CI resolves a nitro/vite combination that bundles the SDK, or that test is currently not exercising what it thinks. The build-time-constant design has no runtime fallback and emits no warning when the substitution did not happen. Workaround: Add `noExternals: ['@sentry/tanstackstart-react']` to the `nitro()` Vite plugin options: `nitro({ noExternals: ['@sentry/tanstackstart-react'] })`. Nitro then bundles the SDK into the server output instead of leaving it a bare import, so `sentryTanstackStart()`'s route-pattern plugin can substitute `__SENTRY_ROUTE_PATTERNS__` inside `wrapFetchWithSentry`. Verify it landed with `grep -l 'users/\$userId' .output/server/_libs/sentry__tanstackstart-react.mjs` before deploying. Also use vite 8.x; vite 7.3.2 with nitro 3.0.260903-beta crashes rollup during the server build regardless of Sentry.

Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-tanstack-deno-outgoingfetch/ (app node_modules removed after the run; .output/server is kept and is self-contained, so the deno runs below rerun without reinstalling). Setup (identical to the repo e2e app dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/tanstackstart-react, whose src/, vite.config.ts, tsconfig*.json I copied verbatim; only the two db routes were stubbed out and api.fetchout.ts / api.sentinel.ts added): npm install --no-audit --no-fund $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{tanstackstart-react,node,core,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry,browser,react,browser-utils,replay,replay-canvas,feedback,bundler-plugins}-10.67.0.tgz npm install --no-audit --no-fund nitro@latest node node_modules/esbuild/install.js && node node_modules/@swc/core/postinstall.js npx vite build sink.mjs on 43117 (tunnel), recorder.mjs on 43119, app on 43121. I independently hit the build failure the first agent reported, so it is real and reproducible, not an artifact of their config. With the plain documented vite.config.ts (tsConfigPaths, tanstackStart, nitro, viteReact, sentryTanstackStart) `vite build` dies in rollup (build1.log): error during build: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getVariableForExportName') at getVariableForExportNameRecursive (node_modules/rollup/dist/es/shared/node-entry.js:17045:19) My own pre-plugin (vite.config.ts, `sentryExternalShim`) that keeps every `@sentry/*` specifier external in non-client environments behind a `import * as ns from '<pkg>'; export * from '<pkg>'; export default ns;` shim makes the build pass. This is a node/vite/rollup problem, not Deno. CONTROL, same .output under node v26.5.0 (`node --import ./instrument.server.mjs index.mjs`, app-node.log) — works: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/fetchout","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","trace_id":"9b7e0f1801b24ff898f7a41bfebd970a","spans":["middleware globalRequestMiddleware","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:43119/rec"]} recorder: {"url":"/rec","sentryTrace":"9b7e0f1801b24ff898f7a41bfebd970a-a21d8cb876a92bce-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,sentry-public_key=public,sentry-trace_id=9b7e0f1801b24ff898f7a41bfebd970a,sentry-sampled=true,..."} BASELINE, deno 2.9.0, `PORT=43121 deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --allow-ffi deno-entry.mjs` (deno-entry.mjs = `import './instrument.server.mjs'; import './index.mjs';`), traceLifecycle 'static' (app-deno-base.log) — broken: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/fetchout","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","trace_id":"1ea46c9ed6d54b7184dcd122d8844721","spans":["middleware globalRequestMiddleware"]} recorder: {"url":"/rec","sentryTrace":null,"baggage":null} The server span, the tanstackstart middleware span and the sentinel event all arrive, so init and the transport are fine; only the http.client span and the propagation headers are missing. VARIANT traceLifecycle 'stream' on Deno (app-deno-stream.log) — same, still no client span: {"type":"span","trace_id":"9503c55d086c41848d124513ace7543f","items":["middleware globalRequestMiddleware","http.server GET"]} Root cause, read from the source: packages/node/src/integrations/node-fetch/index.ts calls `instrumentUndici()`, and packages/node/src/integrations/node-fetch/undici-instrumentation.ts is a vendored @opentelemetry/instrumentation-undici that only subscribes to the `undici:request:*` diagnostics channels. Deno's `fetch` is the native Rust implementation and never publishes those channels, so nothing fires. No init option, entry shape, trace lifecycle or Deno flag can change that — there is no other hook point in the node SDK for the global `fetch`. REFUTED PARTIALLY by a userland integration (not shipped, not documented): re-implementing @sentry/cloudflare's `fetchIntegration` on top of primitives @sentry/core already exports (`addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest`, which patch `globalThis.fetch`) restores both the span and the headers on Deno. Files: .output/server/deno-fetch-integration.mjs, .output/server/instrument.fetchfix.mjs, .output/server/deno-entry-fetchfix.mjs. static (app-deno-fetchfix-static.log): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/fetchout","op":"http.server","status":"ok","trace_id":"f8e0a54e7ea44c5280007ab146b580e2","spans":["middleware globalRequestMiddleware","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:43119/rec"]} recorder: {"url":"/rec","sentryTrace":"f8e0a54e7ea44c5280007ab146b580e2-b591d3b9aa05a293-1","baggage":"...sentry-trace_id=f8e0a54e7ea44c5280007ab146b580e2,sentry-sampled=true..."} stream (app-deno-fetchfix-stream.log): {"type":"span","trace_id":"7e4595f5e1b6420f978fec414a3a6d14","items":["middleware globalRequestMiddleware","http.client GET 127.0.0.1","http.server GET"],"raw":[...{"name":"GET 127.0.0.1","parent_span_id":"8e01428cf66907ce","origin":"auto.http.fetch"}...]} The client span is correctly parented under the server segment and carries the same trace id, so the OTel context propagation into `startInactiveSpan` works on Deno; only the channel-based trigger is missing. TanStack Start is not implicated anywhere: the framework's own request/function middleware spans and route handling behave the same on both runtimes. Rerun: `cd <probe>/.output/server && PORT=43121 RECORDER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:43119/rec deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --allow-ffi deno-entry.mjs` (broken) vs `... deno-entry-fetchfix.mjs` (works), with `PORT=43117 node ../../sink.mjs` and `PORT=43119 node ../../recorder.mjs` running.
Workaround: Add a global-fetch integration in instrument.server.mjs, built from primitives @sentry/core already exports (this is a copy of @sentry/cloudflare's shipped `fetchIntegration`): import { addFetchInstrumentationHandler, defineIntegration, getClient, instrumentFetchRequest, isSentryRequestUrl, LRUMap, shouldPropagateTraceForUrl } from '@sentry/core'; const denoFetchIntegration = defineIntegration(() => { const headersUrlMap = new LRUMap(100); const spans = {}; return { name: 'DenoGlobalFetch', setupOnce() { addFetchInstrumentationHandler(handlerData => { const client = getClient(); if (!client || isSentryRequestUrl(handlerData.fetchData.url, client)) return; instrumentFetchRequest(handlerData, () => true, url => shouldPropagateTraceForUrl(url, client.getOptions().tracePropagationTargets, headersUrlMap), spans, { spanOrigin: 'auto.http.fetch' }); }); }}; }); Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1, integrations: [denoFetchIntegration()] }); Verified on Deno with both traceLifecycle 'static' and 'stream'. The proper SDK fix is for @sentry/node to fall back to this globalThis.fetch patching when the undici diagnostics channels never fire (non-undici runtimes: Deno, and Bun's native fetch), rather than leaving it to userland. Separately, building this app at all needs a vite pre-plugin that externalizes `@sentry/*` in the non-client environments and gives each one a default export; without it `vite build` fails in rollup with "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getVariableForExportName')" on node too. Full file at <probe>/vite.config.ts.
db spans✓ worksA module-scope `mysql.createConnection` to 127.0.0.1:3307 queried from GET /api/db-mysql produced a nested `db SELECT id, name FROM users` span inside the http.server transaction. No Deno import hook and no @sentry/deno were needed or used. traceLifecycle: 'static'.

Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions TanStack Start on Deno. `grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/tanstackstart-react/` returns nothing, and `grep -rni tanstack docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/` returns nothing. The TanStack Start guide is Node-only by construction: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/tanstackstart-react/manual-setup/index.mdx:9 tags it `server-node`, :300 heads the recommended section "With `--import` Flag (e.g. Node.js Server)", and :372 gives the start script `node --import ./.output/server/instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`, a flag Deno does not have. The only alternative the page offers (:383-389, "when you can't configure Node.js CLI flags") explicitly instruments native Node APIs only. So a user on Deno has no documented init placement; the two-line `deno-entry.mjs` above is what a Deno page would have to show.

Documented: no

A TanStack Start on Deno page must exist. It must say the Nitro `node` output runs under Deno and that errors, per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, database spans and logs all work, and it must replace the Node-only `node --import …` start command at :369-376 with the Deno equivalent. Two build-shape facts must be documented because neither is discoverable. (1) Server route parametrization (`GET /users/$userId` rather than `GET /users/123`) requires `@sentry/tanstackstart-react` to be bundled into the Nitro server build, because the Vite plugin injects the route patterns by transforming the SDK's own source; if the build externalizes the SDK the names stay raw. The verified fix is `nitro({ noExternals: ['@sentry/tanstackstart-react'] })` in `vite.config.ts` (with Vite 8), alongside `tanstackStart()` and `sentryTanstackStart()`. (2) On Deno the server SDK does not instrument outgoing `fetch()` — no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers — so the trace stops at the server boundary. The page must ship the global-fetch integration for `instrument.server.mjs`, built from primitives `@sentry/core` already exports (`addFetchInstrumentationHandler`, `defineIntegration`, `getClient`, `instrumentFetchRequest`, `isSentryRequestUrl`, `LRUMap`, `shouldPropagateTraceForUrl`) — the same body `@sentry/cloudflare` ships as its `fetchIntegration`. It should also note the install shape the run needed: a single `npm install` of all Sentry tarballs plus an explicit `npm install nitro@latest`.

- TanStack Start's nitro node output runs on Deno 2.9 unmodified: SSR page routes, file-based API routes, `$id` params and thrown-error 500s all behave the same as on node v26.5.0. Deno reports itself as `runtime: {name: "node", version: "v26.3.0"}` in Sentry events. - @sentry/node's runtime instrumentation works on Deno through `Module.registerHooks()` (the SDK logs "Registered diagnostics-channel injection via Module.registerHooks()"), and the eager Bun/Deno channel subscriptions fire. This is why the mysql span appears without any @sentry/deno import hook. - Biggest finding, and it is NOT Deno-specific: with this dependency set (npm-installed 10.67.0 tarballs + nitro 3.0.260903-beta + vite 7.3.2 + rollup 4.63.1) `vite build` of the standard tanstackstart-react app fails. Nitro's SSR rollup pass resolves @sentry/* to their CJS builds while resolving what those files `require()` to ESM, so rollup-plugin-commonjs emits `import require$$0 from "@sentry/conventions/attributes"` / `"@sentry/core"` against ESM files with no default export. Contributing factor: `@sentry/tanstackstart-react`'s `exports["."]` map has only `workerd`/`worker`/`browser`/`node` conditions and no `default`, so a bundler environment that matches none of them falls back to the CJS `main`. Nitro also warns `vite@7.3.2 is installed but the vite builder requires ^8`. - A second, independent build defect surfaces once @sentry/* is external: the Sentry Vite plugin's build-time driver instrumentation injects a CJS `require('@sentry/server-utils')` into the bundled `mysql`, which rollup turns into a default import of an ESM-only package and throws at runtime ("does not provide an export named 'default'"). The virtual shim in vite.config.ts is what fixes it. - Consequence of that externalization: `__SENTRY_ROUTE_PATTERNS__` is never substituted, so route parametrization is dead. It is worth checking whether a supported pnpm install of the e2e app still parametrizes on nitro 3.0.260903-beta; I could not test the unmodified config because it does not build here. - Not probed for lack of time: `traceLifecycle: 'stream'`, server functions (`createServerFn`) spans, the managed tunnel route, and the client-side SDK. All results above are `traceLifecycle: 'static'`. - All processes killed (ports 41997/41998/41999 free); app/node_modules removed (199M reclaimed), .output kept.

Remix on Deno M-remix-deno

Remix v2 (2.17.x, Remix Vite plugin, custom node:http server via `createRequestHandler` from `@remix-run/server-runtime`) · Deno 2.9.0, `nodeModulesDir: "manual"`, npm-produced node_modules · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Remix runs on Deno unchanged. Wiring that a docs page would have to show:

1. Install with npm under node (not `deno add`, not `bun add`), so the tarballs' transitive `@sentry/*@10.67.0` deps resolve:
   `npm install --legacy-peer-deps $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{remix,node,core,react,browser,browser-utils,replay,replay-canvas,feedback,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry}-10.67.0.tgz '@remix-run/dev@^2.17.0' '@remix-run/node@^2.17.0' '@remix-run/react@^2.17.0' '@remix-run/server-runtime@^2.17.0' react react-dom vite@^5 mysql2 typescript`
2. `deno.json`: `{ "nodeModulesDir": "manual" }`.
3. `vite.config.ts`: `plugins: [remix(), sentryRemixVitePlugin()]` (from `@remix-run/dev` and `@sentry/remix`). The plugin runs at build time under node and prints `[Sentry Remix] Found 5 static and 3 dynamic routes`; the emitted route manifest is what makes parameterized transaction names work at runtime.
4. `app/entry.server.tsx`: `export const handleError = Sentry.sentryHandleError;`
5. `instrument.server.mjs`: `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/remix'; Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' | 'stream' })`.
6. Server entry: `import './instrument.server.mjs'` first, then `createRequestHandler(Sentry.instrumentBuild(build), 'production')` over `node:http`. Do NOT use `@remix-run/express` / express on Deno — express dies at import on Deno via the known `require('*.json')` bug once the Sentry runtime hook is installed.
7. Build under node: `npx remix vite:build`. Run under Deno: `deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys server.mjs`.

CAVEAT that must be in any such docs page: any CommonJS dependency that does `require('*.json')` (mysql2 does, `mysql2/lib/connection_config.js:13`) must be imported BEFORE `./instrument.server.mjs`, otherwise the process dies at startup. That inverts the usual "instrument first" rule.
