ORDERING RULE I found while testing (worth its own docs line, and it is the thing that would have bitten anyone who put the call in the server entry instead): if `installGlobals()` is called in the server entry rather than entry.server.tsx, it must run AFTER `import './instrument.server.mjs'`. Reproduced with server-flex.mjs + probe.sh: ./probe.sh runD 44333 after 0 -> works, exactly like runG ./probe.sh runC 44332 after 1 -> works ({ nativeFetch: true }, undici globals) ./probe.sh runF 44335 before 0 -> BROKEN. Errors still arrive, but NOT ONE transaction or span envelope is emitted for the whole process, and the outgoing header degrades to a bare propagation context with no sampling decision: {"url":"/fetch","sentryTrace":"54763d3c034e4ea495f3a2f5867c8024-bc4f961a41f22d98","baggage":"sentry-environment=probe,sentry-public_key=public,sentry-trace_id=54763d3c034e4ea495f3a2f5867c8024"} runB (before + nativeFetch:true) is the same failure with `sentry-sampled=false` in baggage. This is the ordinary "Sentry.init first" rule, not an inversion of it — the mysql2 `require('*.json')` caveat (K3) still forces the db module before init, so the working order is: db module -> instrument.server.mjs -> installGlobals(). Not related to the capability but observed: `axios` in a loader on Deno produced neither a request at the recorder nor a span (runA, /out?kind=axios); the request never left the process. Separate issue, not chased. Processes: sink (44311), recorder2 (44312) and every deno server were killed at the end.
Workaround: No workaround needed — this is the framework's own required wiring, not a patch. In `app/entry.server.tsx` add `import { installGlobals } from '@remix-run/node';` and call `installGlobals();` at module top level (this is what `npx remix reveal` generates and what every Remix e2e app in this repo already does). Nothing in the server entry, the Vite config or `Sentry.init()` changes, and no extra dependency is required (`installGlobals()` with no options uses `@remix-run/web-fetch`, already a dep of `@remix-run/node`; `installGlobals({ nativeFetch: true })` works equally well). If you prefer to call it from the custom server entry instead, it must come after `import './instrument.server.mjs'`.
db spans✓* works-waWorks, but only with a non-canonical import order. mysql2 ships its own `diagnostics_channel` instrumentation (`mysql2/lib/tracing.js`), which the SDK subscribes to eagerly on Deno, so no instrumentation path is needed at all: no `@sentry/deno/import` hook, no esbuild/orchestrion plugin, no bundler plugin. With mysql2 imported BEFORE `instrument.server.mjs` a module-scope pool yields `db mysql2.pool.connect`, `db mysql2.connect`, `db SELECT id, name FROM users` (static) / `db SELECT users` (stream) nested under the route transaction. With the canonical order (instrument first, driver after) the process dies at startup: `@sentry/server-runtime-injection`'s module hook makes Deno reject mysql2's `require('../package.json')` with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'`, the same class as known finding K3. The SDK also prints a false-positive warning claiming the injection package was bundled, which it was not. verified: works-after-all REFUTED the "only with a non-canonical import order" part. db spans (and route transactions and errors) work with the canonical order — `import './instrument.server.mjs'` first, mysql2 loaded strictly after `Sentry.init()` — if the server entry is bundled with the Sentry orchestrion esbuild plugin and the runtime module hook is turned off with `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false`. Exact change (two parts, both required): 1. build the server entry with build-time channel injection instead of the runtime hook: `import { sentryOrchestrionPlugin } from '@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild'` in an esbuild build of `server.mjs` (bundle: true, platform node, format esm, external `['@sentry/*','mysql2','react','react-dom','react-dom/server']`, banner `import { createRequire as __sentryCreateRequire } from 'node:module'; const require = __sentryCreateRequire(import.meta.url);`). The banner is mandatory: without it the bundle dies at boot with `Error: Dynamic require of "@sentry/server-utils" is not supported` (runC.log), because the injected snippet inside transformed CJS files uses `require` and esbuild's ESM output has none. 2. `Sentry.init({ ..., enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false })`, which stops `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` from registering `Module.registerHooks` — the hook is what makes Deno reject mysql2's `require('../package.json')` (K3). Evidence, all from my own sink at 127.0.0.1:46311. A) dist-lazy bundle (mysql2 loaded via `await import('mysql2/promise')` AFTER init), injection OFF, static — runH-injectOFF.log: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET db","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.remix","spans":["function LOADER root","function LOADER routes/db","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["function LOADER root","function LOADER routes/users.$id"]} {"type":"event","exception":"Error: probe-loader-boom-7","mechanism":"auto.function.remix.server","handled":false,"transaction":"GET /boom/7"} This is the strongest form: the driver genuinely loads after `Sentry.init()`, so the ordering rule the other agent reported is gone, not hidden. B) Same bundle shape with a module-scope pool (dist-server2), stream lifecycle — runE.log: {"type":"span","items":["function LOADER root","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users","function LOADER routes/db","http.server GET db"],"raw":[{"name":"mysql2.pool.connect","origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel"},...]} Static variant (runD.log) gives the same `GET db` transaction with the three db children. C) Why the hook, not the order, is the defect — dist-lazy bundle with injection ON (default init), runG-injectON.log: [Sentry] `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` was bundled into your application, so mysql2 ... (false positive; it is external here) SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':' at Object.compileFunction (ext:core/01_core.js:1106:31) at Object.<anonymous> (.../node_modules/mysql2/lib/connection_config.js:13:21) D) The obvious one-line "fix" does NOT work on its own — unbundled `server.mjs` + `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false` (runB.log, runI-unbundled-off-stream.log): the process boots, but the sink receives ZERO transactions and ZERO spans, only events. Debug shows `Http.Server Handling incoming request` and no `[Tracing] Starting sampled root span`. Root cause read in the worktree: `packages/remix/src/server/integrations/http.ts:14` sets `disableIncomingRequestSpans: true`, so on Remix the whole server span tree (and with it every db child) comes from the `@remix-run/server-runtime` orchestrion channels — kill runtime injection without replacing it at build time and you lose all tracing. In that state mysql2 produced no db spans either, in static or stream, which also qualifies the other agent's "no instrumentation path is needed at all" claim for mysql2 3.24.3. E) Side observation: with a module-scope pool the bundled entry also boots with injection ON (runF1.log) and records db spans, but only because esbuild hoists the external `import 'mysql2/promise'` above the init body — accidental, and it breaks again the moment the driver is imported lazily (C). So the hoisting is not a recipe. Not reproduced/negative paths: `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false` alone (D). Deno's `--import` hook variant was not retried because it installs the same `Module.registerHooks` transform that crashes in (C). Files (all absolute, in $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-remix-deno-dbspans/): README-rerun.txt, build-server2.mjs, build-lazy.mjs, server.mjs, server-lazy.mjs, db.mjs, db-lazy.mjs, instrument.server.mjs, vite.config.ts, sink.mjs, logs runB..runI. All processes I started were killed.
Workaround: Keep `import './instrument.server.mjs'` as the first line of the server entry and instead of relying on the runtime module hook, bundle the entry with build-time channel injection and switch the hook off: // instrument.server.mjs import * as Sentry from '@sentry/remix'; Sentry.init({ dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' | 'stream', enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false }); // build-server.mjs (run under node, after `npx remix vite:build`) import * as esbuild from 'esbuild'; import { sentryOrchestrionPlugin } from '@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild'; await esbuild.build({ entryPoints: ['./server.mjs'], outfile: './dist-server/server.mjs', bundle: true, platform: 'node', format: 'esm', target: 'node20', external: ['@sentry/*', 'mysql2', 'react', 'react-dom', 'react-dom/server'], banner: { js: "import { createRequire as __sentryCreateRequire } from 'node:module';\nconst require = __sentryCreateRequire(import.meta.url);" }, plugins: [sentryOrchestrionPlugin()], }); Run: `deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys dist-server/server.mjs`. `@remix-run/server-runtime` must be bundled (not external) — that is where the transform lands; mysql2 may stay external because 3.20+ publishes its own diagnostics channels, and @sentry/* must stay external. The old workaround (import the driver before instrument, no bundler) still works but is no longer the only option.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info('probe-log-from-loader', { where: 'remix-deno' })` in a loader arrived as a log envelope item `info: probe-log-from-loader` after the ~7s flush timer. Static lifecycle.

Time-box respected; scaffold reused the Remix app from $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-remix-bun-dbspans (app/, tsconfig, db.mjs) and the Deno adapter shape from $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-reactrouter-deno-outgoingfetch. All processes killed (appA-appH, sink, recorder, plain); node_modules deleted (dir is now 908K). Findings worth flagging beyond the per-capability verdicts: 1. NEW: the "instrument first" ordering that every Sentry docs page teaches is actively harmful for Remix on Deno. `@sentry/server-runtime-injection`'s module hook makes Deno's CJS loader reject `require('*.json')` (`SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'`), so any driver that reads its own package.json (mysql2 does) crashes the process at import if it is loaded after `Sentry.init`. This is the K3 bug reached through @sentry/node rather than through `@sentry/deno/import`. Deno bug denoland/deno#36240, but the SDK is what triggers it. 2. NEW: on Deno the SDK prints "`@sentry/server-runtime-injection` was bundled into your application, so mysql2 ... load uninstrumented" for an entry that is not bundled at all (plain .mjs, real node_modules). The advice in that warning is wrong for this runtime, and it appears immediately before the crash in 1., which will send users down the wrong path. 3. NEW: db spans need no instrumentation path on Deno. mysql2 ships native diagnostics_channel support (`mysql2/lib/tracing.js`) and the SDK's Bun/Deno "subscribing eagerly" branch picks it up, so neither the `@sentry/deno/import` hook nor an esbuild/orchestrion plugin is required. That also means the injection hook buys nothing for mysql2 on Deno while costing the crash in 1. 4. NEW: the obvious userland fix for the missing-fetch-span gap (wiring core's `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest` in a custom integration) propagates `sentry-trace`/`baggage` correctly but silently suppresses every server transaction/span for the whole process. Debug output shows the `http.server` root span is never finished. Worth an SDK issue on its own; it is the workaround a user would most plausibly reach for. 5. Confirms K2 (no fetch span, no trace headers on Deno) for the @sentry/node-based framework SDKs, not just @sentry/deno. 6. `@remix-run/express` was deliberately not used: express hits K3 at import on Deno once the Sentry hook is installed. A `node:http` + `createRequestHandler(Sentry.instrumentBuild(build))` custom server is the only shape that works, and it is undocumented for Remix outside Cloudflare/Hydrogen. 7. Both traceLifecycle values behave the same for every capability tested; stream additionally names the segment span `http.server GET users/:id` with `is_segment: true`, and the db span is the low-cardinality `SELECT users` instead of `SELECT id, name FROM users`. 8. Client-side (browser) Sentry was not probed; the cell is about the server runtime.

SolidStart on Deno M-solidstart-deno

SolidStart 2 (@solidjs/start 2.0.2, nitro 3.0.260610-beta, vite 8) · deno 2.9.0 running the node-server nitro build output (.output/server/index.mjs) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Build on node, run the output on Deno. No Deno-specific SDK package is involved: @sentry/solidstart pulls in @sentry/node and that runs on Deno.

1. Packages (npm, --legacy-peer-deps is required because @sentry/nitro's peer range `nitro@">=3.0.0-0 <4.0.0 || 3.0.260311-beta || 3.0.260415-beta"` does not accept nitro 3.0.260610-beta under npm's prerelease semver rules):
   npm install --legacy-peer-deps @solidjs/start@2.0.2 @solidjs/router solid-js@1.9.14 vite@^8 vite-plugin-solid nitro@3.0.260610-beta mysql2 \
     $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{solidstart,core,nitro,node,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry,solid,browser,browser-utils,replay,replay-canvas,feedback,bundler-plugins}-10.67.0.tgz

2. vite.config.ts:
   import { sentrySolidStart } from '@sentry/solidstart/vite';
   import { solidStart } from '@solidjs/start/config';
   import { nitro } from 'nitro/vite';
   export default defineConfig({ plugins: [solidStart({ appRoot: './src' }), sentrySolidStart({ sourcemaps: { disable: true } }), nitro({ serverDir: './server' })] });

3. Init placement: a Nitro startup plugin, server/plugins/sentry.ts:
   import * as Sentry from '@sentry/solidstart';
   import { definePlugin } from 'nitro';
   export default definePlugin(() => { Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' }); });
   No --import preload, no instrument file: sentrySolidStart's orchestrion pass bakes the library instrumentation into the bundle at build time, which is exactly why mysql2 spans still work under Deno.

4. Build with node: NODE_ENV=production npx vite build  (NODE_ENV must be production, the plugin skips the orchestrion pass in development).
5. Run with Deno: PORT=<port> HOST=127.0.0.1 deno run -A .output/server/index.mjs  -> "➜ Listening on: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/".
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors◐ partialAn error thrown from an API route handler (src/routes/api/error.ts) never reaches Sentry: the request transaction arrives with status internal_error and the client gets HTTP 500, but no event envelope is produced (verified with a sentinel captureMessage that arrived afterwards). SolidStart/Nitro swallows the throw; this is not Deno-specific, the same .output under node behaves identically. Manual Sentry.captureException inside a handler works and the event carries request data, transaction name, stack frames with context lines and mechanism generic/handled=true. static lifecycle. verified: partial Reproduced and then narrowed the claim on deno 2.9.0 running the node-server nitro output of a SolidStart 2 app (@solidjs/start 2.0.2, nitro 3.0.260610-beta, vite 8, develop SDK 10.67.0). Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-solidstart-deno-errors/ (app/ holds src, server/plugins/sentry.ts, vite.config.ts; .output/ kept, node_modules removed). Build: `cd app && npm install --legacy-peer-deps && NODE_ENV=production npx vite build`. Run: `PORT=<p> HOST=127.0.0.1 SENTRY_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:47901/ deno run -A .output/server/index.mjs`. Sink: `PORT=47901 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs`. Every run ended with a `/api/sentinel` captureMessage sentinel and waited for it in the sink. 1) BASELINE — claim CONFIRMED. Documented wiring exactly as the repo's own e2e app solidstart-2 (nitro startup plugin for Sentry.init, `sentrySolidStart()` in vite.config, `src/middleware.ts` with `sentryBeforeResponseMiddleware()` registered via `solidStart({ appRoot: './src', middleware: './src/middleware.ts' })`). A throw from `src/routes/api/error.ts` still produces no event (r3-baseline.log, sink): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/error","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"internal_error","trace_id":"ec5aa74772fe475fac9a56a5eeacd4b2","sdk":"sentry.javascript.solidstart","spans":["http.server GET /api/error","middleware GET /api/error","http.server GET /api/error"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/error-async","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"internal_error","trace_id":"77db87b5240c470aa35db5d2b5f9bff9",...} {"type":"event","message":"sentinel","mechanism":"generic","handled":true,"sdk":"sentry.javascript.solidstart","transaction":"GET /api/sentinel",...} No error event before the sentinel. `sentryBeforeResponseMiddleware()` does not help: its source only injects trace meta tags into text/html bodies. 2) ROOT CAUSE ISOLATED. `@sentry/nitro`'s server plugin IS in the bundle (`.output/server/_libs/@sentry/nitro.mjs:844: nitroApp.hooks.hook("error", captureErrorHook)`), but Nitro never emits that hook here. Registering my own `nitroApp.hooks.hook('error', ...)` in the same startup plugin (PROBE_NITRO_HOOK=1) produced nothing either — sink for that run held only the two transactions and the sentinel. The h3/srvx tracing channels in `captureTracingEvents.ts` do declare `captureError: () => ({ mechanism: { handled: false, type: 'auto.http.nitro.onTraceError' } })`, but SolidStart 2's SSR handler converts the throw into a 500 Response inside h3 (the app log shows h3 wrapping it as `{ status: 500, unhandled: true, cause: Error: solidstart-deno route error }` and console-logging it), so the traced promise resolves and no captureError fires. Not Deno-specific; the sibling bun probe sees the same shape. 3) WORKS AFTER ALL for the documented server-function path. `withServerActionInstrumentation` on a `'use server'` function is captured on Deno with full fidelity, matching the repo's own e2e assertion in dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/solidstart-2/tests/errors.server.test.ts: {"type":"event","exception":"Error: solidstart-deno server action error","mechanism":"auto.function.solidstart","handled":false,"sdk":"sentry.javascript.solidstart","runtime":"node","hasContextLine":true,"transaction":"GET /server-error","trace_id":"ac657f7b60a94f08b8b7b35c1ffe7874","request":{"url":"http://127.0.0.1:47913/server-error","method":"GET"},"environment":"production"} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /server-error","op":"http.server","status":"internal_error","trace_id":"ac657f7b60a94f08b8b7b35c1ffe7874","spans":["http.server GET /server-error","middleware GET /server-error","http.server GET /server-error","function getPrefecture"]} 4) WORKAROUND VERIFIED for API routes. A user-written SolidStart middleware handler that try/catches `next()` captures the throw with correct trace linkage, request data, `handled:false` and stack context lines, for both sync and async handlers, and under both trace lifecycles. static (r3-mw.log): {"type":"event","exception":"Error: solidstart-deno route error","mechanism":"probe.solidstart.middleware","handled":false,"sdk":"sentry.javascript.solidstart","runtime":"node","hasContextLine":true,"transaction":"GET /api/error","trace_id":"fc47096b412f460aae7f93171f5d29db","request":{"url":"http://127.0.0.1:47911/api/error","method":"GET"},"environment":"production"} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/error","op":"http.server","status":"internal_error","trace_id":"fc47096b412f460aae7f93171f5d29db",...} <- same trace_id {"type":"event","exception":"Error: solidstart-deno route error async","mechanism":"probe.solidstart.middleware","handled":false,"transaction":"GET /api/error-async","trace_id":"ea5bd973c1fa438d86c8492fe744fbb8",...} stream (r3-mw-stream.log): {"type":"event","exception":"Error: solidstart-deno route error","mechanism":"probe.solidstart.middleware","handled":false,"hasContextLine":true,"transaction":"GET /api/error","trace_id":"95f654598b24479f979717ea1254be81",...} 5) VARIANTS THAT DID NOT HELP: `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` (baseline still silent), registering the Nitro `error` hook by hand, adding `src/middleware.ts` with only `sentryBeforeResponseMiddleware()`, moving init into the Nitro startup plugin vs. leaving it where it was (both identical). `@sentry/solidstart`'s server entry exports only `init`, `withServerActionInstrumentation` and `sentryBeforeResponseMiddleware` on top of `@sentry/node` — there is no SDK-provided API-route or request-handler wrapper to reach for. So: the reported break is real and is an SDK/framework-integration gap in @sentry/nitro + @sentry/solidstart on SolidStart 2, not a Deno defect, and it is not total — the officially covered server-error path works on Deno, and one small user-land middleware closes the API-route hole. Also seen incidentally: a stale `.output` whose externals were missing (node_modules removed) surfaced `Error: Cannot find module 'sql-escaper'` captured as `auto.http.nitro.onTraceError`, which shows the h3 captureError path itself is live and would fire if the throw ever reached it.
Workaround: Add a wrapping handler to `src/middleware.ts` and register it with `solidStart({ appRoot: './src', middleware: './src/middleware.ts' })`. Verified file at .../deep/verify4-M-solidstart-deno-errors/FIX-middleware-verified.ts: import * as Sentry from '@sentry/solidstart'; import { createMiddleware } from '@solidjs/start/middleware'; export default createMiddleware([ async (event, next) => { try { return await next(); } catch (error) { Sentry.captureException(error, { mechanism: { handled: false, type: 'solidstart.middleware' } }); throw error; } }, ...createMiddleware({ onBeforeResponse: [Sentry.sentryBeforeResponseMiddleware()] }), ]); The spread keeps `sentryBeforeResponseMiddleware()` (trace meta tags for distributed tracing on pageloads) alongside the catch handler. For `'use server'` functions, `withServerActionInstrumentation` already captures automatically and needs no workaround.
route names✗ brokenstatic lifecycle: the transaction for /api/users/42 is named "GET /api/users/42" with transaction_info.source = "url", i.e. the raw path, not the /api/users/:id route pattern (same on node, so it is a SolidStart/Nitro gap, not a Deno one). stream lifecycle is worse: the server span is named "GET" (method only) with no source attribute at all, so the path is gone entirely. verified: confirmed-broken CONFIRMED, and I found the exact mechanism plus a working user-land fix (see workaround). Also one correction to the original report. ROOT CAUSE (read off the build output, not inferred): SolidStart 2 registers exactly ONE Nitro/h3 route and does all of its own routing inside it. In `.output/server/index.mjs` the whole app is: var findRoute = (() => { const data = { route: "/**", handler: wrapHandlerWithTracing(_lazy_j3rF0K) }; ... })(); (the only other entries are `/_build/assets/**` and any real `server/` routes). h3 therefore sets `event.context.matchedRoute = { route: "/**" }`, and `@sentry/nitro`'s `getParameterizedRoute()` (packages/nitro/src/runtime/hooks/captureTracingEvents.ts:81) explicitly drops `'/**'` as a useless catch-all -> no route, so the srvx segment keeps the raw-URL name. Proved at runtime from inside a SolidStart API route (`src/routes/api/w4/[id].ts` dumps the h3 event): {"id":"42","w":4,"nativeKeys":["app","req","url","context"],"ctxKeys":["nitro","params","matchedRoute","routeRules","_sentryServerTimingSet","solidFetchEvent"],"matchedRoute":{"route":"/**","keys":["route","handler"]}} SolidStart's own matcher (`matchAPIRoute` in the ssr bundle) knows `"path": "/api/users/:id"` but returns only `{handler, params, isPage}` and writes just `event.params` — it never surfaces the pattern to h3, and `@sentry/solidstart` has no instrumentation of SolidStart's router. CONTROL RUN (documented wiring, no workarounds; deno 2.9.0, traceLifecycle 'static'), sink verbatim: {"name":"GET /api/users/42","source":"url"} {"name":"GET /users/7","source":"url"} {"name":"GET /api/sentinel","source":"url"} {"name":"GET /api/nusers/:id","source":"route"} <- real Nitro route, see below Same run on node 26.5.0, identical: {"name":"GET /api/users/42","source":"url"} {"name":"GET /users/7","source":"url"} Both page routes (`src/routes/users/[id].tsx`) and API routes (`src/routes/api/users/[id].ts`) are affected, so this is a SolidStart+Nitro SDK gap, not a Deno one — confirmed. STREAM LIFECYCLE control (segment spans only shown, key `sentry.segment.name.source`): {"name":"GET","op":"http.server","src":"url","seg":true} <- /api/users/42 {"name":"GET","op":"http.server","src":"url","seg":true} <- /users/7 CORRECTION to the report: the streamed segment span DOES carry a source attribute, `sentry.segment.name.source: "url"`. The "no source attribute at all" reading is an artifact of the shared sink, which maps `attributes['sentry.source']` (an old key) rather than `sentry.segment.name.source`. The method-only name "GET" is by design (`HTTP_SPAN_NAME_FALLBACK` / low-cardinality rule) once the route is unknown, so the streaming case is the same single defect, not a second, worse one. THE NITRO LAYER ITSELF IS FINE. I added a real Nitro server route `app/server/api/nusers/[id].ts` (picked up by `nitro({ serverDir: './server' })`, registered as `route: "/api/nusers/:id"`). It is named correctly on both runtimes and both lifecycles, with no user code: static: {"name":"GET /api/nusers/:id","source":"route"} stream: {"name":"GET /api/nusers/:id","op":"http.server","src":"route","route":"/api/nusers/:id","seg":true} So `@sentry/nitro`'s h3 hook works; only routes owned by SolidStart's file router are unnamed. WHAT I TRIED AND REJECTED: no init placement, entry shape, lifecycle, or build flag changes this — the route pattern never reaches h3, so nothing the SDK subscribes to can see it. There is no SDK option to supply it. REPO E2E REFERENCE: the SDK's own app agrees with the broken behavior — `dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/solidstart-2/tests/performance.server.test.ts:6` asserts `transactionEvent?.transaction === 'GET /users/6'`, i.e. the raw URL for the `src/routes/users/[id].tsx` route. The shipped e2e suite encodes the URL naming as expected, so this will not be caught by CI. PROBE FILES (rerunnable; `app/.output/` is kept and self-contained, `node_modules` removed): $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-solidstart-deno-routenames/app/{vite.config.ts,package.json} .../app/src/middleware.ts, .../app/src/app.tsx, .../app/src/routes/api/{users,w1,w2,w3,w4}/[id].ts, .../app/src/routes/users/[id].tsx, .../app/server/{plugins/sentry.ts,api/nusers/[id].ts} logs: .../run-static.log, run-static-ctrl.log, run-stream-ctrl.log, run-stream-fix.log, run-static-direct.log, run-node-ctrl.log, raw-stream-ctrl.json, raw-stream-fix2.json, build-v1.log, build-v2.log COMMANDS: npm install --legacy-peer-deps <deps + $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-*.tgz> (as in the original report) cd app && NODE_ENV=production npx vite build PORT=41599 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs & PORT=41611 HOST=127.0.0.1 SENTRY_TUNNEL=http://127.0.0.1:41599/ SENTRY_LIFECYCLE=static [SENTRY_MW_ROUTE=off SENTRY_PAGE_ROUTE=off|direct] deno run -A .output/server/index.mjs curl the endpoints, then curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:41599/__items?raw=1'
Workaround: Two small pieces of user code restore parameterized names on both runtimes and BOTH lifecycles. Verified end to end. 1) API routes — one global SolidStart middleware. `event.params` is populated by SolidStart before `onBeforeResponse`, so the pattern can be rebuilt from it: // src/middleware.ts (register with solidStart({ middleware: './src/middleware.ts' })) import { setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute } from '@sentry/server-utils'; import { createMiddleware } from '@solidjs/start/middleware'; export default createMiddleware({ onBeforeResponse: [(event) => { const params = event.params; if (!params || !Object.keys(params).length) return; const byValue = new Map(Object.entries(params).map(([k, v]) => [String(v), k])); const pattern = new URL(event.request.url).pathname.split('/') .map(s => (byValue.has(s) ? `:${byValue.get(s)}` : s)).join('/'); setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute(pattern); }], }); 2) SSR page routes — call the same helper from the Router root during SSR, where `useCurrentMatches()` knows the pattern: // src/app.tsx import { setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute } from '@sentry/server-utils'; import { Router, useCurrentMatches } from '@solidjs/router'; import { isServer } from 'solid-js/web'; function Root(props) { const matches = useCurrentMatches(); if (isServer) { const last = matches()[matches().length - 1]; const pattern = last?.route?.pattern || last?.route?.originalPath; if (pattern) setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute(pattern); } return <Suspense>{props.children}</Suspense>; } Results with both in place — static lifecycle: {"name":"GET /api/users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","spans":["http.server GET /api/users/42","middleware GET /api/users/42","http.server GET /api/users/42"]} {"name":"GET /users/:id","source":"route"} stream lifecycle (segment spans): {"name":"GET /api/users/:id","op":"http.server","src":"route","route":"/api/users/:id","seg":true} {"name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","src":"route","route":"/users/:id","seg":true} Notes and cheaper variants: - `setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute` is exported from `@sentry/server-utils` (a transitive dep of `@sentry/solidstart`); it is NOT re-exported from `@sentry/solidstart`, so the app has to depend on `@sentry/server-utils` directly. Making `@sentry/solidstart` re-export it would be a one-line SDK improvement. - Per-route variant, no middleware: call `setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute('/api/users/:id')` at the top of the handler -> `{"name":"GET /api/w1/:id","source":"route"}` (route `w1` in the probe). - Without `@sentry/server-utils`, `getRootSpan(getActiveSpan())` + `updateSpanName(root, 'GET /api/x/:id')` + `root.setAttribute('http.route', ...)` also renames, but leaves `source: "custom"` rather than `"route"` (route `w2`: `{"name":"GET /api/w2/:id","source":"custom"}`), because it does not set `sentry.segment.name.source`. - Mutating `getRequestEvent().nativeEvent.context.matchedRoute = { route: '/api/x/:id' }` works too (route `w3`, `source: "route"`), since `@sentry/nitro`'s `beforeSpanEnd` re-reads it — but it pokes an h3 internal, so prefer the helper. - Only the segment span is renamed; the two inner non-segment `http.server` spans stay `"GET"` under stream lifecycle. That is cosmetic and does not affect transaction grouping. - Moving an endpoint out of `src/routes/` into a real Nitro route under `server/` (with `nitro({ serverDir: './server' })`) gets parameterized names with zero Sentry code, if that fits the app. The real fix belongs in the SDK: `@sentry/solidstart` should hook SolidStart's own matcher (it already computes `"path": "/api/users/:id"` in `matchAPIRoute`, and page matches are available via the router) and call `setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute`, the same way `@sentry/nitro` does for h3 routes.
isolation✗ brokenThree concurrent /api/iso?tag=alpha|beta|gamma requests each produced an event with only its own tag and its own trace id. But the FIRST setTag in the process also lands on the shared default isolation scope, so every later request that does not set the tag itself inherits it: after the burst, /api/sentinel events kept reporting tags={'probe-tag':'alpha'} indefinitely. Reproduced after a restart with sequential requests (one, two, three): only the first tag ('one') leaks into later untagged requests. This is Deno-specific: the same .output run under node shows sentinel with tags=None. static lifecycle. verified: confirmed-broken Reproduced from a fresh build and found the reporter's mechanism wrong. Per-request isolation itself works: three concurrent requests produced three events each carrying only its own tag and its own trace id, in both lifecycles. The defect is cross-request: the sentinel request, which sets nothing, kept reporting the first request's tag, on its own event and on its transaction. Instrumenting the scopes disproves the 'first setTag lands on the default isolation scope' explanation. The default isolation scope captured at init stays empty for the whole run, and every request gets its own fresh isolation scope object with a distinct id; each new fork simply inherits the first request's tag. Root cause is the Deno runtime, not the SDK, and it is the same AsyncLocalStorage leak another cell found. A standalone async_hooks and node:http probe shows that on Deno 2.9.0 als.run(store, async () => { await import('./new-module.mjs') }) leaves the store as the root context's store after the handler returns, while Node 26.5.0 does not; plain als.run without a dynamic import does not leak, and only an uncached import leaks, a second request importing the same module does not re-leak. That is exactly why only the first tag sticks: Nitro and SolidStart lazily import each route chunk on its first hit. Warming a route with an untagged request first produced zero leakage afterwards. The identical build under node is clean.
Workaround: Wrap anything that mutates scope inside the route handler in Sentry.withIsolationScope or Sentry.withScope; both were verified clean on Deno. An h3 or Nitro middleware wrapping next() in withIsolationScope does NOT work, verified. Note the side effect: with withIsolationScope the tag is no longer attached to the request transaction, only to events captured inside the block.
incoming trace✓ worksA request with sentry-trace: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa-1000000000000001-1 plus baggage produced a transaction with trace_id aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa and parent_span_id 1000000000000001. static lifecycle.
outgoing fetch✓* works-waA fetch from the handler to the local recorder produced no http.client span in the transaction, and the recorder received the request with no sentry-trace and no baggage header ({"url":"/recorder"}). Under node the identical build produces "http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:47312/recorder" and both headers, so this is the known Deno fetch gap (K2) surfacing through SolidStart unchanged. static and stream lifecycle both. verified: works-after-all Reproduced the report exactly, and no supported SolidStart/Nitro wiring knob changes it. The root cause is in @sentry/node: outgoing `fetch` is instrumented only by the vendored undici instrumentation, which listens on `diagnostics_channel` `undici:request:*` (packages/node/src/integrations/node-fetch/undici-instrumentation.ts, `nativeNodeFetchIntegration`). Deno's `fetch` is native Rust, never publishes those channels, so nothing fires — the SDK emits no warning either. Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-solidstart-deno-outgoingfetch (sources: vite.config.ts, server/plugins/sentry.ts, server/fetch-integration.ts, src/routes/api/{fetchout,fetchout-http,sentinel}.ts, recorder-b.mjs, run-b.sh; reports: report-*.txt). Build: `NODE_ENV=production npx vite build`; run: `./run-b.sh <node|deno> <fix 0|1|2|3> <static|stream>` (sink 52141, recorder 52142, app 52143). node_modules was removed after the last build; `.output/` is kept and still runs with `deno run -A .output/server/index.mjs`. Reinstall for a rebuild: `npm install --legacy-peer-deps` with the tarball set from package.json plus $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-vercel-edge-10.67.0.tgz. 1) NODE control, plugin init, static (report-node-fix0-static via task output): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/fetchout","op":"http.server",...,"spans":["http.server GET /api/fetchout","middleware GET /api/fetchout","http.server GET /api/fetchout","db mysql2.connect","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:52142/recorder"]} recorder: {"url":"/recorder","sentryTrace":"4bf489deb71a459d87f9686275bfaad0-83d59e9e2a9915b6-1","baggage":"yes"} 2) DENO, documented wiring (nitro startup plugin), static — BROKEN, matches the report: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/fetchout","op":"http.server",...,"spans":["http.server GET /api/fetchout","middleware GET /api/fetchout","http.server GET /api/fetchout","db mysql2.connect"]} recorder: {"url":"/recorder"} Same run, `node:http` client on the same Deno process DOES work, which isolates the gap to fetch: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/fetchout-http",...,"spans":[...,"http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:52142/recorder-http"]} recorder: {"url":"/recorder-http","sentryTrace":"6fe72f65896b4602b304bae3071039b3-a28c54be4eeec864-1","baggage":"yes"} 3) DENO, stream lifecycle — same gap (fetchout segment has no client span; the node:http route does): {"type":"span","trace_id":"64d086043f1f4828a89841a82421fe23","items":["middleware GET /api/fetchout","db mysql2.connect","http.server GET","http.server GET","http.server GET"]} recorder: {"url":"/recorder"} 4) Init placement variant `sentrySolidStart({ autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import', instrumentation: './src/instrument.server.ts' })` — worse, not better: the instrument file is never injected into the nitro 3 output (`grep -rl "init via instrument.server" .output` → nothing; no "@sentry/solidstart" top-level import in the server entry), so Sentry never initializes at all. Sink empty, both routes hit the recorder with no headers: ### sink items (rb-deno-fix0-static-instrument) <- empty {"url":"/recorder"} {"url":"/recorder-http"} So on SolidStart 2 + nitro 3 the nitro startup plugin is the only init placement that works, and it does not help fetch. 5) Refutations that DO work (userland integration, not a supported knob): both a hand-written integration built from @sentry/core's `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest` (fix=1) and the shipped `winterCGFetchIntegration()` exported by @sentry/vercel-edge (fix=2/3) fully restore the capability on Deno, in both lifecycles: static, fix=2: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/fetchout",...,"spans":[...,"http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:52142/recorder"]} + {"url":"/recorder","sentryTrace":"2a02828a13234b14ae9b6babaa84f90a-b37c411fcff39f7e-1","baggage":"yes"} stream, fix=2: {"type":"span","trace_id":"66f7ca9e683c4e02bb0fa3bb8eb96daa","items":["middleware GET /api/fetchout","db mysql2.connect","http.client GET 127.0.0.1",...],"raw":[...{"name":"GET 127.0.0.1","status":"ok","parent_span_id":"9ea50cfc7eaced3e","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.http.wintercg_fetch"}...]} + {"url":"/recorder","sentryTrace":"66f7ca9e683c4e02bb0fa3bb8eb96daa-b938eae23f289a56-1","baggage":"yes"} Deno-gated variant (fix=3) verified too: {"url":"/recorder","sentryTrace":"5824e09278f04efaace9dac71b44a9bf-9a0ced3adba59de8-1","baggage":"yes"}. Important side effect: the same integration must NOT be added unconditionally, because on Node it double-instruments — undici plus winterCG produce two client spans for one request: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/fetchout",...,"spans":[...,"http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:52142/recorder","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:52142/recorder"]} Verdict rationale: with every wiring the SolidStart SDK actually supports (nitro plugin init, both trace lifecycles, the vite plugin's autoInject placement, node-server output), outgoing fetch stays uninstrumented on Deno. This is K2 surfacing through SolidStart unchanged, not a SolidStart-specific defect; it is fixable in the SDK by shipping a fetch instrumentation that patches `globalThis.fetch` when the undici channels are absent.
Workaround: Add a WinterCG-style global-fetch integration in the nitro startup plugin, gated on Deno so Node does not get duplicate spans. Verified in server/plugins/sentry.ts: import * as Sentry from '@sentry/solidstart'; import { winterCGFetchIntegration } from '@sentry/vercel-edge'; import { definePlugin } from 'nitro'; export default definePlugin(() => { Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, integrations: typeof globalThis.Deno !== 'undefined' ? [winterCGFetchIntegration()] : [], }); }); (`npm install --legacy-peer-deps @sentry/vercel-edge`, same version as @sentry/solidstart; it bundles cleanly into the nitro node-server output.) If pulling in @sentry/vercel-edge is unwanted, the identical result comes from a ~25 line local integration using `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest` + `shouldPropagateTraceForUrl` from @sentry/core — see server/fetch-integration.ts in the probe dir. Without either, `node:http` / `node:https` clients still produce `http.client` spans with headers on Deno, so switching a critical outbound call off `fetch` is the no-dependency fallback.

Instrumentation path: build-time (orchestrion) instrumentation injected by sentrySolidStart's sentryOrchestrionPlugin during vite build; no Deno import hook and no @sentry/deno were used or needed, mysql2 is bundled into the server output.

Docs today

No page mentions the combination. ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/ (index.mdx, install/, features/, profiling/) contains no occurrence of "deno" at all; the SolidStart guide has no getting-started-prerequisites include of its own (platform-includes/getting-started-prerequisites/ has javascript.solid.mdx but no javascript.solidstart.mdx), so it never states a supported runtime. Conversely docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-18 declares the Deno SDK (sentry.javascript.deno, beta) as a manual-setup server platform and names no framework anywhere in its 232 lines. So a user has nothing telling them that a SolidStart node-server build runs on Deno, nor that on Deno it loses outgoing-fetch tracing and leaks the first scope write.

Documented: no

A page must state that SolidStart 2 is built on Node and its node-server Nitro output runs on Deno 2.9 with @sentry/solidstart, and record four defects with fixes. Unhandled errors from API routes are not captured on Deno; register a try/catch h3 middleware as the first entry of the array form of createMiddleware, which also means the guide's own verification snippet produces no issue as written. Server transaction names cannot be parameterized on SolidStart 2 with Nitro 3 on either runtime, because SolidStart mounts one catch-all route, so transactions arrive as the raw path with source url; a global middleware rebuilding the pattern from event.params is the fix. Outgoing fetch produces no span and no trace headers, because the Node SDK relies on undici channels that Deno's fetch never emits; add a userland fetch integration gated on Deno. Isolation is only partial. Database spans, logs and incoming trace continuation work unmodified. Install needs npm with --legacy-peer-deps for the nitro beta.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/install/deno.mdx (new). Also change guides/solidstart/index.mdx:444-470, add platform-includes/getting-started-prerequisites/javascript.solidstart.mdx, and add platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.solidstart.mdx documenting the Nitro catch-all route-naming limit, which applies on Node too.

guides/solidstart/ (index.mdx, install/, features/, profiling/): grep for deno returns zero; index.mdx:1-7 names no server runtime; no platform-includes/getting-started-prerequisites/javascript.solidstart.mdx exists; index.mdx:444-470 is the tracing verification step whose thrown API-route error is never captured on Deno; guides/deno/index.mdx:1-18 covers only the Deno SDK, not a node-server Nitro build run under Deno.

Key surprise: this combination works far better than expected, because @sentry/solidstart on develop does build-time (orchestrion) instrumentation inside the vite build. The Deno runtime never has to patch modules, so mysql2 db spans work with no @sentry/deno import hook and no --import flag. The server SDK is @sentry/node (index.server.js re-exports it) and its OTel setup boots cleanly under deno 2.9.0. Two Deno-specific defects, both confirmed against a node control run of the exact same .output bundle: 1. Outgoing fetch: no http.client span and no propagation headers (known Deno finding K2), while node produces both. 2. Scope leak: the first Sentry.setTag in the process sticks to the shared default isolation scope and shows up on every later request that does not overwrite it. Node does not leak. Worth an issue: it means one request's tags/user/context can be attributed to unrelated later requests on Deno. Two framework-level gaps that are NOT Deno's fault (node behaves the same): - A throw from an API route handler never becomes a Sentry event; only the transaction turns internal_error. Users must wrap handlers themselves (or use withServerActionInstrumentation for 'use server' functions, which is what the e2e app solidstart-2 does). - Route names are not parameterized: static gives "GET /api/users/42" with source url; stream gives just "GET". Same shape as the Bun/Nitro catch-all finding — the transaction carries the raw URL rather than the route pattern, so the name is high cardinality in static and useless in stream. Packaging friction worth a docs line: npm refuses the install without --legacy-peer-deps because @sentry/nitro's peer range does not accept nitro 3.0.260610-beta (the version @solidjs/start 2.0.2 pulls); pnpm, which the e2e app uses, is more lenient. Everything above is the develop build (10.67.0 tarballs from $REPRO/_toolbox/pack); 10.73.0 was never installed. All processes I started were killed and app/node_modules was removed.

Hono on Cloudflare M-hono-cf

Hono 4 (@sentry/hono/cloudflare middleware, SDK 10.67.0 from develop) · Cloudflare Workers (wrangler 4.129.0 dev, workerd, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, nodejs_compat) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Packages: `npm install @sentry/hono @sentry/cloudflare hono` (peer dep @sentry/cloudflare must be installed but is never imported). For db spans additionally `vite` + `@cloudflare/vite-plugin`.

wrangler.jsonc:
```
{ "name": "app", "main": "src/index.ts",
  "compatibility_date": "2026-05-01",
  "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"] }
```

Entry (src/index.ts) — the middleware is the whole wiring; there is no separate instrument file and no honoIntegration on develop:
```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono';
import * as Sentry from '@sentry/hono/cloudflare';
import { sentry } from '@sentry/hono/cloudflare';

const app = new Hono();
app.use(sentry(app, { dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }));   // or sentry(app, env => ({ dsn: env.SENTRY_DSN }))
app.get('/users/:id', c => c.json({ id: c.req.param('id') }));
export default app;                                             // sentry() mutates app.fetch in place via withSentry
```
`sentry(app, options)` must be the first `app.use` — it calls `withSentry((env) => options, app)` internally, which mutates the handler, so the plain `export default app` stays correct. `@sentry/hono/cloudflare` re-exports all of `@sentry/cloudflare`, so `Sentry.setTag`, `Sentry.captureException`, `Sentry.logger` come from the same import.

Run: `npx wrangler dev --port <port> --inspector-port 0`.

For database spans only, build through Vite instead (vite.config.ts):
```ts
import { cloudflare } from '@cloudflare/vite-plugin';
import { sentryCloudflareVitePlugin } from '@sentry/cloudflare/vite';
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [cloudflare(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ autoInstrumentation: false })],
});
```
`autoInstrumentation: false` because the Hono middleware already applies `withSentry`; `buildTimeInstrumentation` (default true) is the part that injects the `orchestrion:mysql:query` diagnostics channel. Then `npx vite build && npx wrangler dev --config dist/<worker>/wrangler.json --port <port>`.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksAn error thrown in `app.get('/boom/:id')` is captured with mechanism `auto.http.hono.context_error`, `handled: false`, sdk `sentry.javascript.hono`, and `transaction: "GET /boom/:id"`. Hono does not swallow it: it still returns 500 and the server span/transaction gets status `internal_error`. Seen under both stream and static lifecycle. `hasContextLine` is false (no source context in an unminified-but-unmapped dev bundle).
route names✓ worksParameterized route name is `GET /users/:id` with `sentry.segment.name.source = "route"` and `http.route = "/users/:id"` (stream lifecycle), and `transaction: "GET /users/:id"` with `transaction_info.source = "route"` (static lifecycle). Origin is `auto.http.cloudflare`, op `http.server`.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent GET /iso/:tag requests (each setTag then a 60ms await then captureException) produced three events, each carrying only its own `probe_tag` (aaa/bbb/ccc) and its own trace id, matching the trace id of its own http.server span. Stream lifecycle.
incoming trace✓ worksA request with `sentry-trace: 1111…1111-2222222222222222-1` plus baggage produced a server span with `trace_id 11111111111111111111111111111111` and `parent_span_id 2222222222222222`. Stream lifecycle.
outgoing fetch✓ works`fetch()` from inside the handler produced an `http.client` span child of the server span, and the recorder saw `sentry-trace: <traceid>-<spanid>-1` plus a full baggage header including `sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Ffetchout`. Span name is `GET 127.0.0.1` under stream (low-cardinality naming) and `GET http://127.0.0.1:47211/__rec` under static.
db spans✓ worksModule-scope `mysql.createConnection({host:'127.0.0.1',port:3307})` + `conn.query('SELECT id, name FROM users')` inside the handler produced `db | SELECT id, name FROM users` as a child of the server span — but ONLY through the Cloudflare Vite plugin build (`sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()`, buildTimeInstrumentation injects `tracingChannel("orchestrion:mysql:query")` into the bundle). The instrumentation path was needed: with plain `wrangler dev` on the TypeScript entry the identical query returns rows but emits no db span at all (only the bare `http.server | GET /db` span). Static lifecycle for the positive result, stream for the negative control.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info('hono-cf-log-line', { where: 'handler' })` arrived as a `log` envelope item at level info, carrying the same trace id as the enclosing http.server span. Stream lifecycle, read after an 8s wait (logs are timer-flushed).
client errors· not-runNot applicable: this is a server-only Worker with no browser bundle. @sentry/hono/cloudflare has no client-side entry.

Docs today

The Hono guide exists and does cover Cloudflare Workers as a first-class tab. ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hono/index.mdx:12 states "The @sentry/hono SDK supports Hono 4+ across multiple runtimes: Cloudflare Workers, Node.js, Bun, and Deno." :76-77 tells CF users to `npm install @sentry/cloudflare` as a peer dep; :129-135 is an expandable "Cloudflare Workers: Enable Node.js Compatibility" telling them to set `nodejs_compat` for AsyncLocalStorage; :246-270 shows the exact `app.use(sentry(app, { dsn, dataCollection, tracesSampleRate }))` + `export default app` shape I verified; :354-367 shows the `sentry(app, env => ({ dsn: env.SENTRY_DSN }))` callback for Worker bindings. Everything the page claims for CF matched what I observed. Gap: the page never mentions Vite, `@cloudflare/vite-plugin`, `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin` or `buildTimeInstrumentation` (grep for vite/mysql/database over the file only hits :162, which is about Node.js). So a Hono-on-CF user following the docs verbatim gets errors, routes, isolation, trace propagation, fetch spans and logs, but silently gets no database spans, and the docs give them no hint that a Vite build is what turns those on. The two other files in the guide (features/index.mdx, features/error-handler.mdx) do not mention Cloudflare at all.

Documented: partial

The Hono guide documents the middleware wiring correctly, but two things the run needed are absent. (1) Database spans: the probe only got `db` spans after adding `vite` + `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` and the Sentry Cloudflare Vite plugin to the build; the Hono guide's only database sentence (:162) is Node.js-specific and the Cloudflare tab says nothing, so a Workers user following this page gets errors, routes, isolation, trace continuation, fetch and logs but silently no db spans. The Cloudflare Workers section must say that database instrumentation on Workers is build-time only and link to /platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin/. (2) The `nodejs_compat` Expandable at :129-144 sets the flag but never sets `compatibility_date`; the run used `2026-05-01` and the Cloudflare include (getting-started-config/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:5) states a date of `2024-09-23` or later is required, so the Hono Cloudflare tab must state the compatibility_date requirement alongside the flag.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hono/index.mdx — extend the "Cloudflare Workers: Enable Node.js Compatibility" Expandable (:129-144) to also set `compatibility_date`, and add a "Database spans on Cloudflare Workers" subsection after the middleware step (:274) pointing at docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx

docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hono/index.mdx:12 ("supports Hono 4+ across multiple runtimes: Cloudflare Workers, Node.js, Bun, and Deno"); :65-78 (Cloudflare Workers tab: `npm install @sentry/cloudflare` as the peer dependency, "You won't import it directly, but it must be present"); :129-144 (Expandable "Cloudflare Workers: Enable Node.js Compatibility", `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]` for AsyncLocalStorage); :246-274 (the exact `sentry(app, {...})` middleware wiring from `@sentry/hono/cloudflare` that the run used); docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/hono.mdx:6-8 (stub that redirects to the Hono guide); docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:17 (framework list entry). Missing: `grep -rn -i "vite|mysql|database" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hono/` returns only index.mdx:162, which is about Node.js, so nothing in the Hono guide covers database spans on Workers. `compatibility_date` is never mentioned in the Cloudflare Expandable (only the flag, at :140-144), unlike platform-includes/getting-started-config/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:5-21 which the Hono guide does not include.

Viability was never in doubt for the framework itself — Hono is the canonical CF Workers framework and served requests immediately; there was no need for a Sentry-free control run. Findings worth flagging: - `sentry(app, options)` works by mutation: it calls `withSentry(cb, app)` from @sentry/cloudflare, and withSentry mutates `handler.fetch/scheduled/queue/...` in place and returns the same object, which is why `export default app` (not `export default withSentry(...)`) is correct. Source: node_modules/@sentry/hono/build/esm/cloudflare/middleware.js and @sentry/cloudflare/build/esm/dev/withSentry.js. - The CF middleware always strips the Hono integration from user + default integrations (`buildFilteredIntegrations(honoOptions.integrations, true)`) because withSentry already installs it; it also force-appends LOW_QUALITY_TRANSACTION_PATTERNS to `ignoreSpans`. - No middleware spans are emitted on Cloudflare — the transaction's `spans[]` under static lifecycle contains only the db/http.client children, no `middleware.hono` entries. I did not check whether that is intentional on CF vs. Node. - The Cloudflare Vite plugin is safe alongside the Hono middleware, but I set `autoInstrumentation: false` deliberately so the plugin would not apply a second `withSentry` on top of the middleware's. I did not test whether leaving it at the default `true` double-instruments; that is a worthwhile follow-up probe. - `mysql@2` connects to MariaDB on 127.0.0.1:3307 from inside workerd fine under `nodejs_compat` with a module-scope connection, in both the plain and the Vite build; only the span differs. - Environment friction: ports 41337, 47213 and 47212-adjacent were already taken by sibling agents mid-run; I moved to 47211 / 47212 / 53871. Two wrangler starts had to be retried for that reason only. - Stack frames arrive without `context_line` (hasContextLine false) in both builds. Expected for a dev run with no sourcemap upload, not a defect.

Elysia on Cloudflare M-elysia-cf

Elysia 1.4.30 · Cloudflare Workers (wrangler 4.129.0 dev, workerd 1.20260903.1, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, nodejs_compat) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Elysia runs on workerd ONLY with AOT disabled: `new Elysia({ aot: false })`. With the default (aot on) workerd refuses to start the Worker: "Uncaught Error: Disallowed operation called within global scope. Asynchronous I/O ..., setting a timeout, and generating random values are not allowed within global scope ... at worker.js:15:16 in eval / at index.js:20163:4 in composeGeneralHandler" (Elysia's codegen'd handler runs `new Function` at module scope and touches randomness).

Recommended wiring (this is what a docs page should show; it is NOT the plain-withSentry-only shape the task hint assumed):

packages: `npm install @sentry/cloudflare @sentry/elysia elysia wrangler` (for the develop build: `npm install <worktree packs>/sentry-{core,opentelemetry,cloudflare,server-utils}-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{elysia,bun,node,server-runtime-injection}-10.67.0.tgz elysia wrangler@4`)

src/index.ts:
```ts
import { withElysia } from '@sentry/elysia';
import * as Sentry from '@sentry/cloudflare';
import { Elysia } from 'elysia';

// withElysia MUST wrap the instance BEFORE any route is registered
const app = withElysia(new Elysia({ aot: false }))
  .get('/users/:id', ({ params }) => ({ id: params.id }))
  .get('/p/:id/boom', () => { throw new Error('boom'); });

export default Sentry.withSentry(
  (env) => ({ dsn: env.SENTRY_DSN, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, sendDefaultPii: true }),
  { fetch: (request) => app.fetch(request) },
);
```
Init placement: `withSentry` supplies the client, the isolation scope, the root `http.server` span and the incoming-trace continuation. Do NOT call `init` from `@sentry/elysia` (its `sdk.js` imports `node:os` and `@sentry/bun`); only the `withElysia` wrapper is used. Importing `withElysia` from `@sentry/elysia` bundles fine under wrangler/esbuild even though the package's index re-exports `@sentry/bun` — esbuild tree-shakes the Bun/Node side away, so the hint that "@sentry/elysia will most likely not load on workerd" is wrong for the wrapper.

wrangler.jsonc: `{"main":"src/index.ts","compatibility_date":"2026-05-01","compatibility_flags":["nodejs_compat"]}`
run: `npx wrangler dev --port <port> --inspector-port 0`

Fallback (no @sentry/elysia): `withSentry` around `app.fetch` alone also boots and gives spans/logs/isolation/trace propagation, but transaction names stay URL-sourced and handler errors are silently swallowed unless you add your own `.onError(({ error }) => Sentry.captureException(error))`.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksWith `withElysia`, a throw in a handler is captured automatically via Elysia's global onError hook, mechanism `auto.http.elysia.on_error`, handled:false, correct trace id and transaction `GET /p/:id/boom` (traceLifecycle static and stream both). Without `withElysia`, Elysia swallows the error entirely: plain `withSentry(app.fetch)` produced only a transaction with status internal_error and NO event; a hand-written `.onError` hook calling `Sentry.captureException` is then required.
route names✓ worksWith `withElysia` applied to the Elysia instance before routes are registered, the server transaction is `GET /users/:id` with source `route` (static lifecycle) and the streamed segment span is named `GET /users/:id` (stream lifecycle). Silent trap: if `withElysia(app)` is called AFTER the routes are declared, only the error path gets the route name (its onError hook), while the success path stays `GET /users/42` with source `url`. Plain `withSentry` alone is always `GET /users/42` / source `url` (static) or bare `GET` (stream).
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent GET /iso/{alpha,beta,gamma} each setTag('reqtag', ...) and captureException: each event carries only its own tag and its own trace id (8df5cf86..., 298f04fd..., b58f7a27...), and each has its own `GET /iso/:tag` transaction on the matching trace. Isolation comes from `withSentry`, not from `withElysia` (its `app.wrap` isolation branch is Bun-only). traceLifecycle static.
incoming trace✓ worksA request with `sentry-trace: cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc-dddddddddddddddd-1` plus baggage produced a transaction with trace_id `cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc` and parent_span_id `dddddddddddddddd`. Continued by `withSentry`; verified with both plain withSentry and withElysia. traceLifecycle static.
outgoing fetch✓ works`fetch()` from inside an Elysia handler to a local recorder produced `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:52742/recorded-sdk` as a child of the server transaction (static) / `http.client GET 127.0.0.1` with origin auto.http.fetch (stream), and the recorder saw `sentry-trace` and `baggage` whose trace id matched the server transaction. Comes from the Cloudflare SDK's fetch instrumentation.
db spans✓* works-wamysql2 does run on workerd from a module-scope pool, but only with `disableEval: true` (without it every query fails with `Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`); `SELECT * FROM users` returned both rows. No db span is emitted: the `GET /db` transaction had `spans: []`. Instrumentation path used: none, this was a plain wrangler/esbuild build, and no Bun plugin or Deno hook applies here. The Cloudflare Vite plugin's `buildTimeInstrumentation` path was NOT exercised (out of time box), so a Vite-built Worker may differ. verified: works-after-all The exact change that fixes it: build the Worker with Vite + `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` instead of letting `wrangler dev` bundle `src/index.ts` with its own esbuild. Nothing in the app code had to change. The plugin's `buildTimeInstrumentation` (default true) injects `diagnostics_channel.tracingChannel` calls into the bundled `mysql2` and registers the Sentry subscriber factory; plain wrangler/esbuild does not, which is why the original probe saw `spans: []`. Two side findings that also contradict parts of the original report: - `withElysia` from @sentry/elysia bundles cleanly under Vite/rollup as well as esbuild (1801 modules, no externals, no errors), and it fixes transaction naming: `GET /users/:id` with `source: "route"` on BOTH the Vite and the plain-wrangler builds, where the plain-withSentry fallback reported `source: "url"`. - Both trace lifecycles work; the report's `spans: []` was purely a build-pipeline artifact, not a lifecycle or Elysia issue. Still true from the original report and required: `new Elysia({ aot: false })` (aot on still refuses to start the Worker) and `disableEval: true` on the mysql2 pool. The pool must stay at module scope. Reference cross-check: the repo's own e2e app dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/cloudflare-orchestrion-mysql uses exactly this vite.config.ts (`plugins: [cloudflare(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()]`), so the working path is the one the SDK already tests, just never shown for Elysia.
Workaround: Build the Worker with Vite instead of letting wrangler bundle the entry: add `vite.config.mjs` with `plugins: [cloudflare(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()]` (from `@sentry/cloudflare/vite`), run `npx vite build`, then `npx wrangler dev --config dist/<worker-name>/wrangler.json`. No application-code change is needed; keep `new Elysia({ aot: false })`, the module-scope `mysql.createPool({ ..., disableEval: true })`, and `Sentry.withSentry(...)` around `{ fetch: request => app.fetch(request) }`.

Docs today

No page mentions Elysia on Cloudflare Workers. ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/elysia/index.mdx:25 lists the prerequisites as "Bun or Node.js 18+ (with @elysiajs/node adapter)" only, and the install snippets are Bun/Node only (index.mdx:55-56, :82). ~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:11-12 has a "Runtime Behavior" section that covers exactly two runtimes, Bun and Node.js, and says nothing about workerd. The Cloudflare guide's list of frameworks with dedicated setup instructions (~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23: Astro, Hono, Hydrogen, Next.js, Nuxt, Remix, SvelteKit, TanStack Start) does not include Elysia, and `grep -rni elysia docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/` returns nothing. So the combination that actually works today is undocumented in both directions, including the two things a user cannot guess: `aot: false` and wrapping with `withElysia` before declaring routes.

Documented: wrong

The runtime list must gain a third entry: Elysia 1.4.30 runs on Cloudflare Workers with nodejs_compat, and the page must stop implying Bun and Node are the only options. It must state the one mandatory change, constructing the app with ahead-of-time compilation disabled; with it on, workerd refuses to start the Worker because Elysia's generated handler runs new Function and touches randomness at module scope. Errors, route names, isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing fetch spans and logs all work with no extra wiring. Database spans exist only when the Worker is built with Vite and the Sentry Cloudflare plugin, whose build-time instrumentation injects the tracing channels; a wrangler-bundled Worker emits none.

Corrections to the task's setup hint: (a) `@sentry/elysia`'s `withElysia` DOES load and work on workerd. Its own source only imports `@sentry/core` and `@sentry/conventions`; the `@sentry/bun` re-export sits in the package index and esbuild tree-shakes it away when you import just `withElysia`. Only `init` from `@sentry/elysia` is unusable there (sdk.js imports `node:os`, `global.process.env`, and `@sentry/bun`'s init). (b) Plain `withSentry` around `app.fetch` is the strictly worse option: no route names and, worse, zero error events, because Elysia's default error handling turns the throw into a 500 response before it can reach the Worker's fetch handler. Ordering trap worth a docs callout: `withElysia` installs its route-naming hook with `.onAfterHandle({ as: 'global' })`. On workerd with `aot: false`, that hook does not reach routes that were already registered, so `withElysia(appWithRoutes)` names only the error path. `withElysia(new Elysia({aot:false})).get(...)` names everything. On Bun this ordering probably does not matter (the Bun branch of `app.wrap` owns the root span); it does here. No Elysia lifecycle spans on Cloudflare. `platform-includes/.../javascript.elysia.mdx:3-5` promises spans for Request/Parse/Transform/BeforeHandle/Handle/AfterHandle/MapResponse/AfterResponse/Error with `op: request_handler.elysia` / `middleware.elysia`; on workerd every transaction came back with `spans: []` except the `http.client` fetch span. The `app.trace()` handler that creates them depends on `rootSpanForRequest`, which is only populated by the Bun branch of `app.wrap`. Tarball hazard for whoever reruns this: `$REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz` and `$REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz` are older than `$REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-cloudflare-10.67.0.tgz`. Using them together fails the wrangler build with `The path "./no-diagnostic-channels" is not exported by package "@sentry/server-utils"` and then `No matching export in "@sentry/core/build/esm/index.js" for import "spanSourceWasExplicitlySet" / "markSpanForOtelSourceInference" / "_INTERNAL_startInactiveSpan"`. Repacking core, opentelemetry, cloudflare and server-utils from $W fixed it. Also, `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-elysia-...tgz` needs `sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz` on the same command line or it fails with `notarget No matching version found for @sentry/server-runtime-injection@10.67.0`. mysql2 on workerd: works from a module-scope pool over the nodejs_compat TCP polyfill, but only with `disableEval: true`; the default row-parser codegen dies with `Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`. Queries returned real rows from the MariaDB on 3307. Still no db span, and the Cloudflare Vite plugin (`buildTimeInstrumentation`) path was not exercised, so treat the db verdict as "no span from a plain wrangler build" rather than "no span on Cloudflare, ever". Environment friction: ports 41318 and 41319 were already held by another agent's recorder, and my first sink on 41317 was killed by something outside this task mid-run, which cost one repeat of the probe batch. Final ports used were 52741/52742/52744/52745. All processes I started were killed and both `node_modules` trees were removed; the source, configs and logs remain.
