curl -s http://127.0.0.1:52744/sentinel          # sentinel, then read
sleep 6; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:52745/__items
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:52742/__hits            # sentry-trace / baggage on the outgoing fetch

Express on Cloudflare M-express-cf

Express 5 (express@5.2.0) behind `httpServerHandler` from `cloudflare:node` · Cloudflare Workers (workerd 2026-09-03 via wrangler 4.129.0, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, flags `nodejs_compat` + `enable_nodejs_http_server_modules`), @sentry/cloudflare 10.67.0 (develop, tarball) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Express 5 boots on workerd unchanged and Sentry wires up in one place. Two shapes, and the difference matters a lot.

PACKAGES
  npm install express@5 wrangler@4 mysql2 vite@6 @cloudflare/vite-plugin
  npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-cloudflare-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz \
              $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz

wrangler.jsonc
  {
    "name": "m-express-cf",
    "main": "src/index.js",
    "compatibility_date": "2026-05-01",
    "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat", "enable_nodejs_http_server_modules"]
  }

SHAPE A - plain `wrangler dev` (esbuild). Entry file:
  import { httpServerHandler } from 'cloudflare:node';
  import * as Sentry from '@sentry/cloudflare';
  import express from 'express';

  const app = express();
  app.get('/users/:id', (req, res) => res.json({ id: req.params.id }));
  // Required on this shape: express swallows route errors, nothing reaches Sentry without it.
  app.use((err, req, res, _next) => { Sentry.captureException(err); res.status(500).json({ error: err.message }); });
  app.listen(8080);

  export default Sentry.withSentry(
    () => ({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' }),
    httpServerHandler({ port: 8080 }),
  );

  Run: npx wrangler dev --port <port> --inspector-port 0
  Gets: errors (manual only), isolation, incoming trace, http.client spans + headers, logs.
  Does NOT get: parameterized route names (source stays `url`), express handler spans, db spans.

SHAPE B - Vite + `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` (the shape that actually gives express/db instrumentation):
  vite.config.mjs
    import { cloudflare } from '@cloudflare/vite-plugin';
    import { sentryCloudflareVitePlugin } from '@sentry/cloudflare/vite';
    export default defineConfig({ plugins: [cloudflare(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()] });

  The entry MUST NOT register routes at module scope. With `buildTimeInstrumentation` on (the default)
  the injected express channel makes `app.get(...)` at global scope crash the Worker at startup, so the
  app has to be built lazily on the first request:

    let app, listening;
    function ensureApp() {
      if (!listening) { app = buildApp(); listening = new Promise(r => app.listen(8080, r)); }
      return listening;
    }
    const inner = httpServerHandler({ port: 8080 });
    export default Sentry.withSentry(() => ({ dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }), {
      async fetch(request, env, ctx) { await ensureApp(); return inner.fetch(request, env, ctx); },
    });

  Run: npx vite build && npx wrangler dev --config dist/<worker>/wrangler.json --port <port> --inspector-port 0
  Gets everything Shape A gets, plus automatic error capture (`auto.http.express`, handled:false),
  `GET /users/:id` with source `route`, `handler /users/:id` spans, and mysql2 db spans.

mysql2 on workerd additionally needs `disableEval: true` on the connection options; without it every query
fails with `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓* works-waShape B (Vite plugin): a throw in `app.get('/boom')` is captured automatically as `Error: express-cf-boom` with `mechanism: auto.http.express, handled: false`, and the server span gets `status: internal_error`; express still answers 500 to the client. Shape A (plain wrangler dev): express swallows it completely, no event at all reaches the sink, only `transaction GET /boom status=internal_error` — you must add an express error middleware calling `Sentry.captureException(err)`, which then arrives as `mechanism: generic, handled: true`. Both results from traceLifecycle 'static'. verified: works-after-all The "Shape A needs a hand-written middleware calling captureException, which yields mechanism=generic handled=true" half of the claim is wrong. It is wrong because the probe skipped the documented Express wiring: `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler(app)`. With that one line, plain `wrangler dev` (esbuild, NO Vite, NO build-time instrumentation, top-level `app.get(...)` + `app.listen(8080)`) captures every error shape automatically, as unhandled, correctly trace-linked. EXACT CHANGE (Shape A entry, src/c1.js): import { httpServerHandler } from 'cloudflare:node'; import * as Sentry from '@sentry/cloudflare'; import { setupExpressErrorHandler } from '@sentry/server-utils'; // <-- NOT re-exported by @sentry/cloudflare import { buildApp } from './routes.js'; const app = buildApp(); setupExpressErrorHandler(app); // after routes, before listen app.listen(8080); export default Sentry.withSentry( () => ({ dsn, tunnel: 'http://127.0.0.1:44821/', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static', sendDefaultPii: true }), httpServerHandler({ port: 8080 }), ); CONTROL (c0, identical minus that line, port 44822) - reproduces the reported baseline exactly, no event at all: /boom -> 500 /boom-async -> 500 /boom-next -> 500 {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /boom","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"internal_error","trace_id":"3fb8751a537e48709318c801b224d6bc"} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /boom-async","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"internal_error",...} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /boom-next","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"internal_error",...} {"type":"event","message":"sentinel","mechanism":"generic","handled":true,...} <-- sentinel proves nothing was in flight (zero `event` items for the three throws) WITH setupExpressErrorHandler (c1, traceLifecycle 'static', port 44823) - all three captured, auto + unhandled: {"type":"event","exception":"Error: express-cf-boom","mechanism":"auto.middleware.express","handled":false,"sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare","runtime":"cloudflare","trace_id":"33cb6963e06b40a78c8a448f313ece65","user":{"ip_address":"127.0.0.1"},"request":{"url":"http://127.0.0.1:44823/boom","method":"GET"}} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /boom","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"internal_error","trace_id":"33cb6963e06b40a78c8a448f313ece65"} {"type":"event","exception":"Error: express-cf-boom-async","mechanism":"auto.middleware.express","handled":false,"trace_id":"d307adf44bc54ab8bbb8388db35a4996"} {"type":"event","exception":"Error: express-cf-boom-next","mechanism":"auto.middleware.express","handled":false,"trace_id":"b1b8a21579e646eea7cbb60a6bfe5f7a"} {"type":"event","message":"sentinel","mechanism":"generic","handled":true,...} Sync throw, async throw and `next(err)` are all covered; express still answers 500. OTHER TRACE LIFECYCLE (c2, default 'stream', port 44824) - identical error capture, so this is not lifecycle-dependent: {"type":"event","exception":"Error: express-cf-boom","mechanism":"auto.middleware.express","handled":false,"trace_id":"3f0f71fe788b4e59814d7b033c40e963"} {"type":"span","trace_id":"3f0f71fe788b4e59814d7b033c40e963","items":["http.server GET"],"raw":[{"name":"GET","status":"error","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.cloudflare"}]} {"type":"event","exception":"Error: express-cf-boom-async","mechanism":"auto.middleware.express","handled":false,...} {"type":"event","exception":"Error: express-cf-boom-next","mechanism":"auto.middleware.express","handled":false,...} IMPORT PATH IS THE REAL TRAP (and the likely reason the original probe never tried it): `@sentry/cloudflare` 10.67.0 does not export `setupExpressErrorHandler`. `grep -c setupExpressErrorHandler node_modules/@sentry/cloudflare/build/types/index.d.ts` -> 0, and no hit in build/esm/prod/index.js either. `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` (the exact snippet every Express doc page prints) is `undefined` here and throws. It has to come from `@sentry/server-utils`, which must be listed explicitly in package.json. OTHER VARIANTS TRIED (same dir, earlier pass of this task, logs kept): - `integrations: [expressIntegration()]` from @sentry/server-utils on Shape A (src/a6.js, wrangler.a6.jsonc): nothing captured - the OTel-style integration has no channels to hook without build-time instrumentation. Only the error-handler middleware works on this shape. - esbuild + orchestrion-style build-time instrumentation with a lazy app (build2.mjs -> dist-esb2): gives the Shape B behaviour (`auto.http.express`, handled:false, route names, handler spans) but also emits a spurious `TypeError: isPromise3 is not a function` per request - a separate defect, not this capability. - Vite Shape B with top-level routes (vite.config2.mjs on src/a0.js) and esbuild build-time instrumentation with top-level routes: worker fails to boot, "Disallowed operation called within global scope". Confirms the reported lazy-app requirement, but only for build-time-instrumented shapes; Shape A takes top-level `app.get`/`app.listen` fine. - Repo reference app: none exists. `grep -rl "httpServerHandler|cloudflare:node"` over dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications in ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs returns nothing, and packages/cloudflare/src has no express reference. There is no e2e coverage for Express-behind-httpServerHandler on Workers at all. So the only real gap left on Shape A is that the mechanism reads `auto.middleware.express` instead of Shape B's `auto.http.express`, and that Shape A still lacks route names / handler spans / db spans. Error capture itself is automatic and unhandled on both shapes. FILES / COMMANDS (all under $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-express-cf-errors/run-b/): src/routes.js - shared routes (/plain, /users/:id, /boom, /boom-async, /boom-next, /sentinel) src/c0.js + wrangler.c0.jsonc - control, no error handler (log w-c0.log) src/c1.js + wrangler.c1.jsonc - setupExpressErrorHandler, static (log w-c1.log) src/c2.js + wrangler.c2.jsonc - setupExpressErrorHandler, stream (log w-c2.log) src/a6.js, build2.mjs, build3.mjs, vite.config*.mjs - the refuted variants PORT=44821 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs > sink-c.log 2>&1 & npx wrangler dev --config wrangler.c0.jsonc --port 44822 --inspector-port 0 npx wrangler dev --config wrangler.c1.jsonc --port 44823 --inspector-port 0 npx wrangler dev --config wrangler.c2.jsonc --port 44824 --inspector-port 0 for p in /plain /boom /boom-async /boom-next /sentinel; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:<port>$p; done All processes I started were killed (wrangler by config-name match, sink by `lsof -ti tcp:44821`).
Workaround: On plain `wrangler dev` (no Vite plugin, no build-time instrumentation), register the Sentry Express error handler after your routes and before `app.listen`. Because `@sentry/cloudflare` does not re-export it, import it from `@sentry/server-utils` (add it to package.json): import { setupExpressErrorHandler } from '@sentry/server-utils'; const app = express(); // ... routes ... setupExpressErrorHandler(app); app.listen(8080); This captures sync throws, async throws and `next(err)` as `mechanism: auto.middleware.express, handled: false`, trace-linked to the server transaction, under both `traceLifecycle: 'static'` and the default `'stream'`. No hand-written `captureException` middleware is needed, and no lazy app construction is needed on this shape. Route names, handler spans and db spans still require the Vite/build-time-instrumentation shape.
route names✓* works-waShape A: the server transaction is named from the raw URL, `GET /users/42` with `source: url` (high cardinality, no route template). Shape B: `GET /users/:id` with `source: route` under traceLifecycle 'static', and under 'stream' the same `http.server GET /users/:id` span with `http.route: /users/:id` and `sentry.origin: auto.http.cloudflare`. Note the stream-lifecycle span carries `http.route` but no `sentry.source` attribute at all. verified: works-after-all Refuted. Express 5 on workerd gets parameterized route names in BOTH shapes; the reporter's Shape A gap disappears with one added line, and their "no sentry.source attribute" note is a mis-read of the span-v2 attribute name. Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-express-cf-routenames (REPRO3.md has every command). Sink on 48733, workers on 48801-48805. wrangler 4.129.0, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, flags nodejs_compat + enable_nodejs_http_server_modules, express 5.2.1, @sentry/cloudflare 10.67.0 tarball from develop. THE EXACT CHANGE (Shape A, plain `wrangler dev`, esbuild, NO vite plugin) - add two lines to the entry: import { patchExpressModule } from '@sentry/core/server'; import expressMod from 'express'; patchExpressModule(expressMod, () => ({})); // before you build the app srcP2/index.js, wrangler.P2.jsonc, traceLifecycle 'stream' (the develop default), port 48802: {"type":"span","items":["handler /users/:id","http.server GET /users/:id"],"raw":[{"name":"/users/:id","origin":"auto.http.express"},{"name":"GET /users/:id","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.cloudflare"}]} {"type":"span","items":["router /api/orders","handler /api/orders/:orderId/items/:itemId","http.server GET /api/orders/:orderId/items/:itemId"]} raw attributes on that http.server span: GET /users/:id | {"sentry.op":"http.server","sentry.segment.name.source":"route","http.route":"/users/:id","url.full":"http://127.0.0.1:48802/users/42",...} GET /api/orders/:orderId/items/:itemId | {"sentry.segment.name.source":"route","http.route":"/api/orders/:orderId/items/:itemId",...} So the source attribute IS there and IS "route". The reporter looked for `sentry.source`; in span streaming the key is `sentry.segment.name.source` (the toolbox sink's compact mapping only reads `sentry.source`, which is why it looked absent). That sub-claim is refuted, not a bug. NEGATIVE CONTROL (srcN1, same file minus the patch, stream, port 48805) - the win is entirely the patch: {"type":"span","items":["http.server GET"],"raw":[{"name":"GET","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.cloudflare"}]} (method-only, i.e. worse than the reporter's static-lifecycle `GET /users/42`.) RESIDUAL, the one real defect I found: `patchExpressModule` renames the root span ONLY under span streaming. srcP1 (same file, traceLifecycle 'static', port 48801) gets the handler spans but the transaction keeps the raw URL: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /plain","source":"url","spans":["handler /plain"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/42","source":"url","spans":["handler /users/:id"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/orders/7/items/9","source":"url","spans":["router /:orderId/items/:itemId","handler /api/orders/:orderId/items/:itemId"]} Cause, verified in source: packages/core/src/integrations/express/patch-layer.ts:318-346 `applyRouteToRootSpan` returns early on `!hasSpanStreamingEnabled(client)`. The channel-based path used by the vite plugin has no such guard - packages/server-utils/src/utils/setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute.ts renames unconditionally - so the two Express instrumentation paths disagree. Note `patchExpressModule` is marked @deprecated ("will be removed in the next major version") yet it is the only Express instrumentation reachable without the bundler transform, since `expressIntegration()` in @sentry/server-utils only subscribes once orchestrion has injected the channels, and @sentry/cloudflare's default integration set pulls channel integrations from a global marker the vite plugin writes (packages/cloudflare/src/baseSdk.ts:37,70). SHAPE B re-confirmed (vite build + sentryCloudflareVitePlugin(), lazy app, traceLifecycle 'static', port 48803) - route names with zero extra code: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","spans":["handler /users/:id"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/orders/:orderId/items/:itemId","source":"route","spans":["middleware router2","handler /api/orders/:orderId/items/:itemId"]} Repo reference: there is no Express-on-Cloudflare e2e app in dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications, and nothing there uses `httpServerHandler` at all - the closest is cloudflare-orchestrion-mysql, which proves the vite-plugin channel path but not Express. So neither shape has e2e coverage.
Workaround: Two, both verified on plain `wrangler dev` with no bundler plugin. 1) Full instrumentation (handler/router spans + route names), stream lifecycle only. In the entry, before building the app: import { patchExpressModule } from '@sentry/core/server'; import expressMod from 'express'; patchExpressModule(expressMod, () => ({})); Keep the default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'`; under 'static' this renames nothing. 2) Route names only, works under 'static' (and needs no deprecated API). A global middleware that patches res.end so it runs after routing resolved req.route but before the root span closes (routes4.js in the probe dir): app.use((req, res, next) => { const originalEnd = res.end; res.end = function (...args) { const root = Sentry.getActiveSpan() && Sentry.getRootSpan(Sentry.getActiveSpan()); const routePath = req.route?.path; if (root && routePath) { const route = `${req.baseUrl || ''}${routePath}`; Sentry.updateSpanName(root, `${req.method} ${route}`); root.setAttribute('http.route', route); root.setAttribute(SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, 'route'); // from @sentry/conventions/attributes } return originalEnd.apply(this, args); }; next(); }); Verified (srcQ1, port 48804, static): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","source":"route"} and {"name":"GET /api/orders/:orderId/items/:itemId","source":"route"}. 3) Or just use the Vite plugin shape, which needs no app-side code at all.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent GET /tagged requests with 600/300/50 ms awaits inside the handler each produced exactly their own tag pair and their own trace id: gamma/beta/alpha never leaked across events, and each error's trace id matched its own transaction. Verified identically on Shape A and Shape B, traceLifecycle 'static'. The async context established by `withSentry` propagates through the `cloudflare:node` httpServerHandler bridge into express handlers, including across `setTimeout`.
incoming trace✓ worksA request with `sentry-trace: aaaa…aaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` plus baggage produced a transaction with `trace_id: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` and `parent_span_id: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`, and `Sentry.getActiveSpan()` inside the express handler reported the same trace id. Works on both shapes, traceLifecycle 'static'.
outgoing fetch✓ works`fetch('http://127.0.0.1:41339/recorder')` from inside an express handler produced a child span `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41339/recorder` on the server transaction, and the recorder saw `sentry-trace: <same trace id>-87f72dabd083db4a-1` plus a full baggage header (environment, public_key, trace_id, sampled, sample_rand, sample_rate). Works on both shapes, traceLifecycle 'static'.
db spans✓* works-waInstrumentation path: the Cloudflare Vite plugin (`sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()`, `buildTimeInstrumentation` default true), and it was required. With it, a module-scope `import mysql from 'mysql2/promise'` and a query inside the handler yields `db mysql2.connect` and `db SELECT id, name FROM users` ('static') / `db SELECT users` ('stream'). Under plain `wrangler dev` (esbuild, no channel injection) the identical code produces zero db spans. Separately, mysql2 only runs on workerd at all with `disableEval: true`; the default path dies with `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`. verified: works-after-all Reproduced the reporter's setup independently in $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-express-cf-dbspans (express@5.2.0, wrangler 4.129.0, workerd 1.20260903.1, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, flags nodejs_compat + enable_nodejs_http_server_modules, @sentry/cloudflare 10.67.0 from $REPRO/_toolbox/pack tarballs, MariaDB on 127.0.0.1:3307, sink on 43211). db spans are COMPLETE and CORRECT on the documented wiring, so I do not think this is a partial. 1) Vite plugin path, traceLifecycle 'static' (src/index.js, `npx vite build --config vite.config.mjs && npx wrangler dev --config dist/v4_express_db/wrangler.json --port 52411 --inspector-port 0`): transaction | GET /db | source= route | spans= ['handler /db', 'db mysql2.connect', 'db SELECT id, name FROM users'] transaction | GET /db-legacy | source= route | spans= ['handler /db-legacy', 'db SELECT id, name FROM users'] transaction | GET /users/:id | source= route | spans= ['handler /users/:id'] The db spans are nested under the express `handler` span of the same request, not siblings. Both drivers work: `mysql2/promise` AND the plain `mysql@2.18.1` driver used by the repo's own e2e app. 2) Attributes are complete (raw payload from the sink): {"op":"db","description":"SELECT id, name FROM users","status":"ok","data":{"sentry.origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel","sentry.op":"db","db.system.name":"mysql","db.query.text":"SELECT id, name FROM users","db.query.summary":"SELECT users","db.operation.name":"SELECT","db.namespace":"app","server.address":"127.0.0.1","server.port":3307}} {"op":"db","description":"mysql2.connect","data":{"sentry.origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel","db.system.name":"mysql","db.namespace":"app","server.address":"127.0.0.1","server.port":3307}} 3) The other trace lifecycle also works (`--var LIFECYCLE:stream`), with the low-cardinality query name: span envelope | ['db mysql2.connect', 'db SELECT users', 'handler /db', 'http.server GET /db'] 4) Confirmed the reporter's negative: plain `npx wrangler dev --config wrangler.jsonc` over the same source gives transaction | GET /db | source= url | spans= [] and, with debug:true, the SDK installs only Dedupe/EventFilters/FunctionToString/ConversationId/LinkedErrors/Fetch/HttpServer/RequestData/Console — no Mysql2 or Express integration and NO warning that build-time instrumentation is missing. This is by design: packages/cloudflare/src/baseSdk.ts:64 pulls db subscribers from `getRegisteredChannelIntegrations()`, which is only populated by the build-time channel injection; there is no runtime monkey-patching on workerd. Requiring the Vite plugin is therefore the documented, recommended path (~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx:18 "We recommend building your Cloudflare Worker with Vite and the sentryCloudflareVitePlugin plugin. It's the most complete way to get tracing for bundled dependencies in the Workers runtime."), and the repo's own reference app dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/cloudflare-orchestrion-mysql uses exactly `cloudflare() + sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()`. Refutation attempts that did NOT open an alternative path (all recorded, none change the verdict): - Non-Vite bundling: `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild` exists and DOES inject (`orchestrion:mysql2:query` / `orchestrion:mysql2:execute` present in dist-esbuild*/index.js), but a hand-rolled esbuild pre-bundle does not boot on workerd — `Uncaught Error: Dynamic require of "tty" is not supported`, then after node:-prefixing and a createRequire banner `Uncaught Error: No such module "node:process"` — because pre-bundling bypasses wrangler's/@cloudflare/vite-plugin's unenv node-compat aliasing. `@sentry/cloudflare` exports only ".", "./request" and "./vite", so there is no supported non-Vite path. - `vite dev` (which the docs offer as the replacement for `wrangler dev`) cannot start this app at all: `TypeError: The "superCtor.prototype" property must be of type object. Received undefined` in @cloudflare/vite-plugin's runner-worker. This is NOT Sentry's fault — the identical failure occurs with `cloudflare()` alone (vite.config.nosentry.mjs, wDevNS.log). Use `vite build` + `wrangler dev` for express-on-workerd. One real caveat, and it is an express defect rather than a db defect: with `buildTimeInstrumentation` on (the default), registering routes at module scope crashes the Worker at startup — ✘ [ERROR] service core:user:v4_express_db_b: Uncaught Error: Disallowed operation called within global scope. Asynchronous I/O (ex: fetch() or connect()), setting a timeout, and generating random values are not allowed within global scope. at null.<anonymous> (index.js:58643:37) in route2 Line 58643 of distb/v4_express_db_b/index.js is `return tr_ch_apm$register.start.runStores(__apm$ctx, () => {`, i.e. the injected `orchestrion:router:register` channel already has subscribers at module-evaluation time (the injected snippet runs `globalThis.__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION_INJECT__ = orchestrionModuleInjected("router", expressIntegration)` when `router` is first required) and the subscriber does work workerd forbids in global scope. Control proves Sentry causes it: the same src2/index.js built with `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ buildTimeInstrumentation: false })` (vite.config.c.mjs, distc) boots and serves `/db` fine. Module-scope `import mysql from 'mysql2/promise'` is not affected — only calling an instrumented express API at module scope is. Creating the mysql connection inside the request handler is fine on workerd and still produces both db spans. Also confirmed: mysql2 needs `disableEval: true` in the connection options; without it the query text generation throws `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context` (the connect and query spans are still emitted). The `mysql@2` driver needs no such flag. Files: src/index.js (working lazy app), src2/index.js (module-scope crash case), vite.config.mjs / vite.config.b.mjs / vite.config.c.mjs, wrangler.jsonc / wrangler.b.jsonc, build-esbuild{,2,3}.mjs, REPRO.md, logs wS.log wStream.log wA.log wB3.log wC.log wESB*.log wDev.log wDevNS.log — all under $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-express-cf-dbspans/. node_modules removed; reinstall per REPRO.md (remember `npm approve-scripts --allow-scripts-pending && npm rebuild`, otherwise workerd and esbuild have no binary). All processes I started were killed.
Workaround: Build the Worker with Vite: `vite.config.mjs` = `defineConfig({ plugins: [cloudflare(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()] })`, then `npx vite build && npx wrangler dev --config dist/<worker>/wrangler.json` (not plain `wrangler dev`, and not `vite dev` — that shape cannot start express on workerd at all). Because the injected express channel makes a module-scope `app.get(...)` crash the Worker in global scope, build the express app lazily on the first request: keep `const inner = httpServerHandler({ port: 8080 })` at module scope but create the app and call `app.listen` inside `fetch` (`let listening; async fetch(req, env, ctx) { if (!listening) { const app = buildApp(); listening = new Promise(r => app.listen(8080, r)); } await listening; return inner.fetch(req, env, ctx); }`). Create the mysql connection inside the route handler and pass `disableEval: true` for `mysql2`.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info('express-cf-log', { where: 'route' })` inside a handler arrived as a log envelope `info: express-cf-log` on both shapes, on the default (always-on) logging with no `enableLogs` option. Flushed on the timer, visible after ~7s.
client errors· not-runNo browser surface: this is a server-only Express Worker, there is no client bundle or browser SDK in the app.

A page must say that Express 5 boots unchanged on workerd with the nodejs_compat and enable_nodejs_http_server_modules flags behind httpServerHandler from cloudflare:node, a path that is undocumented today. Route errors are only reported as unhandled after calling setupExpressErrorHandler on the app, imported from @sentry/server-utils, which must be installed because @sentry/cloudflare does not re-export it. Handler and router spans with parameterized names on plain wrangler dev require calling patchExpressModule from @sentry/core/server before building the app, and only in the stream lifecycle. Headline: Express 5 runs on Workers today and the develop @sentry/cloudflare SDK covers it better than expected — async context propagates cleanly through the `cloudflare:node` httpServerHandler bridge, so isolation, trace continuation, scope tags and child spans all work inside express handlers with no extra wiring. But two things stand between this and a docs page. 1. BUG (blocking): with the Cloudflare Vite plugin's default `buildTimeInstrumentation: true`, the canonical Express entry — `app.get(...)` and `app.listen()` at module scope, exactly what every Express docs page shows — crashes the Worker at startup with `Disallowed operation called within global scope … generating random values are not allowed within global scope`. The injected wrapper around `Router.prototype.route` finds live channel subscribers during module evaluation and runs the Sentry subscriber (which mints a span id) at global scope. Confirmed by a control build: the same top-level entry with `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ buildTimeInstrumentation: false })` boots fine, and the same entry under plain `wrangler dev` boots fine. Workaround used here is to defer `express()` + route registration + `listen()` into the first request. Either the express subscriber must not start a span for route registration, or `route`/`Router.prototype[method]` should not be an instrumented operation at all. 2. Sharp cliff between the two run shapes. Plain `wrangler dev` gives raw-URL transaction names (`GET /users/42`, source `url`) and silently swallows every route error — the only signal is a transaction with `status: internal_error` and no event. That is the shape a user lands on if they follow the Cloudflare quickstart and add express themselves. Everything good (route templates, `handler` spans, automatic `auto.http.express` error capture, db spans) requires Vite + the Sentry plugin. A docs page must lead with the Vite shape. Smaller observations: - mysql2 needs `disableEval: true` to run on workerd at all (`EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`). Unrelated to Sentry but any db example on this runtime has to say so. - Under traceLifecycle 'stream' the http.server span carries `http.route: /users/:id` but no `sentry.source` attribute at all; the name is already parameterized, so this may be intentional, flagging it for the span-name owner. - `vite build` emits an `assets` entry that makes `wrangler dev --config dist/.../wrangler.json` fail with `The directory specified by the "assets.directory" field … does not exist: dist/client` on a rebuild-triggered reload. Creating an empty `dist/client` works around it. Possibly a @cloudflare/vite-plugin quirk for asset-less workers, not a Sentry issue. - Not tested: `wrapRequestHandler` from `@sentry/cloudflare/request` (withSentry was enough), Durable Objects, deployed (non-local) workerd.

Fastify on Cloudflare M-fastify-cf

Fastify 5.12.3 (find-my-way 9.9.0 router) · Cloudflare Workers (wrangler 4.x dev / workerd 1.20260903.1, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, compatibility_flags ["nodejs_compat", "enable_nodejs_http_server_modules"], httpServerHandler from cloudflare:node) · viable: no

Setup the docs would have to show

Not viable. No wiring exists that makes Fastify serve a request on workerd, so there is nothing a docs page could show. Two independent workerd restrictions block it, in this order:

1) `const app = Fastify()` at module scope throws "Disallowed operation called within global scope" (Fastify's boot sequence generates random values / schedules work). This one IS workaroundable, by constructing the app lazily on the first request:

   let booting;
   function boot() {
     if (!booting) booting = (async () => { const app = Fastify(); app.get('/users/:id', ...); await app.listen({ port: 8080, host: '127.0.0.1' }); })();
     return booting;
   }
   const nodeHandler = httpServerHandler({ port: 8080 });
   export default { async fetch(req, env, ctx) { await boot(); return nodeHandler.fetch(req, env, ctx); } };

2) With that in place, registering ANY route throws `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`. Fastify's router `find-my-way` compiles matchers with `new Function` in four unconditional places, with no non-eval fallback:
   node_modules/find-my-way/lib/node.js:220            (StaticNode._compilePrefixMatch)
   node_modules/find-my-way/lib/handler-storage.js:78  (params object builder)
   node_modules/find-my-way/lib/handler-storage.js:171 (_getHandlerMatchingConstraints)
   node_modules/find-my-way/lib/constrainer.js:172     (deriveSyncConstraints)
   Workers forbid dynamic code generation at runtime and there is no compatibility flag that lifts it, so this is a hard wall, not a configuration problem. Downgrading does not help: find-my-way 7.7.0 (Fastify 4) has the same four `new Function` call sites.

Control test proves the Cloudflare half of the shape is fine: the same wrangler config with a plain `node:http` server behind `httpServerHandler({ port: 8081 })` serves `GET /users/42` with 200 and the correct body. So the blocker is Fastify's router specifically, not `enable_nodejs_http_server_modules`.

@sentry/cloudflare was installed ($REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-cloudflare-10.67.0.tgz + sentry-core) but never wired, because the app never served a request. The intended wiring would have been `export default withSentry(env => ({ dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, tunnel: 'http://127.0.0.1:<port>/' }), { async fetch(req, env, ctx) { await boot(); return nodeHandler.fetch(req, env, ctx); } })`.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors· not-runFastify never serves a request on workerd: route registration throws EvalError before any handler can run, so no error can be thrown from a handler in the first place. No Sentry init was performed.
route names· not-run`/users/:id` cannot be registered at all. `app.get('/users/:id', ...)` is exactly the call that throws `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context` from find-my-way's `_compilePrefixMatch`.
isolation· not-runNo request ever reaches a handler, so no scope isolation can be observed.
incoming trace· not-runNo request ever reaches a handler; every request to the Fastify worker returns 500 with the EvalError.
outgoing fetch· not-runNo handler runs, so no outgoing fetch is made. Cloudflare's own http.client instrumentation is untestable here because the framework never gets to call fetch.
db spans· not-runmysql@2 was installed but never imported into a working worker. No instrumentation path (Cloudflare Vite plugin or otherwise) was exercised, because the framework itself does not boot.
logs· not-runSentry was never initialized in a running worker, so no log envelopes could be produced.

Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions Fastify on Cloudflare. `grep -rni "cloudflare|workerd|worker" ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/fastify/` returns zero hits, and `grep -rni "fastify" ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/` returns zero hits. The Cloudflare guide's own list of supported frameworks (~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-24) names Astro, Hono, Hydrogen, Next.js, Nuxt, Remix, SvelteKit and TanStack Start, and does not include Fastify or any other Node HTTP framework. The only places the two strings co-occur are `<PlatformSection>` supported/notSupported attribute lists in common docs (for example ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/common/tracing/index.mdx:58 and ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/common/logs/index.mdx:212), which list `javascript.fastify` and `javascript.cloudflare` as separate sibling platforms, never as a combination. Nothing needs adding or correcting: the combination is impossible and the docs correctly do not claim it.

Documented: no

The docs are silent, and that silence leads users into a dead end. A page must state that Fastify does not run on Cloudflare Workers behind httpServerHandler, and why: constructing the app at module scope throws a disallowed-global-scope error because Fastify's boot generates random values and schedules work, and lazy construction on first request then hits a second workerd restriction that blocks serving. No Sentry capability could be exercised. The statement must be scoped to Workers; Fastify on Node is unaffected.

Page to write: Add a 'Node HTTP frameworks on Workers' section to guides/cloudflare/index.mdx near Known Limitations at :364 naming Fastify as not viable, plus a one-line runtime note in guides/fastify/index.mdx.

guides/fastify/index.mdx:4-9 (Node-only by declaration, no workerd mention); guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23 (no Fastify); no httpServerHandler or enable_nodejs_http_server_modules mention anywhere under docs or platform-includes.

The blocker is workerd's ban on dynamic code generation, a platform invariant with no compatibility flag. It is not a Sentry issue and not a wiring issue. Fastify's router (find-my-way) compiles path matchers, params builders and constraint deriving with `new Function` at route-registration time, so `app.get('/users/:id', ...)` throws before any request is served. Fastify 4 (find-my-way 7.7.0) has the same four call sites, so downgrading is not an escape. Fastify would additionally hit the same wall in `ajv` (schema validation) and `fast-json-stringify` (response serialization) as soon as any route schema is declared. A nuance worth recording for the other Cloudflare cells: `enable_nodejs_http_server_modules` + `httpServerHandler` itself works fine on this workerd (the control worker served 200s), but most Node frameworks cannot be constructed at module scope, because workerd forbids random-value generation, timers and async I/O in global scope. The lazy-boot-on-first-fetch pattern in app/src/index.mjs is the general workaround for that first failure and is worth reusing in the Express/Hapi/Nest Cloudflare cells. I did not install or test 10.73.0. @sentry/cloudflare 10.67.0 from $REPRO/_toolbox/pack was installed but never initialized, since the app never served a request, so no sink or recorder was started. All processes I started were killed and both node_modules trees were removed; the wrangler/workerd processes still running on this machine belong to other agents' cells (M-express-cf, M-nestjs-cf, M-oak-cf, M-hapi-cf).

Setup the docs would have to show

Koa runs on workerd unchanged once `enable_nodejs_http_server_modules` is on. Verified first WITHOUT Sentry (GET / -> {"ok":true}, GET /users/42 -> {"id":"42"}).

Packages: `npm install koa@3 @koa/router wrangler@4 $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-cloudflare-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz`
IMPORTANT: you must pass the `server-utils` AND `opentelemetry` tarballs too. Installing only the cloudflare + core tarballs makes npm pull the *published* 10.67.0 of those two, and esbuild then fails the wrangler build with `Could not resolve "@sentry/server-utils/no-diagnostic-channels"` and six `No matching export in "@sentry/core/build/esm/index.js" for import "SEMANTIC_ATTRIBUTE_SENTRY_SOURCE" / "SPAN_KIND" / "spanShouldInferOtelSource" / "spanSourceWasExplicitlySet" / "markSpanForOtelSourceInference" / "_INTERNAL_startInactiveSpan"`.

{ "name": "koa-cf-probe", "main": "src/index.js",
  "compatibility_date": "2026-05-01",
  "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat", "enable_nodejs_http_server_modules"] }

Entry (src/index.js) - there is no separate instrument file; `withSentry` wraps the object `httpServerHandler` returns:
```js
import { httpServerHandler } from 'cloudflare:node';
import * as Sentry from '@sentry/cloudflare';
import Koa from 'koa';
import Router from '@koa/router';
import mysql from 'mysql';

const conn = mysql.createConnection({ host: '127.0.0.1', port: 3307, user: 'root', database: 'app' });

const app = new Koa();
const router = new Router();
router.get('/users/:id', ctx => { ctx.body = { id: ctx.params.id }; });

// REQUIRED, otherwise every handler error is silently swallowed
app.on('error', err => Sentry.captureException(err, { mechanism: { type: 'koa.onerror', handled: false } }));

app.use(router.routes()).use(router.allowedMethods());
app.listen(8080);

export default Sentry.withSentry(
  env => ({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }),   // add traceLifecycle: 'static' for transaction envelopes
  httpServerHandler({ port: 8080 }),
);
```
Run: `npx wrangler dev --port <port> --inspector-port 0`.

Do NOT add `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()`: with its default `buildTimeInstrumentation: true` the Koa worker no longer boots at all (see db spans).

Adding `app.on('error', err => Sentry.captureException(err, {mechanism:{type:'koa.onerror',handled:false}}))` (Koa's own idiom) makes it arrive, with sdk `sentry.javascript.cloudflare`, full request data (url/method/headers), and the same trace id as the request span, so the manual capture is correctly scoped to the request. There is no automatic mechanism, so the mechanism type is whatever the user writes. `hasContextLine` is false. Same under stream and static lifecycle; under static the transaction gets `status: "internal_error"`. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. Koa errors ARE captured automatically on Cloudflare with the develop SDK — no `app.on('error')` needed. The reporter's setup was missing the one thing that turns Koa instrumentation on in a Worker: the `@sentry/cloudflare/vite` plugin's build-time instrumentation. A plain `wrangler dev` on a hand-written `src/index.js` (esbuild, no Vite) can never instrument Koa, because on Cloudflare the koa integration is not in the default set at all — `getBaseDefaultIntegrations()` in packages/cloudflare/src/baseSdk.ts only adds `...getRegisteredChannelIntegrations()`, i.e. whatever the Vite plugin registered on `globalThis.__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__.integrations` at build time. `koaIntegration` is wired for that path (packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/config/channel-integration-definitions.ts:48 `{ exportName: 'koaIntegration', modules: ['koa'] }`, config in packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/config/koa.ts), and the integration auto-attaches the error listener on koa's `callback` channel (packages/server-utils/src/integrations/koa/koa-error-handler.ts, `attachKoaErrorHandler`) with `mechanism: { type: 'auto.middleware.koa', handled: false }`, captured inside the stashed request span. WHY THEIR VITE ATTEMPT LOOKED LIKE "DOES NOT BOOT" — and the one real constraint With the plugin on and the Koa app built at module scope (`const app = new Koa(); app.use(router.routes()); app.listen(8080)` at top level), workerd refuses to start: service core:user:koa-cf-c: Uncaught Error: Disallowed operation called within global scope. Asynchronous I/O (ex: fetch() or connect()), setting a timeout, and generating random values are not allowed within global scope. at index.js:54314:34 in use at index.js:57063:5 Line 54314 is inside the instrumented `Application.prototype.use`: `tr_ch_apm$use.start.runStores(__apm$ctx, ...)`. So it is the injected `diagnostics_channel` `runStores` call in `app.use()` — reached because `hasSubscribers` is truthy on workerd's shim — that performs the disallowed global-scope operation, not `app.listen()`. I bisected this: - Vite + `cloudflare()` only, module-scope app: boots, `GET /users/42 -> {"id":"42"}`. - Vite + `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ buildTimeInstrumentation: false })`, module-scope app: boots, `{"id":"42"}`. - Vite + bare `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()`, module-scope app: the error above. - Vite + bare `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()`, app built inside `fetch`: boots and gives everything quoted above. That constraint is real and undocumented, but it is a boot-shape bug in the injected `use` wrapper, not the absence of an error-capture mechanism. Workaround: Two, depending on how much you want to change. 1. Full automatic capture (preferred, refutes the finding): build the Worker with Vite and add the Sentry plugin, then construct the Koa app lazily inside the first request instead of at module scope. vite.config.mjs: ```js import { cloudflare } from '@cloudflare/vite-plugin'; import { sentryCloudflareVitePlugin } from '@sentry/cloudflare/vite'; export default { plugins: [cloudflare(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()] }; ``` src/index.js: ```js import { httpServerHandler } from 'cloudflare:node'; import * as Sentry from '@sentry/cloudflare'; import Koa from 'koa'; import Router from '@koa/router'; let booted = false; function boot() { if (booted) return; booted = true; const app = new Koa(); const router = new Router(); router.get('/users/:id', ctx => { ctx.body = { id: ctx.params.id }; }); app.use(router.routes()).use(router.allowedMethods()); app.listen(8080); // must run inside a handler, not at module scope } const inner = httpServerHandler({ port: 8080 }); // this one is fine at module scope export default Sentry.withSentry( env => ({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }), { fetch(request, env, ctx) { boot(); return inner.fetch(request, env, ctx); } }, ); ``` `vite build`, then `wrangler dev --config dist/<worker>/wrangler.json`. Errors thrown in middleware/routes now arrive with `mechanism.type: 'auto.middleware.koa'`, `handled: false`, correct trace id and request data, and the transaction/server span is route-named. No `app.on('error')`. 2. If you cannot use Vite (hand-written entry + plain `wrangler dev`), the reporter's `app.on('error', err => Sentry.captureException(err, { mechanism: { type: 'koa.onerror', handled: false } }))` remains the only option — and there you also lose the `router` spans and the route-named transaction. Do NOT do 1 with a module-scope `new Koa()` / `app.use()`: the injected `use` wrapper calls `diagnostics_channel` `runStores` there and workerd rejects it with "Disallowed operation called within global scope … at index.js:… in use", so the Worker never starts. `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ buildTimeInstrumentation: false })` avoids the crash but also removes the Koa instrumentation, so it is not a fix.

Stream lifecycle: `GET /users/42` produces a segment named just `GET` with `sentry.segment.name.source = "url"` and no `http.route` attribute. Static lifecycle: `transaction: "GET /users/42"`, `source: "url"` - the raw path, so high cardinality. Manual naming does work from inside a Koa handler: `Sentry.updateSpanName(Sentry.getRootSpan(Sentry.getActiveSpan()), `${ctx.method} ${ctx._matchedRoute}`)` yields `GET /named/:id` with source `custom` in both lifecycles. Koa/@koa/router route names work on Cloudflare Workers with develop (10.67.0). @koa/router IS instrumented: `koaIntegration` lives in `@sentry/server-utils` (`packages/server-utils/src/integrations/koa/index.ts`), its orchestrion transform config is in `packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/config/koa.ts`, and `channel-integration-definitions.ts` maps `{ exportName: 'koaIntegration', modules: ['koa'] }`, so `getBaseDefaultIntegrations` auto-registers it from the global orchestrion marker. It renames the root span via `setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute`. The channels are injected at build time, so the app MUST be built with `@sentry/cloudflare/vite`; plain `wrangler dev` on a hand-written entry (what the original probe did) can never produce them. TWO changes are needed together: 1. Build with Vite: `cloudflare()` from `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` + `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` (all defaults, `buildTimeInstrumentation: true`), then `npx wrangler dev --config dist/<worker>/wrangler.json`. 2. Build the Koa app INSIDE the fetch handler, not at module scope. Why (2): the injected `Application.prototype.use` body ends in `tr_ch_apm$use.start.runStores(...)`, and workerd rejects that outside a request context. I rebuilt the reporter's module-scope shape (src2/index.js + vite.config.top.mjs + wrangler.top.jsonc) and got the identical failure: service core:user:v4_koa_cf_top: Uncaught Error: Disallowed operation called within global scope. Asynchronous I/O (ex: fetch() or connect()), setting a timeout, and generating random values are not allowed within global scope. at null.<anonymous> (index.js:54317:34) in use at null.<anonymous> (index.js:67832:5) index.js:67832 is `app.use(router.routes()).use(router.allowedMethods());` and index.js:54317 is inside the injected Koa wrapper, in the `use` frame: if (!tr_ch_apm_hasSubscribers(tr_ch_apm$use)) return __apm$traced(); return tr_ch_apm$use.start.runStores(__apm$ctx, () => { ... }) // <- line 54317 So `buildTimeInstrumentation` injects an `orchestrion:koa` channel around `Koa.prototype.use`, the Sentry subscriber starts a span there, span-id generation calls a random source, and workerd forbids random values at global scope. It never even reaches `app.listen`. This is why the reporter's mysql-free variant failed identically (it still had `app.use` at module scope) and why the crash disappeared with `buildTimeInstrumentation: false` (no channel, no subscriber, no span). Nothing about mysql or `ssr.noExternal` is involved. It is a real sharp edge: the instrumented `app.use` is what crashes, and the workerd error text points at Cloudflare's handler docs, not at Sentry, so it is very hard to attribute. Not tested: `vite dev` (the sibling express probe found @cloudflare/vite-plugin's own dev runner crashes with `superCtor.prototype ... Received undefined`, unrelated to Sentry) and esbuild + orchestrion (express probe: worker will not boot, `Dynamic require of "tty"`).
Workaround: Build the Koa app and call `app.listen()` inside the `fetch` handler instead of at module scope, and keep `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` at its defaults. Concretely: hoist `const inner = httpServerHandler({ port: 8080 })` to module scope (that is safe), but put `new Koa()`, every `app.use(...)`, the router wiring and `app.listen(8080)` behind a memoized `ensureApp()` that the handler awaits before delegating to `inner.fetch`. With mysql2, also pass `disableEval: true` to `createConnection`.

client errors· not-runNo browser surface: this is a server-only Koa app on workerd, there is no client bundle and no @sentry/browser in play.

Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions Koa on Cloudflare, and nothing in the docs mentions the mechanism this cell depends on. `grep -rin koa docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/` returns nothing; `grep -rin "cloudflare\|workerd" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/koa/` returns nothing; `grep -rin "httpServerHandler\|enable_nodejs_http_server_modules" docs/ platform-includes/` returns nothing at all. The Koa guide is a 12-line stub (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/koa/index.mdx:1-12) declaring `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` and `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, i.e. it sends the reader to @sentry/node, which is not what runs here. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/ lists only astro, hono, hydrogen-react-router, hydrogen-remix, nextjs, nuxt, remix, sveltekit, tanstack-start - no Koa and no generic "node:http server on Workers" page. Separately, docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:63 tells readers to import from `@sentry/cloudflare/nodejs_compat`, an entrypoint that does not exist on develop.

Documented: no

A page must say that Koa 3 with @koa/router runs unchanged on workerd once the Node HTTP server flag is set and the server is served through httpServerHandler. Error capture and route names exist only when the Worker is built with Vite and the Sentry Cloudflare plugin, which injects Koa's diagnostics channels at build time and registers the app error listener; without that build step errors are lost and route names are broken. It must state the module-scope rule that follows: the Koa app, every use call and listen must run inside the fetch handler, because the instrumented use starts a span at worker startup and workerd rejects it; the httpServerHandler call may stay at module scope. Database spans need the same lazy construction plus the plugin. Isolation, incoming trace, outgoing fetch and logs work unaided.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/koa.mdx (new), linked from guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23; the module-scope restriction belongs as a shared note on guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx.

guides/koa/index.mdx:1-12 (12-line stub, Node fallback, body is one include); guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23 (no Koa) and no koa.mdx under guides/cloudflare/frameworks/; grep for httpServerHandler and enable_nodejs_http_server_modules returns zero; guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx:40-44 versus packages/cloudflare/src/vite/index.ts:37,87.

Two findings that are not about a single capability: 1. `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` with its default `buildTimeInstrumentation: true` makes a node:http/`httpServerHandler` worker fail to start on workerd ("Disallowed operation called within global scope"). Bisected across four builds; it is not mysql-specific and not `ssr.noExternal`-specific. This removes the only db-span path on Cloudflare for any framework of this shape (Koa, Express, Fastify behind httpServerHandler), so db spans here are broken rather than merely absent. 2. Installing the develop tarballs partially is a trap. `npm install sentry-cloudflare.tgz sentry-core.tgz` alone makes npm resolve `@sentry/server-utils` and `@sentry/opentelemetry` from the registry at the same 10.67.0 version, and the resulting mix fails the wrangler esbuild step with `Could not resolve "@sentry/server-utils/no-diagnostic-channels"` and six missing `@sentry/core` exports. All five tarballs (cloudflare, core, server-utils, server-runtime-injection, opentelemetry) must be on one command line. Positive surprise worth recording: AsyncLocalStorage propagates cleanly across the `httpServerHandler` -> node:http bridge. `Sentry.getActiveSpan()`, `Sentry.setTag`, `Sentry.captureException` and `Sentry.logger` all resolve to the correct per-request isolation scope inside Koa middleware, and captured events carry the Worker's request data. That is what makes errors, isolation, incoming trace, outgoing fetch and logs all work here despite there being zero Koa-specific instrumentation. The two real gaps a docs page would have to call out are (a) `app.on('error', ...)` is mandatory or Koa eats every handler error, and (b) there are no route names, so the user must call `Sentry.updateSpanName(Sentry.getRootSpan(Sentry.getActiveSpan()), `${ctx.method} ${ctx._matchedRoute}`)` themselves, which gives source `custom`, not `route`. Environment notes: wrangler writes `.wrangler/deploy/config.json` after a `vite build` and silently redirects later plain `wrangler dev` runs to the last dist output - this cost one confusing round of 404s before I spotted it. `client errors` is marked not-run because the app has no browser surface. All processes were killed and `node_modules` (308M) was removed; probe sources, configs and wrangler logs remain.

Hapi on Cloudflare M-hapi-cf

Hapi (@hapi/hapi 21) · cloudflare (workerd 1.20260903.1 via wrangler 4.129.0, compatibility_date 2026-05-01) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Hapi runs on Workers behind the node:http server shim. Two working shapes, they give different results.

A) Plain wrangler (esbuild) build - no framework instrumentation:
  npm install @hapi/hapi@21 mysql@2 wrangler@4 \
    $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-cloudflare-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz \
    $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz \
    $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz
  (all five @sentry tarballs are required: @sentry/cloudflare imports "@sentry/server-utils/no-diagnostic-channels", and npm otherwise resolves @sentry/opentelemetry@10.67.0 from the registry, which does not match the develop core build - see notes.)

  wrangler.jsonc:
    { "name": "m-hapi-cf", "main": "src/index.mjs",
      "compatibility_date": "2026-05-01",
      "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat", "enable_nodejs_http_server_modules"] }

  src/index.mjs:
    import * as Sentry from '@sentry/cloudflare';
    import Hapi from '@hapi/hapi';
    import { httpServerHandler } from 'cloudflare:node';
    const server = Hapi.server({ port: 8080, host: '0.0.0.0' });
    server.route({ method: 'GET', path: '/users/{id}', handler: req => ({ id: req.params.id }) });
    // Hapi swallows handler throws, so capture them yourself:
    server.ext('onPreResponse', (request, h) => {
      const r = request.response;
      if (r && r.isBoom) Sentry.captureException(r, { mechanism: { type: 'hapi.onPreResponse', handled: false } });
      return h.continue;
    });
    await server.start();
    export default Sentry.withSentry(
      env => ({ dsn: '___PUBLIC_DSN___', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' }),
      httpServerHandler({ port: 8080 }),
    );
  Run: npx wrangler dev --port <port> --inspector-port 0

B) Vite build with sentryCloudflareVitePlugin - needed for Hapi route names and db spans:
  npm install vite@6 @cloudflare/vite-plugin   (plus everything from A)
  vite.config.mjs:
    import { cloudflare } from '@cloudflare/vite-plugin';
    import { sentryCloudflareVitePlugin } from '@sentry/cloudflare/vite';
    export default { plugins: [cloudflare(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ autoInstrumentation: false })] };
  Run: npx vite build && npx wrangler dev --config dist/<worker>/wrangler.json --port <port> --inspector-port 0

  IMPORTANT for B: routes must NOT be registered at module scope. With the Sentry Vite plugin active,
  a module-scope server.route(...) throws at isolate startup (see errors evidence). The entry has to
  defer route registration and server.start() into the first fetch:
    let started;
    const nodeHandler = httpServerHandler({ port: 8080 });
    export default Sentry.withSentry(cfg, {
      async fetch(request, env, ctx) {
        started ??= (async () => { registerRoutes(); await server.start(); })();
        await started;
        return nodeHandler.fetch(request, env, ctx);
      },
    });

  mysql: use mysql@2, not mysql2 (mysql2 dies on workerd, see db spans).
  All results below were taken with traceLifecycle: 'static'.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✗ brokenA throw in a Hapi route handler never reaches Sentry, on either build. Hapi converts it to a Boom 500; the worker fetch span records status internal_error but no exception event is emitted. Adding integrations: [hapiIntegration()] from @sentry/server-utils does install ("Integration installed: Hapi") and does attach its handler (server.events['__SENTRY_HAPI_ERROR_HANDLER_STATE__'] === true), but the Hapi request/error podium event never fires on workerd, so nothing is captured. I attached my own listener on the identical event ({name:'request', channels:['error']}) and it never fired either, so this is Hapi's deferred event emission dying in the Workers I/O context, not a Sentry bug. The only mechanism that works is a server.ext('onPreResponse') that calls Sentry.captureException on response.isBoom; that event carries the right trace id and full request data. verified: confirmed-broken Reproduced on both build shapes with develop (10.67.0), workerd 1.20260903.1 / wrangler 4.129.0, and found the exact mechanism. No Sentry-side option, init placement, entry shape, bundler or trace lifecycle fixes it; a two-line app-level patch of workerd's `node:http` ServerResponse does, which proves the defect is in the runtime shim, not in the SDK. ROOT CAUSE (new, not in the original report) workerd's `node:http` ServerResponse emits `'close'` while `writableEnded` is still `false`, on every request, before the body is written. My probe (`run-b`, `/dump` endpoint reading a module-scope trace array, so nothing depends on `console.log` surviving the request context) shows it for a plain 200: onRequest /ok closeListeners=2 ext-onPreResponse /ok boom=false status=200 res-close writableEnded=false <- premature res-finish podium-response /ok boom=true status=499 hasClose=undefined hasError=false hapi reads that as a client disconnect, in two places, both of which key off `writableEnded`: - `@hapi/hapi/lib/request.js` `_listen()` -> `internals.event(...,'close')`: the guard `if (event === 'close' && request.raw.res.writableEnded) return;` does not fire, so hapi logs `['request','error','close']` and sets `request._eventContext.request = null`. - `@hapi/hapi/lib/transmit.js` `internals.pipe` -> `internals.end(env,'close')`: `res.writableEnded` is false, so hapi replaces `request.response` with `new Boom('Request close', { statusCode: disconnectStatusCode /* 499 */ })` and calls `res.end()` immediately. By the time `Request._finalize()` runs, `this.response` is that 499 Boom. `_finalize`'s error emit sits inside `if (this.response._close) { if (statusCode === 500 && this.response._error) this._log(tags, this.response._error, 'error'); ... }` — a Boom has no `_close` and no `_error`, so the whole block is skipped. That `_log(..., 'error')` is the ONLY producer of the `{name:'request', channels:['error']}` podium event that `attachHapiErrorHandler` / `hapiIntegration()` subscribe to. Hence no exception event, on any build. Every request on workerd ends as a hapi 499 "Request close", including successful ones. BASELINE (matches the report) Plain wrangler, `attachHapiErrorHandler(server)` (the `setupHapiErrorHandler` equivalent exported from `@sentry/server-utils`), `traceLifecycle: 'static'`: ok -> 200 len=11 throw/21 -> 500 len=96 sentinel/4 -> 200 len=11 --- SINK --- transaction | GET /ok | ok transaction | GET /throw/21 | internal_error <- no event for the throw event | sentinel-4 | generic transaction | GET /sentinel/4 | ok Vite + `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({autoInstrumentation:false})` + `integrations:[hapiIntegration()]` (`run-c`), same result, with route names working: transaction | GET /throw/{id} | route internal_error ['router GET /throw/{id}'] <- still no event WHAT MAKES IT WORK (app-level shim, not a Sentry setting) Deferring the premature close until 'finish', before `server.start()`: import { ServerResponse } from 'node:http'; const origEmit = ServerResponse.prototype.emit; ServerResponse.prototype.emit = function (event, ...args) { if (event === 'close' && !this.writableEnded && !this.destroyed) { this.once('finish', () => origEmit.call(this, 'close', ...args)); return true; } return origEmit.call(this, event, ...args); }; Plain wrangler + `attachHapiErrorHandler`: event | Error: v4-hapi-throw-31 | auto.function.hapi handled=False | trace ede63bc0aa424936a54505641bbc6ec6 transaction | GET /throw/31 | internal_error | trace ede63bc0aa424936a54505641bbc6ec6 Vite + `hapiIntegration()`, `traceLifecycle: 'static'`: event | Error: v4c-hapi-throw-61 | auto.function.hapi handled=False | transaction=GET /throw/{id} | trace f1c966b5bd65 transaction | GET /throw/{id} | source=route | internal_error | trace f1c966b5bd65 Vite + `hapiIntegration()`, `traceLifecycle: 'stream'`: event | Error: v4c-hapi-throw-71 | auto.function.hapi | transaction=GET /throw/{id} span | ['router /throw/{id}', 'http.server GET /throw/{id}'] So the SDK's hapi error handler, the isolation-scope transaction name and the trace correlation are all correct; they are simply never reached on workerd. VARIANTS THAT DO NOT HELP - `compatibility_date` 2026-09-01 (the newest this workerd accepts) with `nodejs_compat` + `enable_nodejs_http_server_modules`: identical, `res-close writableEnded=false`, no event. - `traceLifecycle` 'static' vs 'stream': no difference. - Plain esbuild vs Vite + `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin`: no difference for errors (Vite only adds route names and `router` spans). - `attachHapiErrorHandler(server)` called explicitly vs auto-registration via `hapiIntegration()`: both install (`server.events.__SENTRY_HAPI_ERROR_HANDLER_STATE__ === true`), both never fire. - Removing only the `_listen()` close listener in an `onRequest` ext: still 499, because `transmit.js internals.pipe` attaches its own `res.on('close')` later. - Buffering the node response body inside the fetch handler before returning: irrelevant, the close is emitted during transmit, not after the fetch resolves. SIDE FINDING (not Sentry's, worth recording) The same premature close truncates response bodies. A 50 KB JSON route returned 10 bytes with no shim, and 0 bytes with the shim (hapi keeps streaming into a response workerd has already finalized). Bodies up to ~100 bytes were intact in both modes. hapi on workerd is not usable for non-trivial payloads regardless of Sentry. Everything I report comes from the clean `run-b/` and `run-c/` subdirectories. REFERENCE APP: ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/node-hapi (src/app.js) is Node-only and relies on exactly the same podium `request`/`error` path, which is why it passes there and cannot pass on workerd. There is no Cloudflare hapi e2e app.
Workaround: Capture from `server.ext('onPreResponse')`, which runs before hapi's transmit and is therefore unaffected: server.ext('onPreResponse', (request, h) => { const r = request.response; if (r?.isBoom && (r.output?.statusCode ?? 500) >= 500) { Sentry.captureException(r, { mechanism: { type: 'hapi.onPreResponse', handled: false } }); } return h.continue; }); This carries the correct trace id and request data, and works on both the plain-wrangler and the Vite build. It is the only workaround that does not touch the runtime. Alternatively, to make the SDK's own `hapiIntegration()` / `attachHapiErrorHandler()` work unchanged, defer workerd's premature ServerResponse 'close' before `server.start()`: import { ServerResponse } from 'node:http'; const origEmit = ServerResponse.prototype.emit; ServerResponse.prototype.emit = function (event, ...args) { if (event === 'close' && !this.writableEnded && !this.destroyed) { this.once('finish', () => origEmit.call(this, 'close', ...args)); return true; } return origEmit.call(this, event, ...args); }; Verified to produce `auto.function.hapi` events with the right transaction name and trace id on both builds and both trace lifecycles, but it makes large/chunked bodies come back empty instead of truncated, so it is a diagnostic shim rather than a recommendation.
route names◐ partialPlain wrangler/esbuild build: transaction name is the raw path, "GET /users/42", source url - the Cloudflare SDK names the request span and knows nothing about Hapi's router. With the Vite build (sentryCloudflareVitePlugin, buildTimeInstrumentation default on) the injected @hapi/hapi channels give "GET /users/{id}" with source route, plus a nested 'router GET /users/{id}' span and a 'middleware ext - onPreResponse' span. verified: partial The reported claim is half right and half too narrow. Confirmed: with no build-time instrumentation the transaction is the raw path. Refuted: Vite is NOT required, and route names are reachable in a plain wrangler build with ~4 lines of user code. Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-hapi-cf-routenames (entries in run2/, results in RESULTS-run2.txt and RESULTS.txt; node_modules removed, restore with `npm install` — package.json points at the $REPRO/_toolbox/pack tarballs). Sink on 53911, worker on 53912/53913, workerd via wrangler 4.129.0, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, flags nodejs_compat + enable_nodejs_http_server_modules, traceLifecycle static unless noted. A) plain wrangler, module-scope routes, no plugin — `npx wrangler dev --config wr2-eager.jsonc --port 53912 --inspector-port 0` transaction | GET /ok | source= url | spans= [] transaction | GET /users/42 | source= url | spans= [] transaction | GET /posts/9/comments/3 | source= url | spans= [] A2) same build, a /probe handler logging Sentry.getActiveSpan() from inside the Hapi handler: PROBE {"hasActive":true,"activeJson":{"name":"GET /probe", ... "sentry.origin":"auto.http.cloudflare","sentry.op":"http.server","sentry.segment.name.source":"url", ...}} The Cloudflare request span is the active span inside Hapi handlers and exts — AsyncLocalStorage survives the node:http server shim — so user code can rename it. This is the key fact the earlier probe missed. B) same plain wrangler build, plus one onPreResponse ext (wr2-manual.jsonc): transaction | GET /ok | source= route | spans= [] transaction | GET /users/{id} | source= route | spans= [] transaction | GET /posts/{pid}/comments/{cid} | source= route | spans= [] B2) identical result on the develop default traceLifecycle 'stream' (wr2-manual-stream.jsonc): span | ["http.server GET /ok"] span | ["http.server GET /users/{id}"] span | ["http.server GET /posts/{pid}/comments/{cid}"] C) no Vite, automatic naming: esbuild + `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild`, driven by wrangler's own `build.command` (run2/build-orch.mjs, wr2-orch.jsonc), so it is still a single `npx wrangler dev`: transaction | GET /users/{id} | source= route | spans= ["router GET /users/{id}"] transaction | GET /posts/{pid}/comments/{cid} | source= route | spans= ["router GET /posts/{pid}/comments/{cid}"] D) documented wiring reproduced first-hand — `npx vite build --config vite.config.run2.mjs` then `npx wrangler dev --config dist-vite2/v4b_hapi_vite/wrangler.json`: transaction | GET /users/{id} | source= route | spans= ["router GET /users/{id}"] E) the residual defect behind the "routes must not be at module scope" caveat, re-confirmed (wr2-orch-eager.jsonc, module-scope server.route() with build-time instrumentation): service core:user:v4b-hapi-orch-eager: Uncaught Error: Disallowed operation called within global scope. Asynchronous I/O (ex: fetch() or connect()), setting a timeout, and generating random values are not allowed within global scope. at worker.js:60489:38 in route at worker.js:81183:10 in registerRoutes Cause is visible in the generated bundle (dist-run2e/worker.mjs:59547): var tr_ch_apm_hasSubscribers = (ch) => ch.start.hasSubscribers || ch.end.hasSubscribers || ch.asyncStart.hasSubscribers || ch.asyncEnd.hasSubscribers || ch.error.hasSubscribers; workerd exposes Channel.hasSubscribers as a method, not the boolean getter Node.js specifies, so the guard is always truthy and every instrumented call enters runStores() even with zero subscribers. Both bundler paths (Vite and esbuild) inherit this, so both force route registration and server.start() into the first fetch. The manual rename in (B) has no such constraint — module-scope Hapi setup is fine there. Why still "partial": automatic route naming needs build-time instrumentation, and a plain wrangler/esbuild deploy without a Sentry bundler plugin never gets it — @sentry/cloudflare names the request span from the URL and knows nothing about Hapi's router. Reference check: the repo has no Hapi-on-Cloudflare e2e app; the only build-time-instrumentation CF app, dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/cloudflare-orchestrion-mysql, uses `cloudflare()` + `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` in vite.config.ts, i.e. the Vite path only.
Workaround: Two, both verified. (1) No bundler plugin at all — keep the plain `wrangler dev`/deploy and module-scope routes, and rename the request span from a Hapi ext (run2/routes.mjs): server.ext('onPreResponse', (request, h) => { const active = Sentry.getActiveSpan(); const root = active ? Sentry.getRootSpan(active) : undefined; if (root && request.route?.path) { Sentry.updateSpanName(root, `${request.method.toUpperCase()} ${request.route.path}`); root.setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, 'route'); } return h.continue; }); `request.route.path` is Hapi's parameterized pattern, so the name stays low cardinality. `updateSpanName` alone would set the source to `custom`; the extra `SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE` attribute (exported from @sentry/cloudflare) makes it `route`. Works on both traceLifecycle values. It gives no `router` child span. (2) Automatic naming without Vite — pre-bundle with esbuild and `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild` (bundle:true, format:'esm', platform:'node', external:['cloudflare:*'], plus a `createRequire` banner), and hang that build off wrangler's `build.command` so `npx wrangler dev`/`wrangler deploy` stays the only command. This yields `GET /users/{id}` with source=route plus a `router GET /users/{id}` child span, identical to the Vite build. With either bundler plugin, `server.route(...)` and `server.start()` must be deferred into the first fetch, otherwise the isolate fails to boot.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent GET /isolate/{tag} requests each did Sentry.setTag('req_tag', tag), slept 50-100ms, then captureException. Each event carried only its own tag and matched its own transaction's trace id. Verified on both builds; withSentry's per-invocation isolation scope propagates through httpServerHandler into the Hapi handler.

db spans✓* works-waNeeded the Cloudflare Vite plugin (buildTimeInstrumentation, on by default). With it, a module-scope mysql@2 pool queried inside the handler produced 'db SELECT id, name FROM users' nested in the transaction. With the plain wrangler/esbuild build the same query ran fine but produced no span at all. mysql2/promise cannot be used on workerd: pool.query rejects with "Code generation from strings disallowed for this context" (mysql2 compiles row parsers with new Function). mysql@2 connects to 127.0.0.1:3307 from the Worker without any extra config. verified: works-after-all REFUTED: db spans on Hapi + Cloudflare Workers do NOT need the Cloudflare Vite plugin. The real requirement is build-time orchestrion instrumentation from ANY of the SDK's bundler plugins. `@sentry/server-utils` ships `./orchestrion/{vite,rollup,esbuild,webpack,webpack-loader,bun}`; `@sentry/cloudflare/vite` is just `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` (vite) + the auto-instrument plugin. Pre-bundling the Worker yourself with esbuild + `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild`, then pointing wrangler at that bundle, gives the same db spans with no vite and no @cloudflare/vite-plugin installed. Exact change (probe at $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-hapi-cf-dbspans/run-b/): build.mjs: import { sentryOrchestrionPlugin } from '@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild'; esbuild.build({ entryPoints:['./src/index.mjs'], outfile:'./dist/worker.mjs', bundle:true, format:'esm', platform:'node', target:'es2022', external:['cloudflare:*'], banner:{ js: <require shim, see below> }, plugins:[forceEsmServerUtils, sentryOrchestrionPlugin()] }) wrangler.jsonc: { "main": "dist/worker.mjs", "compatibility_date": "2026-05-01", "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat","enable_nodejs_http_server_modules"] } Run: node build.mjs && npx wrangler dev --port 43231 --inspector-port 0 WITH the esbuild orchestrion plugin (sink /__items, traceLifecycle 'static', mysql@2 module-scope pool, query inside the Hapi handler): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db/{id}","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare","spans":["router GET /db/{id}","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /ok","op":"http.server","source":"route","spans":["router GET /ok"]} Control, IDENTICAL bundle minus the plugin (`node build.mjs --no-orchestrion`, dist-plain/worker.mjs): {"t":"transaction","n":"GET /db/7","src":"url","spans":[]} {"t":"transaction","n":"GET /sentinel","src":"url","spans":[]} So the plugin, not the banner shim or the entry shape, is what produces the span. Route names (source=route, `router` span) also come with it, so the reported "needs the Vite plugin for Hapi route names" is refuted by the same run. Two gotchas found: 1. esbuild require shim is mandatory. Without a banner, esbuild rewrites the CJS `require()` calls left in Hapi/mysql/the injected orchestrion snippet into `__require()`, and workerd dies at startup: "service core:user:verify4-hapi-esbuild-nobanner: Uncaught Error: Dynamic require of \"node:async_hooks\" is not supported / at worker.js:33:50 in __require2" Fix: `banner.js` that statically imports the node builtins workerd provides and sets `globalThis.require = id => map[id]`. (build-nobanner.mjs reproduces the crash.) 2. The injected snippet's `import '@sentry/server-utils'` resolves to the CJS build under esbuild; a tiny onResolve plugin forcing `node_modules/@sentry/server-utils/build/esm/index.js` avoids that. `@sentry/server-utils` does NOT list `@apm-js-collab/code-transformer-bundler-plugins` as a dependency, but it is vendored into the tarball (build/esm/vendored/...), so no extra install is needed. Also REFUTED, secondary: "mysql2 cannot be used on workerd". mysql2@3.24.3 works and is instrumented once you pass mysql2's own `disableEval: true` pool option: GET /db2/{id} -> {"rows":[{"id":1,"name":"ada"},{"id":2,"name":"linus"}]} {"t":"transaction","n":"GET /db2/{id}","src":"route","spans":["router GET /db2/{id}","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]} Without `disableEval` the same pool returns {"error":"Code generation from strings disallowed for this context"} — a mysql2 configuration issue, not an SDK or workerd-vs-Sentry limitation. Note the span is still emitted for the eval pool because the failure happens after the query span opens. Still true from the original report: `npx wrangler dev` on unbundled source (wrangler's internal esbuild) produces no db span, and there is no supported way to add a plugin to wrangler's own bundler — so "plain wrangler build" remains broken. The reference e2e app (~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/cloudflare-orchestrion-mysql) only covers the vite path. Probe files (node_modules removed; reinstall with `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{cloudflare,core,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry}-10.67.0.tgz @hapi/hapi@21 mysql@2 mysql2@3 wrangler@4 esbuild@0.25`): $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-hapi-cf-dbspans/run-b/src/index.mjs .../run-b/build.mjs, build-nobanner.mjs, wrangler.jsonc, wrangler.plain.jsonc, wrangler.nobanner.jsonc .../run-b/dev-b.log (with plugin), dev-plain.log (control), dev-c.log (mysql2), dev-nobanner.log (__require crash) One environment note: the shared directory carried a stale `.wrangler/deploy/config.json` from an earlier run that silently redirected `wrangler dev` to a different, vite-built worker; I overwrote it per run so each result is against the bundle named in its wrangler config.
Workaround: Bundle the Worker yourself before wrangler sees it: `import { sentryOrchestrionPlugin } from '@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild'` in an esbuild build (format esm, platform node, external ['cloudflare:*'], plus a banner that maps `require` to statically imported node: builtins), set wrangler `main` to the emitted bundle, and run `wrangler dev`. For mysql2 on workerd, pass `disableEval: true` to createPool/createConnection.
