Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions Hapi on Cloudflare. The Hapi guide is Node-only by declaration: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hapi/index.mdx:4-5 sets `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` and `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, and its whole body is `<PlatformContent includePath="getting-started-node" />` (index.mdx:12). The Cloudflare guide's framework list has no hapi page - docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/ holds only astro, hono, hydrogen-react-router, hydrogen-remix, nextjs, nuxt, remix, sveltekit, tanstack-start. Nothing under docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/ mentions hapi at all (grep -ril hapi returns nothing), and nothing mentions `enable_nodejs_http_server_modules` or `httpServerHandler` (grep over the guide dir returns only nodejs_compat hits). The one page that is load-bearing for this cell, docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx, is also stale against develop: line 6 says `<AvailableSince version="10.68.0" />`, and lines 29-46 tell users to opt in with `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ _experimental: { useDiagnosticsChannelInjection: true } })`, while the develop build's vite types expose only top-level `autoInstrumentation` and `buildTimeInstrumentation` (node_modules/@sentry/cloudflare/build/types/vite/index.d.ts), both already on by default.

Documented: no

A page must say that Hapi 21 runs on Workers behind the node:http shim, and document one hard defect plus two build shapes. On workerd the response emits close before finish with writableEnded still false, hapi reads that as a client disconnect, turns every response into a 499, and its request and error events never fire, so the Hapi integration captures nothing. Show the app-side fix, an onRequest extension that drops the premature close before hapi's transmit sees it, which restores capture, the transaction name and the auto.function.hapi mechanism. Parameterized transaction names require build-time instrumentation, either the Cloudflare Vite plugin or the orchestrion plugin for esbuild, rollup or webpack, with a plain-wrangler fallback that renames the root span in an onPreResponse extension. Database spans need the same build-time instrumentation. Isolation, incoming trace, outgoing fetch and logs work unaided.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/hapi.mdx (new), linked from guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23, plus a new shared page guides/cloudflare/features/build-time-instrumentation.mdx covering sentryOrchestrionPlugin for non-Vite bundlers, which is exported but documented nowhere.

guides/hapi/index.mdx:4-5 and :12 (Node fallback, body is one include); guides/cloudflare/frameworks/ has no hapi.mdx; guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23 (no Hapi); no mention of sentryOrchestrionPlugin or @sentry/server-utils/orchestrion anywhere in docs, although packages/server-utils/package.json:30-54 exports six orchestrion entry points.

Three things a docs page for this combination would have to say, and none of them are written down anywhere today: 1. Hapi route handler errors are invisible on Cloudflare. `hapiIntegration()` from @sentry/server-utils is not in @sentry/cloudflare's default integration set and is not re-exported from @sentry/cloudflare, so a user must import it from @sentry/server-utils by hand. Even then it does not work: the integration subscribes to `orchestrion:@hapi/hapi:start` / `:initialize`, `attachHapiErrorHandler` does run (state flag confirmed true on `server.events`), but the `{name:'request', channels:['error']}` podium event that the handler listens for never fires under workerd. A plain listener I registered on the same event never fired either, so Hapi's deferred emit is being dropped by the Workers I/O context, not by Sentry. The only recipe that captures is an `onPreResponse` extension. Worth a Sentry-side decision: either document the extension, or have the hapi integration hook a synchronous path (e.g. the `ext`/`route` channel error context) instead of the podium event. 2. `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` breaks module-scope Hapi route registration. The injected `tr_ch_apm$route.start.runStores(...)` wrapper around `Server.prototype.route` starts a Sentry span, which generates random values, which workerd forbids in global scope. Every Hapi-on-Workers example on the internet registers routes at module scope, so adding the plugin turns a working Worker into one that fails to boot with a message that names neither Sentry nor Hapi. The same is likely true of any framework whose setup calls an injected channel at module scope. Control build without the Sentry plugin boots fine, so the plugin is the cause. 3. Package-resolution trap for anyone following a tarball/local-build workflow: `@sentry/cloudflare` imports `@sentry/server-utils/no-diagnostic-channels`, and npm happily resolves `@sentry/opentelemetry@10.67.0` from the registry (the released v10 build) next to a develop-built `@sentry/core@10.67.0`, which then fails the vite/esbuild bundle with `No matching export in "@sentry/core/build/esm/index.js" for import "spanShouldInferOtelSource"`. Both tarballs must be passed on the install command line. Runtime facts worth recording elsewhere in the matrix: mysql2 is unusable on workerd ("Code generation from strings disallowed for this context") while mysql@2 works, including a module-scope pool reaching 127.0.0.1:3307. Hapi 21 itself needs nothing beyond `nodejs_compat` + `enable_nodejs_http_server_modules` and `httpServerHandler({ port })` - it booted and served parameterized routes on the very first try with no Sentry present.

Oak on Cloudflare M-oak-cf

Oak 17.2.0 (@oak/oak from JSR, installed as npm:@jsr/oak__oak@17.2.0) · Cloudflare Workers (wrangler 4.129.0 / workerd 1.20260903.1, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, nodejs_compat) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Oak's current line ships only to JSR; the npm package @oakserver/oak stops at 14.1.0. Install Oak 17 through the JSR npm bridge.

.npmrc:
  @jsr:registry=https://npm.jsr.io

Install:
  npm install '@oak/oak@npm:@jsr/oak__oak@17.2.0' wrangler@4 \
    $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-cloudflare-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz \
    $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz \
    $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz

@sentry/server-utils must come from the same worktree tarball. If npm resolves @sentry/server-utils@10.67.0 from the public registry, the wrangler build dies with: Could not resolve "@sentry/server-utils/no-diagnostic-channels" ... The path "./no-diagnostic-channels" is not exported by package "@sentry/server-utils".

wrangler.jsonc:
  { "name": "m-oak-cf", "main": "src/index.ts",
    "compatibility_date": "2026-05-01", "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"] }

src/index.ts (the entry shape a docs page would show):
  import { Application, Router } from '@oak/oak';
  import * as Sentry from '@sentry/cloudflare';

  const router = new Router();
  router.get('/users/:id', ctx => { ctx.response.body = { id: ctx.params.id }; });

  const app = new Application();
  app.use(router.routes());
  app.use(router.allowedMethods());

  export default Sentry.withSentry(
    env => ({ dsn: env.SENTRY_DSN, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }),
    {
      fetch(request, env, ctx) { return app.fetch(request, env, ctx); },
    } satisfies ExportedHandler,
  );

Oak documents Application.fetch as a Cloudflare fetch handler itself (node_modules/@oak/oak/application.js:287-302), so no adapter is needed. No Sentry Oak integration exists; withSentry alone is the whole wiring.

Run: npx wrangler dev --port <port> --inspector-port 0

Optional, only if you want parameterized transaction names, an Oak middleware registered before router.routes():
  app.use(async (ctx, next) => {
    await next();
    const matched = ctx.matched;
    const path = matched?.[matched.length - 1]?.path;
    const span = Sentry.getActiveSpan();
    if (path && span) {
      Sentry.updateSpanName(Sentry.getRootSpan(span), `${ctx.request.method} ${path}`);
      Sentry.getRootSpan(span).setAttribute('sentry.source', 'route');
    }
  });

No Vite build is required for anything, including db spans.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksOak does NOT swallow a handler throw: Application.fetch rethrows, workerd renders its default 500 stack page, and withSentry captures the error with mechanism auto.http.cloudflare, handled:false. Same in both lifecycles. One wart: the server transaction/span is still reported with status "ok" even though the request threw.
route names◐ partialOut of the box the parameterized route is never used. traceLifecycle static gives name "GET /users/42" with source "url" (raw path, high cardinality); traceLifecycle stream gives "GET" (method only). A hand-written Oak middleware reading ctx.matched and calling updateSpanName produces "GET /users/:id" with source "route" in stream lifecycle but only source "custom" in static lifecycle, and it never runs on the error path because the throw skips the code after await next(). verified: partial Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-oak-cf-routenames/ (src/index.ts has three modes selected by a `?mode=` query param: `off` = no middleware, `after` = the previously reported middleware verbatim, `fixed` = my corrected one; wrangler.jsonc, sink.mjs, wrangler-static.log, wrangler-stream3.log). Oak 17.2.0 via npm:@jsr/oak__oak, wrangler 4.129.0, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, nodejs_compat, @sentry/cloudflare 10.67.0 tarball, tunnel to a local sink. Rerun: `npm install '@oak/oak@npm:@jsr/oak__oak@17.2.0' wrangler@4 $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{cloudflare,core,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry}-10.67.0.tgz` with `@jsr:registry=https://npm.jsr.io` in .npmrc, then `PORT=52413 node sink.mjs &` and `npx wrangler dev --port 52414 --inspector-port 0` (static, from wrangler.jsonc vars) plus `npx wrangler dev --port 52481 --inspector-port 0 --var SENTRY_LIFECYCLE:stream` (stream). CONFIRMED (the out-of-box half): there is no Oak support anywhere on develop. `grep -rni oak` over packages/cloudflare/src and packages/server-runtime-injection/src finds nothing, there is no dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications app for Oak, and no ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/oak. With no middleware the segment name comes from wrapRequestHandlerWithInit's `getHttpSpanDetailsFromUrlObject`, so: static: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/42","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","trace_id":"d80144d2a6b74d40a9cd88636cd3c92f","sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare","spans":[]} stream: {"type":"span","items":["http.server GET"],"raw":[{"name":"GET","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.cloudflare","segsource":"url"}]} REFUTED (both specific defects in the report): 1. "route source only in stream, custom in static" is a bug in the reported snippet, not the SDK. `SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE` is `'sentry.segment.name.source'` (packages/core/src/index.ts:13, re-exported by packages/cloudflare/src/index.ts:91), and that is the key both lifecycles read: packages/core/src/tracing/sentrySpan.ts:451 `const source = this._attributes[SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE];`. The snippet wrote the legacy `'sentry.source'`, which the SDK ignores, so `updateSpanName`'s own `INTERNAL_setSegmentNameSourceIfSegment(span, 'custom')` (packages/core/src/utils/spanUtils.ts:492-498) stood in both lifecycles. The "route" the reporter saw in stream was their own raw attribute echoed back, not the segment name source. My sink prints both keys and shows exactly that for mode=after: static: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"custom",...} stream: {"type":"span","items":["http.server GET /users/:id"],"raw":[{"name":"GET /users/:id","is_segment":true,"source":"route","segsource":"custom"}]} Setting `Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE` instead gives `route` in both. 2. "never runs on the error path" is fixed by `try { await next(); } finally { ... }`. Oak rethrows out of `Application.fetch`, and the middleware's finally unwinds before wrapRequestHandlerWithInit's own catch, so the rename lands. Working middleware, registered before `router.routes()`: app.use(async (ctx, next) => { try { await next(); } finally { const path = ctx.matched?.[ctx.matched.length - 1]?.path; const span = Sentry.getActiveSpan(); if (path && span) { const root = Sentry.getRootSpan(span); const routeName = `${ctx.request.method} ${path}`; Sentry.updateSpanName(root, routeName); root.setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, 'route'); root.setAttribute('http.route', path); Sentry.getIsolationScope().setTransactionName(routeName); } } }); Result with it (mode=fixed), same worker, both lifecycles, success and error routes: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route",...} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /error/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route",...} {"type":"span","items":["http.server GET /users/:id"],"raw":[{"name":"GET /users/:id","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.cloudflare","segsource":"route"}]} {"type":"span","items":["http.server GET /error/:id"],"raw":[{"name":"GET /error/:id","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.cloudflare","segsource":"route"}]} {"type":"event","transaction":"GET /error/:id","exception":"Error: oak-route-boom","url":"http://127.0.0.1:52481/error/7?mode=fixed"} The `getIsolationScope().setTransactionName(routeName)` line is what puts `transaction: "GET /error/:id"` on the error event; without it the event has no transaction field in either lifecycle (that was also true of the baseline and of the reported snippet). This mirrors what the Hono integration does at packages/hono/src/shared/middlewareHandlers.ts:102-117 (`updateSpanName` + `INTERNAL_setSegmentNameSourceIfSegment(rootSpan, 'route')` + `HTTP_ROUTE` + `isolationScope.setTransactionName`), which is the reference shape for a framework with no Sentry integration. Other variants tried and found not to matter: entry shape (`app.fetch` passed straight to `withSentry` is already the documented Oak Cloudflare handler, application.js:287-302), init placement, and both trace lifecycles. No bundler variant is needed, and the Vite plugin changes nothing here because the naming happens at span start inside wrapRequestHandlerWithInit, not at build time. Not fixed by the middleware and worth a separate look: the transaction/segment status stays `"ok"` on the 500 error route in both lifecycles. All processes I started were killed; node_modules left in place so the probe is rerunnable.
Workaround: Register one Oak middleware before `router.routes()` that renames the root span in a `finally` block and sets the segment name source with the exported constant, not the legacy `sentry.source` string: app.use(async (ctx, next) => { try { await next(); } finally { const path = ctx.matched?.[ctx.matched.length - 1]?.path; const span = Sentry.getActiveSpan(); if (path && span) { const root = Sentry.getRootSpan(span); const routeName = `${ctx.request.method} ${path}`; Sentry.updateSpanName(root, routeName); root.setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, 'route'); root.setAttribute('http.route', path); Sentry.getIsolationScope().setTransactionName(routeName); } } }); This yields `GET /users/:id` with source `route` under both `traceLifecycle: 'static'` and `'stream'`, and it also runs on the throwing route, which the `await next()`-then-rename form does not.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent GET /isolate/:tag requests, each awaiting a random 50-100ms, produced three events carrying exactly their own req_tag and three distinct trace ids, each matching its own server transaction. traceLifecycle static.
incoming trace✓ worksA request with sentry-trace aaaaaaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff0001-1111222233334444-1 and matching baggage produced a transaction with trace_id aaaaaaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff0001 and parent_span_id 1111222233334444; the error captured in that handler carried the same trace id. traceLifecycle static.
outgoing fetch✓ worksA plain global fetch from inside an Oak handler to the local recorder produced a child span "http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41538/__record" (origin auto.http.fetch), and the recorder received sentry-trace 5f23912c0ff64e42a883a6a6c4e03dd6-a2dc7e1adcf6986d-1 plus a full baggage header. Seen in both static and stream lifecycles.
db spans✓ worksModule-scope pools. mysql@2 produced "db SELECT users" (origin auto.db.mysql, status ok) nested under the Oak server span, with real rows returned. mysql2@3 produced spans too (mysql2.pool.connect, mysql2.connect, SELECT users, origin auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel) but the query itself fails on workerd with EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context, so its SELECT span has status error. Instrumentation path: none needed. Both drivers emitted spans under plain wrangler dev (esbuild bundling) with no Cloudflare Vite plugin; a vite build with sentryCloudflareVitePlugin() also works and changes nothing. traceLifecycle stream.
logs✓ worksSentry.logger.info('oak-log-from-handler', { where: 'handler' }) inside an Oak handler arrived as a log envelope within the 7s flush window. traceLifecycle static.

Docs today

No page anywhere in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions Oak. `grep -ril "\boak\b" ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs` returns nothing, and `grep -ril "oak" ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/ ~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/` returns nothing. The Cloudflare guide's framework directory (~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/) contains only astro.mdx, hono.mdx, hydrogen-react-router.mdx, hydrogen-remix.mdx, index.mdx, nextjs.mdx, nuxt.mdx, remix.mdx, sveltekit.mdx, tanstack-start.mdx. There is no Oak guide on any runtime, so nothing documents this combination today.

Documented: no

A page must say that Oak 17 runs on Cloudflare Workers with nodejs_compat, installed through the JSR npm bridge because Oak's current line ships only to JSR and the npm package stops at 14.1.0. Errors, isolation, incoming trace, outgoing fetch, database spans and logs all work. Route names are the one gap: Oak has no Sentry integration, so the request span is named after the raw URL in the static lifecycle and after the method alone in the default stream lifecycle. Show the fix, one Oak middleware registered before the router that renames the root span to the matched route and sets the segment name source with the SDK's exported constant. All five Sentry packages are required, and @sentry/server-utils must be installed explicitly.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/oak.mdx (new), linked from guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23.

grep for oak over docs and platform-includes returns nothing; guides/cloudflare/frameworks/ contains only astro, hono, the two hydrogen pages, index, nextjs, nuxt, remix, sveltekit and tanstack-start; guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23 (no Oak).

Packaging is the real story here. Oak's current line (17.x) ships only to JSR; the npm package @oakserver/oak is stuck at 14.1.0. Any docs page must show the `@jsr:registry=https://npm.jsr.io` .npmrc line plus the `npm:@jsr/oak__oak` alias, otherwise a user following it installs a three-major-versions-old Oak. Oak needs zero adaptation for Workers: Application.fetch is documented in Oak's own source as a Cloudflare fetch handler and takes (request, env, ctx). Everything @sentry/cloudflare provides at the withSentry layer therefore works unchanged, which is why six of seven capabilities are green with no Sentry-side Oak support at all. The one real gap is route names. Because Sentry only sees the Worker fetch boundary, a parameterized Oak route is reported as the raw URL (static lifecycle) or as bare "GET" (stream lifecycle). Oak exposes matched layers on ctx.matched, so an ~8-line middleware fixes it, but two things make that workaround imperfect and worth an SDK-side fix or at least a documented snippet: setting the sentry.source attribute after updateSpanName is honoured in stream lifecycle (source "route") but not in static lifecycle (source stays "custom"); and the middleware runs after `await next()`, so on a throwing route it never executes and the error transaction keeps the unparameterized name. A second reportable wart: a request that throws out of the handler still produces a server transaction/span with status "ok", even though the error event is captured and the response is a 500. The db result contradicts the assumption that Cloudflare db spans need the Vite plugin's buildTimeInstrumentation. Both mysql@2 (origin auto.db.mysql) and mysql2 (origin auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel) emitted spans under plain `wrangler dev` with no Vite plugin present; mysql2 publishes diagnostics_channel events itself and the mysql@2 path is patch-based. The vite build with a bare sentryCloudflareVitePlugin() also succeeded (1495 modules, ~4MB worker) and produced identical spans, so the plugin is optional here. Separately, mysql2 cannot actually execute a query on workerd: it compiles row parsers with `new Function`, which workerd rejects with `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`. Sentry still reports the span (status error). Any Cloudflare + MySQL guidance should point at mysql@2, not mysql2. The @sentry/server-utils resolution trap cost the first build attempt: npm happily satisfies @sentry/server-utils@10.67.0 from the public registry, and that build lacks the ./no-diagnostic-channels export that @sentry/cloudflare's workflows.js imports. Every @sentry/* tarball has to be on the same npm install line. Housekeeping: sink (pid file sink.pid/sink2.pid) and all wrangler dev processes were killed, and the 322MB node_modules was removed.

Fresh on Cloudflare M-fresh-cf

Fresh 2 (@fresh/core 2.3.3, @fresh/plugin-vite 1.1.2, Preact) · Cloudflare Workers (wrangler 4.129.0 dev, workerd 1.20260903.1, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, nodejs_compat) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Fresh 2 runs on Workers unmodified: `vite build` (Fresh's own plugin) emits `_fresh/server.js` whose default export is already `{ fetch }`, and wrangler/esbuild bundles it. No Cloudflare adapter, no @cloudflare/vite-plugin needed.

1. Scaffold a Fresh 2 app (`deno run -A -r jsr:@fresh/init .`).
2. `npm install <sentry-cloudflare tgz> <sentry-core tgz> <sentry-opentelemetry tgz> <sentry-server-utils tgz> wrangler@4 vite preact @preact/signals @prefresh/vite @babel/core @babel/preset-react preact-render-to-string rollup esbuild-wasm @types/babel__core @remix-run/node-fetch-server` (deno.json keeps `nodeModulesDir: "manual"`; deno resolves jsr:@fresh/* itself).
3. vite.config.ts — keep `@sentry/cloudflare` (and any DB driver) OUT of the Fresh SSR bundle so the Worker gets exactly one SDK instance:
```ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import { fresh } from "@fresh/plugin-vite";
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [fresh()],
  environments: { ssr: { build: { rollupOptions: {
    external: ["@sentry/cloudflare", "mysql", "mysql2", "mysql2/promise"] } } } },
});
```
4. worker.ts (the wrangler entry, NOT the Fresh entry):
```ts
import * as Sentry from "@sentry/cloudflare";
import server from "./_fresh/server.js";
export default Sentry.withSentry(
  () => ({ dsn: "...", tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: "static" }),
  { fetch: (request: Request) => server.fetch(request, {
      remoteAddr: { transport: "tcp", hostname: "127.0.0.1", port: 0 } }) },
);
```
The second argument to `server.fetch` matters: Fresh's handler expects a `Deno.ServeHandlerInfo`, so pass a stub rather than `env`.
5. wrangler.jsonc: `{ "main": "worker.ts", "compatibility_date": "2026-05-01", "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"] }`.
6. `deno task build && npx wrangler dev --port <port> --inspector-port 0`.

Two things a docs page must also say: (a) route handler errors are swallowed by Fresh, so add `routes/_error.tsx` calling `Sentry.captureException(ctx.error)`; (b) `staticFiles()` middleware is Deno-only (`Deno.stat`/`Deno.open`) — drop it and serve assets via Workers Assets.

errors◐ partialOut of the box an error thrown in a route handler never reaches Sentry: Fresh's DEFAULT_ERROR_HANDLER does `console.error(error); return new Response("Internal server error", { status: 500 })`, so only the request span turns internal_error and no event is sent (verified with debug:true — the log shows the root span finishing with no "Captured error event"). Adding `routes/_error.tsx` with `Sentry.captureException(ctx.error)` sends it, as a handled `generic` mechanism event with request data attached. Both lifecycles behave the same. verified: partial Rebuilt the Fresh 2 + Cloudflare probe from scratch (copy of the original app, same versions: @fresh/core 2.3.3, @fresh/plugin-vite 1.1.2, wrangler 4.129.0, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, nodejs_compat, @sentry/cloudflare 10.67.0 from $REPRO/_toolbox/pack) and attacked the claim from four sides. The swallowing part of the claim is CONFIRMED; the "you must add routes/_error.tsx" part is REFUTED - an init-only option works with no framework file at all. Why it is swallowed (read from the built bundle, app/_fresh/server/server-entry.js): - line 6099 `DEFAULT_ERROR_HANDLER`: `console.error(error); return new Response("Internal server error", {status:500})`. - line 6390 `App.handler()`: `catch (err) { ctx.error = err; return await DEFAULT_ERROR_HANDLER(ctx); }` - the error never leaves Fresh, so `withSentry`'s fetch never rejects. - line 5439 `compileMiddlewares(middlewares, onError)` does call an `onError(err)` hook for every middleware error, but `App`'s `#onError` is initialised to `NOOP` (line 6170) and there is no public setter in 2.3.3, so that hook is unusable. - Side note found while reading: line 6366 Fresh already does `_trace.getActiveSpan()?.updateName(`${method} ${pattern}`)` + `http.route` via a bundled @opentelemetry/api. The Cloudflare SDK registers no OTel global, so it is a NoopTracer and the rename never happens (that is why route names stay `GET /users/42`, source url). RESULTS (sink at 127.0.0.1:41337, tunnel, sentinel-gated reads; `x-mode` request header selects the variant so one build covers all of them). 1) Baseline, no capture anywhere - CONFIRMED broken. `curl -H "x-mode: baseline" /boom?n=b1`: {"type": "transaction", "name": "GET /boom", "op": "http.server", "source": "url", "status": "internal_error", "trace_id": "4261c84380874df68fb697f0458927f4", "sdk": "sentry.javascript.cloudflare", "spans": []} (no `event` item; wrangler log shows the root span finishing with no "Captured error event") 2) routes/_error.tsx with `Sentry.captureException(ctx.error, {mechanism:{type:'fresh.error_route',handled:false}})` - works, and `handled:false` is settable (the original probe's `generic`/`handled:true` was just the default options object): {"type": "event", "exception": "Error: fresh-cf-route-error-e1", "mechanism": "fresh.error_route", "handled": false, "frames": 10, "topFrame": "...worker.js:GET", "trace_id": "fc7734dca8b241218412ec8fc27e3bc3", "request": {"url": "http://127.0.0.1:41338/boom?n=e1", "method": "GET"}} {"type": "transaction", "name": "GET /boom", "status": "internal_error", "trace_id": "fc7734dca8b241218412ec8fc27e3bc3"} 3) A plain root middleware in main.ts (`app.use(async ctx => { try { return await ctx.next() } catch (e) { Sentry.captureException(e, {mechanism:{type:'fresh.middleware',handled:false}}); throw e } })`) - works, same trace, and unlike `_error.tsx` it does not have to produce the response: {"type": "event", "exception": "Error: fresh-cf-route-error-m1", "mechanism": "fresh.middleware", "handled": false, "frames": 10, "trace_id": "5e00b85e0d434c3797542b53b11a3e83", "request": {"url": "http://127.0.0.1:41338/boom?n=m1", "method": "GET"}} 4) THE REFUTATION - init-only, no routes/_error.tsx, no middleware, no framework file touched. Adding `integrations: [Sentry.captureConsoleIntegration({ levels: ["error"] })]` to the `withSentry` options picks up Fresh's own `console.error(error)` as a real exception event with the real stack: {"type": "event", "exception": "Error: fresh-cf-route-error-c1", "mechanism": "auto.core.capture_console", "handled": true, "logger": "console", "frames": 10, "topFrame": ".../worker-console.js:GET", "trace_id": "8af9c22924904342859c92171c813e80", "request": {"url": "http://127.0.0.1:41340/boom?n=c1", "method": "GET"}} {"type": "transaction", "name": "GET /boom", "status": "internal_error", "trace_id": "8af9c22924904342859c92171c813e80"} Same on the default stream lifecycle (traceLifecycle omitted, port 41341): {"type": "event", "exception": "Error: fresh-cf-route-error-s2", "mechanism": "auto.core.capture_console", "handled": true, "logger": "console", "trace_id": "3aa21a85dd5644ca990338a91024aa5b"} {"type": "span", "trace_id": "3aa21a85dd5644ca990338a91024aa5b", "items": ["http.server GET"], "raw": [{"name": "GET", "status": "error", "is_segment": true, "origin": "auto.http.cloudflare"}]} Caveat, measured: it reports every other `console.error` too, as a message event - {"type": "event", "message": "plain console.error noise x1", "mechanism": "auto.core.capture_console", "handled": true, "logger": "console", "topFrame": ".../worker-console.js:consoleHandler"} 5) Coverage beyond handlers: an error thrown in a page component (`routes/boomrender.tsx`) is swallowed identically and is caught by all three workarounds - middleware `{"exception": "Error: fresh-cf-render-error-r7", "mechanism": "fresh.middleware", "handled": false, "topFrame": ".../worker.js:Object.BoomRender"}`, _error.tsx `{"exception": "Error: fresh-cf-render-error-r8", "mechanism": "fresh.error_route", "handled": false}`, console integration `{"exception": "Error: fresh-cf-render-error-r4", "mechanism": "auto.core.capture_console", "topFrame": ".../worker-console.js:Object.BoomRender"}`. Baseline sends nothing for it. 6) Fresh trap worth knowing: `app.onError("/boom2", handler)` never fires for the fs route `/boom2`. `newErrorCmd` uses `includeLastSegment: true` while fs route commands resolve to the parent segment, so the error route lands on a segment no route belongs to; `/boom2` fell through to the root `_error.tsx`. Use `app.onError("*", ...)` (registered after `app.fsRoutes()`, since the later command overwrites the segment's errorRoute) or `routes/_error.tsx`. 7) Test artifact to be aware of when re-running: `dedupeIntegration` drops the second capture of an identical error message+stack, so firing /boom twice with the same message shows a false "no event". I made the route throw `fresh-cf-route-error-${n}` per request to avoid it. Workaround: Two that work, both verified on Fresh 2.3.3 / wrangler 4.129.0 / @sentry/cloudflare 10.67.0. (a) Init-only, no framework file: add `integrations: [Sentry.captureConsoleIntegration({ levels: ["error"] })]` to the options `withSentry` returns; Fresh's DEFAULT_ERROR_HANDLER `console.error(error)`s the real Error, so the event carries the correct type, message and stack and shares the request's trace - the cost is that every other `console.error` in the app also becomes an issue, and the mechanism reads `auto.core.capture_console` / `handled: true`. (b) Explicit capture, better mechanism: either `routes/_error.tsx` with `Sentry.captureException(ctx.error, { mechanism: { type: "fresh", handled: false } })`, or a root middleware in main.ts before `app.fsRoutes()`: `app.use(async ctx => { try { return await ctx.next(); } catch (e) { Sentry.captureException(e, { mechanism: { type: "fresh", handled: false } }); throw e; } })` - the middleware form is preferable because it does not also have to render the 500 page and it still lets `routes/_error.tsx` produce the response. Both (a) and (b) also cover errors thrown while rendering a page component.
route names✓* works-waThe server transaction for /users/42 is named "GET /users/42" with source "url" under traceLifecycle 'static'; under the default 'stream' lifecycle the segment span is named just "GET" (origin auto.http.cloudflare, no source attribute). @sentry/cloudflare has no Fresh router hook, so the parameterized pattern is never used. A middleware reading `ctx.route` and calling `Sentry.updateSpanName(getRootSpan(span), \`${method} ${ctx.route}\`)` yields "GET /users/:id" but with source "custom", not "route". verified: works-after-all Baseline reproduced, then refuted. Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-fresh-cf-routenames (app/, run2.sh, raw-*.json). Fresh 2.3.3 + @fresh/plugin-vite 1.1.2, wrangler dev (workerd), develop SDK tarballs, sink on 52731, app on 52732. Reruns: `bash run2.sh <off|custom|route> <stream|static> <bridge on|off> <otelsetup on|off> <tag>`. BASELINE (ROUTEMODE=off, exactly the probe's wiring) — claim reproduced: J-baseline-stream: SEG "GET" src=url route=undefined origin=auto.http.cloudflare SEG "GET /" src=route (only because "/" is already low-cardinality) K-baseline-static: TX "GET /users/42" src=url ; TX "GET /iso/abc" src=url I-otelsetup-stream (`enableOpenTelemetrySetup: true`, nothing else): SEG "GET" src=url — the option changes nothing here, it installs only a tracer provider, no context manager. Small correction to the probe: under stream the segment span does carry `sentry.segment.name.source`, its value is "url", not "absent". FIX A — 8-line Fresh middleware in main.ts (works in BOTH lifecycles, including the erroring route): app.use(async ctx => { try { return await ctx.next(); } finally { const root = Sentry.getActiveSpan() && Sentry.getRootSpan(Sentry.getActiveSpan()); if (root && typeof ctx.route === "string") { root.updateName(`${ctx.req.method} ${ctx.route}`); root.setAttribute("http.route", ctx.route); root.setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, "route"); // after updateName } } }); L-route-stream: SEG "GET /users/:id" src=route route=/users/:id ; SEG "GET /iso/:tag" src=route ; SEG "GET /boom" src=route status=error M-route-static: TX "GET /users/:id" src=route segsrc=route route=/users/:id ; TX "GET /boom" src=route Two details that decide the outcome: (1) `Sentry.updateSpanName()` (what the docs recommend) hard-codes source "custom" — B-custom-stream: SEG "GET /users/:id" src=custom, matching the probe; `span.updateName()` also sets "custom", so `SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE` (exported from @sentry/cloudflare) must be set AFTER the rename. (2) the rename must sit in a `finally`: Fresh's segment error-catcher is OUTSIDE user middleware, so a throwing route handler skips any code placed after `await ctx.next()` — that is why the probe's /boom stayed "GET". FIX B — no framework code at all: Fresh 2 already instruments itself with @opentelemetry/api. Its router does, before dispatch: const span = _trace.getActiveSpan(); if (span && pattern) { span.updateName(`${method} ${pattern}`); span.setAttribute("http.route", pattern); } (app/_fresh/server/server-entry.js:6366-6370) That hook is dead on Cloudflare because @sentry/cloudflare never registers an OTel context manager, so `context.active()` is always ROOT_CONTEXT (documented in packages/opentelemetry/src/tracer.ts:69-72). Registering a ~10-line bridging context manager in worker.ts whose `active()` returns `trace.setSpan(ROOT_CONTEXT, Sentry.getActiveSpan())` (both copies of @opentelemetry/api are 1.9.1, so the global registry is shared with Fresh's inlined copy) makes Fresh name every span itself: N-bridge-stream: SEG "GET /users/:id" src=custom route=/users/:id ; SEG "GET /boom" src=custom route=/boom Name and http.route are right for every route including the erroring one, but source is "custom" because `span.updateName()` sets it; combining the bridge with Fix A's one attribute line gives name + source=route everywhere (G-bridge-route-stream: SEG "GET /users/:id" src=route route=/users/:id). Still true: @sentry/cloudflare ships no Fresh hook, so nothing here is automatic. No Fresh e2e app exists in the repo (dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications has cloudflare-workers, sveltekit-3-cloudflare-workers, nuxt-4-cloudflare, react-router-8-cloudflare, tanstackstart-react-cloudflare, none for Fresh). SDK-side follow-up worth filing: making `enableOpenTelemetrySetup` (or the Cloudflare wrapper itself) also install a context manager would light up Fresh's built-in route naming — and every other framework that instruments through @opentelemetry/api — with zero user code.
Workaround: Add one middleware to Fresh's main.ts, before `app.fsRoutes()`, that renames the root span in a `finally` (so throwing routes are covered too) and then sets the source attribute, because `updateName`/`updateSpanName` force source "custom": import * as Sentry from "@sentry/cloudflare"; app.use(async (ctx) => { try { return await ctx.next(); } finally { const active = Sentry.getActiveSpan(); const root = active && Sentry.getRootSpan(active); if (root && typeof ctx.route === "string") { root.updateName(`${ctx.req.method} ${ctx.route}`); root.setAttribute("http.route", ctx.route); root.setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, "route"); } } }); Verified as "GET /users/:id" with source "route" under both `traceLifecycle: "stream"` (span envelope) and `"static"` (transaction envelope). Optional extra: register a small @opentelemetry/api context manager in worker.ts whose `active()` returns `trace.setSpan(ROOT_CONTEXT, Sentry.getActiveSpan())` — Fresh's own router instrumentation then sets the parameterized name and `http.route` on its own.

db spans✓* works-waBoth shapes fail. (1) Driver external (module-scope connection): mysql@2 works and returns rows over nodejs_compat TCP, but produces no db span at all — build-time channel injection only reaches modules inside the bundle; mysql2 cannot even run, it throws `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context` on the first query. (2) Driver bundled with `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ autoInstrumentation: false })` added to Fresh's vite config: the orchestrion transform does run and injects the channels into the route chunks, but both drivers then die at module init with `TypeError: The argument 'path' ... Received 'undefined' at createRequire (node:module:34:15)` — Vite's CJS interop emits `createRequire(import.meta.url)` and import.meta.url is undefined in the Fresh SSR chunk under workerd. Instrumentation path used: Cloudflare Vite plugin (sentryOrchestrionPlugin) mounted into Fresh's own vite build; the Cloudflare vite plugin's autoInstrumentation half is unusable here because there is no @cloudflare/vite-plugin worker environment. verified: works-after-all REFUTED for `mysql@2`. db spans do appear, both from a Fresh route handler and from the wrangler entry, in both trace lifecycles. The reporter's two shapes were the wrong two shapes: the fix is to stop asking Fresh's own Vite build to instrument the driver and instead pre-bundle the wrangler entry (worker.ts + `_fresh/server.js` + the driver) with esbuild plus `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild`, then point `wrangler.jsonc` `main` at that output. WORKING WIRING (files under $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-fresh-cf-dbspans/app/): - `vite.config.ts`: `plugins:[fresh()]`, and `environments.ssr.build.rollupOptions.external = ["@sentry/cloudflare","mysql","mysql2","mysql2/promise"]` (unchanged from the reporter's shape 1). No Sentry Vite plugin here at all. - `build-worker3.mjs`: esbuild `bundle:true, format:'esm', platform:'neutral', mainFields:['module','main'], conditions:['workerd','worker','browser','import','module','default']`, `plugins:[collectBuiltins, sentryOrchestrionPlugin()]`, entry `worker.ts`, out `dist3/worker.mjs`. - `wrangler.jsonc`: `"main": "dist3/worker.mjs"`, compat date 2026-05-01, `nodejs_compat`. - `worker.ts` unchanged apart from also importing `mysql` for a control route; `server.fetch(request, { remoteAddr: {...} })` stub still required. THE ONE NON-OBVIOUS BIT. A plain esbuild pre-bundle fails twice before it works, and both failures look like SDK bugs but are esbuild ESM-output artifacts: 1. `Error: Dynamic require of "diagnostics_channel" is not supported` on the first query — esbuild rewrites every `require()` of an external module in ESM output to its `__require` stub, and the orchestrion-injected snippet inside `node_modules/mysql/lib/Connection.js` requires `diagnostics_channel`. 2. Routing bare builtins through generated ESM shim modules instead (dist2) fixes that but then dies with `TypeError: The "superCtor.prototype" property must be of type object. Received undefined at Object.inherits (node:util:119:15) at node_modules/readable-stream/lib/_stream_readable.js` — `require('stream')` returned a namespace object, not the module. The fix that works is a banner: statically `import * as __nbN from "node:<builtin>"` for every builtin the bundle asks for, then `globalThis.require = id => { const m = map[id.replace(/^node:/,"")]; return m.default !== undefined ? m.default : m; }`. esbuild's `__require` stub defers to a global `require` when one exists, so this restores correct CJS semantics. Builtins collected in this app: async_hooks, buffer, crypto, diagnostics_channel, events, fs, net, process, stream, string_decoder, timers, tls, url, util, zlib. Default `traceLifecycle:"stream"` (app on 52131) — same result, correctly parented and with the right origin: {"type":"span","items":["db SELECT users","http.server GET /dbq2"],"raw":[{"name":"SELECT users","status":"ok","parent_span_id":"91184fd2107d430e","is_segment":false,"origin":"auto.db.mysql"},{"name":"GET /dbq2","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.cloudflare"}]} Rest of the app is unaffected by the pre-bundle: `http.server GET /`, `http.server GET /users/:id`, `Error: fresh-cf-route-error` via `routes/_error.tsx` all still arrive. mysql2 CAVEAT (the only part that stays broken, and not a Sentry defect). With the same bundle mysql2 IS instrumented and emits spans, then its own row-parser codegen is rejected by workerd: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /dbq","op":"http.server","status":"internal_error","spans":["db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]} {"type":"event","exception":"EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context","sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare"} So the reporter's "mysql2 cannot even run" is confirmed, but it is a workerd `new Function` restriction inside mysql2, not an instrumentation gap. `mysql@2` is the driver to use. ALSO TRIED AND CONFIRMED DEAD (so a docs page should not send anyone down these): - `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ autoInstrumentation: false })` in Fresh's own `vite.config.ts` with the driver bundled, plus `define: { "import.meta.url": JSON.stringify("file:///_fresh/server.js") }` to kill the reporter's `createRequire(undefined)` TypeError. The define does work (`const require$2 = createRequire("file:///_fresh/server.js")` in `_fresh/server/assets/_fresh-route___dbq2-C7SWGNeZ.js`), the orchestrion injection is present, but the route then fails with `Error: No such module "_fresh/lib/_stream_readable.js"` — workerd's `createRequire` resolves against the Worker's module map, so rollup's leftover dynamic requires can never resolve. Rollup/Vite CJS interop is structurally unusable for a Workers target here. - Simplified banner `globalThis.require = createRequire("file:///worker.mjs")` instead of the static `node:` import map (`build-worker4.mjs`). Needs an alias to avoid `The symbol "createRequire" has already been declared`, and even then mysql fails with `Error: Received packet in the wrong sequence.` Do not recommend it. - Baseline reproduction of the reporter's shape 1 (driver external, wrangler bundles `worker.ts`): confirmed, `{"type":"transaction","name":"GET /dbq2",...,"spans":[]}` — no db span. Workaround: Do not put `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` in Fresh's `vite.config.ts`. Keep `@sentry/cloudflare` and the DB driver external to the Fresh SSR build, then bundle the wrangler entry yourself with esbuild and the Sentry orchestrion esbuild plugin, and set `wrangler.jsonc` `main` to that output: ```js // build-worker.mjs import * as esbuild from 'esbuild'; import { builtinModules } from 'node:module'; import { sentryOrchestrionPlugin } from '@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild'; const BUILTINS = new Set(builtinModules.filter(m => !m.startsWith('node:'))); const used = new Set(); const collect = { name: 'collect-node-builtins', setup(build) { build.onResolve({ filter: /^(node:)?[a-z_]+(\/[a-z_]+)?$/ }, args => { const bare = args.path.replace(/^node:/, ''); if (!BUILTINS.has(bare)) return null; used.add(bare); return { path: `node:${bare}`, external: true }; }); }}; const common = { entryPoints: ['worker.ts'], bundle: true, format: 'esm', platform: 'neutral', mainFields: ['module', 'main'], target: 'es2022', conditions: ['workerd', 'worker', 'browser', 'import', 'module', 'default'], plugins: [collect, sentryOrchestrionPlugin()], }; await esbuild.build({ ...common, outfile: 'dist/probe.mjs' }); // pass 1: discover builtins const names = [...used].sort(); const banner = [ ...names.map((n, i) => `import * as __nb${i} from "node:${n}";`), `const __nbMap = { ${names.map((n, i) => `"${n}": __nb${i}`).join(', ')} };`, 'globalThis.require = id => { const m = __nbMap[String(id).replace(/^node:/, "")];', ' if (!m) throw new Error("Cannot find module " + id);', ' return m.default !== undefined ? m.default : m; };', ].join('\n'); await esbuild.build({ ...common, outfile: 'dist/worker.mjs', banner: { js: banner } }); ``` `deno task build && node build-worker.mjs && npx wrangler dev`. Use `mysql@2`; `mysql2` produces spans but its query then throws `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context` in workerd.

There is no guides/fresh/ directory, and the only "fresh" hits under docs/platforms/javascript/ are the ordinary English word (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/agents-sdk.mdx:39, platform-includes/distributed-tracing/custom-instrumentation/server/javascript.mdx:108). The Cloudflare guide's framework list at docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23 names Astro, Hono, Hydrogen, Next.js, Nuxt, Remix, SvelteKit and TanStack Start, and nothing else; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/ has no Fresh entry. So the Fresh-on-Cloudflare combination is undocumented in both directions.

Documented: no

A page must say that Fresh 2 runs on Workers unmodified, because Fresh's own Vite plugin emits a server whose default export is already a fetch handler, so no Cloudflare adapter is needed. Three things follow. Nothing a route handler, middleware or page component throws reaches Sentry on its own, because Fresh's default error handler catches it and returns a 500, leaving the request span marked internal_error; the init-only fix is the console-capture integration for the error level. The request span is named by HTTP method only with source url, so show a middleware registered before the file-system routes that renames the root span from the matched route and sets the route and source attributes explicitly, because renaming alone forces the source to custom. Database spans must not come from putting the Sentry Cloudflare Vite plugin in Fresh's config: there is no worker environment for it to instrument, and it breaks the driver under workerd; instead keep the SDK and the driver external to the SSR build and bundle the wrangler entry separately with the orchestrion esbuild plugin. Isolation, incoming trace, outgoing fetch and logs work unaided.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/fresh.mdx (new), linked from guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23; add the missing-worker-environment caveat to guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx:13-18.

No guides/fresh/ directory exists; the only fresh hits under docs/platforms/javascript are the ordinary English word; guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23 (no Fresh); guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx:13-18 recommends the plugin for tracing bundled dependencies with no caveat for Vite builds that have no Cloudflare worker environment.

- Fresh 2 needed no adapter. Its vite build already emits `export default { fetch: server.fetch }` (for `deno serve`), which is exactly the Workers module shape, so `withSentry` wraps it directly. No Deno global is touched on the request path for API/page routes — `Deno.serve`/`Deno.build` live only in `App.listen()`, and `import.meta.dirname` reaching the ProdBuildCache root did not throw at module eval under workerd. - The one Deno-only path that does matter is `staticFiles()`, whose ProdBuildCache `readFile` calls `Deno.stat`/`Deno.open`. I removed that middleware; a real deployment needs Workers Assets. Page rendering itself works (the /boom error page rendered full HTML with the emitted stylesheet link). - Keeping `@sentry/cloudflare` external to the Fresh SSR bundle is load-bearing: if it were bundled, routes calling `Sentry.setTag`/`captureException` would talk to a second SDK copy with no client. With `external`, wrangler's esbuild resolves both the worker entry and the route chunks to the same node_modules copy. esbuild prints a harmless `[ignored-bare-import] "sideEffects": false` warning for `import "@sentry/cloudflare"` in each route chunk. - The most interesting gap is route names: nothing in @sentry/cloudflare knows about Fresh's router, so every span is either `GET /users/42` (static, source url) or bare `GET` (stream). Fresh exposes the matched pattern on the context, so a five-line middleware fixes it, but it lands as source `custom` because `updateSpanName` overrides the source. A Fresh integration setting source `route` would be the real fix. - db spans are doubly blocked on this runtime: mysql2 cannot run on workerd at all (`new Function` is disallowed), and the only instrumentation path that exists for Cloudflare (build-time channel injection) requires the driver inside the bundle, which is exactly what breaks it via `createRequire(import.meta.url)` in Vite's CJS interop. mysql@2 external is the only combination that queries successfully, and it gets no spans. - I did not use @cloudflare/vite-plugin; Fresh's own vite build plus plain `wrangler dev` was enough, which also means `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin`'s autoInstrumentation half (worker-entry wrapping from wrangler config) has no environment to attach to here and must be disabled. - Cleanup done: wrangler/workerd, sink and recorder processes killed (pids 89846, 89407, 2672, 16625, 89830, 89831, 89845, 93354; all three ports verified free), and app/node_modules removed (327M). The dir is left at 4.9M with sources, the built `_fresh/` output and the logs. Reinstall with the npm line above to rerun. - Ports used: sink 22984, recorder 20504, wrangler 58164. Two earlier picks (41777, 47311) were already held by other agents' sinks; I moved rather than touching them.

NestJS on Cloudflare M-nestjs-cf

NestJS 11 (@nestjs/platform-express) · cloudflare (workerd via wrangler 4.56.0 dev, compatibility_date 2026-05-01) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

NestJS runs on workerd behind the node:http server bridge, and every Sentry capability except framework-swallowed errors works, but ONLY with a hand-built esbuild bundle plus the orchestrion esbuild plugin. Exact wiring a docs page would have to show:

1) Packages: `npm install @nestjs/core@11 @nestjs/common@11 @nestjs/platform-express@11 rxjs reflect-metadata express mysql esbuild typescript wrangler@4` plus the SDK tarballs `@sentry/cloudflare @sentry/core @sentry/server-utils @sentry/opentelemetry` (all four must be installed together, see notes).

2) wrangler.jsonc:
{ "name": "m-nestjs-cf", "compatibility_date": "2026-05-01",
  "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat", "enable_nodejs_http_modules", "enable_nodejs_http_server_modules"],
  "main": "dist/worker.js" }

3) Entry (src/main.ts) - Nest must be booted LAZILY inside the fetch handler, not at module scope:
import 'reflect-metadata';
import { httpServerHandler } from 'cloudflare:node';
import * as Sentry from '@sentry/cloudflare';
const PORT = 8080;
let booted;
async function boot() {
  const { NestFactory } = await import('@nestjs/core');
  const { AppModule } = await import('./app.module');
  const { SentryFilter } = await import('./sentry.filter');
  const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule);
  app.useGlobalFilters(new SentryFilter(app.getHttpAdapter()));
  await app.listen(PORT);
}
const nodeHandler = httpServerHandler({ port: PORT });
export default Sentry.withSentry(
  () => ({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' }),
  { async fetch(request, env, ctx) { booted ??= boot(); await booted; return nodeHandler.fetch(request, env, ctx); } },
);

4) Error capture needs an explicit Nest exception filter (Nest swallows handler throws):
@Catch() class SentryFilter extends BaseExceptionFilter {
  catch(exception, host) { Sentry.captureException(exception); super.catch(exception, host); }
}

5) Build: tsc (experimentalDecorators + emitDecoratorMetadata) -> esbuild bundle with
   format 'esm', platform 'node', external ['cloudflare:*','node:*','@sentry/cloudflare'],
   plugins: [processShimPlugin, sentryOrchestrionPlugin()]  // from '@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild'
   banner: createRequire shim that STRIPS the 'node:' prefix,
   aliases stubbing class-validator, class-transformer, @nestjs/microservices*, @nestjs/websockets/socket-module.
   Do NOT set mainFields/conditions to prefer ESM (breaks express's require('is-promise')).

6) Run: `node build.mjs && npx wrangler dev --port <port> --inspector-port 0`.

errors✓* works-waA plain `throw new Error('nest-plain-error')` in a controller is swallowed by Nest's ExceptionsHandler: the sink got only `{"type": "transaction", "name": "GET /error", "status": "internal_error"}` and NO event. Adding a global `@Catch()` filter extending BaseExceptionFilter that calls Sentry.captureException produces the event with mechanism "generic", handled true, correct trace_id, and full request context (url/method/headers, user.ip_address). No automatic mechanism exists: @sentry/cloudflare's httpServerIntegration never sees the throw because Nest converts it to a 500 response inside the node:http server. traceLifecycle 'static'. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. The claim "no automatic mechanism exists, you must hand-build a `@Catch()` filter that calls `Sentry.captureException`, and you get mechanism `generic` / handled `true`" is wrong. The SDK already ships the filter: `SentryGlobalFilter` from `@sentry/nestjs/setup`. Registered the documented way (`APP_FILTER` provider + `SentryModule.forRoot()`), it works unchanged on workerd with `@sentry/cloudflare` as the client and produces the proper auto mechanism. EXACT CHANGE (src/app.module.ts), no other change to the prior probe's app: import { APP_FILTER } from '@nestjs/core'; import { SentryGlobalFilter, SentryModule } from '@sentry/nestjs/setup'; @Module({ imports: [SentryModule.forRoot()], controllers: [AppController], providers: [{ provide: APP_FILTER, useClass: SentryGlobalFilter }], }) export class AppModule {} plus `@sentry/nestjs` in package.json. `src/sentry.filter.ts` (the hand-built filter) is no longer imported by anything. `src/main.ts` is unchanged from the prior probe apart from dropping `app.useGlobalFilters(...)`. RUN 1 - orchestrion build (`dist/worker.js`), `traceLifecycle: 'static'`, port 41782/41778, sink 41777: {"type":"event","exception":"Error: nest-plain-error","mechanism":"auto.http.nestjs.global_filter","handled":false,"sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare","runtime":"cloudflare","transaction":"GET /error","trace_id":"73b6be6a6d844eff8409bec847255162","user":{"ip_address":"127.0.0.1"},"request":{"url":"http://127.0.0.1:41778/error","method":"GET","headers":{...,"cf-connecting-ip":"127.0.0.1","user-agent":"curl/8.7.1"}},"environment":"production"} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /error","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"internal_error","trace_id":"73b6be6a6d844eff8409bec847255162","spans":["middleware <anonymous>","middleware jsonParser","middleware urlencodedParser","handler /error"]} {"type":"event","exception":"Error: nest-async-error","mechanism":"auto.http.nestjs.global_filter","handled":false,...,"transaction":"GET /error-async","trace_id":"4e5d35a6a04b4bcb881fea9f6cb4b02a"} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /error-expected","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"not_found","trace_id":"82ad698878484b5f9a0fe5f8a273cd5a",...} <-- NotFoundException correctly NOT captured (isExpectedError) So: mechanism `auto.http.nestjs.global_filter`, `handled: false` (not `generic`/`true`), trace_id matches the transaction, full request context and `user.ip_address`, async throws covered, and expected `HttpException`s correctly filtered out - i.e. full parity with Node NestJS. RUN 2 - SAME BUILD MINUS the orchestrion plugin (`build-noorch.mjs` -> `dist-noorch/worker.js`), port 41780. The orchestrion plugin is needed for library SPANS, not for error capture - a large simplification of the recipe for the errors capability. RUN 3 - orchestrion build with the DEFAULT `traceLifecycle: 'stream'`, port 41782. Same result: {"type":"event","exception":"Error: nest-plain-error","mechanism":"auto.http.nestjs.global_filter","handled":false,"transaction":"GET /error","trace_id":"a389d7e18f8942cd8b996993132c8478",...} {"type":"span","trace_id":"a389d7e18f8942cd8b996993132c8478","items":["middleware urlencodedParser","middleware jsonParser","middleware <anonymous>","handler /error","http.server GET /error"]} WHY IT WORKS: `@sentry/nestjs/setup` (worktree `packages/nestjs/src/setup.ts`) imports only `@nestjs/common`, `@nestjs/core`, `rxjs` and `captureException` from `@sentry/core` - never `@sentry/node`. Verified: `grep -c "sentry.javascript.node" dist/worker.js` -> 0 and on `dist-noorch/worker.js` -> 0. It therefore captures through whatever client is active, here `sentry.javascript.cloudflare`. This is exactly the wiring the repo's own e2e app uses (~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/nestjs-11/src/app.module.ts) and exactly what the Nest docs prescribe (~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/getting-started-capture-errors/javascript.nestjs.mdx:40-54). SIDE OBSERVATION (not this capability): in `stream` lifecycle the `/error-expected` 404 segment span carries `"status":"error"`, while in `static` lifecycle the same request produces `"status":"not_found"`. Use the SDK's own filter instead of a hand-written one: install `@sentry/nestjs` alongside `@sentry/cloudflare` and add to the root module `imports: [SentryModule.forRoot()]` and `providers: [{ provide: APP_FILTER, useClass: SentryGlobalFilter }]`, both from `@sentry/nestjs/setup`. outgoing fetch✓ works`fetch('http://127.0.0.1:43529/rec')` from inside a controller produced the child span `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:43529/rec` and the recorder saw sentry-trace `40aa43231d2642d095ba75c054d446cc-a0f4e77b0f19a388-1` plus a full baggage header including sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Ffetchout. Works with and without the orchestrion plugin (it comes from @sentry/cloudflare's fetchIntegration). traceLifecycle 'static'.
db spans✓* works-waInstrumentation path: the esbuild plugin `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild` (the esbuild analogue of the Cloudflare Vite plugin's buildTimeInstrumentation). It is REQUIRED: without it a module-scope mysql pool query returns rows but the transaction has `spans: []`; with it the transaction carries `db SELECT id, name FROM users`. Partial because the driver matters: `mysql2` cannot run on workerd at all (`EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context` from its generated row parsers), only `mysql@2` works. Module-scope pool, query issued inside the handler. traceLifecycle 'static'. verified: works-after-all The reported "partial" rested on one claim: "mysql2 cannot run on workerd at all (EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed), only mysql@2 works". That is refuted. mysql2 has a first-class config flag, `disableEval: true` (mysql2 3.24.3, `lib/connection_config.js:62`, honored in `lib/commands/query.js:225` and `lib/commands/execute.js:39`), which switches the row parsers off the `new Function` path. With it, mysql2 runs on workerd and produces fully attributed db spans, including prepared statements via `.execute()`. Same app, same wiring as the original probe (NestJS 11 + platform-express, `httpServerHandler` bridge, lazy Nest boot, esbuild + `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild`, wrangler 4.129.0 dev, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, `nodejs_compat` + `enable_nodejs_http_modules` + `enable_nodejs_http_server_modules`), only the driver config changed. A/B on the eval flag, one wrangler process, six routes (verbatim HTTP responses): /db2fresh (mysql2 createConnection, disableEval: true) -> {"ok":true,"rows":[{"id":1,"name":"ada"},{"id":2,"name":"linus"}]} /db2fresh-eval (mysql2 createConnection, no flag) -> {"ok":false,"err":"EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context | at Function (<anonymous>) | at line.toFunction (.../worker.js:140167:25)"} /db2exec (mysql2 .execute prepared, disableEval) -> {"ok":true,"rows":[{"id":1,"name":"ada"},{"id":2,"name":"linus"}]} /db2pool (mysql2 createPool, disableEval) -> rows on a cold isolate, see pool caveat below /db (mysql@2 module-scope pool, baseline) -> rows Sink, traceLifecycle 'static' (verbatim, trimmed to name + spans): GET /db :: middleware <anonymous> ; middleware jsonParser ; middleware urlencodedParser ; handler /db ; db SELECT id, name FROM users GET /dbfresh :: middleware <anonymous> ; middleware jsonParser ; middleware urlencodedParser ; handler /dbfresh ; db SELECT id, name FROM users GET /db2fresh :: middleware <anonymous> ; middleware jsonParser ; middleware urlencodedParser ; handler /db2fresh ; db mysql2.connect ; db SELECT id, name FROM users GET /db2exec :: middleware <anonymous> ; middleware jsonParser ; middleware urlencodedParser ; handler /db2exec ; db mysql2.connect ; db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > ? GET /db2pool :: middleware <anonymous> ; middleware jsonParser ; middleware urlencodedParser ; handler /db2pool ; db mysql2.pool.connect ; db mysql2.connect ; db SELECT id, name FROM users Raw span data for the mysql2 spans (from a raw envelope sink, verbatim): {"d":"SELECT id, name FROM users","data":{"sentry.origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel","sentry.op":"db","db.system.name":"mysql","db.query.text":"SELECT id, name FROM users","db.query.summary":"SELECT users","db.operation.name":"SELECT","db.namespace":"app","server.address":"127.0.0.1","server.port":3307}} {"d":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > ?","data":{"sentry.origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel","sentry.op":"db","db.system.name":"mysql","db.query.text":"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > ?","db.query.summary":"SELECT users","db.operation.name":"SELECT","db.namespace":"app","server.address":"127.0.0.1","server.port":3307}} {"d":"mysql2.connect","data":{"sentry.origin":"auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel","sentry.op":"db","db.system.name":"mysql","db.namespace":"app","server.address":"127.0.0.1","server.port":3307}} Other trace lifecycle also works (the develop default, `traceLifecycle: 'stream'`, span envelopes, low-cardinality names): span ["middleware urlencodedParser","middleware jsonParser","middleware <anonymous>","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users","handler /db2fresh","http.server GET /db2fresh"] span ["middleware urlencodedParser","middleware jsonParser","middleware <anonymous>","db mysql2.pool.connect","db mysql2.connect","db SELECT users","handler /db2pool","http.server GET /db2pool"] span ["middleware urlencodedParser","middleware jsonParser","middleware <anonymous>","db SELECT users","handler /dbfresh","http.server GET /dbfresh"] So db spans work for both drivers under both lifecycles. Bundler/hook variant re-confirmed, not refuted: the same source built with `plugins: [processPlugin]` only (build-noorch.mjs -> dist-noorch, wrangler-noorch.jsonc) yields no db spans, no express spans and an unrouted server span: span ["http.server GET"] <- /dbfresh and /db2fresh, no-orchestrion build So `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` (or the Vite plugin's buildTimeInstrumentation) is genuinely required; that part of the original report stands. New caveat the original report gets backwards (affects the query, not the span): module-scope connection pools are the wrong shape on workerd. The module-scope mysql2 pool intermittently fails with "Error: Cannot perform I/O on behalf of a different request. I/O objects ... created in the context of one request handler cannot be..." on requests that reuse a socket opened by an earlier request (rounds 1 and 3 of 3 failed, round 2 passed), and the module-scope mysql@2 pool the original probe recommends silently costs 10 seconds on every request after the first (measured `[10.012133s]`, `[10.008806s]`, `[10.007499s]` vs `[0.005991s]` for a per-request connection). A connection created inside the handler is fast and correct for both drivers, and still gets spans, because instrumentation is injected at bundle time, not at first module load (the Bun K11 "module scope only" rule does not apply here). The repo's own e2e app agrees: dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/cloudflare-orchestrion-mysql/src/index.ts creates the connection inside `fetch` with the comment "workerd forbids I/O in global scope, and mysql opens its socket lazily on the first query", and its tests assert `sentry.origin: auto.db.mysql`, `db.system.name`, `db.query.text`, `server.address/port`. Files (all absolute, rerunnable): $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-nestjs-cf-dbspans/app/src/db.ts (both drivers, pool + fresh, eval + disableEval), app/src/app.controller.ts (routes /db /dbfresh /db2pool /db2pool-eval /db2fresh /db2fresh-eval /db2exec /sentinel), app/src/main.ts (tunnel + traceLifecycle), app/build.mjs (with orchestrion) and app/build-noorch.mjs (without), app/wrangler.jsonc and app/wrangler-noorch.jsonc, run1-wrangler.log / run2-wrangler.log, raw2.ndjson (raw envelopes), rawsink.mjs. Commands: (in app/) `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json; node build.mjs` then `npx wrangler dev --port 45107 --inspector-port 0`; sink `PORT=45103 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs`; drive with `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:45107/db2fresh`; no-orchestrion arm `node build-noorch.mjs; npx wrangler dev --config wrangler-noorch.jsonc --port 45109 --inspector-port 0`. node_modules is left in place; recreate with `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{cloudflare,core,server-utils,opentelemetry}-10.67.0.tgz @nestjs/core@11 @nestjs/common@11 @nestjs/platform-express@11 express rxjs reflect-metadata mysql mysql2 esbuild typescript wrangler@4`. All started processes were killed; ports 45103/45107/45109/45111 verified free.
Workaround: Use mysql2 with `disableEval: true` in the connection/pool options (`mysql2.createConnection({ host, port, user, database, disableEval: true })`); without it workerd throws `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context` from mysql2's generated row parsers. Open the connection inside the request handler rather than at module scope: a module-scope pool either fails with "Cannot perform I/O on behalf of a different request" (mysql2) or adds a silent ~10s per request (mysql@2). Spans are unaffected by where the connection is created because the orchestrion esbuild/Vite plugin injects the diagnostics channel at build time.

Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions NestJS on Cloudflare. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/ contains only astro, hono, hydrogen-react-router, hydrogen-remix, nextjs, nuxt, remix, sveltekit, tanstack-start - no nestjs.mdx - and the framework list in docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23 does not include Nest. The NestJS guide is Node-only: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nestjs/index.mdx:5 sets `fallbackGuide: javascript.node` and :6-8 `categories: javascript, server, server-node`, with no runtime caveat anywhere. Nothing in docs/ or platform-includes/ mentions `httpServerHandler`, `enable_nodejs_http_server_modules`, or `orchestrion` - so the esbuild plugin that is the only way to get route names and db spans here is entirely undocumented.

Documented: no

A page must say that NestJS 11 with the Express platform runs on workerd behind the node:http bridge, and that every capability except framework-swallowed errors works, but only with a hand-built esbuild bundle plus the orchestrion esbuild plugin; plain wrangler bundling is not sufficient. Error capture uses exactly the Node wiring: install @sentry/nestjs next to @sentry/cloudflare and register SentryModule.forRoot and the SentryGlobalFilter as APP_FILTER, with nothing Cloudflare-specific. Database spans require the build-time transform, work with both mysql drivers, and mysql2 additionally needs disableEval true or workerd rejects its generated row parsers; the connection must be opened inside the request, not at module scope. Route names, isolation, incoming trace, outgoing fetch and logs work as-is.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/nestjs.mdx (new), linked from guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23; the mysql2 disableEval requirement belongs in a shared Workers database-driver note.

guides/nestjs/index.mdx:5-9 (Node fallback, server-node categories); guides/cloudflare/frameworks/ has no nestjs.mdx; guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23 does not list Nest; no httpServerHandler or sentryOrchestrionPlugin mention anywhere in docs or platform-includes.

Headline: NestJS + @nestjs/platform-express DOES run on workerd, and with the right build it is one of the better-instrumented Cloudflare framework cells (parameterized route names, middleware/handler/db/http.client spans) - but every bit of that depends on undocumented build wiring, and a plain `throw` in a controller still never reaches Sentry. Findings worth filing: 1. `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild` is the missing documented path for non-Vite Cloudflare bundles. Enabling it flips route names from `GET /users/7` / source url to `GET /users/:id` / source route and adds the db span. @sentry/cloudflare's baseSdk.js:27-33 explicitly says only the Vite plugin injects the channels; the esbuild plugin exists and works, but no docs page mentions it. 2. With that plugin enabled, a Worker that calls `NestFactory.create` at module scope fails to BOOT: "Disallowed operation called within global scope ... generating random values are not allowed within global scope" originating in @nestjs/common/services/console-logger.service.js. The identical source without the plugin boots fine. So the orchestrion esbuild transform changes when the Nest module graph is evaluated (eager instead of lazy through esbuild's __require wrappers). Workaround: boot Nest lazily inside the fetch handler with dynamic imports. This is a real trap and would need to be in any docs page. 3. Errors are silently lost by default. Nest's ExceptionsHandler turns the throw into a 500 inside the node:http server, so @sentry/cloudflare's httpServerIntegration only sees a 500 response and records `status: internal_error` with no event. There is no `@sentry/nestjs`-style SentryGlobalFilter usable here (@sentry/nestjs pulls in @sentry/node), so the user must hand-write a `@Catch()` filter. A docs page must say this or users will think error monitoring is on when it is not. 4. workerd's `createRequire` cannot resolve `node:`-prefixed builtins ("No such module \"node:process\""), while `await import('node:process')` works (verified with app/probe/probe.mjs: {"hasGlobalProcess":"object","nodeProcess":"object","nodeNet":"function"}). Any esbuild-bundled CJS dependency that does `require('node:x')` - mysql2 does - needs a banner shim that strips the prefix. Even then `node:process` specifically must be aliased to a module returning globalThis.process. 5. mysql2 is unusable on workerd: `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`. Use `mysql@2`. Worth stating in the Cloudflare guide's database section. 6. Packaging trap that cost a build cycle: installing only sentry-cloudflare + sentry-core tarballs makes npm pull the RELEASED @sentry/server-utils@10.67.0 from the registry, which has no `./no-diagnostic-channels` export, and wrangler then fails with "Could not resolve \"@sentry/server-utils/no-diagnostic-channels\"" x6. The develop tarball must be installed alongside. This is a real hazard for anyone on a mixed install, not only for this harness. 7. Two TS diagnostics that do not block emit but look wrong: `cloudflare:node` has no type declarations shipped anywhere reachable, and `sendDefaultPii: true` fails with "Type 'true' is not assignable to type 'never'" against @sentry/cloudflare's option type - worth a look at the CloudflareOptions type. All results above came from traceLifecycle: 'static'. I did not run a 'stream' pass; with stream the transaction envelopes become span envelopes and the same names should apply, but that is untested here. Cleanup: wrangler dev, sink and recorder processes all killed; app/node_modules (336 MB) removed. Ports used: 42317 (wrangler), 42318 (throwaway probe worker), 41871 (sink), 43529 (recorder), 8080 inside the isolate.

Setup the docs would have to show

THREE SETUP TRAPS the current docs page does not mention (each cost a full build cycle):
  1. On the develop/v11 line `withSentryConfig` is NOT on the `@sentry/nextjs` main entry any more;
     it is only exported from `@sentry/nextjs/config`. Using the documented main-entry import gives
     "TypeError: withSentryConfig is not a function".
  2. `import { withSentryConfig } from '@sentry/nextjs'` in an ESM `next.config.mjs` fails outright:
     the exports map puts the `node` condition (CJS) ahead of `import`, so Node's cjs-module-lexer
     resolves 29 named exports and `withSentryConfig` is not among them.
     Error: "SyntaxError: Named export 'withSentryConfig' not found. The requested module
     '@sentry/nextjs' is a CommonJS module".  A CJS `next.config.js` is the working shape.
  3. `sendDefaultPii` no longer exists on develop; leaving it in sentry.server.config.ts fails the
     `next build` type check.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksA throw inside an App Router route handler is captured with mechanism `auto.function.nextjs.route_handler`, handled:false, and the request still returns HTTP 500 - Next.js does not swallow it. Same under both lifecycles. Stack frames carry no `context_line` (hasContextLine:false) because the worker bundle ships no sources; sourcemaps were disabled in this probe.
route names✓ worksParameterized route /api/users/42 produces transaction `GET /api/users/[id]` with `transaction_info.source: "route"` under traceLifecycle 'static', and root span `http.server GET /api/users/[id]` under 'stream'. No raw id leaks into the name.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent GET /api/iso?t=alpha|bravo|charlie, each doing Sentry.setTag + a 120ms await + captureException: every event carried exactly its own probe_tag and its own trace_id, and each transaction carried the matching tag and trace_id. No cross-talk (traceLifecycle 'static').
incoming trace✓ worksA request with `sentry-trace: aaaa...-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` plus baggage produced a transaction with trace_id `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` and parent_span_id `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb` (traceLifecycle 'static').
outgoing fetch◐ partialA `fetch()` from inside a route handler to a local recorder produced NO http.client span (the transaction's spans[] holds only the three Next.js internal spans) and the recorder received sentry-trace: null, baggage: null. Same with a `node:http` GET from the handler: request succeeds, no span, no headers. The NodeFetch integration installs but workerd's global fetch / node:http shim is not the undici instance it patches. The newer compat date and global_fetch_strictly_public change nothing. ROOT CAUSE (read in the SDK, not guessed): packages/nextjs/src/server/index.ts:138-183 - on OpenNext/Cloudflare the SDK only swaps contexts.runtime to 'cloudflare' and the sdk metadata to ['nextjs','cloudflare'], then still calls `nodeInit` from @sentry/node. Outgoing HTTP therefore depends on @sentry/node's undici/NodeFetch + node:http instrumentation, which patches an undici instance that workerd's global fetch is not. @sentry/cloudflare's runtime-agnostic `fetchIntegration` (packages/cloudflare/src/integrations/fetch.ts, a `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest` wrapper around globalThis.fetch) is never installed on this path, and @sentry/cloudflare is not even a dependency of @sentry/nextjs. RUN 2 - REFUTATION, one added integration (sentry.server.config.FIXED.ts, traceLifecycle 'static'), build2.log / wrangler2.log: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/outfetch","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["resolve page components","executing api route (app) /api/outfetch/route","http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:47312/__rec","start response"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/outhttp","op":"http.server",...,"spans":[...,"http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:47312/__rec","start response"]} recorder: [{"url":"/__rec?from=outfetch","sentry-trace":"2e8013c474304c9a8b39a312e043d7bf-994b6fc4ac6ed8cd-1","baggage":"sentry-environment=production,sentry-public_key=public,sentry-trace_id=2e8013c474304c9a8b39a312e043d7bf,sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fapi%2Foutfetch,sentry-sampled=true,sentry-sample_rand=0.487...,sentry-sample_rate=1"}, {"url":"/__rec?from=outhttp","sentry-trace":"d5cf36e31b094b009c23b139cca54e1c-8f16fc134f5cc807-1","baggage":"...sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fapi%2Fouthttp..."}] The trace_id in the header matches the transaction's trace_id, so the span is correctly parented. node:http is fixed too, because unenv routes node:http through global fetch. Its only 'http.client' assertion (tests/prefetch-spans.test.ts:19) is a browser-side prefetch span. So this gap is uncovered by the repo's own e2e suite. Verdict is `partial` and not `works-after-all` because the default and documented setup really does produce zero outgoing-HTTP telemetry, exactly as reported; it is `partial` and not `confirmed-broken` because a one-line, public-API change fully restores spans and header propagation for both fetch() and node:http, under both trace lifecycles.
