It never mentions that outgoing HTTP is uninstrumented there.
Workaround: Install @sentry/cloudflare alongside @sentry/nextjs (it is NOT a transitive dependency) and add its runtime-agnostic fetch integration to the server config: // sentry.server.config.ts import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nextjs'; import { fetchIntegration } from '@sentry/cloudflare'; Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, integrations: [fetchIntegration()], }); Verified in both traceLifecycle 'static' and 'stream'; no tracePropagationTargets needed (undefined already means propagate everywhere). It fixes global fetch() and node:http alike. Files: .../deep/verify4-M-nextjs-cf-outgoingfetch/sentry.server.config.FIXED.ts vs sentry.server.config.BASELINE-broken.ts. Rerun with: npx opennextjs-cloudflare build && npx wrangler dev --port 47313 --inspector-port 0, sink on 47311, recorder rec.mjs on 47312 (node_modules was removed after the run; reinstall with the two npm install lines above). The proper fix in the SDK would be for packages/nextjs/src/server/index.ts to push @sentry/cloudflare's fetchIntegration into customDefaultIntegrations when getCloudflareRuntimeConfig() detects OpenNext/Cloudflare, the same place it already overrides contexts.runtime and the sdk metadata.
db spans◐ partialmysql2 (module-scope pool) DOES produce db spans with no extra plugin or build step: `db mysql2.pool.connect`, `db mysql2.connect`, `db SELECT id, name FROM users` ('static') / `db SELECT users` ('stream'). The path is mysql2's own built-in diagnostics_channel tracing (.open-next/server-functions/default/node_modules/mysql2/lib/tracing.js publishes `mysql2:query`/`mysql2:connect`/`mysql2:pool:connect`), which @sentry/node subscribes to - no Vite plugin, no Bun plugin, no import hook. Two caveats: (a) the query itself always fails on workerd with `Code generation from strings disallowed for this context` because mysql2 builds row parsers with new Function, so you get spans but a 500; (b) the `mysql`@2 driver runs fine on workerd (rows returned) but produces NO spans at all, because it depends on require-in-the-middle patching which cannot work in the pre-bundled OpenNext worker. Related: at init the SDK logs `Failed to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks, so channel-based integrations will not record spans` / `TypeError: port1.on is not a function` - @sentry/server-runtime-injection cannot register on workerd. verified: partial Re-verified from scratch (fresh `npm install`, fresh `opennextjs-cloudflare build`, new ports) in $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-nextjs-cf-dbspans. Next 15.5.25 App Router + @opennextjs/cloudflare 1.20.6 + @sentry/nextjs 10.67.0 (develop tarballs), wrangler dev 4.129.0, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, nodejs_compat, MariaDB 127.0.0.1:3307. Sink 51873, worker 51874, `traceLifecycle: 'stream'`, documented wiring (`withSentryConfig` from `@sentry/nextjs/config` in a CJS next.config.js, `src/instrumentation.ts` -> `../sentry.server.config`). REFUTED — caveat (a) "you get spans but a 500". mysql2 works end to end; the EvalError was purely mysql2's `new Function` row-parser compiler, and mysql2's own `disableEval: true` connection option removes it. Nothing about the SDK changes: curl /api/db2 -> HTTP 200 {"driver":"mysql2","rows":[{"id":1,"name":"ada"},{"id":2,"name":"linus"}]} sink __items (stream lifecycle): span ['resolve page components', 'db mysql2.pool.connect', 'db mysql2.connect', 'db SELECT users'] span ['executing api route (app) /api/db2/route', 'start response', 'http.server GET /api/db2'] (origin on all three db spans: auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel) With `traceLifecycle: 'static'` (earlier variant D, raw-D.json + wrangler-D.log in the same dir) the same run gives `GET /api/db2 200 OK (253ms)` and a transaction whose spans[] contains db `mysql2.pool.connect` / `mysql2.connect` / `SELECT id, name FROM users`, each `"origin": "auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel"`, `db.system.name: mysql`, `db.namespace: app`, `server.address: 127.0.0.1`, `server.port: 3307`. Without `disableEval` (variant A, wrangler-A.log:231-285) the same route gives the reported failure verbatim: `Sentry Logger [log]: Captured error event `Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`` ... `[wrangler:info] GET /api/db2 500 Internal Server Error (24ms)` — spans still emitted. CONFIRMED — caveat (b) mysql@2 gets no spans. Same run: `curl /api/db -> HTTP 200 {"driver":"mysql","rows":[...]}` and the trace has only `['executing api route (app) /api/db/route', 'start response', 'http.server GET /api/db']`, no db span. Root cause found in the SDK, not just observed: packages/nextjs/src/config/diagnosticsChannelInjection.ts:9 `export const BUNDLE_SAFE_INSTRUMENTED_PACKAGES = ['ioredis'];` — with build-time instrumentation on, only ioredis is dropped from Sentry's `serverExternalPackages` defaults, so every other instrumented package (mysql, pg, ...) stays external and depends on the runtime module hook, and that hook cannot register on workerd: `[Sentry] Failed to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks ... TypeError: port1.on is not a function` / `Sentry Logger [log]: [Sentry] Runtime hook not registered` / `[Sentry] Bundler plugin ran, injected libraries=[]`. Forcing mysql into the webpack bundle (variant B: user `serverExternalPackages` filtered to drop mysql/mysql2) does make injection work — `[instrumentation:mysql] "mysql" injected at runtime, subscribing now` then a `db` span `SELECT id, name FROM users` — but the bundled driver then dies with `Error: Received packet in the wrong sequence.` / `code: 'PROTOCOL_INCORRECT_PACKET_SEQUENCE'` and a 500; variant C shows the identical failure with `buildTimeInstrumentation: false`, so bundling mysql@2 for workerd is broken independently of Sentry. So mysql@2 is a real dead end here, matching the SDK's own comment that mysql 2.x is not bundle-safe. Net: on Next.js/OpenNext/workerd you get db spans only for drivers that publish their own diagnostics channels (mysql2 does; `.open-next/server-functions/default/node_modules/mysql2/lib/tracing.js`). For those, spans and a working query both work with no extra plugin or build step. Reproduce: `npm install`, `npx opennextjs-cloudflare build`, `PORT=51873 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs &`, `npx wrangler dev --port 51874 --inspector-port 0`, `curl 127.0.0.1:51874/api/db2`, `curl 127.0.0.1:51873/__items`. Files: next.config.js, sentry.server.config.ts, src/instrumentation.ts, src/app/api/db/route.ts (mysql@2), src/app/api/db2/route.ts (mysql2 + disableEval), logs build-F.log / wrangler-F.log / sink-F.log plus the earlier per-variant wrangler-A..E.log and raw-D.json, all under that directory. node_modules removed after the run.
Workaround: For mysql2 on Cloudflare Workers, pass mysql2's own `disableEval: true` in the connection/pool options (`mysql2.createPool({ host, port, user, database, disableEval: true })`). workerd forbids `new Function`, and mysql2 compiles its row parsers that way; `disableEval` switches it to the static parsers, after which the query returns rows (HTTP 200) and the `db mysql2.pool.connect` / `db mysql2.connect` / `db SELECT <table>` spans arrive unchanged. This is app-side driver config, no Sentry option involved. There is no workaround for mysql@2 (or any driver without built-in diagnostics channels): the runtime module hook cannot register on workerd, and pulling mysql into the webpack bundle via `serverExternalPackages` yields spans but breaks the driver with PROTOCOL_INCORRECT_PACKET_SEQUENCE even with Sentry's build-time instrumentation disabled.

Docs today

Exactly one page covers this combination: ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/nextjs.mdx (56 lines total). nextjs.mdx:6 claims "The Sentry Next.js SDK supports Next.js applications deployed on Cloudflare Workers, but requires additional configuration". nextjs.mdx:14 points at OpenNext, nextjs.mdx:15 at the plain Next.js install guide. The whole body of advice is two wrangler settings: nextjs.mdx:28-38 `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]`, and nextjs.mdx:40-54 `compatibility_date` >= "2025-08-16" "required to introduce https.request ... which the Sentry SDK needs to send data". nextjs.mdx:56 then says "You should start seeing error events, traces, and logs appear in Sentry." ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/best-practices/deploying-on-cloudflare.mdx:1-7 is a stub that only redirects to that page. Nothing else in docs/platforms/javascript/ or platform-includes/ mentions opennext/open-next. What the page does not say, and my run shows it should: (a) the three setup traps above (withSentryConfig now only on @sentry/nextjs/config on the v11 line, the ESM next.config.mjs named-export failure, sendDefaultPii removed); (b) instrumentation.ts must sit in src/ when the app is in src/app, otherwise register() never runs and there is complete silence with no warning; (c) outgoing fetch and node:http from a handler get no client span and no trace headers, so distributed tracing out of a Cloudflare-hosted Next.js app is dead - the page's blanket "traces" claim overstates it; (d) @sentry/server-runtime-injection cannot register on workerd (`port1.on is not a function`) and the SDK prints a scary warning at every boot; (e) db instrumentation works only for libraries that publish their own diagnostics_channel (mysql2 does, mysql@2 does not) - and mysql2 itself cannot execute a query on workerd because of the codegen restriction. Note also that the page never mentions @sentry/cloudflare; @sentry/nextjs alone is the correct and sufficient package, and the SDK does detect the environment (it sets contexts.runtime.name to "cloudflare" and tags the SDK metadata "nextjs,cloudflare").

Documented: partial

The page's two wrangler settings are correct but incomplete: errors, route names, isolation, incoming trace continuation and logs worked, while two capabilities needed undocumented steps. (1) Outgoing fetch produced no spans and no trace propagation out of the box. The page must state that on Cloudflare Workers the Next.js SDK does not instrument outgoing HTTP automatically, because the Workers runtime provides a native `fetch` instead of the Node.js implementation the SDK patches, and must show the fix: install `@sentry/cloudflare` explicitly (it is not a transitive dependency of `@sentry/nextjs`) and add `fetchIntegration()` from `@sentry/cloudflare` to the `integrations` array in `sentry.server.config.ts`. (2) Database spans work, but only with `disableEval: true` passed to `mysql2`'s `createPool`/`createConnection`; without it the query throws `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed` because workerd forbids `new Function`, which mysql2 uses to compile row parsers. Nothing about the Sentry configuration changes for db spans, and `next.config.js` stays the plain `withSentryConfig` wrapper. The word `disableEval` appears nowhere in the docs today.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/nextjs.mdx — add an "Instrument Outgoing HTTP Requests" section after the Wrangler section (after :54) with the `@sentry/cloudflare` install plus `fetchIntegration()` in `sentry.server.config.ts`, and a "Database Spans" section documenting `disableEval: true` for mysql2

That is the entire body of advice. Missing: `grep -rn disableEval docs/platforms/javascript platform-includes` returns zero hits anywhere in the docs. `@sentry/cloudflare` is never mentioned on nextjs.mdx (the only install instruction is the generic Next.js guide link at :15), and docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/integrations/fetchIntegration.mdx:14-22 documents `Sentry.fetchIntegration` only under the Cloudflare platform (platform-includes/configuration/integrations/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:6), with no cross-reference from the Next.js on Cloudflare page. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:19 links to this page from the framework list.

Ports used: sink 41337, wrangler dev 41338. Both processes killed; node_modules removed. Overall this combination is in good shape: 6 of 7 probed capabilities work, and the one broken capability (outgoing fetch) is the same workerd-vs-undici gap the plain Cloudflare SDK works around with its own fetch instrumentation - @sentry/nextjs running on OpenNext gets @sentry/node's NodeFetch integration instead, which patches an undici that is not there. That is the single highest-value fix or docs caveat for this cell. Both trace lifecycles were exercised end to end. 'static' produced `transaction` envelopes with the Next.js internal spans nested (`resolve page components`, `executing api route (app) /<route>/route`, `start response`) plus the mysql2 db spans; 'stream' produced `span` envelopes with the root named `http.server GET /api/users/[id]`. Route naming, error capture, isolation, incoming-trace continuation and the missing fetch span behaved identically under both; the db span description is the only difference (`SELECT id, name FROM users` under static vs the low-cardinality `SELECT users` under stream). Two incidental environment facts worth passing on: `npm install typescript` now installs TypeScript 7, which Next 15 rejects outright ("TypeScript 7 is not supported by this version of Next.js"), so pin typescript@5. And this npm blocks postinstall scripts (workerd, esbuild) - harmless here because the platform-specific optional packages @cloudflare/workerd-darwin-arm64 and @esbuild/darwin-arm64 are installed directly. Not probed (out of scope for this cell): browser/client-side errors and replay, middleware, server components / server actions, pages router, Durable Objects, and source map upload (sourcemaps were explicitly disabled). The build did warn that no `global-error.js` is present, which is the documented app-router requirement for React render errors.

# 2. sink + build + serve
PORT=41337 node sink.mjs > sink.log 2>&1 &        # extended sink, keeps trace ids / tags / recorder headers
npx opennextjs-cloudflare build
npx wrangler dev --port 41338 --inspector-port 0 > wrangler.log 2>&1 &

# 3. probes
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:41338/api/error          # errors
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:41338/api/users/42                                        # route names
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:41338/api/iso?t=alpha" & curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:41338/api/iso?t=bravo" & \
  curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:41338/api/iso?t=charlie" & wait                        # isolation
curl -s -H "sentry-trace: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1" \
     -H "baggage: sentry-trace_id=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa,sentry-environment=probe-env,sentry-public_key=abc123,sentry-sample_rate=1" \
     http://127.0.0.1:41338/api/ping                                               # incoming trace
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:41338/api/outfetch?rec=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A41337%2F__rec"   # outgoing fetch
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:41338/api/outhttp?rec=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A41337%2F__rec"    # outgoing node:http
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:41338/api/db     # mysql2 db spans
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:41338/api/db2    # mysql@2, no spans
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:41338/api/logs   # logs (wait ~7s or drive more traffic)
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:41338/api/sentinel?n=1"   # sentinel: captureMessage + flush

# 4. read the sink
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:41337/__items | node -e "let s='';process.stdin.on('data',d=>s+=d).on('end',()=>{JSON.parse(s).forEach(i=>console.log(JSON.stringify(i)))})"
curl -s -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:41337/__items

Nuxt on Cloudflare M-nuxt-cf

Nuxt 4.2.x (nitro `cloudflare_module` preset, h3 v1, server routes under `server/api/`) · Cloudflare Workers (workerd via `wrangler dev` 4.129.0, `nodejs_compat`, compatibility_date 2026-05-01) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Packages: `nuxt@^4.1.2`, `wrangler@^4`, plus the develop SDK tarballs `@sentry/nuxt` and `@sentry/cloudflare` (npm also needs `@sentry/{core,node,vue,browser,browser-utils,replay,replay-canvas,feedback,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry,bundler-plugins}` on the same `npm install` line to resolve the 10.67.0 tarball deps). Do NOT install `@sentry/nitro` alongside `@sentry/nuxt`: it drags in `nitro@3.0.0` next to Nuxt 4's nitropack.

`nuxt.config.ts`:
```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  compatibilityDate: '2025-06-06',
  modules: ['@sentry/nuxt/module'],
  nitro: {
    preset: 'cloudflare_module',
    cloudflare: { nodeCompat: true, deployConfig: false },
    // only needed if you bundle the `mysql` driver
    alias: { 'readable-stream': 'node:stream' },
  },
});
```

`server/plugins/sentry.ts` (this is the init; there is no `sentry.server.config.ts` on Cloudflare):
```ts
import { defineNitroPlugin } from '#imports';
import { sentryCloudflareNitroPlugin } from '@sentry/nuxt/module/plugins';

export default defineNitroPlugin(
  sentryCloudflareNitroPlugin({
    dsn: '<dsn>',
    tracesSampleRate: 1.0,
    // traceLifecycle: 'static',  // optional; default is 'stream'
  }),
);
```

`wrangler.jsonc`:
```jsonc
{
  "name": "m-nuxt-cf",
  "main": "./.output/server/index.mjs",
  "compatibility_date": "2026-05-01",
  "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"],
  "assets": { "directory": "./.output/public", "binding": "ASSETS" }
}
```

Run: `npx nuxt build` then `npx wrangler dev --port <port> --inspector-port 0`. Inside route handlers both `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/cloudflare'` and `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nuxt'` work (verified both). No Vite plugin, no bundler plugin, no extra instrumentation step is needed: `@sentry/nuxt/module` detects the `cloudflare*` preset and pushes `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` into the Nitro rollup config itself (`packages/nuxt/src/vite/orchestrion.ts:19-64`, `buildTimeInstrumentation` defaults true). Sentry is inert under `nuxt dev` (orchestrion is skipped in dev and there is no workerd); you must build and run wrangler.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ works`throw new Error('nuxt-cf-route-error')` in `server/api/error.ts` arrives as an event with `mechanism.type: "auto.function.nuxt.nitro"`, `handled: false`, `transaction: "GET /api/error"`, `sdk: sentry.javascript.cloudflare`, captured through Nitro's `error` hook (`sentryCaptureErrorHook`, registered by `sentryCloudflareNitroPlugin`). Nuxt still converts it to a 500 error page but does not swallow it from Sentry; LinkedErrors adds a second `chained`/`source: cause` copy of the same error which sorts first in `exception.values`. Same in both lifecycles.
route names✗ brokenParameterized routes are correct in both lifecycles: static gives transaction `GET /api/users/:id` with `source: "route"`; stream gives segment `http.server GET /api/users/:id` with `sentry.segment.name.source: "route"`, `http.route: "/api/users/:id"`, `url.path.parameter.id: "42"`, `params.id: "42"`. The partial: a NON-parameterized route gets no route attribute at all, because `updateRouteBeforeResponse` only fires when `matchedRoute.path !== event.path`. Under `stream` that leaves `/api/db`, `/api/log`, `/api/sentinel` as the method-only segment `http.server GET`; under `static` they keep the URL-derived `GET /api/db` with `source: "url"`. verified: confirmed-broken Could not refute. Reproduced end to end and the reported defect stands exactly as described: on Nuxt 4.2 + nitro `cloudflare_module` + `@sentry/nuxt` develop (10.67.0), a NON-parameterized Nitro server route gets no `http.route` and no route-sourced segment name. Parameterized routes are correct. App: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-nuxt-cf-routenames/app (nuxt.config.ts, wrangler.jsonc, server/plugins/sentry.ts, server/plugins/route-name.ts, server/api/{db,log,sentinel,users/[id]}.ts). node_modules removed after the run. Install: npm install --no-audit --no-fund nuxt@^4.1.2 wrangler@^4 $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{nuxt,cloudflare,core,node,vue,browser,browser-utils,replay,replay-canvas,feedback,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry,bundler-plugins}-10.67.0.tgz Run: npx nuxt build && npx wrangler dev --port 41791 --inspector-port 0 ; sink: PORT=41777 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs RUN A - stream (default lifecycle), stock SDK, no extra plugin. Sink `span` items: {"type":"span","items":["http.server GET"],"raw":[{"name":"GET","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.cloudflare"}]} <- GET /api/db {"type":"span","items":["http.server GET"],"raw":[{"name":"GET","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.cloudflare"}]} <- GET /api/log {"type":"span","items":["http.server GET /api/users/:id"],"raw":[{"name":"GET /api/users/:id","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.cloudflare"}]} {"type":"span","items":["http.server GET"],...} <- GET /api/sentinel So under `stream` three of four routes collapse to the method-only segment `http.server GET`. RUN D - static lifecycle, stock SDK. Transaction envelopes: {"name":"GET /api/db","src":"url"} {"name":"GET /api/users/:id","src":"route","route":"/api/users/:id","pid":"42"} {"name":"GET /api/sentinel","src":"url"} Static keeps a usable URL-derived name but still has no `http.route` and `transaction_info.source: "url"`. Root cause confirmed in source, not inferred: packages/nuxt/src/module.ts:105-121 registers `route-detector.server` and `update-route-name.server` only when a `sentry.server.config.*` file exists (the Node path). The Cloudflare path has no server config file, so the only route source is `nitroApp.hooks.hook('beforeResponse', updateRouteBeforeResponse)` in packages/nuxt/src/runtime/plugins/sentry-cloudflare.server.ts:103. That hook (packages/nuxt/src/runtime/hooks/updateRouteBeforeResponse.ts:26) gates on if (matchedRoutePath && matchedRoutePath !== requestPath) { so it calls `setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute` only when the matched route differs from the request path, i.e. only for parameterized routes. `event.context.matchedRoute` IS populated for plain routes - I echoed it from the handler: GET /api/db returned `"matchedRoute":{"path":"/api/db","handlers":{}}`. Only the `!==` comparison suppresses it. Refutation attempts that all failed to fix it: - Documented wiring is already what I ran: ~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.nuxt.mdx:287-292 shows exactly this `server/plugins/sentry.ts` with `sentryCloudflareNitroPlugin({ dsn, tracesSampleRate })`. No route-related option is documented or exists. - Other trace lifecycle: RUN D above. `static` masks the severity but does not set `http.route` or `source: route`. - Module/init options: `SentryNuxtModuleOptions` (packages/nuxt/src/common/types.ts) has no route/naming toggle; grep for "route" in that file returns nothing. - Adding a `sentry.server.config.ts` to make `module.ts` register `update-route-name.server` / `route-detector.server` would not help - `update-route-name.server` calls the same `updateRouteBeforeResponse` with the same guard, and `route-detector.server` only handles the SSR page catch-all (`/**`), not `server/api/*`. - Repo e2e reference `dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/nuxt-4-cloudflare` uses this identical wiring and has only `tests/db.test.ts` - no route-name coverage at all, which is why this is unguarded. - Bundler variant: none applies. `@sentry/nuxt/module` pushes `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` into the Nitro rollup config itself for `cloudflare*` presets, so there is no alternative build path to try. RUN C - proof the fix is a one-line SDK change. I patched only the built hook in node_modules (`@sentry/nuxt/build/module/runtime/hooks/updateRouteBeforeResponse.js`), replacing `if (matchedRoutePath && matchedRoutePath !== requestPath)` with `if (matchedRoutePath)` (the `/**` early return kept), user plugin disabled, stream lifecycle. Segment attributes: {"name":"GET /api/db","route":"/api/db","src":"route","path":"/api/db"} {"name":"GET /api/log","route":"/api/log","src":"route","path":"/api/log"} {"name":"GET /api/users/:id","route":"/api/users/:id","src":"route","pid":"42","path":"/api/users/42"} {"name":"GET /api/sentinel","route":"/api/sentinel","src":"route","path":"/api/sentinel"} No regression on the parameterized route, and the SSR page `/` still falls through the `/**` early return.
Workaround: Add a second Nitro plugin next to the Sentry one that sets the route unconditionally. Verified working (RUN B, stream lifecycle, stock SDK) - file at .../verify4-M-nuxt-cf-routenames/app/server/plugins/route-name.ts: import { defineNitroPlugin } from '#imports'; import { getActiveSpan, getRootSpan, spanToJSON } from '@sentry/cloudflare'; export default defineNitroPlugin(nitroApp => { nitroApp.hooks.hook('beforeResponse', (event: any) => { const route = event.context?.matchedRoute?.path ?? event.context?.matchedRoute?.route; if (!route || route === '/**') return; const activeSpan = getActiveSpan(); if (!activeSpan) return; const rootSpan = getRootSpan(activeSpan); if (!rootSpan) return; const attrs = spanToJSON(rootSpan).attributes ?? {}; if (attrs['sentry.op'] !== 'http.server') return; if (attrs['http.route']) return; const method = attrs['http.request.method'] ?? attrs['http.method'] ?? 'GET'; rootSpan.setAttribute('http.route', route); rootSpan.updateName(`${method} ${route}`); rootSpan.setAttribute('sentry.segment.name.source', 'route'); }); }); Result with it in place (stream, unpatched SDK): {"name":"GET /api/db","route":"/api/db","src":"route"} {"name":"GET /api/log","route":"/api/log","src":"route"} {"name":"GET /api/users/:id","route":"/api/users/:id","src":"route","pid":"42"} {"name":"GET /api/sentinel","route":"/api/sentinel","src":"route"} It only fills in what the SDK left empty (the `http.route` guard), so it is safe to keep after the SDK is fixed. `@sentry/server-utils` also exports `setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute` from its main entry and is already a dependency of `@sentry/nuxt`, but it is an internal package and pulls Node-only instrumentation into a workerd bundle, so the `@sentry/cloudflare`-only form above is the one to publish. Proper fix: drop the `matchedRoutePath !== requestPath` comparison in packages/nuxt/src/runtime/hooks/updateRouteBeforeResponse.ts:26 and keep only the `/**` early return. The param-attribute loop below it is already a no-op when `event.context.params` is absent.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent `GET /api/iso?tag=<alpha|beta|gamma>` requests (setTag, await 150ms, captureException) produced three events with exactly one tag each and three distinct trace ids; the matching transactions carry the same per-request tag and trace id. No cross-talk. Run under `traceLifecycle: 'static'`. `sentryCloudflareNitroPlugin` clones the isolation scope per `nitroApp.localFetch` call inside `wrapRequestHandler`.
incoming trace✓ works`GET /api/users/7` with `sentry-trace: aaaa…aaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` and a matching `baggage` produced a transaction with `trace_id: "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"` and `parent_span_id: "bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb"`, and the route name still resolved to `/api/users/:id`. Run under `traceLifecycle: 'static'`.
outgoing fetch✓ works`fetch('http://127.0.0.1:<sink>/__record?from=nuxt')` from inside a handler produced `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:39411/__record` as a child of the request transaction (static) and `http.client GET 127.0.0.1` with `parent_span_id` set (stream); the recorder received both `sentry-trace` and `baggage` with the same trace id as the server span.
db spans✓ worksA module-scope `mysql.createConnection` (MariaDB 127.0.0.1:3307) queried from `server/api/db.ts` produced `db SELECT id, name FROM users` (static) and `db SELECT users` with `sentry.origin: auto.db.mysql`, `sentry.kind: client` (stream). Instrumentation path: none added by hand. `@sentry/nuxt/module` auto-injects `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` into Nitro's rollup config for any `cloudflare*` preset and inlines the instrumented modules, so no Cloudflare Vite plugin and no manual bundler step was needed. The only non-Sentry workaround required was `nitro.alias: { 'readable-stream': 'node:stream' }` so the bundled mysql driver boots under unenv.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info('nuxt-cf-log-probe', { where: 'route-handler' })` arrived as a `log` envelope item `info: nuxt-cf-log-probe` carrying the request's trace id. Verified importing from `@sentry/cloudflare` and, in a second build, from `@sentry/nuxt` (`info: nuxt-import-log-probe`); both work. Read after a `captureMessage('sentinel')` sentinel plus 8s for the log flush timer.

Docs today

The combination IS documented. `~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/nuxt.mdx:1-11` is a "Nuxt on Cloudflare" page stating it covers Nitro's `cloudflare_module` (and the deprecated `cloudflare-pages`) preset; it only pulls in `platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.nuxt.mdx`. The Cloudflare-specific part of that include is `platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.nuxt.mdx:261-322`: "Configure Cloudflare for Sentry" (:263), a warning to delete any existing `sentry.server.config.ts` (:276-279), the `server/plugins/sentry-cloudflare-plugin.ts` snippet with `sentryCloudflareNitroPlugin({ dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 })` (:286-293) and a `nitroApp` callback variant (:306-316). The `nodejs_compat` flag and compatibility_date requirement arrive via `platform-includes/getting-started-config/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:5,14,20`. From the Nuxt side, `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/features/nitro-deployment-presets.mdx:9-11` has a "Cloudflare Pages" section that only links onward, and `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/index.mdx:125` links to that presets page. What the docs do NOT say but my run needed or observed: nothing about setting `nitro.preset: 'cloudflare_module'` / `nitro.cloudflare.nodeCompat` in `nuxt.config.ts` (the reader must already have it); nothing about the `nitro.alias: { 'readable-stream': 'node:stream' }` workaround the bundled `mysql` driver needs; nothing about Sentry being inert under `nuxt dev` on this preset (you must `nuxt build` then `wrangler dev`); no mention of `traceLifecycle`, of which Sentry package to import inside a server route, or that DB/library spans come for free from the module's auto-injected orchestrion rollup plugin (`buildTimeInstrumentation`).

Documented: partial

The documented wiring is correct and six of seven capabilities worked with it verbatim. The missing piece is server route naming: only routes carrying parameters, such as `/api/users/[id]`, are reported under their route pattern. A parameterless server route such as `/api/health` is reported as bare `GET` under the default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'`, and as the full request URL under `traceLifecycle: 'static'` — in both cases with a URL-derived name rather than the Nitro route pattern. The page must state this limitation and show the ship-today fix that was verified to produce identical output to a patched SDK: a second Nitro server plugin registered next to the Sentry one that uses only public `@sentry/cloudflare` exports (`getActiveSpan`, `getRootSpan`, `spanToJSON`) to rename the root span to the matched Nitro route and set the segment-name source accordingly.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/nuxt.mdx — replace the bare include passthrough with a page that keeps the include and adds a "Server Route Names" section documenting the `GET`/URL naming on Workers and the route-naming Nitro plugin workaround

docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/nuxt.mdx:1-11 ("Nuxt on Cloudflare", :6 names Nitro's `cloudflare_module` and the deprecated `cloudflare-pages` preset, :8-11 pulls in the shared include). The Cloudflare branch of that include is platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.nuxt.mdx:261-322: :263-268 "Configure Cloudflare for Sentry" (wrangler config via getting-started-config/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:5-21), :276-279 the warning to delete an existing `sentry.server.config.ts`, :286-293 the `sentryCloudflareNitroPlugin` server plugin, :306-316 the `nitroApp` variant. Cross-links: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/features/nitro-deployment-presets.mdx:9-11; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:20. Missing: `grep -rn -i "transaction_info|route name|segment name" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/ platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.nuxt.mdx` returns zero hits — no page anywhere describes how the root/segment span is named on Cloudflare, and `traceLifecycle` is discussed only at docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:378-384 in the context of `waitUntil()`.

Viability was established before Sentry: a plain Nuxt 4 app with the `cloudflare_module` preset builds and serves on workerd with no Sentry at all (`{"ok":true}` from `/api/hello`). Six of seven capabilities are clean. The one soft spot is route naming for non-parameterized server routes: `updateRouteBeforeResponse` (`packages/nuxt/src/runtime/hooks/updateRouteBeforeResponse.ts:17-40`) only sets the route attribute when `matchedRoute.path !== event.path`, so `/api/db` never gets `http.route` and, under the develop default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'`, its segment is the method-only `http.server GET`. Under `static` the same route still reads `GET /api/db` with `source: "url"`, so the gap is only visible on the streaming default develop now ships. Setting the route attribute whenever `matchedRoutePath` exists and is not `/**` would fix it. Other findings worth carrying forward: - No manual instrumentation step is needed for DB spans on this preset. `@sentry/nuxt/module` matches any `cloudflare*` preset and pushes `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` into `nitroConfig.rollupConfig.plugins`, plus inlines `INSTRUMENTED_MODULE_NAMES` (`packages/nuxt/src/vite/orchestrion.ts:19-64`). No Cloudflare Vite plugin, no Bun/Deno-style hook. - Installing `@sentry/nitro` next to `@sentry/nuxt` pulls `nitro@3.0.0` in beside Nuxt 4's nitropack; I uninstalled it. Only `@sentry/nuxt` + `@sentry/cloudflare` are needed. - Both `@sentry/cloudflare` and `@sentry/nuxt` resolve to a workerd-safe build when imported from a server route; both emitted logs. The docs recommend neither. - The error event's real mechanism is `auto.function.nuxt.nitro` with `handled: false`; LinkedErrors adds a `chained`/`source: cause` duplicate that sorts first in `exception.values`, so a naive `values[0]` read (as the shared sink does) reports `chained`/`handled: true`. Not a bug, but it misleads quick assertions. - Environment friction, not SDK: port 41337 was already held by another agent's Astro server, and a wrangler process I started and abandoned kept a port bound long enough to make a second bind fail. The runs that matter are all on port 52719. - Cleanup: sink and wrangler processes killed (no `M-nuxt-cf` process remains), `app-nuxt/node_modules` (519 MB) removed; the task dir is 4.9 MB.

CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksA throw in src/routes/boom/+server.ts is reported as an unhandled event with mechanism `auto.function.sveltekit.handle_error` (handled:false), sdk `sentry.javascript.cloudflare`, transaction `GET /boom`, correct request context, and the matching transaction gets status `internal_error`. SvelteKit still converts it to a 500 JSON body for the client, so it is swallowed at the HTTP layer but not at the Sentry layer. traceLifecycle 'static'.
route names✗ brokenThe parameterized route only reaches a NESTED span, never the segment. static lifecycle: transaction name `GET /users/42`, transaction_info.source `url`, `sentry.segment.name.source: url`, origin auto.http.cloudflare; its child span is `GET /users/[id]` with `http.route: /users/[id]` and origin auto.http.sveltekit. stream lifecycle (develop default): the is_segment span is named just `GET` with source `url` and no http.route, and `GET /users/[id]` is again a non-segment child. So group-by-transaction in Sentry would see the raw URL (static) or bare `GET` (stream). verified: confirmed-broken Reproduced the reported behavior exactly, with the documented wiring, and could not refute it. Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-sveltekit-cf-routenames/ (app/, logs bB1-bB5.log builds, wB1-wB5.log wrangler, sinkB.log). Same stack as reported: SvelteKit 2.70.3 / svelte 5.57.0 / adapter-cloudflare 5.1.0 / vite 6.4.3, @sentry/sveltekit 10.67.0 from $REPRO/_toolbox/pack, wrangler 4.129.0, compatibility_date 2026-05-01 + nodejs_compat. Sink on 37421, worker on 37422. Commands: (cd app && npm install --no-audit --no-fund) ; PORT=37421 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs & ; (cd app && npx vite build && npx wrangler dev --port 37422 --inspector-port 0) ; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:37422/users/42 ; curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:37422/sentinel?n=N" ; curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:37421/__items?raw=1". VARIANT 1 - docs wiring exactly as in ~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.sveltekit.mdx:331-352 (sequence(initCloudflareSentryHandle({...}), sentryHandle())), stream lifecycle (develop default). Segment loses the route: {"name": "GET /users/[id]", "is_segment": false, "attrs": {"sentry.origin": "auto.http.sveltekit", "sentry.op": "http.server", "url.path": "/users/42", "http.route": "/users/[id]"}} {"name": "GET", "is_segment": true, "attrs": {"sentry.origin": "auto.http.cloudflare", "sentry.op": "http.server", "sentry.segment.name.source": "url", "url.path": "/users/42"}} Worse than reported: this is not limited to parameterized routes. A plain static route loses its name too, because the Cloudflare wrapper only keeps a name whose source is already 'route' (i.e. only "/"): {"name": "GET /sentinel", "is_segment": false, ...auto.http.sveltekit...} {"name": "GET", "is_segment": true, "attrs": {"sentry.origin": "auto.http.cloudflare", "sentry.segment.name.source": "url", "url.path": "/sentinel"}} VARIANT 2 - same wiring, traceLifecycle: 'static'. Segment carries the raw URL: TX GET /users/42 {"source": "url"} {"sentry.origin": "auto.http.cloudflare", "sentry.op": "http.server", "sentry.segment.name.source": "url", "url.path": "/users/42"} span GET /users/[id] {"sentry.origin": "auto.http.sveltekit", "http.route": "/users/[id]"} TX GET /sentinel {"source": "url"} ... span GET /sentinel ... VARIANT 3 - SvelteKit native tracing (svelte.config.js kit.experimental.tracing.server = true), stream lifecycle. This makes it strictly WORSE, not better: sentryHandle skips its own span (kitTracingEnabled), Kit's root span never materializes on Cloudflare, and no route-named http.server span exists at all - the route survives only as an attribute on a `function` span: {"name": "sveltekit.resolve", "is_segment": false, "attrs": {"sentry.origin": "auto.http.sveltekit", "http.route": "/users/[id]", "sentry.op": "function"}} {"name": "sveltekit.handle.sequenced.sentryRequestHandler", "is_segment": false, "attrs": {"sentry.origin": "auto.function.sveltekit.handle", "sentry.op": "function"}} {"name": "GET", "is_segment": true, "attrs": {"sentry.origin": "auto.http.cloudflare", "sentry.op": "http.server", "sentry.segment.name.source": "url", "url.path": "/users/42"}} The SDK already knows about this: packages/sveltekit/src/server-common/integrations/svelteKitSpans.ts has "in Cloudflare, the kit-emitted root span is missing but our cloudflare SDK emits the http.server span". ROOT CAUSE (read in the worktree, not guessed). packages/cloudflare/src/wrapRequestHandlerWithInit.ts creates the segment span and comments "After the handler runs, the span name might have been updated by nested instrumentation (e.g., Remix parameterizing routes)" - i.e. the contract is that the framework layer renames the SEGMENT. packages/sveltekit/src/server-common/handle.ts does not: outside Kit tracing it unconditionally `startSpan(...)`s a NEW child with the route name/http.route, and inside Kit tracing it only renames `event.tracing.root`, which on Cloudflare is not the segment (and here does not exist). Nothing in @sentry/cloudflare or @sentry/sveltekit ever calls getRootSpan()/updateSpanName() on the Cloudflare segment. TEST COVERAGE GAP: dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/sveltekit-3-cloudflare-workers/tests/server.test.ts asserts the segment name is "GET /" for the "/" route. "/" is the one path whose URL-derived name already has source 'route', so the assertion passes while every other route is broken. The app has no parameterized route. Errors are unaffected: the captured event still carries the right grouping name, because sentryHandle sets it on the isolation scope - {"type":"event","message":"sentinel-1","transaction":"GET /sentinel","sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare"}. Only span/transaction naming is wrong.
Workaround: A user-land `handle` inserted between `initCloudflareSentryHandle` and `sentryHandle` fixes both lifecycles. Verified working (file: app/src/hooks.server.workaround.ts in the probe dir): import { getActiveSpan, getRootSpan, handleErrorWithSentry, initCloudflareSentryHandle, sentryHandle } from '@sentry/sveltekit'; import { sequence } from '@sveltejs/kit/hooks'; const nameSegmentByRoute = ({ event, resolve }) => { const routeId = event.route?.id; const activeSpan = getActiveSpan(); if (routeId && activeSpan && !event.isSubRequest) { const segment = getRootSpan(activeSpan); segment.updateName(`${event.request.method} ${routeId}`); segment.setAttributes({ 'sentry.segment.name.source': 'route', 'http.route': routeId }); } return resolve(event); }; export const handle = sequence(initCloudflareSentryHandle({ ... }), nameSegmentByRoute, sentryHandle()); Do NOT use Sentry.updateSpanName() here - it stamps `sentry.segment.name.source: 'custom'`; setting 'route' explicitly is what makes Sentry treat it as a parameterized route. The `!event.isSubRequest` guard keeps a same-origin `fetch` from a server `load` from renaming the outer segment. Stream lifecycle after the workaround: {"name": "GET /users/[id]", "is_segment": true, "attrs": {"sentry.origin": "auto.http.cloudflare", "sentry.op": "http.server", "sentry.segment.name.source": "route", "url.path": "/users/42", "http.route": "/users/[id]"}} Static lifecycle after the workaround: TX GET /users/[id] {"source": "route"} {"sentry.origin": "auto.http.cloudflare", "sentry.segment.name.source": "route", "http.route": "/users/[id]", "url.path": "/users/42"} span GET /users/[id] {"sentry.origin": "auto.http.sveltekit", "http.route": "/users/[id]"} The proper SDK fix is the same three lines moved into `instrumentHandle` in packages/sveltekit/src/server-common/handle.ts: when the active span's root is not the span sentryHandle owns (the Cloudflare wrapper's segment), rename that root instead of, or in addition to, starting the child.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent GET /tagged?tag=alpha|beta|gamma (each Sentry.setTag then 150ms await then captureException) produced three events with exactly their own tag and three distinct trace ids, each matching its own transaction's trace id. No cross-talk. traceLifecycle 'static'.
incoming trace✓ worksGET /users/7 with `sentry-trace: aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff00001111-1111222233334444-1` and a sentry-* baggage header produced a transaction with trace_id aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff00001111 and parent_span_id 1111222233334444. traceLifecycle 'static'.
outgoing fetch✓ worksA plain `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:41325/rec')` inside a +server.ts handler produced `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41325/rec` as a child of the request transaction, and the recorder saw both `sentry-trace` (same trace id, sampled=1) and a full `baggage` header. traceLifecycle 'static'; in stream lifecycle the same span appears as `http.client GET 127.0.0.1` (host-only name).
db spans◐ partialInstrumentation path: the build-time orchestrion transform shipped in `sentrySvelteKit()` (@sentry/server-runtime-injection) - it is required, there is no OTel require-hook in workerd, and the worker log confirms it: `[instrumentation:mysql] "mysql" already injected, subscribing now` / `Integration installed: Mysql`. Once it builds, the span is correct: op `db`, `SELECT * FROM users`, db.system.name mysql, db.namespace app, server.port 3307, nested under the request. BUT with the docs-shaped config `vite build` CRASHES as soon as `mysql` is imported from a route: the transform emits `import require$$0 from "@sentry/core"` into the SSR chunk and SvelteKit's postbuild `analyse` step dies with `SyntaxError: The requested module '@sentry/core' does not provide an export named 'default'`. Removing only `sentrySvelteKit()` makes the same build succeed, so it is Sentry-caused. Adding `ssr: { noExternal: ['@sentry/core','@sentry/conventions','@opentelemetry/api'] }` is what unblocked it. Also note the connection must be created inside the handler (workerd forbids module-scope I/O), which is the opposite of the Bun/Node rule. verified: partial Could not fully refute. The db span itself is unambiguously correct and needs no extra wiring; the build crash is real but is **package-manager-dependent**, which the original report missed. REFUTED PART 1 — with a pnpm install the docs-shaped config builds and works with ZERO workaround. `/private/tmp/.../deep/verify4-M-sveltekit-cf-dbspans/appB` — pnpm, `@sentry/sveltekit` the only direct `@sentry/*` dep (rest via `pnpm.overrides` to the $REPRO/_toolbox/pack tarballs), vite 6.4.3, @sveltejs/kit 2.70.3, adapter-cloudflare 5.1.0, `vite.config.js` = exactly `plugins: [sentrySvelteKit({ autoUploadSourceMaps: false }), sveltekit()]`, no `ssr` block at all. npx vite build -> EXIT=0, "> Using @sveltejs/adapter-cloudflare ✔ done" npx wrangler dev --port 51878 --inspector-port 0 Worker log: `Sentry Logger [log]: [instrumentation:mysql] "mysql" already injected, subscribing now` / `subscribing to channels` / `Integration installed: Mysql`, and NO "Failed to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks" warning. Sink (traceLifecycle 'static'): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db-mysql","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare","spans":["http.server GET /db-mysql","db SELECT * FROM users"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db-mysql-module","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare","spans":["http.server GET /db-mysql-module","db SELECT * FROM users"]} Raw span (`/__items?raw=1`): {"op":"db","description":"SELECT * FROM users","status":"ok","data":{"sentry.origin":"auto.db.mysql","sentry.op":"db","sentry.kind":"client","db.system.name":"mysql","db.connection_string":"jdbc:mysql://127.0.0.1:3307/app","db.namespace":"app","db.user":"root","db.query.text":"SELECT * FROM users","db.query.summary":"SELECT users","server.address":"127.0.0.1","server.port":3307}} REFUTED PART 2 — "the connection must be created inside the handler" is wrong. `/db-mysql-module` creates the connection at module scope and produces the same `db SELECT * FROM users` span (mysql opens its socket lazily on the first query, so workerd's global-scope I/O ban is not hit). Both placements work. CONFIRMED PART — with an npm (hoisted) install the docs-shaped build still crashes, even when `@sentry/sveltekit` is the ONLY direct `@sentry/*` dependency (so it is not an artifact of the tarball install listing every package): `/private/tmp/.../deep/verify4-M-sveltekit-cf-dbspans/appD` (npm, same versions, same sources, `overrides` for the tarballs), `npx vite build`: .svelte-kit/output/server/chunks/index.js:2 import require$$0 from "@sentry/core"; SyntaxError: The requested module '@sentry/core' does not provide an export named 'default' at async analyse (.../node_modules/@sveltejs/kit/src/core/postbuild/analyse.js:106:62) The head of that chunk shows the whole family: `import require$$0$1 from "@sentry/conventions/attributes"`, `import require$$0$3 from "@opentelemetry/api"`, `import require$$4 from "@sentry/core/server"`. ROOT CAUSE (verified, not theorised). `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` (packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/bundler/vite.ts, `config()`) force-bundles the instrumented module plus `@sentry/server-utils`, but NOT `@sentry/core`, `@sentry/conventions` or `@opentelemetry/api`. The snippet injected into CJS `mysql` `require()`s `@sentry/server-utils`; under a hoisted layout that bare specifier resolves normally and vite picks server-utils' **CJS** build, whose `require('@sentry/core')` rollup-commonjs rewrites into a default import of an external named-exports-only ESM package. Under pnpm the bare specifier does not resolve from mysql's isolated location, so the plugin's own `resolveId` fallback (`resolveOrchestrionRuntimeRequest`) resolves the ESM build and the CJS path is never taken. That is why `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` apps (dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/cloudflare-orchestrion-mysql) never see it: the Workers build bundles everything. Variants I tried on the npm app (all in appD, `npx vite build -c <config>`): - vite.config.js (docs shape) -> FAIL, error above - vite.config.a.js ssr.noExternal ['@sentry/core'] -> FAIL, same error moves to '@sentry/conventions/attributes' - vite.config.b.js ssr.noExternal [/^@sentry\//,'@opentelemetry/api'] -> builds, but HARMFUL: it bundles `@sentry/sveltekit` itself and the Node SDK boots instead of the Cloudflare one. Sink shows `"sdk":"sentry.javascript.sveltekit","runtime":"node"`, the `http.server GET /db-mysql` child span disappears (`"spans":["db SELECT * FROM users"]`) and the worker logs `[Sentry] Failed to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks`. Do not document the regex. - vite.config.c.js ssr.noExternal ['@sentry/core','@sentry/conventions','@opentelemetry/api'] -> builds AND correct at runtime: `"sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare","spans":["http.server GET /db-mysql","db SELECT * FROM users"]` - vite.config.d.js sentrySvelteKit({ buildTimeInstrumentation: false }) -> builds, but no transform, so no db spans. Repro files: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-sveltekit-cf-dbspans/ — appB (pnpm, clean pass), appD (npm, repro + 4 variant configs), buildB*.log, buildD*.log, wranglerB_final.log, wranglerD.log. Both apps share src/hooks.server.ts (initCloudflareSentryHandle + sentryHandle + handleErrorWithSentry, tunnel 127.0.0.1:51873, traceLifecycle 'static') and routes /db-mysql (per-request connection) and /db-mysql-module (module-scope connection). Sink: `PORT=51873 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs`. appB node_modules is intact; appD node_modules is intact. All processes I started were killed (ports 51873/51876/51878 verified free).
Workaround: No workaround needed if the app is installed with pnpm (isolated node_modules) — the docs-shaped `plugins: [sentrySvelteKit(...), sveltekit()]` builds and emits the db span as-is. With npm or yarn (hoisted node_modules) add exactly these three to vite.config.js: `ssr: { noExternal: ['@sentry/core', '@sentry/conventions', '@opentelemetry/api'] }`. Do not use a `/^@sentry\//` regex: it force-bundles `@sentry/sveltekit` and boots the Node SDK instead of the Cloudflare one. The real fix belongs in the SDK: `sentryOrchestrionPlugin`'s `config()` hook in packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/bundler/vite.ts should add `@sentry/core`, `@sentry/conventions` and `@opentelemetry/api` to the `ssr.noExternal` list it already builds for `@sentry/server-utils`, or resolve the injected snippet to server-utils' ESM build so the CJS `require('@sentry/core')` path never appears.

client errors· not-runOnly the server side was probed; no hooks.client.ts / browser driver was set up, so client-side error and pageload behavior was not exercised.

Docs today

The combination IS documented. ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/sveltekit.mdx:1-9 is a "SvelteKit on Cloudflare" page that just renders `platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.sveltekit.mdx`; the Cloudflare-only branch of that include is `<PlatformSection supported={["javascript.cloudflare"]}>` at :311, with the `initCloudflareSentryHandle(...) + sentryHandle()` hooks.server snippet at :326-352. The SvelteKit guide links to it from docs/platforms/javascript/guides/sveltekit/index.mdx:69 and manual-setup__v10.7.0.mdx:30,329, both of which call it "Cloudflare Pages" only. Three gaps against develop: 1. The Vite snippets say `import { sentrySvelteKit } from "@sentry/sveltekit"` (platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.sveltekit.mdx:383, and again :421 and :476). On develop `sentrySvelteKit` is only exported from `@sentry/sveltekit/vite` - the main entry does not export it (packages/sveltekit/src/index.worker.ts has `// export * from './vite';` commented out, and index.server.ts/index.types.ts never mention vite). Verified: `import * as m from '@sentry/sveltekit'` -> `'sentrySvelteKit' in m === false`. 2. Nothing on the page mentions Workers (only Pages wording upstream) or shows a wrangler.jsonc with `main: .svelte-kit/cloudflare/_worker.js` + `assets`, which is what adapter-cloudflare 5 needs to run under `wrangler dev`. 3. Nothing warns that pulling a CJS database driver into a route breaks `vite build`, nor documents the `ssr.noExternal` escape hatch.

Documented: partial

Two things the run needed are absent from the include. (1) Route names are confirmed broken on Workers: unlike the Node SvelteKit SDK, the transaction/segment span is named by the Cloudflare request handler and keeps the raw URL — `GET /users/42` with `transaction_info.source: url` under `traceLifecycle: 'static'`, and bare `GET` with source `url` under the default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` — never the SvelteKit route id. The page must state this and show the verified fix: a user-land `handle` inserted between `initCloudflareSentryHandle` and `sentryHandle` in the `sequence`, which renames the Cloudflare segment span using `getActiveSpan`/`getRootSpan` from `@sentry/sveltekit`; it works in both lifecycles. (2) Database spans come from the build-time transform that `sentrySvelteKit()` (:387) already installs, so no extra setup is needed and the connection may live at module scope or inside the handler — but only on pnpm's isolated `node_modules`. On a flat `node_modules` (npm or Yarn) the spans are missing until `ssr: { noExternal: [/^@sentry\//] }` is added to `vite.config.js`; that single regex is the minimal fix (naming only `@sentry/core` is not enough, and `@opentelemetry/api` need not be listed).

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/sveltekit.mdx — replace the bare include passthrough with a page that keeps the include and adds "Route Names on Cloudflare Workers" (the raw-URL naming plus the intermediate `handle` workaround) and "Database Spans" (the npm/Yarn `ssr.noExternal` requirement) sections

docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/sveltekit.mdx:1-9 ("SvelteKit on Cloudflare", renders the shared include). The Cloudflare branch is platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.sveltekit.mdx:311-365 — :316 the hooks description, :322-352 the `sequence(initCloudflareSentryHandle({...}), sentryHandle())` snippet, :354-360 `handleErrorWithSentry`; plus :369-394 "Configure Vite" with `sentrySvelteKit()` before `sveltekit()`, and :396-405 "Configure Cloudflare for Sentry" (wrangler via getting-started-config/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:5-21). :44 points adapter-cloudflare users at the Cloudflare guide; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:22 links back. Missing: `grep -rn noExternal docs/platforms/javascript platform-includes` returns zero hits, and `grep -rn -i "transaction_info|route name|segment name" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/` returns zero hits.

Two findings worth filing. (a) BUILD BREAK, Sentry-caused: with the exact docs config, `vite build` dies in SvelteKit's postbuild `analyse` step the moment a route imports `mysql`. The orchestrion/server-runtime-injection transform run by `sentrySvelteKit()` rewrites the bundled CJS driver and emits `import require$$0 from "@sentry/core"` into the SSR chunk; `@sentry/core` is ESM-only and left external by SvelteKit's SSR externalization, so Node throws `does not provide an export named 'default'`. Control proves it is Sentry's: the identical app builds cleanly with only `sentrySvelteKit()` removed. `ssr: { noExternal: ['@sentry/core','@sentry/conventions','@opentelemetry/api'] }` fixes it (the db-mysql chunk then weighs 2.36 MB). The in-repo e2e app dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/sveltekit-cloudflare-pages has the same mysql route and does NOT carry this workaround, so it is worth checking whether that app's pinned @sveltejs/kit 2.69.1 / pnpm layout hides the same defect. (b) SEGMENT NAME never gets the route. `svelteKitSpansIntegration` sets the parameterized name and `http.route` on a CHILD span, while the segment stays the Cloudflare request span (`GET /users/42` source url under static, bare `GET` under stream). Both lifecycles were checked. On the Node SvelteKit SDK the SvelteKit span IS the root, so this is Cloudflare-specific and means transaction grouping in the product is by URL, not by route. Smaller notes: - `@sentry/sveltekit@10.67.0` cannot be installed from $REPRO/_toolbox/pack alone: its `@sentry/bundler-plugins@10.67.0` dependency is neither in $REPRO/_toolbox/pack nor published (npm latest 10.73.0). It has to be packed from the worktree. Worth adding to $REPRO/_toolbox/pack for other framework cells. - The Worker reaches the host sink at `127.0.0.1:41317` fine; `tunnel` in `initCloudflareSentryHandle` works. - mysql connections must be created INSIDE the handler on workerd (module-scope I/O is forbidden), the inverse of the Bun K11 rule, and spans still attach correctly. - npm 11 skipped the workerd/esbuild postinstall scripts (`npm warn allow-scripts`); the prebuilt binaries were present anyway and wrangler dev started fine, so no approval was needed. - Processes killed (sink 49140, recorder 49142, wrangler 59970); app/node_modules removed, directory down to 6.6 MB.

Astro on Cloudflare M-astro-cf

Astro 7.3.1 with @astrojs/cloudflare 14.3.0 · Cloudflare Workers (wrangler 4.129, workerd 1.20260903.1, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, nodejs_compat) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Packages: astro@7 @astrojs/cloudflare@14 wrangler@4 plus the develop tarballs @sentry/{astro,cloudflare,core,node,browser,browser-utils,replay,replay-canvas,feedback,opentelemetry,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,bundler-plugins}@10.67.0 (npm install, all on one command line). BOTH halves of the docs wiring are required and neither works alone.

1) astro.config.mjs -- output 'server', adapter: cloudflare(), integrations: [sentry()]. This is what installs the Astro request middleware and the build-time instrumentation (server-runtime-injection). Without it you lose route names, error capture and db spans entirely (measured, see evidence).

2) sentry.server.config.ts at the project root:
   import * as Sentry from '@sentry/cloudflare';
   import handler from '@astrojs/cloudflare/entrypoints/server';
   export default Sentry.withSentry((env) => ({ dsn: env.SENTRY_DSN, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }), handler);

3) wrangler.jsonc at the project root -- "main": "./sentry.server.config.ts", "compatibility_date": "2026-05-01", "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"]. The adapter reads this file at build time and emits dist/server/wrangler.json whose entry.mjs default-exports the withSentry-wrapped handler (`var worker_entry_default = sentry_server_config_default ?? {}`). The user-facing wrangler.jsonc must NOT set "main" to a dist path that does not exist yet: @astrojs/cloudflare v14 runs @cloudflare/vite-plugin during `astro build` and hard-fails with "The provided Wrangler config main field ... doesn't point to an existing file".

4) Run: `npx astro build` then `npx wrangler dev --config dist/server/wrangler.json --port <port> --inspector-port 0`.

No @cloudflare/vite-plugin / sentryCloudflareVitePlugin of your own is needed; the Astro integration's own Vite plugin does the build-time channel injection (globalThis.__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__.bundler is present in the emitted entry.mjs).
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksA `throw new Error('astro-cf route boom')` in src/pages/api/error.ts is captured with mechanism `auto.middleware.astro`, handled:false, transaction "GET /api/error", and the route still returns HTTP 500. The capture comes from the @sentry/astro middleware, not from withSentry: with `integrations: [sentry()]` removed from astro.config.mjs the same throw returns 500 but produces NO event at all, so Astro swallows it and only the integration's middleware sees it. Stack frames carry no context_line.
route names✓ worksParameterized route /api/users/[id] hit as /api/users/42 gives name "GET /api/users/[id]" with sentry.segment.name.source = "route" (stream) and transaction_info.source = "route" (static), plus http.route = "/api/users/[id]" and origin auto.http.astro. Depends on the Astro integration: without `integrations: [sentry()]` the name degrades to a bare "GET" with no http.route.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent GET /api/iso?tag=alpha|beta|gamma, each doing Sentry.setTag('probe_tag', tag), a 150ms await, then captureException: each event carried only its own tag and its own distinct trace_id. No cross-talk. (stream lifecycle)
incoming trace✓ worksA request with `sentry-trace: aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff00001111-1122334455667788-1` and a matching baggage header produced a server span with trace_id aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff00001111 and parent_span_id 1122334455667788. (stream lifecycle)
outgoing fetch✓ works`fetch('http://127.0.0.1:37412/rec')` inside an API route produced an http.client span ("http.client GET 127.0.0.1" in stream, "http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:37412/rec" in static) as a child of the server span, and the recorder saw both sentry-trace (same trace id, sampled) and a full baggage header including sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fapi%2Ffetchout.
db spans✓ worksA module-scope `mysql.createConnection({host:'127.0.0.1',port:3307,user:'root',database:'app'})` queried from the handler produced a db span with db.system=mysql: "db SELECT users" (stream) / "db SELECT id, name FROM users" (static). Instrumentation path: the @sentry/astro integration's own build-time injection via @sentry/server-runtime-injection -- NO separate Cloudflare Vite plugin was added. It IS needed: with `integrations: [sentry()]` removed the db span disappears while the query still succeeds.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info('hello from astro on cloudflare', { route: '/api/log' })` imported from @sentry/cloudflare inside the route arrived as a log envelope: `info: hello from astro on cloudflare`. Worked in both lifecycles.
client errors· not-runOnly the server runtime was probed. No browser was driven and no sentry.client.config.js was added, so the @sentry/astro client half is unverified here.

Docs today

There IS a dedicated page: ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/astro.mdx:1-148 ("Astro on Cloudflare"), and ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/index.mdx:24-25 points Cloudflare users to it. The substance lives in ~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.astro.mdx:57-179, gated on `<PlatformSection supported={["javascript.cloudflare"]}>`. It prescribes exactly the shape I verified: install @sentry/astro + @sentry/cloudflare (:65-79), set "main": "./sentry.server.config.ts" in wrangler.jsonc (:104-113), export `Sentry.withSentry((env) => ({...}), handler)` around `import handler from "@astrojs/cloudflare/entrypoints/server"` (:122-145), and register `integrations: [sentry()]` in astro.config.mjs (:160-178). That wiring is correct on develop and it is the only one that works. Three places where the page is stale, wrong, or silent against develop: - astro.mdx:12-13 states prerequisites as "Astro 6.0.0 or above" and "@astrojs/cloudflare v13 or above". npm latest is astro 7.3.1 / @astrojs/cloudflare 14.3.0 and the documented setup works unchanged on those, but the floor wording reads stale. - astro.mdx:21-35 (the "Using Astro 3-5 with @astrojs/cloudflare v12?" expandable) claims "the @sentry/astro integration automatically detects the Cloudflare adapter and wraps your Worker with the @sentry/cloudflare SDK" and tells the reader to skip the custom entry point. On develop with astro 7 / adapter 14 that auto-wrap does not happen at all: with `integrations: [sentry()]` present and only SENTRY_DSN/SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE as wrangler vars, zero envelopes are emitted (control B). The page does scope the claim to Astro 3-5 / adapter v12, which I did not test, but nothing warns that the fallback produces no telemetry rather than an error. - Nothing anywhere says that `integrations: [sentry()]` is what supplies error capture, parameterized route names and library (db) spans on Cloudflare. It is presented as step 3 of 3 ("Register the Sentry Integration") after the entry point, which reads as optional polish; dropping it leaves a Worker that reports method-only "GET" spans, no db spans, and silently swallows thrown route errors.

Documented: yes

No gap surfaced by this run. Both halves of the documented wiring (the `withSentry`-wrapped custom entry at include :127-148 and the `sentry()` integration at include :165-174) were required and neither worked alone, exactly as the page prescribes, and all seven capabilities passed against it. The only refinement the run supports is a version-range confirmation: astro.mdx:13 says `@astrojs/cloudflare` v13 or above, and the run additionally confirms Astro 7.3.1 with adapter 14.3.0 on compatibility_date 2026-05-01. Database spans also worked with no configuration beyond the documented setup, which the page could state explicitly rather than leaving unmentioned.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/astro.mdx — no structural change needed; optionally widen the tested-version statement at :13 and add one line confirming database spans need no extra setup

docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/astro.mdx:1-148 ("Astro on Cloudflare"), :13 requires `@astrojs/cloudflare` v13 or above, :21-23 the Expandable for the older Astro 3-5 / adapter v12 auto-detection path. The substance is platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.astro.mdx:57-180, gated on `<PlatformSection supported={["javascript.cloudflare"]}>`: :59-84 install both `@sentry/astro` and `@sentry/cloudflare`; :89-96 wrangler config via getting-started-config/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:5-21; :98-152 the custom entry point — `"main": "./sentry.server.config.ts"` in wrangler.jsonc (:109-114) plus `Sentry.withSentry((env) => ({...}), handler)` around `@astrojs/cloudflare/entrypoints/server` (:127-148); :154-174 registering `sentry()` alongside `cloudflare()` in `astro.config.mjs`. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/index.mdx:24-25 routes Cloudflare users here; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16 links it from the framework list.

Findings worth carrying forward: 1. Astro on Cloudflare is fully viable on develop and the documented setup is complete and correct. All seven server capabilities pass. 2. The two halves of the setup are BOTH load-bearing and cover different things. `withSentry` in sentry.server.config.ts gives the client, isolation scope, transport, logs and fetch instrumentation. `integrations: [sentry()]` in astro.config.mjs gives error capture (mechanism auto.middleware.astro), parameterized route names / http.route, and build-time channel injection for library spans. Neither substitutes for the other, and dropping the second fails silently and partially (200s and 500s still served, spans still emitted, just degraded and errorless). 3. mysql db spans work on Cloudflare Workers with no Cloudflare-specific Vite plugin at all. The @sentry/astro integration's own Vite plugin already runs @sentry/server-runtime-injection over the server build; `globalThis.__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__.bundler` is present in the emitted dist/server/entry.mjs. A module-scope connection was used, per the Bun K11 guidance, and worked. 4. Build-order trap worth documenting: @astrojs/cloudflare v14 runs @cloudflare/vite-plugin during `astro build`, and that plugin resolves wrangler.jsonc's `main` at config time. Pointing `main` at a dist path (e.g. ./dist/_worker.js/index.js, the shape older Astro-on-Cloudflare guides use) makes `astro build` fail before it can produce that file: "The provided Wrangler config main field (.../dist/_worker.js/index.js) doesn't point to an existing file". The docs' ./sentry.server.config.ts value sidesteps this because the file exists in the source tree, but nothing explains why. 5. `sourceMapsUploadOptions` is now rejected: "[WARN] [@sentry/astro] [Sentry] Removed in v11 and ignored: sourceMapsUploadOptions. Set bundler plugin options directly on the Sentry build options." The Astro guide still documents sourceMapsUploadOptions. 6. Stack frames on captured errors carry no context_line (hasContextLine:false) under wrangler dev even though the build emits sourcemaps. Outside the brief, flagging for whoever looks at Cloudflare source context. 7. Environment friction, for the record: ports 41337, 41998 and 41999 were already held by sibling agents; I moved to 37411 (sink), 37412 (recorder), 37413 (wrangler). npm printed allow-scripts warnings for workerd/esbuild postinstall but the optional platform package workerd-darwin-arm64 was present and wrangler ran fine. 8. Client-side (@sentry/astro browser half, session replay, client route names) was not probed; server runtime only. 9. Cleanup done: wrangler, sink and recorder processes killed by captured pid; app/node_modules removed (probe dir now 4.4M). Rerunning needs the npm install line in `commands` first.

Setup the docs would have to show

    $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-react-router-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-cloudflare-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz \
    $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-browser-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-react-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-browser-utils-10.67.0.tgz \
    $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-replay-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-replay-canvas-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-feedback-10.67.0.tgz \
    $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz \
