react-router.config.ts (REQUIRED, and the only non-obvious bit):
  import type { Config } from '@react-router/dev/config';
  export default { ssr: true, future: { v8_viteEnvironmentApi: true } } satisfies Config;

vite.config.ts:
  import { reactRouter } from '@react-router/dev/vite';
  import { cloudflare } from '@cloudflare/vite-plugin';
  import { sentryCloudflareVitePlugin } from '@sentry/cloudflare/vite';
  import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
  export default defineConfig({
    plugins: [cloudflare({ viteEnvironment: { name: 'ssr' } }), reactRouter(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()],
  });

wrangler.jsonc:
  { "name": "rr-cf-probe", "main": "./workers/app.ts", "compatibility_date": "2026-05-01",
    "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"], "assets": { "directory": "./build/client" } }

workers/app.ts (Sentry init lives here; withSentry sees the entry is already wrapped, so the Vite plugin's autoInstrumentation leaves it alone):
  import * as Sentry from '@sentry/cloudflare';
  import { createRequestHandler } from 'react-router';
  const requestHandler = createRequestHandler(() => import('virtual:react-router/server-build'), import.meta.env.MODE);
  export default Sentry.withSentry(
    () => ({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }),
    { async fetch(request, env, ctx) { return requestHandler(request, { cloudflare: { env, ctx } }); } } satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>,
  );

app/entry.server.tsx (route names + trace meta tags + error capture):
  import * as Sentry from '@sentry/cloudflare';
  import { injectTraceMetaTags, wrapSentryHandleRequest } from '@sentry/react-router/cloudflare';
  ... return new Response(injectTraceMetaTags(body), { headers: responseHeaders, status });
  export const handleError: HandleErrorFunction = (error, { request }) => {
    if (!request.signal.aborted) Sentry.captureException(error);
  };
  export default wrapSentryHandleRequest(handleRequest);

  Note: `createSentryHandleError` is exported only from the node entry (packages/react-router/src/server/index.ts:9); `@sentry/react-router/cloudflare` (packages/react-router/src/cloudflare/index.ts) exports only `../client`, `wrapSentryHandleRequest` and `injectTraceMetaTags`. On Workers the `handleError` export must be hand-rolled with `Sentry.captureException`, exactly as the Hydrogen page shows.

Run: `npx vite build` then `npx wrangler dev --config build/server/wrangler.json --port <port> --inspector-port 0`.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksWith a hand-rolled `export const handleError` calling Sentry.captureException in app/entry.server.tsx, a `throw new Error()` in a loader arrives as an event with mechanism "generic", handled true, sdk sentry.javascript.cloudflare, request url set, on the same trace id as the http.server transaction. Without that export React Router swallows it into the ErrorBoundary: the run before I added handleError produced only `{"type":"transaction","name":"GET /boom","status":"internal_error"}` and no event at all. Both lifecycles behaved the same. `createSentryHandleError` is not reachable from @sentry/react-router/cloudflare, so the wiring has to be manual.
route names✓ workstraceLifecycle static: `{"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route"}` — parameterized and source=route, set by wrapSentryHandleRequest from routerContext.staticHandlerContext.matches. traceLifecycle stream: `http.server | GET /users/:id` in the span envelope (my sink reads the legacy `sentry.source` attribute so it printed src=-; the name itself is parameterized). Without wrapSentryHandleRequest the name would fall back to the method-only Cloudflare request span.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent GETs to /iso/alpha|bravo|charlie, each doing Sentry.setTag then a 120ms await then captureException, produced three events with tags {"iso_tag":"alpha"} / bravo / charlie and three distinct trace ids, each matching its own transaction's trace id. No tag bleed across requests. traceLifecycle static.
incoming trace✓ worksA request with `sentry-trace: aaaa...aaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` plus baggage produced `{"type":"transaction","name":"GET /users/:id","trace_id":"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa","parent_span_id":"bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb"}` — trace continued and parent span id set. traceLifecycle static.
outgoing fetch✓ worksA `fetch()` from a loader to a local recorder produced an `http.client` child span inside the transaction (static: `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:52883/rec`; stream: `http.client | GET 127.0.0.1`, the new low-cardinality name) and the recorder saw sentry-trace `df0ad40c46254aa3a0790bb7a159741e-907e94bd91709b32-1` plus a full baggage header with sentry-sampled=true.
db spans✓ worksModule-scope `mysql.createPool` (mysql@2.18.1) queried from a loader produced `db SELECT id, name FROM users` as a child span (static) / `db | SELECT users` (stream) and returned real rows. Instrumentation path: the Cloudflare Vite plugin's buildTimeInstrumentation, and it IS needed — rebuilding with `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ buildTimeInstrumentation: false })` gave the same working query but `"spans":[]`. Caveat: mysql2/promise emits the spans (`db mysql2.pool.connect`, `db mysql2.connect`, `db SELECT id, name FROM users`) but the query itself fails on workerd with `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`, so use `mysql` v2, not mysql2.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info('rr-cf log from loader', { where: 'loader' })` from a loader arrived as a log envelope: `{"type":"log","items":["info: rr-cf log from loader trace=da1340ec76df4d5eb5cd9fd6a54a3d78"]}`, trace id matching the request's transaction. No enableLogs option needed on develop. Both lifecycles.
client errors· not-runOnly the server side was probed; no browser was driven. The client half (Sentry.init in app/entry.client.tsx from @sentry/react-router/cloudflare, plus injectTraceMetaTags which I did wire and which is what feeds the browser its trace) was not exercised.

Docs today

No page documents React Router framework mode on Cloudflare Workers. ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/ holds only index.mdx and manual-setup.mdx (plus profiling/), and a case-insensitive grep for "cloudflare" across that directory returns zero hits — the guide is Node-only. ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-24 lists the frameworks with Cloudflare-specific setup (Astro, Hono, Hydrogen, Next.js, Nuxt, Remix, SvelteKit, TanStack Start); React Router is absent from that list. The only React Router + Cloudflare page is ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/hydrogen-react-router.mdx, and it is Shopify Oxygen-specific: hydrogen-react-router.mdx:192 warns "On Shopify Oxygen, never import anything directly from @sentry/cloudflare. Only use the @sentry/cloudflare/request subpath", and hydrogen-react-router.mdx:203-243 shows `wrapRequestHandler` in server.ts rather than `withSentry` in workers/app.ts. Its entry.server.tsx snippet (hydrogen-react-router.mdx:294-301, then :302 `export default Sentry.wrapSentryHandleRequest(handleRequest)`) is the only place in the docs that shows the hand-rolled `handleError` that a Workers app needs, and a plain-Workers reader has no reason to find it. Nothing anywhere mentions `future.v8_viteEnvironmentApi`, `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin` for React Router, or that `createSentryHandleError` is unavailable on the cloudflare entry.

Documented: no

A page must exist for React Router 7 framework mode (SSR) on Cloudflare Workers built with `@cloudflare/vite-plugin`, and it must state that all seven capabilities work — errors, route names, request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing fetch spans, database spans and logs — with no workarounds. It must give the package set (`@sentry/react-router` plus `@sentry/cloudflare`, which is a separate install), the `wrangler` config (`nodejs_compat`, compatibility_date `2026-05-01`), the worker entry wiring, and the Vite configuration combining `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` with the React Router dev plugin. It must also be reachable: add React Router to the framework list on the Cloudflare index and add a Cloudflare pointer to the React Router guide, which currently never mentions the runtime.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/react-router.mdx (new), linked from docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23 and from docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/index.mdx

No page covers this combination. `ls docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/` yields only index.mdx, manual-setup.mdx and profiling/, and `grep -rn -i cloudflare docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/` returns zero hits — the guide is Node-only. In the other direction, docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/ contains astro.mdx, hono.mdx, hydrogen-react-router.mdx, hydrogen-remix.mdx, nextjs.mdx, nuxt.mdx, remix.mdx, sveltekit.mdx and tanstack-start.mdx — there is no react-router.mdx, and the framework list at docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23 omits React Router entirely. The nearest page, docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/hydrogen-react-router.mdx:188-212, is Shopify Oxygen-specific and prescribes `wrapRequestHandler` from `@sentry/cloudflare/request`, which is not the wiring that worked here.

Scaffold notes worth carrying into a docs page: - `future: { v8_viteEnvironmentApi: true }` in react-router.config.ts is mandatory for React Router 7.18 + @cloudflare/vite-plugin. Without it `vite build` dies with `[commonjs--resolver] id.endsWith is not a function` on both vite 6.4.3 and 7.3.6, because the ssr environment gets the client route inputs with `{index: 'virtual:cloudflare/worker-entry'}` pushed in as an object. The message names neither plugin and is very hard to attribute; this alone would sink most users. - `@react-router/node` must be pinned to ^7 alongside react-router 7: @sentry/react-router's peer range `">=7.15.0 || ^8.x"` makes npm hoist 8.3.1 and the install aborts with ERESOLVE. Nothing in the app actually uses @react-router/node on Workers. - `createSentryHandleError` is not exported from `@sentry/react-router/cloudflare` (packages/react-router/src/cloudflare/index.ts re-exports only `../client`, `wrapSentryHandleRequest`, `injectTraceMetaTags`). Errors thrown in loaders are silently swallowed into the ErrorBoundary until you write your own `handleError`. This is the single sharpest gap: the app "works", returns 500, and reports a transaction with status internal_error, so it looks instrumented while capturing nothing. - `wrapSentryHandleRequest` calls `flushIfServerless` from `@sentry/core/server`; it bundles and runs fine in workerd. - `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` bare is safe next to a manual `Sentry.withSentry()` in workers/app.ts (autoInstrumentation detects the already-wrapped entry), and its buildTimeInstrumentation is what makes db spans appear. - Use `mysql` v2, not mysql2: mysql2 is instrumented (spans appear) but its query fails on workerd with `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`. - The Cloudflare Vite plugin's dev server (`vite dev`) was not exercised; everything here ran against `vite build` output via `wrangler dev --config build/server/wrangler.json`. - No SDK debug warnings of note; `debug: true` was on for all runs. - Both `traceLifecycle: 'static'` and `'stream'` were run end to end and agreed on every capability. The stream run also confirms the new low-cardinality names (`GET 127.0.0.1` for http.client, `SELECT users` for db). - Cleanup: all node/wrangler processes I started were killed and verified down (ports 47211, 47212, 52881, 52883 free); `node_modules` (398M) was removed, leaving 5.3M of sources and logs.

cd $D && PORT=52883 node recorder.mjs > rec2.log 2>&1 &

# build and run the worker
cd $D && npx vite build
cd $D && npx wrangler dev --config build/server/wrangler.json --port 52881 --inspector-port 0 > app.log 2>&1 &
# readiness: grep "Ready on" app.log

# drive
curl -s -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:47212/__items
curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:52881/boom
curl -s -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:52881/fetchout?target=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A52883%2Frec"
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:52881/db
curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:52881/logs
curl -s -o /dev/null -H "sentry-trace: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1" \
  -H "baggage: sentry-trace_id=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa,sentry-environment=probe,sentry-public_key=public" \
  http://127.0.0.1:52881/users/7
curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:52881/iso/alpha & curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:52881/iso/bravo & curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:52881/iso/charlie & wait
curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:52881/sentinel   # sentinel, wait until it lands
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:47212/__items
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:52883/__hits

# lifecycle switch: edit `traceLifecycle` in workers/app.ts ('static' | 'stream'), then rebuild + restart.

TanStack Start on Cloudflare M-tanstack-cf

TanStack Start (React) v1.136 with @tanstack/react-start file-based routing · Cloudflare Workers (workerd 2026-09-03 via wrangler 4.129.0 local dev, nodejs_compat, compatibility_date 2026-05-01) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Packages (all Sentry from $REPRO/_toolbox/pack develop tarballs, 10.67.0):
  npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{cloudflare,tanstackstart-react,browser,browser-utils,core,node,react,opentelemetry,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,bundler-plugins,replay,replay-canvas,feedback}-10.67.0.tgz
  plus @tanstack/react-start@^1.136 @tanstack/react-router@^1.136 react@19 react-dom@19 mysql@2
  dev: @cloudflare/vite-plugin@^1.35 vite@7.3.2 @vitejs/plugin-react vite-tsconfig-paths wrangler@^4.68 typescript

vite.config.ts (ORDER MATTERS - cloudflare() first, sentryTanstackStart() after tanstackStart()):
  import { cloudflare } from '@cloudflare/vite-plugin';
  import { tanstackStart } from '@tanstack/react-start/plugin/vite';
  import { sentryTanstackStart } from '@sentry/tanstackstart-react/vite';
  export default defineConfig({ plugins: [ cloudflare({ viteEnvironment: { name: 'ssr' } }), tsConfigPaths(), tanstackStart(), sentryTanstackStart({ sourcemaps: { disable: true } }), viteReact() ] });

src/server.ts (server entry, referenced as `main` in wrangler.jsonc):
  import * as Sentry from '@sentry/cloudflare';
  import { wrapFetchWithSentry } from '@sentry/tanstackstart-react';
  import handler from '@tanstack/react-start/server-entry';
  export default Sentry.withSentry(
    (env: Env) => ({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static', tunnel: 'http://127.0.0.1:33517/' }),
    wrapFetchWithSentry(handler),   // docs add `// @ts-expect-error` here
  );

src/start.ts (global middlewares, Sentry first in each array):
  import { sentryGlobalFunctionMiddleware, sentryGlobalRequestMiddleware } from '@sentry/tanstackstart-react';
  export const startInstance = createStart(() => ({ requestMiddleware: [sentryGlobalRequestMiddleware], functionMiddleware: [sentryGlobalFunctionMiddleware] }));

src/instrument.client.ts imported first in src/client.tsx does Sentry.init from @sentry/browser (client side).

wrangler.jsonc: { "name": "m-tanstack-cf", "compatibility_date": "2026-05-01", "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"], "main": "src/server.ts" }

Run: NODE_ENV=production npx vite build   ->   npx wrangler dev --config dist/server/wrangler.json --port <port> --inspector-port 0
No /nodejs_compat subpath, no @sentry/node import path, no wrapRequestHandler needed. `export * from '@sentry/node'` inside @sentry/tanstackstart-react does NOT break the workerd build because the vite/workerd export condition maps the package to index.server and the Cloudflare vite plugin tree-shakes it; only the helpers actually imported are pulled in.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓ worksAn Error thrown from a `createFileRoute('/users/$id').server.handlers.GET` handler reaches Sentry as an unhandled exception with mechanism `auto.middleware.tanstackstart.request` (the `sentryGlobalRequestMiddleware` catch/rethrow), `handled: false`, and `transaction: "GET /users/$id"`. The framework does not swallow it: the request still returns HTTP 500 and the accompanying transaction has `status: internal_error`. Same result in both static and stream lifecycle. Stack frames have no `context_line` because I disabled sourcemaps in the build.
route names✓ worksstatic lifecycle: `transaction: "GET /users/$id"`, `source: "route"`, `http.route: "/users/$id"`. stream lifecycle: span `http.server GET /users/$id` with `sentry.segment.name.source = route`. This depends entirely on `sentryTanstackStart()` being in vite.config.ts - its `makeRoutePatternPlugin` defines `__SENTRY_ROUTE_PATTERNS__`, which `wrapFetchWithSentry` reads. With the plugin removed (i.e. the exact config the docs page shows) the same request produced `"GET /users/123"` with `source: "url"` and no `http.route`.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent GETs to /iso/alpha, /iso/bravo, /iso/charlie, each calling Sentry.setTag('probe_tag', <tag>), sleeping 120ms, then captureException. Each of the three events carried exactly its own tag and nothing else, and each event's trace_id matched its own transaction's trace_id (alpha=0d48d885…, bravo=bfadcc15…, charlie=3ca5fa81…). No cross-talk. static lifecycle.
incoming trace✓ worksGET /users/77 with `sentry-trace: aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff00001111-1122334455667788-1` and a matching baggage header produced a transaction with `trace_id: aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff00001111` and `parent_span_id: 1122334455667788`, still named `GET /users/$id` with `source: route`. static lifecycle.
outgoing fetch✓ worksA `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:33518/rec')` from inside a route handler produced an `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:33518/rec` child span in the transaction (stream lifecycle names it `http.client GET 127.0.0.1`, the new low-cardinality name), and the recorder saw both `sentry-trace: 1618d771012e44be8077b306c7408659-b87a74f6c91b675a-1` and a full baggage header including `sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fapi%2Fprobe-fetch`. Trace id matches the server transaction.
db spans✓ worksModule-scope `mysql.createPool({host:'127.0.0.1',port:3307,...})` plus `pool.query('SELECT id, name FROM users')` inside the handler returned real rows from MariaDB and produced a `db SELECT id, name FROM users` child span (stream lifecycle: `db SELECT users`). Instrumentation path: the Cloudflare-side Vite plugin chain, specifically `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` inside `sentryTanstackStart()` - NOT `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin`, which is not used at all in a TanStack Start app. It was needed: the bundle grew from 191kB to 2.6MB (the plugin's `ssr.noExternal` force-bundles mysql) and contains the injected channels `orchestrion:mysql:query`, `orchestrion:mysql2:query`, `orchestrion:mysql2:execute`. With `sentryTanstackStart()` removed the identical request produced a transaction with `spans: []`. Note the plugin is production-only (`process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'` returns early), so `vite dev` gets no db spans.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info('tanstack cf probe log', { where: 'route-handler' })` from a route handler arrived as a `log` envelope item `info: tanstack cf probe log` carrying the same trace_id (502d6782cfa04424b727e0df8a0e4b77) as the enclosing `GET /api/probe-log` transaction. No `enableLogs` option needed on develop. Flushed within the 8s wait. static lifecycle.

It shows exactly the wiring I used: `Sentry.withSentry(() => ({...}), wrapFetchWithSentry(handler))` in src/server.ts (lines 65-105, including the `// @ts-expect-error` note at line 71), the wrangler.jsonc `main` change (line ~121), the client `instrument.client`/router setup (lines 143-172), and `sentryGlobalRequestMiddleware` + `sentryGlobalFunctionMiddleware` in src/start.ts (lines 200-230). Gap: the page never tells the user to add `sentryTanstackStart()` from `@sentry/tanstackstart-react/vite` to vite.config.ts. Line 10 is the ONLY occurrence of the string "vite" in the whole file, and it is prose ("using the `@cloudflare/vite-plugin`"); there is no vite.config.ts snippet anywhere. `grep -n "sentryTanstackStart\|vite.config" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/tanstack-start.mdx` returns nothing. Following the page literally therefore yields url-source transaction names (`GET /users/123`) and zero db/library spans, which I confirmed with the control run above. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/tanstack-start.mdx:1-290 ("TanStack Start on Cloudflare"). :10 scopes the page to Cloudflare Workers using `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` and points Node.js users elsewhere; :16-47 install; :50 states you must wrap the server entry with `Sentry.withSentry` from `@sentry/cloudflare`; :59-102 the custom server entry, including `wrapFetchWithSentry` from `@sentry/tanstackstart-react` (:67, :80) inside `Sentry.withSentry(...)` (:83-101); :108-125 the `"main": "src/server.ts"` wrangler change; :131 client-side configuration; :197 server-side error capture; :234 source maps; :241 verification. Linked from docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:23.

- TanStack Start on Workers is fully viable and every probed capability passed. This is the strongest Cloudflare framework result I would expect: parametrized route names, working isolation across concurrent requests, trace continuation, client-span headers, db spans and logs all work with one build config. - Every result above came from `traceLifecycle: 'static'` except the block explicitly labelled stream; I re-ran errors, route names, outgoing fetch and db spans under `'stream'` too and all four held (stream additionally gave the new low-cardinality names `db SELECT users` and `http.client GET 127.0.0.1`). - The single load-bearing thing the docs omit is `sentryTanstackStart()` in vite.config.ts. It is what defines `__SENTRY_ROUTE_PATTERNS__` (read by `wrapFetchWithSentry` -> `updateSpanWithRouteParametrization`) and what runs `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` for db/library instrumentation. Note also that `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` is skipped when `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'`, so `vite dev` never produces db spans on this stack - only `vite build` + `wrangler dev` does. - `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` from `@sentry/cloudflare/vite` is NOT part of this setup and should not be added; the TanStack Start plugin chain plus explicit `withSentry` in src/server.ts covers it. - `@sentry/tanstackstart-react`'s server entry does `export * from '@sentry/node'`, which sounds fatal on workerd but is not: the package's `workerd`/`worker` export conditions map to index.server, and the Cloudflare Vite plugin tree-shakes away everything except the helpers actually imported (`wrapFetchWithSentry`, the two middlewares). Worth knowing because it looks like a blocker on inspection. - Not probed: server functions (`createServerFn`) - the app has the routes from the e2e scaffold but I focused the seven listed capabilities on route handlers. The `sentryGlobalFunctionMiddleware` renames those spans to `GET /_serverFn/<name>` per src/server/globalMiddleware.ts. - Environment friction, not SDK: ports 41337/41338 and 52731 were already held by other agents' processes on this machine; I moved to 33517/33518/33519. Also, backgrounding a server with `&` inside a plain Bash call makes the call hang until the 2-minute timeout and then kills the child - servers must be started with `run_in_background`. - Cleanup done: all three background processes stopped, ports 33517/33518/33519 verified free, `node_modules` (375M) removed. The MariaDB container was pre-existing and left untouched.

Remix on Cloudflare M-remix-cf

Remix v2 (2.17.5, Remix Vite plugin, resource routes) · Cloudflare Workers (wrangler 4.129.0 dev / workerd, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, nodejs_compat) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

Remix v2 runs on Workers without Hydrogen/Oxygen. Working wiring (all 7 probes green):

1) Packages (npm needs --legacy-peer-deps: @remix-run/cloudflare pins @cloudflare/workers-types ^4, wrangler 4 pins ^5):
npm install --legacy-peer-deps @remix-run/cloudflare@^2.17.5 @remix-run/react@^2.17.5 @remix-run/dev@^2.17.5 react@^18.3.1 react-dom@^18.3.1 isbot@^4 vite@^6.4.3 wrangler@^4 mysql@^2.18.1 $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{remix,cloudflare,core,node,react,browser,browser-utils,replay,replay-canvas,feedback,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry,bundler-plugins}-10.67.0.tgz

2) vite.config.ts
import { vitePlugin as remix } from '@remix-run/dev';
import { sentryCloudflareVitePlugin } from '@sentry/cloudflare/vite';
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [remix({ future: { v3_fetcherPersist: true, v3_relativeSplatPath: true, v3_throwAbortReason: true, v3_singleFetch: false, v3_lazyRouteDiscovery: true } }),
            ...sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ autoInstrumentation: false })],   // only needed for db spans
  ssr: { target: 'webworker', resolve: { externalConditions: ['workerd', 'worker'] }, noExternal: true },
});

3) app/entry.server.tsx (MANDATORY for error capture)
import { sentryHandleError } from '@sentry/remix/cloudflare';
export const handleError = sentryHandleError;
export default async function handleRequest(...) { /* renderToReadableStream from react-dom/server */ }

4) server.ts (worker entry)
import { createRequestHandler } from '@remix-run/cloudflare';
import * as SentryCF from '@sentry/cloudflare';
import { wrapRequestHandler } from '@sentry/cloudflare/request';
import { instrumentBuild } from '@sentry/remix/cloudflare';
import * as remixBuild from './build/server/index.js';

SentryCF.setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy();   // MANDATORY, see isolation finding

const handleRequest = createRequestHandler(instrumentBuild(remixBuild), 'production');

export default {
  async fetch(request, env, ctx) {
    return wrapRequestHandler(
      { options: { dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static', tunnel: 'http://127.0.0.1:41731/' }, request, context: ctx },
      async () => (await handleRequest(request, { env, ctx })),
    );
  },
};

5) wrangler.jsonc: { "main": "./server.ts", "compatibility_date": "2026-05-01", "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"], "assets": { "directory": "./build/client" } }

6) Run: npx remix vite:build   (plain `vite build` builds ONLY the client under Vite 6, it silently skips build/server — must use `remix vite:build`) then npx wrangler dev --port <port> --inspector-port 0.

Do NOT use makeWrappedCreateRequestHandler on Cloudflare (see notes: it double-reports every request in two different traces).

errors◐ partialA loader throw reaches Sentry as an unhandled event with mechanism `auto.function.remix.server`, handled:false, only if `export const handleError = sentryHandleError` is present in app/entry.server.tsx. Without that line Remix swallows the error entirely: I got the 500 response and the transaction with status internal_error but zero event envelopes (`errorHandleDataFunction` in packages/remix/src/server/errors.ts:105-111 only captures thrown Responses; everything else is left to handleError). traceLifecycle: static. verified: partial Reproduced independently in $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-remix-cf-errors (Remix 2.17.5 + Remix Vite plugin, wrangler 4.129.0 dev, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, nodejs_compat, develop SDK 10.67.0, sink 38411 / worker 38412). Could not refute the claim; it is correct and the real situation is worse than reported. 1) CONFIRMED, and worse: the DOCUMENTED snippet captures nothing. ~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.remix.mdx:321-342 tells you to write `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/remix'; export const handleError = Sentry.sentryHandleError;`. On a workerd SSR build that specifier resolves to the BROWSER build, because the "." exports map in packages/remix/package.json lists `browser` BEFORE `worker`, and Vite's webworker SSR environment has both conditions active. `npx remix vite:build` only warns: app/entry.server.tsx (7:34): "sentryHandleError" is not exported by "node_modules/@sentry/remix/build/esm/index.client.js", imported by "app/entry.server.tsx". The build succeeds, `handleError` is `undefined` at runtime, and only the thrown Response is captured (build-docs.log, /__items): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /boom/:id","status":"internal_error","spans":["function routes/boom.$id","function GET /boom/:id"]} <- no event {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/boom","status":"internal_error"} <- no event {"type":"transaction","name":"POST /act","status":"internal_error"} <- no event {"type":"event","exception":"Error: remix-cf thrown response 1","mechanism":"auto.function.remix.server","handled":false} <- only this one Verified at the module level too: require('@sentry/remix/build/cjs/index.client.js').sentryHandleError === undefined. 2) With no handleError export at all (build-A.log): boom=500, api/boom=500, zero error events, sentinel-a arrived. Matches the reporter's baseline exactly. 3) Working shape (build-B.log), the one change that fixes it: `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/remix/cloudflare'` (the /cloudflare subpath has no `browser` key, so it resolves correctly). All four error shapes captured, each correlated with its transaction: {"type":"event","exception":"Error: remix-cf loader error 2","mechanism":"auto.function.remix.server","handled":false,"trace_id":"2ddafe80..."} + {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /boom/:id","status":"internal_error","trace_id":"2ddafe80..."} {"type":"event","exception":"Error: remix-cf resource route error",...,"trace_id":"4bf278e0..."} + {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/boom","trace_id":"4bf278e0..."} {"type":"event","exception":"Error: remix-cf action error",...,"trace_id":"7d3a114b..."} + {"type":"transaction","name":"POST /act","trace_id":"7d3a114b..."} 4) Other trace lifecycle (build-S.log): removing traceLifecycle (stream default) changes nothing for errors: {"type":"event","exception":"Error: remix-cf loader error 6","mechanism":"auto.function.remix.server","handled":false} {"type":"span","items":["function routes/boom.$id","function GET /boom/:id","http.server GET /boom/:id"]} 5) Root cause of the "handleError is mandatory" half: packages/remix/src/server/instrumentServer.ts:442-500 `instrumentBuildCallback` already clones `build.entry.module` and wraps `default` (documentRequest) plus every route loader/action, but it never touches `entry.module.handleError`; `grep -n handleError packages/remix/src/` shows only the JSDoc and the two helper definitions. So nothing in the SDK auto-installs it. I proved a 6-line fix works: patching the built `instrumentBuildCallback` with if (!wrappedEntry.module.handleError) { wrappedEntry.module.handleError = sentryHandleError; } else if (!wrappedEntry.module.handleError.__sentry_original__) { fill(wrappedEntry.module, "handleError", wrapHandleErrorWithSentry); } made ALL four error shapes capture with NO user-side handleError export, and did not duplicate the thrown Response (sentryHandleError skips Responses): {"type":"event","exception":"Error: remix-cf loader error 4",...} / "Error: remix-cf resource route error" / "Error: remix-cf action error" / "Error: remix-cf thrown response 4" (one event each). Patch reverted afterwards. 6) Additional gap: `wrapHandleErrorWithSentry` is not exported from `@sentry/remix/cloudflare` at all (packages/remix/src/cloudflare/index.ts re-exports only `sentryHandleError` and `makeWrappedCreateRequestHandler`); `require('@sentry/remix/build/cjs/cloudflare/index.js').wrapHandleErrorWithSentry === undefined`. The docs' preferred variant (wrap your own handler) therefore has no Cloudflare equivalent. 7) The repo's own reference app corroborates the hole: dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/remix-hydrogen (the only Workers-runtime Remix app, wrapRequestHandler + instrumentBuild) has NO handleError export anywhere and no server-error test (tests/ has only client-errors, client-transactions, server-timing-header, server-transactions). Every Node Remix e2e app (create-remix-app-v2, create-remix-app-express, remix-server-timing) does export handleError. Files: server.ts, vite.config.ts, wrangler.jsonc, app/entry.server.tsx, app/routes/{boom.$id,boomresp.$id,api.boom,act,sentinel}.tsx, NOTES-verify4.txt (rerun recipe + variant->log map), build-{docs,A,B,C,S}.log, wr-{docs,patch,C,S}.log. node_modules removed after the run; reinstall with `npm install --legacy-peer-deps` (package-lock.json is committed in the dir).
Workaround: Two changes on top of the reported wiring. (a) Import from the Cloudflare subpath, not the bare package, in app/entry.server.tsx: `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/remix/cloudflare'; export const handleError = Sentry.sentryHandleError;`. (b) If you must keep the docs-verbatim `@sentry/remix` specifier, force the worker condition ahead of browser in vite.config.ts: `ssr: { target: 'webworker', resolve: { conditions: ['workerd', 'worker', 'module', 'import', 'default'], externalConditions: ['workerd', 'worker'] }, noExternal: true }` — verified in build-C.log, the rollup "not exported" warning disappears and loader/action errors are captured. A third, entry.server-free option that also works: in server.ts do `const build = instrumentBuild(remixBuild); build.entry.module.handleError = sentryHandleError;` before `createRequestHandler(build, 'production')`. Do not use `wrapHandleErrorWithSentry` on Cloudflare, it is not exported from `@sentry/remix/cloudflare`; hand-roll `export const handleError = (err, args) => { myHandler(err, args); Sentry.sentryHandleError(err, args); }` instead.

Same under traceLifecycle 'stream': span `http.server GET /users/:id` with sentry.segment.name.source=route. The naming comes from the wrapped loader (updateSpanWithRoute renames the enclosing @sentry/cloudflare root span), so a route with no loader/action would stay method-only.
isolation✓* works-waThree concurrent requests each setting a distinct tag: all three events carried `probe_tag: bravo`, and so did a later unrelated /sentinel request. Trace ids were distinct, tags and request data were not. Cause is in the SDK, not Remix: `wrapRequestHandler` from @sentry/cloudflare/request is the only entry point that never calls setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy() (grep of packages/cloudflare/src: withSentry.ts:40, pages-plugin.ts:78, durableobject.ts:54, workflows.ts:247, instrumentWorkerEntrypoint.ts:153 all do), so withInvocationIsolationScope falls back to the stack strategy, which its own comment says degrades the fork to a no-op. Adding `SentryCF.setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy()` at module scope fixes it completely (each event then carries only its own tag, own URL and own trace id). Note the fix requires importing the @sentry/cloudflare main entry, which the Hydrogen docs page explicitly forbids on Oxygen. traceLifecycle: static. verified: works-after-all Reproduced the reported break, then made isolation work with a documented entry shape. Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-remix-cf-isolation (RERUN.txt has the commands). Remix 2.17.5 + Remix Vite plugin, wrangler 4.129.0 dev / workerd, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, nodejs_compat, develop SDK 10.67.0 tarballs. Probe: GET /tag/alpha|bravo|charlie fired concurrently, each loader does setTag('probe_tag', t), sleeps 400ms, then captureMessage; then GET /sentinel as an unrelated later request. (B) BROKEN, as reported — server-B-baseline.ts = wrapRequestHandler from @sentry/cloudflare/request, traceLifecycle static, no ALS strategy: {"type":"event","message":"probe-msg-alpha","tags":{"probe_tag":"bravo"},"trace":"0127aa8054f3439385f235584953a4f5"} {"type":"event","message":"probe-msg-charlie","tags":{"probe_tag":"bravo"},"trace":"699d433f5d344165a7049b88d9703660"} {"type":"event","message":"probe-msg-bravo","tags":{"probe_tag":"bravo"},"trace":"18c4734abda74080b27f2ca6998e885c"} {"type":"event","message":"sentinel","tags":{"probe_tag":"bravo"},"trace":"3195c696b56c48f2b36485f11f761f7b"} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /tag/:t","tags":{"probe_tag":"bravo"},...} (all three) Extra detail the earlier report did not name: in this shape NO event carries request data at all — every event and transaction has `request.url` absent, even though wrapRequestHandlerWithInit calls addRequest(isolationScope, request). Events also land in a trace that is not their own request's transaction trace (probe-msg-alpha in 0127aa..., which is the /tag/charlie transaction's trace). (C) WORKS — server-C-withsentry.ts = Sentry.withSentry() from the @sentry/cloudflare MAIN entry wrapping the Remix fetch handler, everything else identical (instrumentBuild + sentryHandleError kept), traceLifecycle static: {"type":"event","message":"probe-msg-alpha","tags":{"probe_tag":"alpha"},"url":"http://127.0.0.1:47217/tag/alpha","trace":"3197c866dce547c8b8ac38a7efbc4451"} {"type":"event","message":"probe-msg-bravo","tags":{"probe_tag":"bravo"},"url":"http://127.0.0.1:47217/tag/bravo","trace":"b4ab25eb24cc49bd8221a9aafdc482f0"} {"type":"event","message":"probe-msg-charlie","tags":{"probe_tag":"charlie"},"url":"http://127.0.0.1:47217/tag/charlie","trace":"02bff4e2fa11456a8a11f7c50b2aacc1"} {"type":"event","message":"sentinel","url":"http://127.0.0.1:47217/sentinel","trace":"aeb8fadb82c241dda0e6f5beb4e956e3"} <- no probe_tag at all Each transaction pairs with its own event's trace and URL. Request data is present again. (E) WORKS on the other trace lifecycle too — same withSentry entry with the develop default (stream), server-E-stream.ts: {"type":"event","message":"probe-msg-alpha","tags":{"probe_tag":"alpha"},"url":".../tag/alpha","trace":"251b12f4154548b799d383513a59a3c7"} {"type":"span","items":[{"name":"routes/tag.$t","trace":"251b12f4154548b799d383513a59a3c7"},{"name":"GET /tag/:t","trace":"251b12f4154548b799d383513a59a3c7","attrs":{"url.full":".../tag/alpha"}}]} ...charlie/bravo likewise on their own trace ids; sentinel event carries no tag. (D) WORKS — the reported fix, wrapRequestHandler + SentryCF.setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy() at module scope: each event carries only its own tag, own URL, own trace id. No regression from switching to withSentry: GET /boom/7 still yields {"type":"event","exception":"remix-cf loader error 7","url":".../boom/7","trace":"843aadefd24249eba377b9f8421b451b"} plus {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /boom/:id","source":"route","status":"internal_error","spans":["function routes/boom.$id"]} on the same trace (entry.server.tsx keeps `export const handleError = sentryHandleError`). Root cause confirmed in source, and it is narrower than "the SDK is broken": packages/cloudflare/src/request.ts routes through wrapRequestHandlerWithInit -> withInvocationIsolationScope (packages/cloudflare/src/utils/invocationScope.ts), and that file's own JSDoc says the stack fallback "does not fork ... there the fork degrades to a no-op". The /request entry deliberately omits setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy because it is the entry for runtimes that CANNOT enable nodejs_compat (its JSDoc names Shopify Oxygen), and the strategy needs node:async_hooks. So on plain Workers with nodejs_compat the fix is to use the documented Workers entry (withSentry), not /request. The repo's own e2e app dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/remix-hydrogen/server.ts uses the wrapRequestHandler shape without the strategy call, so a Hydrogen/Oxygen app is still exposed; @sentry/remix/cloudflare does not re-export setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy (build/esm/cloudflare/index.js), so an Oxygen user must import the @sentry/cloudflare main entry to get it.
Workaround: On Cloudflare Workers (nodejs_compat available), do not use wrapRequestHandler from @sentry/cloudflare/request for a Remix worker entry. Use the main entry instead: import { createRequestHandler } from '@remix-run/cloudflare'; import * as Sentry from '@sentry/cloudflare'; import { instrumentBuild } from '@sentry/remix/cloudflare'; import * as remixBuild from './build/server/index.js'; const handleRequest = createRequestHandler(instrumentBuild(remixBuild), 'production'); export default Sentry.withSentry( () => ({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }), { async fetch(request, env, ctx) { return handleRequest(request, { env, ctx }); } }, ); Keep `export const handleError = sentryHandleError` in app/entry.server.tsx. Works on both traceLifecycle 'static' and the default 'stream'. If you must keep wrapRequestHandler (Hydrogen on Oxygen, or any shape already built on @sentry/cloudflare/request) and the runtime does have AsyncLocalStorage, add at module scope of the worker entry: import * as SentryCF from '@sentry/cloudflare'; SentryCF.setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy(); That also fixes it, at the cost of importing the main entry.

db spans✓* works-wamysql@2 with a module-scope createConnection works and yields `db SELECT id, name FROM users` as a child span, but ONLY after adding `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ autoInstrumentation: false })` to the Remix Vite config together with `ssr.noExternal: true` so the driver lands in the Vite SSR bundle where the plugin can inject the diagnostics channels; the same route with the plugin absent produced the query result and no db span. The instrumentation path is the Cloudflare Vite plugin, and it was needed. mysql2 is unusable on workerd for reasons unrelated to Sentry: its parser compiler throws `Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`. verified: works-after-all Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-remix-cf-dbspans (server.ts, vite.config.ts switched by PLUGIN=none|bare|noauto and NOEXT=all|mysql|min, app/db.server.ts with both a module-scope and a per-request mysql connection, app/routes/db-module.tsx, app/routes/db-request.tsx, app/routes/sentinel.tsx). Sink on 38217, wrangler dev on 38219. Build: `PLUGIN=<x> NOEXT=<y> npx remix vite:build`, then `npx wrangler dev --port 38219 --inspector-port 0`. db spans DO work, and two of the three extra requirements in the report are wrong. 1) `autoInstrumentation: false` is NOT needed. A bare `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` (autoInstrumentation defaults to true on develop) builds fine on top of the Remix Vite plugin and produces db spans. It also does not double-report: exactly one transaction per request, even though server.ts already calls wrapRequestHandler. V1 = PLUGIN=bare NOEXT=all, sink (traceLifecycle 'static'): {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db-module","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["function routes/db-module","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db-request","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["function routes/db-request","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]} Note both scopes work: the per-request `createConnection` is instrumented too, so the module-scope requirement the report implies (and Bun's K11) does not apply on workerd. 2) `ssr.noExternal: true` is NOT needed. The minimal set is enough. V4 = PLUGIN=bare, `ssr.noExternal: ['mysql', /^@sentry\//, '@opentelemetry/api']`: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db-module","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["function routes/db-module","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db-request","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","spans":["function routes/db-request","db SELECT id, name FROM users"]} `mysql` must be in the list because the plugin injects into the bundled driver; `@sentry/*` + `@opentelemetry/api` must be in it for the reason in point 4. 3) Both trace lifecycles work. V5 = same build, traceLifecycle 'stream' (the develop default): {"type":"span","items":["db SELECT users","function routes/db-module","http.server GET /db-module"]} {"type":"span","items":["db SELECT users","function routes/db-request","http.server GET /db-request"]} Stream names the db span `SELECT users` (low cardinality), static names it `SELECT id, name FROM users`. 4) Real defect found along the way (not the db-span claim itself): with the Sentry plugin present and Vite's default SSR externalization for `@sentry/*` (NOEXT=mysql or no noExternal), `remix vite:build` succeeds but emits a bundle wrangler cannot build. build/server/index.js lines 11-17 contain `import require$$0$1 from "@sentry/conventions/attributes"; import require$$0 from "@sentry/core"; import require$$2 from "@sentry/conventions/op"; import require$$4 from "@sentry/core/server";` and wrangler dev fails: ✘ [ERROR] No matching export in "node_modules/@sentry/core/build/esm/index.js" for import "default" ✘ [ERROR] No matching export in "node_modules/@sentry/core/build/esm/server.js" for import "default" ✘ [ERROR] No matching export in "node_modules/@sentry/conventions/dist/attributes.mjs" for import "default" ✘ [ERROR] No matching export in "node_modules/@sentry/conventions/dist/op.mjs" for import "default" Control PLUGIN=none NOEXT=mysql builds a bundle with no `@sentry/*` default-import interop at all, so the CJS-interop default imports are introduced by the Sentry Cloudflare Vite plugin's injected instrumentation. The plugin therefore silently requires its own runtime deps to be bundled, and the failure surfaces only at `wrangler dev`, with an error that names esbuild and @sentry/core and says nothing about noExternal. 5) The one requirement that stands is the plugin itself, and that is the documented mechanism, not a gap. PLUGIN=none NOEXT=mysql runs fine and returns the rows but records no db span: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db-module","op":"http.server","spans":["function routes/db-module"]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /db-request","op":"http.server","spans":["function routes/db-request"]} workerd has no runtime require hook, so build-time channel injection is the only path. ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx:15 says the plugin "automatically instruments supported packages in your bundle (such as database clients like `mysql`) at build time", and :18 "We recommend building your Cloudflare Worker with Vite and the `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin` plugin. It's the most complete way to get tracing for bundled dependencies in the Workers runtime." The repo's own reference app dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/cloudflare-orchestrion-mysql uses exactly `plugins: [cloudflare(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()]` with no options and no ssr config, because there the Cloudflare Vite plugin bundles everything for workerd anyway. So the capability is not partial: db spans work with the documented plugin call, on both connection scopes and both lifecycles. What is missing is one config line that no docs page mentions, and a build-time error message that does not point at it.
Workaround: Keep the bare, documented plugin call and add the narrow noExternal list. In vite.config.ts: import { vitePlugin as remix } from '@remix-run/dev'; import { sentryCloudflareVitePlugin } from '@sentry/cloudflare/vite'; export default defineConfig({ plugins: [remix({ future: { /* ... */ } }), ...sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()], ssr: { target: 'webworker', resolve: { externalConditions: ['workerd', 'worker'] }, noExternal: ['mysql', /^@sentry\//, '@opentelemetry/api'], }, }); Every driver you want instrumented goes in `noExternal` next to 'mysql' (Remix's Vite SSR build externalizes deps by default, and the plugin can only inject into what it bundles). `/^@sentry\//` and '@opentelemetry/api' are what keep wrangler's esbuild from failing on the injected code's CJS default imports. `ssr.noExternal: true` also works and is the blunt version. No `autoInstrumentation: false` needed. If you build with @cloudflare/vite-plugin instead of the Remix Vite plugin, none of this applies: `plugins: [cloudflare(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()]` is enough.

There is a "Remix on Cloudflare" page and it is wrong for Workers. ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/remix.mdx is 60 lines: it installs only `@sentry/remix` (remix.mdx:40) and then embeds the Node/Express getting-started include via `<PlatformContent includePath="getting-started-complete" platform="javascript.remix" />` (remix.mdx:55-58). That include, ~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.remix.mdx, tells the user to create `instrument.server.mjs` (line 160), run `NODE_OPTIONS='--import=./instrument.server.mjs' remix-serve build` (line 223) and wire an Express server (line 250) - none of which exists on Workers. The page never mentions `@sentry/cloudflare`, `wrapRequestHandler`, `instrumentBuild` from `@sentry/remix/cloudflare`, `nodejs_compat`, or `setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy`. It does inherit the one thing my probe proved mandatory, `export const handleError = Sentry.sentryHandleError` (javascript.remix.mdx:321-342). The only page with a working Cloudflare wiring is ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/hydrogen-remix.mdx:19 (`npm install @sentry/remix @sentry/cloudflare`) and :41-69 (`wrapRequestHandler` from `@sentry/cloudflare/request` + `instrumentBuild` from `@sentry/remix/cloudflare`), but it is scoped to Shopify Hydrogen/Oxygen and at :36 explicitly forbids importing anything from the `@sentry/cloudflare` main entry - which is where the `setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy` fix for the isolation bug lives. ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/remix/frameworks/index.mdx:8-9 links to both.

Documented: wrong

The page contradicts the run on three points and must be rewritten for Workers. (1) Error capture: on Cloudflare Workers and Pages the `handleError` import must come from `@sentry/remix/cloudflare`, never bare `@sentry/remix` — the bare specifier silently captures nothing in a `webworker` SSR build. Both `export const handleError = sentryHandleError` and `wrapHandleErrorWithSentry` work from that subpath, on both trace lifecycles, for loaders, actions, resource routes and thrown 5xx Responses. (2) Request isolation: the worker entry must be wrapped with `withSentry` from `@sentry/cloudflare` around a handler built with `instrumentBuild` from `@sentry/remix/cloudflare`. `wrapRequestHandler` from `@sentry/cloudflare/request` exists only for runtimes that cannot enable `nodejs_compat` (Shopify Oxygen); on Workers it does not establish isolation unless `setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy` is called first. (3) Database spans require the build-time transform: add `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` to the Vite config alongside the Remix plugin — defaults are sufficient, `autoInstrumentation: false` is unnecessary, and the connection may sit at module scope or inside the loader — and set `ssr: { target: 'webworker', noExternal: true }`. Without the plugin, queries run normally, no `db` span appears, and the SDK logs no warning. The `_experimental.useDiagnosticsChannelInjection: true` requirement stated on the Vite plugin page is no longer needed on the v11 line and must be corrected there too. Finally, the page must also install `@sentry/cloudflare`, not just `@sentry/remix`.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/remix.mdx — rewrite to cover Workers: add `@sentry/cloudflare` to the install at :39-49, add a Workers entry section (`withSentry` + `instrumentBuild`), override the include's `@sentry/remix` import with `@sentry/remix/cloudflare`, and add a database-spans section (`sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` plus `ssr.noExternal`); additionally correct docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx:30-47 where `useDiagnosticsChannelInjection` is presented as required

docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/remix.mdx is 60 lines and is wrong for Workers: :39-49 installs only `@sentry/remix` (no `@sentry/cloudflare`), and :55-58 embeds the shared include. In that include, the Cloudflare branch platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.remix.mdx:263-313 covers Cloudflare Pages only — a `functions/_middleware.js` using `Sentry.sentryPagesPlugin` (:274-307) — with no Workers entry at all. The "Capture Server-Side Errors" step at :315-347 is outside any PlatformSection and tells every reader, Cloudflare included, to `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/remix"` (:333) and assign `Sentry.wrapHandleErrorWithSentry` / `Sentry.sentryHandleError` (:335-342). The run contradicts this: the bare specifier resolves to the browser build in the Remix Vite `webworker` SSR build, leaving `handleError` undefined and capturing nothing, with only a rollup warning. `instrumentBuild` and `@sentry/remix/cloudflare` appear in the docs only on the Oxygen page, docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/hydrogen-remix.mdx:32-42 and :91. `grep -rn noExternal` over docs and platform-includes returns zero hits. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx:30-47 tells users to enable `_experimental.useDiagnosticsChannelInjection: true`, which the run shows is not needed.

Two SDK-side findings worth filing. 1) `wrapRequestHandler` from `@sentry/cloudflare/request` has no request isolation. It is the only wrapper in packages/cloudflare/src that does not call `setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy()`, so `withInvocationIsolationScope` (packages/cloudflare/src/utils/invocationScope.ts) sees the stack strategy, `getIsolationScope() === getDefaultIsolationScope()` stays true and the fork is a no-op, exactly as its own comment predicts. Under concurrency every `setTag`/`setUser`/request-data write is global to the isolate and bleeds into unrelated later requests. This is the path the repo's own e2e app dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/remix-hydrogen/server.ts uses, and the path hydrogen-remix.mdx documents. Whether the fix belongs in `wrapRequestHandler` itself is a judgement call (the entry point exists to work without `nodejs_compat`, where AsyncLocalStorage is absent), but today neither the code nor the docs give the user any way to know isolation is off. 2) `makeWrappedCreateRequestHandler` from `@sentry/remix/cloudflare` double-reports on Cloudflare. Composed with `wrapRequestHandler` (the only sane way to get a client on Workers) it emits two `http.server` transactions per request in two different trace ids, because its `continueTrace` + `startSpan` (packages/remix/src/server/instrumentServer.ts:394-410) starts a fresh root instead of nesting under the Cloudflare root span; the outgoing-fetch headers then propagate the Remix trace and the Cloudflare transaction is orphaned. With an inbound sentry-trace header both roots share the incoming trace id, so the duplication is visible but the split is not. `instrumentBuild` alone avoids this entirely and still yields route-named transactions (its `updateSpanWithRoute` renames the enclosing Cloudflare root), so it is the shape to document, and the shape I ran the capability matrix on. Smaller observations: - With `instrumentBuild` alone the event's `transaction` field is unset (nothing calls `isolationScope.setTransactionName`); the transaction envelope is still named correctly. With the double-wrap the field is set. Minor grouping gap. - Under Vite 6 a plain `vite build` builds only `build/client` and silently skips the Remix SSR build. `npx remix vite:build` is required. Anyone following a generic "run vite build" instruction gets a worker entry that imports a non-existent `build/server/index.js`. - `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ autoInstrumentation: false })` composes fine with the Remix Vite plugin without `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` present; only its build-time channel injection is used, and it needs `ssr.noExternal: true` so the driver is inside the Vite SSR bundle rather than left for wrangler's esbuild. - npm needs `--legacy-peer-deps`: `@remix-run/cloudflare@2.17.5` peers `@cloudflare/workers-types@^4`, wrangler 4.129 peers `^5`. - No dual-@sentry/core problem despite @sentry/remix being bundled by Vite and @sentry/cloudflare by wrangler: the `globalThis.__SENTRY__` carrier is shared, and a tag set through the Vite-bundled copy isolates correctly once the ALS strategy is installed by the wrangler-bundled copy. - Probe routes are Remix resource routes (loader only, no component) so responses are JSON; the React render path was exercised only by `/` and the error boundary. - All processes killed, `node_modules` removed.
