SolidStart on Cloudflare M-solidstart-cf

SolidStart 1.3 (vinxi 0.5 + Nitro, `cloudflare-module` preset) · Cloudflare Workers (workerd via wrangler 4.129.0 dev, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, nodejs_compat) · viable: yes

Setup the docs would have to show

SolidStart runs on Cloudflare fine, but `@sentry/solidstart` does NOT: its server entry is `initNodeSdk` from `@sentry/node` (packages/solidstart/src/server/sdk.ts:3) and it depends on `@sentry/node` + `@sentry/nitro`, neither of which loads on workerd. There is no `@sentry/solidstart/cloudflare` export and no cloudflare code path anywhere in packages/solidstart or packages/nitro. The only wiring that works today is hand-rolled: keep `@sentry/solidstart` for the browser and wrap the Nitro worker output with `@sentry/cloudflare` yourself.

1) packages: `npm install @sentry/cloudflare @sentry/solidstart` (server SDK = cloudflare, client SDK = solidstart).

2) `app.config.ts` — the Sentry package MUST be left external, otherwise Nitro inlines a second copy of `@sentry/cloudflare` into `.output/server/index.mjs` and the `Sentry.*` calls in route handlers hit a different module instance than the one `withSentry` initialised:
```ts
import { defineConfig } from '@solidjs/start/config';
export default defineConfig({
  server: { preset: 'cloudflare-module', rollupConfig: { external: ['@sentry/cloudflare'] } },
});
```

3) `worker.mjs` (a hand-written wrapper entry, NOT the Nitro output):
```js
import * as Sentry from '@sentry/cloudflare';
import nitroHandler from './.output/server/index.mjs';
export default Sentry.withSentry(
  () => ({ dsn: '...', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' }),
  nitroHandler,
);
```

4) `wrangler.jsonc` points `main` at the wrapper, not at `.output/server/index.mjs`:
```jsonc
{ "name": "...", "main": "worker.mjs", "compatibility_date": "2026-05-01",
  "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"],
  "assets": { "directory": ".output/public", "binding": "ASSETS" } }
```
Nitro does NOT emit a wrangler config for this preset (`.output/` holds only nitro.json, package.json, public/, server/), so you write it by hand.

5) client: `src/entry-client.tsx` calls `Sentry.init` from `@sentry/solidstart` before `mount()` (the "browser" export condition resolves to the Solid browser SDK, so the Node deps never enter the client bundle).

6) run: `npx vinxi build && npx wrangler dev --config wrangler.jsonc --port <port> --inspector-port 0`.

Nuxt already ships exactly this shape as a supported plugin (`sentryCloudflareNitroPlugin`, packages/nuxt/src/runtime/plugins/sentry-cloudflare.server.ts, using `wrapRequestHandler` from `@sentry/cloudflare/request`). SolidStart, which is also Nitro-based, has no equivalent.
CapabilityVerdictDetail
errors✓* works-waManual `Sentry.captureException` inside a route handler reaches Sentry (sdk `sentry.javascript.cloudflare`, mechanism `generic`, handled true), which also proves the external-Sentry/dedupe wiring works. But an error THROWN from a route handler never becomes an event: Nitro/h3 catches it, logs `[request error] [unhandled]` and returns a 500 Response, so `withSentry` only sees a 500 and marks the request transaction `internal_error`. The framework swallows it, and there is no SolidStart-side hook (no `@sentry/solidstart` server middleware) available on this runtime to re-raise it. traceLifecycle: 'static'. verified: works-after-all REFUTED. A thrown route-handler error does become a Sentry event on SolidStart 1.3 + Cloudflare Workers. The missing piece is not a SolidStart hook, it is a **Nitro plugin registering the h3 `error` hook** — the same hook `@sentry/nitro` (packages/nitro/src/runtime/plugins/server.ts:7) and `@sentry/nuxt` (sentry-cloudflare.server.ts:128) register. SolidStart forwards `server.plugins` in `app.config.ts` straight to Nitro, so the hook is available on workerd; the previous probe simply did not register one. Probe dir: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-solidstart-cf-errors (node_modules removed; `npm install` restores it). Files: app.config.ts, src/server-plugin.ts (= RECIPE-nitro-error-plugin.ts), worker.mjs, wrangler.jsonc, src/routes/api/{boom,trace,sentinel}.ts, src/routes/ssrboom.tsx, sinkraw.mjs, raw-final.jsonl, wr-b.log. Rerun: `npm install` ; `PORT=47311 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs > sink-b.log 2>&1 &` ; `npx vinxi build` ; `npx wrangler dev --config wrangler.jsonc --port 47312 --inspector-port 0` ; `curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:47312/api/boom`. CONTROL (identical build, only `plugins: ['./src/server-plugin.ts']` removed from app.config.ts) — `GET /api/boom` 500, no event, exactly as reported: /api/boom=500 CONTROL span {"items":[{"name":"GET", ... "status":"e... <- only the errored server span CONTROL event [('trace-probe','generic',True)] <- manual capture still works CONTROL event [('sentinel','generic',True)] WITH the plugin (traceLifecycle 'static', sink /__items, request/user trimmed): {"type": "event", "exception": "Error: solidstart-cf boom", "mechanism": "chained", "handled": true, "sdk": "sentry.javascript.cloudflare", "trace_id": "92b8ab0e54a34586bea8489731033862"} {"type": "transaction", "name": "GET /api/boom", "op": "http.server", "source": "url", "status": "internal_error", "trace_id": "92b8ab0e54a34586bea8489731033862", "spans": []} (the compact sink prints `exception.values[0]`, which is the H3 error's `cause`. The raw envelope, raw-final.jsonl, shows the top-level mechanism is the unhandled one:) Error | solidstart-cf boom | {"handled": true, "type": "chained", "source": "cause", "exception_id": 1, "parent_id": 0} Error | solidstart-cf boom | {"type": "auto.function.nitro.captureErrorHook", "handled": false, "exception_id": 0} contexts.nitro: {"method": "GET", "path": "/api/boom"} The event shares the request's trace_id with the transaction, carries request URL/headers/user.ip_address, and wrangler logs `Sentry Logger [log]: Captured error event \`solidstart-cf boom\`` right before the `[request error] [unhandled]` line. Also verified: works identically on the develop default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` (event + `span` envelope, trace d1bda53e…); the 3xx/4xx guard in the plugin mirrors the SDK's own `captureErrorHook`; `@sentry/cloudflare` must stay in `rollupConfig.external` or the plugin gets a second module instance. RESIDUAL GAP (new, not in the original report): an error thrown while Solid renders a *page* (src/routes/ssrboom.tsx) still produces no event — only `{"type":"transaction","name":"GET /ssrboom","status":"internal_error"}`. SolidStart's cloudflare path does `renderToStream(...)` then `stream.pipeTo(writable); return readable`, so the render error surfaces inside the detached pipe after the Response was returned; neither Nitro's `error` hook nor `withSentry` ever sees it. Two dead ends tried: `createHandler(fn, { onError })` — solid's `onError` is the seroval *serializer* callback, never fired for render errors; `mode: 'sync'` — swallows the error entirely and returns 200 with partial HTML, which is worse. API routes, server functions and anything else that throws into h3 are covered by the hook.
Workaround: Add a Nitro plugin and register it in app.config.ts (full file at .../verify4-M-solidstart-cf-errors/RECIPE-nitro-error-plugin.ts): // src/server-plugin.ts import * as Sentry from '@sentry/cloudflare'; export default function sentryNitroPlugin(nitroApp: any) { nitroApp.hooks.hook('error', (error: any, errorContext: any) => { const status = error?.statusCode ?? error?.status; if (typeof status === 'number' && status >= 300 && status < 500) return; Sentry.captureException(error, { captureContext: { contexts: { nitro: { method: errorContext?.event?.method, path: errorContext?.event?.path } } }, mechanism: { handled: false, type: 'auto.function.nitro.captureErrorHook' }, }); }); } // app.config.ts export default defineConfig({ server: { preset: 'cloudflare-module', plugins: ['./src/server-plugin.ts'], rollupConfig: { external: ['@sentry/cloudflare'] }, // required: keeps one module instance }, }); Everything else stays as reported: worker.mjs wraps `.output/server/index.mjs` in `Sentry.withSentry`, wrangler.jsonc points `main` at worker.mjs. SDK-side follow-up: `@sentry/solidstart` could ship this as a cloudflare entry the way `@sentry/nuxt` ships `sentryCloudflareNitroPlugin`.
route names✗ broken`/api/users/42` produced transaction name `GET /api/users/42` with `source: "url"` — the raw path, not the `/api/users/:id` file-route pattern. `@sentry/cloudflare` has no knowledge of the Nitro/SolidStart router, and nothing parameterizes the name, so every distinct id is a distinct transaction name. traceLifecycle: 'static'. verified: confirmed-broken Reproduced the report exactly, then found no supported wiring that fixes it, only hand-written user code. App: $REPRO/refutations/verify4-M-solidstart-cf-routenames/app (SolidStart 1.3.2, vinxi 0.5.11, preset cloudflare-module, worker.mjs = Sentry.withSentry(...) around .output/server/index.mjs, wrangler 4.129.0 dev, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, nodejs_compat, @sentry/cloudflare 10.67.0 from $REPRO/_toolbox/pack). node_modules was removed at the end; rerun with `npm install --no-audit --no-fund` in app/. Rerun commands: PORT=52117 node $REPRO/_toolbox/sink.mjs > sinkB.log 2>&1 & (cd app && npx vinxi build && npx wrangler dev --config wrangler-static-b.jsonc --port 52118 --inspector-port 0) curl http://127.0.0.1:52118/api/users/42 # baseline curl -H 'x-route-mw: router' http://127.0.0.1:52118/api/users/42 # middleware recipe curl -s http://127.0.0.1:52117/__items 1) Baseline (withSentry only, traceLifecycle 'static'), sink verbatim: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/users/42","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","trace_id":"5e77d2837aef44e69f3e3b5afbb7db7c","sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare","spans":[]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/sentinel","op":"http.server","source":"url","status":"ok","trace_id":"88060890255a41329da9918e5c0d0abc","sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare","spans":[]} The report's claim holds: raw path, source "url", one transaction name per id. 2) traceLifecycle 'stream' is not better, it is worse for grouping in the other direction, the name loses the path entirely: {"type":"span","trace_id":"ed784f5a2e20414c98d513cbee944d83","items":["http.server GET"],"raw":[{"name":"GET","status":"ok","is_segment":true,"origin":"auto.http.cloudflare"}]} raw attributes: {"sentry.op":"http.server","sentry.segment.name.source":"url","sentry.segment.name":"GET"} 3) Why nothing in the SDK can fix it today. @sentry/solidstart exports only ".", "./solidrouter", "./vite" (no /cloudflare), and its server SDK is initNodeSdk. @sentry/nitro does parameterize (packages/nitro/src/runtime/hooks/captureTracingEvents.ts:72 getParameterizedRoute reads event.context.matchedRoute.route) but that path is unreachable here twice over: it needs @sentry/node, and on this preset the h3 context has no matchedRoute at all. Probe route /api/probe/[id] on the running Worker returned: "nativeContextKeys": ["_platform","cf","cloudflare","nitro","waitUntil","_nitro","solidFetchEvent"], "matchedRoute": null, "nativeParams": null, "nativePath": "/api/probe/7", "rootSpanAttrs": {"sentry.origin":"auto.http.cloudflare","sentry.op":"http.server","sentry.segment.name.source":"url","url.path":"/api/probe/7", ...} So even a straight port of the Nuxt/Nitro hook shape to @sentry/cloudflare would find nothing to read: SolidStart routes through its own router, and only its file-route table (vinxi/routes) or @solidjs/start's event.params carry the pattern. 4) What did work (user-land middleware, see workaround). Same app, header-gated so both paths are in one build. Static lifecycle, sink verbatim: {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_id":"4f6c0026031f4eff98c5c1812c7ad164","sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare","spans":[]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/users/:id","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_id":"9c485452bacd49fe928acfffb4d830a6","sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare","spans":[]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /things/:slug","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_id":"e4e38a8af9b041ed9ed9444a3cc19a7d","sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare","spans":[]} {"type":"transaction","name":"GET /api/hello","op":"http.server","source":"route","status":"ok","trace_id":"f7d416b6c5a34cfe9ab266a501925369","sdk":"sentry.javascript.cloudflare","spans":[]} Stream lifecycle, same build, raw span attributes: {"name":"GET /api/users/:id","is_segment":true,"attrs":{"sentry.op":"http.server","sentry.segment.name.source":"route","http.route":"/api/users/:id","sentry.segment.name":"GET /api/users/:id"}} {"name":"GET /things/:slug","is_segment":true,"attrs":{"sentry.op":"http.server","sentry.segment.name.source":"route","http.route":"/things/:slug","sentry.segment.name":"GET /things/:slug"}} It covers API routes and SSR page routes, in both lifecycles, and sets http.route plus source "route". 5) Variants I tried and rejected: - Deriving the pattern from event.params in onBeforeResponse instead of a route table: works for API routes ("GET /api/users/:id") but NOT for SSR page routes, params is empty there, so /things/xyz stayed {"name":"GET /things/xyz","source":"url"}. Do not document this variant. - Renaming inside a single route handler works ({"name":"GET /api/manual/:id","source":"route"}) but obviously does not scale. - Inlining @sentry/cloudflare instead of leaving it external in rollupConfig gives the middleware a second module instance, getActiveSpan() is undefined there and nothing renames. The external entry is load-bearing for the fix, not just for withSentry. Not attempted, out of reach: @sentry/solidstart's own vite plugin / server entry cannot be used at all on workerd (it pulls @sentry/node), so there is no "different init placement" to test on the SDK side. Repo reference apps dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/solidstart* are all Node/vinxi-node and assert Node-side nitro naming, none has a Cloudflare target. Files: app/src/middleware.ts (both modes), app/src/routes/api/probe/[id].ts (context dump), app/wrangler-static-b.jsonc, app/wrangler-stream-b.jsonc, app/wrangler-stream-raw.jsonc, rawsink.mjs (span-attribute sink), RECIPE-verified.md, logs wB-static.log / wB-stream.log / wB-stream-raw.log / wB-probe.log, all under .../deep/verify4-M-solidstart-cf-routenames/.
Workaround: Add a SolidStart middleware that matches the request path against the vinxi file-route table and renames the Cloudflare root span. Full text in .../deep/verify4-M-solidstart-cf-routenames/RECIPE-verified.md and app/src/middleware.ts. app.config.ts: export default defineConfig({ middleware: './src/middleware.ts', server: { preset: 'cloudflare-module', rollupConfig: { external: ['@sentry/cloudflare'] } }, }); src/middleware.ts: import { createMiddleware } from '@solidjs/start/middleware'; import { getActiveSpan, getRootSpan, spanToJSON, SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE } from '@sentry/cloudflare'; import { createRouter } from 'radix3'; import fileRoutes from 'vinxi/routes'; const normalize = (p) => p.replace(/\([^)/]+\)/g, '').replace(/\/+/g, '/').replace(/\*([^/]*)/g, (_m, m) => `**:${m}`); const router = createRouter({ routes: fileRoutes.reduce((memo, r) => { const pattern = normalize(r.path) || '/'; memo[pattern] = { pattern }; return memo; }, {}), }); export default createMiddleware({ onRequest(event) { const match = router.lookup(new URL(event.request.url).pathname); if (!match?.pattern) return; const active = getActiveSpan(); const root = active && getRootSpan(active); if (!root) return; const attrs = spanToJSON(root).attributes || {}; if (attrs['sentry.op'] !== 'http.server') return; root.setAttribute('http.route', match.pattern); root.updateName(`${attrs['http.request.method'] || 'GET'} ${match.pattern}`); root.setAttribute(SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, 'route'); }, }); Constraints: @sentry/cloudflare must stay in rollupConfig.external (a second inlined copy breaks getActiveSpan in the middleware); radix3 comes in transitively with nitro, add it explicitly under strict hoisting; works in both traceLifecycle 'static' and 'stream'.
isolation✓ worksThree concurrent GETs to /api/iso?who=alpha|beta|gamma (each with a 50-150ms random await between setTag and captureException) produced three events each carrying only its own `who` tag and its own trace id (a993566e…, dfc8c9a5…, dfd04c9a…), and the three request transactions carried the matching tag and trace id. traceLifecycle: 'static'.
incoming trace✓ worksA request with `sentry-trace: aaaa…aaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` and a matching baggage header produced both the event and the request transaction with `trace_id: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` and `parent_span_id: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`. traceLifecycle: 'static'.
outgoing fetch✓ worksA `fetch()` from inside a route handler to a local recorder produced a child span `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:53819/rec` on the request transaction, and the recorder saw `sentry-trace: 17b563b8968242ddb69fd63b93baf171-a0929cbc2b0df026-1` plus a full baggage header whose trace_id matches the transaction. traceLifecycle: 'static'.
db spans· not-runmysql2 could not be loaded at all: a module-scope `mysql.createPool` in a route died on workerd with `TypeError: _3.hasOwnProperty is not a function` inside Nitro's rollup CJS interop shim (.output/server/chunks/_/promise.mjs), so no query ever ran. Independently, no Sentry DB instrumentation path exists for this build shape — the build is vinxi/Nitro/rollup, not `@cloudflare/vite-plugin`, so `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin`'s `buildTimeInstrumentation` channel injection is not in play and there is no Bun plugin or Deno hook equivalent.
logs✓ works`Sentry.logger.info('solidstart-cf log line', { where: 'route-handler' })` in a route handler arrived as a log envelope carrying the request's trace id (eedeb885f6e94d328c02c1f5e2f1ff7d), matching the /api/logme transaction. traceLifecycle: 'static'.
client errors✓ worksWith `Sentry.init` from `@sentry/solidstart` in `src/entry-client.tsx`, an unhandled `setTimeout` throw on the /clienterr route arrived as an event with `sdk: sentry.javascript.solidstart`, `mechanism: auto.browser.browserapierrors.setTimeout`, `handled: false`, plus a `pageload` transaction with browser/resource spans. The pageload trace id (4c6e507d…) is unrelated to the SSR request trace id, i.e. no server->client trace continuation, because nothing injects a sentry-trace meta tag into the SSR HTML on this path.

Docs today

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions SolidStart on Cloudflare. `grep -rn -i cloudflare docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/` returns nothing across index.mdx, install/{index,cli-import,dynamic-import,limited-server-tracing}.mdx, features/ and profiling/. In the other direction, `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/` holds astro, hono, hydrogen-react-router, hydrogen-remix, nextjs, nuxt, remix, sveltekit and tanstack-start — there is no solidstart.mdx, and `grep -rn -i solidstart docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/` returns nothing. The nearest precedent is docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/nuxt.mdx:6, "This guide will show you how to set up the SDK with Nitro's `cloudflare_module` (or their deprecated `cloudflare-pages`) deployment preset." — the same Nitro preset family SolidStart uses, backed by packages/nuxt/src/runtime/plugins/sentry-cloudflare.server.ts:3 (`wrapRequestHandler` from `@sentry/cloudflare/request`). SolidStart has no such runtime plugin and no such page. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/index.mdx:11 still flags the whole SolidStart SDK as beta.

Documented: no

A page must exist and must open by stating that `@sentry/solidstart` itself does not run on Workers — its server entry initializes the Node SDK, and there is no `@sentry/solidstart/cloudflare` export or Cloudflare code path — so the runtime is wired by hand: keep `@sentry/solidstart` for the browser and wrap the built Nitro handler with `Sentry.withSentry` from `@sentry/cloudflare` in your own `worker.mjs`, keeping `@sentry/cloudflare` external via `server.rollupConfig` so Nitro does not inline a second copy. It must then document the two capabilities that need extra work beyond that wrapper. (1) Server errors are not captured by the wrapper alone: add a Nitro server plugin that forwards Nitro's `error` hook to `Sentry.captureException` and register it with `server.plugins: ['./src/server-plugin.ts']` in `app.config.ts`. (2) Route names are wrong: add `src/middleware.ts` (registered via `middleware: './src/middleware.ts'` in `app.config.ts`) that builds a radix3 router from vinxi's route manifest and renames the Cloudflare root span per request using `getActiveSpan`/`getRootSpan`/`spanToJSON` and the segment-name-source attribute. With those in place isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing fetch, logs and client-side errors all work; database spans were not exercised.

Page to write: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/solidstart.mdx (new), linked from docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23 and from docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/index.mdx

No page mentions this combination in either direction. `grep -rn -i cloudflare docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/` returns zero hits across index.mdx, install/, features/ and profiling/. `ls docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/` contains astro, hono, hydrogen-react-router, hydrogen-remix, nextjs, nuxt, remix, sveltekit and tanstack-start — there is no solidstart.mdx — and the framework list at docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23 omits SolidStart. SolidStart appears in the docs only inside PlatformSection exclusion lists, for example docs/platforms/javascript/common/tracing/streamed-spans/index.mdx:76 and docs/platforms/javascript/common/index.mdx:31. The generic Cloudflare `withSentry` entry pattern the run relied on is documented only at docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:111 ("Setup for Cloudflare Workers"), with no SolidStart context.

Headline: SolidStart itself runs on Cloudflare Workers out of the box (`preset: 'cloudflare-module'` builds, and /, /api/* and file routes all serve correctly under wrangler dev), but `@sentry/solidstart` cannot: its server half is `@sentry/node` (packages/solidstart/src/server/sdk.ts:3) and it also pulls `@sentry/nitro`, so the documented `Sentry.init` from `@sentry/solidstart` in a server entry is unusable on workerd. Everything I measured came from hand-wiring `@sentry/cloudflare`'s `withSentry` around the Nitro output; a user following the current SolidStart docs gets nothing on the server. Three concrete gaps a docs page or SDK change would have to close: 1. There is no `sentryCloudflareNitroPlugin` equivalent for SolidStart. Nuxt has exactly this (packages/nuxt/src/runtime/plugins/sentry-cloudflare.server.ts) and SolidStart is the same Nitro substrate, so the port looks mechanical. 2. The `rollupConfig: { external: ['@sentry/cloudflare'] }` step is non-obvious and silently fatal if you skip it: without it Nitro inlines a second `@sentry/cloudflare` into `.output/server/index.mjs`, so `Sentry.setTag` / `captureException` in a route handler run against an uninitialised client and produce nothing, while the request transactions from the wrapper still arrive and make it look like the SDK is working. 3. Nitro's cloudflare-module preset emits no wrangler config, so `main` has to point at a hand-written wrapper entry rather than at `.output/server/index.mjs`. Two behaviours worth filing regardless of docs: thrown route errors are swallowed by Nitro/h3 before `withSentry` sees them (only a 500 and an `internal_error` transaction survive), and transaction names are raw URLs (`GET /api/users/42`, source `url`) because nothing feeds the SolidStart file-route pattern to `@sentry/cloudflare`. Both are exactly what a real SolidStart-on-Cloudflare integration would need to fix; both are already solved on the Node path by the SolidStart server middleware. Also: no server-to-client trace continuation. The SSR HTML carries no sentry-trace meta tag, so the browser pageload starts a fresh trace. Version tested: develop only, the 10.67.0 tarballs from $REPRO/_toolbox/pack. 10.73.0 was never installed. All processes killed and node_modules removed.

Findings the docs need to absorb

Numbered so the docs items can cite them. K1 to K12 from the earlier audit keep their numbers.

Bun

  • F1. 10.73.0 does not trace outgoing fetch on Bun [B04, B13, B15, B19; confirmed twice]. No span, no sentry-trace, no baggage, even inside Sentry.startSpan: the SDK relies on undici's diagnostics channels, which Bun never publishes. The Bun integrations table lists nativeNodeFetchIntegration as auto-enabled; it never fires. develop ships fetchIntegration. Workaround on 10.73.0, verified: pass a globalThis.fetch patching integration, for example fetchIntegration() from @sentry/cloudflare@10.73.0 or winterCGFetchIntegration() from @sentry/vercel-edge (already a dependency of @sentry/nextjs), or a 30-line integration built from addFetchInstrumentationHandler and instrumentFetchRequest in @sentry/core. The Bun guide must say that distributed tracing out of Bun needs one of these until v11.
  • F2. 10.73.0 has no request isolation for node:http servers on Bun [B03, B18; confirmed twice]. Tags set in one request land on the events of every concurrent request, all share one trace id, and no http.server transaction is emitted, because the SDK's server instrumentation waits for the http.server.request.start diagnostics channel that Bun never publishes. Express, Koa, Hapi, Fastify and next start all run on node:http. develop's bunHttpServerIntegration fixes it. One-line workaround on 10.73.0, verified on Bun 1.3.14 and 1.4.0: after http.createServer(...), publish the channel yourself, channel("http.server.request.start").publish({ server }) from node:diagnostics_channel; the SDK then isolates every request and emits GET /path transactions. This is the paragraph most out of line with the released version on the Bun guide.
  • F3. Bun.serve never captures request bodies [B09; confirmed], on both versions, whatever dataCollection says. The guide's httpBodies: [] comment implies bodies are sent. bunServerIntegration() has no body options; only the node:http path has them. Workaround: in the handler, await captureBodyFromWinterCGRequest(req, getIsolationScope(), "medium") from @sentry/core, after which the body lands on the event and the transaction.
  • F4. Bun.serve streaming responses end the span at return [B10; confirmed]. A stream that runs 900 ms records a 0 ms span with status ok, and a client abort is invisible. No option changes it; a node:http server on Bun ends the span on response close (907 ms full, 305 ms on abort), and a manual startSpanManual around the body works. Bun users streaming from Bun.serve get wrong durations.
  • F5. Lazily loaded instrumented modules lose their spans [X02, B17, K11; confirmed twice]. Root cause: Bun's node:diagnostics_channel drops a channel and its subscribers on garbage collection when nothing holds a strong reference, on 1.4.0 and 1.3.14 alike. The SDK discards the channel object it subscribes to (packages/server-utils/src/tracing-channel.ts:200-208). The condition is when the instrumented file first evaluates, not when a connection is created: a static import mysql2 with per-request connections is fine, a dynamic import() inside a request or mysql@2's lazy require('./lib/Connection') on first createConnection is not. Fix: retain the channels in a module-level set. Workarounds: create the pool at module scope, add import "mysql/lib/Connection" next to import mysql, or hold the channel yourself. The earlier claim that only 1.4.0 is affected was wrong.
  • F6. The plugin build on 10.73.0 covers database drivers and OpenAI, not Express, Koa, Hapi, Fastify [B11, B17, B19]. Express spans on 10.73.0 need an active http.server root span, which is F2 again, and Express error capture needs the documented Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler(app); with both (the channel publish from F2 and the error handler) Express works on 10.73.0 in a plugin build and in a compiled binary. The docs must separate "what the plugin gives you on 10.x" from "on 11.x".
  • F7. Single-file executables work with the plugin, but the recommended external: ["@sentry/*"] breaks them [B11; confirmed]. Bun.build({ compile: true, plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] }) produces a working binary with Express spans on develop; with external the binary dies at boot (Cannot find module '@sentry/bun'). The CLI form bun build --compile cannot take plugins. The Bun guide's "single-file executables cannot be instrumented" alert is wrong; the quick start's external line needs a compile caveat.
  • F8. bun --hot stacks one Bun.serve proxy per reload when the SDK is initialized from the entry file [B12; refuted for the documented wiring]. With import "./instrument" in the hot-reloaded entry, each reload re-evaluates the SDK and every request emits N+1 root spans after N reloads, silently. With the documented bun --hot --preload ./instrument.ts app.ts (or preload in bunfig.toml) the preloaded module is not re-evaluated and everything stays clean. So --preload is not only an ordering convenience: the guide (and the proposed quick start, which leads with the entry-file import) must keep --preload as the primary form for anyone using --hot.
  • F9. @sentry/elysia reports sdk.name: sentry.javascript.bun [B13; confirmed twice]. applySdkMetadata runs on the wrong object in packages/elysia/src/sdk.ts. One-line fix; passing _metadata: {} to init works around it. The Elysia guide is otherwise accurate, apart from F1 on 10.73.0.
  • F10. Hono bundled with hono inlined and @sentry/hono external crashes the middleware [X01, K7; confirmed]. The two copies carry different GET_MATCH_RESULT symbols, so matchedRoutes throws before next() and every request is a 500. Never split hono and @sentry/hono across the bundle boundary: either bundle everything (no external) or keep both external.
  • F11. process.exit() right after capture loses the event [B08; confirmed]. Same on Deno with Deno.exit() [D08; confirmed twice]. Natural exit, await Sentry.flush(2000), Sentry.close(2000).then(() => process.exit()) and process.exitCode = n all deliver. The Node guide's drain include is not shown on the Bun and Deno guides; it should be.
  • F12. unhandledRejection default mode warn changes Bun's exit behavior [B01]. Bare Bun exits 1 on an unhandled rejection; with the SDK the process prints a warning and continues. The integration page should say so and point at mode: 'strict'.
  • F13. Bun native APIs are not instrumented [B16]: bun:sqlite, Bun.sql, Bun.redis produce no spans on either build path. Worth one sentence on the integrations page so nobody expects the mysql or redis integrations to cover them.
  • F14. Next.js on Bun with 10.73.0 needs different wiring than the repo's e2e app [B15]. bunHttpServerIntegration and fetchIntegration do not exist on 10.73.0; bunServerIntegration() alone gives errors, route transactions and isolation, and winterCGFetchIntegration() from @sentry/vercel-edge (already installed with @sentry/nextjs) restores outgoing fetch spans and headers, verified. The runtime is reported as node.
  • F15. NestJS on Bun works through the plugin build [B14; refuted as a defect, qualified by the round-three cell]. Route names arrive only when the init comes from @sentry/bun with nestIntegration() added; the documented @sentry/nestjs init keeps errors but loses route names on Bun. Express spans and SentryGlobalFilter error capture work once @sentry/nestjs is bundled together with the app; the crash seen first came from external: ["@sentry/*"], which loads a second @nestjs/core copy. Rule for the docs: do not externalize @sentry/* in a Bun bundle that uses @sentry/nestjs/setup.

Deno

  • F16. Outgoing fetch is not traced [D04, K2], both versions: no span, no headers, trace ends at the first fetch to another service; node:http clients propagate fine.
  • F17. The hook crashes without --allow-env [D02; confirmed twice]. import "@sentry/deno/import" loads a vendored debug package that reads process.env at import; a scoped --allow-env=DEBUG is not enough. Without the hook, --allow-net alone works but loses server_name, os.version, context lines and app:// paths. The guide's --allow-read=./src is also too narrow: the SDK queries read permission on the working directory, so context lines and app:// paths need --allow-read=.; server_name and the OS version need --allow-sys=hostname,osRelease.
  • F18. The hook only transforms modules under a local node_modules [D18, K12]. With Deno's default npm cache layout nothing is injected and nothing warns, with or without debug: true. nodeModulesDir: "auto" is required.
  • F19. The hook cannot instrument statically imported ESM packages, and crashes the ones it does transform [D17; the defect stands, a configuration fixes it]. Deno loads the whole static module graph before the hook registers, so import OpenAI from "openai" is never transformed; a dynamic import after init is transformed, but Deno reports format: undefined for .mjs, so the transformer injects a require() into an ES module and the app dies. Verified ways out on develop: resolve the package to its CommonJS build ("openai": "npm:openai/index.js" in the import map, or --conditions=require), after which the static import is instrumented normally. On 10.73.0, which has no OpenAI integration in the Deno defaults, instrumentOpenAiClient(client) from @sentry/core works without the hook.
  • F20. Any require() of a JSON file fails under the hook [X03, D15, K3; confirmed on 2.8.3 and 2.9.0]. A Deno bug in the registerHooks load path (format never set); Express, Hapi, Fastify and mysql2 crash at import. Verified workaround: register a second load hook after the Sentry one that sets format: 'json' when the URL ends in .json; with it Express imports and gets injected. The same six lines belong in register.ts until Deno ships denoland/deno#36243. Koa fails on a second loader path (generator-function/require.mjs) that the JSON fix does not cover.
  • F21. mysql2 3.20 and later works without the hook [D15; refuted as "no spans on 10.73.0"]. It publishes its own channels; @sentry/deno develop ships mysql2Integration in the defaults, and on 10.73.0 mysql2Integration from @sentry/server-utils@10.73.0 (a dependency of @sentry/deno) can be passed to init and works. The docs can list it as "no hook needed", together with Fastify.
  • F22. denoCronIntegration crashes init() on Deno 2.9.0 [D11; confirmed four times]. Deno.cron became a getter-only accessor; the integration assigns to it. Works on 2.8.3. Without --unstable-cron it no-ops silently. Workaround: before init, redefine Deno.cron as a writable data property with Object.defineProperty; the SDK fix is the same call in deno-cron.ts. The Deno crons page is wrong on the current Deno.
  • F23. 10.73.0 never captures request bodies on Deno.serve [D09]; develop does, with denoServeIntegration({ maxRequestBodySize }). The guide's httpBodies: [] comment is misleading for 10.x.
  • F24. Streaming: client cancel is not propagated upstream, and application/octet-stream is not treated as streaming [D10, gist D5]. Update: develop fixed the cancel half on 2026-09-06 in c619da370 (monitorStream now forwards cancel(reason) to the source reader, with a regression test). The octet-stream half stands.
  • F25. Sessions exist for node:http requests on develop only; Deno.serve never produces them [D05]. A sync throw in a node:http listener is swallowed by Deno's compat layer (client gets 400, nothing captured) [D14].
  • F26. Oak works when mounted on Deno.serve, not with app.listen() [D12; refuted as a limitation]. app.listen() runs middleware in its own loop outside the SDK's request scope, so errors are swallowed and events are not linked to the request. Deno.serve({ port }, req => app.fetch(req, {}, info)) runs Oak inside the instrumented handler: route errors are captured automatically and linked to the span. That is the sentence a Deno frameworks page needs.
  • F27. deno compile works, hook included, at 99 MB for the minimal install [D16]; source maps, CJS builds and type declarations make up most of the embedded size. enableLogs: true fails Deno's type check on develop.

Cloudflare

  • F28. Errors inside ctx.waitUntil() are lost on both versions [C01; confirmed four times]. workerd logs Uncaught Error, nothing reaches Sentry, and no option changes it. Users must attach a .catch(e => Sentry.captureException(e)) to every promise they hand to waitUntil; on 10.73.0 do not await Sentry.flush() inside that task, it deadlocks the flush lock. No page says so.
  • F29. 10.73.0 shares one trace id across all scheduled and queue invocations of an isolate [C04, C05; confirmed]. Cron runs, their check-ins and errors are stitched into one trace, because 10.x's withIsolationScope reuses the isolate's current scope and its propagation context. Fixed on develop. Workarounds on 10.73.0: set a fresh propagation context in the withSentry options callback for scheduled, and wrap the SDK-wrapped queue handler in Sentry.startNewTrace.
  • F30. 10.73.0 ignores dataCollection: { httpBodies: [] } for incoming bodies [C13; confirmed twice, by design in 10.x source]; httpServerIntegration({ maxRequestBodySize: 'none' }) works. The index page presents httpBodies: [] as the way to disable bodies.
  • F31. develop: the cached client makes Dedupe drop repeated errors across requests [C10, C14; confirmed twice]. Two identical errors from two requests yield one event; a repeated captureMessage is dropped until a different event intervenes. Seen on Pages and Workers, and inside Workflows (C26). cacheClient: false or removing the Dedupe integration restores per-request delivery. This needs a decision before v11 ships.
  • F32. develop: @sentry/cloudflare/request runs without the AsyncLocalStorage strategy [C09; confirmed twice]. Under the stream lifecycle a request without I/O is sent as a legacy transaction envelope and a following event was dropped; traceLifecycle: 'static' (what the Hydrogen apps and the repo suite pass) or calling setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy() at module scope fixes it. 10.73.0 is unaffected because it defaults to the static lifecycle.
  • F33. Pages middleware spans static assets too [C10]. GET /app.js produces a transaction; the docs snippet at the root _middleware.js does not mention scoping.
  • F34. Workflows capture step errors only on the final attempt [C26; confirmed]. A step that throws once and then succeeds produces no event; the docs' "capture all step failures" wording only held for engines without step context (the repo's legacy e2e app pins wrangler 4.70 for that). Capturing inside the step and, on develop, cacheClient: false for the workflow client give one event per attempt.
  • F35. KV produces no spans; R2, Queues, D1, DO storage do, and none of those four is documented [C05 to C08]. Queue publish spans are named after the binding, process spans after the queue.
  • F36. No automatic sessions on Workers [C12; refuted as "impossible"]. @sentry/cloudflare does not re-export the session API, but startSession, captureSession and endSession from @sentry/core (a dependency) work inside the withSentry handler on both versions and produce valid session envelopes. The same manual pattern works on Bun and Deno (B05, D05). Worth one paragraph on each runtime guide.
  • F37. The docs' "Astro 3-5 auto-wrap via env vars" path is dead on adapter 14 [C18]. The @sentry/astro Cloudflare plugin regex targets the old virtual entry; a Sentry.init server config on adapter 13+ silently boots the browser SDK inside the Worker and loses the first requests. The documented main: sentry.server.config.ts + withSentry setup works.
  • F38. React Router 7 and TanStack Start work on Workers with 10.73.0 and have no Cloudflare docs [C20, C21]. SvelteKit, Nuxt, Next.js (OpenNext) and Hono work as documented [C17, C19, C22, C15]; on 10.73.0 sentrySvelteKit is on the root export.
  • F39. OpenAI on Workers: the Vite plugin instruments an unwrapped client [C16]. The OpenAI page says unwrapped clients produce no spans on Cloudflare; with the plugin they do, on both versions.
  • F40. Service binding and Durable Object stub fetch inject headers but create no http.client span, and no caller-side span exists for RPC calls [C08, C25]; instrumentFetcher's JSDoc says otherwise.

Follow-up round: ten more behaviors

A completeness critic (Opus) read the probe list and the guide pages and named ten behaviors nobody had run. All ten ran, their failures went through two independent Opus refuters each, and a docs pass followed. Verdicts: 8 works, 14 partial, 2 broken across the version pairs; of the 16 failures sent to refuters, 2 were refuted.

  • F41. The Deno guide's two permission flags are both too narrow [N1; confirmed three times]. --allow-read=./src gives context lines only for files under that path, so the entry file stays bare, and app:/// path normalization needs read access to ./. --allow-sys is never mentioned and is what restores server_name and contexts.os.version. Nothing prompts and nothing warns: every permission is queried first and the field is dropped when it is not granted. The one hard failure is the hook, which dies at import without --allow-env. Correct line for the guide: deno run --allow-net=<ingest> --allow-read=. --allow-sys=hostname,osRelease --allow-env main.ts. Side finding: under a proxied Deno.permissions shim (a Deno Deploy simulation) the SDK throws this.querySync is not a function internally and that internal error replaces the user's event.
  • F42. The @sentry/cloudflare/nodejs_compat entrypoint works on 10.73.0 and is gone on develop [N2; the develop "broken" verdict was refuted as an intentional v11 change]. On 10.73.0 the subpath boots and prismaIntegration from it instruments Prisma end to end. On develop the subpath does not exist and prismaIntegration lives on the main entry, so every sample on the nodejs-compat and Cloudflare Prisma pages fails at bundle time once v11 ships. MIGRATION.md documents the move; the docs pages do not.
  • F43. The Vite plugin page matches 10.73.0 exactly and describes a different API than develop [N3; confirmed twice]. On 10.73.0 the options really are _experimental.autoInstrumentation and _experimental.useDiagnosticsChannelInjection, both default false, and a bare plugin call really is a no-op. On develop they are top-level autoInstrumentation and buildTimeInstrumentation, both default true, so sentryCloudflareVitePlugin() alone wraps the entry, the Durable Object, the WorkerEntrypoint and injects channels. Two things no version of the page says: the plugin also wraps WorkerEntrypoint classes, and it auto-populates rpcTracePropagationBindings.
  • F44. The Agents SDK page describes attributes the SDK does not set [N4; confirmed three times]. The callable RPC span carries the agent class only, and that class is the base class name, not the exported wrapped class; there is no instance-name attribute. The automatic conversation ID is a fresh uuid4 that rotates on message:clear, never the agent instance name, which makes the page's per-user and singleton advice wrong. Setting Sentry.setConversationId yourself works, as the same page recommends further down for another reason. On develop the page's enableRpcTracePropagation sample is a type error.
  • F45. Durable Object websocket and alarm spans are real and undocumented [N5; confirmed twice]. One span per webSocketMessage and per webSocketClose, one function alarm span per alarm with the throw captured as auto.faas.cloudflare.durable_object, tags isolated per connection, and the documented cf_, cf:, __ps_, / key filtering holds for get, put, delete and list. The page mentions only the storage spans.
  • F46. contextLinesIntegration is not exported by @sentry/cloudflare on either version [N6; confirmed twice]. The Cloudflare contextlines include shows a call that cannot run, and the common page marks Cloudflare as unsupported, so the include is unreachable as well as wrong. Delete it. The other five documented optional integrations work on all three runtimes. Two smaller corrections: extraErrorDataIntegration puts its data under contexts.<ErrorName>, not under extra, and on 10.73.0 Bun an outgoing fetch produces no breadcrumb at all, which is worse than F1 alone.
  • F47. The Bun OpenTelemetry setup page cannot be followed on either version [N7; confirmed three times]. On 10.73.0 three defects: the install line omits @sentry/node-core, which the snippets import and which only resolves by hoisting; the NodeSDK tab's import is missing SentrySpanProcessor; and the error-monitoring-only snippet calls provider.addSpanProcessor(), removed in OpenTelemetry JS 2.x. On develop the page cannot be assembled at all, since @sentry/node-core no longer exists, but a v11 path does exist and the page needs rewriting rather than porting.
  • F48. deno serve works and is documented nowhere [N8; works on both versions]. export default { fetch } under deno serve is instrumented exactly like Deno.serve, the hook applies, errors are captured, and --parallel runs one Sentry.init per worker (16 in one process) with no duplicated telemetry. The Deno guide shows only deno run.
  • F49. Fresh 2 boots but loses route names and route errors [N9; confirmed, with verified fixes]. Fresh 2.3.3 runs with the hook in both vite dev and the built deno serve shape, and K3 does not bite it. But transactions are named by raw path, so /api/[name].tsx never becomes a route pattern, and an error thrown in a route handler is swallowed by Fresh's 500 renderer and never reaches Sentry. A three-line middleware registered after app.use(staticFiles()) fixes both. No Fresh page exists.
  • F50. Debug IDs: the Cloudflare claim was wrong, the Bun one holds [N10; refuted for Cloudflare, confirmed for Bun]. sentryCloudflareVitePlugin is an instrumentation plugin and has nothing to do with source maps; the documented flow (@sentry/vite-plugin, or the wizard, or sentry-cli sourcemaps inject) does produce debug IDs. On Bun, sentryBunPlugin injects none either, so the explicit sentry-cli sourcemaps inject step is required, which is what the proposed Bun quick start already says.

What to do with this

  1. Bun guide, released version. State F1, F2, F3 plainly in a "What the SDK records on Bun" table with a column per SDK version, and move the plugin into the install flow (F6, F7). This is the page most out of line with its SDK.
  2. Deno guide. Fix the permission line first (F41), add deno serve (F48) and a Fresh page (F49), then add the hook step with its preconditions (nodeModulesDir, --allow-env, CommonJS builds only) and the crash list with the two-line JSON fix (F17 to F20). Fix the permission flags (--allow-read=., --allow-sys=hostname,osRelease). List Fastify and mysql2 as "no hook needed" (F21) and Oak as "mount on Deno.serve" (F26). Fix the crons page for Deno 2.9 (F22).
  3. Cloudflare guide. Add the bindings and handlers table (F35), the waitUntil note (F28), the Pages scoping note (F33), the Workflows retry note (F34), the Durable Object websocket and alarm spans (F45), and the two framework pages (F38). Correct the OpenAI page (F39), the Agents SDK attributes (F44) and the Vite plugin page for v11 (F43). Delete the Cloudflare contextlines include (F46). Version-tag the 10.73.0 defects and the v11 entrypoint move (F29, F30, F42).
  4. SDK tickets. F5 (channel retention), F9 (Elysia metadata), F10 (Hono symbols), F19 and F20 (Deno hook: static graph, .mjs format, JSON format workaround), F22 (Deno.cron accessor), F31 and F32 (develop regressions), F3 and F4 (Bun.serve bodies and streams), F24 (Deno stream cancel, now landed on develop as c619da370; the octet-stream classification remains), F28 (waitUntil), F40 (fetcher spans). The earlier audit's K11 text needs the corrected root cause.
  5. Bun OpenTelemetry page (F47) needs a rewrite per version, not a port.
  6. Quick start correction. The proposed Bun quick start leads with import "./instrument"; given F8 it must lead with --preload and mention the entry import only as the alternative for runs without --hot.

What was not measured

A completeness check on 2026-09-07 compared the probe list with the SDK exports on develop and with the docs pages shown to these runtimes. These are the gaps that remain. None of them is a verdict; each is a place where the docs claim or the SDK ships something this audit did not run.

Capabilities inside the framework cells

  • Browser-side errors ran in one cell of 51 (SolidStart on Cloudflare). Every meta-framework guide documents a client config next to the server one; the framework verdicts here are server-side measurements.
  • Release health sessions, metrics, cron monitors, source maps, profiling, request bodies and streaming were probed per runtime (the B, D and C probes) but never inside a framework cell.
  • Fastify on Cloudflare has no capability entries at all; the cell is a boot failure, not a measurement.

SDK features with no probe

  • Bun: bunRuntimeMetricsIntegration, the Sentry.cron helpers (the Bun crons include promises automatic instrumentation of cron, node-cron and node-schedule, which are plugin-build libraries), the profiler export (the docs mark Bun unsupported), the pino, winston and consola transports, fsIntegration, localVariablesIntegration, anrIntegration, trpcMiddleware, wrapMcpServerWithSentry.
  • Deno: denoRuntimeMetricsIntegration, the default OpenTelemetry tracer setup (enableOpenTelemetrySetup), otlpIntegration, the deprecated deno* integration aliases, the breadcrumbsIntegration and normalizePathsIntegration pages, and fifteen default library integrations that never ran on Deno (aws, firebase, kafka, graphql, knex, dataloader, genericPool, tedious, lruMemoizer, postgresJs, langChain, langGraph, anthropicAI, googleGenAI, vercelAI). Finding F19 suggests the import hook cannot transform the ESM-only ones.
  • Cloudflare: the email and tail handlers that withSentry wraps, Workers AI spans, instrumentWorkerEntrypoint as its own shape, SQL and sync-KV Durable Object storage, defineCloudflareOptions, setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy, enableDedupe, Spotlight, the disabled rate-limiter spans, moduleMetadataIntegration, growthbookIntegration, setConversationId outside the Agents SDK page.

Deployment shapes with no cell

  • Cloudflare Pages Functions running a framework. Every framework verdict is a Workers verdict, while the Cloudflare frameworks index still speaks of Pages.
  • Deno Deploy. No local node_modules there, which finding F18 says disables the import hook, and a proxied Deno.permissions made the SDK throw internally in finding F41.
  • Bun single-file executables per framework, deno compile with a framework, a Durable Object or a scheduled or queue handler inside a framework Worker, standalone Nitro on the three presets, and @sentry/effect on any of the three runtimes.

Docs pages the audit never cited

The stream-mode includes for all three runtimes, the crons setup includes for Bun and Deno, the Bun OpenTelemetry setup includes, the Cloudflare source-map includes, the dedupe, extra-error-data, rewrite-frames and feature-flag includes for the three runtimes, the v7-deprecation migration includes for Bun and Deno, the Hono error-handler page, and the Cloudflare Durable Object and Workflows feature pages. The ones with a verifiable defect are itemized in section 6 of the docs audit.

Probe records

One section per probe. develop is the v11 line at 6f2da7483d, 10.73.0 the published release. Verification: every broken or partial result was handed to two independent agents told to make it work; "confirmed" means neither could. Docs status comes from a separate pass over getsentry/sentry-docs.

Bun probes

B01. B01. Process-level errors in a Bun script

develop: works. Uncaught exception (timer or top level): one event, mechanism auto.node.onuncaughtexception, handled=false, level fatal, exit code 1 (same as the no-SDK baseline; the SDK prints the error and calls process.exit(1) after flushing). Unhandled rejection: one event, mechanism auto.node.onunhandledrejection, handled=false, level error, extra.unhandledPromiseRejection=true; with the default mode 'warn' the SDK prints the Node-style warning and the process keeps running and exits 0, whereas the no-SDK baseline exits 1 (Bun crashes on unhandled rejections by default). With mode 'strict' the event is fatal and the process exits 1. With a user process.on('uncaughtException') handler and the default exitEvenIfOtherHandlersAreRegistered=false the event is captured but the SDK does not exit (exit 0, same as baseline with a handler); with exitEvenIfOtherHandlersAreRegistered: true the user handler...

throw-timer: {"type":"event","exception":"B01 uncaught exception (timer)","mechanism":"auto.node.onuncaughtexception","level":"fatal","handled":false,...} EXIT_CODE=1; reject-default: {"mechanism":"auto.node.onunhandledrejection","level":"error","extra":{"unhandledPromiseRejection":true},"handled":false} then warning printed, EXIT_CODE=0; BASELINE no SDK: reject-default EXIT_CODE=1; reject-strict: level fatal, EXIT_CODE=1; userhandler default: event + sentinel, EXIT_CODE=0; userhandler + exitEven: event, EXIT_CODE=1

Repro: $REPRO/probes/B01-rerun/run.sh $REPRO/probes/B01-rerun/develop bun140 bun; $REPRO/probes/B01-rerun/run.sh $REPRO/probes/B01-rerun/develop bun1314 $SCRATCH/bun1314/bun-darwin-aarch64/bun; $REPRO/probes/B01-rerun/run-baseline.sh bun140 bu, files in $REPRO/probes/B01-rerun/develop/{instrument.ts,throw.ts,reject.ts,results-bun140.log,results-bun1314.log}, runner $REPRO/probes/B01-rerun/run.sh, baseline $REPRO/probes/B01-rerun/baseline/. 10.73.0: works. Identical to develop for every case: uncaught exception exits 1 with a fatal event; user handler + default options: captured, no exit; exitEvenIfOtherHandlersAreRegistered true: exits 1; unhandled rejection: error event, warning printed, process continues, exit 0 (baseline exits 1); strict: fatal, exit 1. Cosmetic: 10.73.0 always prints the 'This error originated either by...' warning in strict mode.

same seven cases, identical events and exit codes on Bun 1.4.0 and 1.3.14 (results-bun140.log, results-bun1314.log)

Repro: $REPRO/probes/B01-rerun/run.sh $REPRO/probes/B01-rerun/10.73.0 bun140 bun; ... bun1314 ..., files in $REPRO/probes/B01-rerun/10.73.0/{instrument.ts,throw.ts,reject.ts,results-*.log}. Docs: partial. docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/integrations/onuncaughtexception.mdx:24,40-42,56; docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/integrations/unhandledrejection.mdx:24,83-94; platform-includes/configuration/integrations/javascript.bun.mdx:25-26 The OnUnhandledRejection page should say that on Bun the default mode 'warn' changes the runtime's behavior: without the SDK Bun exits with code 1 on an unhandled rejection, with the SDK the rejection is captured (level error, handled=false), a warning is printed and the process keeps running and exits 0; use mode: 'strict' to keep the crash (fatal event, exit 1). The OnUncaughtException page matches the observed Bun behavior (fatal event, exit 1; with a user handler and the default exitEvenI... Notes: Mechanism types are auto.node.onuncaughtexception / auto.node.onunhandledrejection on both versions. Bun quirk in the baseline: on an unhandled rejection Bun fires process 'exit' with code 0 but the real exit status is 1.

B02. Enrichment on Bun events

develop: works. Docs: wrong. platform-includes/configuration/integrations/javascript.bun.mdx:6,13; docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/integrations/http.mdx:24,30,38-41,107-128; docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/integrations/bunserver.mdx:3,18; docs/platforms/javascript/common/enriching-events/request-is The BunServer page should say that every Bun.serve request gets its own isolation scope, so Sentry.setTag/setUser and captured errors stay per request and each request has its own trace and http.server transaction/span, and the Request Isolation page should be enabled for Bun. The Bun integrations table lists httpIntegration as auto-enabled and the Http page promises incoming request spans and options, but on @sentry/bun 10.73.0 a node:http createServer app has no per-request isolation at all (tags leak across concurrent requests, one shared trace_id, no request data, no http.server transactions) because Bun does not emit the diagnostics channel the integration relies on; node:http servers are only isolated and traced on the develop build that adds bunHttpServerIntegration, which is not documented anywhere.

Notes: Root cause for the 10.73.0 node:http failure: Bun's node:http does not publish the http.server.request.start diagnostics channel (dc-probe.ts prints 'fired: 0'), so @sentry/node's httpIntegration never forks an isolation scope or starts a server span; all requests share the global/default isolation scope and setTag races (last writer t5 wins, all events share one trace id). develop closes this with bunHttpServerIntegration (packages/bun/src/integrations/bunHttpServer.ts, patches http.Server.prototype.emit and hands the server to core's getHttpServerSubscriptions), which is in the default integration set, and its errors carry transaction 'GET /a'. Evidence above is from the fresh r2-* runs; an earlier run of the same probes (drive-develop-*.log, drive-v1073-*.log, plus *-bun1314.log using $SCRATCH/bun1314 Bun 1.3.14 for the node:http variant) gave identical verdicts on both Bun versions. B05. Release health sessions on Bun

develop: partial. Bun.serve with release "1.0.0" and default options never produces a `sessions` aggregate (not after the sentinel, not at t+65s, not after process exit); the only session data is the single process session from processSessionIntegration, which is sent immediately as a `session` envelope with status `crashed` when the throwing request is captured (mechanism auto.http.bun.serve, handled:false), even though the process keeps serving. A node:http server DOES get request session aggregates on develop (bunHttpServerIntegration, sessions default true): with a handled captureException the `sessions` envelope arrives at the 60s flush with exited:3 errored:1, and the process session is later sent as `exited` at beforeExit; with a throwing handler the throw is an uncaught exception that kills the process, so the aggregate is flushed at once with exited:2 (the crashed request is not counted) plus a crashed process session.

[confirmed-broken] Could not refute. `process.exit(0)` right after `Sentry.captureException()` loses the event on every run, on Bun 1.4.0 and the CI-pinned 1.3.14, with @sentry/bun 10.67.0 (develop, node_modules/@sentry/* symlinked to ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/packages/*). B10. Streaming responses on Bun.serve

develop: broken. The http.server transaction for a route returning new Response(ReadableStream) ends the moment the handler returns the Response object (1-3 ms), not when the stream finishes (~900 ms; client measured 915 ms for the full body). Client cancel after the first chunk is invisible to the SDK: the transaction had already ended with status ok / http.response.status_code 200 before the cancel happened, and no error event is captured. Identical on Bun 1.4.0 and CI-pinned Bun 1.3.14.

Docs: no. docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/integrations/bunserver.mdx:3,18; docs/platforms/javascript/common/tracing/distributed-tracing/index.mdx:58 The BunServer page should say that the http.server span for a handler returning new Response(ReadableStream) ends when the handler returns the Response object (0-1 ms), not when the body finishes streaming, so the span duration excludes streaming time and a client abort mid-stream is still reported as status ok / http 200 with no error event, in both static and stream trace lifecycles. The 'trace stays active until the response is sent' statement on the distributed tracing page does not hold for streamed responses on Bun.serve.

Notes: Root cause is visible in the SDK source: ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/packages/bun/src/integrations/bunserver.ts:249-275 wraps the handler in startSpan and only awaits `target.apply(thisArg, args)`, i.e. the Response object; it calls setHttpStatus(span, response.status) from the status code and never observes the body ReadableStream, so the span cannot see stream completion, stream errors, or client cancellation. Consequences: (1) http.server duration for SSE/streaming/long-poll routes is always ~0 ms; (2) any child spans started while producing chunks (DB calls, fetches inside the stream's pull/start) would start after the parent already ended; (3) a client abort produces status ok and no event (Bun does call the ReadableStream cancel() callback, so a hook point exists). Notes: 1) Bun 1.4.0's `Bun.build` JS API supports `compile: boolean | target | { outfile, target, execArgv, ... }` (bun-types 1.4.0 bun.d.ts:3332) and it accepts plugins; the CLI `bun build --compile` has no `--plugin` flag, so the JS API is the only way to get the Sentry plugin into an executable. 2) The `external: ['@sentry/*']` pattern used in the non-compile quick-start build.ts is fatal for compiled binaries on both versions: Bun resolves externals from the virtual `/$bunfs/root/` and does not fall back to the cwd's node_modules, so `@sentry/bun` must be bundled into the executable (the plugin's `withoutInstrumentedExternals` only un-externalizes instrumented packages, not `@sentry/*`). Docs/quick-starts for compile should not carry that `external` line. 3) Inside the develop executable the SDK still logs `Sentry Logger [warn]: No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injectio

B12. bun --watch and --hot dev modes

develop: partial. `bun --watch app.ts` works fully: init, the route error (mechanism auto.http.bun.serve) and one http.server span per request arrive, and after editing app.ts the runtime restarts with fresh module state (instrument evaluated once again, one client, one Bun.serve wrapper) and everything still arrives once. `bun --hot app.ts` with `import "./instrument"` as the first line works before the first edit, but every hot reload re-evaluates the whole module graph including @sentry/bun: Sentry.init runs again (a new client each time, no warning), the module-level `hasPatchedBunServe` guard resets so Bun.serve is wrapped in a Proxy again on top of the previous Proxy, and uncaughtException/unhandledRejection listeners accumulate. Result: after N-1 reloads each request produces N `http.server` root spans, each in its own trace (2 after one edit, 3 after two); the error event still arrives once only because the second wrapper hits the `__sentry_captured__` dedupe. Using `bun --hot --preload ./instrument.ts app.ts` instead of the in-file import avoids all of it: instrument.ts is evaluated once, Bun.serve stays wrapped once, one span per request and events keep arriving after reloads.

Docs: no. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx:94-107 The Apply Instrumentation step only shows `bun --preload ./instrument.js app.js`. It should say that `bun --watch` restarts cleanly, but that `bun --hot` re-evaluates `@sentry/bun` on every reload, so each reload stacks another `Bun.serve` wrapper (after N reloads every request emits N+1 `http.server` root spans in separate traces) and adds another `uncaughtException`/`unhandledRejection` listener, silently; error events are still captured once. Recommend `--watch` instead of `--hot` during development.

Notes: Root cause of the --hot duplication is in packages/bun/src/integrations/bunserver.ts: `let hasPatchedBunServe = false` is module state, and `bun --hot` re-evaluates node_modules along with the app (sameSentryNs=false after reload), so each reload wraps the already-proxied `Bun.serve` again; likewise Sentry.init creates a new client on every reload and the onUncaughtException/onUnhandledRejection integrations add another process listener each time (listener counts grow 1,2,3). The duplicated spans are separate root spans in separate traces (not nested children), so the Sentry UI would show N transactions per request. Error events are deduped only by the __sentry_captured__ flag on the error object. The reload guard should live on globalThis (or the SDK should detect a prior init) to survive --hot. B14. NestJS on Bun via the plugin build

develop: partial. Bundling a NestJS 12 app (platform-express) with Bun.build + sentryBunPlugin and running it on Bun 1.4.0 (and 1.3.14) gives request spans with route names (`http.server GET /cats/:id`, http.route=/cats/:id), Express middleware/handler spans and, with `nestIntegration()` from a self-built @sentry/nestjs added to the @sentry/bun init, the Nest spans (`Create Nest App`, `CatsController.getCat`, `Request handler`, exception_filter) and error capture through `SentryGlobalFilter` (`auto.http.nestjs.global_filter`). Two things break: (1) with the documented `external: ["@sentry/*"]`, `SentryGlobalFilter` from `@sentry/nestjs/setup` runs against a second, external copy of `@nestjs/core`, so its `httpAdapterHost` is never injected and every error request crashes with `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'applicationRef.isHeadersSent')` (the error IS still captured, but the client gets Express's HTML 500 instead of Nest's JSON 500); (2) bundling `@sentry/nestjs` instead trips a Bun bundler bug on `export * from '@sentry/node'` (`ReferenceError: node is not defined`). A build that keeps exactly `@sentry/nestjs` external via an onResolve plugin but bundles `@sentry/nestjs/setup` works end to end. Without @sentry/nestjs at all (plain @sentry/bun), controller exceptions are swallowed by Nest's ExceptionsHandler and never reach Sentry.

With plain `bun run` and with the sentryBunPlugin build (identical results), a node:http server on Bun produces NO http.server transactions or spans at all and no per-request isolation: all 3 concurrent requests, the sentinel and both errors share one trace id, the `reqid` tag set by the last-started request (C) bleeds onto every event (iso-A, iso-B, sentinel-1, the errors), and no event carries request data. X01. Hono on Bun bundled: hono inlined vs external (K7)

develop: partial. Unbundled `bun run app.ts` and the bundle with `external: ["@sentry/*", "hono"]` both work: route-parameterized span names (`GET /hello/:name`, `GET /sub/item/:id`) and both route errors (main app and sub-app) captured with mechanism `auto.http.hono.context_error`. The bundle with only `external: ["@sentry/*"]` (hono inlined) is broken: every request returns 500, no error event is captured, and spans are named just `GET`. Cause: the external `@sentry/hono/bun` loads its own `hono` copy from node_modules whose `hono/route` `matchedRoutes` reads `c.req[GET_MATCH_RESULT]` with a `Symbol()` that differs from the inlined hono's Symbol, so `requestHandler` throws `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'c.req[GET_MATCH_RESULT][0]')` before `next()` runs.

Docs: no. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hono/index.mdx:12, docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hono/index.mdx:290-292, docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx:96-98 The Hono guide documents the `@sentry/hono/bun` middleware but says nothing about bundling. It should say that when bundling with `Bun.build`, `hono` must be kept external alongside `@sentry/*` (`external: ["@sentry/*", "hono"]`): with hono inlined and `@sentry/hono` external, every request returns 500, no error event is captured and spans lose their route names, because the external middleware loads its own `hono` copy whose `hono/route` Symbol does not match the bundled one (`TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'c.req[GET_MATCH_RESULT][0]')`). Unbundled and hono-external builds give `GET /hello/:name` route names and `auto.http.hono.context_error` events on both versions.

Notes: The inlined-hono failure is not a Sentry-side patching miss but a hard crash of the Sentry middleware itself: `@sentry/hono` (kept external) imports `matchedRoutes` from `hono/route` out of node_modules, and that helper indexes `c.req` with a module-local `Symbol()` (`hono/dist/request/constants.js`). The bundle carries a second copy of that Symbol (dist-inline/app.js:49), so the lookup returns undefined and `requestHandler` throws before `next()`; Hono's default error handler turns it into a 500 and Sentry never sees the error (no event in either version). Effectively any bundle that inlines hono while keeping @sentry/* external takes the whole app down, not just the route naming. Same behavior on develop (10.67.0 tarballs, stream lifecycle) and 10.73.0 (static lifecycle), hono 4.13.5, Bun 1.4.0. X02. K11 independent re-verification (lazy module load under Bun)

develop: broken. K11 reproduces identically on Bun 1.4.0 AND Bun 1.3.14 (the earlier claim that 1.3.14 differs does not hold). With the sentryBunPlugin bundle, a module-scope mysql connection yields the db span; createConnection inside the request (static top-level `import mysql`) yields no db span because mysql's index.js lazily requires lib/Connection.js on first createConnection, so the instrumented module first evaluates inside the request; dynamic `await import('mysql')` in the handler behaves the same. The no-SDK variant (plain `dc.tracingChannel('orchestrion:mysql:query').subscribe(...)` at module scope, mysql loaded in the handler) fires zero channel events on both Bun versions, while the same subscriber with mysql loaded at module scope fires start/end/asyncStart/asyncEnd once per query. Root cause (verified with a 20-line script, no SDK, no bundle): Bun's node:diagnostics_channel drops a channel and its subscribers on GC when no user code holds a strong reference to the Channel/TracingChannel object (even plain `dc.subscribe(name, fn)` is lost); Node keeps subscribed channels alive. The SDK's mysqlIntegration calls bindTracingChannelToSpan(diagnosticsChannel.tracingChannel(...)) and discards the returned `channel` handle (packages/server-utils/src/tracing-channel.ts:200-208, packages/server-utils/src/integrations/mysql.ts:79-80), so after a GC the lazily evaluated Connection.js gets a fresh, unsubscribed channel. Holding a strong reference from user code (`globalThis.__keepMysqlChannel = dc.tracingChannel('orchestrion:mysql:query')` at module scope) makes the lazy case produce the db span on both Bun versions, which confirms the mechanism and is a user-side workaround; the SDK-side fix is to retain the channel objects it subscribes to (e.g. a module-level Map/Set of bound channels).

Workaround: Make sure the instrumented module is evaluated at boot, not on first use inside a request. Concretely: (a) create the connection/pool at module scope (the documented pattern); or (b) for drivers whose entry point requires the instrumented file lazily (mysql@2: lib/Connection.js), add a top-level side-effect import of that file, e.g. `import "mysql/lib/Connection";` next to `import mysql from "mysq

Docs: wrong. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx:96-98, docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/integrations/mysql.mdx:24-38, platform-includes/configuration/integrations/javascript.bun.mdx:21 The Bun guide claims bundled code cannot be auto-instrumented, but mysql `db` spans on Bun come only from the `sentryBunPlugin` bundle. The page should add the module-load requirement: the instrumented driver module must be evaluated at startup, so create the mysql connection at module scope; a `createConnection()` inside a request handler (mysql lazily loads `lib/Connection.js` on first call) or a dynamic `await import('mysql')` in the handler yields no db span and no warning, on Bun 1.4.0 and 1.3.14 alike, because Bun's `diagnostics_channel` drops subscribed channels on GC when nothing holds a strong reference to them.

Notes: 1) The TOOLBOX statement "on Bun 1.4.0 the injected channel does not even fire in that case" implies a difference from 1.3.14; I see no difference: both Bun versions lose the subscription in every lazy variant, and both work in every module-scope variant (2 requests each, bundles built with the matching Bun). 2) "createConnection inside the request" with a static top-level `import mysql` is already the lazy case: mysql@2's index.js requires lib/Connection.js on the first createConnection call, so the instrumented file evaluates inside the request; `loadedBefore:[]` on the first request confirms the plugin's module-injected snippet had not run before the handler. 3) Mechanism, isolated from the SDK: Bun's diagnostics_channel keeps only weak references to channels, even after subscribe (Node incRefs subscribed channels). dc-gc.mjs shows `dc.tracingChannel('dropped:query').subscribe(...)` a

The documented setup cannot be assembled at all on the v11 line. `@sentry/node-core` does not exist (no `packages/node-core` in the monorepo, and npm's latest is 10.73.0, so there is no 10.67.0 to install), so `bun --preload ./instrument.ts` dies on the include's second line before Sentry.init runs. Even after removing that import, `@sentry/opentelemetry@10.67.0` exports neither `SentrySampler`, `SentrySpanProcessor` nor `wrapSamplingDecision`, and the string `skipOpenTelemetrySetup` appears nowhere in the develop source, so the option is silently ignored. 10.73.0: partial. The NodeTracerProvider tab runs verbatim and mostly works: `@sentry/node-core` resolves (hoisted from `@sentry/node` - it is NOT a declared dependency of `@sentry/bun@10.73.0`, and the include never tells you to install it), OTEL-created spans DO reach Sentry (`tracer.startActiveSpan('manual')` arrives as a child of the BunServer transaction), and captured errors work. Three real defects: (1) `validateOpenTelemetrySetup()` writes through `debug.*`, so with the snippet as written (no `debug: true`) it prints nothing whether the setup is right or wrong - verified with a negative control that only spoke once `debug: true` was added; (2) the NodeSDK tab crashes verbatim - it calls `new SentrySpanProcessor()` but its import line only pulls `SentryPropagator, SentrySampler`; (3) the error-monitoring-only variant crashes verbatim on `provider.addSpanProcessor` (removed in OTel JS SDK 2.x) and pins `@opentelemetry/exporter-otlp-http`, deprecated since 0.26.0 (2021, peer `@opentelemetry/api ^1.0.2`). With both import/API fixes applied, both tabs behave as documented. Trace propagation on outgoing `fetch` does NOT work - but a control run proves that is a pre-existing Bun condition, not caused by skipOpenTelemetrySetup: the default setup on the same app also sends no headers and no http.client span (same on bun 1.3.14, and to both a Bun.serve and an express target). Side effect worth noting: with skipOpenTelemetrySetup the server transaction name degrades from `GET /work` to `GET http://127.0.0.1:51357/work`.

Deno probes

D01. Process-level errors in a Deno script

develop: works. Both an uncaught error thrown from a setTimeout callback and an unhandled promise rejection are captured by the Deno GlobalHandlers integration as level=fatal, handled=false events with mechanism auto.deno.global_handlers.error / auto.deno.global_handlers.unhandledrejection, with context lines. Identical with and without `import "@sentry/deno/import"`. The SDK flushes the event, then rethrows, so the process exits with code 1 (same as a plain Deno script without Sentry); the 2s 'STILL ALIVE' timer never fires. Only cosmetic difference: Deno prints `Uncaught (in promise) Error: ...` instead of `Uncaught Error: ...` because the SDK rethrows from inside flush().then().

Notes: Both versions behave the same. Observations: (1) Deno prints the rethrown error as `Uncaught (in promise) Error: ...` in every case, even for a plain sync throw, because the SDK rethrows from inside flush().then(); the original message and source frame are preserved, exit code is 1 which matches a Sentry-less baseline (deno run baseline-throw.ts also exit=1). (2) A synchronous `throw` at module top level is reported with mechanism auto.deno.global_handlers.unhandledrejection, not .error, because Deno evaluates ES modules as a promise; the message/stack are still correct. (3) Non-Error rejections become excType UnhandledRejection with "Non-Error promise rejection captured with value: ...", no context line. (4) No session envelope is sent by these scripts (no autoSessionTracking in the Deno SDK). (5) $REPRO/probes/D01/develop and $REPRO/probes/D01/10.73.0 already contained an earlier run of this same

D02. Enrichment on Deno events

develop: partial. With all four permissions every enrichment lands: user, tags, extra, custom context, manual + console + fetch breadcrumbs, app:// filenames with context_line (5 lines pre/post), contexts.runtime/os(with version)/v8/typescript/app/device, server_name. With --allow-net only the SDK still sends the event but drops server_name, os.version, app:// normalisation and context lines. However the documented hook entry `import "@sentry/deno/import"` crashes the process at startup under --allow-net only (NotCapable: Requires env access from the `debug` package's `Object.keys(process.env)`), so no event is sent at all; adding --allow-env is required for the hook. Sentinel arrived in the sink before the exception event (contextlines is async), so sentinel ordering does not hold on Deno.

D03. Request isolation under concurrency on Deno.serve

develop: works. On develop (worktree packages 10.67.0, deno 2.9.0, hook via `import "@sentry/deno/import"`) 5 concurrent GET /a?tag=t1..t5 requests each produced exactly one error event carrying only its own `reqtag`, one `http.server` span per request with the matching `url.full` and `reqtag` attribute, 5 distinct trace ids, and each event's trace id equals its request's server span trace id. Same result for the Deno.serve app and the node:http createServer app. Stream lifecycle: server spans arrive as `span` envelopes named `GET` (no route), events carry no `transaction` field on Deno.serve (they do on node:http).

D04. Incoming trace continuation on Deno.serve and node:http

develop: partial. Incoming sentry-trace/baggage are continued on both Deno.serve and node:http servers (server span trace_id = aaaa...ab, parent_span_id = bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb, DSC in the envelope header carries the upstream baggage values). An outgoing node:http request from inside the handler carries sentry-trace (same trace, parent = the server span) and the upstream baggage. An outgoing fetch from inside the same handler carries no sentry-trace, no baggage, no traceparent, and gets no http.client span (K2 confirmed, even inside an active continued trace). Identical with default traceLifecycle 'stream' (span envelopes) and with 'static' (transaction envelopes).
