Docs: wrong. docs/platforms/javascript/common/tracing/distributed-tracing/index.mdx:55-58,75; platform-includes/distributed-tracing/how-to-use/javascript.mdx:1,13-20 (browser fallback shown to Deno); docs/platforms/javascript/common/tracing/instrumentation/requests-module.mdx:7; docs/platforms/javascript/common/ The Deno distributed-tracing page should say that incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers are continued automatically for both `Deno.serve` and `node:http` servers (observed: parent span id and upstream DSC preserved, no configuration needed, no `browserTracingIntegration`), and that outgoing `node:http` requests get an `http.client` span and propagate the headers. It must also state that outgoing `fetch` calls on Deno currently create no span and send no `sentry-trace`/`baggage`/`traceparent` header, so a trace breaks at `fetch` unless headers are added manually with `Sentry.getTraceData()`; the current claims that the SDK instruments all outgoing HTTP/fetch requests are contradicted by the observation on both develop and 10.73.0.

Notes: 1) Verdict is partial on both versions for the same reason: incoming continuation and node:http outgoing propagation work; outgoing fetch from inside a continued, sampled server span carries neither sentry-trace nor baggage nor traceparent and produces no http.client span. This extends known K2 to the "active continued trace" case, and it is identical on develop (10.67.0 @ 6f2da7483d) and 10.73.0. 2) The app does NOT use the `@sentry/deno/import` hook (plain `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno"`), so this is the no-hook path; per the toolbox Deno.serve/node:http instrumentation does not need it. 3) develop stream lifecycle batches both servers' segments and their http.client children into one span envelope; the envelope-level DSC there is the upstream baggage (environment=upstreamenv, transaction=upstream-tx), i.e. the DSC is correctly frozen from the incoming baggage on both versions

D05. Release health sessions on Deno

develop: partial. node:http requests are tracked as request-mode sessions: after 3 node:http requests (2 ok, 1 handled captureException + 500) a `sessions` aggregate envelope with release 1.0.0 arrived (exited 2, errored 1). Deno.serve requests produce no session at all (3 Deno.serve requests incl. one that throws, plus sentinel, 10s wait: 0 session envelopes). A handler that throws inside a node:http listener is swallowed by Deno's node:http compat (client gets HTTP 400, no Sentry event), so that session is counted as `exited`, never `crashed`.

Docs: partial. platform-includes/configuration/auto-session-tracking/javascript.mdx:20-36 (server sessions paragraph hidden for javascript.deno),38-41; docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/releases.mdx:30-43; docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/integrations/http.mdx:4-26,143-152 (page not show The Release Health section shown to Deno users should say that on 10.x no request sessions are sent at all (nothing arrives even after the 60s flush window), and that starting with the develop behavior only `node:http` requests are tracked as sessions via `denoHttpIntegration({ sessions, sessionFlushingDelayMS })`, while `Deno.serve` requests produce no session data. It should also note that an uncaught throw inside a `node:http` listener on Deno is swallowed by the runtime (client gets 400, no error event), so such sessions are recorded as `ok` and a `crashed` session is not reachable that way; `errored` works via `captureException`.

Notes: 1) Deno.serve is not covered by sessions on either version; only node:http servers get request-mode session aggregates on develop (packages/deno/src/integrations/deno-serve.ts has no session code). For an app that uses Deno.serve, which is the idiomatic Deno server, release health still shows no session data after upgrading. 2) A synchronous throw inside a node:http request listener is swallowed by Deno's node:http compat layer: the client receives HTTP 400, no uncaught-exception event reaches Sentry on either version, and on develop the request session is recorded as `ok`/`exited`, so `crashed` can never be counted from node:http on Deno (drive-d05-throw.out: exited 3, errored 0, crashed 0). D10. Streaming responses on Deno.serve

develop: partial. Full read: the http.server transaction covers the whole stream (906ms for text/plain, 909ms for text/event-stream, status ok) but only when the content-type matches the SDK's streaming heuristic; application/octet-stream gets a 0ms span. Client cancel after the first chunk: the span does NOT end on disconnect, it ends only when the app enqueues the NEXT chunk into its stream (605ms with 300ms chunks; 6007ms with 3s chunks, i.e. the span was still open 1.5s after the client cancelled), always with status ok / http 200 and no cancellation marker. The app's ReadableStream cancel() is never invoked with Sentry active (without Sentry, Deno cancels it with reason 'resource closed' 3ms after the client leaves), so the producer keeps running and enqueues all remaining chunks.

Docs: no. docs/platforms/javascript/common/tracing/instrumentation/automatic-instrumentation.mdx:23-33 (browser-only table shown to Deno); platform-includes/configuration/integrations/javascript.deno.mdx:3-21 (no denoServeIntegration entry); docs/platforms/javascript/common/tracing/streamed-spans/index.mdx:86 A Deno page should say that for `Deno.serve` responses with `text/event-stream`, `application/(x-)ndjson`, `application/stream+json`, or `text/plain` without content-length, the `http.server` span stays open until the stream closes, while any other content type (e.g. `application/octet-stream`) ends the span before the first chunk. It should also warn that when a client disconnects mid-stream the SDK's stream wrapper does not propagate cancellation to the app's ReadableStream: the upstream `cancel()` is never invoked, the app keeps producing chunks, and the span only ends on the next enqueue with status `ok`/200 instead of shortly after the disconnect as plain `Deno.serve` does.

Notes: Root cause is visible in the worktree source, ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/packages/deno/src/utils/streaming.ts: (1) classifyResponseStreaming only treats text/event-stream, application/(x-)ndjson, application/stream+json and text/plain-without-content-length as streaming, so any other content-type (application/octet-stream, application/json, text/html) ends the span before the body is sent (0ms span even though the client read for 909ms). (2) monitorStream wraps the body in a new ReadableStream with only a start() pump and no cancel() hook; on client disconnect Deno cancels the wrapper (no-op), the pump only notices when the next controller.enqueue throws, then calls reader.releaseLock() (not reader.cancel()), so the span ends one chunk late and the app's upstream ReadableStream is never cancelled (cancel() never runs, timers keep firing, all remaining chunks are produced).

develop: partial. On Deno 2.9.0 (the machine default) with --unstable-cron, Sentry.init() itself crashes the process: denoCronIntegration does `Deno.cron = new Proxy(...)` but Deno 2.9.0 exposes Deno.cron as a getter-only accessor, so init throws `TypeError: Cannot set property cron of #<Object> which has only a getter` and the app exits 1 before any user code runs. On Deno 2.8.3 (CI pin, Deno.cron is a writable data property) the integration works: one in_progress and one ok check_in with monitor_slug "probe" and crontab schedule "* * * * *" arrived after the cron fired at the minute boundary. Without --unstable-cron, init succeeds (integration no-ops because Deno.cron is undefined) and the user's own Deno.cron(...) call throws `TypeError: Deno.cron is not a function`; no check_in envelopes.

D12. Oak framework on Deno

develop: partial. Deno.serve request spans appear for Oak (jsr:@oak/oak@17.2.0) as streamed `span` envelopes named by method only (`http.server GET`, url.full carries the raw path, /error gets status=error http.status=500), but ONLY when Sentry.init runs in a separate module imported before Oak: Oak's http_server_native.ts binds `globalThis.Deno.serve` at module-evaluation time, so with `Sentry.init` in the same file as `import { Application } from "@oak/oak"` (imports hoisted) no request spans are produced at all. The thrown route error is never captured by the SDK on its own (Oak catches it, answers 500 and logs `[uncaught application error]`); `app.addEventListener("error", evt => Sentry.captureException(evt.error))` is required and then yields an event, but that event is not linked to the request trace (its trace_id equals the global isolation-scope trace, not the request span's), because Oak runs middleware outside the wrapped handler's async context: `Sentry.getActiveSpan()` inside a route handler is null and the isolation scope is shared across requests. The `@sentry/deno/import` hook makes no difference (Oak is a jsr package, not under node_modules).

Notes: 1) Root cause of the missing spans in the single-file layout: jsr:@oak/oak@17.2.0 http_server_native.ts line 25-26 does `const serve = ... globalThis.Deno.serve.bind(globalThis.Deno)` at module evaluation; ESM import hoisting evaluates Oak before `Sentry.init()` in the same module runs, so denoServeIntegration's Proxy is never used. Fix on the user side: put Sentry.init in `instrument.ts` and import it first (the documented Node-style pattern), or dynamic-import Oak after init. This affects both versions identically. 2) Root cause of the missing trace context: Oak's Server hands each request from the Deno.serve handler to an async iterator consumed by `Application.listen`'s loop, so middleware runs outside `wrapDenoRequestHandler`'s AsyncLocalStorage context. D14. node:http server on Deno (no framework)

develop: partial. http.createServer on Deno 2.9.0 with @sentry/deno 10.67.0 (no import hook needed) produces http.server spans/transactions with full request attributes, correct per-request isolation under concurrency, and outgoing node:http client spans with sentry-trace/baggage propagation into a child http.server span (same trace). What does not work: a synchronous throw inside the request listener is swallowed by Deno itself (client gets an empty 400, no error event, and the SDK records the transaction as status ok / http.response.status_code 200), and an async throw is captured only via the global unhandledrejection handler, after which the SDK rethrows and the whole server process exits (response never sent, later requests ECONNREFUSED). Deno.serve captures both cases with mechanism auto.http.deno, answers 500 and keeps running. Naming: stream lifecycle (default) names the segment span just "GET" (sentry.segment.name.source: url, url.path attribute carries the path); traceLifecycle:'static' yields transactions "GET /hello/world", source url. Outgoing fetch gets no span and no headers (known K2), same as Deno.serve.

Notes: 1. Root cause of the sync-throw gap is Deno, not the SDK: without Sentry, a throw inside the node:http request listener is swallowed by Deno's node:http shim, the client receives an empty HTTP 400 with Connection: close, and nothing reaches globalThis 'error' or the server 'error' event (bare-drive-b.out). Because the response object is never written, response.statusCode stays 200 and the SDK ends the span with status ok / http.response.status_code 200 while the client actually got 400. On Node the same throw would surface as uncaughtException and be captured. 2. The async-throw process exit is SDK-intended behaviour: packages/deno/src/integrations/globalhandlers.ts:86-125 captures the rejection, calls e.preventDefault(), flushes, then rethrows "to replicate Deno default behavior". For a node:http server this means one rejected handler promise kills the server; Deno.serve wraps the handl

10.73.0: broken. With the hook (`import "@sentry/deno/import"`) and `import OpenAI from "openai"` (openai 7.9.0 via `deno add npm:openai`, nodeModulesDir auto), only the `GET /ai` transaction with empty spans arrives; no gen_ai span. Without the hook: same, none. Two independent causes: (1) the ESM `completions.mjs` is not transformed by the hook on Deno (CJS `completions.js` is), and (2) @sentry/deno@10.73.0 neither exports openAIIntegration nor registers the openai channel integration by default (its defaults cover amqplib, koa, mongo, mongoose, mysql, postgres only). Adding `openaiChannelIntegration()` from `npm:@sentry/server-utils@10.73.0/orchestrion` AND loading openai via `createRequire` yields a full gen_ai.chat span; the explicit integration with the ESM import still yields nothing.

The page should state explicitly that the OpenAI SDK is not auto-instrumented on Deno: a static `import OpenAI from "openai"` with the `@sentry/deno/import` hook yields no gen_ai span, loading openai after the hook (dynamic import or `--import`) crashes with `ReferenceError: require is not defined` in openai's .mjs files, and on the upcoming version a `gen_ai.chat` span only appears when openai is loaded via `createRequire(import.meta.url)("openai")`.

Notes: Root cause of the ESM miss (same on both versions): the hook's load path in @apm-js-collab/tracing-hooks@0.13.0 hook.mjs `loadResult` derives moduleType from `result.format` ('module' -> esm, 'commonjs' -> cjs, else 'unknown'). On Deno 2.9.0, `Module.registerHooks` `nextLoad` returns `format: undefined` for openai's `resources/chat/completions/completions.mjs` (probe-format.ts), so the ESM file is handed back untransformed and no `failed to inject` warning is logged; the CJS `completions.js` (loaded via createRequire) does get the `__apm$` wrapper. Therefore any Deno app that uses the natural `import OpenAI from "openai"` gets no OpenAI spans even with the hook, on both develop and 10.73.0; only a CJS require path works. On develop the openai channel integration is registered by default (Integration installed: OpenAI) and reports `sentry.origin: auto.ai.openai` with `gen_ai.provider.name

X03. K3 independent re-verification (JSON require under a load hook)

develop: broken. K3 confirmed independently on both deno 2.9.0 and 2.8.3: a CJS file doing require('./x.json') works with no hook and with a resolve-only hook, but fails with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` under ANY node:module registerHooks({load}) hook, even a pure pass-through no-op, so the defect is in Deno, not in the Sentry transform. Root cause visible from inside the hook: Deno's nextLoad() returns `format: undefined` for both .cjs and .json (Node returns 'commonjs'/'json'), and Deno's CJS loader then compiles the JSON text as JS via Module._compile/compileFunction. The @sentry/deno/import hook (c-sentry) and `import 'express'` under the hook (d-express, first failing require is node_modules/statuses/index.js:15 `require('./codes.json')`) fail identically; express imports fine without the hook. No --unstable-* flag changes anything. A load hook that sets `format = 'json'` on .json URLs (or hands back `module.exports=<json>` as commonjs) makes require work, and layering that fix outside the Sentry hook (f-sentry-fixed) makes express import AND get injected (`__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__.runtime = ["express","express"]`), so an SDK-side workaround in register.ts is feasible. Koa is a separate Deno bug: under any load hook it dies with `Cannot resolve module "./index.js" from .../generator-function/require.mjs` in loadESMFromCJS, unaffected by the JSON fix.

Notes: 1. Only the develop version was requested, so no 10.73.0 entry. The failure is independent of the SDK anyway: b-noop.mjs (no @sentry code at all, just `registerHooks({ load(url, ctx, next) { return next(url, ctx) } })`) reproduces it on both Deno 2.9.0 and 2.8.3.\n2. Mechanism: with a sync load hook registered, Deno's `nextLoad` result has no `format` field (e2-ctx shows only shortCircuit/source), and Deno's CJS `Module._load` path then treats every hooked file as JS. Explicitly returning `format: 'json'` from the hook fixes it (e-format-json). The @apm-js-collab/tracing-hooks `loadSync` returns the nextLoad result unchanged for non-instrumented URLs, so the SDK cannot avoid it today, but `registerDiagnosticsChannelInjection` in packages/server-runtime-injection/src/register.ts could wrap `load` on Deno and set `format = 'json'` when it is missing for `.json` URLs; f-sentry-fixed.mjs pro

Notes: Verdict in one line: the `deno serve` entry shape works on both versions, `--parallel` does not duplicate anything, and nothing about it is documented. Why it works: `denoServeIntegration` installs a Proxy over `globalThis.Deno.serve` in `setupOnce` (packages/deno/src/integrations/deno-serve.ts:98-116). `deno serve` calls `Deno.serve` from JS (ext:deno_http/00_serve.ts) *after* it has loaded the user module, so the patch is already in place and the default export's `fetch` gets wrapped. The uncaught-error stack proves it: `at handler (ext:deno_http/00_serve.ts:1168:26)` sits directly above `packages/deno/src/integrations/deno-serve.ts:72` and `wrap-deno-request-handler.ts:129`. What `--parallel` actually does here: one OS process (single pid), N worker threads (16 = hw.ncpu on this machine), each of which re-executes the entry module. So there are 16 `Sentry.init` calls, 16 clients, 16

N9. Fresh 2 on Deno

develop (10.67.0, worktree ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs): partial. Fresh 2.3.3 (Vite-based) boots fine with `import "@sentry/deno/import"` as the first line of main.ts, in both `vite` dev and the built `deno serve -A _fresh/server.js` production shape. K3 does NOT bite Fresh: no boot error at all, and removing the hook line changes nothing. What is missing is the two things a Fresh user most needs: (1) errors thrown in a Fresh route handler are swallowed by Fresh's own 500 renderer and NEVER reach Sentry - the sink shows only a span and no `event`; (2) server spans are named `GET` (method only) with no path and no Fresh route pattern, so `/api/[name].tsx` hits are indistinguishable. Fresh 2 already instruments `renderRoute` through `@opentelemetry/api`, but @sentry/deno registers no TracerProvider so those spans hit `NoopTracer` and are discarded (visible verbatim in the stack trace below). Outgoing `fetch` from a route produced no client span (K2 holds). A 4-line try/catch middleware registered right after `app.use(staticFiles())` does capture the route error correctly, with source context - that is the workaround the guide would have to document.

ALL THREE OBSERVED SYMPTOMS REPRODUCE EXACTLY, but the reported CAUSE for the missing spans is REFUTED and two of the three symptoms are fixable in user code. 1) Boot: confirmed works. `import "@s Workaround: A single Fresh middleware registered before `app.fsRoutes()` fixes route naming AND error capture on stock 10.73.0 (verified, prod 51844): app.use(async (ctx) => { try { const res = await ctx.next(); const span = Sentry.getActiveSpan(); if (span && ctx.route) { Sentry.updateSpanName(span, `${ctx.req.method} ${ctx.route}`); span.setAttribute("http.route", ctx.route); [partial] Independent rebuild, different wiring than the original probe: fresh `jsr:@fresh/init@^2` scaffold (Fresh 2.3.3), `nodeModulesDir: "auto"` (original used "manual"), Sentry init factored into a separate `instrument.ts` imported as line 1 of `main.ts` (original inlined it), own sink on 38471 and own echo upstream on 38474. CONFIRMED (out of the box, dev and prod): - Boots cleanly with `import "@sentry/deno/import"` in both `vite` dev and `deno serve _fresh/server.js`. K3 does not hit Fresh. `vite Workaround: Three separate pieces, all verified end to end on 10.73.0 + Fresh 2.3.3. 1) Fresh's own spans (`middlewares`, `lazy-route`, `handler`, `render`): put `Sentry.init()` in a module that the server entry evaluates BEFORE the Fresh build. Do not put it inside `main.ts` - in the production bundle Fresh's core module body runs first. Add `serve-entry.ts` next to `_fresh/`: import "./instrument.ts";

Docs: no. no match for "Fresh" anywhere under docs/, platform-includes/ or includes/ (grep); docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx is the only Deno entry point and covers only a plain script There is no Fresh guide, so a Fresh 2 user has nowhere to look. A guide should say that Fresh 2.3.3 boots with `import "@sentry/deno/import"` as the first line of main.ts in both `vite` dev and the built `deno serve _fresh/server.js` shape, but that errors thrown in a route handler are swallowed by Fresh's 500 renderer and never reach Sentry, and show the try/catch middleware registered after `app.use(staticFiles())` that captures them. It should also record that transactions are named from the raw path (`GET /api/alice`), never the Fresh route pattern, and that Fresh's own `@opentelemetry/api` `renderRoute` spans are dropped because `@sentry/deno` registers no TracerProvider.

Notes: Bottom line for the guide: Fresh 2 is safe to declare supported on Deno. The predicted K3 import-time crash does not happen - Fresh routes its dependencies through Vite/JSR rather than through a node_modules `require` of a JSON file, so the `@sentry/deno/import` hook is inert here (removing it changes nothing on either version, verified on both). Two warnings are worth more than the K3 one: (1) unhandled errors in a Fresh route handler are swallowed by Fresh's 500 renderer and never captured on either version, so the guide must show the try/catch middleware placed right after `app.use(staticFiles())` (verified working, with source context); (2) server span/transaction names carry no Fresh route pattern - on 10.73.0 they are `GET <raw path>` with source `url` (high cardinality: `GET /api/alice` vs `GET /api/bob`), on develop they collapse to bare `GET`. C03. Incoming trace continuation on Workers

With incoming sentry-trace aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaab-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1 plus baggage, the http.server segment span keeps trace_id aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaab and parent_span_id bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb, the envelope DSC carries the upstream baggage (environment upstream-env, release upstream@2.0.0) instead of the Worker's own, and the outgoing fetch inside the handler reached the host downstream server with sentry-trace/baggage whose span id equals the recorded http.client span (a284697ef07f0866). C04. Scheduled handler and cron monitors on Workers

develop: works. The withSentry-wrapped scheduled handler emits a segment span named "Scheduled Cron * * * * *" with op "function" (source task, origin auto.faas.cloudflare.scheduled, faas.cron/faas.time/faas.trigger attributes) as a `span` envelope (stream lifecycle). withMonitor sends check_in in_progress then ok on run 1, and in_progress then error on run 2, all carrying monitor_config.schedule and a trace context. The thrown error on run 2 is captured as an unhandled event with mechanism auto.faas.cloudflare.scheduled, the segment span status becomes error, and the exception is rethrown (wrangler returns 500 on /__scheduled). Every scheduled invocation gets its own trace_id.

Wrap the SDK-instrumented `scheduled` and re-seed the isolate's default scope before each run: const wrapped = Sentry.withSentry((env) => ({ dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }), handler); // Outside any invocation this is the isolate's default current scope, which the scheduled wrapper reuses for every cron run. const isolateScope = Sentry.getCu [works-after-all] Reproduced the reported failure with the default configuration, then found a userland change that makes every scheduled run get its own trace on 10.73.0. Setup: $SCRATCH/deep/verify2-C04-10730-2/{plain,optcb,stream}/ (node_modules -> $SCRATCH/qs/qs10/cloudflare/node_modules, @sentry/cloudflare 10.73.0 from npm; wrangler.jsonc: compatibility_date 2026-05-01, nodejs_compat, crons ["* * * * *", "*/5 * * * *"]); sink copied to $SCRATCH/deep/verify2-C04-10730-2/sink.mjs. Docs: partial. platform-includes/crons/setup/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:1-11; includes/javascript-crons-job-monitoring.mdx:1-15; docs/platforms/javascript/common/crons/index.mdx:26,31-35; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:111-159 withMonitor check-ins (in_progress then ok/error) and the trace association matched the crons include on both versions. The Cloudflare guide never mentions that withSentry also instruments the scheduled handler: it emits a 'Scheduled Cron <cron>' span (op function on develop, faas.cron on 10.73.0, origin auto.faas.cloudflare.scheduled) and captures and rethrows errors from the handler. It should also warn that on 10.73.0 every scheduled run in a warm isolate shares one trace id (check-ins and errors of unrelated runs are stitched into one trace), while develop gives each run its own trace.

Notes: 1) Root cause of the shared trace_id on 10.73.0 (verified in source): @sentry/cloudflare 10.73.0 build/esm/async.js `withIsolationScope` clones only the isolation scope and reuses the current scope by reference (`const scope = getScopes().scope`). A scheduled invocation runs outside any request ALS context, so it always sees the default current scope, whose propagation context traceId is generated once per isolate. develop's packages/server-utils/src/async-context.ts `withIsolationScope` clones the current scope and, unless continuing an incoming trace, assigns a fresh traceId/sampleRand, which is why each cron run gets its own trace on develop. Consequence on 10.73.0: all cron runs of a warm isolate (and their check-ins and errors) land in one trace in Sentry. 2) Op name differs: develop emits op "function" (conventions FUNCTION) for the scheduled segment, 10.73.0 emits "faas.cron". C05. Queues producer and consumer locally

develop: works. With a plain withSentry() ExportedHandler, env.Q.send() and env.Q.sendBatch() produced `queue.publish` spans named `send Q` (binding name, not the queue name) as children of the http.server segment, with messaging.* attributes including messaging.batch.message_count: 2 and body sizes for the batch. The queue(batch) handler produced `queue.process` segment spans named `process probe-q` with messaging.batch.message_count, messaging.message.retry.count (0 then 1 on the workerd retry), and the thrown consumer error was captured as an unhandled event with mechanism auto.faas.cloudflare.queue and the process span status set to error/internal_error. Each queue invocation got its own trace_id.

Docs: no. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:111-159; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/index.mdx:1-8 No page mentions Queues. A features page should say that withSentry instruments env.<binding>.send/sendBatch as queue.publish spans named 'send <binding name>' (with messaging.batch.message_count and body size) and the queue handler as a segment 'process <queue name>' (op queue.process, faas.trigger pubsub, batch and retry counts) with thrown errors captured as auto.faas.cloudflare.queue. It should note that no trace propagates from producer to consumer, and that on 10.73.0 all queue batches in the same isolate share one trace id (develop gives each batch its own).

Notes: Setup: wrangler.jsonc with queues.producers [{binding:"Q", queue:"probe-q"}] and queues.consumers [{queue:"probe-q", max_batch_size:10, max_batch_timeout:1, max_retries:1}], compatibility_date 2026-05-01, nodejs_compat. Worker: fetch routes /send (env.Q.send({n:1}) + env.Q.sendBatch([{body:{n:2}},{body:{n:3}}])), /send-bad (send {n:99}), /send-sentinel (send {n:7}); queue handler throws for n===99, captureMessage('sentinel-queue') for n===7, acks the rest. Driver waits 3s between requests so each lands in its own batch, then waits for the sentinel-queue event in the sink. Local queues worked in wrangler dev 4.128.0 without extra flags, retries happen immediately after the throw. develop: works. With env.DB used directly inside withSentry (no wrapper), every D1 call produced a db.query span with origin auto.db.cloudflare.d1: exec, prepare().bind().run(), .all(), .first() and batch(). In the default stream lifecycle the span name is the low-cardinality query summary ("CREATE TABLE users", "INSERT users", "SELECT users", "D1 batch") with the full statement in db.query.text and the summary in db.query.summary; with traceLifecycle: 'static' the transaction's child spans carry the full SQL as description. cloudflare.d1.duration/rows_read/rows_written are set on run() and all() only (first(), exec() and batch() get none, matching the source), and batch adds db.operation.batch.size and the joined statements in db.query.text. C07. R2 and KV locally

develop: works. With r2_buckets BUCKET and kv_namespaces KV in wrangler.jsonc and plain `npx wrangler dev`, BUCKET.put/get/head/list/delete each produce one child span under the http.server segment: ops object.put/object.get/object.head/object.list/object.delete, names r2_put/r2_get/r2_head/r2_list/r2_delete, origin auto.faas.cloudflare.r2, attributes cloudflare.r2.operation (PutObject/GetObject/HeadObject/ListObjects/DeleteObject), cloudflare.r2.bucket=BUCKET, cloudflare.r2.request.key=probe/k1 (list: cloudflare.r2.request.prefix=probe/). KV.put/get/list/delete produce no spans at all: the /kv request yields only the http.server segment span. Same result with traceLifecycle 'static' (transaction GET /r2 with the five nested spans, GET /kv with spans: []). Default lifecycle is stream, so R2 spans arrive in a `span` envelope with the segment named GET.

C09. wrapRequestHandler without nodejs_compat

develop: partial. `wrapRequestHandler` from `@sentry/cloudflare/request` with only `nodejs_als` boots, captures the thrown error, emits a request span, propagates sentry-trace/baggage on outgoing fetch (http.client span parented to the request span, same trace id) and installs the base integration set including SpanStreaming. Removing all compatibility flags gives the identical result (no `node:` import in the `/request` chain, no failure to record). Defect: `/request` never installs the AsyncLocalStorage context strategy, so the SDK runs on the stack strategy; a request with no I/O and nothing captured (`/hello`) is emitted as a legacy `transaction` envelope (empty `trace: {}` DSC) instead of a `span` envelope, and in a curl `/hello` then `/sentinel` sequence the sentinel event was dropped. Calling `setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy()` from `@sentry/server-utils/no-diagnostic-channels` at module scope fixes both.

No page says which compatibility flags the wrapper needs: it ran with only nodejs_als and even with no flags on both versions, unlike withSentry which needs nodejs_compat per getting-started-config:5. Docs should also say that '/request' does not install the AsyncLocalStorage context strategy, and that on develop this makes requests without I/O go out as legacy transaction envelopes and can drop events unless setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy() is called at module scope.

Notes: 1. Neither `/request` entry point (develop or 10.73.0) installs the AsyncLocalStorage async-context strategy; both run on core's global stack strategy (stack traces show `AsyncContextStack.withScope`). On 10.73.0 (static lifecycle) this is invisible in the envelopes. On develop (stream lifecycle) it is: `getClient()` after the `await handler()` boundary resolves to no client for a request without I/O, so `_onSpanEnded` in `packages/core/src/tracing/sentrySpan.ts` takes the `_convertSpanToTransaction` path and the segment is sent as a `transaction` envelope with empty `trace: {}` DSC, while requests that did I/O or captured something go out as `span` envelopes; a curl `/hello` + `/sentinel` sequence lost the sentinel event. Adding `import { setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy } from '@sentry/server-utils/no-diagnostic-channels'; setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy();` at module

C10. Cloudflare Pages with sentryPagesPlugin

develop: partial. sentryPagesPlugin (10.67.0 tarball) boots under `wrangler pages dev`: the thrown function error arrives as an unhandled `auto.http.cloudflare` event and every request, including static assets `/` and `/app.js`, produces an `http.server` span envelope (stream lifecycle) named `GET /` for the root and just `GET` for every other path (`url.path` carried as an attribute, source `url`). Two regressions vs 10.73.0: (1) the client is cached in the isolate (`clientCache.js`, `__SENTRY_CLOUDFLARE_CLIENT__`) so the Dedupe integration's state survives across requests, and identical events from separate requests are dropped: two consecutive `GET /api/error` requests yield ONE error event, and a repeated `captureMessage('sentinel')` from separate requests is dropped with `Event dropped due to being a duplicate of previously captured event.` until a different event intervenes; (2) the span for the throwing request ends with `status: ok` and no `http.response.status_code`. Also `attachStacktrace` now defaults to true (core client.js:92) so message events carry an `exception` value with a synthetic stack.

Docs: partial. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:161-205; includes/cloudflare-pages-middleware-intro.mdx:1; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/astro.mdx:28-31; docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/integrations/dedupe.mdx:8-10 The Pages setup matches, but the page should say that a root functions/_middleware.js wraps every request including static assets, so GET / and GET /app.js produce spans or transactions unless the middleware is scoped to a subdirectory. It should add that on develop the client is cached per isolate so the default dedupeIntegration drops identical errors and captureMessage calls from consecutive requests (10.73.0 creates a fresh client per request and delivers all of them), and that the request span of a throwing handler carries no error status or http.response.status_code on either version.

Notes: 1) Static assets: on both versions the root `functions/_middleware.js` wraps every request, so `GET /` and `GET /app.js` (a plain static file) produce a span/transaction. Users who only want function spans need to scope the middleware (e.g. `functions/api/_middleware.js`) or filter; the docs do not mention this. 2) Develop span names: `/` keeps its path (`GET /`, segment source `route`), everything else is method-only (`GET`, source `url`) with `url.path` as an attribute. This follows wrapRequestHandlerWithInit.js: name = rawName when source is `route` or streaming is off, else the bare method. 3) Develop regression, likely affects withSentry Workers too, not just Pages: the client is cached per isolate (build/esm/prod/clientCache.js, GLOBAL_OBJ.__SENTRY_CLOUDFLARE_CLIENT__), so the default Dedupe integration compares against the previous request's event. develop: works. With no dsn in code, withSentry(env => ({ tunnel })) picked up SENTRY_DSN, SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT=qa, SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE=1 and SENTRY_RELEASE=r1 from wrangler vars: error and message events carry release r1 / environment qa, every request produced a sampled http.server span (stream lifecycle, sentry.sample_rate=1, DSC sampled=true). C12. Sessions, metrics and logs on Workers

develop: partial. Metrics (Sentry.metrics.count/gauge) and logs (Sentry.logger.info plus consoleLoggingIntegration for console.log/warn) arrive as trace_metric and log envelopes, flushed at the end of the request that produced them (they land before the next request's span envelope; no 7s wait or explicit ctx.waitUntil(Sentry.flush()) needed, though both variants also work). No session or sessions envelope is ever sent: two OK requests plus one throwing request with release set produce only span envelopes and the error event; the package exports no startSession/captureSession/endSession either. Sessions are therefore absent, which matches the docs (cloudflare is excluded from auto session tracking).

C13. Request body capture on Workers

develop: works. With dataCollection: {} the JSON body of a POST to a throwing route lands in request.data on both the error event and the transaction (static lifecycle), and as http.request.body.data on the http.server segment span (stream lifecycle). Disabling bodies either via httpServerIntegration({ maxRequestBodySize: 'none' }) or via dataCollection: { httpBodies: [] } removes request.data from both event and transaction. Built types expose maxRequestBodySize?: MaxRequestBodySize with @default 'medium' on HttpServerIntegrationOptions.

C14. Streaming responses and work after the response on Workers

develop: works. Default (stream) lifecycle: the request span for /stream (ReadableStream, 3 chunks 300ms apart) covers the whole stream (604-631ms, end timestamp equals the third chunk's timestamp), and the "after" span from ctx.waitUntil(Sentry.startSpan(...)) arrives ~500ms after the response as its own span envelope, non-segment, with the request span as parent and the same trace id. With traceLifecycle: 'static' the request transactions still cover the stream (GET /stream, 604ms) but the "after" span is lost entirely: the GET /after transaction is sent 1ms after the response with spans: [], no follow-up envelope ever arrives (checked 3s after a unique sentinel), and the debug log shows the child span finishing after the root span had already been sent.

Docs: partial. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:372-410 The waitUntil section is accurate but hedges with 'may be missing'; in practice a span started in ctx.waitUntil that finishes after the response is always dropped under the static lifecycle, silently, with no debug-log warning. The page should state that plainly and add that streamed ReadableStream responses are covered by the request span until the body stream closes (not when headers are sent), in both lifecycles.

Notes: 1) Sentinel gotcha on Workers: a repeated Sentry.captureMessage('sentinel') with the identical message is dropped by the Dedupe integration after the first one, because wrangler dev reuses the isolate across requests (first run had the event, later runs silently had none). Use a unique message per run (drive.sh uses sentinel-$RANDOM). 2) Timing sentinel: the "after" span ends 500ms after the response, so the sentinel must be sent after that (drive.sh sleeps 1s before /sentinel); an immediate sentinel arrives before the after span and gives a false negative. 3) In stream mode the request span's end for /stream matches the last chunk's enqueue time (end 1788510383.938 vs chunk-3 1788510383938), i.e. the span is ended when the response body stream closes, not when headers are sent (ttfb 9ms). Static mode shows the same 604ms coverage for the transaction. 4) Static-mode loss is silent: no SD

C20. React Router framework mode on Cloudflare Workers

10.73.0: works. React Router 7.16.0 framework mode (v7 branch of the cloudflare template, react-router build + @cloudflare/vite-plugin, vite 8.2.2, wrangler 4.129.0) wrapped with @sentry/cloudflare withSentry and @sentry/react-router/cloudflare in entry.server.tsx. The loader throw is captured as an error event (once per request, via handleError -> Sentry.captureException, mechanism generic, handled true) and every request produces a parametrized http.server transaction (GET /ok/:id, source route) with a child http.client span for a loader fetch; injectTraceMetaTags emits sentry-trace/baggage meta tags into the HTML. The only hiccup: the scaffold's react-router.config.ts enables v8_middleware, so passing the template-style `{ cloudflare: { env, ctx } }` load context makes every request 500 with 'Invalid `context` value provided to `handleRequest`' (a React Router constraint, not an SDK bug; the Sentry event and internal_error transaction were still reported correctly for that failure). Docs: wrong. platform-includes/distributed-tracing/how-to-use/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:11,26,57,66; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/agents-sdk.mdx:29; docs/platforms/javascript/common/agent-tracing/openai.mdx:107; docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/durableobject.mdx:39-41 Every page tells users to set `enableRpcTracePropagation: true`; on 10.73.0 that option is deprecated in favor of `rpcTracePropagationBindings: ["BINDING"]`, and on develop it no longer exists, so the documented option gives no rpc span and a separate trace. The pages should switch to `rpcTracePropagationBindings` on both caller and receiver, and note that no caller-side rpc span or http.client span is created for service-binding calls (only the receiver's `rpc <method>` span, parented to the caller's http.server span).

Notes: Both versions pass. Extra findings: (1) Neither version emits an http.client span for env.SELF.fetch(); instrumentFetcher (develop packages/cloudflare/src/instrumentations/worker/instrumentFetcher.ts, same in 10.73.0) only injects sentry-trace/baggage headers, even though its JSDoc says it creates a span. The callee http.server span's parent is therefore the caller's http.server span directly. (2) Neither version creates a caller-side span for the RPC method call; the only `rpc` span is the receiver-side one, so an RPC to a non-Sentry receiver is invisible in the trace. (3) On develop the receiver creates the rpc span only when RPC meta arrives (spanName callback returns undefined otherwise): without rpcTracePropagationBindings the negative control showed no rpc span at all, and the error captured inside hello() had its own trace_id, so the option gates both propagation and the span, not

C26. Workflows locally

develop: partial. Step spans and the deterministic trace id work: each step.do produces a `function` segment span named after the step (attributes code.function.name, workflow.step.name, cloudflare.workflow.attempt/retries.*, origin auto.faas.cloudflare.workflow, source task), and every span/event of an instance carries trace_id = instanceId without dashes (UUID ids) or the SHA-1-derived id (non-UUID id `probe-c26-nonuuid-1788510789726` -> `82f4e4ec1be76973794b1bb7c7bc954f`, matching the SDK formula). Error capture does NOT match the claim: the local engine (wrangler 4.128.0) passes a step context with `attempt` and `config.retries.limit`, so the SDK only captures the error on the final attempt. A step that throws once and then succeeds (limit 3) produces zero exception events; an always-failing step with limit 1 produces one event (attempt 2), not two. That is the intended feature-detection behavior in workflows.ts, but 'both failures captured' does not hold.

Docs: partial. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/workflows.mdx:8-30 The trace_id derivation and sampling rules are accurate. The page should add that step errors are only captured on the final retry attempt when the engine passes a step context (a step that fails once then succeeds sends no event), that each step.do is its own segment/transaction sharing the instance trace_id with no per-run root span, and that the step span op is `function.step.do` on 10.x and `function` on develop.

Notes: 1) The "both failures captured since dedupe is off" expectation cannot be observed with the local engine: wrangler 4.128.0 / workerd passes a step context `{step:{name,count},attempt,config:{retries:{limit,backoff,delay},timeout}}` (logged in app.log), so both SDK versions apply the feature-detected final-attempt gating from workflows.ts (`isFinalAttempt = !hasStepContext || attempt > retryLimit`). With the default retry config a step that throws only on early attempts never reaches Sentry at all, which is a user-facing surprise worth documenting. Dedupe-off could not be exercised as intended here because at most one event per instance can be emitted. 2) Op difference: develop emits `function` (conventions FUNCTION), 10.73.0 emits `function.step.do`. 3) Every step is its own segment (develop) / transaction (10.73.0) sharing the instance trace id; there is no root span per run, so retries

Step 1 BROKEN: `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/cloudflare/nodejs_compat"` does not build - the subpath export was deleted on develop (exports are only `.`, `./request`, `./vite`, and there is no `build/*/nodejs_compat/` directory at all). Every code sample on features/nodejs-compat.mdx and on the Cloudflare prisma.mdx page therefore fails at bundle time on the very version the nodejs-compat page names as its future default (v11). Step 2 WORKS via the main entry: `prismaIntegration()` imported from `@sentry/cloudflare` produces a full prisma span tree, and develop is strictly better than 10.73.0 here because it sets `sentry.op: "db"` on the SQL spans (10.73.0 leaves op unset). Separate non-Sentry finding: creating the `PrismaMariaDb` adapter at module scope hangs workerd (pool timeout after 10001ms, plus an `Uncaught RuntimeError: unreachable` wasm trap); the adapter must be constructed inside the request handler. Raw `node:net` connect and the raw `mariadb@3.4.5` driver both work fine at either scope, so this is a Prisma-adapter/global-scope-I/O issue, not a workerd socket restriction.

10.73.0: works. Both documented claims hold. Step 1: a Worker whose only change is `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/cloudflare/nodejs_compat"` boots under `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]` and serves requests; the namespace carries 107 exports including `prismaIntegration`. Step 2: `Sentry.prismaIntegration()` from that entrypoint instruments Prisma 6.19.3 + @prisma/adapter-mariadb against MariaDB and emits the full prisma span tree, including `prisma:client:operation` (with `model`/`method`) and a span whose description is the raw SQL carrying `db.query.text` and `db.system`. Same module-scope caveat as develop: the `PrismaMariaDb` adapter must be constructed inside the request handler, not at module scope.

N3. Cloudflare Vite plugin: autoInstrumentation, option names and defaults

develop: broken. The SDK does exactly what the develop JSDoc says, and the docs page describes a different API. `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` with NO options auto-wraps everything: options are top-level `autoInstrumentation` / `buildTimeInstrumentation` and both default to TRUE. A plain, never-wrapped default export produced a request span; the DurableObject, the WorkerEntrypoint and the module-scope mysql query all produced child spans in the SAME trace as the request, and the unhandled route error was captured. `_experimental.autoInstrumentation` / `_experimental.useDiagnosticsChannelInjection` (the only names the docs page documents) do not exist on develop: passing them is a TS error and at runtime they are ignored, so a reader copying the documented snippet gets full auto-instrumentation by accident rather than by the flags they set. Opt-outs verified separately: `{ autoInstrumentation: false }` wraps nothing (empty sink) while still injecting the mysql channel; `{ buildTimeInstrumentation: false }` keeps all wrapping but drops the db span. WorkerEntrypoint wrapping and auto-populated `rpcTracePropagationBindings` are real and are not on the docs page at all. Two extra gaps found: (1) the develop JSDoc at packages/cloudflare/src/vite/index.ts:39 says options come from a co-located `instrument.*` file, but instrumentFile.ts:16 hardcodes basename `instrument.server` — the docs page is right here and the JSDoc is wrong; (2) `cloudflare({ configPath: './wrangler.agent.jsonc' })` WITHOUT `wranglerConfigPath` silently falls back to the root `wrangler.jsonc`, whose `main` names a different entry, so nothing is wrapped and NO warning is emitted.

10.73.0: works. The docs page matches the shipped 10.73.0 plugin on every point it makes. The options really are `_experimental.autoInstrumentation` and `_experimental.useDiagnosticsChannelInjection`, they really default to false, and a bare `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` really is a complete no-op (nothing wrapped, no channel injection, empty sink). With both flags set to true, the entire auto-wrapping half works: a plain unwrapped default export got a `GET /db` transaction, the DurableObject and the WorkerEntrypoint got `bump` / `ping` rpc transactions in the SAME trace as their request, mysql produced a `db SELECT 1 + 1 AS two` child span, and the unhandled error was captured. Two behaviors are real but absent from the page: the plugin also wraps a self-bound `WorkerEntrypoint` class (with `withSentry`, origin auto.faas.cloudflare.worker_entrypoint) and auto-populates `rpcTracePropagationBindings` — the page's feature list (:16) and the `_experimental.autoInstrumentation` option body (:146) name only Durable Objects, Workflows and Agents SDK classes. Same as develop, the re-exported-DO caveat at :101 is accurate and the build emits a matching warning, and `wranglerConfigPath` behaves as documented.

N4. Cloudflare Agents SDK: instrumentAgentWithSentry, callable spans and conversation IDs

develop (worktree build, @sentry/cloudflare 10.67.0, v11 line): partial. instrumentAgentWithSentry works: one `rpc` span per @callable() over WebSocket, a conversation ID on every gen_ai span for HTTP/RPC/chat-turn units of work, rotation on `message:clear` (including the real `cf_agent_chat_clear` message on AIChatAgent), and DO storage spans only for the non-framework key. Three docs claims are wrong: (a) the callable span carries the agent class ONLY, there is no instance-name attribute; (b) the class it carries is the *base* class name (`MyAgentBase`), not the exported/bound class (`MyAgent`); (c) the conversation ID is a fresh uuid4, NOT the agent instance name (`room-1`) as features/agents-sdk.mdx:39 claims. The page's main sample also fails `tsc` on develop because `enableRpcTracePropagation` was removed; at runtime it is silently ignored.

The automatic conversation ID is a fresh uuid4 that rotates on `message:clear` / `cf_agent_chat_clear`, never the agent instance name, so :39 and the per-user/singleton reasoning at :41 need rewriting: overriding with `setConversationId` is about mapping to your own chat session ID, not about escaping instance-name collisions. Both SDK versions ship byte-identical agent instrumentation (I diffed the develop sources against the published 10.73.0 build under node_modules/@sentry/cloudflare/build/esm/instrumentations/agents/), so every behavioural difference reported above between the two comes from the surrounding SDK (traceLifecycle default, option typing), not from the agents feature itself. N5. Durable Object websockets, alarms and storage key filtering

develop (6f2da7483d, 10.67.0 tarballs): works. instrumentDurableObjectWithSentry produces one `websocket webSocketMessage` span per websocket message (both hibernatable connections), one `websocket webSocketClose` span per close, one `function alarm` span per alarm invocation with the throw captured as mechanism `auto.faas.cloudflare.durable_object` / handled=false, and storage spans only for the non-prefixed key. Tags set inside a handler stay on that invocation's event/span, no cross-talk between the two connections. One caveat that is not a docs claim: every websocket handler invocation shares a single trace_id for the lifetime of the DO isolate, across both connections and across a second, later pair of connections.

N10. Debug IDs and source maps, verified without a Sentry account

develop: partial. No debug ID is produced anywhere in the documented flow on any of the three runtimes: sentryCloudflareVitePlugin() and sentryBunPlugin() contain no debug-ID code at all (grep for debugId/_sentryDebugIds in packages/cloudflare/src/vite/ and packages/bun/src/plugin.ts returns nothing), the emitted .map has no debug_id key, the bundle has no _sentryDebugIds registration snippet, and every runtime event arrives with debug_meta.images: [] and no debug_id on any frame. The runtime half of the SDK is fine: hand-injecting the standard _sentryDebugIds snippet into the built Worker bundle makes the very next event carry a matching debug_meta image, so the missing piece is purely injection. The consequence differs per runtime. Cloudflare is the broken case: frames point at the built bundle (dist/qs_cloudflare/index.js:11569:9, with no context_line, because workerd has no filesystem), so without a debug ID the wizard flow has to fall back to release+path matching. Bun and Deno are effectively unaffected: their runtimes already resolve frames to the original sources (lib/boom.ts:2:13, app:///lib/boom.ts:2:9) with context_line populated, even from a bun build --compile / deno compile single-file binary, so uploading a source map for the bundle would have nothing to match against. The .map Vite emits is correct, applying it by hand resolves the top frame exactly (11569:9 -> ../../src/boom.ts:2:8).

Identical to develop in every respect that matters here, so this is neither a regression nor a fix on either side. sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({_experimental:{useDiagnosticsChannelInjection:true}}) with build.sourcemap: true emits a bundle with zero _sentryDebugIds registrations, no //# debugId= comment, and a .map with no debug_id key; the resulting event carries debug_meta.images: [] and frames at dist/qs_cloudflare/index.js:11612:9 with no context_line. Plain wrangler dev with "upload_source_maps": true behaves the same, with frames at the .wrangler/tmp/dev-*/index.js scratch bundle. Bun's own bundler again stamps //# debugId= plus a camelCase debugId map key that is not what Sentry reads, and the runtime resolves frames to the original .ts sources anyway; bun build --compile leaves that debugId empty. Deno resolves to app:///lib/boom.ts:2:9 under deno run and to a /var/folders/.../T/deno-compile-n10-bin/ VFS path under deno compile. So on 10.73.0 too, the documented "Add Readable Stack Traces With Source Maps" flow has no debug-ID linkage to work with on any of the three runtimes.

Verification: refuted: an independent run made it work. [works-after-all] The symptom reproduces exactly as reported, but the conclusion does not survive: the reporter used a plugin that has nothing to do with source maps. On 10.73.0 `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin` is only an instrumentation plugin, it never injects debug IDs. Its whole body is (cf-vite/node_modules/@sentry/cloudflare/build/esm/vite/index.js): function sentryCloudflareVitePlugin(options = {}) { return [ ...options._experimental?.useDiagnosticsChannelInjection ? [sentryOrchestrionPlugin({ inj Workaround: Cloudflare + Vite: `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin` does not handle source maps at all; add `@sentry/vite-plugin` as the last entry in `plugins`, exactly as docs/platforms/javascript/common/sourcemaps/uploading/vite.mdx says. // npm i -D @sentry/vite-plugin import { cloudflare } from "@cloudflare/vite-plugin"; import { sentryCloudflareVitePlugin } from "@sentry/cloudflare/vite"; import { sent

Docs: partial. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:242, guides/bun/index.mdx:115, guides/deno/index.mdx:134 (all include getting-started-sourcemaps-short-version); platform-includes/getting-started-sourcemaps-short-version/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:5-19 (upload_source_maps + wizard) and javascrip The Cloudflare source maps flow should state that neither `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin` nor plain `wrangler --upload-source-maps` injects debug IDs (the bundle gets no `_sentryDebugIds` registration, the emitted `.map` has no `debug_id`, and events arrive with `debug_meta.images: []`), so resolution falls back to release plus path matching and readers who want debug IDs must add `@sentry/vite-plugin` alongside the Cloudflare plugin. The Bun and Deno guides should say that this step is usually unnecessary: both runtimes already resolve frames to the original `.ts` sources with context lines, including from `bun build --compile` and `deno compile` binaries, and Bun's own bundler writes a camelCase `debugId` map key that Sentry does not read.

Notes: Central result: the debug-ID half of the flow is absent at the source level, not merely misconfigured. `grep -rn "debug.?[Ii]d|debugId|sentry-debug-id|debug_id"` over ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/packages/cloudflare/src/vite/ and packages/bun/src/plugin.ts returns zero hits on develop; `@sentry/cloudflare/vite` is just `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` + `sentryCloudflareAutoInstrumentPlugin`, and `@sentry/bun/plugin` is a one-line re-export of `sentryOrchestrionPlugin`. Debug-ID injection would have to come from `@sentry/vite-plugin` / `sentry-cli sourcemaps inject`, which the wizard adds separately and which no guide mentions alongside the SDK plugin.
